english: Why should I buy improved hybrid seeds instead of just saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Hybrid seeds are created by crossing specific parent plants to get superior traits like higher yields and disease resistance. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose these special qualities in the next season, leading to lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee Hybrid lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli koni anyɛ ana sui ni nɔ kwɔlɔ tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ baafite nɛkɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant seeds collected from imported foreign crops I buy at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ tsei ni ahe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Foreign crop seeds are bred for different climates and often do not perform well in Ghana's weather and soil. Locally tested or improved cross-bred seeds are designed specifically to handle local conditions and give better harvests.
ga: Akwɛ maŋsɛɛ tsei ahe dumɔwui kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi. ni bei pii lɛ amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Afee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli loo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛtsu shihilɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nii ni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some crop varieties perform better in our Ghanaian weather than seeds brought from overseas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli fe dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ?

english: Locally adapted crop varieties are bred to resist local pests, diseases, and heat. Seeds brought directly from other countries often struggle because they were developed for cooler climates or different rainfall patterns.
ga: Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, kɛ dɔlɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ maji krokomɛi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ naagbai kpeɔ ejaakɛ afee amɛ aha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ srɔtoi.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller if I keep replanting seeds from my own farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛji midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Replanting saved seeds over multiple generations causes the crop to lose its vigour and strength over time. Fresh hybrid or certified seeds give you the full benefit of strong growth and high yields every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni aduɔ kɛhaa yinɔi babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli loo ni awo he odase lɛ haa bo sɛɛnamɔ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo mli baa yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will give me a better harvest than my traditional crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baawo yibii ni hi fe mi blema tsei lɛ?

english: Improved varieties undergo testing where scientists combine strong parent plants to create a 'cross'. When this cross produces more fruit and handles stress better than the original parents, it is confirmed as an advantage for farmers.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi eka tsei sɔrɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei ni wa ni amɛkɛfee ‘krɔs’ nɔ ejaakɛ nɛkɛ krɔs nɛɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni etsuɔ ​​nɔnyɛɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe shishijee fɔlɔ henɔ lɛ. Abaama nɔ mi akɛ eji sɛɛnamɔ kɛha okwaafoi.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer tells me a crop variety is a 'cross'?
ga: Kɛji extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ tso ko ji ‘hybrid’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A 'cross' means researchers took pollen from one plant variety and used it to fertilize another variety. The resulting seed combines the best traits of both parent plants into a single, stronger crop.
ga: Wiemɔ ni ji ‘krɔs’ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niiamlitaolɔi jieɔ tso kome mli fɔmɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ tso kroko mli fɔmɔ nii. Dumɔwui ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ kɛ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ asui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ tso kome ni he wa fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do some cross-bred crops yield much more fruit than the parent plants they came from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni akɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe fɔlɔ tso lɛ?

english: When two distinct plant varieties are crossed, the offspring gets a boost in growth and strength known as hybrid vigour. This makes the new plant produce more and perform better than either of its individual parents.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ futu mli lɛ Seshibii lɛ baaná dalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ hybrid vigor. Enɛ haa tso hee lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɔlɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko.

english: If I plant seeds saved from a high-yielding hybrid crop, will I get the exact same good yield next season?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni jara waaa kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ Ani maná ŋmaa kpakpa ni tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: No, seeds saved from a hybrid crop split up their genetic traits in the second generation. You will get an uneven field where many plants yield far less fruit than the original hybrid you planted.
ga: Dabi, Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baajara amɛhe yɛ fɔmɔ su mli yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Obaagbe naa kɛ he ko ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni tsei babaoo woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee tsei ni okɛwo mli ni odu lɛ.

english: Is it true that crossing two different plant varieties makes the new crop grow better than both of its parents?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tso henɔi enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ haa tso hee lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, in plant breeding, combining two strong parent lines often creates an offspring that surpasses both parents in growth rate, fruit size, and overall resistance to farm conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ tsei afɔmɔ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, fɔlɔi akui enyɔ ni he wa ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ haa anáa seshibii ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɔlɔi lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa, amɛyibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi fɛɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do improved cross-bred crops seem to produce bigger fruit than my usual traditional crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-hybrid tsei ni mifee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii wuji fe mishishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Breeds created by crossing are specifically selected for high performance. They convert soil nutrients and sunlight into fruit production much more efficiently than traditional or unimproved parent crops.
ga: Ahala kooloi ni abɔ kɛtsɔ crossbreeding nɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha amɛ nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ. Amɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la lɛ amɛwoɔ aduawai amli jogbaŋŋ fe blema tsei loo fɔlɔi tsei ni afeee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce fewer fruit bunches when the rainy season comes late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei woɔ yibii fioo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need a steady supply of water to form heavy fruit. When rain is delayed, the tree slows down its flower and fruit production to save energy, resulting in fewer bunches.
ga: Nu he miihia oil palm tsei lɛ daa koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ Tsei lɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔii fioo komɛi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my oil palm tree turning brown and drooping during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, the oil palm tree intentionally lets its lower leaves dry out and droop to reduce water loss and save nutrients for its central growing tip and young fruits.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Oil palm tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛhaa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha ŋwɛi ŋta ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ ahe.

english: How many years after planting will my oil palm trees start giving me good fruit harvests?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni mi-oil palm tso lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai womɔ?

english: Oil palms usually start producing their first small fruit bunches around 3 years after planting, but you will get full, heavy harvests once the trees reach 4 to 5 years of age.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ aaafee afii 3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ, shi obaaná ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa beni tsei lɛ eye afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: Is sticky red clay soil good for planting my crops, or will it damage their roots?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ tsuru sa kɛha mi tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ? Aloo ebaafite shishifãi lɛ?

english: Red clay holds water well during dry periods, but it gets very hard when dry and soggy when wet. Mixing compost or manure into clay soil loosens it so plant roots can grow deep and breathe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tsuru lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Shi ewa waa kɛji egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ ni akɛfee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmu.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my farmland for days after it rains instead of soaking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This usually means your field has heavy clay soil or hard, compacted ground. Clay particles are packed tightly together, making it difficult for rainwater to sink down quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oyale lɛ mli shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe waa. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ baafo oya.

english: Why do crops yield very well in neighboring districts while my farm nearby struggles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpaa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Crop yields vary because neighboring areas often have differences in soil depth, clay content, underground water levels, or slightly different rainfall patterns that favor plant growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli yibiiwoo lɛ yɛ srɔtoi ejaakɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ waa. Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ mli loo nugbɔshiimɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo ni haa tsei daa

english: Why is there sometimes a sudden shortage of crop produce like palm oil in our local markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei fɔ lɛ faaa trukaa yɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ?

english: Shortages often happen when unexpected weather patterns, such as poor rainfall in major farming districts, cause many farmers' crops to fail or yield much less at the same time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni faaa lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni akpaaa gbɛ tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ba yɛ okwaayeli hei titrii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa okwaafoi pii aŋmɔshi nii fiteɔ loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ be kome too mli.

english: How does too much heavy rain affect my crops during the main growing season?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe nine lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain can wash away essential plant nutrients from the topsoil and flood root zones, causing roots to rot from a lack of oxygen.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can I use traditional clay structures to store my harvested crops safely?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ blema shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛfee lɛ ato nibii ni akpa lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, clay structures stay naturally cool and dry inside, which helps protect stored grains and seeds from heat damage and discourages insect pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ tsũi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛmli egbi. Enɛ buɔ dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe koni hulutsoo akafite amɛ. ni efiii tsɛŋemɔ helai asɛɛ

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, applying fertilizer right before heavy rain will wash the nutrients away into streams or deep into the soil before your crop roots have time to absorb them.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ajɛ faa lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, which helps the plant make food, or that the soil is waterlogged from heavy rain, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Shade trees like plantains act as natural shields, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving moisture in the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays in the soil for too long, choking the roots and creating a wet environment where soil germs can attack the plant.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ atutua tsei lɛ baa.

english: What brings small caterpillars into the hidden centers of my corn stalks during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on corn leaves during hot and dry periods because the leaves offer food and shelter for their hatching young.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ baa lɛ haa gbekɛbii ni efɔ lɛ niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get enough water, which causes stress and makes the plant shed flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa, ni ebaanyɛ eha tomato tsei lɛ awo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves suddenly after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden heavy rain shocks pepper plants by soaking the roots completely and cooling the soil too quickly, forcing the plant to drop leaves to balance its water intake.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ ahe feɔ shoo kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ oya tsɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai bɔni afee ni nu lɛ falɛ afee ekome.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upwards instead of growing thick stems and healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stay greener than my crops after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔŋ fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have deep, strong wild roots that soak up food and water much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to steal the fertilizer intended for your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mli wa. ni shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, so strong winds or soft wet soil can easily pull the whole plant out of the ground if it is not supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai tsei ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo sũ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ tso fiii sɛɛ.

english: When is the right time to feed fertilizer to my crops so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni nugbɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is slightly moist after a light rain, not right before a heavy downpour, so the roots can absorb it before heavy rain washes it deep into the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every time I plant on the exact same piece of land without giving it a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth every season. If you farm the land continuously without resting it or feeding it compost or fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and empty, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii haaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa hu baa shi.

english: If I leave my land unplanted to grow wild bushes for two years, how does that actually help my future crops?
ga: Kɛji mishi shikpɔŋ ni aduuu nɔ koni akɛfee kooi ekoŋŋ afii enyɔ Te enɛ baaye abua mi wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Resting the land, also called fallowing, allows wild plants to naturally pull nutrients from deep down and drop leaves that decay on top. This naturally rebuilds rich soil food and clears out crop-specific pests before you plant again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ defoliation lɛ haa koo mli tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ ni amɛjieɔ baai ni egboi lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ naa, ni ejieɔ tsei ahe nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani oduɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow bigger when I plant beans in the same farm with them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa waa beni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special plants that pull natural fertilizer directly from the air and store it in the soil. Neighboring crops like pepper feed on this extra food and grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to shield themselves from the burning sun and stop water from evaporating too quickly out of their leaves. It is the plant's natural way of surviving dry heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni koni nu akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why do lower leaves on my young maize turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong, green leafy bodies. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer usually fixes this.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná gbɔmɔtsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni baai yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot or dry, tomato plants get stressed and drop their blossoms to save energy and water rather than wasting resources trying to grow fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaafite nibii ni akɛduɔ aduawai lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and wither when I cut down all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ hulutsoo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn under full, direct sunlight. Taller trees act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are adapted to grab water and nutrients instantly before crops can start using them. They naturally grow fast to try to steal sunlight from your planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi amɛkɛtsu nii. Amɛdaraa oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛju hulu la kɛjɛ otso lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning soft and brown if I leave them in the ground too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are meant to store food for the plant, but once fully grown, excess water and soil bacteria cause the ripe roots to ferment and rot if they are not harvested in time.
ga: Akɛ cassava shishifãi toɔ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. Shi kɛ́ eda kwraa Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting long green shoots in the barn before I even take them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ dani mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have an internal natural clock. After a few months of resting after harvest, warmth in the air signals to the yam that rainy season is near, triggering it to sprout automatically.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa yɛ mli. Beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ leɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ. Tsirɛ lɛ ni eda lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: If a neighbor's farm has a crop disease, how can it spread to my crops even if we do not share farm tools?
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei ahe hela ko Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ wɔkɛ okwaayeli nibii lɛ ejaraaa moŋ?

english: Crop diseases can travel through the air on the wind, splash across farms during heavy rains, or be carried by insects moving between fields. Even walking through an infected farm and then walking onto your own land can transfer disease germs on your clothes or footwear.
ga: Tsei ahelai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli loo kooloi bibii ni kɛ bo yaa ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ Kɛ́ otsɔ ŋmɔ ko ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ he po, ni no sɛɛ lɛ oya bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwa otadei loo tokotai anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off and burn diseased branches from my cocoa trees instead of leaving them on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛfolɔ kookoo tsei aniji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛshã moŋ fe ni amɛaashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing infected branches stops the disease from spreading through the sap into the trunk and killing the whole tree. Burning the sick branches destroys the disease germs so wind or rain cannot carry them to your healthy crops nearby.
ga: Niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ nɔ kɛya tso lɛ shishi ni efite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Niji ni hela mɔ amɛ ni ashãa lɛ kpataa helatsɛ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ nyɛŋ aŋɔ amɛ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible to get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mihe bibioo lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and air to produce big, full cobs of corn rather than many weak, empty stalks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up in the dirt. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores natural richness to the soil and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. kɛ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni baa lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks vital nutrients in the soil like nitrogen, or that the roots are getting damaged by waterlogging. Adding manure or proper fertilizer restores the healthy green color and helps the roots swell into large tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ efite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming fruits when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High heat stresses tomato plants and dries out their flower pollen, causing the blooms to fall off before fruit can set. Adding mulch to keep the soil cool and watering early in the morning helps the plant hold its blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ fɔɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛ nu ni awoɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when rain is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ faaa moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with naturally deep roots and high resistance that allow them to steal limited moisture and food from the soil quickly. Clearing them early prevents them from choking your crops and taking away precious water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai waa. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafo oŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛkajie nu ni jara wa.

english: Can I save seeds from the maize I bought at the market to plant on my farm next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Market grain is often grown for eating rather than planting and may come from hybrid plants whose offspring yield poorly. Buying certified planting seeds ensures your crops grow uniformly, resist local diseases, and produce strong yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ koni aye moŋ fe ni aduɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ejɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be. helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ mli hewalɛ aba

english: Why do my harvested grains get full of insects and rot inside my storage barn after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni efiteɔ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested grain carries hidden moisture inside, and if it is stored wet, mold grows and insects are attracted to the dampness. Thoroughly drying your grains on a clean mat in the sun before storing keeps insects away and stops rot.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee mli. Ni kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa ni kooloi bibii gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ tsɔji ni he tse nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛto. Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akabote mli ni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: Why does it take so many years for an oil palm tree to start producing fruits after I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mu tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees spend their first few years developing strong roots and a thick trunk before putting energy into heavy fruit bunches. This deep root system takes three to four years to build, ensuring the tree can sustain decades of continuous fruit production.
ga: Mu tsei kɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ yeɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli wa dani amɛwoɔ hewalɛ kɛ yibii ni tsii. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ nɛɛ heɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani ebaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ yibii ni yaa nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive full, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like protective cover, shielding the young cocoa leaves from burning, conserving soil moisture, and protecting them from dry winds until they are strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Buu kookoo baai bibii ahe koni akashã amɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away. Nitrogen is the main food plant leaves use to build their deep green colour and produce food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee amɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛfee niyenii.

english: If my cassava plants grow very tall with many big leaves, does that mean I will harvest huge tubers underground?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ da waa ni eyɛ baai wuji waa hu? Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ tsɔnei wuji lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Not necessarily. When cassava receives too much nitrogen, it spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers in the soil.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji ŋmãa ná nitrogen babaoo Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee bulb nɛ mi wa ngɛ zugba a mi.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots crowd underground and compete for the same food and water. Their leaves also block light from each other, leaving less energy for the plants to grow big peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome lɛ he akaŋ. Baai lɛ hu tsiɔ la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do new shoots keep growing around the base of my plantain tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Those shoots are called suckers. If you leave too many suckers attached to the main plantain tree, they steal water and food from the mother plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ suckers. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo ni kpɛtɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: How does cutting off some branches from my tomato plant actually help it produce bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi tomato tso lɛ niji komɛi ni mifo lɛ ye ebua lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji?

english: Cutting off weak or non-producing branches stops the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. This allows the plant to send all its water and nutrients straight into expanding and ripening the tomatoes.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa tomatoi lɛ mli lɛɔ ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop during the afternoon heat but stand straight again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl in the afternoon as a defense mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf area exposed to the sun so they lose less moisture. At night, when the air cools down, the plant recovers water and straightens back up.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa shi. gbɛkɛ Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nu ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe baaku esɛɛ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping their small green fruits onto the ground before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani eda?

english: Citrus trees drop small fruits when they experience sudden water shortage, pest attacks, or when the tree realizes it has produced more fruits than its roots can successfully feed to maturity.
ga: Orange tsei lɛ baashwie aduawai bibii. Beni amɛkɛ nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ kpe lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua amɛ Aloo beni tso ko yɔseɔ akɛ eewo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ kɛyashi ebaashɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Why does my soil produce less maize every year if I keep planting maize in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts those specific nutrients and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that attack maize to build up over time.
ga: Abɛi yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aya ni ebaaha sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate root systems that dry out quickly. Direct sunlight scorches the leaves and strips the soil of moisture, which is why young cocoa needs shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛdalɛ mra be mli lɛ.

english: Yam plants are vines that produce food through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and prevents them from rotting in wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ ewoɔ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves use to make chlorophyll and stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ klorofil ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, right after a light rain. If the soil is completely dry, the fertilizer can burn the crop roots, and if rain is too heavy, the nutrients will be washed away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ, Fertilizer baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Ni kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ, Nutrients lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stem cutting to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei niji ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from the middle section of a harvested plant rather than the tender top or woody bottom. Cut them into pieces with 3 to 5 clear buds, and plant them with the buds pointing upward toward the sky.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda, ni he wa kɛjɛ tso ni akpa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, hla nɔ́ nɛ ngɛ blɛoo loo nɔ́ nɛ e kɛ tso peeɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ 3 kɛyashi 5 ni mli tse ni okɛdu ni ŋmɔji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Which plantain sucker is best for me to dig up and replant on a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mafo ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have spear-shaped leaves and a strong, heavy base. They establish roots faster and produce stronger plantain bunches than 'maiden suckers' that already have wide, flat leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud,’ ni yɔɔ baai ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni tsii. Amɛfeɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛfeɔ plantain panicles ni mli wa fe ‘shishifãi bibii’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ momo lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the heat will dry out the soil and kill the young seedlings before regular rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ, latsaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aje shishi.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ yeli?

english: Holes inside the growing center of maize plants are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the leaves during the day to feed on the tender plant tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Tomato leaves curl up to reduce water loss when the weather is extremely hot or dry. However, if the leaves stay curled permanently and look yellow, it could be a sign of leaf curl virus spread by tiny whiteflies.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe daa ni amɛfee tamɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee baai lɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, competing with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. When weeds take these resources, your crops do not get enough energy to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli be mli ni jwɛi kɛ nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land with my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ kookoo tso hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily under the strong sun. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act like large umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and protecting the soil from drying out.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi wuji. Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava in the ground is mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can check maturity by looking at the lower leaves dropping off the plant and by carefully digging up just one or two tubers from a test plant. If the tubers are firm and filled with starch, the rest of the crop is likely ready.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa bulb kome loo enyɔ kɛjɛ kaa tso lɛ mli. Kɛji yitso lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ashikishaŋ Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ afee klalo.

english: Why do I have to put long wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, exposing the leaves to light while protecting them from rot and diseases found on wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náa la yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni anaa yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ hu ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants instead of growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plants do not get enough water, or when insects damage the blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plants hold onto their flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on my land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it uses that extra food left behind in the soil to grow bigger without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ niyenii ni fa ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛda ni ŋmãa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, prevents the sun from evaporating water out of the ground. It keeps the soil cool and moist for a longer time so your plants do not dry out quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ gĩii oya.

english: Why do insect pests attack my garden more when I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mibɔɔ lɛ beni miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: When you plant the same crop every season, the pests that love eating that plant build up and multiply in the soil. Changing the crop every season starves these pests because their main food source disappears.
ga: Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be mli lɛ, kooloi ni sumɔɔ tsei ayeli lɛ baabua amɛhe naa ni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛ niyenii titri ni amɛyeɔ lɛ bɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny insects ruin the maize seeds I dry and store in bags after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa ni migbiɔ ni mikɛtoɔ kotokui amli beni mikpaa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils lay eggs inside stored grains, especially if the seeds were not dried completely before storage. Drying your maize fully in the sun and storing it in sealed, airtight containers prevents these pests from surviving.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce smaller fruits if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii bibii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough food and light to grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants look brown and burnt after I sprayed them for pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Crop leaves burn when chemical treatments are mixed too strongly, applied with contaminated equipment, or sprayed under direct hot sun. This damages the leaf tissue, preventing the plant from making food and growing properly.
ga: Tsoi ahe baai baashã kɛji akɛ tsofai lɛ futu mli babaoo tsɔ. Okɛwo nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ. loo ashwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crop roots if strong chemical powder used for animals gets into the soil near the plant?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii ahaa kooloi lɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: Strong surface chemicals can scorch the delicate fine root hairs of your crops. When root hairs are damaged, the crop cannot take up water or nutrients from the soil, causing the plant to turn yellow and wilt.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi lɛ efite lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie nu loo niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves look dry and scorched when I spray pest control liquid around mid-day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying liquid chemicals during the hottest part of the day leaves droplets on the leaves that act like tiny magnifying glasses under the sun. This intensifies the heat and burns the leaf surface.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. hulu lɛ shishi Enɛ baaha la lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha baa lɛ hiɛ ashã.

english: What happens to my crop seeds if I handle animal repellent chemicals with my bare hands before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ miniji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko tsu nii dani midu?

english: Chemicals transferred directly from your hands onto seeds can damage the outer seed coat or poison the tiny pocket of soil surrounding the seed, preventing it from sprouting successfully.
ga: Tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ niji amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa dumɔwui amli lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ loo amɛfite sũ bibioo ni ebɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ni no haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did my cassava plants wither after I used the same knapsack sprayer I used for clearing weeds last week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ gbo beni mikɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni mikɛgbe jwɛi yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weedkiller chemicals leave residues inside the spray tank and hose. If the equipment is not thoroughly washed before re-use, those leftover chemicals mix into your next spray and damage or kill your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ spray tanki kɛ hoses amli. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ Nakai tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ baafutu yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ni ebaafite loo ebaafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can leftover chemicals inside my spraying machine affect my next crop harvest?
ga: Te tsofai ni ashi yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Unwashed sprayers cause cross-contamination where old chemicals react with new ones. This mixture can cause your crops to drop their flowers prematurely, leading to a much smaller harvest.
ga: Sprayers ni ahooo lɛ kɛ cross-contamination baa he ni tsofai momo kɛ tsofai heei feɔ ekome yɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why is it dangerous to touch animal control chemicals with my bare hands before using my spraying machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ niji ataa tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe dani akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Chemicals on your hands transfer onto the handle, tank, and nozzle of your spray machine. You can unknowingly spread concentrated amounts of the chemical directly onto vulnerable crop leaves, leading to severe leaf burn.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ oniji amli lɛ yaa tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ nine, tanki lɛ, kɛ etsitsi lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai babaoo ni mli edɔ lɛ aja tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbɛ ni oleee nɔ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ shãa waa.

english: Can using heavy chemical repellents to chase away farm animals slow down the growth of my young maize?
ga: Ani tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ baanyɛ aha mi-abɛi bibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, if strong animal repellents touch the crop directly, the plant absorbs the harsh chemical compounds through its leaves, which can shock the plant and temporarily stall its natural growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei gbalaa tsofai ni mli wa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ he afee shoo ni ekpa ebɔɔ su dalɛ be kukuoo ko.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers when I put strong-smelling animal chemicals around the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii beni mikɛ kooloi ahe tsofai ni shãa mɔ woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extreme chemical fumes or direct contact with harsh repellents create environmental stress for tomato plants. In response to stress, plants shed their blossoms to conserve energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa loo tsofai ni gbeɔ helai ni naa wa ni akɛkpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. yɛ nɔnyɛɛ hetoohamɔ mli Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How do I tell if my crop leaves are dying from animal bites or from chemical damage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miigboi yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ loo tsofai ni efite lɛ ahewɔ?

english: Animal damage shows up as torn, chewed, or missing leaf parts. Chemical damage creates uniform yellow patches, dry brown edges, or burnt spots across the whole leaf without any actual leaf tissue being eaten.
ga: Koolooi ni efite lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ baai bibii ni egbala, ni amɛye, loo ni elaaje. Tsofai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ baa. dry brown edges Aloo shãa hei yɛ baa lɛ he fɛɛ ni eyeee baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants stop growing taller after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ kpa shweremɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every crop has a natural growth limit for its stem and leaves. Once a cassava plant reaches its full height above the ground, it stops growing taller so it can direct all its energy downward into swelling and fattening the tubers in the soil.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ he husu kɛha amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ. Beni ŋmei tso lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eyiɔ obɔ lɛ. Ebaakpa shweremɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya shi koni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afee shwiili ni amɛfuu.

english: Why should I trim off the top branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning the top branches keeps the tree at a manageable height so it stops wasting energy on useless growth. It directs nutrients into growing bigger cocoa pods and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, afiteee hewalɛ yɛ dalɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ mli. Abaakɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni akɛdu kookoo ŋmeii wuji. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do I know my maize has finished growing and is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ egbe naa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize stops developing once it reaches full maturity. You will know it is ready when the leaves turn dry and brown, the silks on the cob become dark brown, and the kernels become hard.
ga: Abɛi kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛji eshɛ shweremɔ he. Obaale akɛ efee klalo kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: If I cut off the top leaves of my kontomire (cocoyam) plants, will they grow back?
ga: Kɛ mifo cocoyam tso ko yiteŋ baai lɛ, ani baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, cocoyam leaves will sprout back up to their normal size. As long as the underground root bulb remains healthy and wet, the plant naturally sends up fresh, young leaves after being harvested.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛda bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmli edɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ baai bibii heei tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my corn stalks growing very tall and weak without producing big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight and stretch upward past their normal height. Because all their energy is spent growing tall to beat their neighbors for light, they have no strength left to grow thick cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛbaashɛ amɛhe fe bɔ ni sa. Ejaakɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ koni amɛye amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ kunim kɛha la. Amɛbɛ hewalɛ ko kwraa ni amɛkɛaawo jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my mango tree drop many small fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango shwieɔ aduawai bibii lɛ? Babaoo dani eda?

english: Fruit trees naturally drop excess young fruit when they realize they cannot support all of them. The tree reduces the fruit count to a limit it can handle so the remaining fruits get enough water and nutrients to grow large.
ga: Yibii tsei shwieɔ yibii bibii ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛyɔseɔ akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ amɛ fɛɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ baa aduawai lɛ ayibɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko bɔni afee ni aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara.

english: Why do I need to prune the shade trees in my cocoa farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Trimming shade trees keeps their foliage at the right thickness, allowing just enough sunlight to filter down to the cocoa trees below while preventing excessive humidity that causes black pod disease.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni sa. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni oooha ekpɛ yɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ naa.

english: Why have my pepper plants stayed very short and stopped growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ kuku waa ni ekpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants stop growing when the soil lacks food or when the roots cannot breathe due to hard soil. Adding compost or manure feeds the roots, allowing the plant to reach its normal size.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ shwie shi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ feɔ nɔ ni sa

english: Why do sweet potato vines stop spreading on top of the ground after some time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ kpaɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ be fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines naturally limit their leafy growth above ground once the plant transitions into its secondary phase, shifting food storage down into the sweet potatoes underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tsiɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ tsakeɔ kɛyaa efã ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa shi kɛyaa sweet potato shishigbɛ tsũ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants stop producing new flowers after a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi heei yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have a natural life limit. Once they produce a full load of fruit, the plant ages and naturally stops putting out new leaves and flowers as its life cycle comes to an end.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala be. Kɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkpaa baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei feemɔ kɛji amɛshihilɛ be lɛ ba naagbee.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and drop off when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get stressed under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown nearby to shield them from high heat and retain moisture in the soil until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ amɛhe kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Crop roots can only drink in nutrients when they are dissolved in water. Applying dry fertilizer without water can scorch and damage the plant's roots.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni nu bɛ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess water fills all the soil pockets, drowning the roots and encouraging fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baayi shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the deep center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the growing point of corn plants because the tissue there is soft, sweet, and rich in nutrients.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli fãji lɛ yɛ blɛoo, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or lack of water, as the plant saves its energy to stay alive rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Yam vines naturally search for height to expose as many leaves as possible to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ koni amɛjie tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I wait for the rainy season to properly settle before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli dani adu dumɔwui?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture once they start sprouting; if the rains pause right after planting, the germinating seeds will dry up and die.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be kɛji amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their leaves block each other from getting sunlight and their roots fight over the same soil food and water.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important to use a straight rope when planting my crops in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ kpãa ni ja atsu nii kɛ́ oodu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Using a straight lining rope ensures your plants are arranged in neat rows. This makes it much easier to walk through the farm, clear weeds, apply fertilizer evenly, and ensure no plant is crowded out by another.
ga: Kpãa ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa otoɔ otsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa, ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa. ni amɛkwɛ koni tsei komɛi akabɔle amɛhe

english: How do I measure the right distance between my trees when setting up a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu gbɛ ni sa ni kã mi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: You can use a standard measuring tape or a marked wooden stick—such as measuring six meters apart for large trees—to ensure each plant has enough room for its roots to spread and find food without competing with nearby plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tɛi ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe loo tso ni akadi lɛ atsu nii, ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ni okɛsusu mitai enumɔ kɛjɛ amɛhe kɛha tsei wuji. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛna niyenii ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ebɔi akaŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda ebɔleko mihe lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops or leaving tall shade trees provides shade that protects the young plants until their roots are deep enough to handle full heat.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ loo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛfee hulutsoo ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ dɔlɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I cut down or trim the top branches of big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo mafolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aniji lɛ?

english: Removing excessive upper leaf layers allows useful sunlight to filter down to your crops beneath. Too much heavy shade creates damp air that promotes crop diseases like black pod.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Shade babaoo haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni kɛ tsei ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa.

english: How should I arrange different types of crops on the same piece of land?
ga: Mato ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ahe gbɛjianɔ. Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ehi shikpɔŋ kuku kome nɔ?

english: Arrange taller crops so they do not completely block light from shorter crops. Placing food crops and tree crops in organized alternating rows helps both types get enough light, water, and nutrients.
ga: Too tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkatsi la ni jɛɔ tsei kukuji amli lɛ naa kwraa. Niyenii tsei kɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni akɛtoɔ gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ naa la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa.

english: How do I choose the best seeds from my harvest to save for the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛto kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Select seeds only from the strongest, healthiest plants that produced the largest yield and showed no signs of disease or insect damage throughout the growing season.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui pɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. ni hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe okadi ko bɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How many times can I plant the same crop on my farm land before the soil gets weak?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients over three or four seasons. Rotating your main crop with leguminous plants like beans helps restore natural nutrients to the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be yɛ bei etɛ loo ejwɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it bad for my farm if I clear off and remove the top layer of dark soil?
ga: Ani ebaaye miŋmɔ lɛ awui kɛji mijie shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ ni mijie?

english: Yes, because the top layer of dark soil contains the rich, decayed plant material that feeds your crops. Scraper or washing away this top layer leaves behind poor soil where crops struggle to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni fiteɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋwɛi ŋta nɛɛ shwieɔ loo efɔɔ he ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni ebaawa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: My elders say traditional farm rituals protect crops, but does scientific farming really give better yields?
ga: Mi onukpai lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, ŋmɔ mli kusumii ni afeɔ yɛ blema beaŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Shi ani jeŋ nilee mli okwaayeli woɔ yibii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: While traditional customs carry important cultural value, crop growth relies on practical factors like soil nutrients, clean water, correct planting distance, and protection from pests.
ga: Enɛ ji anɔkwale ni eji akɛ kusum nifeemɔi yɛ kusum mli sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Tso dalɛ damɔ nibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu ni mli tse, kɛ he ni sa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe

english: How can I accurately estimate the size of my farm field without expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can measure field boundaries using standard farm measuring ropes or by pacing out standard meter distances, which helps you buy the exact amount of seeds and fertilizer required without wasting money.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔ mli susumɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ asusu oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe. aloo kɛtsɔ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni oookwɛ nɔ yɛ mita ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ naa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oheɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ni okɛ shikatoohe lɛ ekuuu mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key plant nutrient, or that the roots are waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving field drainage helps plants regain green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei loo shishifãi lɛ amli nu eyi mli obɔ Kɛ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I stop insects and mold from ruining my harvested maize bags before I take them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ kotokui lɛ anaa dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: Maize spoils when stored with too much moisture inside the grain. Thoroughly sun-drying your maize until the kernels are hard before bagging, and storing bags off the floor in dry, well-ventilated spaces, protects your harvest from rot and pests.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni mli edɔ babaoo mli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okɛwo kotoku mli. Ni okɛ kotoku lɛ ato shikpɔŋ yɛ he ko ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants struggle and fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller yields than plants with proper spacing.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Should I plant my crops immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after the first rain is risky because it might be followed by a long dry spell that kills germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the soil stays consistently moist for early seed growth.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ aba daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, or will they choke my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaatsĩ midumɔ nii lɛ anaa?

english: Cowpeas and maize work well together when planted properly. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which actually helps the maize grow better while giving you a second crop from the same field.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ hu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slower and yield less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal essential water, soil fertilizers, and sunlight away from your crops. Removing weeds early in the season leaves all those vital resources for your main crop to build bigger leaves and produce more food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa nakai nibii ni he hiaa lɛ yeɔ amɛhe kɛhaa onibii titri lɛ koni amɛwo baai wuji ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hidden inside the central plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm, a destructive pest that feeds on young crop leaves. Spraying recommended biological or chemical controls directly into the plant funnel early in the morning or late evening stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ tsei bibii ahe baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller grain yields every year when I grow maize on the same plot repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dumɔwui faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and resets the field for healthy growth.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni eha jɛmɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ

english: Certified hybrid seeds are bred for maximum yield, uniform growth, and disease defense. Seeds saved from a harvested hybrid crop lose those superior traits in the next generation, leading to uneven and weaker yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. uniform growth kɛ helai atsimɔ Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ejaaa ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to protect themselves from excessive heat. By curling up, the plant reduces its leaf surface area exposed to the sun to slow down moisture loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the plants the food they need to grow strong, healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every year even though I use the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil. Changing the crop every season, like planting beans or peanuts after maize, helps the soil recover its natural fertility.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ daa be, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops close together so I can harvest more food from my small farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ madu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli? Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?
