english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow big and produce a much larger yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ oha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can catch full sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off wet ground, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: This black pod condition is caused by a mold that spreads when the farm is too wet and shaded. Pruning extra shade branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to dry out the trees and stop the mold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod shihilɛ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji ŋmɔji lɛ amli edɔ tsɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha tsei lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or when the soil dries out completely. Watering your tomatoes regularly around the root area helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tomato mli daa yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ tomato.

english: How do tiny caterpillars destroy my young maize leaves so fast?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide inside the growing center of the maize plant where the softest leaves are. Checking your plants early and applying treatment while the pests are small stops them from multiplying.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli he ni baai lɛ ji bibii fe fɛɛ lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra ni atsa amɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ darako lɛ. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafɔ bii.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much rainwater sits around them without draining. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra water to run off, keeping the roots safe and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. ni nu shwieee shi Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi babaoo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: No, a heavy downpour will wash your expensive fertilizer off the land into nearby streams before the plant roots can swallow it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ ami lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, meaning they steal water, light, and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds while your crops are still small keeps them from suffocating your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Because each plant gets only a small portion of energy, they cannot grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu mli ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe Enɛ ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ adu cob agbo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly full of holes and covered in small sawdust-like dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu trukaa ni muji bibii ehà nɔ lɛ? Ani etamɔ tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ sawdust lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the center shoot of the maize plant. It eats the tender leaves and leaves behind its waste, which looks like sawdust, and can ruin the crop if left untreated.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ baai bibii ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei. ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the young pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up before they grow full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by small sap-sucking insects called capsids (or akate). When they bite into young cocoa pods and shoots, they inject a toxic liquid that kills the plant tissue, turning the pods black and dry.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids lɛ. (loo Akate) beni amɛyeɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Amɛwoɔ nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ tsei amli fãji. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards, getting thick, and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe, amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Your tomatoes have Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Once infected, the plant stops growing properly and struggles to bear fruit.
ga: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Hela, ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ emɔ omatoi lɛ amli. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ lɛ pɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bugs living on their roots that trap free nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, this nitrogen feeds the next crop like natural fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ hiɛɔ kooloi bibii. ni hiɔ shi yɛ eshishifãi anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ haa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I wait for rain before putting fertilizer on my farm instead of putting it on dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni oookɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before a plant's roots can drink it in. If you put fertilizer on dry soil during a hot day, it will evaporate into the air or scorch the roots of your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop leaves to turn yellow and stop growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves that drink the water and eat the soil food meant for your crops. When weeds surround your plants, your crops starve, lose their green color, and become weak.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii. Beni jwɛi ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii. Ehiɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft, black, and smelly underground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is cassava root rot, caused by excess water staying in heavy soil for too long. Cassava roots need air to breathe, and when the soil stays waterlogged, fungi attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei shishifã ni egbo. Nu ni fa fe nine ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. ni beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu yɔɔ lolo lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots and becoming light in weight when stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ akɛto mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are alive and use the food stored inside their tubers to sprout when they feel warmth and light. As the green sprout grows, it drinks up the water and starch inside the yam, making the tuber soft, light, and spongy.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛhe edɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ebaanu nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ sponji.

english: Why should I trim and cut away some branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ni mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary branches so the tree doesn't waste energy on them. It allows sunlight and air to reach the middle of the tree, which keeps the farm dry enough to prevent fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce more flowers.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. koni tsei akafite hewalɛ Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo he hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear all the weeds off my cocoa farm early in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, light, and nutrients from the soil that your cocoa trees need to grow. Clearing them early ensures that your crop gets all the food and water available when the growing season begins.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa ni o-cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná amɛ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: What is the difference between putting regular fertilizer in the soil and spraying liquid fertilizer on my cocoa leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ anɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Soil fertilizer feeds the roots slowly over time to keep the main tree strong, while liquid fertilizer sprayed directly on leaves is absorbed very fast to give the tree an immediate boost, especially when it needs extra strength to produce flowers.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii fiofio. Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli oya koni eha tso lɛ aya hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ hewalɛ kroko he miihia yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do farmers start preparing their land and applying fertilizers around February?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi jeɔ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shishi yɛ February aaafee lɛ?

english: February is right before the early rains start in Ghana. Giving the soil and trees nutrients just before the rain comes helps the roots soak up the fertilizer quickly as soon as the ground gets wet.
ga: February ji dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi mra yɛ Ghana. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I apply too much fertilizer at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn the roots and leaves of the cocoa tree, cause young flowers to drop off, and waste your money. Crops need the right balance of nutrients, not just a high quantity.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi bibii shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ shika. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Jeee bɔ ni gbee lɛ naa wa ha lɛ pɛ.

english: How do chemical sprays protect my cocoa trees from damage?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ buɔ cacao tsei ahe koni amɛkafite lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Chemical sprays act as a shield by killing insects like capsids and mirids that suck juices from young pods and leaves, preventing insects from destroying your yield.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids kɛ mirids ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai bibii amli lɛ agbemɔ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Can I spray chemical pesticides on my cocoa farm at the same time the trees are flowering?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ?

english: You must be very careful when spraying flowering cocoa trees. Strong chemical sprays can burn delicate flowers or drive away beneficial insects that help the flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ oofɔ cacao tsei ni fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ashwie kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do the small flowers on my cocoa tree actually turn into big pods?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmeii wuji?

english: Tiny insects called midges carry pollen from one flower to another in a process called pollination. Once a flower is pollinated and receives enough plant nutrients, it begins to swell and grow into a cocoa pod.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollination nɔ. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ wo pollination mli ni amɛná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ tsei amli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaatsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do many flowers on my cocoa tree dry up and drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off if the tree is stressed by drought, lacks nutrients, or is attacked by pests. Feeding the tree well and keeping it free from insects helps it hold onto its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua tso lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ajie lɛ kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni efeɔ ŋmeii.

english: If I do not have enough strength or money to clear my whole farm at once, which parts should I focus on first?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ hewalɛ loo shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛjie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ shikome hu? Mɛɛ fã esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Focus first on clearing the weeds directly around the bases of your cocoa trees and removing dead branches. This directly protects the main trunk and leaves, letting you handle the outer areas as you gain more time or help.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ, ni ojie tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ buɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai titrii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsuɔ kponɔgbɛ hei ahe nii beni oyɔɔ be babaoo loo yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is weak and needs fertilizer or a soil vitalizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: When soil loses its nutrients, crops grow slowly, leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and yields drop significantly. Adding compost or soil vitalizers restores these missing nutrients so plants can feed properly again.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni elaaje nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba. koni tsei ana niyenii ekoŋŋ

english: Can I use decayed farm waste and animal dung to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, decomposing crop leftovers and animal manure turns into organic fertilizer or soil vitalizers, which enrich the soil with natural nutrients and help it hold water better for your plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni fiteɔ kɛ kooloi ashishifãi tsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu hiɔ otsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ

english: If I clear new land to expand my maize farm, how long should I wait before sowing my seeds?
ga: Kɛji mijie shikpɔŋ hee koni mikɛgbala mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni madu dumɔwui?

english: After clearing new land, you should let the cleared vegetation dry and decompose or burn safely, then give the soil about two weeks to settle after tilling before planting your seeds to prevent seed rot.
ga: Beni ojie he hee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ oha tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbi ni amɛfite loo oshã amɛ shweshweeshwe. No sɛɛ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ ni ekɛba shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsu lɛ sɛɛ. Dani abaadu dumɔwui koni dumɔwui lɛ akafite

english: What happens to my maize crops if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together causes the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive drought. As long as the stem remains healthy, the plant will sprout new leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops stay green during short dry spells while mine wilt quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkutsoŋbii lɛ aŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Taakɛ minɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the ground cool and traps soil moisture, stopping water from evaporating too quickly during dry weather.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha onibii ahe (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and hot winds; they need fast-growing shade crops like plantains to protect them while their roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my young maize leaves mostly at night or early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ loo leebi lɛ?

english: Many pests avoid the hot afternoon sun to stay cool and hidden during the day, coming out in the cooler night and early morning hours to feed on fresh leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛtee amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Je kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli kɛ leebi maŋkpa koni oye baai heei lɛ.

english: If I plant tomatoes on the same plot of land every year, why do they keep getting sick?
ga: Kɛji akɛ aduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ tomato hela mɔɔ lɛ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every season allows soil-borne diseases and pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the soil; rotating with crops like maize or beans starves those pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ nibii ni adu lɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaaha nakai ŋmeii lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to harvest from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and dry, and the inside of the pods turns dark brown when you pull up a sample plant and shell a few pods.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni pod lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ kɛji ogbala nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi ni ojie pod lɛ hewolo lɛ eko.

english: Why do I need to clear all the weeds and bush before I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. It ensures your young maize seeds get all the food they need to sprout strong without being choked by wild bush.
ga: Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni yɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni o-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni koo mli jwɛi tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Should I burn the bushes I cleared from my plot, or is there a better way to clean the land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo gbɛ ni hi fe enɛ yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Instead of burning, letting cleared plants decompose on the soil forms a protective mulch. This keeps the ground cool, saves moisture during hot days, and naturally fertilizes your crops.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ, ha tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why must I break up and loosen the hard soil on my land before sowing seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie sũ ni wa lɛ? Yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu dumɔwui?

english: Loosening hard soil makes it easier for tender roots to push deep into the earth to find water and food. It also helps rainwater soak into the ground instead of washing your seeds away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii. Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How can I stop bush animals like grasscutters from eating my young cassava stalks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Fencing your land with fine wire mesh or planting bitter barrier plants like neem or chili peppers around your plot boundary deters wild animals like grasscutters from entering and chewing your cassava.
ga: Kɛ waya kpakpa atswa oshikpɔŋ lɛ he gbogbo loo dumɔ tsei ni mli edɔ tamɔ neem loo chili yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he fɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ, tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi akabote mli ni amɛbaye o-cassava lɛ.

english: If I leave tall wild grass growing near my crop field, will it attract pests?
ga: Kɛ mishi koo mli jwɛi kakadaji komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ ni miduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ masɛi lɛ Ani ebaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, overgrown wild grass acts as a breeding home for insects, rodents, and snakes. Keeping the surroundings of your plot clear prevents these pests from invading your farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, kɛ onufui fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ oha he ni ebɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight one another for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni haa tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and get scorched by harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains alongside them provides shade and moisture to protect them while they are small.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baabu tso lɛ he be mli ni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests that target maize to build up, reducing your harvest over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji ŋmãa lɛ yiŋtoo lɛ anaa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without making peppers when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni efeee pepper kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants don't get enough water during hot spells, they drop their flowers to save energy and protect themselves from dying of heat stress.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil without draining away properly. The trapped standing water starves roots of air and allows rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi ni emɔ shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why am I getting a small harvest even when I apply fertilizer and water my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibii babaoo nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ nu woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Water and fertilizer help crops grow, but plants also need high-yielding seed varieties (good genetics) to break past low yield limits and produce a much bigger harvest.
ga: Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa. Shi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo hu he miihia tsei. (genetics kpakpa) koni eye yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ nɔ kunim ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo aba

english: My crop harvest seems stuck at the same low weight every season; what is keeping my crops from growing more?
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehi shi yɛ shwiili ni baa shi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli daa be. Mɛni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akakwɛ̃ babaoo?

english: Crops hit a yield ceiling when they lack the right combination of upgraded seed varieties, adequate soil nutrients, and consistent water necessary to reach their full growth capacity.
ga: Tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛ yibiiwoo he husu lɛ he beni amɛbɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ. niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa, ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does it mean when agricultural experts say a seed variety has high yield potential?
ga: Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nilelɔi kɛɛ akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: It means the plant has the built-in genetic strength to produce a heavy harvest, but it requires proper feeding through fertilizer and consistent water to achieve that maximum weight.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei yɛ fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ ni ama amɛmli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi ebiɔ niyenii ni sa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa nɔ koni enyɛ eshɛ nakai muji ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he.

english: Will combining both fertilizer and artificial watering really increase my crop yield significantly?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni akɛfee lɛ fɛɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ aya hiɛ waa?

english: Yes, pairing proper fertilizer application with consistent irrigation works together to unlock the plant's natural growth ability, dramatically increasing your total tons harvested per acre.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ fata he lɛ tsuɔ nii ekome kɛgbeleɔ tso ko adebɔɔ mli dalɛ nyɛmɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha tɔni ni akpaa yɛ acre kome mli lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Does applying fertilizer alone guarantee that my crops will yield their maximum possible weight?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ pɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii fe fɛɛ?

english: No, fertilizer alone is only part of the solution. Without sufficient water to dissolve and carry those nutrients into the roots, the crop cannot reach its full potential.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ ji tsabaa lɛ fã ko kɛkɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsɔ mli ni ekɛya shishifãi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the most effective way to make sure the money I spend on fertilizer is not wasted?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ koni shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akafite?

english: Ensure your crops receive adequate and timely water through irrigation or rain, as water allows plant roots to efficiently absorb and use the nutrients in the fertilizer.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni otsei lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ be ni sa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops if I rely only on unpredictable rainfall during the dry season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to work effectively; using it without guaranteed water can stress plants or leave expensive nutrients trapped unused in dry soil.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli ni nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ loo eha niyenii ni jara wa ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers get much higher yields than me even when we use similar amounts of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa yibii babaoo fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: The difference often comes down to the seed quality and watering methods. High-performing seeds combined with reliable irrigation convert plant foods into yield much more efficiently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi lɛ damɔ bɔ ni dumɔwu lɛ hi ha kɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afɔseɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ fataa he lɛ tsakeɔ tsei aniyenii kɛfeɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is rainfall alone sometimes not enough to get the best harvest from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Irregular rainfall leaves plants stressed at key growth stages, whereas controlled irrigation keeps moisture levels steady so crops can continuously take up soil nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ shi ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi daa. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa.

english: How can agricultural research findings help me produce more food on my small piece of land?
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ baaye abua mi ni maná niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: Research identifies the exact combination of improved seeds, ideal fertilizer rates, and watering schedules needed to maximize crop output without needing more land.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ tsɔɔ bɔ ni akɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ekome pɛpɛɛpɛ Ideal Fertilizer Rate lɛ mli, ni etsɔɔ be ni he hiaa ni akɛwoɔ nu mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba yibii babaoo ni ekɛ he kroko fataaa he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth, or that excessive rain is suffocating the roots. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers if tiny pollinating insects called midges are missing, or if the tree is stressed by high heat and dry conditions. Maintaining shade trees on your farm keeps the soil cool and provides a moist habitat for these midges to pollinate your trees.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji kooloi bibii wo amɛmli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ laaje. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be mli Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa kooloi nɛɛ anáa he ko ni mli ejɔ koni amɛwo otsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up much faster when my farm is full of weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa be mli ni jwɛi eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors; their roots steal moisture and fertilizer from the soil before your crops can absorb them. Clearing weeds early leaves more water and nutrients available for your crops to survive dry periods.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii aná nu kɛ niyenii babaoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli.

english: Tuber rot is caused by excess water sitting around the roots, especially in heavy clay soil during the rainy season, which encourages fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tuber rot baa. Titri lɛ, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa waa nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What makes the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects that suck sap from the leaves. Using physical insect barriers, companion planting, or spraying natural neem oil can control whiteflies and protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ Kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni tsiɔ nii anaa lɛ nɔ kɛduɔ nii Loo kɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ ŋmeii yɛji ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or nutrient deficiencies. Mulching the soil around the plants with dry grass helps hold moisture and lowers root temperature, encouraging the flowers to stay and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi shwieɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ aba shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant beans like cowpea together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the maize. In return, the tall maize supports the bean vines, allowing you to harvest two crops from the same field while improving soil fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiɔ ŋmãa wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using bamboo or wood?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei loo tsei adu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the damp soil with stakes gives the leaves maximum sunlight and protects them from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers from around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Midumɔwu titri lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow around one stem, they compete with the main tree for light, water, and nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches. Leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main stem produces large, high-quality bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Eshwɛɔ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right after a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Heavy rains flood the soil and cause water runoff that washes fertilizer away before plants can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not waterlogged so the roots can draw in the nutrients effectively.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dropping off when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because their tender leaves burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving shade trees provides the shelter and cooler soil environment young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo hulutsoo tsei ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ koni amɛha wɔɔhe kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are small worms eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that burrows into the growing center of maize plants. Spraying targeted pest control treatments early in the morning or late evening directly into the center leaf whorl helps protect the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the main rains start and rain falls consistently 2 to 3 times within a week to thoroughly wet the soil. Planting in soil that is only slightly damp after a single short rain can cause seeds to sprout and quickly dry up.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ titri ni nɛɔ kɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaje shishi shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ otsi kome mli koni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and curl up during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings recommended by agricultural officers prevents this virus from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall green leaves after I apply fertilizer, but still fail to yield big fruits or cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kakadaji yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ? Shi ani enyɛɛɛ ewo aduawai wuji loo ŋmeii lolo?

english: Different plant foods serve different roles; high-nitrogen fertilizer builds leaves and stems, while phosphorus and potassium are required for strong roots, flowers, and fruits. Using a balanced fertilizer at the flowering stage ensures energy goes into crop yields rather than just leafy growth.
ga: Tso niyenii srɔtoi tsuɔ gbɛfaŋnɔi srɔtoi ahe nii. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ be mli ni fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he hiaa koni shishifãi, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ mli. Jeee baa dalɛ pɛ he ewieɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when the soil gets too dry or when daytime temperatures are extremely hot. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering and placing dry grass mulch around the base helps the plants hold onto their flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha ni okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi awo shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds around my crops in their very first month of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital sunlight, water, and soil food away from them. Clearing weeds during early growth ensures your crops receive all available nutrition to grow strong stems and roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ mra be mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their underground roots compete fiercely for space and nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small tubers. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to form large, heavy roots.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ bulb bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why does my plantain plant yield small bunches when many young shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots suck away food and water meant for the main mother plant. Removing excess shoots so that only two or three healthy stems remain per stand ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛhaa fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shi yɛ tso kome mli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into powder and get filled with tiny holes during storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ feɔ powder ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ

english: Powder and holes in stored maize are caused by grain weevils that attack grains stored with too much moisture. Thoroughly drying your maize until the kernels are hard and using protective storage bags prevents these insects from ruining your grain.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ powda kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ baa ji ŋmãa ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni okɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ he ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii koni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients out of reach of the plant's roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Cassava root rot usually occurs when soil stays waterlogged for too long or when soil fungi attack the roots during periods of heavy rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that causes leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, usually triggered by inconsistent watering while the tomatoes are developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ni ejaaa be mli ni tomato lɛ miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How long will my cassava crop take before the roots are ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ afee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Traditional cassava varieties take about 9 to 12 months to mature fully, while improved varieties can be ready for harvest within 6 to 8 months.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmei lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ ŋmei he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli.

english: How do I know for sure that my field maize is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Maize is ready when the outer leaves turn dry and brown, the silks at the top turn dark, and the corn kernels become hard.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ. ni ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Plantains have shallow roots and broad leaves that lose moisture quickly, so the plant sheds older leaves to survive periods without rain.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai momo lɛ koni amɛhi shi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight, so fast-growing plantain trees are planted to provide shade and hold soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, aduɔ dumɔwui ni daa oya koni amɛha hulutsoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea crops stop producing new pods after the first picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii heei feemɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas complete their natural lifecycle after their main flush of pods matures, but dry spells or insect damage on late flowers can also stop new pod growth.
ga: Cowpeas gbeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wala shihilɛ naa beni pod titri lɛ edara sɛɛ. Shi hulutsoo be loo kooloi ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ akpa pod heei adalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to arrange buyers before harvesting my fresh vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masaa mɔ ni baahe nii lɛ dani makpa mi-aduawai heei lɛ?

english: Perishable crops like tomatoes and peppers spoil quickly after harvest, so securing market buyers early prevents crop loss and helps you get a better price before the local market gets oversupplied.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ oya tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ ni anáa yɛ jara lɛ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite ni eye ebua bo ni oná jara kpakpa dani maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ afee nɔ ni fe nine.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there are no plantain trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong sunlight and excessive heat. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that cools the ground and preserves soil moisture, allowing the cocoa to survive its early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he waa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i akafee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa kookoo hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize crop turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the lower parts of a maize plant usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to produce healthy green leaves that catch sunlight to form full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ aba koni amɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut to ensure my new planting grows strong tubers?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo koni maná ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha midumɔ hee lɛ?

english: You should select mature, healthy cassava stems from the middle portion of the stalk, cutting them into pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long with 4 to 6 clear buds, as these sprout much better than soft green tops or old woody bases.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmei tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ. Afolɔ mli bibii aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni eyɛ ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni mli tse, ejaakɛ edaa jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsei shishitoo momoi.

english: Why do extension workers recommend planting cover crops like beans or mucuna between my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii? yɛ mi tsei titrii lɛ ateŋ

english: Cover crops carpet the ground to block weeds, keep moisture in the soil during dry spells, and naturally add nitrogen food back into the earth to feed your main crop.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ feɔ kapɛti ni buɔ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, okɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha onibii titrii lɛ niyenii.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves with little dirt-like grains inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli ewo muji ni eyɛ dumɔwui ni tamɔ muji yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of young maize during the day and feed on the leaves, which weakens the crop if left untreated.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant my seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops end up competing with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa bibioo ko.

english: Why should I leave dry grass or plant leaves on top of my soil around my crops instead of sweeping it away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie amɛ kɛya?

english: Leaving dry organic matter on the soil creates mulch, which shields the earth from intense sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and gradually rots into natural fertilizer for the soil.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya ni efite fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to produce big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up in the air to capture sunlight efficient for food production. Staking keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and encouraging large tuber growth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji lɛ daraa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to stress caused by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady while the plant blossoms helps it retain flowers and grow fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be be mli ni tso lɛ miifɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil is properly wet enough to start planting seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil is ready for planting when you can squeeze a handful into a firm ball that crumbles easily when gently pressed. If the soil drips water or sticks like wet clay, it is too wet and may rot the seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni obaanyɛ okɛ onine awo mli ni ofee bɔɔlu ni mli wa, ni kɛji akɛ onyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, efoɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwie loo ekpɛtɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: What is the difference between the seeds I save from my own harvest and the seeds I buy from a seed company?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhe ko dɛŋ lɛ teŋ?

english: Seeds from certified seed companies are specially bred and tested to resist diseases and produce higher yields. Seeds saved from your own harvest lose these good qualities over time, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ dumɔwui nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpamɔ mli lɛ baafite sui kpakpai nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo.

english: Why should I buy fresh seeds every season instead of planting what I harvested last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei daa afi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu nɔ ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Improved crop seeds lose their vigor and yield potential after one planting cycle. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures your crops grow uniformly and produce the highest possible yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ dumɔwui shikome sɛɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ.

english: What happens to my farm if I plant uncertified seeds bought from the local open market?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe ni agbele naa lɛ mli?

english: Uncertified seeds may carry hidden diseases, sprout unevenly, or fail to germinate entirely, which wastes your land, time, and fertilizer investments.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni anaaa he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kwɛɛɛ Enɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ, be kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do seeds bought from certified seed dealers sprout faster and more evenly in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds go through quality controls to ensure high germination rates and uniform growth, meaning almost every seed you plant will sprout healthy at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa daa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni obaadu lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kome mli.

english: What are foundation seeds, and why do agricultural officers talk about them so much?
ga: Mɛni ji Shishitoo Dumɔwu? Ni mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai wieɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ ahe babaoo lɛ?

english: Foundation seeds are pure, high-grade seeds grown by specialized research centers. Seed companies buy these foundation seeds to plant and multiply them into the certified seeds that you buy for your farm.
ga: Shishijee dumɔwui ji dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni niiamlitaomɔ hei pɔtɛɛi duɔ. Dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei heɔ nɛkɛ shishijee dumɔwui nɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfɔ amɛ ni amɛfee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni oheɔ kɛhaa oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Can I buy foundation seeds directly and plant them on my farm to sell crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe shishitoo dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Foundation seeds are mainly meant for certified seed producers to multiply under strict supervision. As a general farmer, buying certified seeds from seed companies gives you the best balance of cost, ease, and high yield.
ga: Dumɔwui shishijee yɛ kɛha dumɔwui afeelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi. Ákɛ okwaafonyo wulu lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni oheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui nitsumɔhe ko dɛŋ lɛ haa onáa shika, mlɛofeemɔ, kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo teŋ.

english: Can I grow foundation seeds on my land and sell them to my neighbors as planting seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu shishitoo dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ maha akutsoŋbii koni amɛdu dumɔwui?

english: Growing true foundation seeds requires special training, strict isolation distances, and official government inspection to prevent contamination. Without certification, you cannot legally or reliably sell them as quality seeds.
ga: Anɔkwa shishitoo dumɔwui ni aaakwɛ̃ lɛ biɔ tsɔsemɔ krɛdɛɛ. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni mli wa kɛ nɔyeli lɛ mli kwɛmɔi ni akɛtsiɔ mujiwoo naa. Kɛji akɛ odaseyeli ko bɛ Onyɛŋ ohɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ mla naa loo yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: How do government seed programs actually help a small-scale farmer like me?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: The government funds research centers to produce plenty of high-quality foundation seeds. This helps seed companies produce large quantities of reliable seeds so you can easily buy them at affordable prices.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ haa niiamlitaomɔ hei shika koni amɛfee shishitoo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ ohe amɛ yɛ jara ni waaa nɔ oya.

english: Why are there so many improved seed varieties available in Ghana this year compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ babaoo yɛ Ghana afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Institutions and seed producers have increased the production of foundation seeds to align with national farming initiatives, ensuring farmers across the country have reliable access to high-yielding seeds.
ga: Nitsumɔhei kɛ dumɔwui afeelɔi eha shishijee dumɔwui afeemɔ etee hiɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi lɛ anaa. Enɛ ji koni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ aná dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: How does using certified seeds support the food supply of the whole country?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua maŋ lɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ?

english: When many farmers use certified high-yield seeds, national crop yields increase significantly, ensuring there is enough food in the markets and helping Ghana become self-sufficient.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli tsuɔ nii lɛ. Maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ waa. Enɛ haa anáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jara lɛ nɔ. ni eye ebua Ghana ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ ehe nɔ.

english: Why are the branches and stems of my cocoa trees swelling and growing out of shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ efuu ni amɛbɛ su lɛ?

english: Swelling on cocoa branches is a key sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. It chokes the tree's internal water pipes, stopping pod production and eventually killing the tree.
ga: Kookoo niji ni efuu lɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo hela ni jɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ mli fũuɔ lɛ mli baa. ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs. Ehaa nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa pod feemɔ kpaa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp, and cold conditions. Clearing excess shade, removing infested pods, and applying recommended fungicides help protect your farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ. Jiemɔ shade ni fa fe nine lɛ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do very small young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn dark before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ duŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This issue, known as cherelle wilt, happens when a tree produces more pods than it can feed, or when mirid bugs suck sap from young pods. Applying fertilizer and spraying for pests helps save more of your yield.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt lɛ baa kɛ́ tso ko wo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo po aba shi.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cocoa pods and sticky sap dripping from them?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii? Yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji kɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi mli lɛ Mine shwie shi.

english: This damage is caused by mirid bugs, locally known as 'akate'. They pierce the pod skin to feed on sap, which lets in rot and reduces the size and quality of your beans.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji mirid ŋmeii, ni ale amɛ yɛ jɛmɛ akɛ ‘akate’, ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni ehaa kɔfe yibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhe kpakpa baa shi.

english: Why are green caterpillars eating the leaves and inside of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛmli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a destructive insect pest that feeds heavily on maize leaves and growing stems. Spotting them early and using safe insecticides or recommended natural remedies keeps your field safe.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ babaoo. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that water is sitting around their roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizers like urea or organic compost restores their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ loo nu yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo organic compost ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I pour my chemical fertilizer right at the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo kookoo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, putting chemical fertilizer directly against the trunk will burn the bark and roots. You should spread or place it in a wide ring about two feet away from the trunk where the feeding roots absorb nutrients safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ ogbɛ amɛ oshwã loo okɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee ninetalɔi 2 he ni shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same farm as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and get scorched by direct heat from the sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ haa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce fewer pods even when I clear the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi efo mli moŋ?

english: Over time, thick overgrown upper canopy branches block sunlight, preventing flowers from forming. Pruning wild branches lets in sunlight and air, stimulating the tree to flower and produce more pods.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ ŋwɛi tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ babaoo lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkafee Efoɔ koo mli niji koni amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ Ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize right after the very first rainy day of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period, which dries out the soil and kills freshly germinated seeds. It is safer to wait until the rainy season fully establishes before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekpata dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baagbe naa dani odu.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither so fast after I bring them home from the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ amɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛbaa shia lɛ?

english: Seedlings wither quickly when they suffer from transplant shock, loss of root moisture, or exposure to harsh direct sunlight during transport. Keeping them in a cool, shaded place and keeping the root soil damp helps them stay fresh until you plant them.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ oya kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe gbeyeishemɔ mli. shishifãi lɛ amli nu ni baa shi loo hulu la ni naa wa ni baa mɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi obaadu amɛ.

english: How can I store leftover plant seedlings for a few days so they do not rot or die before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ ato gbii fioo komɛi koni amɛkagboi loo amɛkagboi dani adu?

english: Store unused seedlings under shade on elevated ground or wooden pallets so air circulates underneath. Water them lightly in the early morning so the soil stays moist, but do not flood them, as standing water will cause root rot.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ato hulutsoo shishi yɛ saatso ni awo nɔ loo yɛ tso nɔ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ abɔle shishi lɛ, shwiemɔ nu fioo leebi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi kaahã nu afua miiho. Ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: What is the best way to keep nursery shoots green and healthy if I cannot plant them right away?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa? Kɛji minyɛɛɛ madu amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Place the shoots in a covered, humid area protected from strong wind and hot sun. Keep the soil around their roots damp like a wrung-out sponge, which allows them to rest without exhausting their stored food and water.
ga: Okɛ tso lɛ awo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Buu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ sponji ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfiteee niyenii kɛ nu ni ato lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a batch of nursery seedlings is healthy enough to buy for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui abɔ ko yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Healthy seedlings have firm, bright green leaves, sturdy central stems, and soil-packed roots that hold together. Avoid buying plants that are already drooping, turning yellow, or showing dark, slimy patches at the root base.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. tso ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni sũ ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ eyi mli obɔ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni egbee shi lɛ ahemɔ he. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishifã lɛ shishi

english: Why do some seedlings rot while others stay fresh even when kept in the same storage spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi ehee eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ amɛ toɔ he kome moŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings rot if their stems were bruised during handling or if they were overcrowded and overwatered without proper air movement. Healthy, uninjured plant shoots with good spacing resist rot much better.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ amɛhe wa tsɔ ni nu babaoo yɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsoi ahe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni pilaaa ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ fitemɔ.

english: How should I cover and move my plant shoots to the farm so they do not wither on the journey?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-bamboo tsei lɛ ahe ni mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbo yɛ gbɛfaa lɛ mli?

english: Transport seedlings during the cool early morning or evening, cover them loosely with a palm leaf or cloth shade to block wind and sun, and secure them so they do not bounce around and break their roots.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ aya leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso, ni okɛ ŋmei tsei ahe baai loo hulutsoo aha amɛhe jogbaŋŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la he. ni omɔ mli shiŋŋ koni ekafo kɛbɔle ehe ni efo shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my newly transplanted seedlings dry up even after I water them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ egbi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: If the roots were broken or disturbed too much during planting, the seedling cannot draw up water even if the soil is wet. Protecting root soil during planting and providing temporary shade prevents this drying.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fã loo agbala amɛ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Kɛ́ abu shishifã shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ, ni aha lɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbi.

english: What causes plant cuttings or shoots to rot in the ground right after I put them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni afolɔ loo amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shoots rot in the soil when the ground is too wet and heavy, or if the soil contains fungal diseases. Planting in raised beds with good drainage prevents water from choking the roots and causing rot.
ga: Tsoi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ tsiimɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ adu yɛ saatso ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekafee shishifãi lɛ ekome ni eha amɛgboi.

english: How long can a nursery seedling stay in its small container before it starts to spoil or weaken?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi tsɛnsii bibii amli dani amɛje shishi amɛgboi loo amɛfee blɛoo?

english: Most seedlings start to weaken after a few weeks in small containers because the roots get tangled and bound up. Once root-bound, the plant cannot absorb enough nutrients and begins to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ tsɛnsii bibii amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛbɔle amɛhe. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛ amɛhe lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ebɔi ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ

english: Does giving extra water to withered seedlings make them turn green and strong again?
ga: Ani nu kroko ni akɛaaha dumɔwui ni egboi lɛ baaha amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Watering helps if the plant is only slightly thirsty, but if the roots have already dried out completely or rotted, adding more water will not save the plant and may cause the dead stem to rot faster.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛji kumai miiye tso lɛ fioo kɛkɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbi kwraa loo amɛgboi momo lɛ, Nu ni akɛbaafata he lɛ hereee tso lɛ yiwala, ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi ni egboi lɛ agboi oya.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa trees on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii woɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, offering shade and keeping the soil moist for young cocoa plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field as my cocoa, or will it hurt the cocoa plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-kookoo lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ? Aloo ebaaye kookoo tso lɛ awui?

english: Cassava roots grow large and spread quickly, competing with young cocoa trees for soil nutrients and root space. If planted too close, cassava can stunt cocoa growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya. Amɛkɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu Cassava yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha cocoa lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: When is the right time to cut down plantain shade trees in my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ afo shade dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should reduce or cut plantain shade after three to five years, when the cocoa trees have grown tall enough to form their own canopy and shade the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ shade plantains lɛ aba shi loo ofolɔ amɛhe yɛ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni efee ŋwɛitsu ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hɔnɔ lɛ,.

english: Why do suckers keep growing around the base of my plantain stems after I harvest the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ beni mikpa aduawai lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Plantain stems naturally produce baby shoots called suckers from underground bulbs to reproduce, which you can remove to plant in new areas or leave one to grow the next batch of fruit.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli koni amɛfɔ. Obaanyɛ ojie kɛjɛ jɛmɛ koni oyadu yɛ he ko hee loo oshi lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does cocoa farming seem harder today than it was 20 years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, kookoo dumɔ wa fe afii 20 ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Over the last 20 years, rainfall patterns have changed, heat has increased, and older farm soils have lost nutrients, making trees more stressed and sensitive to pests and drought than before.
ga: Yɛ afii 20 ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ etsake. dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ Ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji momoi amli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe waa ni amɛnuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ he waa fe tsutsu ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel and turn dark before they grow big?
