ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ duŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This behavior is known as cherelle wilt. It happens when the tree experiences stress from lack of water, shade, or nutrients, causing it to drop surplus pods to protect the main tree.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Ebaa kɛji tso ko na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmeii ni eshwɛɔ ni baabu tso titri lɛ he.

english: Why do yellow leaves appear on my cocoa trees during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ŋmɔŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop yellow leaves in hot weather to reduce water loss through evaporation, helping the tree conserve internal moisture until rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do cassava plants survive dry spells better than most other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Cassava has deep, strong root systems that store nutrients and moisture, allowing the plant to drop its leaves to save water and remain alive during long dry spells.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni toɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu mli nu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can keeping goats help improve the growth of my food crops and cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tooi akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Goat droppings can be collected and added to soil as organic manure, which feeds essential nutrients like nitrogen back into the ground for healthier crops.
ga: Abaanyɛ abua too ŋmei naa ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If my soil is tired from growing heavy crops like plantain and cassava, will young cocoa still grow well there?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava ni miduɔ lɛ hu? Ani kookoo bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ lolo?

english: Heavy crops draw nutrients out of the soil, so tired ground must be restored with compost, animal manure, or natural soil improvers before planting sensitive cocoa seedlings.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ wuji gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tsakemɔi awo hei ni etɔ lɛ amli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Dani abaadu kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ

english: Why do my soybean roots have tiny round bumps on them, and are they a disease harming my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ni ani amɛji helai ni yeɔ midumɔ nii lɛ awui?

english: Those bumps are called root nodules and they are very healthy. They contain helpful bacteria that pull nitrogen out of the air and feed it directly to the plant, helping soybeans grow rich in protein without needing excessive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa. Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛhaa tsei tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ mli. Ehaa soybean lɛ daa ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo awo mli.

english: Why does my maize turn light yellow and stay stunted if I do not add fertilizer early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that requires a lot of nitrogen to build strong stalks and leaves. If it lacks nutrients during its early growth stage, the leaves lose their green color starting from the tips and the whole plant stops growing properly.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ nitrogen babaoo koni ekɛma ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ faaa yɛ shishijee bei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ baafite amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baakpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting soybeans on my land this year will make my maize grow better next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu soybean yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi nɛɛ, ebaaha mi-ŋmã lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Soybeans fix nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. When you harvest the soybeans and leave the roots to decay, that natural fertility stays in the soil, giving the following season's maize crop free nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Soybean lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okpa soybeans ni oha shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Nakai adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into narrow tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural defense against extreme heat and drought. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and wind, trapping moisture inside so it does not dry out and die.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ.

english: Why does the hybrid maize seed I buy in sealed bags yield so much more than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni miheɔ yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are produced by crossing two specific parent plants to combine their strongest traits. The grain you harvest from those crops loses that special vigor, so replanting saved seed results in smaller cobs and uneven growth.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii sɔrɔtoi lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni akɛ sui ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ afee ekome lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni okpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my soybean pods split open and drop all their seeds on the dirt if I delay harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean ŋmɔji lɛ tswaa ni amɛshiɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa sɛɛ?

english: Soybean pods naturally burst open—a process called shattering—once they become completely dry in the sun. This is the plant's wild way of spreading seeds, so you must harvest the crop as soon as the leaves drop and the pods turn golden-brown.
ga: Soybean ŋmeii lɛ baatswa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ shwiemɔ. Beni amɛgbi kwraa yɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ eshwaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ shika tsuru.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing grains and patches of empty spaces on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii ni elaaje ni amɛyɛ he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Empty spots on a maize cob happen when pollination fails. If the weather is too dry or hot when the silks emerge, the pollen grains dry up before they can fertilize every individual silk, leaving blank spaces where corn kernels should have formed.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ waa beni siliki jeɔ kpo lɛ, Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani siliki tsɔji aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ baanyɛ afee fɔmɔ kotoku. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and get full of insects when I bag it right after removing it from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ efite ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ beni mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly picked maize grains still hold a lot of water inside. If you bag them immediately, trapped moisture creates heat and humidity, which causes destructive mold to grow and attracts grain weevils.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ni ajie ehee lɛ mli lolo. Kɛji akɛ okɛ baagi wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Trapped moisture lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ dalɛ ni egbalaa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds choke and destroy young soybean plants much faster than mature ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ soybean dumɔwui anɔ ni egbeɔ amɛ oya fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young soybeans grow slowly during their first few weeks and have small leaves that cannot block the sun. Fast-growing weeds easily outcompete young soybeans for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients until the soybean leaves grow wide enough to shade the ground.
ga: Soybean bibii lɛ daa blɛoo. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli ni eyɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ atsĩ hulu la lɛ naa. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ soybean bibii anɔ kunim yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he oya. Kɛyashi soybean baai lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin stems and fall over easily when I plant three or four seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishifãi bibii ni egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crowded stems to stretch upward desperately fighting each other for sunlight. This makes the stems long, thin, and weak, while their root systems remain too shallow to hold the heavy plants upright during strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ amɛhe lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya ŋwɛi ni amɛye akaŋ kɛha hulu la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, eyɛ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ, yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ emɔ tso ni tsii lɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth and strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why should I plant leguminous crops like cowpeas on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer, feeding the soil for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is my yam crop growing thick green leaves but producing very small yams underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi eyɛ bibioo kwraa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes yam plants spend all their energy growing vines and leaves above ground instead of sending stored food down into the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ amaje shi kɛya yitso lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants look like they are wilting in the afternoon even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to protect themselves from intense heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper pollination. Without pollination, the plant drops the flower to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Tsei baajie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi be mli ni amɛmaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot quickly if I leave them in the ground too long during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ ashi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ?

english: Excessive water in the soil drowns the roots by blocking air, which causes fungi and bacteria to multiply and rapidly rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: What is the benefit of buying certified seeds instead of using seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ he yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and diseases, handle short dry spells better, and produce uniform crops with higher yields compared to saved seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi bibii kɛ helai. Ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuji lɛ akwɛmɔ mli. ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni yaa nɔ daa ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your main crop gets a chance to build a strong root system.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa. Dani onibii titri lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa,

english: How does planting crops in straight rows help me get better yields than scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest efficiently.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni obaakpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight because their young leaves lose water quickly. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide shade with their large leaves, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ haa baai agboi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ he feɔ fɛo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the corn is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves are a clear sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil food. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it, so applying fertilizer like NPK early in the season keeps the leaves green and productive.
ga: Abɛi baa ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaku shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need support to lift their leaves off the ground and capture bright sunlight. Better exposure to sunlight allows the plant leaves to make more food, resulting in much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛya hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather becomes too hot, when the soil alternates rapidly between very wet and very dry, or when tiny pests damage the blossoms before fruits can set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nɔ ni mli egbi waa teŋ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it beneficial for my land to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on a plot where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔji ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts absorb nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally fertilize the soil, making it richer for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the next planting season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛfɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce very small yields even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds surround your crops, your main plants get starved of the nutrients needed to produce healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Otso titri lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds close together so I can fit more crops into my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the roots and leaves choke each other while fighting for soil nutrients and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each stalk grows strong and produces larger, fuller corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni amɛmiitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni ewoɔ ŋmãa ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil when I plant right after a prolonged heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Excess water fills all the tiny air spaces in flooded soil, preventing planted seeds from breathing oxygen. Without air, seeds quickly die and rot underground before they can sprout.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ amli obɔ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsĩɔ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ oya ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by microscopic insects, such as aphids or mites, that attach under the leaves to suck plant sap and spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛkpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu tsei amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛ helai ni haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that create shade, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the leaf tip in a V-shape usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong stems.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naa ni feɔ V su lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce big bushy leaves but small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai agboi shi ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants receive too much shade, the cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo babaoo. Kasava lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Flowers fall off pepper plants when temperatures become too hot, water is irregular, or the soil lacks enough phosphorus to support fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛjɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam plants with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato tso ni tso kakadaŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up toward direct sunlight. Staking helps leaves capture sunlight to manufacture the food needed to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Atomɔ tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ naa hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa koni sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and growing small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies transmitting a plant virus, or by extreme heat and uneven watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli

english: Why should I remove excess suckers growing around my plantain tree base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Each sucker competes with the main mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces a large bunch.
ga: Sucker lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato roots rot and turn black when I flood my field every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ nu hoɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli daa gbi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like they need water. Flooding soil constantly drives out air pockets, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing fungi to attack them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and tall with tiny ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ toi bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded crops must stretch upward to fight each other for limited sunlight, leaving insufficient light and nutrients to form healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Ehe baahia ni tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛye hulu la ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. La kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afee lɛ ni ashieee

english: Why do my stored maize sacks get warm and moldy when I stack them directly on the bare floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã kotokui ni mikɛto lɛ mli woɔ la ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grain breathes and gives off small amounts of moisture. When sacks rest directly on a cold concrete or dirt floor, that moisture gets trapped underneath, creating heat and dampness where mold and insects thrive.
ga: Ŋmãa lɛ muɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko haa. Kɛ akɛ kotoku lɛ fɔ kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ Nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shishi. Enɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice to stack my bags of harvested crops right against the storeroom wall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ kotokui baawo nitoohe lɛ gbogbo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Walls absorb moisture from rain and ground dampness. If your crop bags touch the wall, they absorb that trapped dampness, causing the crops inside to become wet, moldy, and prone to rot.
ga: Gbogboi lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu. Kɛji o-grow bag lɛ ta gbogbo lɛ he Ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I know if my harvested maize is dry enough to put into sacks without it spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo kotoku mli ni efiteee?

english: You can test it by biting a grain—if it cracks sharply without denting, it is dry. Alternatively, mix a handful of grain with dry salt in a closed jar; if the salt sticks to the sides of the jar, the grain is still too wet to store.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni oooye lɛ nɔ. Kɛji egbɛ eshwa ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi Aloo okɛ dumɔwui fioo ko afutu ŋmei ni egbi yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni aŋã mli. Kɛji ŋmei kpɛtɛɔ tɔ lɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lolo tsɔ ni esaaa akɛ akɛtoɔ.

english: Why do weevils destroy my harvested beans so fast after I put them in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-kɔfi yibii ni mikpa lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevils often lay tiny, unseen eggs inside the bean pods while they are still growing in the field. Once stored in warm conditions, those eggs hatch into larvae that eat the crop from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lolo lɛ. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing shoots even when they are kept inside a building?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii babaoo shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto shĩa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living roots that naturally wake up and sprout after a period of rest. Keeping them in warm, dark, or poorly ventilated rooms speeds up this natural process, causing them to lose weight and quality.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be ko sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shwiili lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why does keeping my harvested corn in a sealed room without windows make it spoil faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ tsu ko ni aŋã mli ni samfɛji bɛ mli lɛ haa egboɔ oya lɛ?

english: Harvested crops continue to sweat out moisture. Without proper ventilation to carry the damp air away, the humidity builds up in the room and creates a breeding ground for mold and fungal rot.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ ni baajie kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i buaa ehe naa yɛ tsu lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees lose their leaves and dry up when planted in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots. Harsh direct sun burns the leaves and dries out the soil faster than roots can drink, which is why temporary shade crops like plantains are needed to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni akɛbu amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains last for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Soaked soil fills all air pockets with water, preventing cassava roots from breathing. Without oxygen, the roots weaken, allowing soil fungi to easily invade and rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni afɔ lɛ ewo kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli kɛ nu. Etsiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akpaa.

english: High air humidity during the rainy season allows fungal spores to multiply rapidly. Raindrops splash these spores from pod to pod, causing black pod disease to spread quickly across the farm.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli. Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my groundnuts turn moldy and taste bitter if I harvest them while the soil is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Harvesting in wet soil traps moisture inside the groundnut shells. This damp environment encourages dangerous molds to grow on the nuts, producing toxins that create a bitter, spoiled taste.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ nɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ejieɔ tsofai fɔji ni haa ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ V-shape ni yɔɔ amɛnajiaŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to build strong green leaves, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or peanuts on my land help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and peanuts belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen gas out of the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When the legume crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground to nourish whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after planting my seeds before putting down fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni midu dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Newly planted seeds do not have roots yet, so placing fertilizer right next to them cannot be used by the seed and can actually burn tender sprouting leaves. Waiting until seedlings have visible leaves and roots ensures they can safely absorb the plant food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ bɛ shishifãi lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsu nii kɛha dumɔwui. ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashã. Mɛɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo faŋŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. They require shade trees or fast-growing shelter crops like plantains to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to keep moisture in the soil until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo loo tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he kɛyashi amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm early instead of waiting until the crops are tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are too weak to fight against fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without having to share them.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛja.

english: Why am I seeing small holes and sawdust-like waste inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii abifao lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the growing leaf funnel of the maize plant. Spraying targeted organic or recommended remedies directly into the leaf funnel early stops them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmei tso lɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs tall stakes to lift its leaves up toward the sun. When the leaves catch maximum sunlight, the plant creates more energy to grow large, healthy tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Beni baai lɛ náa hulu la babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni eha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Spacing cassava stems about one meter apart gives each plant enough space to spread its roots and foliage. This prevents plants from shading each other and allows underground tubers room to expand without crowding.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee mita kome, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwa. Enɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee amɛhe shade. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni mɛi babaoo ehiɛɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my crops on raised earth mounds or ridges during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges raise plant roots above standing water, preventing roots from rotting in waterlogged soil while also loosening the dirt so root crops can easily grow deep and wide.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ woɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛmli kwɔ ni amɛshwere oya.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This issue is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, often due to uneven watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant draw up the calcium it needs to form solid, healthy fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat, their delicate leaves burn, dry out, and drop off to protect the plant from losing too much water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ Koni hulutsoo ni naa wa akafee Amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why do some of my neighbors plant cassava and maize together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋbii lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together makes good use of space and nutrients. Maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving the ground open for cassava, which takes longer to mature, to fill in and grow without competing for light.
ga: Kasava kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa akɛ he kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ahaa ŋmei lɛ, ni eheɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Koni eyi obɔ kɛ eda ni ekɛ la akaŋ akaŋ

english: Why do my maize plants roll their leaves into tight tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsiɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a maize plant's natural defense mechanism against heat. By curling up, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which keeps it from losing precious water through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji abele tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei baa shikpɔŋ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ shi kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa nu ni jara wa lɛ afite kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into peppers when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants get stressed and prioritize survival over reproducing. They shed their flowers to conserve water and energy until cooler conditions return.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛhaa wala ni amɛhiɔ shi lɛ yeɔ hiɛ fe fɔmɔ. Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing huge green leaves but failing to give me any big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ebɛ aduawai agboi kɛha mi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. High nitrogen makes plants focus all their energy on growing leafy branches instead of setting flowers and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ fa babaoo ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei niji ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Yellowing in the center of older maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant is moving its limited nitrogen supply up to the newer, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛmiiya baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is the traditional planting time for maize in April not working as well as it used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ April mli kusum be ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Changing rainfall patterns mean the rainy season often starts later or becomes unpredictable. Planting strictly by old calendar dates can lead to seeds germinating during sudden dry spells, so farmers now need to wait for reliable rains before sowing.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi ni tsakeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ loo anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ blema kalanda gbii anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ amɛmɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani amɛdu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small when planted during prolonged dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stores extra energy in its roots as starch. During a dry spell, the plant slows down root expansion and uses its energy just to keep its leaves and stems alive until water becomes available again.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ kroko toɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ ŋmei gbɛ nɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ yaa hiɛ fioo ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi kɛkɛ kɛyashi nu baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up short and bent instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle shi moŋ ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers turn short or crooked when they hit hard, compacted soil or rocks underground. Loose, deep mounds give the root room to stretch straight down as it grows.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kuku loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli ŋtayaa lɛ feɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do plantain suckers planted late in the rainy season take longer to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need constant moisture during their early growth phase to build strong roots. If planted late, the coming dry season stunts their root development, delaying flowering and fruiting by several months.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu daa yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ mli koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji adu sɛɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my crops yield so little even when I clear and plant a very large piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie shikpɔŋ ni da waa ni midu nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting a plot that is too large for one person to manage means you cannot do all the necessary weeding, fertilizing, and pruning on time. Focusing your labor on a smaller, well-cared-for plot often produces a higher harvest than spreading your effort thin over a big area.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni da tsɔ ni mɔ kome nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onyɛɛɛ okɛ jwɛi awo mli, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okɛ jwɛi awo mli yɛ be naa. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni akɛaama shikpɔji bibii anɔ Shikpɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo fe nɔ ni abɔ mɔdɛŋ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year when I continue planting on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi be mli ni miyaa nɔ miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil over time. Rotating different crops or letting the land rest allows the soil to rebuild its nutrients and sustain healthier crops.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Aloo, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ saa ehe nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahe ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die under the direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides the necessary living shade and moisture for them to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ aba.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I delay weeding my plot by a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ sɛɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Delaying weeding allows weeds to steal these vital resources early on, which permanently stunts crop growth and significantly reduces your final yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ juɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ afee mlɛo kwraa. ni ebaanyɛ eba naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ shi waa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves and spreading plant diseases. Applying safe pest management solutions early protects the plant and keeps it producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii mra lɛ Ebaabu tso lɛ he ni eye ebua lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce large leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plants focus all their energy on growing upper leaves instead of sending food down to develop thick roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow during seasons with heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in waterlogged soil starves plant roots of oxygen and washes nitrogen away from the root zone, causing the leaves to turn yellow from nutrient lack.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ, ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it safe for my soil and crops if I plant beans and maize together on one plot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping beans with maize is beneficial because beans take nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which helps feed the maize while allowing you to harvest two crops from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akɛ ŋmãa lɛ aha kooloi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do store-bought certified seeds produce better harvests than the seeds I save from my previous crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred and tested to resist local diseases, tolerate dry weather, and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over multiple generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli.

english: How can I involve my children in managing my crop plots so they learn to farm successfully?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mibii lɛ awo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ mli koni amɛkase okwaayeli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Giving children small, manageable sections of a plot to care for teaches them practical skills like proper spacing, planting, and crop care, building both their experience and passion for farming.
ga: Kɛ́ aha gbekɛbii lɛ he bibioo ko ni amɛkwɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔɔ amɛ nibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ gbɛ ni sa, dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛ suɔmɔ kɛha okwaayeli fɛɛ.

english: How can I check if my farmland is fertile enough to give me a good harvest before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo yibii kpakpai bɔ ni sa dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: You can check your soil's fertility by collecting soil samples from different parts of your field and taking them to a local agricultural laboratory or extension officer for testing. This test tells you the exact nutrient levels in your land so you can prepare it properly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ shwereɔ ehaa lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni oooŋɔ kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ nɔ. ni ji oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛya maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he laboratori loo extension officer lɛ koni aka lɛ akwɛ. Ka nɛɛ tsɔɔ bo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ osaa oniyenii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I test my soil before planting instead of just planting directly like we traditionally do in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka shikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani madu nii moŋ fe ni madu tɛ̃ɛ tamɔ bɔ ni wɔfeɔ yɛ Ghana kusum mli lɛ?

english: Testing your soil before planting prevents wasted money on the wrong fertilizers and protects your crops from failing. It gives you clear knowledge about your land's health, allowing you to feed your crops exactly what they need to thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shika ni afite lɛ akakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii, ni ebaabu onibii ahe koni amɛkafite. Ehaa onáa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he nilee ni mli ka shi faŋŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ niyenii haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is there a simple method I can use on my farm to collect soil samples for a fertility check?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ matsɔ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛbua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii anaa koni makwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ yɔɔ ha?

english: Yes, you can walk across your farm in a zigzag pattern, clear the top leaves, and use a cutlass or trowel to dig a small V-shaped hole about 15 centimeters deep. Collect a slice of soil from 5 to 10 spots, mix them thoroughly in a clean bucket, and take a small portion of that mixture for testing.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ zigzag gbɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tsɔne loo trowel atsa bu bibioo ko ni tamɔ V ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 15. Bua shikpɔŋ hei 5 kɛyashi 10 naa ni okɛfutu yɛ baagi ni mli tse mli. ni okɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ fioo ko aka lɛ akwɛ.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to test my farm's soil fertility?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛkaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ?

english: The best time to test your soil is during the dry season or a few weeks before land preparation and planting begin. This gives you enough time to get the results back and add any required nutrients to the soil before putting seeds in the ground.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ ji yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo otsii fioo komɛi dani shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi. Enɛ baaha oná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛ nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What signs on my field can show me that my land is losing its strength and needs testing?
ga: Ani okadii komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ atsɔɔ mi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni aka lɛ akwɛ?

english: Common signs of weak land include slow or stunted crop growth, leaves turning yellow early, poor root development, water failing to drain properly, and getting smaller harvests every year despite receiving good rain.
ga: Okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ekomɛi ji tsei ni edaa blɛoo loo amɛyaa hiɛ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. Shishifãi ni edako jogbaŋŋ Nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni kpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I tell if my land is fertile just by looking at the soil color, or do I need a formal lab test?
ga: Ani manyɛ mana kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ matsɔ laboratorio mli kaa ko mli?

english: While dark soil often indicates good organic matter, color alone cannot tell you if the soil lacks critical hidden nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus, or if it is too acidic. A laboratory soil test gives you precise information that visual checks cannot reveal.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nibii kpakpai yɛ mli moŋ, shi su pɛ nyɛŋ atsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus bɛ mli. Aloo eyɛ acid tsɔ? Laboratory shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa haa anaa saji ni ja ni hiŋmɛi nɔ kwɛmɔ nyɛŋ ajie lɛ kpo.

english: How does knowing my land's fertility status help me increase my crop yield?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ shihilɛ ni mile lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ?

english: Knowing your land's fertility lets you apply the correct type and exact quantity of fertilizer your soil lacks. This ensures your crops receive balanced nutrition, preventing under-feeding or over-fertilizing, both of which reduce yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ha lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni sa tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni faaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa. Tsi niyenii ni falɛ faaa loo fɔmɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa. Nibii enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Do different crops require different levels of soil strength and nutrients on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Yes, different crops have different nutritional demands. For example, maize and leafy vegetables require high nitrogen, while root crops like cassava and yam need more potassium; testing helps you match the right crop to your soil's current strength.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei srɔtoi yɛ niyenii he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ he miihia nitrogen babaoo. Yɛ be mli ni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei biɔ potassium babaoo. Kaa lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ he.

english: Is testing my farmland worth the extra time and investment when starting a new farm?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kaa lɛ sa be kɛ shika ni fata he lɛ he beni mijeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, testing your soil saves money in the long run. It prevents crop failure, stops you from buying expensive fertilizers your land does not need, and ensures your farm investment yields maximum profits.
ga: Hɛɛ, oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooka lɛ haa okɛ shika baafite yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni he ehiaaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ. ni ekwɛɔ koni shika ni okɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba sɛɛnamɔ bɔ ni abaanyɛ.

english: Where can I take my soil sample in Ghana to find out if my land is ready for planting?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maŋɔ shikpɔŋ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ yɛ Ghana koni mana kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ?

english: You can take your soil samples to your local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) district office, agricultural extension officers, or research institutions like the CSIR-Soil Research Institute.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ aya he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ. loo niiamlitaomɔ hei tamɔ CSIR-Shikpɔŋ He Nibii Amli Taomɔ He

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from harsh direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantain plants nearby to block the hot sun, the young leaves dry out and the seedlings die.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa lɛ, baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow and showing ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni buji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with ragged holes are a sign that destructive caterpillars like Fall Armyworm are eating the plant, or that the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer. Identifying these signs early allows you to treat the crop before it is ruined.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmeii efo mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ miiye tso lɛ. loo tsei ni nitrogen fertilizer bɛ mli Okadii nɛɛ ni oooyɔse mra Ehaa onyɛɔ ohereɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani akpãtãa amɛhiɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking from the swelling roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of essential soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing proper manure or fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and grow into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer directly touching the main stem can burn the outer bark and roots of the plant. Fertilizers should be applied a few inches away from the stem in a ring so the roots can safely reach out and absorb the nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛŋɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Having too many shoots growing from the same plant creates competition for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce large, heavy fruits.
ga: Tso kome mli ŋmeii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it important to provide wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tso aha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises the yam leaves high into the sunlight, allowing the plant to make more energy to swell the underground tubers, while also keeping the leaves off the damp ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akashɛ ohe.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rainy season sets in. Seeds planted too early will germinate after the first rain and then dry up and die if follow-up rains do not come promptly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni no sɛɛ lɛ ebaagbi ni egbo kɛji nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaa yɛ be naa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays or neem oil keeps the leaves healthy and open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa loo neem fɔ ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛgbele.

english: How does adding decomposed animal manure to my farmland help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure by helping hard ground stay soft and retaining soil moisture longer during hot days, while slowly releasing natural nutrients that make crops grow strong and green.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ koni ehi shi blɛoo ni ehiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ kpo.

english: Look for certified seed packages with clear labels that display details like the crop variety, germination percentage, purity, and expiry date. Avoid buying loose, unlabelled seeds if you want a reliable and high-yielding harvest.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui akui ni awo he odase ni yɔɔ nɔ ni tsɔɔ mli fitsofitso tamɔ tso henɔi, kwɛ̃mɔ oha mlijaa. hetsemɔ kɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akadiko nɔ kɛ nɔ ni akadiko nɔ lɛ hemɔ he kɛji oosumɔ ŋmaa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What information should I look for on a seed label before paying for it?
ga: Mɛɛ saji esa akɛ matao yɛ dumɔwui ahe wolo nɔ dani mawo nyɔmɔ?

english: Always check the crop variety name, germination percentage, test date, batch number, and the producer's details. This information proves that the seeds have been tested for quality and are suitable for planting.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ gbɛi Be fɛɛ be lɛ kwɛ̃mɔ oha mlijaa, kaa gbi, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ yibɔ kɛ mɔ ni fee lɛ mli fitsofitso. Saji nɛɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ aka dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ kɛji amɛhi jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛhi kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why are certified seeds packaged with printed labels instead of sold loose?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ kotoku mli kɛ woji ni akala nɔ moŋ fe ni ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Printed labels act as an official quality guarantee from seed inspection authorities, showing that the seeds met official standards for purity, disease resistance, and sprouting power before being sold.
ga: Nɔ ni akala lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔmimaa ni jɛɔ dumɔwui akwɛmɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ dɛŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ hetsemɔ he mlai ni maŋ lɛ kɛma shi lɛ anɔ. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ dani ahɔ̃ɔ

english: Is it better to buy labeled seeds from a store or save seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni aŋmala nɔ nibii awo nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shwapo mli loo oookɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified labeled seeds are carefully tested for high germination rates and disease resistance, usually giving much higher yields. Saved seeds often lose their strength over generations and can carry diseases into your soil.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛhe saji awo mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What does 'germination percentage' on a seed bag actually mean for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ‘shweremɔ mlijaa oha mlijaa’ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui kotoku nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Germination percentage tells you how many seeds out of 100 are expected to successfully sprout under good conditions. A high percentage like 85% or 90% means almost all the seeds you plant will grow into healthy seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa tsɔɔ bo dumɔwui enyiɛ yɛ 100 mli ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi kpakpai amli. Oha mlijaa 100 ni fa babaoo, tamɔ 85% loo 90% lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to grow even after I water the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni mifɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are old, damaged, poorly stored, or have a low germination rate. Poor soil contact, planting too deep, or soil pests can also prevent good seeds from germinating.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ, amɛfite, akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ, loo amɛkwɛ̃mɔ oya. shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni aduɔ yɛ mli tsɔ Aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dumɔwui kpakpai anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: What will happen to my field if I plant seeds with a low germination rate?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni shweremɔ fioo pɛ?

english: Planting low-germination seeds creates wide empty gaps in your field, resulting in fewer plants, wasted fertilizer, increased weed growth in bare spots, and a much smaller harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa he ko bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei fioo komɛi. Afiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa jwɛi ni yɔɔ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni kpamɔ lɛ hu faaa kwraa

english: How can I test if my stored seeds will sprout before I plant my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baakwɛ̃ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can do a simple ragdoll test by placing 10 or 20 seeds inside a damp cloth or paper towel. Keep it moist in a warm place for a few days, then count how many seeds sprout to calculate your germination percentage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ragdoll lɛ okwɛ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 loo 20 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. loo toilet wolo Ha ehi he ko ni mli edɔ gbii fioo komɛi, no sɛɛ lɛ kanemɔ dumɔwui ayibɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ koni ona bɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ oha mlijaa 100 lɛ he akɔntaa.

english: Why does the crop variety name written on the seed package matter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ gbɛi ni aŋma yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ he hiaa lɛ?

english: Different varieties of the same crop behave differently in the soil—some mature faster, resist local pests better, or survive dry weather better. The variety name helps you know exactly how that plant will grow on your farm.
ga: Tso kome lɛ mli henɔi srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Henɔi komɛi daa oya. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Loo ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛi srɔtoi lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How should I store my leftover seeds so they still sprout well next season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ ato koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Store seeds in a cool, dry, dark place inside airtight containers. Heat, moisture, and sunlight degrade seed life quickly and drastically lower their germination percentage over time.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni yɔɔ duŋ yɛ tsinsii ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Dɔlɛ, latsaa, kɛ hulu la haa dumɔwui awala feɔ kuku oya ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ baa shi kwraa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Do I need to do hand pollination across my entire cocoa farm, or should I only focus on specific trees?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ miniji awo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama tsei komɛi pɛ anɔ?

english: Hand pollination can be done on the whole farm, but it is labor-intensive. Farmers often focus on mature, healthy trees in open areas that receive good light, as these give the highest pod yields per flower pollinated.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ niji afee pollination yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shi ebiɔ nitsumɔ babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hei ni kane kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ woɔ pod yibii ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni awo mli pollen lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli.

english: What is the best time of day to pollinate crop flowers on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Early morning is the best time because flowers are freshly opened, pollen is moist and sticky, and pollinating insects are most active before the heat of the day dries out the blossoms.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ fɔfɔi lɛ miikwɛ kɛkɛ. Pollen lɛ mli edɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he. Ni ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii waa dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why are some of my cocoa trees dropping their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifɔlɔ ni amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when they fail to get pollinated by tiny insects like midges, or when the tree lacks water and nutrients. Keeping leaf litter on the farm floor creates a moist environment where these pollinating insects can breed.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛhe fɔfɔi, loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii. Baai amli jwɛi ni abua naa yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baanyɛ afɔ́ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tiny cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally thins out pods it cannot feed, or it is caused by pest attacks. Pruning excessive shade and fertilizing the soil help the tree hold on to more healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji hela ko ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jeee adebɔɔ naa nɔ ni ayeɔ lɛ. aloo nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ He ni afoɔ, ni akɛhaa hulutsoo fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa lɛ amli.

english: I noticed some cocoa pods on my farm look pale white like 'morepre agu' while others are dark green. Why do they look different?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ, kookoo ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ futafuta tamɔ ‘morepre agu’, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ futafuta tamɔ ‘morepre agu’. Eji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. Mɛni hewɔ amɛhiɛ yɔɔ srɔto lɛ?

english: Different cocoa varieties naturally have different pod colors when young, ranging from pale green or whitish to dark green or purple. As long as the tree is healthy, color variation simply shows you have different varieties on your farm.
ga: Cocoa henɔi srɔtoi lɛ yɛ pod sui srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdarako lɛ. Kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo eyɛŋ nɔ kɛyashi eŋɔli ni mli edɔ loo purple nɔ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ Sui srɔtoi hu tsɔɔ akɛ oyɛ srɔtoi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting trees too close together in an old farm affect their ability to produce fruit?
ga: Te tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ momo ko mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, their branches block sunlight from reaching lower flowers, and their roots fight over groundwater and soil nutrients, leading to fewer flowers and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso niji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ni tsei shishifãi wuɔ amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii fioo pɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: How much sun or shade do my cocoa trees need to bloom properly?
ga: Hulu loo hulutsoo be enyiɛ ehe hiaa mi-kokoo tso lɛ koni ekwɛ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Young crops need thick shade from plantain leaves to protect them from burning, but mature bearing trees need moderate sunlight to trigger abundant flowering and pod growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ni mli wa kɛjɛ plantain baai lɛ amli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Shi tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekanya fɔfɔi kɛ pod dalɛ babaoo.

english: Why are the old trees I inherited from my family producing much smaller pods than newer planted trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso momo ni miná akɛ gboshinii kɛjɛ miweku lɛ dɛŋ lɛ wo ŋmeii bibii kwraa fe tso ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: As trees age, their internal water passages weaken and roots become less efficient at absorbing soil nutrients. Pruning old branches or replacing aged trees helps bring back strong pod growth.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ da Nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Niji ni egbɔ ni afolɔ loo tsei ni egbɔ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crops in one part of my farm yield heavily while trees in another section hardly produce anything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Soil quality, moisture levels, and sunlight vary across a farm. Sections with deeper, nutrient-rich soil and good drainage naturally support healthier trees and bigger yields than rocky or waterlogged areas.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, hulutsoo kɛ hulu la lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Fã ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ Niyenii nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Kɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo fe hei ni tɛi yɔɔ loo hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Can I grow different varieties of cocoa side by side without them spoiling each other's yields?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo henɔi srɔtoi yɛ he kome ni miyeee miteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui?

english: Yes, planting different varieties together is safe and can protect your farm from complete crop loss if a disease hits, as long as all trees receive proper spacing, sunlight, and pruning.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ srɔtoi srɔtoi Kɛ amɛfee ekome lɛ, amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kwraa lɛ he kɛji hela ba. Shii abɔ ni tsei fɛɛ naa gbɛ ni sa, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii,

english: How do I know when my cocoa trees need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When cocoa leaves start turning yellow or the tree stops producing pods during the normal season, it usually means the soil lacks nutrients. Applying specialized cocoa fertilizer gives the tree essential minerals to make leaves green again and encourage healthy pod growth.
ga: Enɛ ji be mli ni kookoo baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni sa mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ, ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time of the year to apply fertilizer to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The best time is at the start of the rainy season, usually around May or June, because the moisture in the soil helps dissolve the fertilizer so the roots can easily drink it in.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee May loo June. Ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu mlɛo.

english: Can I plant cocoa on any type of soil on my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi fɛɛ nɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, cocoa grows best in deep, rich soil that holds moisture well without staying waterlogged. Hard clay or very sandy soils struggle to hold water and nutrients, which stops cocoa roots from spreading.
ga: Dabi, Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baatsi kookoo shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.
