english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that burn and dry out easily under harsh sun. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to provide cool cover until they grow mature and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree is stressed by drought or lack of food, or if tiny beneficial insects called midges are not available to pollinate them. Keeping damp shade under the trees helps pollinators thrive and helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollination. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ha tsei ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa pollinators lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ pods.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing very small pods this harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ wo ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ kpamɔɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Small pods usually happen when the tree lacks water, potassium, or other key nutrients during pod development. Feeding the soil properly and keeping weeds down ensures the tree has enough energy to grow full-sized pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii feɔ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu, potassium, loo niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa. Yɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ be mli Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ pods ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What causes the black spots on my cocoa pods that make them rot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi anɔ ni haa amɛgboɔ lɛ baa?

english: Black spots are usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming overcrowded branches lets in air and sunlight to dry out the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni ji black pod lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli agbiɔ.

english: Will cutting off branches from my cocoa tree harm my yield?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaná mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ?

english: Pruning unnecessary or sick branches actually increases your yield. It opens up the tree canopy so sunlight can reach the trunk and air can flow through, reducing fungal diseases and helping the tree focus energy on pod growth.
ga: Tsei ni he ehiaaa loo ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaakpa lɛ baaha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Gbelemɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa pod lɛ dalɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds growing around my cocoa trees affect my harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te cacao tsei náa mikpamɔ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your cocoa trees can get them. Keeping the ground clear ensures your crop gets all the nutrition it needs.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii dani o-cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why should I attend agricultural extension programs if I already know how to farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo Okwaayeli He Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mile bɔ ni afeɔ okwaayeli momo?

english: Farming conditions change over time due to weather, new pests, and soil depletion. Extension officers share updated, scientific techniques that help you get much higher yields and profits from the same plot of land.
ga: Okwaayeli shihilɛi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Nibii heei ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ Extension nitsulɔi lɛ jaa jeŋ nilee mli ŋaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ ni baaye abua bo ni oná sɛɛnamɔi ni fa babaoo kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Can I plant the same yams that I buy from the market to eat, or do I need special seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato tamɔ nɔ ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi atsu nii?

english: You can use market yams, but it is best to cut healthy tubers into smaller pieces or save small whole tubers from a disease-free farm. These 'seed yams' sprout better and ensure you get a strong crop without carrying diseases into your soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sweet potato atsu nii yɛ jara nɔ. Shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli bibii bibii. loo kwɛ yitsei bibii Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ jɛɔ ŋmɔ ko ni hela bɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ‘yam dumɔwui’ nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua bo ni oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni hela kɛbaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I decide how much of my yam harvest I should save for planting next season versus selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ mlijaa enyiɛ ni mikɛto kɛha dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ he kɛto jarayeli he?

english: A practical approach is to set aside roughly one-fifth to one-quarter of your healthiest, medium-sized tubers specifically for planting. Saving good planting stock saves you money next season and guarantees you have healthy material to start with.
ga: Nifeemɔ kpakpa ji ni akɛ aaafee bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mlijaa enumɔ mli ekome kɛyashi ejwɛ mli ekome ato he pɔtɛɛ kɛha dumɔ. Nibii ni hi ni aduɔ lɛ ni oooŋɔ lɛ baaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli, ni ebaaha oná nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛje shishi.

english: What happens if I plant a cut yam piece with the cut flesh facing upwards toward the sun?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato ŋmɔtɔi ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ kwɛ ŋwɛi kɛtee hulu lɛ he?

english: If the exposed cut flesh faces upward, the sun can dry it out and rot can easily set in before it sprouts. Placing the cut side downward into the moist soil protects the seed piece and lets the skin side sprout easily upward.
ga: Kɛji he ni afo lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Hulu lɛ baanyɛ aha loo lɛ agbi ni ebaanyɛ egbo oya dani ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ fã ni afo lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ebaaha hewolo fã lɛ adara kɛya ŋwɛi mlɛo.

english: Why do yams seem to grow so well in transition areas like Atebubu and the Northern region compared to wet forest areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni yams kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsakemɔ hei tamɔ Atebubu kɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ, kɛ akɛto kooi ni mli efɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yams prefer deep, loose soil and a climate with a clear dry season and moderate rainfall. Areas like Atebubu and the North have ideal savannah soil that allows yam tubers to expand deep underground without rotting in waterlogged soil.
ga: Atomɔ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse. Eyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ srɔto kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Hei tamɔ Atebubu kɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ savannah shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why must I build high soil mounds or ridges before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large and deep into the ground. Raising the soil into loose mounds gives the tubers soft earth to expand smoothly while keeping excess water away from the root so the crop does not rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ owó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtee gɔŋ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha bulb lɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ akafite.

english: Yam vines are climbers that need sunlight to produce energy. Raising the vines on sticks spreads the leaves out to catch solar light, which feeds the plant and directly increases the size of the tuber growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji ŋmeii ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ. Wein tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei aniji anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. ni haa tsei niyenii ni ehaa bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ daraa.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are mature and ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You know the crop is ready when the green leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. This change shows that the plant has stopped growing leaves and has finished sending all its energy down into the tuber.
ga: O le kaa ngmɔ ní ɔmɛ pee klaalo ke tsohi nɛ a ngɛ ŋmɔji kɛ wai tso ɔmɛ pee ŋmɔŋ nɛ a gbi ngɛ adebɔ mi ɔ. Tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etsu nii kɛtee bulb lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting or decaying when I keep them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ loo egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛto beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up and sprout when the air gets warm, and they rot if trapped in hot or damp places. Storing them on open wooden racks under cool shade keeps fresh air circulating and slows down sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi ni amɛshwereɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ. Ni ebaagbo kɛji ekã he ko ni edɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo tso ni agbele nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aya nɔ abɔle ohe ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo oya.

english: Why do yams harvested during the dry season taste better and last longer in the market than those harvested right after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ waa ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams dug up in dry weather contain less water and more concentrated starch, giving them better taste and firm texture. Excess moisture from recent rain makes the tubers soft and much more prone to fungal rotting during transport.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni atsa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi lɛ bɛ nu babaoo, ni starch hu fa babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ŋmeii baanyɛ afite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested yams come out of the ground with dark cracks or small holes on the surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ loo buji bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Dark cracks and holes on yam tubers are usually caused by tiny soil pests like nematodes or beetles feeding on the growing skin. Planting clean seed material and moving your yam field to fresh ground each year helps break their life cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ hewolo ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ bu ni yɔɔ sweet potato ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni aduɔ kɛ sweet potato ŋmɔji ni ajieɔ kɛyaa he ko hee daa afi lɛ baaye abua ni aku amɛshihilɛ mli shihilɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough for me to plant maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa?

english: You can check by looking at the soil's color and feel, or by having an extension officer test it. Maize prefers rich, dark soil that drains water easily so the plant roots do not rot in standing water.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni enuɔ he ehaa lɛ nɔ. aloo ha mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ afee kaa lɛ Abele sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteee yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why should I test or check my soil before I start planting a new crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ loo makwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani mabɔi tsei heei akwɛmɔ?

english: Checking your soil tells you what nutrients are already inside and what is missing. This prevents you from wasting money on seeds or fertilizers that will not do well on your specific piece of land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ ni okɛ shika akafite yɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Is it good for me to burn the bush on my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys key nutrients and living organisms in the top layer of earth. Over time, burning leaves your soil weak and dry, making it harder for future crops to thrive.
ga: Shãa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse oya. Mohu ɔ, e kpataɔ niye ní nɛ he hia kɛ wami nɛ ngɛ Zugba a nɔ ɔ hɛ mi. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of my farm's soil, and how does that harm my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te nakai feemɔ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The top layer of soil contains most of the natural food plants need to grow. When rain washes this layer away, your crops lose their main source of nourishment and their roots lose support.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ji he ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛshwere lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɔɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ shwie nɛkɛ ŋtayaa nɛɛ nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite niyenii titri ni amɛnáa lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu baafite yelikɛbuamɔ.

english: Why do some crops grow very well on my neighbor's land but fail completely on mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋbii lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛyeee lɛ?

english: Soil properties can change even between nearby farms. Your neighbor's land might hold water differently or have different natural nutrients than yours, allowing certain crops to thrive there while struggling on your land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ po. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu loo adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔto fe onɔ̃ lɛ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi akwɛ̃ be mli ni okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ miiwuu lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When soil gets soaked with too much standing water, plant roots cannot breathe to draw up nutrients like nitrogen. The lack of air in soggy soil causes the leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plant leaves droop in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the ground. Drooping is the plant's natural way of hiding its leaf surface from the sun to save water until the weather cools down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ baai lɛ hiɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hulu la he koni ekɛbu nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on my land while my planted crops struggle to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miidara oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds are tough wild plants adapted to survive in poor soil conditions with very little nourishment. Main crops are more delicate and need well-prepared, nutrient-rich soil to grow faster than the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa, ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya fe jwɛi.

english: How can I choose the best crop to plant on a dry piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Look for crops with deep roots or natural drought tolerance, like cassava or cowpeas. These crops can search deep underground for moisture and survive with less rainwater compared to crops like cabbage.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ loo ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ gbɛ yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa, tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛtaoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo mli kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ kaabe he.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require the right mix of soil moisture, softness, and warmth to wake up. If the soil is packed too hard, too dry, or completely waterlogged, the seeds will rot or fail to push through to the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, bɔdɔɔfeemɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa koni amɛte shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, egbi tsɔ, loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die in the swampy parts of my farm after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on the land for too long, it drowns the roots, stopping them from taking up plant food, which causes the crop to turn yellow and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Etsiɔ gbɔmɛi anaa koni amɛkaye tsei aniyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo.

english: What kind of crops can I plant in the low parts of my land that stay full of water?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ shishigbɛ?

english: Crops like rice and cocoyam naturally love wet conditions and thrive in soggy soil, whereas crops like maize or cassava will rot if their roots stay in standing water.
ga: Dumɔwui tamɔ omɔ kɛ kookoo sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baafite kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear all the weeds and bush before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbours—they steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from your young crops. Clearing them gives your seeds a clean start to grow strong without fighting for survival.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofɔ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close to each other on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for root space and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small harvests instead of big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Ebaafee akaŋ kɛha shishifãi kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is fertile enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Good, fertile soil is usually dark in colour, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms or decaying leaves that feed your plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni baa nii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai ni fiteɔ ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei yɛ.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year, will it affect how the crops grow?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, Ani ebaana tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the ground and attracts pests that love that crop, causing your yield to drop smaller and smaller each season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbalaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ehaa onitsumɔ lɛ baa shi fiofio. yɛ be fɛɛ mli

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with big leaves but produce very little food at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plants put all their energy into leaves and tall stems when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer or shade, leaving no energy left over to form big grains or tubers.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kakadaji kɛ tsei ashishifãi amli kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo hulutsoo babaoo. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni baaha etsɔ dumɔwui loo bulb agbo.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize so that it doesn't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni ekafite yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the corn kernels are hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha otsitsii lɛ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the dry season, and will the crop survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to protect itself and conserve water. Once the rains return, the plant will shoot out fresh green leaves and continue growing underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ebu ehe ni ekɛ nu akafite. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes my seeds to rot underground before they even sprout into young plants?
ga: Mɛni miiha midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbatsɔ dumɔwui bibii po?

english: Seeds rot when the ground is too wet and cold, or if they are buried too deep in the soil where soil insects and mold can attack them before they wake up and grow.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ afu lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua lɛ dani amɛte shi ni amɛdara.

english: Why is it better to clear unwanted wild trees from my farm while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ majie koo mli tsei ni ataooo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ?

english: Removing young wild trees is easy and takes less effort. If you let them grow big, their deep roots will steal water and food from your crops, and cutting them down later can destroy your mature crops when the giant trees fall.
ga: Tsei bibii ni ajieɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ waaa, ni ebiii mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo. Kɛji oha amɛdara Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ni kɛ́ afo amɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ kɛ́ tsei wuji gbee shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow strong green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so adding manure or fertilizer will help bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special plants that can pull food (nitrogen) directly out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you plant them with maize, they share this free natural food with the maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ agbala niyenii mli hewalɛ (nitrogen) kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ atswa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ okɛ ŋmãa du lɛ Amɛbaajara adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that dry out quickly under direct hot sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted next to them to block the harsh heat until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli aba mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry bush grass help them survive hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (called mulching) works like a blanket that keeps the hot sun from evaporating water from the soil. It keeps the ground cool and moist so your crop roots do not dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa Mulching (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This causes them to grow thin and weak, producing smaller yields than plants given enough space to grow properly.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ shwɛm ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi fe tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the bottom leaves stop growing, turn yellow, and drop off, leaving a bare stem. You will also see the soil around the base of the stem start to crack as the tubers push upward.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ kpa shweremɔ. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi, ni eshi tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Obaana shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa beni yitso lɛ tsiɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers without forming any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo tomato yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when they do not get steady water. When the plant gets stressed by heat, it drops flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Kɛ tsei miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the central funnels of my young maize plants and chewing the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛmiiye baai lɛ?

english: These are caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which prefer to hide deep inside the soft central leaves where birds cannot reach them. Spraying organic or approved control measures late in the afternoon reaches them when they come out to feed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni okpoi nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baashɛ amɛhe beni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii lɛ.

english: Can I use any cut piece of a harvested yam tuber to plant a new yam field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ atsu nii kɛdu sweet potato ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Not all parts of a yam grow the same way; the top 'head' part sprouts fastest because that is where the main growth buds are located. Using the head cuts or healthy small whole seed yams gives you the strongest new plants.
ga: Jeee sweet potato lɛ fãi fɛɛ daa yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ, ‘yitso’ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni ŋmeii titrii lɛ yɔɔ. Kɛtsɔ tubers ni afolɔ loo yams bibii ni eye emuu ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaha oná tsei heei ni he wa fe fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living shade, giving young cocoa the protection and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hebuu kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close to each other so I can harvest more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes all the plants grow tall and weak, resulting in smaller yields than if they had enough space.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo fe kɛji akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sun on their leaves to make food that grows large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii beni amɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the water supply is irregular, such as going from very dry soil to suddenly flooding it with rain or water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ, tamɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ni kɛ nugbɔ loo nu baa trukaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips living under the leaves, or a virus transmitted by these insects that stunts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa ni haa tsei kpaɔ amɛdalɛ.

english: Should I apply my granular fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer down into the deep soil or off your farm before your plants' roots get the chance to absorb it, wasting your money.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛfite oshika.

english: Weeds are wild, native plants that have adapted over hundreds of years to survive in local soils with very little care, making them much faster at stealing food and water than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside funnel leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ahe baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides deep inside the growing tip of maize plants to feed on tender leaves, which can destroy the plant if not managed early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tsei ahiɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting when the stem turns woody, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base starts cracking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ tsei. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a cleared open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas to shield them from high heat and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize make my maize grow greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa ehe waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so the cowpeas act as a natural fertilizer for the surrounding maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsina ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛha ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ amɛmligbɛ tsitsii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crop leaves droop and wilt under the hot afternoon sun even when the leaves look healthy in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ leebi moŋ.

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant wilts to conserve moisture, then recovers overnight as it absorbs water continuously.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ gboɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli beni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my watermelon vines falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ wain tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Watermelons have separate male and female flowers on the same vine. If bees and insects are not visiting to carry pollen from the male flowers to the female flowers, the unpollinated female flowers will drop off.
ga: Watermelon yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ wain tso kome nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii saraaa koni amɛbaŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei lɛ anɔ. Fɔfɔi yei ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open on the vine after sudden heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a dry period is followed by heavy rain, the tomato plant drinks up water very quickly. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to crack open.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato tsei lɛ baanu nu oya. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli fãa.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites feeding on the plant juice and transmitting leaf curl viruses, which disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ baa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when rain falls heavily right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa dani kpamɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause water to pool around the roots, blocking oxygen from reaching the soil. Soil fungi thrive in wet conditions and attack oxygen-starved cassava tubers, causing root rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ mli ni amɛtutuaa ŋmei shishifãi ni bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms even when the stem is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi wa moŋ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; they have shallow root systems. When heavy fruit bunches weight down the top and rain softens the soil, strong wind can easily uproot the whole plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Beni aduawai ni tsii kpɛtɛɔ yitsei lɛ ahe ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie tsei muu fɛɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi amli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams refuse to sprout for several months after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ nyɔji babaoo beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. Internal plant chemicals prevent sprouting until this resting period ends, ensuring the seed yam only sprouts when the next rainy season approaches.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Tsofai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ shweremɔ naa kɛyashiɔ be ni nɛkɛ wɔɔhe nɛɛ baa naagbee. Enɛ ji koni akwɛ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ pɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ba.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes are usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with proper sprays or protective nets keeps the disease from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa loo tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the leaf and moves down the center in a V-shape means the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the plant's growth helps the leaves turn green again and grow strong cobs.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to protect itself and save water. Once the rains return, the plant will naturally sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ebu ehe ni ekɛ nu akafite. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baajɛ adebɔɔ mli ebaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 25 to 30 centimeters between individual plants ensures each stalk gets enough sunlight, water, and food from the soil without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Abɛi ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 75 ni ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from extreme sun heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during hot days helps the flowers stay on and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in three months, while cassava grows slowly over a full year. This allows you to harvest maize early while the cassava continues to use the space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ he lɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local diseases, withstand dry periods better, and yield more grain. Saved seeds lose their strength over time and often produce smaller harvests.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ fioo.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the plant roots absorb moisture before the afternoon sun heats up the soil, and wet leaves dry quickly in the sun, preventing leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani shwane hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ baagbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Koni akɛtsi fungal helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa

english: Why does my harvested maize get damaged by insects even when I put it inside a dry barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni egbi mli moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils attack maize if the grains still hold hidden moisture inside. Drying maize thoroughly in the sun until the kernels are very hard, and storing them in airtight bags, prevents pests from destroying the harvest.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa kɛji ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee mli lolo. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa Ni akɛwo vacuum kotoku mli lɛ baatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so when the soil runs out, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, bottom leaves to feed the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting groundnuts in my field help my soil for next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. This leaves natural fertilizer in the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When planted too close, cocoa trees fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Dense planting also stops air from flowing between trees, creating trapped dampness that causes black pod disease to spread quickly.
ga: Kɛ adu Cacao tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Nibii ni aduɔ babaoo lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Yam leaves need direct sun to make food through sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes spreads the leaves out to get maximum sun, which directs energy downward to build larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhoo kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaagbɛ efoji lɛ eshwa koni ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: If you leave too many suckers, they steal water and food from the main mother plant. Pruning away the extra suckers leaves just one or two shoots, ensuring the main tree has enough energy to grow big bunches.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ koni tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee kuu agbo.

english: The first rain of the season is often a false start, followed by several weeks of heat and dry weather. If you plant immediately, your seeds will sprout but then wither and die when the ground dries up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji otsii babaoo ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ba. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for a long time without draining properly. Wet soil starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and staying tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. These insects suck out plant juices, causing the leaves to twist and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of bees for pollination. When stressed by heat or water shortage, the plant sheds blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni baahã amɛfɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛji hulutsoo haomɔ loo nu ni faaa ba Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why are small green worms eating big holes through my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye buji wuji kɛmiitsɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those worms are caterpillars, the young offspring of the Diamondback moth. The moth lays eggs on the leaves, and when they hatch, the caterpillars feed aggressively on the cabbage leaves to grow.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmeii. ni ji diamondback ŋmei lɛ bii lɛ Ŋmei fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ amɛfɔ lɛ, Caterpillars lɛ kɛ ekãa yeɔ cabbage baai koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die if I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains provides a canopy that protects young seedlings from scorching and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni ashiɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the soil stays flooded after continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ sɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi lɛ?

english: When soil remains flooded for too long, air cannot reach the roots. Without air, the roots cannot absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stunt.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whitefly insects. The virus weakens the leaves so they cannot produce food properly, leading to smaller roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when stressed by sudden dry heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to spend its energy on growing big leaves instead of holding onto flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni mli egbi trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai wuji yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ.

english: How does plowing my land with a heavy tractor change the way crop roots grow deep into the ground?
ga: Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni akɛ traktɔi wuji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Plowing breaks up hard surface soil so roots can push down easily. However, running heavy machinery over wet soil can compact the layer underneath, creating a hard pan that roots cannot easily cross.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre lɛ shi mlɛo. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ afee mlɛo. Enɛ haa pan ni wa ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ afo mli mlɛo lɛ baa.

english: Why does placing fertilizer too close to my crop stems burn the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated chemical salts. When placed right next to stems, it pulls moisture out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them, causing the edges of the leaves to dry up and look burnt.
ga: Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ masɛi lɛ Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: Tomato plants roll their leaves inward during high temperatures to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and wind. This helps the plant slow down water loss through its leaves.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni nu ni amɛlaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce small, thin cobs when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with maize for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds are allowed to stay close to the crop, they steal the essential food the maize plant needs to form full cobs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa koni ekwɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mature yam tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in wet soil past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni eda lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: When mature yams sit in waterlogged soil for too long, lack of air and excessive moisture cause rot-causing fungi and bacteria to thrive, which damages the stored food inside the tuber.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ tara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ daa. ni fiteɔ niyenii ni ato yɛ yitso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods when I plant them late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas react strongly to changes in daylight hours and rainfall. Planting them at the wrong time of the year pushes the crop to keep producing leafy growth instead of triggering flowering and pod formation.
ga: Cowpea tsuɔ nii waa kɛji tsakemɔi ni ba yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli lɛ, ebaatsirɛ tso lɛ kɛya baai lɛ adalɛ babaoo nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ fɔɔ, nɛ e haa nɛ a peeɔ pod.

english: How do I know the exact right time to put fertilizer on my maize plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele tsei lɛ amli?

english: Maize plants need nutrients most when they are young and growing fast, usually two to three weeks after planting, and again when they start flowering. Applying fertilizer at these specific growth stages ensures the plant uses the nutrients to build strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa ŋmãa tsei fe fɛɛ beni amɛji gbekɛbii ni amɛdaraa oya, bei pii lɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni fɔfɔi jeɔ shishi lɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ be pɔtɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Should I place fertilizer directly at the root stem of my crops or further away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ loo kɛjɛ tso lɛ he?

english: You should place fertilizer in a small ring or hole a few centimeters away from the plant stem, never directly touching it. Direct contact can burn the stems, while putting it slightly away allows the roots to safely reach out and absorb nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. loo bu ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi ni okata he tɛ̃ɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishi. Shi kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fioo lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my crop growth slow down even after I apply fertilizer during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away fertilizer before the roots have a chance to drink it, a process known as leaching. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours so the plant gets the full benefit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ amɛnu. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi otsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ana sɛɛnamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I apply too much fertilizer to make them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Applying too much fertilizer builds up salts in the soil that can burn crop roots and turn leaf edges brown. Excess fertilizer can actually weaken or kill the plant and attract more insect pests.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ŋmeii buaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa, ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbe amɛ ni egbala tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kɛba.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are common signs of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. When a plant gets this virus, it cannot make food properly from sunlight, leading to stunted roots and a poor harvest.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ cassava mosaic hela he. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ tsei ná nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ Enyɛŋ ekɛ hulu la lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ hu ehiii.

english: What causes small holes to appear in my pepper plant leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper baai lɛ amli buji bibii? lɛ je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli

english: Small holes in leaves are usually caused by night-feeding pests like caterpillars or beetles. Identifying these insect attacks early allows you to protect the foliage so the plant can keep growing healthily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbɛkɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ ayɔsemɔ mra Ehaa obuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do when I see a single crop plant showing signs of severe disease in my field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina tso kome ni miitsɔɔ hela ni naa wa he okadi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should carefully uproot and remove the infected plant from your field immediately. Leaving a diseased plant in the farm allows wind, rain, or insects to spread the sickness to your remaining healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ oyale mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, loo kooloi bibii agbɛ hela amɛshwã oŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants look strong in the morning but wilt in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa leebi lɛ? Shi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it up during hot afternoons, causing temporary wilting. However, if the soil is wet and the plant stays droopy, it may be a sign of bacterial wilt or root disease.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ tee nɔ egbo lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ bacteria wilt loo shishifãi hela miiye.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my bean plants without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients like phosphorus. When a plant feels weak or stressed, it drops its flowers to conserve energy instead of producing seeds.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai tamɔ fɔsfɔs hao tsei lɛ. Beni tsei lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛgbɔjɔ loo amɛmiifee basaa. Ebaashɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo dumɔwui.

english: Why do my crops look pale green and grow slowly compared to other healthy fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves and slow growth usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps plants turn dark green and grow vigorously.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni eda waa.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted oil palm tree to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Oil palm trees usually start producing their first fruit bunches about 3 to 4 years after planting, and they can continue yielding fruit for over 25 to 30 years if given proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to prune old fronds from oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ mu tsei ahe baai momo lɛ?

english: Trimming away dead or lower fronds helps direct the plant's energy into developing fruit bunches, allows sunlight to reach the fruits, and prevents pests from hiding in the tree.
ga: Baai ni egboi loo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo. Ehaa hulu la shɛɔ aduawai lɛ ahe. ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee tsei lɛ amli.

english: Can I use leftover palm kernel waste or empty fruit bunches as fertilizer for my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso yibii ni eshwɛ loo aduawai akui ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, palm kernel cake and decomposed fruit bunches serve as rich organic matter that restores nutrients to the soil and helps retain soil moisture during dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso yibii keekii kɛ aduawai akui ni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do flowers drop off my crops before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall early when the plant undergoes stress, such as a sudden dry spell, extreme heat, pest infestation, or poor nutrient levels in the soil.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ be ni nu hɔmɔ baa trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛhe, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between young oil palm trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi mu tsei ateŋ?

english: Yes, while oil palm trees are small and their branches have not fully spread out, you can intercrop with short-term crops like cassava or maize to maximize land use and earn early income.
ga: Yes, even though the oil palm tree is small and the branches are not yet fully spread out, You can intercrop with short-term crops such as cassava or corn. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he fe fɛɛ ni aná shika mra.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa, ni no haa yibii bibii baa.

english: How do weeds affect the growth and yield of my main crops?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow rapidly and steal essential fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving your plants and reducing harvest quality.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I buy high-yielding seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Improved seed varieties are specially bred to fight off local diseases, tolerate dry conditions better, and produce much higher yields than seeds saved from regular harvests.
ga: Atsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni akpaa daa lɛ mli.

english: The first rain often heats up the soil without soaking deep enough. If a hot dry stretch follows, the seeds dry out and die before they can fully germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji ogbala mli kɛ la Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food leaves need to grow. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil and prevent the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa baa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu.

english: Why is it bad for me to put fertilizer directly against the main stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo pepper tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong, almost like salt. Placing it directly against the plant stem can burn the skin of the plant and damage its roots. It is safer to dig a small ring a few inches away from the stem and put the fertilizer there.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he wa waa, eshwɛ fioo ni ebaafee tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooofo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko. Okɛ inchi fioo komɛi awo tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Why does Striga weed keep growing near my maize and making the crop dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi ni ehaa mi ŋmãa lɛ miigbi lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots underground directly into your maize roots. It drinks the water and steals the food meant for your maize, causing the crop to look burnt and dry.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ŋmɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ o-corn shishifãi lɛ amli. Ebaanu nu ni ebaaju niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha o-corn lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many green leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in rich soil without enough phosphorus and potassium, it puts all its energy into making big leaves on top instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by dry weather or lack of shade. Flowers also drop if small flying insects called midges are not available to carry pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi hu shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a natural way for tomato plants to shield themselves from extreme heat. By curling up, the leaf shrinks its exposed surface area so it loses less water to the dry air.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tomato tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ he ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small fruits before they are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa

english: Young pepper fruits fall off when the plant undergoes stress from irregular watering, sudden high heat, or poor soil nutrients. The plant sheds the extra fruits it knows it cannot support with food and water.
ga: Pepper yibii bibii lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni ekɛhaaa lɛ daa lɛ miihao lɛ. hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine ni amɛle akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛna niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why do I need to leave enough space between my cassava stems when planting instead of placing them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ama amɛhe lɛ

english: Giving each cassava stem its own space ensures that the roots do not fight underground for water and soil nutrients. Proper spacing also allows sunlight to reach every plant so the tubers can grow large.
ga: Kɛ́ aha ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ewuuuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa hu haa hulu la shɛɔ tso fɛɛ tso he. koni yitso lɛ atsɔ agbo

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes elevates the leaves into the sunlight so they can manufacture food efficiently. It also keeps the leaves off the hot ground and improves air flow, preventing wet rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain stem for water, light, and fertilizer. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring your main plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why does my farm soil crack and become so hard when the weather gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli fãa ni ewaa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy clay soil loses all its moisture to heat, it shrinks and pulls apart, creating deep cracks. Adding dry leaves, crop leftovers, or animal manure into the soil helps it hold onto water so it stays soft and protects plant roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ emli nu fɛɛ yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbala mli. ni kɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ baa Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse, loo kooloi ashishifãi fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ nu mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe.

english: Why do my crops stop yielding well if I farm the same land every year without letting it rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji mitsuɔ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he nii afi fɛɛ afi ni mihaaa ejɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Farming the same soil repeatedly drains all its natural nutrients, leaving the dirt weak and exhausted. Planting leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the land so it recovers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ Ebaafite adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni eye ebua ni ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does rainwater wash away my topsoil and leave big gullies on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eshiɔ faai wuji yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: When land is cleared completely bare, heavy rains hit the dirt directly and carry away the rich upper soil. Planting crops across the slope or growing cover plants keeps the soil tied down so rain cannot wash it away.
ga: Beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baakpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Nugbɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afɔ lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass over my farm soil help my crops stay alive when rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Covering your soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, works like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the ground cool and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: How do I know the right time to put my seeds in the ground when the rains are late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant after just one short rainfall, because the ground underneath is still dry and seeds will spoil. Wait until heavy rain falls consistently over a few days so the deep soil is wet enough to support seed germination.
ga: Kaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ be kukuoo ko pɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishigbɛ he lɛ mli egbi lolo ni dumɔwui lɛ baagboi. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aya nɔ gbii fioo komɛi koni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: What will happen to my maize seeds if I plant them in dry soil and the rain delays for weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ otsii komɛi?

english: Seeds placed in dry, hot dirt will either rot from intense soil heat or get eaten by birds and ants before rain arrives. It is better to store seeds safely indoors until the rainy season firmly establishes.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baagboi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ mli. Aloo okpoi kɛ ŋmeii aye bo dani nugbɔ lɛ aba. Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ato shĩa mli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do strong storm winds blow down my tall maize plants right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Tall crops fall over easily if their root systems are shallow or if the soil around their base is loose. Banking soil firmly around the stems of your plants as they grow gives them strong support against heavy winds.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishi lɛ mli etse. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni atswaa shi shiŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and look wilted during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves during peak afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, saving internal water. Once the sun cools down in the evening, the leaves usually stretch back out.
ga: Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni haa nu hiɔ mli Kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Baai lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn brown and dry during the Harmattan season even when there are no insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Harmattan winds carry very dry air that sucks water directly out of crop leaves faster than roots can draw moisture from the soil. Keeping soil mulched and wet helps protect plants from drying out during this season.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli tɛ̃ɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ be nɛɛ mli.
