english: Why do the flowers and tiny fruits fall off my trees when sudden strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii Koni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa trukaa waa lɛ?

english: Strong winds violent shake tree branches and stress plants, causing them to shed delicate flowers to save energy. Planting boundary trees like teak or cassia around your farm creates a windbreak that shields your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa tswaa tsei kɛ tsei aniji anɔ, ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ koni akɛbaa hewalɛ. Husu tsei tamɔ teak loo cassia ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baa.

english: Does it matter which way I point the cassava stem when I plant it in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ otsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, you must plant the cassava stem with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant it upside down, the shoots will struggle to reach the surface, leading to weak plants and a low harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni odu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ Shoots lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight to make food for the tuber growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot, wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping tubers grow much bigger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awó amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu lɛ ajie amɛ kpo koni amɛná niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai akabote hei ni mli edɔ ni edɔ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main tree. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Egbɛfaŋnɔ ji ni eju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ baaná plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Yellowing in the center of maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the roots will help them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛbɔle Shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly even when there is heavy rain in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Too much heavy rain can wash away nutrients from the soil or flood the ground, drowning plant roots so they cannot breathe. Creating raised beds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely while keeping the soil fertile.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛmuɔ. Saji loo ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because it scorches their leaves and dries them out. Leaving some tall trees or planting plantains nearby provides necessary shade while the young cocoa roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ ebaashã ni ebaaha baai lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, which often happens when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the roots absorb the calcium needed to build healthy tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Water your plants consistently during hot periods to help the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Ha tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni eye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Young crops have small roots and easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops the best chance to establish themselves strongly.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ mlɛo koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkɛto shihilɛ ni mli wa shishi.

english: How do insects get into my harvested dried corn even when I store it in clean bags?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii boteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ kotoku ni mli tse mli moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs are often laid inside the corn grains while the crop is still in the field before harvest. Drying your corn thoroughly in the sun and using proper grain protection treatments destroys these hidden eggs before they hatch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii awoɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo dani akpaa. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ dani amɛfɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes like beans or groundnuts in rotation puts nutrients back into the soil to keep leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo ni aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil solution or insecticidal soap early helps stop these pests from damaging the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and drying up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shady conditions. Pruning extra cocoa branches to let sunlight in and regularly removing affected pods stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɔ́, kɛ shade tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo niji krokomɛi koni hulu la babaoo aba mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ daa koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if fall armyworms are attacking my young maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji cutworms miitutua mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms feed inside the central funnel of young maize plants, leaving ragged holes in leaves and whitish, sawdust-like droppings. Checking your fields early in the morning helps you spot them early before severe damage happens.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ. Amɛshiɔ bu ni etsilɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaaha ona amɛ mra. dani nɔ ko ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli baafite

english: Why does my tomato plant drop its blossoms without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when air temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch protects the plant from stress and helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ haomɔ he, ni ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines die off early before the tubers are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gboɔ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Early vine death can happen if the plant lacks strong support stakes, suffers from fungal leaf spot, or gets attacked by beetles. Staking vines early allows leaves to catch sunlight and produce food to feed the growing tubers underground.
ga: Wein tso lɛ gbele baanyɛ aba mra kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nɔ ko ni fiɔ esɛɛ waa. Fungal leaf spot hela ni yeɔ mɔ awui. loo ladybugs tutuaa Wein tsei ni aduɔ mra Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni amɛwoɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce a cluster of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Plantains need lots of food and water to fruit quickly. If you allow too many side suckers to grow around one main stem, they compete for nutrients, which delays fruiting; pruning down to one or two strong suckers speeds up growth.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ewo yibii oya. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni sɛɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa aduawai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ dalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Wait until the soil receives steady rain that penetrates deep into the ground rather than planting right after the first light rain shower. Planting in well-moistened soil ensures seeds germinate quickly and do not dry out.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ ɔ se amlɔ nɔuu. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, holds moisture in the soil so you water less often, stops weeds from taking over, and keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant moves what little it has from the older bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of big green leaves but only produce small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? shi eyɛ yitso bibioo yɛ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and thick foliage instead of sending energy down to build big starch-filled roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse. Mohu ɔ, a haa he wami kɛ baa si konɛ e kɛ pee sisi agbohi nɛ a mi mi ɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young yam vines as soon as they start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu mi sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɔ pɛ.

english: Young yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for forming tubers underground. Tall weeds shadow the vines and steal moisture and nutrients from the soil, causing the yam roots to stay thin.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejuɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee bibioo.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants before any fruits form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly between very dry and very wet. Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to shed flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ.

english: Upward curling pepper leaves are often caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from under the leaves, or by intense heat causing the leaf to fold to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, cabbage leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up. The leaves wilt to reduce their surface area and save moisture, usually standing back up in the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Cabbage baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: How does using a heavy tractor to plow my wet field hurt my crop growth?
ga: Te traktɔ agbo ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ miŋmɔji ni efɔ lɛ amli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Plowing wet soil with a heavy tractor squashes the soil particles tightly together, creating a hard underground layer. This hard layer stops crop roots from spreading easily and prevents rainwater from sinking into the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛ trakta agbo tsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ tsũ ko ni wa baa. Nɛkɛ fã ni wa nɛɛ haaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya, ni ehaaa nugbɔ nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into narrow strips when there is strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split along their natural veins during windy conditions to allow air to pass through easily. This prevents the strong winds from snapping the main stem or blowing the entire plant over.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛfeɔ fãji yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akakumɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ loo ekatswa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shi.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping their small pods during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees drop small pods during dry spells to protect themselves from dying of thirst. Sacrificing the small pods helps the main tree save water and survive until the rains return.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni obu ohe kɛjɛ kumai he. Shaa pod bibioo ko afɔle Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ he ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmeii ni midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special natural microbes on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free nutrients behind for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Eshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ koni eye.

english: Why does handling fertilizers without protection make me or my farm workers sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni abuuu he lɛ haa mi loo miŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ yeɔ hela lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain strong chemical nutrients that can irritate your skin, eyes, and lungs. Breathing in fertilizer dust or touching it with bare hands allows these chemicals to enter your body, causing headaches, skin rashes, stomach pain, or respiratory problems.
ga: Tsofai ni haa mɔ he waa ni baanyɛ aha hewolo, hiŋmɛii, kɛ fɛ̃i mli afu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ mɔ ko miimu ŋmɔshi nibii amli sũ loo ekɛ eniji ni bɛ nɔ ko taa he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofai nɛɛ abote gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli. ekɛ yitsoŋ hela baa Hewolo nɔ tsɔi, musu mli piŋmɔ, loo mumɔ mli naagbai

english: Why should I wash my hands and change my clothes immediately after applying fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ miniji ahe ni matsake atadei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer residue stays on your skin and clothes long after you finish working. Washing removes these harmful chemicals so you do not accidentally swallow them while eating or transfer them to your family at home.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ ohewolo kɛ otadei anɔ be kakadaŋŋ beni oshi nitsumɔ sɛɛ. He ni ooofɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ tsofai nɛɛ wooo ohe yɛ oshara mli beni oyeɔ nii loo okɛhaa owekumɛi yɛ shia.

english: How far should I keep stored fertilizer away from my family's cooking area and drinking water?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-fertilizer ni mikɛto lɛ ato he ni miweku lɛ hoɔ nii yɛ kɛ he ni amɛnuɔ nii yɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: Always store fertilizers in a separate, dry shed away from food and water sources. Chemical dust or spills can easily drift into drinking water or meal preparation areas, leading to severe chemical poisoning for your household.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, too ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he ko ni egbi, ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ niyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhei ahe. Muji loo tsofai ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nu ni anuɔ loo hei ni asaa niyenii yɛ lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa tsofai fɔji ni naa wa baa oshia lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I reuse empty fertilizer bags to store harvested food crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ nɔ ko mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ kɛtoɔ niyenii ni akpa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Empty fertilizer bags hold chemical residues deep within their fibers even if they look clean. Storing food crops inside these bags contaminates your harvest, making the food unsafe and toxic for your family and customers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kotokui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ hiɛɔ tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ tsɔji lɛ amli shɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse po. Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kotokui nɛɛ amli lɛ baafite nibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehaa oweku lɛ kɛ mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ yeɔ awui.

english: Why do my crops dry up and burn when I place fertilizer too close to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts. When placed directly against a plant's stem or roots, the fertilizer pulls moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it, causing the leaves to dry up and burn.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ akɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger and produce more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the soil, supplying key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. These nutrients help crops build strong roots, grow green leaves, and produce larger, healthier fruits and grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa. dumɔ baai eŋɔli ni ewo aduawai kɛ ŋmaa ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe dani ahum ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away from your crop roots before the plants can absorb it. This wastes your money and causes the chemicals to run off into local streams where people drink water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tso shishifãi amli dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ. Enɛ heɔ shika ni ehaa tsofai shwieɔ maŋ lɛ mli faai ni gbɔmɛi nuɔ nu yɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves still turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops turn yellow when they receive the wrong type of fertilizer, too little water, or too much fertilizer that burns the roots. Roots damaged by improper fertilizer application cannot absorb nutrients effectively.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa. nine shɛ nu fioo tsɔ nɔ Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he ni eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Shishifãi ni fɔmɔ nii ni ejaaa efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can involving women in specific farming activities help increase our total household income?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ yei ni akɛaawo okwaayeli nitsumɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli lɛ baanyɛ aha shika fɛɛ ni oshia lɛ náa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Women play a vital role in planting, weeding, crop processing, and marketing. Organizing farm tasks together allows your family to manage larger field areas, reduce crop waste after harvest, and earn higher profits at the market.
ga: Yei tsuɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ ko ni he hiaa he nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. weeding Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ kɛ jarayeli Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa oweku lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ ŋmɔji babaoo nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ nibii ni afiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ jara nɔ.

english: What kind of fast-growing crops can women in my home cultivate to support family meals and income?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yei ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ baanyɛ adu koni amɛkɛha amɛwekui lɛ niyenii kɛ shika?

english: Vegetables like pepper, okra, garden eggs, and leafy greens are ideal because they grow quickly, require less land clearing, and provide both nutritious food for the home and frequent income from local sales.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii, okra, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya. Ebiɔ ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii babaoo ni ekɛ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli aha shia lɛ kɛ shika ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ shii abɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Heavy rain fills all the open soil spaces with water, starving the roots of oxygen and encouraging water mold fungi that turn the tubers soft and rotten.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ ni kã shi lɛ nɔ yi obɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots even when I keep them stored in a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams have a natural internal timer called dormancy. After resting for a few months after harvest, the tuber naturally breaks dormancy and uses its stored energy to push out new shoots for the next growing season.
ga: Atomɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli be he ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bulbs lɛ fiteɔ shihilɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsiɔ tsei heei kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen nutrient, or waterlogging from recent rains is preventing the roots from absorbing the food already in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu ni nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ ni jɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ mli ekã shi yɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop covered in ragged holes overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe baai lɛ ha ŋmeii amli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in maize leaves are a standard sign of fall armyworm caterpillars, which crawl into the central leaves during the day to hide and chew aggressively on the plant at night.
ga: Buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa ni egbee shi lɛ he. ni shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli koni ekɛtee ni ekɛye tso lɛ waa gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants bend and fall flat on the ground just when the heads are ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛmli ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over—a problem called lodging—when heavy rain or wind pushes against heavy grain heads, especially if the crop received too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the lower stems tall and weak.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbee shi - naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ shĩa - kɛji nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa omɔ tsei lɛ waa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop tiny young pods before they can mature into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛbii bibii lɛ? Dani pod lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Small cocoa pods shrivel and turn black through a natural process called cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree naturally sheds extra fruit it cannot supply with enough water and energy.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei jieɔ yibii ni fa fe nine yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have huge leaves that lose water very quickly in intense sun. Drooping and rolling up is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce its surface area exposed to heat and preserve stem moisture.
ga: Plantain yɛ baai agboi ni kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Foliation kɛ curling ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni ajie ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulutsoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni aha tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when hot weather or dry soil stresses the plant, making the flower's pollen sticky or inactive so fertilization cannot take place to form a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi miiha tso lɛ miifee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi loo etsuuu nii. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ fɔ awo mli ni efee tomato.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into tight cups and stop growing wider?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by insects that disrupt normal plant cell growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ thrips loo mites. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ tso mli wala yibii lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cowpea roots have small round bumps on them, and are they harming my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Those bumps are root nodules filled with beneficial soil bacteria. Far from harming the plant, they collect nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into free plant food, naturally fertilizing your soil.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji shishifãi ni eyi obɔ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Amɛbuaa nitrogen gas naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni amɛyeee tsei lɛ awui. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because strong heat dries out their shallow roots and burns their young leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava creates a cool, moist environment that keeps cocoa seedlings alive until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ejaakɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Egbiɔ ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: What type of plantain suckers should I dig up from an old farm to plant a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: You should pick 'sword suckers'—the young shoots that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a broad base underground. These shoots grow faster, establish stronger roots, and produce bigger bunches of plantains compared to 'water suckers' that have broad leaves early on.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tseee ni tamɔ lance, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ da yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni efee plantains kuu ko ni da kɛ akɛto ‘nu-nu-nu-ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip down the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the leaf and moves down the central leaf rib is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers, like Urea or well-rotted animal manure, helps the plant build healthy green leaves and strong stems.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize seeds after the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the ground receives two or three steady, heavy rains that soak deep into the soil. Sowing seeds after the very first light rain is risky because a dry spell right after can dry out and kill the germinating seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ daa enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ yɛ oshara. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ no sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Always plant cassava cuttings with the growth buds or nodes pointing upward toward the sky, placed slightly slanting or straight down into the soil. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downward first, which weakens the plant and reduces your harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Okɛwo he ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo loo odu yɛ shikpɔŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛya shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha kpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight and off the wet ground. When leaves get maximum sunlight, they manufacture more energy to produce large tubers underground, while keeping leaves away from moisture prevents rotting diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo nɔ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya ŋwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ ŋmɔtɔ he koni amɛkafite.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. When the groundnut roots decay in the dirt, they feed the surrounding soil and supply free nitrogen to your maize crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko aha o-ŋmei tsei lɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects attack my cowpea crop mostly when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ babaoo beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ?

english: Pests like flower thrips and pod borers are naturally drawn to cowpea flowers because they feed on the sweet nectar and tender blossom tissues. Inspecting your field early and spraying recommended organic or chemical treatments right at the flowering stage saves your crop from major damage.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers lɛ ji mɛi ni sumɔɔ cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ amɛyeɔ fɔfɔi amli nu kɛ fɔfɔi amli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that shields the earth from harsh sun. It stops water from evaporating quickly, keeps root systems cool, and prevents weeds from popping up and stealing plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaje kpo ni amɛju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do the yellow blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of bee activity for pollination. Giving plants steady moisture at the soil level and avoiding overhead watering helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ pollination mli lɛ Kɛ́ tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie nu ni akɛhaa amɛyiteŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni wa.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees like plantain along with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains kɛfata mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and keeping moisture in the soil while the crop gets established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni aduɔ tsei lɛ.

english: How long will my new cocoa trees take from planting before I see pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi cacao tso hee lɛ baajie pods kpo?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually start bearing pods in 3 to 5 years. However, modern hybrid varieties introduced by extension programs can start producing fruit in as little as 2 to 3 years if given proper water and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli. Shi, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛwoɔ nibii amli lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help indicating that the plant lacks important nutrients in the soil, like nitrogen, or that the soil is either too dry or holding too much water around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers want me to cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ miitao ni afolɔ kookoo niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the center of the tree so sunlight and fresh air can pass through. This keeps dampness away, reduces fungal diseases, and helps the tree direct its strength into growing bigger pods instead of extra leafy branches.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ hela aba shi, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewaje etsitsii wuji lɛ moŋ fe ni eeená niji ni yɔɔ baai babaoo.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn completely black and dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in wet and shady conditions. Removing infected pods immediately and keeping weeds low prevents the moisture that spreads the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni aha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How do the tiny flowers growing on my cocoa tree trunk actually turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fɔfɔi bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ kookoo ŋmɔji?

english: Very tiny, beneficial insects called midges visit the small flowers to feed and carry pollen from flower to flower. Once pollinated, the flower grows into a tiny pod called a cherelle, which eventually matures into a full pod.
ga: kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ saraa fɔfɔi bibii lɛ. Koni ekɛ niyenii aha ni ekɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli Kɛji akɛ pollen wo mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaada ni etsɔ pod ni eyi obɔ

english: Why are many of the small, young pods on my cocoa tree shriveling up and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mikoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: This shedding is often called cherelle wilt. It happens naturally when the tree produces more pods than it has energy, water, or nutrients to feed, so it drops some to protect the remaining fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Ebaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso ko wo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ, nu, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, fertilizer, and groundwater directly from your crop's roots. Keeping the farm floor clean ensures your trees get all the food and water available while removing hiding spots for harmful pests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why is my old cocoa farm giving me fewer pods now than it gave me years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoe ŋmɔ momo lɛ haa mi pods fioo fe bɔ ni ekɛha mi afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow beyond 25 to 30 years old, their natural strength declines, branches become woody, and roots absorb nutrients less effectively. Old trees require careful pruning, soil feeding, or gradual replanting to restore production.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Niji lɛ baatsɔ tsei. ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii fioo ko Tsei momo biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ fiofio koni ekɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow on the main trunk instead of out on the leafy branches like other fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ moŋ fe niji ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ aduawai tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are very heavy and filled with wet seeds. Growing directly on the sturdy trunk and thick limbs gives the tree the structural support it needs to hold heavy fruit without snapping thin branches.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ amli tsii ni dumɔwui ni efɔ eyi mli obɔ. Tso lɛ ni edaa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ náa yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa koni enyɛ ehiɛ aduawai ni tsii ni efoŋ niji bibii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and leaves are delicate. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain around them blocks the harsh heat and keeps humidity in the soil so the young trees can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ amɛbaai ni waaa lɛ ahewɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plant before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: When heat gets too high or watering is irregular, the pepper plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to protect itself and conserve energy rather than trying to feed developing fruit.
ga: Beni la lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rain falls continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Continuous heavy rain fills all the tiny soil air pockets with water, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rot to spread quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tee nɔ eba, ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku bibioo ko ba. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Why do my yam vines grow very big green leaves but produce only tiny yams underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai ni dara waa lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii bibii pɛ afeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the yam plant uses all its energy to grow leaves and vines above the ground instead of sending energy down to build heavy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeetsu lɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Crowding seeds together forces the young plants to compete for the same sunlight, space, and soil food. They stretch upward quickly to reach light, resulting in tall, weak stems and small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛmiimii amɛhe lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, he ko, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable plants stop growing and turn pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-vegetables lɛ miikpa kwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have stronger roots and grow faster than most vegetables. They steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crop, leaving the vegetables starved.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe aduawai babaoo. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. ni haa hɔmɔ yeɔ aduawai

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil quickly if I leave them in the sun after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛji mishi yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes produce a natural gas called ethylene that makes them ripen. Sun heat speeds up this natural gas production and break-down process, causing the fruit to soften and rot rapidly.
ga: Tomatoi jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni haa amɛshwereɔ. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli la ni ji gas lɛ feɔ oya, ni ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ oya.

english: Why do small insects appear inside my sealed sacks of stored maize after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele kotokui ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevil eggs often hide inside the grain while still on the farm. If the maize is not dried completely before bagging, the warm, moist conditions inside the sack cause the eggs to hatch into insects that eat the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii awoɔ dumɔwui amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani awo kotoku mli Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and non-woody stems. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs physical support from propping poles to prevent the stem from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni jeee tsei. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Tso lɛ hu baafee tsii ni ebaabi gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ sɛɛfimɔ tsei amli koni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ akakumɔ loo eshishifã.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my corn plants turn yellow and die while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: As the corn plant forms cobs, it automatically moves stored food like nitrogen from its oldest bottom leaves up to feed the growing grain at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fee ŋmãa Ejieɔ niyenii ni ato, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK, or improving soil drainage, helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛbaafata he loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Jiemɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing excess suckers and leaving only one or two allows the mother tree to give all its energy to producing a heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ haa ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and lack of water. Controlling whiteflies with sticky traps or insecticidal sprays and keeping soil moist helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli Akɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akudɔɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ mli kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays saturated with water for long periods because the roots cannot breathe and fungi easily attack them. Harvesting at maturity before heavy rainfall prevents tuber decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni ŋmeii tutuaa amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛdara kwraa dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni bulb lɛ akafite.

english: Why do most of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers when they experience water stress, nutrient shortages, or lack of pollination by small midges. Proper shade control and soil moisture help the tree retain flowers and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu faaa yɛ amɛmli, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, loo ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ amɛmli lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. Kɛ́ akudɔ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high, soil moisture drops sharply, or the soil lacks nutrients like calcium. Regular watering and mulching keep the root environment cool and steady.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baa shi oya. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using wood sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso atsu nii ni mikɛjie mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to light and keeping them safe from rot and ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ la awo mli ni obu he kɛjɛ fitemɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How do groundnut plants produce nuts underground after flowering above the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After the yellow flowers on top of the groundnut plant are pollinated, the plant sends down long stems called pegs into the soil. Once inside the soil, the tips expand to form groundnut pods.
ga: Beni ekɛ fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ewo mli sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ tsuɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Naa lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my swamp rice seeds fail to sprout if the water in my field is too deep at planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi marsh rice dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: Rice seeds require oxygen from the air to germinate properly. Deep standing water smothers the seeds before shoots can reach the surface, so fields should be kept moist rather than deeply flooded during early planting.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baajɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ miɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni oooha nu afua ni mli kwɔ aba mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large open leaves without forming tight heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ daa ni efeɔ baai agboi ni egbele ni efeee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when there is too much nitrogen causing leafy growth or when temperatures are too hot. Balanced fertilization and planting in cooler months encourage the plant to fold its leaves tightly.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ ajie eyitso kɛji nitrogen babaoo haa baa lɛ daa loo kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli jogbaŋŋ ni adu yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ abɔle shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is that large watering machine I see on big commercial farms, and how does it help crops grow better than relying on rain?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɔnei wuji ni akɛ nu woɔ mli ni minaa yɛ jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ?

english: That machine is called a center pivot irrigation system. It spreads water evenly across crops on a scheduled basis, ensuring plants get steady moisture even during dry seasons so they do not wither or rely only on rain.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsɔne lɛ akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Ejaraa nu lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fɛɛ yɛ be ni ato lɛ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli po. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gbooo loo amɛdamɔɔɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ.

english: If I get a motorized water pump to draw water to my farm, is it safe to water my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ nu pɔmp ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni mikɛwoɔ nu mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: It is best to water crops early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering under the hot mid-day sun causes most of the water to evaporate quickly before the roots can soak it up, and it can heat up the soil too much.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ tsɔ

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun is very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo amɛmli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense to trap moisture inside and reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing the plant from losing too much water during extreme heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba mli ni ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my vegetable crops are dying from too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-vegetables lɛ miigboi yɛ nu babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa hewɔ?

english: If crops lack water, their leaves wilt, feel dry, or turn brown at the edges. If they get too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow, the roots rot because they cannot breathe, and the surrounding soil stays soggy and smelly.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ baagboi, amɛbaanu he akɛ amɛgbi, loo amɛbaatsɔ asarasu yɛ amɛnaa. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaafu.

english: How can I easily check if my farm soil has enough moisture before deciding whether to water my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa dani makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu loo mawooo amɛ nu?

english: Push a finger or a small stick about two inches deep into the soil. If the stick comes out dry and dusty, your crops need water; if damp soil clings to it, there is still enough moisture for the plants.
ga: Okɛ oniji loo tso bibioo ko atsu nii. Tsɔ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi enyɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ aniji lɛ egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia onibii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around the base of their crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (called mulching) shades the ground from direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and keeps moisture in the ground much longer for the roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops when the farm soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofa baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve so crop roots can safely drink them in. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil concentrates the chemicals and can burn or scorch the crop roots, damaging the plant.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afee ekome ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo eshã tsei shishifãi. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ

english: What crops can I plant during the dry season if I do not have an artificial watering system on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli? Kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛfee lɛ bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Deep-rooted or drought-tolerant crops like cassava, cowpeas, or sorghum are ideal for dry periods because they can reach deep water pockets underground or survive on very little rainfall compared to leafy vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe loo amɛhi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ kɛ akɛto aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ahe.

english: Why do tomato plants need full direct sunlight, while my young cocoa seedlings die if they do not have shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la he hiaa tomato tsei tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gboɔ ni ebɛ hulutsoo.

english: Different crops have different light needs. Tomatoes need full sun to produce strong flowers and fruit, while tender young cocoa trees burn easily in intense sunlight and need temporary shade trees to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ kane he hiamɔ nii sɔrɔtoi. Tomato he miihia hulu ni fa kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛha tomatoi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I use the exact same knapsack sprayer to apply liquid fertilizer that I previously used to kill weeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi ni ji nu ni mikɛyeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii?

english: It is safer to use separate sprayers. If weedkiller residue remains in the sprayer, even a small trace mixed with your fertilizer can damage or kill your crops when sprayed on them.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi baatsu nii. Kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tee nɔ ehi tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ Nibii bibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli lɛ po baanyɛ afite loo efite oŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly full of holes and covered in small dirt-like powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai eyi kɛ bu ni sũ bibii ni tamɔ muji ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: That powder is waste left behind by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These pests hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day and eat the soft leaves, which can ruin the crop if you do not apply recommended control measures early.
ga: Pauda lɛ ji jwɛi ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ tsuuu nii mra.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow in a V-shape and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ, V-shaped, ni egbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tip of lower leaves means your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help replenish the soil.
ga: Yellow ni jɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is making the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and show light green and yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni haa yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It prevents the cassava from making food properly, resulting in small roots, so it is best to plant disease-resistant cassava stems.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Etsiɔ cassava naa koni ekahoo jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi bibii No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up into tight tubes during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn leaves roll up like straws to protect themselves from losing too much water when the air gets hot and dry. By rolling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the harsh sun.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi koni akɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛji okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu la fioo pɛ baashɛ baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when daytime temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Steady watering and light shade during extreme heat help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant cowpeas or beans before planting my main crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the bean plants decay, they leave behind free plant food that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni ŋmei tso lɛ miifite lɛ Eshiɔ tso niyenii yɛ esɛɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots even while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli po lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally rest for a few months after harvest. When their resting period ends, they use the food stored inside the tuber to sprout green shoots for the next planting season.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii eŋɔli kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does leaving tall weeds around my cassava reduce the size of the roots under the ground?
ga: jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crop. When cassava has to compete with weeds, it spends all its energy fighting for survival instead of building big, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Beni esa akɛ ŋmei kɛ jwɛi abɔ akaŋ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwu koni ehi shi. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsɔwi nguahi nɛ a he wa ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking, twisting, and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ, amɛmiitsɔ, ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus they transmit. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from curling up and stopping plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni ebaatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain of the season often heats up dry soil without soaking deep enough, and it is usually followed by a hot dry spell. Seeds need steady moisture to sprout, so planting too early exposes them to heat and dry soil, causing them to rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. ni bei pii lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni mli egbi lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Dumɔwui he miihia hulutsoo be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná dɔlɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point the stem when sticking cassava cuttings into the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the new shoots have to bend around to grow up, wasting energy and resulting in weak plants with fewer tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Esa akɛ abɔle ŋmeii heei koni amɛkwɛ̃. Hewalɛ ni efiteɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebɛ ŋmeii fioo.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from hot sunlight. It keeps the earth cool, traps moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa je lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts improves the soil for next season's maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmãa ni abaadu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny nodes on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that natural plant food stays behind in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛji okpa lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die if I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. Big trees provide shade like an umbrella, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist during their first few years of growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to cut long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ? Koni eha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which travels down the stem to build larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Enɛ fãa gbɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: A single plantain stem produces many small shoots called suckers around its base. If you do not remove extra suckers, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, leaving less energy for big bunches.
ga: Plantain tso kome pɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he. Kɛji ojieee ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa hewalɛ faaa kɛhaa kuu agbo ko.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the soil is running low on nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant lacks food, it drains nutrients from its old bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the sap. Removing these pests restores healthy, flat leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil damp with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from heat and retains soil moisture until the trees are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ baa. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves toward the sun to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil to prevent rotting and ensures the plant catches enough sunlight to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛhoo. Staking haa tso lɛ baa lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ekafite, ni ehaa tso lɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the crop needs to grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and produce bigger corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ waa yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do some extension officers recommend planting cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo beans yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-corn lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. Planting them with maize naturally enriches the soil so the maize gets free nutrients to grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon but look healthy again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the dry soil. Drooping is their natural way of reducing surface area to save water until the evening cool arrives.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Drooping ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi koni akɛto nu he kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Covering the soil, also called mulching, keeps the ground cool under the hot sun and traps water so it doesn't evaporate quickly. It also stops weeds from taking over and stealing food from your tomato plants.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni ehiɛ nu mli koni ekatsɔ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi akaye nɔ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too high, when the soil stays too dry, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the healthy branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can flow through the branches. This prevents moisture from getting trapped, which reduces fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa shi, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with weak stems and very small or missing corn cobs.
