ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu feɔ bibii waa loo amɛbɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to swell and crack open as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and need shade to grow well. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa protects the young plants from direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and helps them retain moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: How does spreading dry leaves and grass around the base of my pepper plants help them stay healthy during dry periods?
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around plants with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps moisture in the soil, protects plant roots from hot weather, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni okɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Buu tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off before the corn stalks fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Will I harvest more corn if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the same row?
ga: Ani makpaa ŋmãa babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year when I keep planting maize on the exact same plot without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lolo ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nutrients back into the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake o-ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing yellowish patches instead of staying flat and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural extension services is the best way to keep your farm safe.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Agricultural Extension Agency lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing lots of tall green branches and leaves but failing to grow flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: When tomato plants receive too much nitrogen or grow bushy without proper trimming, they direct all their energy into leafy growth instead of fruit. Trimming extra suckers allows the plant to focus energy on producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni afolɔɔɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi amli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni ekɛbaa lɛ he nii.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds right after the very first shower of rain in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall is often followed by a dry hot spell that can dry out the soil and kill freshly germinated seeds. Waiting until the major rains are established ensures the soil stays consistently moist for young roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha shishifãi bibii.

english: Why does a grafted mango seedling bear fruit much sooner than a mango tree I plant directly from a seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa fe mango tsei ni mikɛdu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A seed grows slowly from infancy, taking many years to reach reproductive age. A grafted seedling combines a strong root base with a branch taken from a mature fruit-producing tree, allowing it to yield fruit within two to three years.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo. Kɛjɛ be mli ni miji abifao Ni eheɔ afii babaoo dani mishɛɔ fɔmɔ afii ahe. Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa kɛ tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni edara ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ekome. Koni enyɛ ewo yibii yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop mold and turn powdery white after I store it inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsɔɔ powda yɛŋ beni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mold grows when maize is stored before it is completely dry inside. Sun-drying your corn until the kernels are hard and crisp before bagging prevents fungal growth and keeps grain safe for long-term storage.
ga: Mold lɛ daa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa yɛ emli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains planted nearby to provide shelter, excessive heat and lack of moisture cause the leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, dumɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhiɔ. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They feed on young leaves inside the crop's growing point, which weakens the plant and reduces grain yields if not spotted and managed early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa dumɔwui ni baa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ anaaa lɛ mra ni atsaaa lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites. As they feed on the underside of leaves, they damage the leaf structure and can spread viral diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, kɛ amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛfiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why does Striga weed keep growing around my maize plants and causing them to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ?

english: Striga, also known as witchweed, is a parasitic plant that attaches its roots directly to maize roots to steal water and nutrients. It thrives in poor, low-nutrient soil, so adding manure or rotating crops helps suppress it.
ga: Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed lɛ ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Eshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpai bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni mawo ŋmɔshi nibii dani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Signs of tired soil include pale or yellowish crop leaves, slow growth, and poor yields from previous harvests. Adding organic manure or compost helps rebuild the soil's natural nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji tso baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii ni jɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts improves the soil for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay in the ground, they release this nitrogen, providing free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli beni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kpo. akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainfall drain away from the root zone, preventing rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei loo gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa

english: Why do I need to put stakes or wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei loo tsei awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food for the plant, which leads to larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers, but the flowers fall off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer is used, which causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, loo kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Allowing too many shoot suckers to grow forces them to compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Leaving only two or three strong suckers ensures the main stem yields a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains babaoo.

english: How can I tell if the first rainfall of the season is enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: You should wait until the soil is consistently moist a few inches deep across several days. Planting immediately after just one heavy rain can ruin your seeds if the weather goes dry right afterward.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, aaafee 2-3 inches, gbii babaoo. Nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa kome sɛɛ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Is it possible to know early in the season whether my crops will yield well by harvest time?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ale mra yɛ be lɛ mli kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ be shɛ ni abaakpa nii?

english: While exact harvest size cannot be guaranteed early on, strong early root development, uniform seedling growth, and consistent rain in the first month are reliable early indicators of a good crop.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ bɔ ni kpamɔ lɛ dalɛ ji pɔtɛɛ ha mra moŋ. Shi shishifãi ni wa ni yaa hiɛ yɛ mra be mli dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ mli Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji mra be mli nɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai eba.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills all the air spaces in the soil with water, which suffocates the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they fail to absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen, making the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does sudden heavy rain affect seeds that I have just sown in the ground?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ saa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy downpours can wash light seeds away or push them too deep into the soil. Rain can also pack the top layer of dirt tightly, making it hard for young sprouts to break through.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ loo ekɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ. Nugbɔ baanyɛ amɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hu. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei bibii akɛ amɛaabote mli.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants whenever a heavy downpour occurs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy raindrops can physically knock fragile blossoms off the stem. High humidity and wet flowers also prevent pollen from transferring properly, causing unpollinated flowers to drop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atswa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɔfɔi ni efɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ pollen lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ he kroko jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall during long rainy periods but produce small fruit or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli shi amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii loo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: When there is excess water combined with low sunlight, crops spend all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of developing flowers, pods, or grain heads.
ga: Beni nu babaoo yɔɔ ni hulu la fioo pɛ fata he lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ fɔfɔi, ŋmɔtɔ, aloo du yihi.

english: What simple steps can I take to stop heavy rainwater from washing away my topsoil and plants?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Creating soil ridges or mounds across slopes helps slow down running water. Planting cover crops also holds the soil together with their roots, allowing rainwater to soak in safely.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋkpɔ ko ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ fioo. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Should I apply fertilizer on my farm while heavy rain is actively falling?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: No, applying fertilizer during active rainfall causes the water to carry the nutrients away before plant roots can drink them, which wastes your money and effort.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii yaa dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baafite shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Which basic crops survive best if a rainy season brings far more water than usual?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee tsei baahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ nu babaoo ba fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Crops like rice and certain varieties of cocoyam perform well in waterlogged soils, whereas root crops like cassava or legumes like cowpeas easily rot in excess water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ kookoo henɔi komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tamɔ tsina ŋmei fiteɔ oya kɛji nu fa babaoo.

english: What happens to my harvested crops if rain falls on them while they are drying outside?
ga: Mɛni baa mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Wet conditions cause damp harvested crops to attract mold and fungi quickly, which spoils the grain or tubers and makes them unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Enɛ baafite dumɔwui loo ŋmeii lɛ. ni ehaa ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deep into the ground away from roots, requiring nitrogen fertilizer or manure to fix.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ biɔ ni asaa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and bushy leaves but very small tubers inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When the soil contains too much nitrogen or receives excess water late in the growing period, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing starch in its root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ebaai kɛ eniji anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool humidity cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they ever grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This usually happens due to black pod disease caused by heavy rain and humidity, or natural pod wilt when the tree carries more young fruit than its nutrients can support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ black pod hela ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. loo adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ beni tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii tsɔ kɛha niyenii ni baanyɛ aye abua lɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize pulls a lot of nitrogen out of the soil, while leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, restoring fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli babaoo aba ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my yam plants grow bigger tubers when I lift their vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni miwoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for tuber growth using sunlight on their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they capture maximum sunlight and avoid rot, sending more energy into building big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei haa niyenii kɛha tuber dalɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkafite. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do caterpillars keep hiding deep inside the central leaves of my maize during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-abele lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the cool center of the plant during hot daylight hours to avoid drying out and to stay safe from birds, coming out to eat leaf tissue when temperatures drop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haaa egbi, ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha okpoi. Amɛbaaje kpo koni amɛbaye baai amli fãji kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing any fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the pollen inside tomato blossoms becomes dry and sterile. Unpollinated flowers cannot form fruit, so the plant drops them to conserve water.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain usually wets only the surface soil. If a dry spell follows, the soil dries up quickly, killing tender seeds that have just started to sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui bibii ni eje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young crops even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but weeds aggressive roots steal nutrients and fertilizer directly from your crop's root zone while their fast-growing leaves block sunlight from reaching your plants.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi jwɛi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛbaai ni daa oya lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do crop seeds brought from outside Ghana sometimes fail to grow well on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Foreign seeds are often bred for different weather, soil type, and daylight hours. When planted in Ghana's warm, tropical environment without proper care, they can struggle against local heat, soil conditions, and native pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi, shikpɔŋ henɔi kɛ hulutsoo be. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ Ghana he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛwu amɛshi he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ, kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do some plant varieties survive hot weather and dry spells better than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have natural traits that help them adapt. Drought-tolerant varieties have deep roots or leaf features that store water, while sensitive varieties dry out quickly when rain is scarce.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli sui ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe. Henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi. yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni nuɔ he waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and why are some delicate crops grown inside it instead of the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli moŋ fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ?

english: A greenhouse is a protective shelter made of clear plastic or mesh that controls sunlight, heat, and moisture. It acts like a shield, protecting young or delicate crops from insect pests, harsh rain, and extreme heat.
ga: Greenhouse ji shĩa ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋloo ni mli tse fee ni kudɔɔ hulu la, dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibii ni buɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: How does raising young seedlings in a protected nursery prevent crop loss later on?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui bibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ mli lɛ atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ anaa?

english: A protected nursery keeps young seedlings safe from heavy rain, bright burning sun, and pests while their roots are small. Starting plants in a controlled environment makes them strong enough to survive when transplanted into the main field.
ga: He ni abuɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ darako lɛ. Tsei ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings suddenly wilt and die even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Young plants often suffer from soil-borne fungal diseases like damping-off. Too much soil moisture or infected soil allows fungi to attack the tender stem at ground level, causing the seedling to rot and collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, sũ ni mli edɔ fe nine loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi.

english: How do killer crop diseases spread so fast from plant to plant on the farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Crop diseases spread easily through tiny fungal spores, bacteria, or viruses carried by wind, splashing rainwater, contaminated cutlasses and boots, or sap-sucking insects moving between plants.
ga: Tse helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ fungal spores, bacteria, loo virus bibii anɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwieɔ nugbɔ nu ni mli ewo muji dadei kɛ atadei loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut down and burn diseased plants instead of leaving them to recover?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ akɛ amɛfolɔ amɛ ni amɛshã amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaashi amɛ koni amɛhe ewa amɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving a sick plant on the field allows it to act as a breeding ground for pests and diseases. Removing and burning infected plants stops the disease from spreading to the rest of your healthy crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛfee he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai fɔɔ yɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ ni ashãa lɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What simple steps can I take to prevent killer diseases from getting into my farm?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni mafee koni hela akabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can prevent diseases by planting certified disease-resistant seed varieties, cleaning your farm tools regularly, removing weeds that harbor pests, and avoiding bringing unverified plant materials onto your land.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi hela naa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Tsumɔ oŋmɔ mli nibii ahe daa. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ahe nibii ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni okɛbaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do some crops produce strong new shoots and plenty of fruit while neighboring crops remain weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi shwereɔ ŋmeii heei ni mli wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Plants compete with each other for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. A weaker plant might have root damage from hidden soil pests, or its roots may be crowded, preventing it from taking in fertilizer properly.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛshishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli. Aloo, amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ anyɛŋ awo amɛmli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can a crop disease destroy an entire farm yield if it is not caught early?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ afite ŋmɔ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ oya?

english: Yes, aggressive crop diseases like cassava mosaic disease or cocoa swollen shoot disease can spread rapidly through a farm, destroying the plants' ability to feed themselves and leading to total harvest loss if left unchecked.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai ni naa wa tamɔ ŋmei mosaic loo kookoo tip ni efuu lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛkwɛɔ ehe lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ laajeɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa beans get rejected by buyers when I use strong chemicals close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpooɔ lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni mli ewo muji tsuɔ nii yɛ be ni bɛŋkɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying heavy chemicals close to harvest leaves chemical residues on the beans that ruin their flavor and make them unsafe for chocolate production, causing buyers to reject the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni bɛŋkɛ kpamɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni efiteɔ amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsokolate feemɔ. ni haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How can I protect my cocoa pods from pests without relying heavily on chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: You can reduce pests naturally by pruning overgrown branches to let in light, removing infected pods quickly, and keeping the farm floor clean to destroy pest breeding sites.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ koni ekɛ la aba lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he atse koni efite hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods for the best quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their color changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting at this stage ensures the beans inside have full flavor and oil content.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fɔ.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions when trees are planted too close together or lack proper pruning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli fe nine mli. Beni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo ni afolɔko amɛhe jogbaŋŋ

english: Will using mechanical tools to cut cocoa pods damage my trees for next season?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ baafite mitso lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: When used correctly, harvesting tools make clean cuts on the pod stalk without stripping the bark, which actually protects the tree from infections and allows new flowers to grow next season.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ejieee hewolo lɛ. Enɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wilt when planted in open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees to shelter their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of beneficial insects that pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni bɛ

english: How does keeping large forest trees on my cocoa farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ koo mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Permanent shade trees regulate farm temperature, trap soil moisture during the dry season, and block harsh winds that break heavy cocoa branches.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli, ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni gbáa kookoo niji ni tsii lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it necessary to ferment cocoa beans under banana leaves instead of drying them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ afeɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ banana baai ashishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha amɛgbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans naturally to kill the seed inside, remove bitterness, and unlock the rich chocolate taste and brown color that chocolate makers require.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni egbe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ejie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbele tsokolate lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni feɔ tsokolate lɛ taoɔ lɛ naa.

english: What happens if I dry my harvested cocoa beans too quickly using artificial heat?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ akɛ la ni akɛfee lɛ tsu nii ni akpa kookoo yibii lɛ oya tsɔ?

english: Drying beans too fast traps harsh acids inside the bean, making the cocoa taste sour and brittle, which lowers the market value of your harvest.
ga: Beans ni agbiɔ oya tsɔ lɛ baaha acid ni mli wa ahi dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa jara ni akɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my crops drying up even when it rains a little bit nowadays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbi yɛ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Changes in local weather make rains unpredictable and ground temperatures higher. When rain comes in short, heavy bursts instead of steady showers, the soil stays dry underneath, causing crop leaves to heat up and wilt quickly.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ejaaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa ni yaa hiɛ miiba. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ kuku ni ebaanɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi yɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya.

english: How do I make sure my yams grow large and smooth so buyers at the market will want them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-sweet potato lɛ afee agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ asumɔ?

english: Yams need loose, fertile soil in well-made mounds or ridges to expand without obstruction. Keeping weeds down early and protecting the underground tubers from beetle damage ensures smooth, healthy yams that attract buyers.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ nɔ koni egbɛ eshwa ni nɔ ko akatsi enaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ waa.

english: If the weather on my farm has changed and my usual crops keep failing, how do I choose a new crop to plant?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsake ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ daa lɛ ehiii hu? Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei heei ni madu?

english: When weather patterns shift, look for short-duration or heat-tolerant crops like cowpeas, cassava, or early-maturing maize varieties. These require less rainfall and adapt better to unpredictable weather conditions.
ga: Beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ lɛ Taomɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi be kuku loo ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa, tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ oya. Enɛɛmɛi biɔ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my yams are fully mature and ready to be harvested from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yams show they are mature when the leaves and vines stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry up completely. Harvesting at this stage ensures the tubers have reached full size and will store well.
ga: Abuɔ sweet potato akɛ edara kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa dalɛ. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ kwraa Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha bulbs lɛ ashɛ amɛdalɛ he ni amɛto jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grow very well on one portion of my land but look stunted and yellow on another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality varies across the same farm due to differences in organic matter, water retention, and depth. Areas where water collects or where soil is compacted prevent plant roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Yɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ Nu ni ahiɔ mli kɛ emlibotemɔ. He ni nu buaa ehe naa loo he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔle he lɛ haaa tsei shishifãi amu ni amɛkaná niyenii.

english: Why are the main rains coming later in the year now, and how does that affect when I should plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ titri lɛ baa yɛ afi nɛɛ naagbee lɛ? Ni te enáa be ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shifting climate patterns have altered traditional rainfall calendars in Ghana. Planting seeds in dry soil before steady rains begin causes seeds to spoil in the hot ground, so planting must be adjusted to align with the actual start of regular rainfall.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi etsake blema nugbɔshiimɔ kalanda ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha amɛgboi yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ atsake dumɔwui lɛ koni ekɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ shishijee lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Which fast-growing crops can I plant right after harvesting my yams to keep my land productive?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu kɛji mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts are ideal after yam harvesting. They grow quickly, suppress weeds, and naturally add nitrogen back into the soil to feed the next main crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛdaraa oya. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some of my yams rot quickly after harvest while others stay good for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi hi lolo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, stored in hot spaces, or kept in humid, unventilated areas. Storing clean, undamaged tubers on raised wooden racks in a cool, shaded barn prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Too yɛ hei ni mli edɔ. Aloo okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni efiteee lɛ to tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, saving its internal water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akashwie oya tsɔ.

english: How does resting my land or changing what I plant there help restore the soil for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo nɔ ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating crops or leaving land fallow restores soil energy and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: What is dry season farming, and how is it different from regular farming?
ga: Mɛni ji hɔmɔ be mli okwaayeli? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ he?

english: Dry season farming is the practice of growing crops during months when there is no rain by using artificial water sources like river pumps or wells. Regular farming relies entirely on natural rainfall, but dry season farming lets you grow crops all year round.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nugbɔshiimɔ be mli okwaayeli he ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu jɛɛhe ko ni akɛfee, tamɔ faa mli pɔmp loo nu bu nɔ. Okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ damɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ kwraa. Shi okwaayeli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can I keep growing crops even when the rains completely stop for several months?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu tsei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ nyɔji babaoo po?

english: Yes, you can continue farming during dry months by using small-scale irrigation machines or pumps to pull water from rivers, dugouts, or wells directly to your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oya nɔ otsu okwaayeli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ nu bibioo loo pɔmp ni okɛbaatsu nii ni okɛgbala nu kɛjɛ faa, ŋshɔnaa ŋshɔnaa, loo nu bu mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya onibii amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers prefer growing garden eggs and okra during the dry season instead of crops like corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi sumɔɔ ni amɛdu abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ okra yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Vegetables like garden eggs and okra have short growing cycles and high market demand during dry periods. They are well-suited for small land spaces and give quick financial returns when watered regularly using small irrigation setups.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ okra lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛdaraa, ni amɛjara wa waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei bibii ni ekɛ shika baa oya kɛji akɛ akɛ nu shwieɔ shi daa kɛtsɔ nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo bibioo ko nɔ.

english: Is a small plot of land enough for me to make money growing vegetables in the dry season?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ bibioo ko pɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ana shika kɛdu aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Yes, because fresh vegetables like garden eggs and okra become scarce and expensive in the dry season. A small, well-watered plot can produce high yields that sell for good prices at local markets.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ aduawai heei tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ okra lɛ namɔ wa ni amɛjara hu wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Hei bibii ni nu fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo aba, ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara kpakpa yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: How does using an irrigation machine help my crop plants grow when there is no rain?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: An irrigation machine pumps water directly onto your farmland, keeping the soil damp so that plant roots can continuously absorb the moisture and nutrients they need to grow, blossom, and bear fruit without waiting for rain.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ fɛ̃i kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara, amɛwo fɔfɔi, ni amɛwo yibii be fɛɛ be ni amɛmɛɛɛɛ nugbɔ.

english: How often do vegetable crops like okra need water when the sun is very hot and dry?
ga: Shii enyiɛ aduawai tamɔ okra he hiaa nu kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ shɛ amɛhe?

english: Vegetables have shallow roots that dry out quickly under intense sun, so they usually need consistent water every one to two days to keep their leaves from wilting and to keep producing fresh pods.
ga: Aduawai lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ aduawai anɔ nu daa gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ koni baai lɛ akagbo, ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants drop their flowers when the ground gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: When a garden egg plant lacks water, it gets stressed and drops its flowers to conserve energy and survive. Giving the plant reliable water through irrigation prevents flower drop and allows those blossoms to turn into fruits.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ehaoɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ehi shi. Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa tsei kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi ni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do okra plants grow and produce pods so fast when supplied with heat and light watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okra tsei lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii oya kɛji akɛ amɛwo hulutsoo kɛ nu fioo ko mli lɛ?

english: Okra loves warm sunlight, and when given steady water, its natural growth speeds up, allowing it to produce flowers and ready-to-harvest pods every few days.
ga: Roselle sumɔɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ. ni kɛ́ onine shɛ nu nɔ daa Adebɔɔ mli dalɛ baafee oya. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ daa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn dry and yellow when there is no rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Water carries nutrients from the soil up into the plant's leaves. Without water, the plant cannot feed itself, causing the leaves to lose their green color, turn yellow, and dry up.
ga: Nu hiɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei ahe baai amli. Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ amɛhe. ni haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ Tsɔmɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ

english: Why do garden egg fruits turn out small and bitter if I don't give them enough water during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mihaaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Garden egg fruits rely heavily on water to expand and develop a juicy, sweet flavor. Without enough moisture, the plant produces stunted fruits that taste bitter due to concentrated stress compounds.
ga: Orchard eggplant kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ waa koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ e-fleve ni ŋɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ aba. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ, tso lɛ baawo aduawai bibii ni ŋɔɔ yɛ stress compounds ni fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil. Adding manure or balanced fertilizer around the base of the plant gives it the nutrient boost it needs to grow dark green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa abɔle he. Tso shishi kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa fataa he kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa, eŋɔli ni tsuɔ.

english: How can I start growing pepper and garden eggs if I don't have a large farm plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabɔi ŋmeii kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii akwɛmɔ kɛji mibɛ ŋmɔ mli he ko ni da?

english: You can plant vegetables in old rice sacks, plastic container buckets, or small raised beds in a small compound. Container farming uses little space and allows you to easily manage soil quality and watering.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu aduawai yɛ ŋmãa kotokui momoi amli, plastic tsɛnsii amli, loo saatsoi bibii ni awó nɔ yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ. Okwaayeli ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ heɔ he ko fioo pɛ ni ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nyɔji babaoo po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose soil to expand its tubers. If the ground is packed hard, the roots struggle to swell, so building soft soil mounds before planting helps the tubers grow thick.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava koni ekɛdu ŋmeii. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ooofee dani odu lɛ baaye abua ni bulb lɛ adara babaoo.

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell that can dry up newly sprouted seeds before the next rain comes. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ agbi dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the heat is too intense or when water supply in the soil is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting during cooler windows helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ samflɛ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Yam leaves catch sunlight to make energy that swells the tuber underground. Staking keeps leaves lifted toward the light and off the damp ground, preventing rot and increasing yam size.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fũuɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ woɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛyaa la lɛ he ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm crops are getting too much water during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When roots sit in water for too long, they starve of air, causing leaves to turn soft, yellow, and droopy even though the soil is wet. Creating small drainage ditches lets extra rain run off safely.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi lɛ hi nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafee nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli, ni no baaha baai lɛ afee blɛoo, amɛfee ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nu tsɔji bibii ni afee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nugbɔ anɛ babaoo shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I fix it simply?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Small caterpillars eat cabbage leaves as they hatch. Spraying a gentle natural mixture made from neem leaves crushed in soapy water deters insects without damaging the vegetable.
ga: Kplukai bibii lɛ yeɔ kaabɛji baai kɛ́ amɛfɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ ni akɛfutu mli blɛoo ni ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ lɛ shwie nu ni akɛ samla fee lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi lɛ akabote mli ni eyeee aduawai lɛ awui.

english: Why do my groundnuts turn moldy after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ mli tsɔi beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested groundnuts hold a lot of water inside their shells. If they are not dried thoroughly in the sun before storage, trapped dampness causes harmful mold to grow.
ga: Akpɔlɔi ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ hulu lɛ mli dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big trees away from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving some big trees or planting food crops like plantains provides shade and creates a cool, moist environment for the cocoa to grow safely.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni aaashi loo niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli aba koni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing small holes and full of tiny caterpillars inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii Yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Your maize is likely being attacked by Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves and stems. Catching them early by inspecting your field weekly and applying recommended biological or chemical sprays will protect your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ abele bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tutuaa o-abele lɛ. Amɛ ni ooomɔ mra Kɛtsɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ daa otsi ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaaye obua ni obu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, turning yellow, and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and by planting stem cuttings from infected plants. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties from certified sources is the most effective way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni jɛ hei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowish, stunted maize usually means your soil lacks essential nutrients, especially nitrogen. Adding organic compost, animal manure, or balanced fertilizers like NPK gives the plants the food they need to grow tall and green.
ga: Yellow dwarf corn tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rains keep changing every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu tsei? Be ni nugbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi?

english: Instead of planting strictly by traditional dates, wait until the soil gets a deep soak from two or three good rains. Planting in well-moistened soil ensures seeds germinate strong and do not dry up during early dry spells.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ blema date tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility so you get better yields with less fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa tsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná yibii kpakpai kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly after I stack them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fite oya beni mikɛto ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest, exposed to heat, or stored without good airflow. Storing undamaged tubers in raised, shaded, and well-ventilated yam barns keeps them cool and prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. ni akɛwoɔ la mli loo ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Okɛ ŋmeii ni efiteee lɛ ato sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛkafite.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to quickly capture light, water, and nutrients before young crops can establish. Clearing early, using mulch, or planting cover crops helps shade out weeds and gives your main crops a head start.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii oya dani tsei bibii lɛ adara. Kpeemɔ mra Kɛ okɛ mulch loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat and dry soil because the plant gets stressed. Watering consistently at the roots early in the morning and providing light shade helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ eshɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ haoɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa leebi kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest give me a smaller yield than the certified seed I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds bought from certified dealers lose their vigor and high yield strength after the first generation. Replanting saved hybrid seeds results in weaker plants, so buying fresh certified seed each season ensures maximum yield.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa anáa yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why should I bother trimming or pruning my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ haomɔ ni ji mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming and pruning cocoa trees encourages them to trigger fresh growth and bring out flowers much earlier, which ultimately helps you get a bigger harvest.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ ni afoɔ ni afoɔ lɛ woɔ shweremɔ hee kɛ fɔfɔii ni baa oya lɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ baaye abua bo yɛ naagbee ni okpa babaoo.

english: Is it safe to cut back my cocoa trees, or will it damage the farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ? Aloo ebaafite ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: It is completely safe and beneficial. Pruning branches and flowers actually triggers the cocoa tree to release fresh, healthy new flowers faster.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he Niji kɛ fɔfɔi ni afolɔ mli lɛ baaha cacao tso lɛ ajie fɔfɔi heei, ni yɔɔ ehee, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ oya.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to start pruning my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje kookoo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ shishi?

english: The best time to start pruning your cocoa trees is right as the March, April, and May rains begin, as the rainfall helps the trees recover and grow quickly.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje kookoo tsei lɛ ashishifomɔ shishi ji nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji ni ji March, April, kɛ May lɛ amli, ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: How should I prepare my cocoa trees when the March to May rainy season begins?
ga: Kokoo tsei: Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi yɛ March kɛyashi May lɛ, te esa akɛ asaa kookoo tsei lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should start pruning your cocoa trees as soon as these rains begin, because combining rainfall with pruning forces the tree to push out leaves and flowers early.
ga: Esa akɛ oje kookoo tsei lɛ ashishifãa shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ kɛ tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ajie baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ oya.

english: How can I get my cocoa trees to produce flowers earlier in the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ afɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Pruning your cocoa trees right at the start of the rainy season stimulates the trees to bring out fresh flowers earlier than they normally would.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ kookoo tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees taking so long to bring out flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees often delay flowering if they are left unpruned; pruning branches signals to the tree that it is time to produce fresh flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔii asɛɛ tsɛmɔ kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ amɛ. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ kɛha fɔfɔi heei.

english: What should I do when I see fresh new leaves starting to sprout on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina akɛ baai heei miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ?

english: When new leaves appear, it means the tree is actively growing. Pruning at this exact time helps force the tree to bring out a high volume of new flowers.
ga: Kɛji baai heei je kpo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miida waa. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni enyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewo fɔfɔi heei babaoo.

english: What simple practice can I do to make my cocoa trees yield in abundance this year?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei lɛ afee babaoo afi nɛɛ?

english: Pruning your cocoa trees when new leaves appear during the early rains encourages heavy flowering, which leads to an abundant pod harvest.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi beni baai heei jeɔ kpo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli lɛ baawo fɔfɔi babaoo he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa anáa pod ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Will pruning my cocoa trees really increase the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni mifoɔ lɛ haa cacao ni mikpaa lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, proper pruning encourages early and abundant flowering, directly resulting in a much higher yield of cocoa pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni baa mra ni amɛbaa babaoo lɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa baa.

english: How do I know if my timing for farm maintenance will lead to a good cocoa yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ be lɛ baaha maná kookoo yibii kpakpai?

english: If you align your pruning with the arrival of the March-May rains and the growth of new leaves, your cocoa trees will flower heavily and produce an abundant harvest.
ga: Kɛji oto ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛ March-May nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ aba, kɛ baai heei ni baa lɛ akpã gbee O-cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why should I draw straight lines and measure distances when planting my crops instead of just scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo linei ni ja ni masusu he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã kɛkɛ?

english: Planting in measured lines gives every plant enough space to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to keep large shade trees scattered inside our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tall shade trees protect young cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, reduce heat stress, and create natural fertilizer when their fallen leaves rot into the soil.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi ni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does planting plantains too close to my house cause cracks in the floor and walls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shia lɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ kɛ gbogboi lɛ fãa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have strong, rapidly expanding root systems and underground bulbs that absorb lots of water and expand underground, which can push against and damage weak building foundations.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya. Ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii komɛi yɛ ni shwieɔ nu babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi. ni baanyɛ ashɛre ni efite tsumaa shishitoo ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do deep tree roots sometimes cause nearby smaller food crops to wilt and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa niyenii tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Large trees have extensive root systems that spread out underground and aggressively suck up water and plant food from the topsoil, leaving nearby smaller crops with nothing.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi babaoo ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛmuɔ nu waa ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ eshwɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he.

english: How does a disease spread from one cocoa tree to another across my whole farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus or black pod move tree by tree when sap-sucking insects like mealybugs carry the virus, or when wind and rain splash disease spores onto healthy neighboring trees.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus loo ŋmeii diji lɛ fãa tsei lɛ amli ekomekomei. Kɛji akɛ kooloi tamɔ mealybugs ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ hela lɛ baa. aloo beni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ gbɛɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: What is attacking my cassava stem and leaving tiny holes and dust on the bark all day long?
ga: Mɛni tutua mi-cassava tso lɛ? ni eshiɔ bu bibioo ko Ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Stem borers or termites burrow inside the stem to feed continuously on the inner tissues, weakening the plant so it easily breaks in strong winds.
ga: Stem borers loo termites baafo tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni amɛye emli fãji lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, amɛkumɔ oya.

english: Why is the trunk of my tree oozing sticky liquid and peeling bark near the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ? Ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Oozing and peeling bark usually mean a fungal or bacterial infection has entered the tree through wounds caused by farm tools or pests feeding on the trunk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ bote tso lɛ mli.

english: How do creeping weed vines manage to destroy a whole tree if left alone?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni wain tso ni shwereɔ lɛ akpãtã tso muu fɛɛ hiɛ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ pɛ?

english: Climbing vines grow rapidly up the trunk to reach sunlight, eventually wrapping around branches and covering the leaves, which blocks sunlight and starves the tree.
ga: Wein tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ tso lɛ mli koni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebɔleɔ tso nine lɛ he ni ehaa baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do so many small shoots grow around the base of my plantain tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe. mi plantain shishitoo Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Plantains produce shoots called suckers to multiply, but if you leave too many around the main plant, they steal water and nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii kɛha shweremɔ. Shi kɛji oshi lɛ ebɔle Tsei titrii babaoo tsɔ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: What does it mean when the leaves on my crops turn yellow and dry up from the tips?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips are a warning signal from the plant that it lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, is suffering from drought, or has damaged roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni jɛ tso lɛ ŋɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ hɔmɔ miikpe loo eshishifãi efite

english: How do I know if my harvested maize is dry enough to sell to buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ?

english: Buyers check the moisture content of your maize before buying. Dry maize reaches a safe dryness range that prevents mold, showing buyers that the grain is high quality and safe to purchase.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni o-corn lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha dani amɛheɔ. Agbiɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsiɔ ŋmãa naa. Tsɔɔmɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil so quickly when I pack it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils quickly if it still holds too much water from the farm. Properly drying and processing your maize removes excess moisture, which stops rot and makes the grain last much longer.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ oya kɛji nu ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fa lolo. Abɛi ni agbiɔ ni atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do buyers test my grain moisture before giving permission to purchase it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kaa midumɔwui lɛ amɛkwɛɔ kɛji amɛmli edɔ dani amɛŋmɛɔ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛheɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers check moisture levels to ensure the maize won't rot during transport or long storage. Meeting their required dryness range gives them confidence to buy your crop.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ ha koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbooo yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa loo akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ amɛshɛ be ni hɔmɔ baa ni ataoɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hekɛnɔfɔɔ ni amɛkɛheɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Does drying my maize well really help it stay good for a long time?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, proper processing and thorough drying stop insects and mold from growing. Well-processed maize can stay fresh and usable for nearly a full year in proper storage.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akadara. Abɛi ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ehee ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii aaafee afi muu fɛɛ kɛji akɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize weigh slightly less after I leave it out to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi fioo beni miha egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize loses weight during drying because water trapped inside the grain is evaporating. Losing this moisture is necessary so the grain can be stored safely without decaying.
ga: Abɛi lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ, be mli ni nu ni emɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni baa shi lɛ he miihia bɔni afee ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato shweshweeshwe ni amɛkafite.

english: How long can I safely keep my maize in a storage room before it spoils?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa awo mi nitoohe lɛ shweshweeshwe dani efite?

english: If your maize is thoroughly dried and properly processed before putting it away, it can stay safely in a good storage room for eleven months to a full year.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-abele lɛ egbi kwraa ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ dani oshɛrɛ lɛ ashwie lɛ, Abele baanyɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ nitoohe kpakpa mli nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome kɛyashi afi muu fɛɛ.

english: What happens if I store my maize in a room without checking its dryness first?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa to tsu ko mli ni mikwɛɛɛ kɛji egbi klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: If you store maize that has high moisture, heat builds up inside the bag. This causes mold to grow and attract insects, ruining your harvest within a few weeks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa to he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ baabua ehe naa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii. Efiteɔ onibii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli

english: What basic steps should I take before putting my grain into long-term storage?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee dani mikɛ dumɔwui awo he ko ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You should clean out dirt and damaged kernels, dry the grain until it reaches the safe moisture range, and ensure your storage room is clean, dry, and cool.
ga: Esa akɛ otsumɔ muji kɛ dumɔwui ni efite lɛ ahe. Gbimɔ ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ebaashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ he ni okɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he tse, egbi, ni edɔ.

english: Why does mold grow on my corn even when it is inside a closed store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ miikwɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ he ko ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni agbe naa lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Mold grows because the maize was either put in the room while still damp, or moisture from the floor and walls got into the grain. Dampness is what feeds the mold.
ga: Muji daa ejaakɛ akɛ ŋmãa toɔ tsu lɛ mli be mli ni edɔ lolo. Aloo nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ gbogboi amli lɛ boteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Fɛ̃i ji nɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I store my maize for a whole year without losing its quality?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ato afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ efooo?

english: Yes, you can keep maize for up to eleven months or a full year if it is properly dried to the right moisture level before storage and kept in a cool, protected room.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa ato kɛyashi nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ ekome loo afi muu fɛɛ kɛji akɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ni hulutsoo be ni sa yɔɔ mli dani okɛto. ni akɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense sun and heat. They need temporary shade from larger plants, like plantains or shade trees, to keep their roots cool and retain moisture until they are strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plant produces bigger and heavier plantain bunches.
