ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so when soil nutrients drop, the plant moves leftover nitrogen to new upper leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes and powdery waste inside the leaf whorls of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? No mli lɛ, ashɛre ni sũ ni efite lɛ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the top center of the maize plant during the day and eat the tender leaf tissue, which slows down growth if not treated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛye baa bibii amli fãji Enɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: Which direction should the leaf buds point when I am planting cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the small leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems struggle to grow upward and the plant produces a much lower harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Ewa akɛ eshishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni tso lɛ baaná ŋmaa bibioo kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce food for underground tuber growth. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also protects the foliage from rotting and spreading fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely high heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ yibii ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper garden early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can absorb water before the heat sets in. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots, and heat stress can harm wet leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni dɔlɛ he haomɔ baanyɛ aye baai ni efɔ lɛ awui.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas before my maize crop make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural bacteria in their roots that fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. When the roots decay, this nitrogen stays in the ground and acts like natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ saa amɛhe yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite Nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ

english: Is it better for me to sell my biggest harvested yams at the market or save them to plant next season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ wulu fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ jara nɔ loo mikɛto koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Selling your biggest yams brings in the highest amount of money at the market. You can make a substantial profit from these large tubers and use a portion of that money to buy smaller, cheaper seed yams for your next planting season.
ga: O-sweet potato ni da fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ lɛ baaha oná shika babaoo fe fɛɛ yɛ jara nɔ. Obaanyɛ oná sɛɛnamɔi babaoo kɛjɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii wuji nɛɛ amli. Ni okɛ shika lɛ eko ahe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni jara waaa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does selling my yam harvest directly at the market help my farm business grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ jara nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Directly selling your fresh harvest gives you immediate cash income. Since high-quality, well-cultivated yams command good market prices, this cash flow allows you to reinvest in your farm, purchase affordable planting seeds, and make a strong profit.
ga: Onibii heei ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa onine shɛɔ shika nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ jara kpakpa. Shika ni hoɔ nɛɛ haa okɛ shika woɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Hemɔ tsei dumɔwui ni jara waaa ni oná sɛɛnamɔi ni mli wa

english: Why is buying seed yams sometimes smarter than using my own harvest for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ eji nilee akɛ mahe ŋmeii fe ni mikɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ minibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu lɛ?

english: Your large harvested yams are worth a lot of money to consumers. By selling them at top market prices and buying cheaper, smaller yams to use as seeds, you keep the extra profit while still securing the materials you need to plant your next crop.
ga: O ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okpaa lɛ jara wa waa kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ. Kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni jara waaa ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahemɔ nɔ. Obaahiɛ sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi amli yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ nibii ni he hiaa bo koni okɛdu oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ lolo.

english: Can I plant small yams and still get a big harvest, or do I need large yams to get large crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato bibii ni maná yibii babaoo lolo? Aloo sweet potato agbo he miihia mi koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Small yams contain all the necessary nutrients and shoot buds to grow into strong plants. When planted in good soil with proper care, a small seed yam will sprout and produce brand-new, full-sized large tubers.
ga: Atomɔ bibii yɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii heei ni da waa.

english: Will a small seed yam produce a weak crop compared to a larger piece of yam?
ga: Ani dumɔwui bibii lɛ baawo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui wuji ahe?

english: Not at all. A small, healthy seed yam serves simply as a starter power pack for the young plant; once its roots establish in well-prepared soil, the crop draws energy from the earth and sun to grow into a large tuber.
ga: Jee nakai kraa. Atomɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shishijee hewalɛ jɛɛhe kɛha tsei bibii. Kɛ́ eshishifãi lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃.

english: What kind of small yams should I look to buy when I want to plant my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii esa akɛ matao beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Look for healthy, small seed yams that are firm, free from rot or insect damage, and have visible growth eyes or small sprouts starting to show, as these will germinate quickly in the soil.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ŋɔɔ. ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni fiteee loo kooloi fiteee lɛ ni eyɛ hiŋmɛii wuji loo ŋmeii bibii ni anaa jogbaŋŋ Ejaakɛ nibii nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my yam plants produce huge tubers while others produce small ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ekrokomɛi hu woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large when the soil is properly cultivated into deep, loose mounds, allowing the roots to expand freely without hard earth blocking them, alongside adequate water and nutrients.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiii amɛnaa. kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: What causes yam tubers to expand and grow so big under the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers serve as the plant's food storage. When you cultivate the soil well and keep the plant healthy, the leaves make extra food through sunlight and send it underground, causing the tuber to swell and grow large.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he. Kɛji otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ ni oha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Baai lɛ feɔ niyenii krokomɛi kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ ni amɛkɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni edaa.

english: How do I cultivate my field properly to ensure my yams grow as big as possible?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu he ni miyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni mi-sweet potatoes lɛ adara bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: Good cultivation involves clearing weeds early, making large, soft soil mounds or ridges, and protecting the young plants so their roots can spread easily and collect water and nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ahe ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra. Gɔji loo ŋshɔkei wuji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afeɔ. kɛ tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛhiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers have reached their full size and are ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When the yam plant's leafy vines stop growing, turn yellow, and begin to dry up, it means the plant has finished storing food underground, signaling that the tubers have reached full size and are ready to harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ wain tsei ni yɔɔ sweet potato tso lɛ mli lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ niyenii eto shikpɔŋ shishi momo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: When is the most critical time to make sure my crops get enough water so I do not lose my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite?

english: Crops need water most urgently during their flowering and fruiting stages. If plants suffer from drought during flowering, they drop their blossoms or produce empty, undersized seeds and fruits, causing severe yield losses.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei oya fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi loo amɛbaawo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ ni fiteɔ waa.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle full sunlight and dry harmattan winds. Without shade plants like plantains to shelter them and retain soil moisture, the sun scorches them quickly.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ekãa ni baaha sũ lɛ nɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ miitso oya.

english: When soil remains flooded with excess water, air cannot reach the root zone. This causes roots to drown and creates the ideal environment for fungal diseases to attack and rot the cassava tubers underground.
ga: Beni nu ni fa fe nine eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmeii shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Nitrogen washes away easily with heavy rain, leaving plants weak if soil fertility is not replenished.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen lɛ hoɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, crop roots and leaves crowd each other out. They end up fighting for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, weak stems and very small ears.
ga: adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ebɔ he. Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsitsi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, ni etoi lɛ hu feɔ bibii waa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences extreme temperature stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. The plant protects itself by shedding flowers it cannot support.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Tsei buɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops much more when the crop is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui fe tsutsu lɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Young crops have tiny root systems and small leaves, making them weak competitors against fast-growing weeds. Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight the young crop needs to establish itself.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa efeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛha jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa tsei bibii koni amɛtswa amɛhe amɛma shi lɛ.

english: Why do pests get worse when I grow maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ mli woɔ wu waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in the same soil gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home and food supply, allowing their populations to multiply year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai náa shia kɛ niyenii ni baahi shi daa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni gbɔmɛi ayibɔ yaa hiɛ daa afi.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from being destroyed by insects in my storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ he koni nitoohe mli kooloi akafite?

english: Insects thrive on moisture in stored grains. Drying your grain thoroughly until it is hard and dry before storing it in clean, airtight bags or treated silos prevents weevils from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Akɛ ŋmaa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni egbi dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui ni mli tse loo silos ni atsa mli lɛ amli. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafee babaoo.

english: Why does cutting off the small lower branches of my pepper plants help produce bigger peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔi wuji baa.

english: Pruning unnecessary lower branches removes foliage that consumes plant food uselessly. It directs the plant's food energy away from stem growth and straight into forming larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ baai ni yeɔ tsei aniyenii ni he ehiaaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe kɛyaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feemɔ mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when heavy rains wash away soil food, preventing the plant from making green leaves.
ga: Abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo baai eŋɔli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide wide leaf shade and keep the soil moist, protecting young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo, baai ni mli kwɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil stress, or a lack of helpful insects like bees to transfer pollen between blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ wuobii nyɛɛɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ bɔ ni sa

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the tender center of my maize plants during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which hide inside the plant's funnel during the heat of the day to protect themselves while feeding on soft growth at night.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu amɛhe he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by microscopic insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on sap and transmitting plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ mli helai ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli.

english: How do small insects get inside my closed bags of stored corn even when I sealed them tight?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kooloo bibioo ko bote mi-abele kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ mli? Kɛji mikɛ mihe wo mli shiŋŋ po

english: Weevils often lay tiny hidden eggs inside the grain kernels while the corn is still in the field; once stored, the eggs hatch into insects inside the sealed bag.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Kɛ akɛwo ŋmaa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ, kɛ́ akɛto lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn black or grow white mold when I store it inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize retains internal water after harvest. If stored before drying thoroughly under the sun, trapped moisture encourages fungal mold to grow on the grains.
ga: Abɛi hiɛɔ nu yɛ emli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛto dani egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot just a few days after I dig them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots undergo natural chemical decay because their skin loses protection from moisture loss, making them deteriorate quickly unless processed or preserved.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ, amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ tsofai. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhewolo lɛ bɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa efiteɔ oya, ja atsu he nii loo akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing new shoots while sitting in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni mita mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally enter a sleeping phase after harvest, but after a few months, the living tuber breaks dormancy and spends its stored energy to sprout fresh shoots for the next season.
ga: Sweet potatoes yaa adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ, Living bulbs lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe ni amɛtoɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I easily know if my harvested corn is dry enough to safely store for a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Dry corn kernels feel very hard, make a sharp cracking sound when bitten, and do not leave moisture or dents when pressed firmly with a fingernail.
ga: Abele ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ wa waa. Gbee ko ni tswaa kɛji akɛ mɔ lɛ ŋmɔ. Ni eshiuuu ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ nineshi ŋmei mimɔ mli shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year if I plant on the exact same field without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Soil contains nutrients that crops feed on to grow. Every time you harvest, you remove those nutrients, so without giving the land time to rest or adding organic manure, the soil becomes exhausted and yield drops.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni tsei yeɔ koni amɛdara lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa nii lɛ Esa akɛ ojie nakai niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of strength from the soil, but crops like cowpeas and groundnuts actually fix nitrogen back into the earth through their roots, helping to restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele heɔ ehewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for water and plant food, while their leaves fight for sunlight. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough food to grow strong.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu ni amɛdu niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the food that gives leaves their dark green color and helps the plant grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily get scorched by strong sunlight. Keeping bigger shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields the young cocoa from harsh heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shãa oya. Kookoo tso nɔkwɛmɔ koni efee agbo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ebaabu kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after I planted them very deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they exhaust all the energy stored inside them trying to push through the heavy soil before they can reach sunlight and air, causing them to die underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ dani hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba enɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do cassava roots rot underground when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni miŋmɔ lɛ mli nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, they cannot breathe and fungi in the wet soil cause them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni efɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable plants with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeping moisture near the roots so plants stay hydrated longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Ha nu ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses to the plant, which distorts leaf growth and weakens fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni kɛ helai baa tsei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa baa lɛ dalɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops suffer even when I give my farm enough fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miipiŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that grow faster than cultivated crops, meaning they steal the fertilizer and water meant for your crops before your crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ dani otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and turning yellow during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their root systems are shallow and leaves burn easily. They need living shade crops, like plantains, to lower the heat and keep the soil moist until the cocoa canopy matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha dɔlɛ aba shi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping plantains with young cocoa is very beneficial. Fast-growing plantain leaves act as natural umbrellas to shade the young cocoa from harsh weather, while providing early food and income for your family before cocoa harvest begins.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii kwɛɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe kɛha oweku lɛ dani kookoo kpamɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When nitrogen is lacking, the maize plant takes whatever remaining nutrients it has from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing upper leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ, Abɛi baaŋɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer on my farm right when heavy rains start falling?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer away into water gutters before plant roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not flooded, so nutrients remain in the root zone.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ nubui lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ. koni niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi shishifã lɛ he

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water stays on the land for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air pockets in the soil to breathe. Prolonged standing water suffocates root tissues and creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungi to rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the growing top?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ muji tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: This leaf damage and waste (frass) are classic signs of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar burrows inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on soft leaf tissue away from heat.
ga: Nɛkɛ baa ni efite kɛ jwɛi (frass) nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii ni ale waa. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants dry up and wilt suddenly during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt living in the soil. Bacteria enter root wounds and multiply, clogging the internal tubes that pump water from roots up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Muawai boteɔ shishifã lɛ mli ni amɛshwereɔ. Etsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without growing any peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni eduuu pepper yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, forcing them to drop blossoms to conserve water and energy. Without flowers remaining attached to be pollinated, fruit formation stops.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛji fɔfɔii komɛi eshwɛɛɛ kɛha pollination Yibii feemɔ kpaɔ.

english: If I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree, will that not reduce the number of pods I get?
ga: Kɛ mifo niji babaoo kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ Ani no haŋ ŋmeii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Pruning actually increases yields over time. Removing dead, side, or overlapping branches opens up space for sunlight and airflow, which reduces black pod fungal disease and encourages the main trunk to flower heavily.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Niji ni egboi, ni yɔɔ afã loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbeleɔ he lɛ gbɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa black pod fungal hela lɛ baa shi ni ewoɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi waa.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to light to generate energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking also keeps leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal infections from spreading across the foliage.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia kane tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa baai lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside cocoa provides canopy cover to protect young trees while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing well after I plant them on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ beni adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen in the soil. When you plant maize repeatedly on the same plot without resting the soil or rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or soybeans, the soil loses essential nutrients, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ loo okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo soybeans tsakeee. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting soybeans before planting my maize crop help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soybeans ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Soybeans have natural beneficial bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When maize is planted afterward, it uses this leftover nitrogen as natural fertilizer to grow stronger and produce better yields.
ga: Soybeans mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli Akɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni haa ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ waa ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize crops more during dry spells than during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms multiply faster in warm, dry weather. Heavy rains can physically wash young caterpillars off leaves and out of the central whorls of maize plants, naturally reducing their numbers.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ faa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ayibɔ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing successful pollination. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant sheds them to conserve its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni ehaa pollination lɛ yeee omanye. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollen lɛ Tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and watery if I harvest them right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni mli jɔ kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: At the start of the rainy season, cassava plants quickly absorb water to grow new stems and leaves. This sudden intake lowers the starch concentration inside the tubers, making them watery and reduced in quality.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ŋmei tsei gbalaa nu oya koni amɛfee tsei kɛ baai heei. Nɛkɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ trukaa nɛɛ haa starch ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. ni haa nu kɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi

english: Why do my harvested maize grains rot quickly in storage even though the cobs felt dry on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Maize grains can feel dry on the outside while still retaining moisture deep inside the cob. If not thoroughly dried on tarpaulins after harvest, trapped moisture encourages fungal growth and mold inside storage bags.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa lɛ baanu he akɛ egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ tarpaulin nɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground when I plant them on flat land instead of raised mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ moŋ fe gɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need well-drained, loose soil to breathe and expand. Flat land traps excess rainwater around the root zone, suffocating the roots and allowing rotting fungi to multiply.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛmu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni oha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why does weed growth slow down my pepper plants even when I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miida lɛ miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifee mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger root systems than pepper plants, so they consume most of the applied fertilizer and soil moisture first, depriving your crop of nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa fe ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last maize harvest yield less food than the certified hybrid seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum yield in their first generation. Seeds saved from those harvested plants lose these special traits in subsequent plantings, resulting in weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why should I wash my cutlass and boots with water before moving to work on another farm block?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu afɔ mi-kɔɔji kɛ mi-boots lɛ he dani maya ŋmɔ kroko mli koni mayatsu nii lɛ?

english: Soil and plant fluids can carry invisible crop diseases like fungi and bacteria. Cleaning your boots and tools prevents you from carrying sickness from infected plants to healthy areas of your farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei amli nu baanyɛ aŋɔ tsei ahe helai ni anaaa tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ. Kɛ́ otsumɔ o-boots kɛ onitsumɔ dadei lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ ni okɛ helai akajɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to pluck off black, rotting pods and remove them from my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii diji ni miifite lɛ ni majie amɛ kɛjɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotting pods carry the black pod fungus. Leaving diseased pods on the tree or on the ground allows rain drops and wind to splash spores onto healthy cocoa pods, spreading the rot.
ga: Pods ni egboi lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ black pod fungus lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashwie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. ni ekɛ hela ni fiteɔ nii baa

english: How does leaving enough space between my pepper plants help stop them from falling sick?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni kɛ́ mashi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni hela akamɔ amɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, air cannot move freely and moisture stays trapped on the leaves. Proper spacing allows sunlight and breeze to dry the plants, which stops fungal sicknesses from growing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ aya he fɛɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akaya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them without any plantain trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni dumɔwui ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide tall, broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading young cocoa plants and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil when I plant them in flooded ground right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to breathe and sprout. When soil is completely filled with standing water, the seeds drown, suffocate, and rot before they can grow shoots.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food. The plant naturally steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled, patchy leaves on cassava are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava cuttings for planting is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii bibii. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Cassava ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ odumɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why do caterpillars hide and eat inside the central funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, and they target the tender, hidden parts inside the maize funnel where it is moist and safe from predators. Treating them early prevents them from destroying the growing core of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛtutuaa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli hei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ. Kɛ́ atsa amɛ mra lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ mli fã ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous maize harvest grow weaker plants than certified seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are special hybrids bred for high yields in the first planting. Saving seeds from that harvest causes the next generation to lose strength, producing smaller cobs and weaker plants.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, flat rot at the bottom end before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant transport calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some crops on my farm growing much bigger than the others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa babaoo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Crops grow bigger when they receive more nutrients, water, and sunlight. If certain parts of your field have richer soil or received more fertilizer, those specific plants will grow larger and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Tsei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛji amɛna niyenii babaoo, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni jara wa loo amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Nakai tsei pɔtɛɛi lɛ baadara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that they are receiving too much or too little water. Applying the right fertilizer or adjusting your watering can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli loo atsake nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops remaining short and weak even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for crops to grow strong; they also need food from nutrients in the soil. If your soil lacks these nutrients, adding organic manure or fertilizer will give your crops the food they need to grow tall.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii ni jɛɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu he miihia amɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii nɛɛ Humus loo organic fertilizer ni okɛbaafata he lɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: How do I know the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually early in the morning or late afternoon a few weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer to wet soil helps the roots absorb nutrients quickly without burning the plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli leebi loo shwane mli. Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: How can I make my soil richer so my crops produce bigger yields next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can enrich your soil by mixing in animal manure, compost, or decayed plant leaves, and by rotating crops like beans or groundnuts. Rich soil holds water better and provides steady food for your crops throughout the season.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ahe baai ni egbo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nii lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition causes the plants to stay small and yield fewer or smaller fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why did some of the seeds I planted fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are old, damaged, planted too deep in the earth, or if the soil is too dry or overly wet. Planting good quality seeds at the correct depth ensures a higher sprouting rate.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ, amɛfite, loo adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni sa lɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by taking the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the available resources to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ aná koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: What causes holes to appear on the leaves of my food crops?
ga: Mɛni haa buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi niyenii tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in leaves are typically caused by insects and pests feeding on your plants. Checking your crops regularly and using approved organic or chemical pest control can protect the leaves from damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ otsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ onibii amli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe fitemɔ naa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my plants before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mitso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off due to stress caused by extreme heat, dry soil, strong winds, or a lack of key nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and protecting your plants helps the flowers stay on and develop into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni obu otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide vital shade and hold moisture in the soil to protect young cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops too close to one another in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots compete for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them properly allows each plant to grow stronger and produce higher yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen, which plants need to build strong green leaves. Applying organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni dalɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave dried leaves and grass covering the soil around my plant roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi akɛ muji ni bɔleɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating out of the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and slow-rots into rich natural fertilizer.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ fitemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and side shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ esɛɛ tsei krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Removing non-producing shoots, called chupons, prevents the tree from wasting energy on extra leaves. Pruning lets sunlight and air pass through the tree, reducing diseases like black pod and helping pods grow bigger.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii ni wooo yibii, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa efite hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli, ehaa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I remove some of the young suckers growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow together, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in small bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones to produce large plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo efee ekome Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ ni amɛwoɔ plantain tsei wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so weak and slow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Keeping your farm clean ensures your main crops get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa branches swell up and lose their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo niji bibii lɛ fũuɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen branches are a symptom of swollen shoot disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The disease stops water and food from moving through the plant, eventually causing the tree to die.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji tso hela ni efuu lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs. Hela nɛɛ haaa nu kɛ niyenii atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, eha tso lɛ gbo.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree during a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers during dry spells to protect themselves from dying of thirst. Without enough water in the ground, the tree stops flower production to keep its main stem and leaves alive.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔii feemɔ koni ekɛbu shishifã lɛ kɛ baai titrii lɛ ahe.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my farm crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied during the early rainy season while the soil is moist. Heavy rains can wash fertilizer away, while dry soil can burn plant roots when fertilizer is added.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii. Be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã kɛji akɛ awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because harsh, direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil around their shallow roots. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔleɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads easily when air cannot move through the farm and water sits on the pods. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and wind to dry the farm, stopping the fungus from growing.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu baa pods lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni fa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi. ni ekpaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and manufacture food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ baai lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛha niyenii aha tso lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do crops like cowpeas and groundnuts help improve my farm soil?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds the next crops you plant on that land.
ga: Legumes yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away, keeping the roots dry and safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Ha shishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my plantain tree give smaller bunches when I leave many shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ daa bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ he lɛ? mi plantain lɛ

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for food, water, and sunlight. Cutting away extra suckers and keeping only two or three allows the main tree to focus its energy on producing large plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa panicles wuji ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they suffer from intense heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Watering your tomato plants regularly at the roots during dry weather helps them hold onto their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Kɛ́ okɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ nu nu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the harvest I get from my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing weeds while your crops are still young ensures your plants get all the nutrients they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni otsei lɛ darako lɛ, ehaa amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ akatsɔ oya. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I leave them in the soil too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ?

english: If you leave cassava in the ground long past maturity, the tubers begin to lose their starch content, turn woody, or even rot underground, ruining your yield.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ koni ekwɛ̃ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baabɔi ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ fomɔ. tsɔ tso loo egbo po yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ afitemɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and light when I delay harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ be ni mikɛkpaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: When mature cassava stays in the soil—especially during rains—the plant starts using up its stored starch for new growth, leaving the tubers watery and soft.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei lɛ egbɔ lɛ, eyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Tso lɛ baaje shishi ekɛ e-starch ni eto lɛ atsu nii kɛha dalɛ hee. Ehaa yitso lɛ mli nu ni efeɔ blɛoo.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crop is fully mature and ready for uprooting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the soil around the plant base starts cracking, and the crop reaches its maturity age (usually 9 to 12 months depending on the variety).
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabote fɔmɔ afii amli. (Be pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ.)

english: Is it safe to leave my mature root crops in the ground until I find a buyer?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi shishifãi ni edara lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni mana mɔ ni baahe?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field exposes them to pests, soil diseases, and over-maturity. It is better to harvest on time or arrange your market before the crop reaches peak maturity.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ baa amɛnɔ. Esa akɛ akpa yɛ be naa loo awo jara nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I properly take stem cuttings from my cassava plants for replanting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmei tso niji ekoŋŋ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from the middle section of the plant. Cut them cleanly into pieces about 20 to 25 cm long, ensuring each cutting has at least 3 to 5 clear buds or nodes.
ga: Halamɔ tso lɛ tso ni mli wa, ni eda kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee 20 kɛyashi 25 cm, ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eko fɛɛ eko hiɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi 3 kɛyashi 5.

english: Can I remove stem cuttings from a living plant without uprooting the whole crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo tso ni hiɛ ka lɛ nine ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔko?

english: Yes, you can carefully cut off mature branches or upper stems to use as planting material while leaving the tubers in the soil to be harvested later.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo tsei niji ni eda loo ŋwɛi tsei lɛ amli ni okɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii yɛ be mli ni oshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni okpa sɛɛ mli.

english: How should I store my stem cuttings if I cannot plant them immediately?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahere ŋmeii lɛ kɛji minyɛɛɛ madu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Store your stem cuttings vertically in a shaded, cool place with their bottom ends buried slightly in moist soil or covered with mulch to keep them fresh until planting.
ga: Kɛ tsei niji lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ha shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ afu fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ehi shi ehee kɛyashi be mli ni aduɔ.

english: What should I do if I am delayed and cannot harvest my crop on time?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miba sɛɛ ni minyɛɛɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ be naa?

english: If you must delay, clear weeds around the stems to prevent pest damage, but try to harvest as soon as possible before the roots spoil or attract burrowing animals.
ga: Kɛ ehe bahia ni okɛ be atsu nii Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. trunk koni akafite tsɛŋemɔ helai. Shi bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni okpa oya dani shishifãi lɛ agbo loo egbala kooloi ni shwieɔ bu lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow very tall stems but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi eshishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant receives too much nitrogen or shade, causing it to spend its energy growing tall leaves and branches instead of expanding its underground roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen loo hulutsoo babaoo nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is the best technique to uproot cassava without breaking the tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbalaa ŋmeii ni akuuu ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: Cut the main stem about 30 cm above the ground to use as a handle, loosen the soil around the base with a hoe, and pull gently straight upward.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tso titri lɛ aaafee 30cm kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛtsu nii akɛ nine. Kɛ ŋmei atsu shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ he nii ni okɛgbala lɛ blɛoo kɛya ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn even starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po je shishi ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can produce big, healthy corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ woɔ ŋmãa agboi ni mli wa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves. Controlling these insects early with appropriate spraying prevents the leaves from twisting and stops fruit growth from slowing down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ adalɛ akafee mlɛo.

english: My cassava plants are flowering, does this mean the roots under the ground are ready to harvest?
ga: Mi-cassava tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: No, cassava flowers are just how the plant reproduces above ground and do not show if the tubers are ready. You should judge maturity by the age of the crop—usually 9 to 12 months after planting—or by carefully digging around one plant to check the tuber size.
ga: Dabi, yucca fɔfɔi lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ni etsɔɔɔ kɛji yitso lɛ efee klalo loo efeee klalo. Esa akɛ okɛ afii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye lɛ akojo bɔ ni edara ha, bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ tso kome he ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni eyitso lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when many small shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lɛ Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he?

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. If you prune away most of the extra suckers and leave only one or two strong ones, the main tree receives all the energy it needs to grow a much larger bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ekɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu he. Kɛji ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make the food required to grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf rot and allows the plant to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ahi hulutsoo be mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that dry out quickly under direct, intense sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates a leafy canopy that protects the young seedlings from heat until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the air gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough steady water. When the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry soil, it sheds its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miigba tsei anaa lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so fast after I clear my farm with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ shwere oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds with a cutlass only cuts the tops, leaving their roots and hidden seeds alive inside the soil. When rain and sunlight hit the cleared ground, those seeds quickly germinate, so uprooting them or covering the soil helps keep them away longer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne miijie jwɛi lɛ, ŋmɔmɔ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni hulu la lɛ tswaa he ni agbele lɛ. Dumɔwui nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hiding inside the central funnel of the plant. Checking the funnels early and applying recommended treatments stops the caterpillars before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli. Kwɛmɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ mra ni akɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that traps water in the soil and blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops moisture from evaporating quickly, helping your vegetables survive longer without rain.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Ye obua o-vegetables lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Officer, what is the work of a sticking agent or 'staker' when I am mixing chemicals to spray my crops?
ga: Officer Mɛni ji binder loo ‘staeger’ lɛ nitsumɔ beni mikɛ tsofai futuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: A sticking agent helps the chemical spread evenly and glue itself to the crop leaves. This prevents rain, dew, or wind from washing the chemical off, allowing the treatment to stay on the plant and work longer.
ga: Binders yeɔ ebuaa tsofai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe baai ahe. Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ akajie tsofai kɛya. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How many days does a chemical spray usually stay active on my crop leaves before it loses its power?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii bɔ ni sa dani efite?

english: Most standard farm chemical sprays remain effective on plant leaves for about six days. After that, exposure to sunlight, rain, and fresh plant growth naturally weakens the chemical's strength.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ aaafee gbii enumɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ hewalɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some chemical sprays fail to protect my crops when it rains shortly after I spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛɛɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Without a sticking agent in the mixture, rainwater washes the liquid chemical off the smooth leaves before the plant can absorb it or before it can kill the pests.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ tsofai ni ji nu ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Dani tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ loo dani ebaanyɛ egbe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ni nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to mix four different farm chemicals together into one spray tank to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ejwɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baafutu mli yɛ tsɔne kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Yes, farmers often use multi-action or four-in-one chemical mixtures to fight insects, fungi, and boost growth all at once, as long as the chemicals are compatible and mixed in the correct proportions.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ tsofai babaoo loo ejwɛ ni akɛfee ekome tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwu ashi kooloi bibii, ŋmeii kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ shikome. Shii abɔ ni tsofai lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee ni akɛfutuɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to re-apply pesticide on my farm every six days instead of spraying just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ daa gbii enumɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛshwie nɔ shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical protection weakens after about six days, and new leaves grow out without protection. Regular spraying intervals ensure newly hatched pests and fresh plant growth are constantly protected.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ aaafee gbii enumɔ sɛɛ. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ ni abuuu he. Be ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ daa lɛ haa abuɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee kɛ tsei heei ni eda lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I need to use wooden sticks to support my tomato plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso atsu nii kɛfi mi-tomato tsei lɛ asɛɛ be mli ni miduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Staking holds the plant off the wet soil, preventing leaves and fruits from rotting. It also improves airflow and makes it much easier to spray chemicals evenly underneath the leaves.
ga: Staking haaa tso lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai kɛ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafite. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaashwie tsofa lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: What causes severe crop diseases to spread through an entire farm so fast and destroy everything?
