ga: Mɛni haa tsei ahe hela ko ni naa wa gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ ko mli oya ni efiteɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Aggressive viral or fungal disease outbreaks spread rapidly through wind, rain, and contaminated tools. Once inside the plant, they block water and nutrient flow, causing the crop to collapse rapidly.
ga: Virus loo fungal helai ni naa wa ni baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ. Kɛji obote nitsumɔhe lɛ Ebaatsi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi oya

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are burning from strong chemicals or suffering from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni mli wa eshã mitso lɛ baai lɛ loo hela emɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical burn usually causes rapid, crisp brown edges right after spraying. Disease damage usually starts as small spreading spots, yellowing patches, or mold that develops gradually over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni shãa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, helai ni fiteɔ mɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ fiofio lɛ. lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli

english: Why do my crops suddenly look weak and miserable even after I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ trukaa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: If the roots or stems are already damaged by a severe fungal disease or insect attack, the plant cannot absorb the fertilizer you apply, causing it to wilt despite receiving nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ lɛ efite shishifãi loo tsei lɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ po.

english: Why do pests keep damaging my crops even after I spray them with strong chemical mixtures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Pests can survive if the spray does not coat the leaves properly, if the chemical has degraded after several days, or if the pests have built resistance to that specific chemical over time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ efɔɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shi. Kɛji tsofa lɛ fite yɛ gbii komɛi asɛɛ loo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ma hewalɛ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ nakai tsofa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: If I have a small piece of land, why is it better to grow vegetables like tomatoes instead of maize?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu aduawai tamɔ tomato moŋ fe ŋmãa?

english: Maize sells for a low price per bag and requires a large field to make a reasonable income. Vegetables like tomatoes or chilies are high-value crops, meaning you can sell a smaller harvest for a much higher price and make a good profit even on small land.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa jara baa shi yɛ kotoku kome mli, ni ebiɔ he ko ni da koni anyɛ ana shika ni sa. Aduawai tamɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa nɔ, ni oná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔji bibii po anɔ.

english: Why do chili pepper plants make more money for farmers than traditional staple grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ chili tsei haa okwaafoi náa shika babaoo fe blema ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Chili peppers are constantly in high demand in Ghanaian markets for cooking. Because you can pick peppers multiple times from the same plant over several months, the continuous yield brings in higher total sales compared to a single harvest of grain.
ga: Chili pepper ji nɔ ni ataoɔ waa yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛha niyenii homɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ atsu nii shii abɔ kɛjɛ tso kome mli yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii ni afeɔ daa lɛ haa nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmaa ni akpaa shikome lɛ he.

english: Why do high-value crops like tomatoes require me to spend money upfront before I see any returns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa tamɔ tomato biɔ ni mawo nyɔmɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ dani mana nɔ ko ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ?

english: High-value crops are like fast-growing livestock—they need quality seeds, good fertilizer, and pest protection to produce top-quality fruits. Investing a little money early gives the plants the strength to produce a massive yield that pays back your investment.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni jara wa waa lɛ tamɔ kooloi ni daa oya. Amɛmiitao dumɔwui ni hi, ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahebuu koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛ shika awo mli fioo mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛ shika babaoo aba ni ekɛwo shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers sometimes dry up and drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Giving the plants steady water and adding compost or manure provides the strength needed for the flowers to set into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni esaaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛto tomatoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ama shi.

english: How do I decide whether to invest my money in growing peppers or growing maize this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ mishika baawo ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Compare your field size and target earnings. If you have limited land and want maximum income, choose peppers because their market value per basket is high; if you have large land and want low-maintenance crops mainly for family food, choose maize.
ga: Okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ shika ni okɛtaoɔ lɛ ato he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ oyɔɔ ni oosumɔ shika babaoo lɛ Halamɔ chili peppers ejaakɛ jara ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi kome mli lɛ fa. Kɛji oyɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa tsɔ lɛ he miihia bo koni okɛye oweku lɛ niyenii titri. Halamɔ ŋmãa

english: Why do tomato plants need to be tied to wooden stakes while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tomato tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As tomatoes grow heavy with fruit, their stems become too weak to stand upright. Tying them to wooden stakes keeps the fruit off the wet ground, preventing rot, soil pests, and disease while making harvesting much easier.
ga: Beni tomatoi lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ, no mli lɛ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛfi tso ko he lɛ, ehaa aduawai lɛ taraaa hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai anaa yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa

english: Why do high-value vegetables get attacked by pests more often than maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa aduawai ni jara wa waa lɛ shii abɔ fe ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants like peppers and tomatoes have soft leaves and juicy, sweet fruits that attract insects easily. Hardier crops like cassava and maize have tougher leaves and protective husks that naturally repel many common farm pests.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ shito kɛ tomato yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ, ni mli ewo muji ni gbalaa koolooi oya. Tsei ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ baai ni wa kɛ ŋmãa ni buɔ mɔ he ni shwieɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo.

english: Why do vegetable crops require more frequent watering than cereal crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni afɔ aduawai aŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu shii abɔ fe ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Vegetables have shallow root systems and build juicy fruits that consist mostly of water. Unlike maize, which can send roots deeper to survive short dry spells, vegetables will wilt quickly and drop their fruit without regular moisture.
ga: Aduawai yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni mli ewo muji babaoo. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ ŋmãa, ni baanyɛ atswa shishifãi kɛya shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli. Aduawai baagboi oya ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli daa.

english: Why do pepper plants produce small, yellowish leaves and few fruits when grown in tired soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu pepper tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, amɛwoɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants are heavy feeders that need rich nutrients to produce bright green leaves and many fruits. Pale yellow leaves mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which can be corrected by adding well-rotted animal manure or fertilizer.
ga: Pepper tsei ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ niyenii ni mli wa koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ aduawai babaoo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo kooloi ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the price of fresh tomatoes in Ghana change so drastically between seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato hee ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jara tsakeɔ waa yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ?

english: Most farmers plant tomatoes during the major rainy season, creating a huge market supply that drives prices down. During the dry season, fewer farmers can irrigate tomatoes, so supply drops and buyers pay much higher prices for the limited harvest.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo duɔ tomato yɛ nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii babaoo baa jara nɔ, ni no haa tomato jara baa shi. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Okwaafoi baanyɛ afɔ tomato fioo ko nɔ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe baahia ni tomatoi ni akɛhaa kɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ awo nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa kɛha ŋmaa fioo ko.

english: Why do the bottom leaves on my maize plants turn yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient the plant needs to build food and form big, heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow when I cut down all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full sun; shade trees protect them from extreme heat and help keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava plants rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water around cassava roots, it suffocates the roots and creates the right environment for rotting fungi to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ he fɛɛ he. cassava root Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ adalɛ baa.

english: Can I plant coffee trees in the dry parts of northern Ghana, or do they only do well in forest areas?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kɔfi tsei yɛ hei ni nu bɛ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ? Aloo ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ lɛ pɛ?

english: Coffee trees need high rainfall and cooler conditions found in forest zones, so they produce poorly in hot, dry northern climates.
ga: Kɔfi tsei biɔ nugbɔshiimɔ babaoo kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ fe nɔ ni anaa yɛ kooi amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ewooo yibii kpakpai yɛ kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit when the hot season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, causing the plant to drop its blooms instead of turning them into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites, or viruses passed on by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ

english: Planting maize too close forces the plants to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stems and small, empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baa.

english: Why is it important for me to trim or prune branches off my coffee trees after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-coffee tsei lɛ amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes old, unproductive branches and allows sunlight to reach the inner tree, encouraging new shoots that will bear fresh berries next season.
ga: Niji ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ, ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Ekanyaa tsei heei ni baawo yibii heei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the plant leaves turn yellow and dry up, and the inner lining of the groundnut shells shows dark vein patterns.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni ŋmei ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ jieɔ ŋmei diji ni mli edɔ lɛ he mfoniri ko kpo.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my hybrid maize crop last year yield much less when I plant them again this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo kwraa beni midu ekoŋŋ afi nɛɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give strong yields only in their first generation; planting saved hybrid seeds causes the crop to lose its yield vigor.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere lɛ ni aaadu lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing small holes and white patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii yɛŋ?

english: Small holes and ragged white patches on young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the crop. Treating the central whorl of the plant early helps prevent the pest from destroying the growing tip and reducing your grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe lɛ baa. Tsɔɔmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ, ni ehaa oŋmaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water mold fungus that thrives in excess shade and high humidity. Pruning overgrown tree branches lets sunlight into the farm and improves air circulation, which keeps the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo mli. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why should I plant my yams on high soil mounds instead of directly on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand their tubers without obstruction. High mounds provide soft earth for long tuber growth and protect the roots from sitting in stagnant water, which prevents root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes koni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko etsĩii amɛ gbɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛha tuber dalɛ, ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe koni amɛkabote nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge tubers in one field but very thin ones in another field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers struggle to grow thick in compacted or heavy clay soils because the hard ground restricts expansion. Fields with loose, sandy-loam soil allow the roots to easily swell into full-sized tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ tsiɔ shweremɔ naa. Gbɛjegbɛi ni sũ ni mli tse ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baafu ni amɛtsɔ bulbs ni dalɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my seeds right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often moistens only the top layer of soil and is frequently followed by a dry heat spell. Sowing too early causes seeds to germinate and then dry up before the full rainy season stably begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fũuɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, la ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when day or night temperatures get extremely high because intense heat damages the pollen, preventing pollination and fruit setup.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa shwane loo gbɛkɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Etsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or beans together with my maize make the maize stalks look greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. Maize plants take up this natural nitrogen, which promotes healthy green leaf growth and better yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi tsei kɛ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii. ni haa baai eŋɔli ni mli wa lɛ daa ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa

english: Why should I leave dry maize leaves on the ground around my vegetables instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmãa baai ni egbi lɛ mabɔle mihe? Aduawai moŋ fe ni abaashã?

english: Covering the ground with dry maize leaves creates mulch that blocks direct sunlight, holds soil moisture during hot days, and gradually rots into natural plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ baa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: How do I know that my plantain bunch is ripe enough to harvest before the birds eat it on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain tsei lɛ ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa dani okpoi lɛ aye amɛ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Plantain is ready for harvest when the individual fingers lose their sharp green corners and become full and rounded, and when the top leaves of the plant start turning yellow naturally.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni nineshi nine fɛɛ nine ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. kɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yiteŋ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Why do weevils attack my harvested maize in storage even when the bags are tightly sealed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ nitoohe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ atsĩ kotokui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs are often laid inside the seeds while the maize is still in the field. If the grain is not dried completely to a hard, low-moisture state before storage, those hidden eggs will hatch inside the bags and eat the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa kɛyashi ebaawa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Nakai ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni eyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do crops like cocoa grow very well in the southern part of Ghana but struggle in the north?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ lɛ? Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ?

english: Southern Ghana has a forest zone with high rainfall, humid air, and rich moist soils which cocoa trees need to thrive. In contrast, the northern savannah is much hotter and drier with long dry seasons that cause cocoa plants to dry up.
ga: Ghana kooyigbɛ yɛ kooi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mli, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa ni kookoo tsei lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ enɛ lɛ, Kooyigbɛ savannah lɛ mli edɔ waa ni egbiɔ, ni hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ haa kookoo tsei lɛ gbiɔ.

english: What kind of cash crops can I plant if my farm is located in the dry northern savannah region?
ga: Mɛɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ Savannah kooyigbɛ he ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: In the drier northern savannah zone, cash crops like cashew, shea, mango, and sesame do best because they have deep root systems and can naturally withstand heat and long periods without rain.
ga: Yɛ Savannah kooyigbɛ kpokpai ni mli egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ, shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cashew, chia, mango kɛ sesame tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ adebɔɔ mli latsaa kɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Without shade from larger trees or companion plants like plantains to shelter them, intense sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tso agbo ko loo nanemɛi tso ko ni he wa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why is my old cocoa farm producing much fewer pods now than it did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow old, their internal channels for carrying water and food get weak, soil nutrients become exhausted, and the trees become more vulnerable to diseases, causing their yield to drop naturally.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii yaa mli lɛ baa shi. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Ni tso lɛ baafee mɔ ni helai baanyɛ aba enɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is the main difference between a cash crop like cocoa and regular food crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ niyenii ni afɔɔ feemɔ tamɔ ŋmãa teŋ?

english: Food crops like maize or cassava are grown primarily to feed your family directly and are harvested quickly, while cash crops like cocoa or cashew are grown mainly to be sold in markets for long-term income.
ga: Aduɔ niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛha oweku lɛ niyenii ni akpaa oya. Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ shika nibii tamɔ kookoo loo cashew ŋmeii titri koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ koni akɛná shika ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why does it take several years for cash crops like cocoa or cashew trees to start producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo cashew tsei jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Tree cash crops spend their first few years building strong trunks and deep underground root systems to support decades of harvest, unlike annual crops that produce food and die within a single season.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ jwɛi mli lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ maa tsei akutsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni amɛkɛye amɛbua afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ afi tsei ni woɔ niyenii ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ.

english: Why do crops in the northern savannah need deeper root systems than crops growing in southern forest areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ kooi lɛ amli lɛ biɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ fe nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ anaigbɛ kooi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: In the savannah, water sits deep beneath the ground because rain falls less often. Crops there must grow long, deep roots to search for underground moisture during dry months.
ga: Yɛ Savannah lɛ, nu lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ejaakɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ shii abɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ shishifãi kakadaji ni mli kwɔ koni amɛtao shikpɔŋ shishi nu yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cashew trees together with cocoa trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu cashew tsei kɛ cocoa tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is not ideal because cashew trees thrive in open, hot, and drier conditions, while cocoa trees need shade and high humidity. Trying to grow them together makes it hard for both to get their ideal environment.
ga: Enɛ ejaaa ejaakɛ cashew tsei lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli tse, ni mli edɔ, ni jɛmɛ egbi, yɛ be mli ni cocoa tsei biɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni amɛfee ekome kɛdara lɛ haa ewaa ahaa gbalashihilɛ mli hefatalɔi lɛ akɛ amɛaashɛ shihilɛ ni sa jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: How do tree crops in the southern forest zone help keep the soil fertile for farming?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ kooi ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa okwaayeli?

english: Forest trees continuously drop leaves and small twigs onto the ground. As these decay, they turn into rich organic fertilizer that feeds the soil and keeps it moist.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ shwie amɛbaai kɛ amɛniji bibii lɛ anɔ. be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ nibii nɛɛ fite lɛ Amɛbafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does heavy rain in the forest zone affect the food in the soil for my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ kooi amli lɛ saa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains can wash soluble plant nutrients deep into the ground where shallow roots cannot reach them—a process called leaching. Adding organic matter helps hold those nutrients near the surface.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsei amli niyenii ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear all the grass and weeds off my field before planting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Clearing the land removes wild weeds that fight with your corn for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When the field is clean, young corn seedlings can grow strong root systems without being choked or shaded out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ koo mli jwɛi ni kɛ ŋmãa lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ he lɛ he tse Abele dumɔwui bibii lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe.

english: If crops from your last harvest grew slowly, had thin stalks, or produced small cobs with pale leaves, your soil is exhausted. Adding fertilizer replenishes key nutrients like nitrogen so new crops can thrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpa yɛ naagbee lɛ mli lɛ miida blɛoo, eyɛ ŋmeii bibii, loo eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efo ohe. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni tsei heei anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How exactly does adding fertilizer help my maize crops produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for plants, supplying essential minerals that soil loses over time. It gives corn the energy to grow thick stalks, dark green leaves, and fully filled cobs.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Kɛtsɔ shika tsuru ni he hiaa ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni laajeɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmãa ni mli tse. baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi kɛ dumɔwui

english: Why do the leaves on my corn plants roll up tightly during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up as a natural defense against hot sun to conserve moisture. By rolling inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to heat so it loses less water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ nɔ Tsei haa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ.

english: Why do certified seeds bought from an officer yield more than the corn seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ maŋ onukpa ko dɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred hybrids designed for high yield and disease resistance. Seeds saved from past harvests lose these strong traits over time, resulting in smaller cobs and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: What causes some of my corn plants to grow tall but produce very small or empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: Tall plants with small cobs usually suffer from a lack of nutrients during the flowering stage or were planted too close together, forcing them to spend all their energy growing tall instead of filling out cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ loo aduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii koni amɛdara yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: How many bags of maize can I reasonably expect to harvest from one acre of land?
ga: Abele kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: With good quality certified seeds, proper spacing, and correct fertilizer use, an acre can yield around 2 to 3 large bags of maize, whereas poor seed or exhausted soil may yield less than 1 bag per acre.
ga: Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ nɔ lɛ, sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Acre kome baanyɛ aha ŋmãa kotokui wuji 2 kɛyashi 3, yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ni shɛɛɛ kotoku 1 yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why is it important for me to measure my land in acres before buying seeds and fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ acre mli dani mahe dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Knowing your exact acreage helps you buy the correct amount of seeds and fertilizer. Using too little starves your crops, while using too much wastes money and can burn your plants.
ga: Kɛ́ ole he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohé dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni efiteɔ shika babaoo ni ehaa tsei lɛ shãa.

english: What happens to my maize crops if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and small, underdeveloped cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni edako lɛ baa.

english: Why do my corn stalks break and fall over easily before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Corn plants fall over (known as lodging) when stalks are weak due to lack of nutrients, pest damage to roots, or being planted in soil that hasn't been cleared and tilled properly to support strong roots.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shĩa) kɛji tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hewɔ, kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, loo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ewo shishifãi ni wa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field when I am resting the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Plants in the bean family have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them during a break restores soil fertility naturally so your next crops grow much stronger.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ legume weku lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara babaoo.

english: Is it true that burying green weeds into my soil before planting helps my crops yield better?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ jwɛi eŋɔli ni mikɛfuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, burying green plant material allows it to rot directly in the ground, creating organic matter that feeds beneficial soil organisms, holds moisture, and slowly releases rich nutrients to your crop roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni ooofu lɛ baaha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ejieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛyaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli fiofio.

english: How do the roots of cassava affect my farm soil after I harvest them?
ga: Te ŋmei shishifãi lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots feed heavily on soil nutrients to grow large tubers, which can leave the ground tired. Rotating cassava with leguminous crops like beans helps restore the missing nutrients back to the land.
ga: Cassava shishifãi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kasava ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni elaaje lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does that stubborn bush weed keep coming back so quickly even after I burn my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya nɛkɛ beni mishã ŋmɔ lɛ dani midu lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning off top vegetation triggers dormant seeds buried in the earth to germinate and leaves deep roots alive underground. Clearing by slashing and leaving cover crops smothers those weeds without waking them up.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ashãa lɛ haa dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ ni afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛshiɔ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛhaa he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbeɔ nakai jwɛi lɛ ni ehaaa amɛhe afee gbeyei.

english: Why does my soil get hard and stop absorbing rainwater after a few years of continuous farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ekpaa nugbɔ nu lɛ ŋmɔmɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi ni mikɛtsu okwaayeli ni mikɛtee nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without adding organic matter breaks down the natural structure of the soil. Adding animal manure, plant mulches, or leaving deep-rooted plants helps open up channels for water to sink in.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni akɛbaafata he, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni agbele gbɛ ko ni nu lɛ baatsɔ mli.

english: What causes my maize leaves to turn yellow at the tips even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key plant food. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep past the reach of young roots, or the soil may simply be depleted from previous crop harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during strong winds, even when they have many green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread near the surface rather than going deep. If the root system gets damaged by soil pests like nematodes or waterlogged ground, the plant loses its anchor and falls.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeeya shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Tso lɛ baafite eŋmei lɛ ni ebaagbee shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when the ground around them is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in damp soil is often caused by root rot or bacterial wilt living in the ground. Excess moisture combined with poor drainage starves the roots of air and allows root diseases to destroy the plant's water pipes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni fiteɔ trukaa lɛ kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi ahe helai fiteɔ tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam mounds dry out and bake during the hot season, causing my tubers to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ mli lɛ egbi ni ashãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ehaa miyitso feɔ bibioo

english: Bare soil mounds lose moisture rapidly under direct sunlight. Covering your yam mounds with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool, preserves moisture, and creates a soft environment for tubers to expand.
ga: Gɔji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni oha shihilɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo aba koni tubers lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: How do shade trees in my cocoa farm help my cocoa trees produce more pods in the long run?
ga: Te tsei ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa from scorching sun, block heavy winds, and drop falling leaves that decay into rich natural fertilizer, keeping the root zone moist and healthy for long-term pod production.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa, ni amɛfiteɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha pod feemɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted poultry manure helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do elders advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them restores soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce very small yields when I plant many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow healthy and yield large tubers or fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo bulbs loo aduawai wuji.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make the food that grows the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so all leaves get full sunlight while protecting them from fungal diseases in wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli. Staking woɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu he.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo tsei bibii adu dumɔwui?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that create living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving soil moisture during its critical first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2-3 lɛ mli lɛ he miihia

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting in the soil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does sorghum survive drought in Northern Ghana much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni ba yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has a deep, dense root system that searches far underground for water, and its leaves automatically roll up during hot dry spells to conserve moisture, whereas maize loses water quickly through its leaves.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ana nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu hulutsoo be lɛ he. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, nu fiteɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes with ragged edges in young maize shoots are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the plant. Identifying them early and applying organic treatments like neem oil or appropriate sprays stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ayɔse amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hela ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. kɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a plant virus spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. Managing whiteflies early with sticky traps or soap-and-neem sprays prevents the virus from stunting your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni foɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli ni akɛ tsɔne ni shwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ whiteflies nɔ Loo samla kɛ neem ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or severe dry spells. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root area during hot periods helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ He ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I keep farming and harvesting crops all year round when the rains stop for months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu okwaayeli ni makpa ŋmɔshi nii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: To farm all year round, you must move away from relying only on rainfall by setting up simple irrigation systems, like fetching water from small wells or using hose pipes and drip lines, to keep the soil moist during the dry season.
ga: yɛ okwaayeli mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ Ehe miihia ni okpa nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ okɛ ohe afɔ̃ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ rɔba hose kɛ drip line atsu nii. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die whenever the rain stops falling for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crops need water to transport essential nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. When the rain stops and the ground dries up, the plant starves and dries out under the hot sun.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni he hia kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ Tsei lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the planting months that my fathers taught me no longer working for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nyɔji ni akɛduɔ nii ni Ataa tsɔɔ wɔ lɛ tsuuu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns have changed over time, making rainfall unpredictable. Relying solely on historical calendars can cause seeds to dry up in dusty soil, so farmers now need water systems or drought-resistant seeds to protect their investments.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ehaa anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ aha. Yinɔsane mli kalandai pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ, no hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi lɛ hia dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni nyɛɔ nu loo hɔmɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu amɛshika ni amɛkɛwo mli lɛ he.

english: Why do seeds I put in the ground fail to sprout when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kwɛɛɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds are dormant until water softens their outer shell and signals them to start growing. Without moisture in the soil, the seed remains asleep or gets scorched by the hot earth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he amɛhi shi kɛyashi nu baaha kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ afee blɛoo ni etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi dalɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he amɛwɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã amɛ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and grow so slowly during dry periods even if I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛdaraa fiofio yɛ fɛ̃i be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they close tiny pores on their leaves to prevent moisture loss. This saves their lives but also stops them from breathing in nutrients needed to grow bigger.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaŋã bu bibioo lɛ. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite Enɛ hereɔ amɛwala shi ehaa amɛmuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ hu.

english: If my crop leaves start drooping because of lack of rain, can watering them bring them back to life?
ga: Kɛji mi tsei lɛ baai lɛ bɔi gbee yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ hewɔ lɛ Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ?

english: If you water plants quickly when they first droop, their leaves will fill with water and stand up straight again. However, if they stay dry for too long, the leaves burn permanently and cannot recover.
ga: Kɛji okɛ nu ha tso lɛ oya beni egbee shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Ebaai lɛ baayi kɛ nu ni amɛbaadamɔ shi ekoŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ ashi amɛ ni amɛgbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ. Baai lɛ shãa kɛyaa naanɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsa.

english: How does covering my soil with dried grass or leaves help my crops survive dry weather?
ga: Te baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering your crop beds with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a shade block. It keeps the sun off the bare earth, keeping the soil cool and stopping wetness from evaporating into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha odumɔ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops have enough water in the root zone without waiting for rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni mimɛɛɛ nugbɔ?

english: Push your finger about two inches deep into the soil near the plant. If the earth feels cool and sticks slightly to your skin, there is enough water; if it feels dusty and dry, your crops need watering immediately.
ga: Nyɛɛ onine nɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nu he akɛ edɔ fioo ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ ohewolo he lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lolo. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ sũ ni egbi Ehe miihia ni okɛ nu awo Onibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Which crops can I plant on my farm that do not require continuous rainfall to yield well?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and certain types of cowpeas have deep root systems or tough leaves that retain moisture, allowing them to yield food even when rain is scarce.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tsina ŋmãa komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo po nɛ.

english: What simple method can I use to feed water directly to my crop roots without wasting water?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha nu tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛdu shishifãi ni nu afiteee?

english: Using a drip irrigation system or placing plastic bottles with small holes near the base of your plants feeds water directly to the roots drop by drop, preventing waste from sun evaporation.
ga: Kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo plastic kɔɔpoo ni bu bibioo ko yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, akɛ nu yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Koni abu jwɛi he kɛjɛ hulu la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the cobs are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to stay green and grow strong cobs. This often happens if the soil is exhausted or if heavy rains have washed nutrients away.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil, leading to weaker crops each year.
ga: Abele ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa abele lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: Why are the young flowers on my cocoa trees falling off instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree experiences stress from hot weather, prolonged dry spells, too much direct sunlight, or attacks by small insects like mirids that feed on delicate flower stems.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ashwishwɛi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever heavy rains and wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow roots and heavy tops. Tiny worms in the soil called nematodes or root rot can weaken these shallow roots, making the heavy plant topple over under wind or weight of the fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii. Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni eha tsei ni tsii lɛ ajɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo aduawai lɛ amli tsiimɔ mli amɛgbee shi.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I even dig them up for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ po koni mikɛkpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when the soil holds too much water during heavy rains without proper drainage. Waterlogged soil prevents the roots from breathing and encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots inside the storage barn before it is time to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani dumɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally sprout in storage as the atmosphere warms up before the rainy season because the tuber senses the climate changing and prepares to grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ yɛ nitoohe lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛdu wain tsei heei.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and the leaves looking small and bunched up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Ni baai lɛ tamɔ bibii ni amɛbua amɛhe naa?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and lack of water which causes the plant to curl its leaves to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni nu akafite.

english: Pepper plants automatically drop their blossoms during very hot weather to conserve moisture and energy, preventing the plant from getting too weak to survive the heat.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baa fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbu fɛ̃i kɛ hewalɛ he. Tsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew large holes through my cabbage leaves so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ buji wuji amli kɛtsɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage leaves are soft and nutritious, attracting moths that lay tiny eggs under the leaves. When weather is warm, these eggs hatch quickly into hungry caterpillars that feed continuously on the leaves.
ga: Kaabeji baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Egbalaa ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ wuji nɛɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crop so that it works well?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied into moist soil right after a light rain or early in the morning, giving the plant roots time to drink it in before heavy rains wash it away or dry sun evaporates it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo leebi maŋkpa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ loo hulu ni miigbi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young maize plants roll up their leaves tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward as a natural defense mechanism to shrink the leaf area exposed to direct sunlight, which helps them reduce water loss through evaporation during high heat.
ga: Abele shwieɔ ebaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa baai lɛ ahe hei ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ashwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the long dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves naturally during severe dry spells to conserve water and protect the stem and roots. The plant goes dormant rather than dying, and it will sprout fresh green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Tso lɛ baaho shi yɛ gbele najiaŋ. Ni baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn brown when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Large canopy trees provide essential shade, lower the surrounding air temperature, and maintain the soil moisture young cocoa plants need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa. Tsɔɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa cacao tsei bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my plantain produce very small bunches when I let all the small shoots keep growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bibii nɛkɛ beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal essential water and soil nutrients from the main plantain stem. Removing surplus suckers leaves enough food for the primary stem to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii loo suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ yitso lɛ koni efee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without setting any fruits when the sun becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress that dries up tomato pollen, preventing flowers from fertilizing properly. When pollination fails, the plant aborts the unfertilized flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni haa tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ baa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ baashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ ashwie koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cowpea roots have small round bumps on them, and are these bumps a sign of disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ni ani nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji hela he okadi?

english: Those bumps are root nodules filled with beneficial soil bacteria. These friendly microbes capture nitrogen from the air and turn it into free, high-quality plant food that feeds your crops and enriches your soil.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji shishifãi ni eyi obɔ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ tsei aniyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni ewajeɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on before I can get big underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa ni ekɛ tso kakadaŋŋ akwɔ dani enyɛ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves require direct exposure to sunlight to create the energy necessary to build heavy underground tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the ground where they can catch sunlight and stay free from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii. Ajieɔ staking lifts kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ, ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting upward and curling into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a viral infection transmitted by insects that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does lowland swamp rice grow well in standing water while my other crops rot and die in waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Mi nɔ lɛ miifite ni miigbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Lowland rice has special internal air tubes within its stems that carry oxygen down to the roots underwater. The standing water also suffocates common farm weeds, giving rice an advantage.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ mli yɛ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni haa ŋmãa náa sɛɛnamɔ

english: Why do cassava roots rot under the ground if heavy rains leave water sitting on the farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air within the soil to stay alive. When heavy water stays trapped in the soil, it cuts off oxygen supply, causing underground roots to suffocate and rot rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji akɛ muji lɛ tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: How can I kill an old tree stump on my farm without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbe tsei akutsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: You can kill an unwanted tree stump by cutting off the top, digging or drilling a hole deep into the trunk, filling that hole with salt, and covering it. The salt draws out all the moisture inside the stump, preventing it from sprouting new shoots and causing it to dry out and die.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbe ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ loo gbá bu ko ni mli kwɔ awo tso lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋoo awo bu lɛ mli ni okɛha nɔ. Nu lɛ gbalaa nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does salt kill tree stumps when I pour it inside a hole cut into the wood?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei gbe tsei akutsei beni mikɛshwieɔ bu ko ni afo yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Salt acts as a powerful drying agent. When placed inside the living trunk of a tree or stump, it pulls water out of the plant's cells through a process called osmosis. Without water, the tree tissues starve, dry out, and rot.
ga: Nuŋ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso loo shishifã ni hiɛ ka lɛ mli lɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ osmosis lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei amli fãji lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ, amɛbaagbi, ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Can I plant cassava and plantain on the same piece of land where I have planted young mango trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ mango tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop plantains and cassava with young mango trees. Because mango trees grow slowly at first, short-term food crops like plantain and cassava give you early harvests while providing beneficial shade and ground cover for the young mango seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmei dumɔwui kɛ mango tsei bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mango tso lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shishijee mli. Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa oya Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa mango tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: In what order should I plant food crops when starting a permanent fruit farm with mangoes?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli esa akɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mije aduawai ŋmɔ ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ shishi kɛ mango?

english: It is best to plant your main tree crop, like mangoes, first or alongside fast-growing shade crops like plantains. After establishing the mangoes, you can fill the surrounding spaces with food crops like cassava, making sure to leave enough space around each mango tree so it isn't choked.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tso titri ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo, tamɔ mango, dani okɛ shade tsei krokomɛi ni daa oya lɛ afata he. Beni obɔ mango lɛ sɛɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ ŋmei awo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli, ni okwɛ koni he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi mango tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he koni ekɛtsi ehe kɛjɛ he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ he.

english: How long does a mango tree take to grow and start giving fruits after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango tso ko daa ni ebɔi yibiiwoo beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A standard mango tree planted from seed takes about 4 to 6 years to start producing fruit. However, if you plant grafted mango seedlings, they grow faster and can begin fruiting within 2 to 3 years.
ga: Mango tso ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 6 dani ebɔi yibiiwoo. Shi, kɛji akɛ odu mango dumɔwu ni akɛwo mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli.

english: How does a plantain sucker grow into a full mature plant that produces fruit?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni plantain sucker lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii?

english: A plantain sucker grows from an underground root system called a corm. As it absorbs water and soil nutrients, it shoots out green leaves that roll out from the center, forming a thick stem. After about 9 to 12 months, a big flower emerges from the top, which then develops into a bunch of plantains.
ga: Sucker dumɔwui lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ rhizome lɛ mli. beni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Baai eŋɔli baajɛ teŋgbɛ, ni efee tsei ni mli tse. Yɛ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi agboi baaje kpo kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛkɛ lɛ, etsɔɔ plantains kuu ko.

english: How do cassava stem cuttings transform into mature cassava tubers underground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso ni afoɔ lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmei shishifã ni eda kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When you plant a cassava stem cutting in moist soil, small roots sprout from the buried nodes. Over the next few months, the leaves process sunlight to feed the plant, causing several of those underground roots to swell up and store starch, forming the thick tubers you harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii baakwɛ̃ kɛjɛ ŋmei ni afu lɛ mli. Yɛ nyɔji fioo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ, baai lɛ tsuɔ hulu la he nii koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fũuɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ebafeɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ ni obaanyɛ okpa.

english: How many times each year do I need to clear weeds from my cassava farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi mli?

english: You generally need to weed a cassava farm 3 to 4 times during the first six months. Once the cassava plants grow tall and form a dense canopy of leaves, they block sunlight from reaching the ground, naturally slowing down weed growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ jwɛi awo o-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enumɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ da ni efee baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, Ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How often should I weed around my young mango trees every year?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ mi mango tso lɛ he daa afi?

english: Young mango trees should be weeded about 3 to 4 times a year, particularly during the rainy season when weeds grow rapidly. Keeping a clean circle around the base of each tree prevents weeds from stealing water and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie mango tsei lɛ shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ kooloo ko ni he tse bɔle tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches even when I weed around them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi miibɔle he moŋ Eyɛ mli akɛ eji daa moŋ

english: Weeding helps, but plantains often produce small bunches if too many suckers grow from the same base, competing for soil nutrients. To get larger bunches, prune away extra shoots so that only 2 or 3 strong stems remain per plantain stand.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi plantains lɛ fɔɔ feemɔ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni miida kɛmiijɛ shishitoo kome mli lɛ miitswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi plantain kome mli.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build strong roots and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight, which the plant uses to make food for growing big tubers underground. Keeping leaves off the damp soil also prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Akɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛduɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant starves itself by moving whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei yeɔ amɛhe hɔmɔ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the exact same nutrients year after year. It also allows specific soil pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in large numbers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ aba afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi pɔtɛɛi kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa babaoo.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass help them grow?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating in the hot sun, keeps the crop roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants instead of growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from environmental stress, such as intense heat, irregular watering, or dry winds. The plant drops flowers to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ miikpe amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long due to poor drainage. Excessive water starves the roots of air and creates ideal conditions for soil fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ amli nu fiteɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites, thrips, or aphids sucking sap from the tender leaves, or by a viral infection spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leaves but produce very few bean pods when I give them rich manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ha amɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally produce their own nitrogen with the help of beneficial bacteria in their roots. Adding extra nitrogen-rich manure tricks the plant into using its energy for heavy leaf growth instead of flowering and setting pods.
ga: Cowpea feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ helatsɛmɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ayebuamɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii kɛha baai ni tsii ni baakwɛ̃. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pods awo mli lɛ

english: Why do my crops keep falling sick even when I plant at the right time of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Kɛji midu yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ be lɛ mli po.

english: Crop sickness usually happens when plants are stressed by weak soil, poor air circulation, or hidden pests. Even with good planting timing, crops need active care like proper spacing, weeding, and balanced nutrients so they stay strong enough to resist diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai baa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ miigba tsei anaa. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei kpakpai yɛ ni akɛduɔ nii moŋ, shi ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsei anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ nɔ lolo, tamɔ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ niyenii ni ja Koni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai

english: How can I tell if my crops are catching a sickness early before it destroys my entire harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya dani efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Early warning signs include leaves turning yellow out of season, dark spots appearing on foliage or stems, stunted growth, or wilting during the cooler parts of the day. Checking your farm regularly allows you to spot these signs and act before the disease spreads.
ga: Kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ mra lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni sa mli. Hei diji jeɔ kpo yɛ baai loo tsei lɛ anɔ. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shwiemɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii nɛɛ ni ofee nɔ ko dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops look healthy while mine in the next plot are dying from disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni mi nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ hela miigbe lɛ lɛ?
