english: Plants get sick when small management details are missed. If diseased plant materials are left in the field, weeds are left to multiply, or plants are not fed properly, disease organisms build up quickly on one plot even if the next plot remains healthy.
ga: Tsei yeɔ hela kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he saji bibii amli fitsofitso kɛji akɛ ashi tsei ahe nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Aŋmɛɔ jwɛi gbɛ koni amɛshwere. aloo ahaaa amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ Helai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo po.

english: Does planting my seeds too close together make my crops more likely to get sick?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni miduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa hela mɔɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes. When crops are planted too close together, leaves touch and trap damp air between plants. This dark, humid environment allows plant diseases and fungi to grow rapidly and spread easily from one stalk to another.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ taa amɛhe ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmeii daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ oya.

english: What basic things can I do on my farm to prevent crop diseases before they even start?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛtsi tsei ahe helai anaa dani amɛje shishi amɛgbɛ amɛshwã?

english: Preventive care includes removing and burning already diseased plants, giving crops adequate spacing, keeping weeds controlled, and applying good compost or fertilizer. Caring for plants early keeps their immune defenses high so diseases cannot take hold.
ga: Nɔ ni fata helatsamɔ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ he ji tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ shãa. Ha gbɛ ni sa. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebaaye ebua ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Koni helai srɔtoi akaye nɔ.

english: Can poor soil quality cause my crops to catch sickness more easily?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baaha helai aba miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ oya?

english: Yes. Soil lacking essential nutrients produces weak crops that cannot defend themselves against pest and disease attacks. Nourishing your soil with compost or proper fertilizers makes your plants tough and resilient.
ga: Hɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ahe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli awa ni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows crop-specific diseases and pests to build up in the soil over time. Rotating different crops starves these soil-borne diseases, keeping your land healthy for future harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli daa lɛ baaha helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ kpamɔ.

english: Is it true that there are crop varieties that sickness cannot easily touch?
ga: Ani tsei sɔrɔtoi komɛi yɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni helai nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ amɛ awo mli oya?

english: Yes. Agricultural officers and seed producers supply improved crop varieties bred specifically to resist local pests and diseases. Planting these resistant seeds protects your farm naturally without needing extra chemical treatments.
ga: Hɛɛ. Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai lɛ haa. Dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ helai nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: How will planting permanent tree crops like oil palm help protect my farm against total failure?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mu tso lɛ adumɔ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekafite kwraa?

english: Oil palm trees are hardy, long-lasting crops that resist erratic weather and diseases better than delicate annual food crops. Once established, they provide a stable harvest and steady income even if seasonal crops suffer from pests or drought.
ga: Mu tsei ji tsei ni wa ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ helai ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ fe niyenii tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yeɔ daa afi lɛ. Kɛ ato amɛ shishi lɛ Amɛbaahã ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aba. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ be mli lɛ ahe amanehulu po lɛ,.

english: Is it wise for a smallholder farmer like me to plant tree crops alongside my seasonal food crops?
ga: Ani nilee yɛ mli akɛ okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo yɛ be mli niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Yes. Mixing long-term tree crops like oil palm with seasonal crops creates a balanced farm. Tree crops develop deep root systems that withstand harsh conditions, ensuring you still have a source of income if your seasonal crops get damaged.
ga: Hɛɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ mu tso, kɛ be mli nibii ni akɛfutuɔ. ŋmɔ ni ja ni afeɔ Herbaceous tsei lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai anaa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ona nɔmimaa akɛ oyɛ shika jɛɛhe lolo kɛji akɛ tsei ni okɛwoɔ be mli lɛ fite.

english: What is a good crop for me to start with if this is my very first time farming?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi kɛha mi akɛ mikɛje shishi kɛji akɛ enɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ be ni mifeɔ okwaayeli?

english: Cassava or maize are great starting crops because they are tough, require basic care, and grow well in most soil types across Ghana with strong local market demand.
ga: Cassava loo ŋmãa ji shishijee tsei ni hi ejaakɛ amɛhe wa. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji babaoo anɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ he ni maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow weak instead of producing full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daaa ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my pawpaw plants rot and fall over after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ fiteɔ ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees are very delicate plants with roots that rot easily when left in standing water, so they need high ground or well-drained soil to survive.
ga: Papaw tsei ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa. Eyɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia lɛ dani enyɛ ehi shi.

english: Pawpaw plants have different sexes, and male pawpaw trees only produce flowers to carry pollen to female trees, so they will never produce fruit themselves.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ yɛ bɔlɛnamɔi srɔtoi. Ni pawpaw tsei hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi pɛ koni amɛkɛ pollen aya tsei yei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, a be nyɛe maa wo yiblii ngɛ mɛ nitsɛmɛ a he wami nya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young pawpaw seedlings turning yellow and wilting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi paw paw dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Young pawpaw seedlings are very delicate and sensitive to heat shock, so yellowing leaves usually mean they are getting scorched by strong sun or are receiving too little water.
ga: Papaya dumɔwui lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ dɔlɛ mli lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu etswa amɛ loo nu fioo pɛ amɛnáa.

english: How can I protect my tender young crops from breaking during heavy winds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkakumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: Planting a boundary line of tall grasses or trees along the edges of your farm creates a windbreak that slows down harsh winds before they reach your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo tsei kakadaji ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa shi dani eshɛɔ onibii ahe.

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to soak up the water into the roots before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it away.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ lɛ.

english: High humidity and continuous moisture during the rainy season create ideal conditions for microscopic fungal diseases to multiply on wet leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii bibii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough to grow crops without chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ tsei ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Dark, crumbly soil that holds moisture well and contains earthworms or broken-down plant leaves is naturally fertile and rich in nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo muji ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe baai ni ekumɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds sprout and spread so much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, and thousands of weed seeds lie dormant in the dirt ready to sprout the moment clearing opens up light and rain.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Ni jwɛi dumɔwui akpei abɔ kã shi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji la kɛ nugbɔ bote mli pɛ.

english: When is the best time of day to feed my crops with fertilizer so it benefits them the most?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ená he sɛɛ babaoo?

english: Crops absorb nutrients best in the cool early morning or late afternoon when the soil is moist. Applying fertilizer during the mid-day heat can burn the plant roots and waste nutrients through drying.
ga: Tsei lɛ nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ni hulu lɛ miitso. ni ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ afite kɛjɛ amɛgbimɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning from too much water. Proper feeding with plant food and ensuring good soil drainage helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ nu babaoo mli. Tsei lɛ niyenii ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Does applying organic manure work the same way as feeding my crops with mineral fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ mineral ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Organic manure feeds both the crop and the soil over a long time by improving soil texture, while mineral fertilizer gives crops a fast, immediate boost of nutrients but does not build soil long-term health.
ga: Organic fertilizers haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa efeɔ fɛo lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni mineral fertilizers lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii oya ni amɛnáa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi ekɛ hewalɛ kpakpa baaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can I inspect my crop field quickly to catch insect attacks early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ nibii ni midu lɛ amli oya koni mana kooloi ni baatutua mi lɛ mra?

english: Walking through your field in an 'X' or 'S' pattern twice a week and checking under the leaves of young crops allows you to catch pests early before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ 'X' loo 'S' gbɛ nɔ shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Ni kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai mra. Dani amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural self-defense against hot weather. The crop curls its leaves to reduce water loss from the afternoon heat, but it should uncurl once temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni jɛɔ shwane latsaa mli lɛ aba shi. Shi esa akɛ ejie ehe kpo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and shrivel on the branch before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, humid environments. Pruning excess canopy branches allows sunlight and air to dry the pods and prevent the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, inconsistent watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tomato tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and bigger than my young crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with stronger root systems that absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and sunlight from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why is planting my maize in straight lines better than scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛ niji baagbɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop equal space, sunlight, and nutrients. It also makes weeding, feeding, and harvesting much easier, leading to higher overall crop yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, niyenii kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: How does testing my farm soil before planting help my crops yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikaa dani miduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Soil testing tells you the exact nutrients missing in your land so you can feed your crops precisely what they need, saving money on unnecessary fertilizers and improving overall harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ aha onibii lɛ. Kɛ shika ato ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo he. ni eha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I protect my vegetables from pest insects without using chemical sprays that could harm my family's health?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni baanyɛ aye miweku lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ awui lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can use natural neem tree leaf extracts mixed with mild soapy water. Spraying this on leaves repels pests naturally without leaving toxic chemical residues on food crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso mli nu ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ okɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaashwie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eshiŋ tsofa fɔŋ ko yɛ niyenii ni adu lɛ nɔ.

english: How does adding animal manure help my cassava grow better than using only chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi aŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure and holds moisture in the ground for longer periods, whereas chemical fertilizers only provide quick, short-term nutrients that easily wash away during heavy rains.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛ oya. ni baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas alongside my maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for the maize growing next to them.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Namɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yellow leaves often mean waterlogging is drowning the roots, preventing the plant from breathing and absorbing nutrients, or that heavy rain washed the nitrogen out of the soil before the plant could take it up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ miiha shishifãi lɛ miiho. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: If I plant my tomatoes very close together, won't I harvest more fruit from the same small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tomato ni bɛŋkɛ he waa lɛ makpa aduawai babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani enyɛŋ efee nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin plants with small fruits and allows fungal leaf diseases to spread quickly between crowded leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la he. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fungal leaf helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wilt quickly during hot days even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: Without a layer of organic mulch like dry grass covering the bare earth, the hot sun rapidly evaporates soil moisture and bakes the shallow feeder roots of plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni eshãa tso ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my harvested maize produce smaller yields when I plant them the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo beni miduɔ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crop varieties lose their genetic vigor in the next generation, leading to uneven growth and lower yields compared to planting fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛmli hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛmɔ he.

english: Why are fall armyworms attacking the young leaves inside my corn plants every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ daa be lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths prefer laying eggs in the tight center roll of young corn leaves because it offers soft leaf tissue to eat and protection from predators while the plant is growing.
ga: Cutworm ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni afee lɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ amli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ baa bibii yɛ ni ayeɔ ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in wet, shaded conditions. It spreads fast when trees are too dark and dense, preventing air from flowing through to dry off wet pods.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ tso lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: How does joining a farmer cooperative group help me control pests on my farm better than working alone?
ga: Te okwaafoi akuu ko ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikome too matsu nii?

english: When neighboring farmers coordinate through a cooperative to control pests at the same time, it prevents insects from simply flying from an untreated farm onto your clear farm.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ fee ekome kɛtsɔ kuu nɔ koni amɛye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli Ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo kɛjɛ oŋmɔ ni otsuuu he nii lɛ mli kɛya oŋmɔ ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How many bags of cocoa should I aim to harvest to know my farm is doing well?
ga: Cocoa kotokui enyiɛ esa akɛ mafee miyiŋ akɛ makpa koni male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A healthy, well-managed farm should produce a strong yield, often targeted at ten or more bags per season depending on farm size. Harvesting lower amounts usually indicates that your trees are not getting proper care, light, or nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo yibii babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, amɛtaoɔ baagi nyɔŋma loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Edamɔ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ nɔ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni akpaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ enaaa kwɛmɔ, la, loo niyenii kpakpai ni sa.

english: How do modern farming techniques actually help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛ̀i baanyɛ aye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: New measures like clearing the tree base, proper spacing, and systematic pruning allow cocoa trees to use nutrients efficiently, reduce disease spread, and focus energy on growing healthy pods rather than excess foliage.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi heei tamɔ tso shishifãi ni abua naa yɛ he ko ni sa Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai babaoo.

english: Why is it necessary to clear the grass and weeds right around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing around the trunk prevents weeds from stealing fertilizer and water from the root zone. It also eliminates humid hiding places for pests and fungal diseases like black pod near the tree.
ga: clearing around Tsoi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ejieɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni etsɔ diŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ hu.

english: What happens to my harvest if I leave weeds to grow freely in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa trees for soil nutrients and moisture. This competition weakens the trees, slows down pod development, and significantly lowers your overall yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shweremɔ baa shi. Ni ebaa onitsumɔ fɛɛ ni otsuɔ lɛ shi waa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches when my cocoa tree looks big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ be mli ni mi-kookoo tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda ni eyɛ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that block sunlight and air. Good airflow and sunlight reach the main stems where pods grow, reducing humidity that causes rot while helping the tree direct food into pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii baa koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by lack of water, excessive shade, poor soil nutrients, or when there are not enough beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao. Shade babaoo Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee pollin lɛ bɛ.

english: This is usually black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady, and uncleaned farms. Keeping the farm base clear and removing affected pods stops the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni amɛhe tseee lɛ amli. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ shishi afee faŋŋ ni ojie pods ni ena naagbai lɛ koni ekpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch when exposed to direct, strong sunlight without shade trees nearby. Yellowing can also mean the roots are lacking key soil nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ haaa amɛhe ajɔ amɛ. Yellow baanyɛ atsɔɔ hu akɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What causes mature cocoa trees to stop bringing out new leaves and pods?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei ni eda lɛ kpaɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii heei ni amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: When trees stop growing new shoots or pods, it is often due to nutrient-depleted soil, overgrown weeds competing for water, or root damage from soil pests.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ kpa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃mɔ Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi babaoo ni miitswa akaŋ kɛha nu. aloo shishifãi lɛ efite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe

english: Why do cocoa trees planted too close together produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Overcrowded cocoa trees fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. The excessive shade also traps moisture, making trees more vulnerable to diseases that destroy pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Shade babaoo hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ oya.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant crops on raised ridges instead of flat land when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Raised ridges allow excess rainwater to drain away from plant roots. This keeps the soil around the roots from staying completely soaked, allowing roots to breathe air and preventing root rot.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akakwɛ̃. Shishifãi lɛ efɔ kwraa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why do my pepper plants wither and look droopy even when the ground around them is completely soaked with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miigbo ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli egbi moŋ lɛ? Ani nu baaha enɔ?

english: When soil stays flooded, plant roots run out of oxygen and start to rot. Once the roots rot and stop working, they can no longer suck up water to feed the plant, making it look like it is drying up even in wet soil.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi lɛ faaa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite ni amɛkpa nitsumɔ lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu nu ni amɛkɛha tsei lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant in low swampy areas on my farm where rainwater gathers and stays for a long time?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmeii yɔɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops like rice, cocoyam, and sugarcane grow very well in wet, swampy soils. Unlike crops like maize or cassava, their stems and roots are naturally built to handle standing water without drowning.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ omɔ, kookoo, kɛ shɛ̃ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ jɛ adebɔɔ mli koni amɛye amɛbua nu ni damɔ shi ni nu lɛ shwieee amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop black spots on their leaves right after heavy rain soaks my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi diji yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni eha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Raindrops splashing on wet soil spread invisible disease germs (fungi) onto the plant leaves. The continuous wetness on the leaves creates the perfect environment for these germs to grow and cause black spots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ helai ni anaaa (fungi) lɛ eshwaa tsei ahe baai amli. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ adara ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy and firm. When rainwater fills all the air spaces in the soil for many days, the tubers suffocate, drown, and turn soft from rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli gbii babaoo Yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi, efoɔ nu mli ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ mli.

english: What happens to the fertilizer I put around my maize if heavy rain floods my farm immediately after?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away from the crop roots, either carrying it off the farm or driving it too deep into the ground where the roots cannot reach it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli. Ekolɛ, okɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo okɛtsɔ tsɔne mli kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why does heavy rainwater washing across my land make my crops grow poorly in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fast-moving rainwater carries away the dark top layer of soil, which holds most of the natural food and nutrients crops need. Without topsoil, the remaining hard soil cannot feed plants well.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ kɛyaa. Amɛtoɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni eshwɛ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua tsei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does rainwater stay sitting on top of clay soil for days while sinking quickly into sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ be mli ni efoɔ oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clay soil is made of tiny, tightly packed particles that leave very little room for water to pass through quickly, while sandy soil has large spaces that let water drain straight down like a sieve.
ga: Sũ lɛ ji nibii bibii bibii. tightly packed ni haa he ko fioo pɛ nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli yɛ Be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii amli

english: How can I tell if I am giving my vegetable crops too much water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mitsei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Vegetables getting too much water usually show pale yellow leaves, stunted growth, and soil around the stem that smells sour or feels mushy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ jieɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo. Dalɛ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ sũ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he ni ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What should I do on my farmland right after flood waters settle to save my standing crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nu afua ko sɛɛ koni mikɛhere miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala?

english: You should dig simple, shallow gutters to lead stagnant water off the farm, gently wash thick mud off the leaves, and wait until the soil dries out slightly before applying any fresh fertilizer.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa nubu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni mli ekwɔɔɔ koni ojie nu ni damɔ shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Okɛ muji ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ afɔ he blɛoo. Ni mɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi fioo dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei awo mli.

english: Why does my local rice smell sweet when it is growing, but some other rice varieties don't have any scent?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ adu lɛ? Shi ani ŋmãa henɔi krokomɛi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔ kwraa?

english: Certain local rice varieties naturally produce natural aromatic compounds while growing. This scented quality is an inherent trait of specific perfumed varieties, which often makes them sell at a higher price in local Ghanaian markets.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jieɔ tsofai ni ŋɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ su ni ŋɔɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kadiɔ tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ enɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant improved seed varieties or stick to the local seeds I saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo makɛ mihe akpɛtɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Improved seeds are bred to give higher yields and fight off diseases better, but they require good fertilizer and water management. Local saved seeds are cheaper and well adapted to local weather, but they usually yield less fruit.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛkɛ helai awuu jogbaŋŋ. Shi ebiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jara waaa ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Shi efɔɔ kaa akɛ etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the bottom while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves usually shows that the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant naturally moves nitrogen from its older lower leaves up to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural defense to stop water loss. Once the rains start again, the plant will quickly sprout fresh new leaves from its stem.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi oya.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward to reach sunlight instead of spending energy to build strong stems and produce large crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛma tsei ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather becomes extremely hot or when water supply changes suddenly from dry to overly wet. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to drop flowers that were not fertilized.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi tsɔ kɛtee he ni edɔ tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is my maize plant producing tassels at the top before the cob ears even start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dani toi lɛ po jeɔ shishi ejieɔ ehe kpo lɛ?

english: Maize naturally flowers at the top first so wind can carry pollen down to the silks below. However, if the cob ears appear much later than the tassels, it usually means the plant is stressed by drought or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Abɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atswa pollen lɛ kɛya siliki ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ cob toi lɛ je kpo sɛɛ mli kwraa fe tassels lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Why do some of my rice plants grow much taller than the rest of the field and mature at a different time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ daa fe tsei krokomɛi lɛ? babaoo ni amɛdaraa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli

english: This happens when your seed supply is mixed with wild rice or seeds from different varieties. Using certified uniform seed guarantees that all plants grow, flower, and mature evenly for easier harvesting.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ okɛ koo mli ŋmãa loo dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa srɔtoi amli lɛ futu mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tsei fɛɛ adara, amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛshwere pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: How can I tell what nutrients my soil is missing just by looking at my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ kɛtsɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: Plants communicate through their leaves: yellowing leaves point to low nitrogen, purplish leaves signal a lack of phosphorus, and leaves with burnt edges show a shortage of potassium.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe gbaa sane kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli. Ni baai ni amɛhe shã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested grain go bad or get moldy quickly even when I keep it inside a clean store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ nibii atoohe ni mli tse mli moŋ?

english: Grain spoils inside storage if it was not completely dried under the sun after harvest. Trapped moisture inside the grain creates a damp home for mold and insects to multiply rapidly.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa baafite yɛ nitoohe lɛ mli kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii feɔ shia ni mli ejɔ koni amɛshwere oya.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, cool, and overly shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeded areas around the base helps stop the moisture that allows the fungus to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba mli, ni ojie jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Removing heavily infected plants and spraying neem oil or recommended organic insecticides early can keep insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Akɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ he ŋaawoo haa. Ebaanyɛ eha kooloi akabote mli

english: What causes tiny worms to eat holes through the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu ko yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing point ('funnel') of maize plants. Checking your field early in the morning and applying recommended treatments into the central whorl of the leaf helps kill the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ (‘cones’) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo baai lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and their leaves burn under full direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cooler soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔji ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi lolo.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them trail on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato tso lɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ekpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, which gives them maximum sunlight and protects the leaves from rotting or catching diseases from damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni haa hulu la babaoo baa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ loo helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: If a plantain plant has too many suckers, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil, leading to small bunches. Removing extra suckers and keeping only 2 or 3 of different heights allows the main plant to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo Amɛbaatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahiɛ srɔtofeemɔi 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ amɛlɛɛmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ agbala ejwɛŋmɔ kɛya aduawai akui wuji ni tsii ni baa lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tip along the central vein is a clear sign that the plant lacks Nitrogen, a major food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-composted manure restores the leaf color and growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni akɛyeɔ nii titri ni ehe miihia ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year if I keep planting maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize field with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and resets the pest cycle.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yaa nɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn beds lɛ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know my cassava is ready for harvesting since the tubers grow hidden underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ? Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava shows readiness when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack open as the tubers expand. Most varieties reach maturity between 9 and 12 months after planting.
ga: Yucca jieɔ hesaamɔ kpo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Eshwɛ tso ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. ni he ni ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ. Henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shɛɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant receives irregular watering, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil causing lush foliage at the expense of fruit. Keeping the soil consistently moist and shading young flowers during extreme heat helps them set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛ aduawai ni efiteɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni aha fɔfɔi bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or the roots are overwhelmed by standing water. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color and produce full ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛwo baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores soil nitrogen.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I pack seeds close together to fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed well and produce bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: How does letting weeds grow around my crops reduce my harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your crops. Keeping your farm free of weeds ensures your crops get full nourishment to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii Oŋmɔ lɛ ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ muji yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is typical damage caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the leaves of young maize plants and should be controlled early using recommended botanical sprays like neem water or approved insecticides before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ fe fɛɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai amli. ni esa akɛ akudɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. dani ekpãtãa he ni edaa lɛ hiɛ

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences extreme hot weather, dry soil, or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant retain its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni no hewɔ lɛ ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop stems with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the sun from drying out the ground, lowers root temperature, and preserves soil moisture for much longer.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why is it risky for me to plant seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mawo oshara mli akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often a 'false rain' followed by several days of heat. Planting too early can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up in the hot soil before the continuous rains actually begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale nugbɔ’, ni gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ aya nɔ anɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains shields young cocoa from scorching sun and keeps the surrounding soil cool and humid during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to dig up without disturbing the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ni ogbalaaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ naa?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the main leaves start turning yellow and dropping, and the soil right around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Can crop diseases move from my neighbor's farm to my plantain farm on my cutlass or boots?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ dade loo bɔɔtu nɔ?

english: Yes, plant diseases like Black Sigatoka and Fusarium wilt produce microscopic spores that cling to soil on cutlasses, boots, and farm tools, easily spreading from an infected field to a clean one.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka kɛ Fusarium lɛ jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ dadei, bɔɔtui kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: How does Fall Armyworm get onto my maize farm if I did not bring any infested crops into my field?
ga: Te Fall Armyworm feɔ tɛŋŋ eboteɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu?

english: Fall Armyworm adult moths fly long distances at night across farms and lay hundreds of eggs on young maize leaves, allowing the pest to invade clean fields through the air.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii ni eda lɛ foɔ gbɛ kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli gbɛkɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmeii ohai abɔ fɔɔ ŋmeii baai bibii anɔ Ha ŋmeii atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli amɛbote ŋmɔji ni mli tse amli.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee shwiili ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow thin and tall when planted too closely together because they compete with each other for sunlight, stretching upward rather than building thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ekwɛɔ kɛji adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ. Ejaakɛ amɛshiɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Ebaakpã kɛya ŋwɛi moŋ, ni ebaafee tso ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants temporarily roll their leaves inward during peak heat to reduce their exposed surface area and trap moisture, preventing excessive water loss.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ dɔlɛ be mli. Koni ajie ŋwɛi he ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ shi ni ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Koni nu akafite fe nine

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛfee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by severe heat, dry spells, or low soil nutrients as a survival mechanism to preserve water and food reserves.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni faaa lɛ hao amɛ. Koni efee gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛhiɔ shi koni akɛkwɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow in a V-shape down the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shishigbɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that begins at the tip and moves down the middle vein of older leaves is a direct sign that your soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for green leaves.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi tɛ̃ɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects or by planting stem cuttings taken from plants that are already sick.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why did many of my groundnut seeds rot in the ground without sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ babaoo miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds rot before sprouting if they are planted too deeply, planted in waterlogged soil lacking air, or planted right before a heavy, pooling rain.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui lɛ baagboi dani amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo aduɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa

english: What is this thread-like yellow vine creeping over my field and choking my crops?
ga: Ani wain tso ni tamɔ kpãa ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ miiho yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni eeye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: This parasitic weed is called Dodder. It has no roots of its own, so it attaches directly to crop stems to suck out their water and nutrients until the crop weakens or dies.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ nɛɛ akɛ Dodder. Ebɛ shishifãi ni ji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots and softening inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months of storage, using their internal moisture and nutrients to push out new sprouts to start a new lifecycle.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsiɔ dumɔwui heei kɛjɛɔ mli koni ekɛje wala shihilɛ hee shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their root systems are still small and fragile. They need living shade plants like plantains to act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa leaves from scorching until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo ni amɛhe waaa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni hiɛ ka, ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara.

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that thrives when the air around your cocoa trees is too dark and humid. Pruning excess branches and weeding regularly allows sunlight and air to circulate, drying out the leaves and stems so the fungus cannot easily infect the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu. ni baakwɛ̃ beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Cocoa tso lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ojie jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ehaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ shɛɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I plant my maize seeds in straight, measured rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni masusu amɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Planting in spaced rows ensures every single plant receives enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants. It also leaves clear pathways for you to walk through when weeding, applying fertilizer, or harvesting.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Eyɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ kɛ́ ookpa jwɛi, oowo ŋmɔshi nibii loo ookpa nii.

english: Why do I get a smaller yield when I plant seeds saved from my previous maize harvest compared to buying new seed packets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibiiwoo bibioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ lɛ he

english: Seeds saved from harvested hybrid crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the next generation, producing weaker plants with smaller cob sizes. Fresh certified seeds are specially bred to give strong, uniform growth and maximum yield every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ cob dalɛi bibii baa. Akwɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo dalɛ ni mli wa. Yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli

english: Why is my cassava crop growing very tall with thick green leaves, but producing tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground. To grow large root tubers, cassava needs balanced nutrients like potassium and plenty of direct sunlight.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ shishifãi wuji ni miida lɛ mli lɛ, niyenii ni ja, tamɔ potassium, kɛ hulu la babaoo ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia Cassava.

english: How can I tell if my soil is worn out and lacks nutrients before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli dani madu?

english: If previous crops grew slowly, had pale or yellowing leaves, or yielded tiny fruits, your soil nutrients are depleted. Soil that dries out very fast or struggles to support even wild weeds is also a clear sign that it needs organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo Ehiɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo eha yibii bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ etã. Shikpɔŋ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya waa loo ebɔɔɔ mɔdɛŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ koo mli jwɛi po lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia humus loo humus.

english: Will planting cowpeas between my maize crop steal nutrients away from the maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas do not steal nutrients; they actually feed the maize. Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil, acts as a living cover to prevent weeds, and leaves the soil richer for your maize.
ga: Cowpeas juuu niyenii mli hewalɛ nii. Amɛkwɛɔ ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why does the Striga weed keep coming back in my maize field even after I pull it out by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ minine jie lɛ moŋ

english: Striga is a parasitic weed whose seeds stay alive in the soil for years and attach directly to the roots of maize underground before you ever see it. Pulling it above ground helps, but rotating your field with crops like soybean or groundnut is necessary to starve out the weed seeds.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni edumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ dani onaa lɛ pɛŋ. Kɛ́ agbala kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa. Shi kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ soybeans loo peanuts tsake oŋmɔji lɛ Ehe miihia ni hɔmɔ aye jwɛi dumɔwui.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot and dry, the heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing pollination. Without pollination, the plant cannot form fruit and drops the flower to conserve water.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Koni akɛtsi pollination naa Kɛji pollination bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛjie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my hot peppers so the plant keeps producing more?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii koni mitsei lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: Pick peppers as soon as they reach full size and start changing to their mature color (such as bright red or yellow). Harvest regularly using a sharp cut on the stem; leaving old fruit on the branch signals the plant to stop producing new flowers.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔi kɛji amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he pɛ ni amɛbɔi amɛhe su tsakemɔ (tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse). Kpaa amɛ daa kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi aduawai momo yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ ekpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is good for planting local rice varieties?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Rice grows best in flat, low-lying areas or valley bottoms that hold water well. Soil with high clay content stays wet longer, which helps rice plants thrive compared to dry, sandy soils.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni nu hiɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔji ni shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli babaoo lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ.

english: Is it better to use a tractor to clear my field or can I just use manual labor with hoes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ traktɔ atsu nii kɛjie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo manyɛ mikɛ niji atsu nii kɛ ŋmei?

english: Using machines or a tractor breaks up the deep, hard soil much better than hand hoes, allowing crop roots to penetrate deeper, find water easily, and grow stronger plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ loo trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni wa lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei. Ehaa tsei shishifãi boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, amɛnaa nu mlɛo, ni amɛkwɛɔ tsei ni he wa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when water stays on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air just like humans do. When water covers the soil completely for days without draining, the roots drown, stop taking in nutrients, and cause the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa gbii komɛi ni nu hoɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aná. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I buy packaged seed from an agricultural agent instead of using leftover seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo kotoku mli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Packaged seeds are specially treated to resist local pests and diseases, giving higher yields. Leftover seeds from previous harvests lose their strength over time and often carry diseases into the new season.
ga: Akɛ tsofa krɛdɛɛ ko tsuɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ ahe nii koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa babaoo Dumɔwui ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ he waaa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, ni bei pii lɛ ekɛ helai baa be hee lɛ mli.

english: How often does my rice farm need water while the crops are flowering?
ga: Shii enyiɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa nu yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Rice requires consistent moisture, especially during flowering and grain formation. If the soil dries out during this period, the grains will remain empty and dry up inside the husk.
ga: Omɔ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Ŋmaa lɛ baakã he ahi shi efolo ni ebaagbi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why did my maize not grow well even after I sprinkled fertilizer on top of the soil during the dry sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo hulu la ni mli egbi lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so root systems can soak it up. When placed on dry ground under hot sun, the nutrients evaporate into the air or get blown away before plants can use them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo ajieɔ kɛyaa dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants that produce smaller grains or fruits.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ dumɔwui bibii loo aduawai baa.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the leaves of my young crop plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Midumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Holes in young leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles feeding on the plant. Removing these pests early allows the leaves to grow fully and make food for the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni eha niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to the soil. They sprout quickly to grab sunlight and nutrients before your planted crops have a chance to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani otso lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get moldy inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ efite ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when they are stored with moisture still inside them. Drying your harvested crops thoroughly in the sun until they are hard and dry stops mold and insects from destroying your store.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Akɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni akɛgbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ oshwapo lɛ.

english: Why do people say tomato farming requires much more hard work than pepper farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tomato dumɔ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo fe ŋmɔtɔ dumɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are sensitive to many pests and diseases, requiring frequent spraying, staking, and regular pruning. Peppers are naturally hardier, less prone to quick pest destruction, and need less intensive daily attention.
ga: Tomato lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ helai babaoo baanyɛ amɔ lɛ oya. Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ, akɛ stake awo nɔ ni akpɛtɛ he daa. Chili ŋmɔtɔ ji nɔ ni mli wa fe adebɔɔ mli. Ewaaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ afite amɛ. ni ebiɔ daa gbi kwɛmɔ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo

english: As a new vegetable farmer with limited help on the field, which crop is easiest to start with between tomatoes and peppers?
ga: Ákɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma okwaafonyo hee ni yelikɛbuamɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Tsei ni shishijee yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ, tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Peppers are generally easier for beginners because they can tolerate harsher weather, require fewer chemical sprays, and do not need to be supported with sticks like tomatoes do.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, chili peppers lɛ waaa kɛhaa mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ anaa. Ebiɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fioo Ni ehe ehiaaa ni aye abua lɛ tamɔ tomato.

english: Is cucumber a difficult crop for a small-scale farmer to manage?
ga: Ani kukumba ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa kɛha okwaafoi bibii akɛ amɛaakwɛ nɔ?

english: Cucumbers are moderately demanding because they grow extremely fast and need trellises or supports to keep the fruit off the ground, but they mature quickly so you can harvest sooner than tomatoes.
ga: Kukumba biɔ nibii babaoo yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya waa ni amɛbiɔ ni akɛ tsɔne loo nɔ ko ni akɛfiɔ he koni aduawai lɛ akagbee shikpɔŋ. Shi amɛdaraa oya hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa amɛ oya fe tomato.

english: Why do my pepper plants survive dry spells better than my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe mi-tomato tso lɛ?

english: Pepper plants have tougher leaves and deeper roots that allow them to conserve water, whereas fleshy tomato plants lose water rapidly and wilt easily under high heat.
ga: Pepper tsei yɛ baai ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tomato tsei ni yɔɔ loo lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa shishi.

english: Why do tomato fruits rot easily if they touch the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji amɛta shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Soil contains fungi and bacteria that attack soft tomato skins when wet. Staking tomato vines keeps the leaves and fruits elevated, clean, and dry.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tutuaa tomato hewolo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛji edɔ. Tomato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ feɔ shɔŋŋ, amɛhe tseɔ, ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do pests seem to attack tomato flowers more than pepper flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa tomato fɔfɔi fe pepper fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers and soft leaves attract targeted pests like caterpillars and whiteflies easily, whereas hot pepper plants contain natural bitter compounds that deter many insects.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi kɛ baai bibii lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni baanyɛ atsĩ kooloi babaoo anaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do cucumber leaves wilt and turn yellow so quickly in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kukumba baai lɛ shwieɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Cucumber leaves are large and broad, losing water rapidly through transpiration. They need consistent soil moisture and organic manure to keep their leaves green and hydrated.
ga: Kukumba baai lɛ dara ni amɛmli lɛɛ. Nu ni laajeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ nu ni faaa mli lɛ Amɛmiitao shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: Do I need to spend more money on agricultural chemicals when growing tomatoes compared to peppers?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafite shika babaoo yɛ okwaayeli tsofai ahe kɛ́ midu tomato kɛ akɛto ŋmɔtɔ he?

english: Yes, tomatoes usually require a higher financial investment in fungicides and insecticides throughout their growth cycle to protect them from common fungal blights and fruit borers.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tomato biɔ ni akɛ shika babaoo awo tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ fɛɛ mli. Koni abu tomato he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ aduawai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How soon can I expect to harvest cucumbers after planting them?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii migbe naa lɛ, te manyɛ makpa kukumba lɛ mra tɛŋŋ?

english: Cucumbers are fast-growing crops that can be harvested within 45 to 60 days after planting, making them a quick source of income compared to longer-term crops.
ga: Kukumba ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ gbii 45 kɛyashi 60 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, ni no haa anáa shika oya kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some farmers choose to grow high-maintenance crops like tomatoes despite the heavy work involved?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi halaa akɛ amɛbaadu nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ tomato, yɛ nitsumɔ ni wa ni amɛtsuɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Even though tomatoes demand more labor and money for care, they often yield high market prices during periods of low supply, making the extra work potentially very profitable.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tomato biɔ nitsumɔ kɛ shika babaoo koni akɛkwɛ nɔ moŋ, shi tomato fɔɔ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ he famɔ yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni fata he lɛ he baa sɛɛnamɔ waa.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or taller trees to shield them from the scorching sun and retain soil moisture while their root systems establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the ears even grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ po kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts from the bottom leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves at the bottom to support the new foliage growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvest reduce every year when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Every crop draws specific nutrients from the soil. Planting the same crop continuously depletes those specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that target that crop to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows signs of maturity when its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a tuft of leaves at the top, and the base of the main stem grows thick and sturdy.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ eshishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ashiɔ baai lɛ yɛ kuu mli yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ni tso titri lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I put many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo fataa he Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?
