english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing strong stalks and large cobs, the plants waste energy growing tall to reach light.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ tsohi agbohi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛná la.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground so all the leaves can capture direct sunlight without shading one another.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni baai lɛ fɛɛ anyɛ aná hulu la lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into tiny bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, aphids, or thrips, or a virus transmitted by them. Damaged leaves lose their structure and cannot make proper food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites, thrips, loo helai ni jɛɔ amɛmli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Baai ni efite lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii ni sa amɛha tso lɛ.

english: Why do the central leaves of my young maize crops look ragged and chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni egbala ni amɛye nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This is a typical sign of Fall Armyworm damage. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant during the day and feed on tender leaves, leaving ragged holes and dark droppings behind.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm fitemɔ he. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni amɛshiɔ buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when soil moisture fluctuates wildly or when temperatures get too high. Extreme heat damages the pollen, preventing the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. haa fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often heats up dry soil without penetrating deeply. If dry weather follows that single rain, seeds sit in hot, damp soil and rot before they can properly germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eboteee mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nifeemɔ kome pɛ nyiɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa amɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and stopping the plant from bearing good fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant juice and spread plant viruses. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. small pest control Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout and just dry up in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekomɛi edaaa ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings can dry up if planted upside down, if taken from watery top stems instead of mature woody stems, or if planted in dry soil without enough initial soil moisture to start root growth.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ baanyɛ agbi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli yɛ tso ni eda kwraa lɛ najiaŋ. aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni shishijee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli ni baaha shishifãi lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ duɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ mikɛ babaoo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This competition makes all the plants grow tall, weak, and produce small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ daraa, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi bibii.

english: Staking holds the yam leaves up off the ground so they can catch full sunlight and make energy. Leaving vines on the wet ground exposes leaves to diseases and reduces the size of the tuber below.
ga: Okɛ sweet potato baai lɛ awo ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baa hela aba ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin roots that cannot handle strong, direct heat. They require shade trees or plantains nearby to block harsh sunlight and keep the air cool until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛtsi hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Should I water my vegetable farm in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: It is best to avoid afternoon watering because heat makes the water evaporate into the air before roots can drink it, and hot droplets on leaves can scorch the plant. Water early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ he yɛ shwane mli ejaakɛ latsaa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ. Nu yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes holes in my maize leaves and a sawdust-like powder inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the plant during the day, chewing young leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii ni oshi nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even if I give my crop enough fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight before your main crop gets a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ hulu la dani otsei titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is short in the soil, the plant moves what little food it has from its older bottom leaves up to the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with huge leaves but yield small, thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is grown in extremely rich soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in its roots below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb sticks to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akwɔ tsei aniji koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking spreads the leaves out to catch solar energy, which the plant then sends down into the ground to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni emɔ hulu hewalɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ tso lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Young and mature cocoa trees get stressed under direct, scorching sunlight. Shade trees keep the farm cool, preserve soil moisture, and protect the cocoa leaves, allowing the tree to retain flowers and produce more pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii ni eda lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni haoɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obu kookoo baai ahe Enɛ haa tso lɛ buaa fɔfɔi babaoo naa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when plants do not get consistent water. Heat and drought prevent proper pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ tsiɔ pollination naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rainfall is often followed by a dry spell of several hot days. If tender seeds germinate in that brief wet period, the hot days that follow will dry out the topsoil and kill the young seedlings before their roots grow deep.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui bibii kwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize leaves faster during dry spells than during heavy rain days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ mi-corn baai lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain physically washes small armyworms off the maize leaves and promotes natural fungal diseases that kill the caterpillars. Dry weather allows them to feed continuously and multiply quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ asraafoi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ ahe lɛ ahe nii, ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa hela ko ni gbeɔ ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa amɛyeɔ nii be fɛɛ be ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and wrinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from underneath the leaves. They can also pass viral diseases to the plant while feeding, which stunts its overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ hu amɛshwã tsei amli be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ haa edalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like cement after the rain dries up, making my crops struggle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ simenti yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure to hold its structure open. Adding decomposed organic material creates spaces in the soil for water to sink in and roots to spread freely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baagbele egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ naa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa gbɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nu abote mli ni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow well and stay green even when I do not apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ fataaa he moŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, meaning their roots work with beneficial natural bacteria in the soil to grab nitrogen directly from the air and feed it to the plant naturally.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛha tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: My neighbor gave me some new crop seeds as a gift, but can I get into legal trouble for planting them?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ha mi tso dumɔwui heei komɛi akɛ nikeenii. Shi ani manyɛ mabote mla naa haomɔ mli yɛ amɛkwɛmɔ mli?

english: If those seeds are protected crop varieties owned by a company or research institution, multiplying or selling them without proper authorization can lead to legal action, even if they were given to you as a gift.
ga: Kɛji nakai dumɔwui lɛ ji tsei srɔtoi ni abuɔ he ni nitsumɔhe ko loo niiamlitaomɔ he ko yɔɔ lɛ, Egbɛɛmɔ loo jarayeli ni ahaaa hegbɛ ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aha akɛ mla awo mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ ha bo akɛ nikeenii po.

english: Can someone take legal action against me if I plant a special variety of seed I found on another person's farm?
ga: Ani mɔ ko baanyɛ ekɛ mi awo mla naa? Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui krɛdɛɛ ko ni ana yɛ mɔ kroko ŋmɔ mli hu?

english: Yes, planting or reproducing patented or registered seed varieties without permission from the legal owner can lead to legal action through regulatory channels.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ loo afee amɛ ekoŋŋ ni mla naa nuŋtsɔ lɛ eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha awo mɔ ko tsuŋ kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I just use part of the grain I harvested from my crop as seed for the next planting season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpaa kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ekomɛi atsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: While you can plant harvested grain, saved seeds often give lower yields and lose disease resistance compared to certified seeds, which are specially produced under strict supervision.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ moŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo ni baa shi ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ lɛ ahe. Afee amɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi.

english: Why do crops planted from my own saved seeds grow weaker than the store-bought ones I planted last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa mɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ shwapo mli ni midu yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many improved seed varieties lose their special strengths like high yield and disease resistance after the first harvest, so saving seeds from them results in weaker offspring.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo ni atsake amɛ lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛi krɛdɛɛi tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ni abuɔ he lɛ haa seshibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: What is the work of PPRSD inspectors when they come to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ PPRSD mlikwɛlɔ ko baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: PPRSD inspectors check your crops to ensure they are healthy, free from dangerous pests and diseases, and grown according to national agricultural quality standards.
ga: PPRSD mlikwɛlɔi lɛ kwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Ebɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui. ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ okwaayeli he mlai anaa

english: How do crop inspectors determine if my seed production process is going well?
ga: Te mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛle kɛji midumɔwui afeemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Inspectors regularly visit your farm during different growth stages to check plant health, field spacing, and crop purity to verify that your seed production follows standard practices.
ga: Mɛi ni baakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baasara oŋmɔ lɛ daa yɛ shweremɔ bei srɔtoi amli. Koni okwɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ Plot sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsemɔ Koni okwɛ akɛ odumɔwui afeemɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ nifeemɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do crop inspectors look closely at the leaves and stems of my crops during farm visits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kwɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli saramɔi amli lɛ?

english: They examine leaves and stems for early signs of pests, viruses, or fungal diseases to prevent dangerous infections from spreading throughout your farm or into the wider community.
ga: Amɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛji amɛna mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai eba. Enɛ ji koni helai ni yɔɔ oshara akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo akutso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need an official inspection on my farm before I can export or supply my crops to major buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ dani manyɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya maŋsɛɛ loo mikɛha mɔ ko ni heɔ nii waa lɛ?

english: Official inspections prove to commercial buyers that your produce is grown safely, meets legal regulatory requirements, and is free from disease or harmful contamination.
ga: Amralo lɛ mlikwɛmɔi maa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ anɔ mi akɛ onibii lɛ miida shweshweeshwe. Eshɛɔ mla taomɔ nii ahe ni hela loo mujiwoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ mli

english: What do I need to do if I want to legally sell the seeds I harvest on my farm to other farmers?
ga: Mɛni mafee kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mahã okwaafoi krokomɛi yɛ mla naa?

english: To legally sell seeds, your farm must be inspected, tested, and certified by PPRSD to guarantee that the seeds are disease-free, pure, and have high germination rates.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui yɛ mla naa lɛ Esa akɛ PPRSD akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, aka lɛ akwɛ ni etsɔɔ akɛ hela bɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli, amɛhe tse ni amɛshwereɔ babaoo.

english: What makes certified seeds from agro-dealers better than seeds I buy from general sellers in the local market?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ daa yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ adɛŋ?

english: Certified seeds undergo strict quality checks by inspectors like PPRSD to guarantee high yields and disease resistance, whereas ordinary market seeds have no quality guarantees and may fail to grow well.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ kwɛlɔi tamɔ PPRSD nɔ koni amɛna nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaawo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ bɛ nɔmimaa ko akɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ, ni ekolɛ amɛkwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen, which is a major food source it needs to grow. The plant takes nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdu nii. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or lack of moisture in the soil. When stressed, the plant saves its energy by discarding flowers instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni bɛ lɛ ha amɛhao. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain leaves fold during peak sun to protect themselves from losing too much water through heat evaporation. It is a natural defense mechanism to keep the plant from drying out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ dɔlɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily. They need taller trees or plantain plants nearby to give them protective shade while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni kwɔlɔ loo plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛná hulutsoo be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot on the soil if I do not prop them up with sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei niji tsuuu nii kɛfiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato vines are weak and lay on the wet ground under the weight of their fruit. Lifting and tying them to sticks keeps the leaves and fruits dry and away from soil diseases and insects.
ga: Tomato wain tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ amli tsiimɔ shishi. Kɛ́ owó nɔ ni okɛfi tsei niji ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ akagbi. Ekɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crop cuttings after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil stays moist for a few consecutive days after a heavy rain. Planting immediately after a single light rain can cause seeds or cuttings to dry up if hot days follow.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ lɛ Baanyɛ aha dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni afo lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are ready to harvest under the ground without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ amɛ tsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yam is ready for harvest when the leaves and vines on top stop growing green, turn yellow, and begin to dry up naturally, showing that the plant has transferred all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tso lɛ yiteŋ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than the actual crops I planted in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so their roots quickly absorb water and soil food before your cultivated crops can get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani onibii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crop yields drop if I keep planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil every season and allows specific crop pests and diseases to build up in that ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking key nutrients like nitrogen or not getting enough water. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to stay green and produce full corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and turn dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl to reduce water loss when the sun is very hot, or because tiny insects like whiteflies are sucking nutrients from the leaves. Mulching the soil to hold moisture and controlling sap-sucking pests helps the plants stay green.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies miimu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Mulching koni akɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni akudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli.

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand easily underground. If the soil is hard, compacted, or full of rocks, the tuber cannot push straight through. Building high, soft soil mounds allows the yams to stretch downwards without obstruction.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ baa shi ni nɔ ko tsiii enaa.

english: How does planting my seeds in straight rows help crops grow better than scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without crowding. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛjɛɛɛ amɛhe. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: What causes my cowpea plants to grow plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cowpea tso lɛ baa eŋɔli babaoo shi eshishifãi fioo pɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or excessive rain during early growth encourages cowpea plants to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to form abundant flowers that turn into pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get extremely high or when soil moisture fluctuates too drastically. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root area helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can set.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake fe nine. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Why do crops in demonstration farms look much bigger and healthier than crops in my traditional farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishishijee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Demonstration farms follow strict guidelines such as correct seed spacing, timely weeding, and balanced feeding. When crops do not have to fight weeds for nutrients and have enough space to breathe, they grow much larger.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli wa sɛɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa Beni ehe ehiaaa ni tsei kɛ jwɛi awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛmuɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baatsɔ agbo babaoo.

english: Why is it good for my soil when I plant crops like maize and legumes together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ mikɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea or groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, which feeds companion crops like maize. Mixing these crops naturally improves soil fertility and protects against total crop failure.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa niyenii kɛhaa nanemɛi tsei tamɔ ŋmãa. Tsei nɛɛ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa shoots wither when they get direct sun all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a living umbrella that shields them until they grow mature enough to handle full light.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating different types of crops keeps the soil rich and starves out harmful pests naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings die when I leave them under direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate like newborn babies. Direct hot sunlight dries out their weak roots quickly and burns their leaves before they are strong enough to draw sufficient water from the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ. Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni eshãa baai lɛ dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to build a shade canopy with palm fronds over my vegetable nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shade kɛ ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The canopy protects fragile seeds and sprout leaves from being crushed by heavy raindrops and shields them from scorching sun rays, keeping the soil moist so seeds can germinate evenly.
ga: Kpoji lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa kɛ baai ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akakumɔ amɛ. ni obu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why should I clean my cutlass or pruning knife before moving to a different crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ mi-cutlery loo tsɔji ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe dani mikɛya he kroko ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Uncleaned tools can carry plant diseases, bacteria, or fungi from infected crops in one area and transfer them directly into the fresh cuts of healthy plants in another field.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni he tseee lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsei ahe helai, helatsɛmɛi, loo ŋmeii ni jɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli yɛ he kome ni amɛkɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kroko mli lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do officer friends tell me to carry sick crop leaves far away from my farm instead of dropping them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaanyo asraafonyo nukpa lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ aya he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ moŋ fe ni mashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving diseased leaves on the farm floor allows wind and rain splashing to bounce the disease spores back onto your healthy plants, keeping the sickness alive in your soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ajie helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli kɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Koni hela ahi shi yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why should I avoid letting too many farm helpers or visitors walk through my field when the crops are wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli yelikɛbualɔi loo saralɔi babaoo ni miitsɔ miŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edɔ lɛ he?

english: Water droplets on leaves help plant diseases travel easily. When people brush against wet crops, their clothes and boots spread fungi and microscopic pests from sick plants to healthy ones.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ahelai ni amɛfãa gbɛ mlɛo. Beni gbɔmɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛnyanyɔji anɔ lɛ Amɛ atadei kɛ amɛ atadei lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from water loss. By rolling up, less leaf surface area is exposed to the scorching sun and hot dry wind.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akafite. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves to conserve water and energy when water is scarce, saving its strength to keep the stems and underground roots alive until rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ shi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛji nu faaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the air becomes too hot, or when soil moisture changes drastically, which causes stress and prevents proper pollination inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ni ehaa pollination ni sa baa fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without making good fruits if I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni yibii kpakpai baaa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overcrowded crops compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward trying to reach light instead of using their energy to develop thick stems and big fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow when rain leaves stagnant water sitting on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates crop roots by cutting off air in the soil. Without air, roots cannot breathe or absorb the nutrients required to keep leaves dark green and healthy.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when there is full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains during their first two years to trap moisture and protect them from direct heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. The maize plant is moving whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves up to the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Abɛi tsei miitsi nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller crops when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that like maize to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts helps put good food back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ niyenii kpakpa Ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that roots can safely drink. On dry soil, chemical fertilizer sits around the roots concentrated like salt, which can burn and damage the crop roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛfee nɔ ko ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu shweshweeshwe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hiɔ he fɛɛ he. Shishifãi ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ ŋmei Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juice, or passing a virus to the plant. Treating the farm early for tiny sucking pests prevents this leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa curl baa. loo ekɛ hela lɛ aya tso lɛ nɔ Okwaafoi lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Koni ana kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ baaye abua ni akafite baa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during windstorms even when the stem looks strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall over easily when invisible worm-like pests called nematodes or stem borers destroy the underground roots. Without strong roots anchoring them tightly into the earth, the weight of the bunch causes the tree to tip over in high wind.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ atswaa dumɔwui lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tsiimɔ baaha tso lɛ agbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain sits in the ground without draining away, water replaces the air in the soil, suffocating the tubers and causing rot-producing fungi to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme afternoon heat causes tomato plants to get stressed, making their pollen dry out and become ineffective. When flowers do not get pollinated properly, the plant drops them to save its energy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ mli egbiɔ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔii lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ashwieɔ tsei koni akɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines produce tubers using sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into open sunlight and air, allowing the plant to make more food and grow much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tswaa baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce tiny yields even if the rain falls well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal fertilizer nutrients, ground moisture, and sunlight away from your main crops. Even with good rain, crops cannot grow big if weeds are drinking up their food first.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli hewalɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ babaoo nɛɔ moŋ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu nyɛŋ adara babaoo kɛji jwɛi ye amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why should I buy improved seed varieties instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to resist common local pests, tolerate dry spells, and yield significantly more harvest compared to traditional saved seeds, which lose their strength over generations.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ shiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ekɛ ŋmaa ni fa babaoo baa kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe. ni ehewalɛ baaje mli kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli

english: How do improved crop varieties help me get a bigger harvest on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Improved varieties are developed to convert nutrients and sunlight into fruit or grain more efficiently, grow uniformly, and resist diseases that would normally reduce your total yield.
ga: Afee tsofai srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛtsake niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ amɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ daa ni ote shi owo helai ni baaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi lɛ.

english: Can seeds brought from neighboring African countries grow well on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛba kɛjɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ Afrika lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Not always automatically. Crops depend on specific soil types, day lengths, and rain patterns, so seeds from other regions need to be tested to ensure they suit Ghana's climate before planting heavily.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be lɛ, nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ, gbi lɛ sɛɛtsɛmɔ, kɛ nugbɔ pɔtɛɛ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni aka dumɔwui ni jɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ akwɛ. Enɛ ji koni ana akɛ ehi kɛha Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ dani adu nii waa.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall stems but produce very few leaves or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi ewoɔ baai loo aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops usually stretch tall without fruiting when they are planted too close together, lack enough direct sunlight, or receive too much nitrogen fertilizer which encourages stem growth over fruit development.
ga: Tsei lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni anáa, ni woɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ fe aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji egbi be kukuoo ko lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean the plant is stressed and unable to take up nitrogen from dry soil, as plant roots require soil moisture to absorb essential nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: How does mixing legumes with my main crops help my farm stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛfutuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds neighboring crops and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei, naagbai ni jɛɔ mli baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do insects attack my crops much more during the warm, rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up insect breeding, while humidity and fresh green plant growth provide ideal shelter and food for pests to multiply rapidly.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔji heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa wɔɔhe kɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ koni amɛshwere oya.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their blossoms before any pepper grows?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani pepper lɛ kwɛ̃?

english: Blossom drop happens when plants experience extreme heat stress, uneven watering, or nutrient imbalances, causing the plant to shed flowers to save its own life.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ajie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is forming good roots under the ground without digging everything up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava lɛ yɛ shishifãi kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ efoŋ?

english: Thick stems, healthy dark green leaves, and slight cracking of the soil around the base of the plant are good signs that roots are expanding properly beneath the surface.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni mli tse, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛ eshwa fioo ni ebɔle shishi lɛ ji okadii kpakpai ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why are my crops taking longer to mature than what the seed supplier told me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni mɔ ni kɛ midumɔwui lɛ haa lɛ kɛɛ mi lɛ?

english: Maturation times depend on weather and soil. Poor soil fertility, irregular rainfall, or cooler night temperatures slow down a plant's growth process, delaying harvest day.
ga: Be ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ ejaaa. loo gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni mli ejɔ Haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji nikpamɔ gbi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Can I uproot rubber seeds that sprouted naturally on the ground and replant them on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie rɔbɔt dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can use naturally sprouted seedlings, but you must dig deep to keep the taproot intact and protect the soil around the roots. If the main taproot breaks during uprooting, the plant will struggle to absorb water and may die.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ atsu nii. Shi esa akɛ otsa shi kɛya shɔŋŋ koni taproot lɛ akafite. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he kɛji shishifã titri lɛ fã yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ baaná naagba akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu ni ebaanyɛ egbo.

english: How should I carry young crop seedlings from where they sprouted to my main field without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maŋɔ dumɔwui bibii kɛjɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ kɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Always dig around the seedling to leave a ball of earth around the roots, place them in a tray or bag, and shade them from direct sun during transport. Exposing bare roots to hot air quickly dries them out and kills the plant.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni sũ ŋmɔtɔ abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Okɛwo trati loo kotoku mli. ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shishifãi ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ wo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi oya ni egbe tso lɛ.

english: Is it better to grow seeds in nursery polybags or just collect wild sprouts from under old trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotokui amli loo abaabua koo mli ŋmeii ni jɛ tsei momoi ashishi lɛ anaa kɛkɛ?

english: Nursery polybags are better because the root system stays protected in the bag, allowing for easy transplanting without disturbing the roots. Wild sprouts often suffer severe root damage when pulled from the ground.
ga: Poly kotokui ni akɛfɔɔ bii lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ abuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsake ni agbalaaa shishifãi lɛ anaa. Bei pii lɛ, koo mli ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi fiteɔ waa kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to transplant young sprouted seedlings into my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to transplant early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is weak. Planting under a hot afternoon sun causes the young leaves to lose water faster than the damaged roots can drink, causing the seedling to wilt.
ga: Esa akɛ atsake lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waaa lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa baai bibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni efite lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbi.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when transplanting a young tree seedling?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu mli kɛyashɛ he ni kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui bibii miidu lɛ?

english: Dig the hole deep and wide enough so the roots can spread naturally without bending, but keep the plant at the exact same depth it was growing before. Covering the stem too high with soil can cause it to rot.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni elɛɛmɔ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkuuu amɛhe. Shi ha tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ bɔ ni etsɔ hiɛ eda lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ha tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ agbo.

english: Should I trim some leaves off a young seedling before moving it to the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ dani mikɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, gently removing a few lower leaves reduces water loss through evaporation while the root system is recovering from being moved, helping the plant stay hydrated.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni ajieɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ blɛoo. Enɛ baaha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miihe amɛhe kɛjɛ he ni ajieɔ lɛ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my young transplanted crops droop or lose leaves during the first week after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛbaa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by root disturbance during moving. The plant drops leaves to conserve moisture until its roots establish themselves in the new soil and begin taking up water again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi lɛ ni agbalaa amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ shi koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatswa shi yɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛnáa nu ekoŋŋ.

english: Do I need to water newly transplanted seedlings immediately, even if the soil feels slightly damp?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mawo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ fioo?

english: Yes, watering right after transplanting is critical because it closes air pockets in the soil around the root zone, ensuring the fine roots make direct contact with moist earth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔse nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie lɛ awo mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi kpakpai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If my newly transplanted seedling is not growing well, what can I do to help it survive?
ga: Kɛji mi dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ Mɛni mafee koni maye mabua lɛ ni ehi shi?

english: Provide artificial shade using palm fronds, keep the soil moist, and clear away weeds around the base so the weak seedling does not have to fight for light, water, and nutrients.
ga: Ha shade ni akɛfee kɛtsɔ ŋmei baai anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishitoo ji koni ehe akahia ni dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha la, nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do tree crop seedlings stay thin and weak if I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight for the same sunlight, soil space, and nutrients, causing all of them to grow tall, thin, and weak instead of developing thick, strong stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, egbɔjɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená tsei ni mli tse ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems are not fully established yet. They need temporary shade plants, like plantain or cassava, to act as natural sunshades until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ egbeko naa lolo. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo nɔ Kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on my maize crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: You should walk through your field at least twice a week. Regular field checks allow you to catch early signs of pest infestations, such as fall armyworm, or nutrient deficiency signs before they cause widespread damage to your crop.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oyale mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ ni ooofee daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ miigbɛ eshwa lɛ mra. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ he okadii dani ekɛ naagbai ni gbɛ eshwa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tips and moves down the middle of older leaves usually means the crop lacks nitrogen. The plant is taking available nitrogen from its older leaves to nourish the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shi kɛyaa baai ni edara lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Will allowing tall weeds to grow around my cassava plants affect how large the roots get?
ga: Ani jwɛi kakadaji ni maŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaná shishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, tall weeds compete directly with cassava for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which prevents the roots from swelling into large tubers. Weeds also harbor pests and trap damp air, which can cause diseases.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi kakadaji kɛ yucca yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Jwɛi lɛ hu hiɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ, ni baanyɛ ekɛ helai aba.

english: What happens if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ pepper dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting too close makes the pepper plants fight each other for nutrients, water, and sunlight. This results in tall, thin, weak stems with few pepper fruits, and increases the spread of fungal diseases due to lack of airflow between plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni pepper yibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. ni ehaa ŋmeii helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does my mature cocoa tree stop producing pods even though it has plenty of green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso ni eda lɛ ekpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo moŋ?

english: When a cocoa tree grows a canopy that is too dense or has too many unnecessary suckers (chupons), it uses all its food energy to feed leaves instead of growing flowers and pods. Trimming excess branches lets in sunlight to trigger pod production.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko da ni etsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli edɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni he ehiaaa (chupons) lɛ, ekɛ niyenii ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛyeɔ baai niyenii yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ewo pod feemɔ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl upward during the hottest time of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during peak afternoon heat is a natural survival trick tomato plants use to minimize water loss from their leaf surface. If the leaves unfold again in the cooler evening, the plant is healthy and simply conserving moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni ehe baahia ni ekwɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas in between my rows of maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, cowpeas belong to the legume family and can pull nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil naturally. This helps feed your maize crop while giving you a second crop of beans from the same piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii fata legume weku lɛ he ni ebaanyɛ ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni oha o-abele lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni okɛ dumɔwu ni ji enyɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ haa.

english: Why are there small round holes in my cabbage leaves when I don't see any insects around during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabe baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Akɛni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi ni ebɔle mihe hewɔ lɛ Gbi lɛ mli?

english: Many leaf-eating pests, such as moth caterpillars, hide underneath the leaves or in the soil during the daytime to avoid the heat and birds, coming out to feed only at night. Inspecting your plants early in the morning will help you spot them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ baai babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ okpoi ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii gbɛkɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ otsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona amɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvest without uprooting the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mijieee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is generally mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the lower stem turns woody and brown. You can carefully dig up the soil on one side of a plant to inspect the size of the tuber before deciding to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ tsɔɔ tso kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso lɛ fã kome he nii koni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha dani okpɛ oyiŋ akɛ obaakpa amɛ.

english: Why should I plant shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily scorch and dry out under direct sunlight. Planting shade trees creates a cool environment, reduces heat stress, and keeps moisture in the soil for your cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shi

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up so quickly when the farm area is completely open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli kpokpaa lɛ nɔ egbele kwraa lɛ?

english: Without surrounding trees to block the sun and wind, moisture evaporates rapidly from both the soil and the leaves, causing tender young cocoa seedlings to wither and die.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni ebɔle he lɛ bɛ ni baatsi hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ Fɛ̃i shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How long does it take for planted shade trees to start protecting my cocoa crop?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ baaje mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe buu shishi?

english: Most shade tree species take about 2 to 3 years of steady growth before their leaves spread wide enough to provide good shelter and canopy protection for cocoa.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 dani amɛdaraa daa. Dani baai lɛ baagbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa ni baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋwɛitsu hebuu kpakpa aha kookoo lɛ,.

english: Why do some trees on my land survive harsh weather while all the small crops around them die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Certain mature tree species have deep taproots that reach underground water sources, allowing them to remain green and alive even when shallow-rooted crops perish from drought.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛɔ shi kɛji tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ gboi yɛ hɔmɔ mli po.

english: What happens to the soil on my farm if all the tall trees around it die?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji tsei kakadaji ni bɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ fɛɛ gboi?

english: When big trees die, the soil loses its natural cover. Direct sunlight bakes the earth, drying out organic matter and making the land too poor and hot for delicate crops to grow well.
ga: Kɛ tso agbo ko gbo Shikpɔŋ lɛ efite bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ. egbiɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ohiafo ni edɔɔ tsɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If a portion of my farm land dries up and dies off, can I restore it by planting shade trees?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko gĩ ni egbo Ani manyɛ mawo jɛmɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni madu lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting hardy trees in bare or ruined patches helps rebuild the soil structure, traps ground moisture, and creates the shade needed to successfully replant crops later.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ loo hei ni efite lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni anyɛ akwɛ tsei heei yɛ omanyeyeli mli yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it necessary to hire extra farm labor when starting a new tree planting setup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aŋɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi krokomɛi afata he beni ajeɔ tso dumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young planted trees require frequent weeding, clearing of dense bush, and protection from pests during their early years so they are not choked before they can grow tall.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni ajie jwɛi shii abɔ. Afolɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli Koni akagbe lɛ dani eda.

english: Can I leave existing wild trees standing when clearing bush to plant new cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ni amɛkafite beni mijieɔ brɔshi koni mikɛdu kookoo hee lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving selected beneficial tall trees standing gives your new cocoa instant natural shade and saves you the years it would take to grow new shade trees from scratch.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oshi tsei ni kɛlɛ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha o-cocoa hee lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni ehaa okɛ afii babaoo ni okɛduɔ tsei heei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee lɛ yeɔ omanye.

english: How do I know if a tree on my farm is good for shade or if it will harm my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo kpakpa loo amɛbaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Good shade trees have high branches with light leaves that let filtered sunlight through and do not attract cocoa diseases, whereas harmful trees compete heavily for nutrients or carry pests.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ niji kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa hulu la tsɔɔ mli ni egbalaaa kookoo hela. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ loo akɛ amɛji mɛi ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: Is it helpful to plant food crops together with young shade trees on the same land?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ abaadu niyenii ni akɛ dumɔwui awo mli yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, intercropping temporary food plants with young shade trees provides immediate food and income while giving the shade trees time to grow big over two or three years.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduɔ niyenii ni akɛyeɔ nii yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni haa niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ be ni amɛdara yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if polluted water from nearby streams is harming my growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ miigba mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ?

english: If water contains harmful chemicals, your maize plants will develop burnt leaf tips, yellowing stems, or stunted growth even when the ground is wet. Healthy water keeps the leaves deep green and firm.
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ, Abɛi baaná baai lɛ ashishifãi ni shãa, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛkwɛɛɛ kwraa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ shiŋŋ.

english: How do chemical spills or polluted water in the soil affect my crops for the next planting season?
ga: Te tsofai ni hoɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Harsh chemicals stay in the ground and kill helpful earthworms and soil bacteria that feed plant roots. This causes future crops to grow weakly until the soil is treated with fresh organic manure.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa hiɔ sũ lɛ mli ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ sũ mli helai ni haa tsei shishifãi niyenii lɛ. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akɛ humus hee baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry weather to conserve water and protect themselves from heat. Planting shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia helps them retain moisture and keep their leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo gliricidia ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekwɛɔ efoji lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look wilted even though I water them every afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu haa daa gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering under the bright afternoon sun causes water to evaporate too quickly and can heat up the roots. Watering early in the morning or late evening allows roots to absorb moisture safely.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ adɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and watery instead of big and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ nu moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay small when the soil is packed too hard or lacks essential nutrients. Loosening the soil and adding organic compost gives the roots space to expand and store starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atoɔ.

english: Will spraying chemical weed killers around my crops make the food unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ he lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: Chemical weed killers can be absorbed into plant roots and remain in the harvest if sprayed too close to harvest time. Always follow recommended waiting periods after spraying before harvesting.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ abote tsei shishifãi amli ni ehi kpamɔ be lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ be ni bɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli tsɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, nyiɛmɔ be ni akɛha akɛ esa akɛ amɛmɛ lɛ sɛɛ yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do yellow spots appear on my tomato leaves before the whole plant dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ dani tomato tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow spots usually mean a fungal disease or small insects are attacking the leaves, stopping the plant from making food from sunlight. Removing infected leaves early prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii hela loo kooloo bibioo ko miitutua baai lɛ, ni no miitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast with big leaves that act like natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans pull natural food from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This feeds the neighboring maize plants, helping them grow taller without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Beans jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aná niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by sudden dry heat, lack of water, or applying too much fertilizer at once. Regular watering and gentle feeding keep the flowers attached to produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni haa amɛgbiɔ trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hao amɛ yɛ be kome mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa amɛ blɛoo lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize needs to grow strong. Applying the right fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help restore the green color and improve your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni sa loo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the earth, naturally refreshing your land for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to form big, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni mli wa.

english: What causes my pepper plant flowers to fall off before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ebafeɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during intense heat helps save the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily under the blazing sun. Keeping larger trees provides essential shade and keeps the air and soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ akwɛmɔ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Controlling these insect pests early prevents the disease from stunt-growing your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for a long time and naturally grow faster because they are adapted to thrive in harsh conditions. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing light, water, and food from your young seedlings.
