ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaafee yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it risky to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rainfall of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can dry out seeds right after they germinate. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the young plants receive continuous moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa koni eha tsei bibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from my harvest produce smaller cobs than certified seeds bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Many high-yielding farm seeds are hybrid varieties made for one-time planting. Seeds saved from your own harvest lose their vigor in the second generation, leading to smaller cobs and unequal plant sizes.
ga: Tsei dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ji tsei ni afee amɛ ekome ni aduɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpamɔ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni tsei lɛ adalɛi jeee ekome.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting in the barn just a few weeks after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Yams decay quickly if they suffer cuts or bruises during harvesting or if they are stored in a warm room without air circulating. Careful digging and storing yams on raised bamboo racks in a cool shed prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite oya kɛji akɛ afo loo atswa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsa sweet potatoi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto ŋmei shɛlɛf ni awó nɔ yɛ tsũ ko ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees or plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide living shade, cool down the soil, and retain moisture, which helps young cocoa seedlings survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is stressed, either from getting too much direct sunlight without shade, or because the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Adding shade or appropriate cocoa fertilizer can help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Eji kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli. aloo akɛni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do the small flowers on my cocoa tree actually turn into big cocoa pods?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fɔfɔi bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ cacao tso agbo ko?

english: Flowers turn into pods through a process called pollination. Tiny beneficial insects transfer pollen from the male part of a flower to the female part. Once fertilized, the flower stops dropping and slowly grows into a cocoa pod.
ga: Fɔfɔi bafeɔ pods kɛtsɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollination nɔ. kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Etsuɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ mli kɛyaa yoo lɛ fã ni ji yoo lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ awo lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baakpa gbee ni fiofio lɛ Ebaatsɔ kookoo ŋmeii

english: Why do so many of the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Most cocoa flowers drop off because they were not pollinated by insects, or because the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to support them. A healthy cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage will successfully turn into pods.
ga: Kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo akɛni tsei lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ lɛ hewɔ? Kakao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ yeɔ omanye ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ pods.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does it help my farm produce more cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewo kookoo babaoo?

english: Hand pollination is when a farmer manually picks a male flower part and touches it to the female flower part to ensure transfer of pollen. This guarantees that more flowers get fertilized, resulting in significantly more pods on each tree.
ga: Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ji be mli ni okwaafoi kɛ amɛdɛŋ holeɔ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ fã lɛ ni amɛtswaa yoo fɔfɔi lɛ fã lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ etsɔ mli. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ abaawo fɔfɔi babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa tso fɛɛ tso nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid spraying chemical insecticides when my cocoa trees are full of flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe be mli ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ eyi kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals during flowering can kill tiny insects like midges, which are responsible for natural pollination. Without these helpful insects to transfer pollen, fewer flowers will become pods, leading to a lower harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni ji adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔii ni baa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ bɛ ni baajie pollen lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why do I need to cut off some branches from my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can flow through the tree. Good airflow keeps the tree dry and reduces fungal diseases, while allowing energy to go into producing larger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa akɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, wet, and humid conditions. Water drops splash the fungus from the soil or infected pods onto healthy ones, causing them to turn black and rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. ni haa etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Why is it bad to leave overgrown weeds around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and valuable soil nutrients away from your cocoa trees. Dense weeds also trap high humidity around the trunk, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases and pests thrive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa hulutsoo shihilɛ baa. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its skin completely changes color, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to deep orange-yellow. Harvesting at full ripeness ensures the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhiɛ su etsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nikpamɔ beni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a primary food plant need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn pale green during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating too quickly during severe heat or drought stress, but it can also be a sign of virus transmission by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ be mli lɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ efee hela ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why does my cassava shed all its leaves during the dry season, and is the crop dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ hu?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water in its stems and roots. The plant is not dead; it is sleeping to survive the heat and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ewɔɔ koni ehi wala mli yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, Baai heei baakwɛ̃.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are too few pollinating insects like bees around to turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa, tamɔ ŋmeii, faaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsake fɔfɔi amɛfee aduawai.

english: Why does my okra produce small, woody fruits when planted during heavy downpours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni tamɔ tsei kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall leaves soil waterlogged, depriving roots of oxygen and washing away soil nutrients. This stresses the okra plant, causing it to produce tiny, tough fruits instead of healthy ones.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ, ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ maa gumbo lɛ nɔ mi. Enɛ haa ewoɔ yibii bibii ni wa yɛ yibii kpakpai najiaŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short, crooked, and small under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ji kukuji, ebɔle amɛhe, ni amɛji bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, soft, and deep soil to expand downward smoothly. Hard, compact soil or hidden stones block tuber growth, forcing the yams to become stunted and misshapen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tsiɔ tuber dalɛ naa. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and greener than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild species adapted over thousands of years to survive tough conditions, allowing them to steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni atsake amɛ yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la kɛ nu mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees produce fewer pods when surrounded by very large forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni koo mli tsei wuji waa ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: While young cocoa needs shade, mature cocoa requires ample sunlight to flower heavily and form pods. Too much shade creates dark, moist conditions that encourage black pod disease and reduce yields.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo. Kookoo ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi babaoo ni efee ŋmeii. Shade babaoo haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ ni woɔ black pod hela he hewalɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do insects appear inside my bagged maize even after I tie the sacks tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the grains while the crop is still standing in the field. If the grain is not thoroughly dried or treated before bagging, those hidden eggs hatch inside the sealed sacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmaa mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa loo atsuuu he nii dani awoɔ kotoku mli. Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli.

english: Why does cutting down big trees on my farm seem to cause rain to stop falling on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Trees release water vapor into the air through their leaves, which helps build local clouds and attract rainfall. When large areas of trees are cleared, the local air becomes drier, leading to delayed or reduced rainfall.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu lasu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa atatui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baa ni egbalaa nugbɔ. Kɛji ajie tsei wuji lɛ Kuu lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nugbɔ lɛ baatsɛ loo ebaa shi.

english: Why do my young crops wilt much faster after all the surrounding shade trees are removed from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ oya waa beni tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ egbi lɛ sɛɛ? Ani ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Large trees shield smaller crops from direct, harsh sunlight and strong winds that strip moisture from soil and leaves. Without shade trees, the hot sun dries out the soil and plants very quickly during dry spells.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni tsei daa oya waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get very hard after heavy tractors drive over it to work the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa beni traktɔi wuji hoɔ kɛhoɔ koni amɛbatsu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy tractors press the soil particles tightly together, causing soil compaction. This reduces the air spaces in the soil, making it harder for water to soak in and for crop roots to grow deep.
ga: Traktɔi wuji nyɛɔ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ anɔ waa aahu akɛ amɛhaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa nu akɛ ebaabote mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Does clearing and plowing my whole field with machines cause the soil to dry out faster?
ga: Ani ŋmɔji amli ni atseɔ ni akɛ tsɔnei tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya?

english: Yes, turning up the soil and exposing it directly to the sun accelerates evaporation. Without grass or mulch covering the soil, the ground loses stored moisture quickly before rain falls.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ otsake shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛwo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Kɛji jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ nu ni ato lɛ oya dani nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Does removing tree roots with heavy machinery hurt the soil quality for my crops?
ga: Ani tsei shishifãi ni akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii jieɔ lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni mikwɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: While uprooting trees clears space, it breaks up the topsoil structure. Loose topsoil can easily wash away during heavy rains or blow away in the wind, taking vital nutrients with it.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha he ko babaoo ahi shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔne lɛ efo. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa kɛya. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni okɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I use a tractor planter instead of planting my seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ trakta atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baadu dumɔwui?

english: A tractor planter places seeds at a uniform depth and exact distance apart across the whole farm. This ensures every seed gets an equal share of soil nutrients, sunlight, and moisture to grow evenly.
ga: Trakta lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa sũ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. ekomefeemɔ kɛha dalɛ ni yeɔ egbɔ

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them with a machine right before a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ tsɔne du amɛ dani hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ?

english: Machine planting loosens the soil and exposes seeds to air. If rain does not fall shortly after planting, the seeds dry out inside the loose soil before their roots can take hold.
ga: Tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ etsɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why is it better to use a tractor spreader to apply fertilizer instead of scattering it by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ trakta baagbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwã moŋ fe ni akɛ nine aaagbɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: A mechanical spreader distributes fertilizer evenly across the entire field. This prevents over-fertilizing some spots, which can burn crops, and under-fertilizing others, which leaves plants weak.
ga: Mɛi ni kɛ tsɔnei shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi hei komɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine, ni baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa. Ni kaawo hei krokomɛi ŋmɔtɔ fioo tsɔ, ni no baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why won't the fertilizer spread by my tractor work if the rain fails to fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi trakta lɛ egbɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before crop roots can absorb its nutrients. If there is no rain or moisture in the soil, the fertilizer sits harmlessly or burns the plant leaves without feeding the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi ni eyeee tso lɛ baai lɛ awui loo eshãaa lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ yeee nii.

english: Why do my crops grow more evenly when I completely clear the land with machines before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ́ mikɛ tsɔne tsu he lɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Completely clearing the land eliminates competition from wild weeds and aggressive tree roots, giving your planted crops full access to sunlight, soil space, and water.
ga: He lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kwraa lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni jɛɔ koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsei shishifãi ni baa lɛ amli lɛ kɛyaa. Ha otsei lɛ aná hulu la, shikpɔŋ, kɛ nu kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. Applying a balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the roots will supply the needed food to make the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ abɔle tso lɛ he. Shishifãi lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that create shade, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and preserving soil moisture until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are holes appearing in the middle of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in the center leaves of young maize are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the leaves. Checking your farm early and applying safe, approved pest control remedies protects the central growing tip so the crop can mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my cassava field before clearing the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ mi-cassava saatso lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the food provided by the fertilizer before your cassava roots can reach it. Clearing the weeds first ensures all the nutrients go directly into feeding your cassava plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni ebaaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa o-cassava tso lɛ niyenii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it better to leave space between my pepper plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oooshi gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are spaced properly, sunlight and fresh air can move easily between them, which stops diseases from spreading in damp leaves. Proper space also means the roots do not compete with each other for water and nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ha gbɛ ni sa kɛjɛ oteŋ. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nyiɛɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ mlɛo. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã baai ni mli efɔ lɛ anɔ. He ni sa lɛ hu tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ atswa nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the ground, acting as natural food for the next crop you plant in that field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my hybrid maize harvest for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one generation only. If you save seeds from your harvested hybrid maize and plant them again, the new plants will grow unevenly and produce smaller cobs with much lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ kɛhaa yinɔ kome pɛ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ to lɛ, du ekoŋŋ. Tsei heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Leaf curling in the hot sun is a defensive reaction where the tomato plant reduces its leaf surface to prevent losing too much water. If the leaves bounce back in the evening, the plant is managing the heat, but watering the root area early in the morning helps it handle high temperatures better.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Tomato tsei lɛ baa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine. Kɛji baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo lɛ miikpe. Shi kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shishifã lɛ he lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni enyɛ ekpee hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ edara ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the harvested shells has dark brown markings instead of being white or light-colored, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yibii ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my harvested grains mold quickly if I put them in sacks right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo kotokui amli beni mikpaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains contain trapped moisture inside them. Storing them in closed sacks immediately causes steam and humidity to build up, creating the exact environment mold and fungi need to rot your crop. Drying the grains in the sun until they crack cleanly when bitten prevents mold.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ emli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo kotokui ni aŋã mli lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa lasu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli ni tsɔɔ akɛ ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu la mli kɛyashi amɛbaakumɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mɔ ko ŋmɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, your maize is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants need to stay green and grow fast, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with huge leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: This happens when soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium. The plant uses all its energy to grow lush stems and leaves above ground instead of feeding and swelling the roots below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni amɛaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii ni amɛfuu.

english: How do I know if my crops are dying from too much water or from dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigboi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: When plants lack water, leaves turn brown, dry, and crispy at the edges. When plants get flooded with too much water, their roots drown, causing leaves to turn soft, pale yellow, and droop even though the soil is wet.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ. Kɛ́ nu babaoo eyi tsei amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni egbeeɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are soil improvers. They take nitrogen from the air and drop it into the soil through their roots, which helps feed the corn next to them without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to give a high yield only once. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the new plants will grow unevenly and produce very small cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo shikome pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei heei daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why does removing weeds early in the season give me a bigger harvest than weeding late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop plants are weak and must compete with weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Weeding early lets your crops drink all the nutrients while they are growing fastest.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni esa akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or water is irregular. High heat prevents pollination, so the plant sheds the useless flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination naa. Bɔni afee ni ato hewalɛ he lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms have invaded my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji cutworms ebote mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look inside the central funnel of young maize plants. If you see ragged holes in the leaf blades and tiny dark spots that look like sawdust, armyworms are inside eating the fresh growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo ko teŋgbɛ. Kɛji ona buji ni etse yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye aduawai ni yɔɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Curled, wrinkled pepper leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, or if stored in a hot room without airflow. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, shaded place with good wind prevents rot organisms from entering.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni efiteee lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ akabote mli.

english: What does a three-crop cycle mean, and how will it benefit my farm?
ga: Mɛni tsei akui etɛ lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni te ebaaye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A three-crop cycle means growing three different crops in sequence on the same land throughout the year. This keeps your soil fertile, breaks pest cycles, and gives you multiple harvests instead of relying on just one crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ shii etɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aaadu nibii sɔrɔtoi etɛ yɛ he kome yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii. Gbalamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni oha okpa ŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ohe aaafɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii henɔ kome pɛ nɔ.

english: Can I grow short-season food crops between my young mango trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ niyenii tsei ni yeɔ be kuku yɛ mango tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping crops like maize, cassava, or vegetables between young mango trees is a great practice. It provides food and extra income while the mango trees grow, and keeps weeds away from the tree roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ mango tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Ehaa niyenii kɛ shika kroko fataa he yɛ be mli ni mango tso lɛ daa lɛ, ni ehaa jwɛi bɛŋkɛɛɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Can growing mango trees bring in as much income for my family as a cocoa farm?
ga: Ani mango tsei ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miweku lɛ aná shika babaoo tamɔ kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Yes, mature mango trees can produce very high yield and income comparable to cocoa. Mangoes are in high demand for local fresh markets and processing factories, making them a profitable cash crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, mango tso ni eda lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo ni ená shika ni akɛtoɔ kookoo he. Mango he miihia waa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli hei heei kɛ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ mango lɛ. Ha efee shika gbɛfaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he.

english: Why do my mango trees produce a massive harvest one year and very little fruit the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ kpaa yibii babaoo afi kome shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called alternate bearing. Producing a huge harvest exhausts the tree's energy reserves, so it needs a year to rebuild. Proper pruning, regular watering, and adding fertilizer help the tree bear good fruit every year.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ sɛɛkuu bearing. Nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ haa hewalɛ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe afi dani anyɛ ama ekoŋŋ. pruning Nu daa Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai daa afi.

english: How long will I have to wait for my new mango seedlings to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni mango tso hee ko aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted mango seedlings usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years. Trees planted directly from seed take much longer, often 7 to 10 years, to yield fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli. Tsei ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo (bei pii lɛ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani ewoɔ yibii).

english: Why are the blossoms on my mango tree falling off before fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop early due to dry weather, strong winds, or pests like thrips. Ensuring the soil has enough moisture during flowering and managing pests protects the blossoms so they turn into fruit.
ga: Mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle in full sunlight while my mango seedlings handle the heat better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, mi mango tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and lose water quickly in direct sun, requiring shade trees like plantain to survive. Mango trees naturally have tougher leaves and deeper roots that tolerate strong sunlight and dry weather better.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la kpɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdamɔɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Mango tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa.

english: How do mango trees handle long dry seasons compared to cocoa trees?
ga: Te mango tsei yeɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ nɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto cacao tsei ahe?

english: Mango trees develop a deep taproot that reaches water far below the ground, allowing them to stay green during dry spells. Cocoa trees have shallow roots and lose leaves quickly when the topsoil dries out.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Cocoa tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ mli egbi.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my mango tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ mi mango tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the center of the tree so sunlight and fresh air can reach inner branches. This prevents fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing larger, higher-quality fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ anyɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested mangoes from bruising and rotting when transported over rough feeder roads?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-mango ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite ni ekafite kɛ́ akɛmiiya gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ anɔ?

english: Harvest mangoes when they are fully grown but still firm and green. Packing them in padded wooden or plastic crates rather than overloaded sacks protects them from bruising on bumpy roads.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ mango beni edara jogbaŋŋ shi eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo tso loo plastic adekai ni akɛ tsɔne ewo mli lɛ amli moŋ fe kotokui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee mɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I correctly measure liquid crop treatments using standard spoons like tablespoons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu nu mli tsei ahe tsofafeemɔi lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ spuni ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ spuni ni akɛwoɔ okpɔlɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Using standard spoons like a tablespoon helps ensure you give crops the exact recommended dose. Applying too little chemical will not protect the crop from pests, while applying too much can scorch the leaves or stunt plant growth.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ spuni ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ okpɔlɔ nɔ spuni tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ falɛ ni atsɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsofai fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ebuuu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛŋ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. yɛ be mli ni kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai loo atsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops produce a better harvest when I follow strict mixing instructions instead of guessing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ fe ni masusu he lɛ?

english: Crops absorb treatments safely only at specific concentrations. Guessing measurements can chemically burn the roots and foliage, whereas exact mixtures allow the plant to stay healthy and direct its energy into producing yield.
ga: Tsei baaŋɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ bɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɛ mli. Susumɔ lɛ he susumɔ baanyɛ aha tsofa ashã shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to apply chemical sprays on my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: No, spraying in intense heat can cause liquid treatments to evaporate too quickly or burn the leaves under strong sunlight. It is best to apply sprays early in the morning or late afternoon when temperatures are cooler.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nu ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo eha baai lɛ ashã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baatsu nii leebi loo shwane mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow or show burn marks after I spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛyɛ shãa okadii beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing or leaf burn usually happens when a chemical treatment is mixed too strong, sprayed at the wrong time of day, or applied in quantities larger than the crop can safely tolerate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsɔ futu mli. Ni akɛ tsofa lɛ baashwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli loo akɛtsu nii babaoo fe bɔ ni tsei lɛ baanyɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Lack of water usually causes plants to wilt uniformly during the hottest part of the day, while diseases often cause spotty leaf discoloration, powdery patches, or localized rotting even when the soil is damp.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ he ko kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ po.

english: Why do some seeds need to be treated with special protection powders before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ powda krɛdɛɛ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu dumɔwui komɛi ahe nii dani adu lɛ?

english: Treating seeds shields them from fungi, rot, and insects in the soil during early germination, ensuring more seeds successfully sprout into strong, healthy plants.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe. ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do different crops on my farm need different chemical treatments?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai srɔtoi atsu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nii lɛ?

english: Different crops attract different pests and diseases due to their leaves, roots, and sap composition. Using a treatment targeted to a specific crop type ensures effective protection without harming the plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛbaai, amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛmli nu lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ hewɔ. Tsofai ni akɛma tso pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa abuɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni eyeee tso lɛ awui.

english: What main factors cause my crops to produce a high yield at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: High crop yields depend on giving plants proper nutrients, protecting them from pests and weeds early, ensuring adequate water, and applying recommended care practices at every growth stage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ babaoo lɛ damɔ niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ nɔ. Tsei ahebuu mra kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi ahe Kwɛmɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shi ni akɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ amɛdalɛ fãi fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow healthy leaves at first but fail to produce good fruit later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli shi sɛɛ mli lɛ ewooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Crops require different nutrients at different stages. High nitrogen promotes early leaf growth, but plants need phosphorus and potassium later on to blossom and produce healthy fruit.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Shi tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ potassium bɔni afee ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds steal vital resources like moisture, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your young plants, causing the crop to grow slowly and yield less.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are short of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make green leaves and grow tall. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why will my maize yield less if I plant too many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant enough space allows them to develop strong stems and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli: Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my piece of land give me smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that particular plant loves from the soil. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts lets the soil rebuild its richness naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli tsei ni miida lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or lack of water during hot periods. Applying too much chemical fertilizer can also cause the plant to produce thick green leaves while shedding its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná baai eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and smelly in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water settles around the roots for too long during heavy rains, causing fungi to attack the plant. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cabbage plants covered in tiny holes overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani aha he gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually made by small caterpillars that hide under the leaves during the hot daytime and feed at night. Inspecting under the leaves early in the morning helps you catch and remove them early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa kaabeji baai amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ ni ojie amɛ mra.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agricultural shop produce better crops than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred to fight diseases and give high yields. Seeds saved from a previous harvest lose those special qualities in the next generation, often resulting in weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛ helai awuu ni ewo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl inward during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the hot sun, which keeps the plant from losing too much moisture. As long as the plants receive enough water, they unfold when the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi tomato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaajie ehe kpo beni gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully matured and ready to be pulled from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the plant leaves start turning yellow and dry out. You can confirm by digging up a sample pod; if the inside of the shell has dark veins and the seeds fully fill the pod, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ oma enɛ nɔ mi kɛtsɔ pod nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ nii ni ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ amli eyi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why does my cassava start rotting in the soil before I even dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ po shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays too wet for a long time, or when the roots stay in the ground past their fully matured stage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. aloo beni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛho amɛdalɛ be ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he.

english: Why do cassava roots turn soft and spoil if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots pass their peak maturity, they begin to break down, lose starch, and attract soil fungus that turns the roots soft and rotten.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara babaoo lɛ Ebaabɔi gbee, e-starch lɛ baafite, ni ebaagbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: How does heavy rainfall kill crops that are already growing well?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ momo lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil with water, which suffocates the roots and breeds disease organisms that destroy the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii feɔ. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ tso lɛ baa.

english: What can I do to stop water from standing in my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ nu naa koni ekahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: You can dig simple drainage channels to lead extra water away and plant your crops on raised mounds or ridges to keep the roots above standing water.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. koni ekɛ nu aya ni edu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava when the rainy season is at its peak?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Planting during extreme heavy rains often rots fresh stem cuttings before they can develop roots, so it is better to plant when rains are steady but moderate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei niji heei lɛ fiteɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa shi eshɛɔ he ni sa.

english: Can spraying weed killer on my farm harm or kill my main crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ awui loo efite?

english: Yes, if the weed chemical touches the leaves of your main crop or if you use the wrong type of herbicide, it can damage or kill the crop alongside the weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe baai kpe. aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ejaaa tsu nii. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite loo amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛfata jwɛi ahe.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and die right after I apply weed chemical?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: This happens when the wind carries chemical spray droplets onto your crop leaves, or when rain washes the chemical into the roots of your plants.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwie tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Aloo beni nugbɔ lɛ kɛ tsofai baa otso lɛ shishifãi amli lɛ.

english: When is the best time of day to spray weedicide on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning when the air is calm and cool so the wind does not blow the spray onto your crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatswa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant a very large farm of crops like cassava all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: If you plant a huge acreage all at once without a guaranteed buyer or enough workers, the crops will mature at the same time and rot before you can harvest them.
ga: Kɛji odu he ko ni da yɛ be kome mli ni mɛi ni baahe lɛ bɛ nɔmimaa loo nitsulɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome ni egboɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvest from going to waste if I cannot sell it right away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: You can prevent total crop loss by processing fresh cassava into long-lasting foods like gari or flour, or by planting in smaller batches at different times of the year.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni baafite lɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni ooofee niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ nɔ, loo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli

english: Why is it better for me to spray crop medicine early in the morning instead of during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ tsofa awo mli yɛ shwane mli?

english: Morning temperatures are cooler and wind is usually calm, which prevents the liquid spray from drying up too fast on the leaves or blowing away before it can work.
ga: Leebi hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu feɔ dioo. Enɛ haaa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ baai lɛ anɔ loo efo kɛya dani akɛtsu nii.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying medicine on my vegetables before I can safely harvest and sell them at the market?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ wo aduawai amli sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ akpa amɛ shweshweeshwe ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Every chemical has a safe waiting time (called a pre-harvest interval) listed on its container, which allows the chemical to break down so the food becomes safe for people to eat.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa yɛ be ni sa ni ekɛbaamɛ. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani kpamɔ be) lɛ ji nɔ ni atsɔɔ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ ni niyenii lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: If I spray my crop medicine once and the insects die, do I still need to spray again after a few weeks?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie tsei lɛ anɔ shikome ni kooloi lɛ gboi. Ani ehe miihia ni awo mi tsofa kroko lolo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Yes, because the first spray often does not kill insect eggs. Spraying again after two to three weeks kills the newly hatched pests before they can grow and lay more eggs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ egbeee kooloi awui. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ otsii 2-3 sɛɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi ni fɔmɔ ehee lɛ dani amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Can I mix two different chemical medicines together in my knapsack sprayer to save time on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai enyɔ afutu yɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should not mix chemicals unless the instructions specifically say it is safe. Mixing the wrong chemicals can destroy their power or create a mixture that burns your crop leaves.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofai futuɔ tsofai kɔkɔɔkɔ ja gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ kɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ amɛhe yɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ loo efee nɔ ko ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni shãa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are being attacked by worms before the leaves start showing big holes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii etutua mi-abele lɛ dani baai lɛ aje shishi amɛjie buji wuji akpo?

english: Check deep inside the central funnel of young maize plants; early pests like fall armyworms hide inside and leave tiny pinholes or wet, sawdust-like droppings before major leaf damage appears.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Mra be mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ, teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo ŋmeii ni efɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii dani baai lɛ afiteɔ waa.

english: How many days should I wait after spraying a chemical before deciding whether it is actually working on my farm?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ sɛɛ Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Most farm medicines take about three to seven days to show clear results, as pests slowly stop feeding and die off or fungal spots stop spreading.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee gbii etɛ kɛyashi kpawo dani etsɔɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ni kadiɔ mɔ. Ejaakɛ fiofio lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Kpaa niyeli ni egboɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kpaɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants start developing dark spots and rotting as soon as the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛhe feɔ duŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji wɔná nugbɔ ni naa wa pɛ?

english: Rainwater splashes fungal spores from the soil onto your plant leaves, and the warm, wet weather creates the perfect condition for fungus to spread quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ nu shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen fertilizer, forcing the plant to move nutrients from old bottom leaves up to the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: When cassava sticks are planted too close, their roots compete fiercely for soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight, leaving little energy for the tubers to swell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ eshiɔ yitso lɛ koni ekɛgbala mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster on my farm than the crops I planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to thrive in harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni ehiii amli. Enɛ haa amɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender roots and thin leaves that lose water very fast under intense heat. Without taller plants like plantains or shade trees to block the sun, the young cocoa gets heat-stressed and dries out before its roots can grow deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains loo shade trees bɛ Cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable roots with dry grass help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mishishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket that shields the soil from the sun's direct heat. It keeps the moisture in the soil from evaporating quickly, ensuring the crop roots stay cool and hydrated for longer.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ akafite oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and strong growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the maize plant steals it from older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tsei niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly microbes living on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When these plants finish growing and decay, they leave behind rich natural plant food that feeds whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tsei nɛɛ daraa ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ, Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii babaoo yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛye ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce energy, which then travels down to build large underground tubers. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also protects them from rotting and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills all the air spaces in the soil with water. Cassava roots need air to breathe, and when trapped in waterlogged ground for too long, they suffocate and begin to decay unless planted on raised soil mounds or ridges.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. ni kɛji akɛ ehi ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ ewo muji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ. ja adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy winds blow during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow and stay close to the surface of the soil. When heavy bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, and wet soil weakens the roots' grip, making it easy for wind to push the tree down unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji fɔfɔi agbo ko da yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili. Ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni ekɛ tsei baashwie shi. Ja nɔ ko ni akɛ tso fee lɛ yɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences severe stress from high heat or irregular watering. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination of the flowers, causing the plant to shed them rather than try to grow fruit under harsh conditions.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ ni naa wa kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Ha tso lɛ ajie baai lɛ moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Upward curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of new growth, or by viruses carried by these pests. This damages the leaf tissue and stops the plant from growing healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei ni eda lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe nibii ni baa lɛ nɔ Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow weak and produce small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mitso titri lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ewooo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and have strong root systems that aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your main crops. When weeds take up these essential resources first, your main crop goes hungry and cannot produce a full yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Beni jwɛi yeɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating the leaves and the inside of my young maize stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mibi lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛmli lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a very common pest in Ghana that targets young maize. They hide inside the central whorl of the plant to eat soft leaves. Inspecting your field early and applying approved treatments when plants are young prevents them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ efiteɔ onibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow, curling up, and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Curled ni ekwɛɔ ni efite?

english: This distortion is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents and pulling out infected plants early.
ga: Nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɔ ni kwɛɔ bo nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mra.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Rotating them naturally feeds your soil for the next crop season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from growing and stealing food from your vegetables.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ o-vegetables lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing your seeds properly ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when heavy rains and winds come just before the bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the soil, making heavy fruiting trees top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with bamboo or wooden prop poles prevents strong winds from pulling the root system out of the wet ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ feɔ tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee tso lɛ fi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to produce the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground into the sun and prevents fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ lɛ, ni ebaatsi fungal leaf helai anaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate roots and cannot handle dry Harmattan winds and direct sun. Planting plantain trees alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the soil moist and protects tender leaves until the cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii duɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebu baa bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi kookoo shishifãi lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Putting dry fertilizer on dry ground can burn and damage plant roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out flower pollen, preventing fruits from forming. Watering regularly at the roots and providing light shade during peak heat helps the flowers stay healthy and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafee Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa ni ahaa amɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely together, they compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Spacing plants properly allows each crop to get enough food and light to develop bigger leaves and larger yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ baai wuji aba ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I squeeze as many pepper seedlings as possible into my small plot?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui babaoo shwie miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: No, planting too densely usually lowers your overall harvest. Overcrowded pepper plants choke each other out, produce fewer and smaller fruits, and trap moisture that encourages diseases to spread.
ga: Dabi, ni aduɔ babaoo tsɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ baa shi. Chili tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibioo ni efeɔ bibioo. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni woɔ hela hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables rot on the stem when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, air cannot flow freely between them. Dampness from dew or rain gets trapped under the thick leaf canopy, creating a moist environment where fungal rot thrives.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abɔle nakai tsei lɛ ateŋ oya. Fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo nugbɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni etse amɛhe banee lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato stems growing tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants stretch upward when they are not receiving enough direct sunlight. The plant stretches toward the light to survive, which makes the main stem weak and unable to support heavy fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa la lɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant shade trees alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛfataa kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under strong direct sunlight. Shade trees act as living umbrellas, shielding young plants from harsh heat until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants yellow and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shedding leaves is a natural survival mechanism for cassava during dry periods. By dropping its leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and keeps its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala yɛ ŋmei be mli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my corn turn yellow and die while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the corn lacks key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. The plant responds by moving the remaining nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to the top growing leaves.
