ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei haa hetoo kɛtsɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Extreme heat or lack of water causes stress that prevents tomato flowers from pollinating properly. When pollination fails due to heat stress, the plant drops the unfertilized flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ baa. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ latsaa he haomɔ hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even after I have already added fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight intended for your crops. Even with fertilizer, weeds will consume the food first if they are not cleared away.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ, jwɛi lɛ baaye nii klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji ajieee amɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ jie

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, draw water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree. Removing excess suckers leaves the strongest shoot to grow, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi loo suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ baagbala nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ adara. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunshine because their leaves are thin and tender. They need shade crops like plantains grown alongside them to block intense sunlight and hold moisture in the soil while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face extreme stress, such as very high temperatures, irregular watering, or getting too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: The very first rain after a long dry spell often wet only the top soil without providing deep moisture. Planting right away can cause your seeds to sprout and then wither if rain does not fall again within a few days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ haaa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turn dark brown and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen gives plants their green color, and when there isn't enough in the soil, the plant steals it from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crops.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava crop producing very large stems and leaves but tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai wuji waa lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy foliage above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes inside the hidden center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm. The adult moth lays eggs on the leaves, and once the caterpillars hatch, they crawl deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant where it is dark and safe to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni eda ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Amɛhe yɛ ediŋŋ ni niyenii taomɔ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants twisted, small, and covered in yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, bibii ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from producing food properly, causing them to curl, shrink, and turn yellow.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots inside the barn even before I take them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ dani mikɛ amɛ po yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living organisms. Once their natural resting phase (dormancy) ends, the warm air triggers the tuber to use its stored water and energy to grow shoots in preparation for the next rainy season.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli. Kɛji adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be (wɔɔ) lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛsaa tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do older farmers always advise me to plant plantains on the same land with my new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko woɔ mi ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ madu kookoo hee yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain grows fast and tall, providing temporary shade that protects delicate young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ekwɛɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I mix my cassava plants directly into the same plot with cocoa and plantain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ futuɔ kookoo kɛ plantains ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cassava spreads roots heavily and consumes large amounts of nutrients and water, which can compete with young cocoa trees and stunt their growth.
ga: Cassava gbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa babaoo ni eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ abɔ akaŋ ni etsĩ amɛdalɛ naa.

english: What simple steps can I take to get a high yield from my cocoa farm?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Getting a good harvest requires keeping proper shade balance, regularly pruning dead or overgrown branches, clearing weeds, and protecting the trees from pests and diseases like black pod.
ga: Nikpamɔ kpakpa biɔ ni ahiɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni obu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe.

english: Why is cassava able to grow in drier sections of the farm where cocoa dies off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi ni kookoo gboɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a tough crop with deep tuber roots that store moisture and nutrients, making it drought-resistant, whereas young cocoa needs soft, moist, and shaded soil to survive.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni toɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo bibioo he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli efɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ehi shi.

english: What is the benefit of separating different crop types into distinct sections on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni ajara mli awoɔ fãi srɔtoi amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Grouping compatible crops together prevents stronger plants from stealing light and food from weaker ones, makes weeding easier, and helps you manage each crop's specific needs better.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee lɛ ni akɛaafee kuu lɛ tsiɔ tsei ni he wa lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. ni eye ebua bo ni okwɛ tso fɛɛ tso hiamɔ nii krɛdɛɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting cocoa before I get a good harvest?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani ená yibii kpakpai?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years, while traditional varieties may take 4 to 5 years to produce a full yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will growing plantain beside cocoa hurt the soil nutrients over time?
ga: plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani kookoo baaná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Plantain uses nutrients, but when you cut down the leaves and stems after harvest and leave them on the ground, they decay and return organic food back into the soil for the cocoa.
ga: Plantains kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii Shi kɛ́ ofolɔ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ beni okpa ni oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Plantains lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ kookoo.

english: Can underground cassava tubers damage the root system of nearby cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ afite cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, as cassava tubers swell, they compact the surrounding earth and block cocoa roots from spreading outwards to find water and nutrients.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã kponɔgbɛ koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Does planting temporary food crops with cocoa reduce the quality of the cocoa harvest?
ga: Ani niyenii ni akɛ kookoo duɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haa kookoo ni akpaa lɛ baa shi?

english: No, planting the right nurse crops like plantain actually protects young cocoa and supports healthy tree growth, which leads to better yields later on.
ga: Dabi, nurse tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he ni ehaa tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa yibii kpakpai baa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some cocoa trees on my land produce many pods while others right next to them yield very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ?

english: Yield differences usually come from variations in soil richness, how much shade or sunlight a specific tree gets, pests attacking certain trees, or differences in the age and health of the seedling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi amli. Bɔ ni tso lɛ náa hulutsoo loo hulu la babaoo. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa tsei komɛi loo srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ afii kɛ amɛhewalɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green and leafy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure brings back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ená baai. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and twisted even when the leaves and vines grow very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni efite lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ edara waa moŋ?

english: Yam vines grow large when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, but tubers need potassium and loose soil to expand. Mounding the soil well and using balanced fertilizer helps the tubers grow large and straight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa babaoo kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi potassium kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia bulb lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Curling yellow leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural offices is the best way to keep the crop healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle yucca he lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai ni Okwaayeli Nitsumɔhe lɛ etsɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: What causes small green worms to eat holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli?

english: Those worms are caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by small moths. Planting cabbage alongside strong-smelling crops like onions or using recommended neem-based sprays can protect the leaves from getting eaten.
ga: Nomɛi ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa, tamɔ ŋmei, loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni neem yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ naa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp weather. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and clearing away infected pods prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures are extremely high or when the soil gets too dry. Mulching the soil with dry grass keeps it cool and moist, helping the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomato.

english: Why does my pepper plant stop making new leaves once it starts growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ baai heei feemɔ beni mibɔi lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants direct most of their food energy into growing the fruit rather than leaves. Picking peppers regularly when they are ripe encourages the plant to produce new leaves and more flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo woɔ aduawai lɛ amli moŋ fe baai lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwie shi daa kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo baai heei kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why are my watermelon vines spreading all over the farm but producing very few melons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons produce separate male and female flowers and rely on bees to carry pollen between them. If there are few bees or if chemical sprays are used during the day, fewer flowers get pollinated to produce melons.
ga: Watermelon yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. ni amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ ŋmeii anɔ koni amɛkɛ pollen awo fɔfɔii ateŋ Kɛji ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ loo akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli Abaawo fɔfɔi hu pollen koni ekɛ melon fioo aba.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into thin strips during windy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally along their veins in high winds to protect the central stem from snapping. It is a normal survival habit of the plant, though planting windbreak trees around your farm reduces heavy leaf damage.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa koni ekɛtsi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ. Eji tsei ashihilɛ su ni yaa nɔ daa. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ haa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi babaoo po.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cowpea seeds require moisture to wake up and start growing. If the soil is too dry, the seed stays dormant or dies inside the ground before it can break through the soil surface.
ga: Cowpea dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. loo egbo yɛ sũ lɛ mli dani enyɛ ebote sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers put three seeds in one hole when planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ dumɔwui etɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ́ amɛmiidu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Planting three seeds per hole acts as an insurance policy. If insects eat one seed or another fails to sprout, you still get healthy plants. Once they grow, you can thin out the weakest shoot so the remaining stalks get enough space and food.
ga: Dumɔwui etɛ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ ji inshuɔrans he mla. Kɛji kooloo ko ye dumɔwui lɛ eko lɛ ekwɛɛɛ. Obaaná tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lolo. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ baaha tso ni eshwɛ lɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I leave measured spacing between my crop rows instead of planting seeds closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stems and produce large fruits or cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso ni wa ni ewo yibii loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen from excess manure or chemical fertilizer. Nitrogen forces the plant to focus all its energy on leaf growth above ground rather than swelling the tubers under the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli. Nitrogen nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense sunlight, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. Wilting is a natural defense mechanism where the plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss until the heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Withering ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi la ni tsoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds grow faster than domesticated crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your soil. Clearing them early ensures your crop gets full access to nutrients during its critical early growth phase.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense full sunshine. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and preserving soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for expanding the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight while keeping them away from hot soil and rot-causing fungi.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ akabɔ he.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei ashishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is full of concentrated salts that draw moisture out of plant tissues, causing severe burning to delicate stems and surface roots. Placing fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away allows feeder roots to absorb it safely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli. Ekɛ shãa ni naa wa baa tsei kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Kɛ́ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow when water stays on my field for days after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flooded soil pushes out all the air pockets that roots need to breathe. Without oxygen, plant roots stall and cannot absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the foliage to turn pale yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ais ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly on the same plot depletes the specific soil nutrients that crop loves and allows specialized pests and soil diseases to multiply. Rotating crops starves out pests and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight during their first few years. Leaving some tall shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside them creates protective shade and keeps the moisture in the soil that young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha hulutsoo loo dumɔ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ tsei nɛɛ ahe. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ he ni ebuɔ he lɛ baa.

english: Why do my mature cashew trees produce fewer nuts when the branches grow very close together and block out the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni eniji lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers need direct sunlight and good airflow to develop into nuts. When branches become too thick and crowded, inner leaves get shaded out and trapped moisture encourages fungal growth, which stops flower buds from forming properly.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔii lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu ni emɔ mli lɛ baawo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts from the leaf tip and moves down the middle of lower leaves means the plant is starving for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food maize uses to build green leaves and grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai eŋɔli ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji ni mli wa.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground. When these plants harvest or decay, they leave behind rich, natural nitrogen fertilizer in the soil.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ akpa tsei nɛɛ loo amɛgboi lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the farm during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in heavy soil fills up the air spaces around the roots, making it hard for the cassava to breathe. Wet underground conditions allow water-loving rot fungi to attack and destroy the mature cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmei lɛ akɛ ebaamu. Shikpɔŋ shishi shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ haa hydrophilic rot fungi lɛ tutuaa ni efiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni eeenyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce enough energy to build large tubers underground. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also protects them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing fertilization. When a flower cannot be fertilized, the plant naturally sheds the blossom to conserve its water and nutrients.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Beni anyɛɛɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ko Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛbu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my hot pepper plants curling upward and remaining small and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually a response to tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or transmitting a leaf-curl virus that disrupts normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hetoo kɛha kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. loo egbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain mats produce smaller fruit bunches when I allow many shoots to grow around the main mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, directing energy into growing larger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa hewalɛ lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do many small, young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the stem before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii babaoo feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This condition, known as wilt or pod rot, occurs when the tree is stressed by nutrient deficiencies, prolonged dry spells, or fungal infections like black pod disease, causing the tree to discard excess pods it cannot feed.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ wilt loo pod rot. Ebaa beni tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eye lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture quickly from young cocoa trees. Keeping shade trees like plantains and applying dry grass mulch around the base holds moisture in the soil and protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ Konii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ shãaa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ Mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to fight for the same water and soil food. Keeping only one main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures the plant has enough energy to grow large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdumɔwui wuji ni tsii baa.

english: This is typically the Fall Armyworm, a pest common in maize fields. They hide inside the central leaves (the whorl), so applying recommended treatments or neem liquid early in the morning directly into the center of the plant helps stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni afɔɔ naa waa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fɔɔ baa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (rings), no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem tsofa lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa amɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots feed calcium to the developing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium aha tomatoi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts before maize make my maize grow stronger the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ mli waa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen from the air and leaves it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses this natural nitrogen as fertilizer to grow tall and green.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cassava stems growing very tall and leafy, but the roots under the ground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo be babaoo. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: The first rain often wets only the top surface of the dry soil and is usually followed by hot, dry days. If seeds germinate without deep soil moisture, the young roots will dry out and die before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ bɛ mli. Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings grow thin and fall over when I raise them under heavy shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch upward and grow weak stems when searching for sunlight. Giving them partial sunlight in the nursery makes the stems thick and strong enough to survive being transplanted into the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ be mli ni amɛtaoɔ hulu la lɛ. Hulu ni shɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fã ko haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsake kɛya saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within a few months, while cassava grows slowly. Once the maize is harvested, the cassava spreads out and takes over the space, giving you two crops from the same land without them choking each other.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo Beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ni eŋɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome ni amɛtsiii amɛhe naa.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crop more during the first few weeks after planting than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small roots and leaves, so they easily lose the battle against fast-growing weeds for sunlight and water. Once the crops grow taller and shade the ground, they naturally prevent weeds from growing.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhe feɔ oya kɛji amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛha hulu la kɛ nu. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo Jwɛi lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct, hot sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees on your farm protects young cocoa from sun scorch and helps retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaabu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: If too many young shoots grow around one plantain tree, they fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Ekɛ dumɔwui baawu koni ena niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient it needs to stay green and build heavy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni aná su ni ji eŋɔli ni haa ŋmãa toi ni tsii baa.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help the soil grow better crops later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotting while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato shishi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or water consistently while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi moŋ ni eeekwɛ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, drought, or poor pollination, which forces the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ he. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy required to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha bulb agbo ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil during periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when left in waterlogged soil because the trapped water starves the roots of air, causing fungal diseases to attack and decompose the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni emɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why does clearing weeds early in the season make my crops yield much bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer away from your crops, so clearing them early allows your crops to get all the resources they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more when I grow the same vegetable in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshinii lɛ beni miduɔ aduawai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly allows pests that eat that specific plant to survive in the soil year after year and build up massive populations.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ekɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo aba

english: How do I know it is the right time to start planting my maize after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath might still be too dry. Wait until you get a few steady rains so the soil stays moist enough for the seeds to germinate and grow without drying out.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why should I leave space between my crop plants instead of planting them very close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and air to grow strong and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda waa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from shade trees or food crops like plantains during their first few years to keep their leaves from burning and to preserve soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ hulutsoo tsei loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akashã, ni koni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant is under stress. This is commonly caused by a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, prolonged dry spells, or sap-sucking pests like mealybugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very beneficial. Beans absorb nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch direct sunlight. Exposing the leaves to sunlight allows the plant to produce enough energy to grow big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ wo hulu la mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are all just plants growing in the dirt?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ ji amɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal essential water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops. This starves your crops, making them weak and significantly reducing your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain, but not during heavy downpours. Covering the fertilizer lightly with soil near the base of the plant stops the rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the growing tip of the maize plant and eats the young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from my previous maize harvest for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops lose their strength and disease resistance over time, leading to lower yields. Using fresh certified seeds ensures uniform growth and a much stronger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛdaraa daa ni amɛkpaa nii waa.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat vegetables right after I spray them with farm medicine?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye aduawai amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ wo amɛmli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, it is not safe. Every crop medicine has a required waiting period called a pre-harvest interval. You must wait a specific number of days after spraying before harvesting so the chemical breaks down fully and the produce becomes safe to consume.
ga: Dabi, ebɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani akpaa ŋmaa. Esa akɛ omɛ gbii ayibɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ yɛ tsofa ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okpa. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afite kwraa ni nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha niyenii.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key food crops need to build leaf greenness. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help your maize turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua o-ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my fertilizer burn my crops when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shãa ŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can absorb it safely. When the soil is dry, concentrated fertilizer sits against the roots and sucks water out of the plant instead of feeding it, which causes the leaves to scorch and dry up.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fĩɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaaha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have small holes in them, and what can I do to stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baa lɛ mli bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni mɛni mafee koni makpa amɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by tiny caterpillars eating the crop. You can protect your cabbages by checking the undersides of leaves early and spraying recommended organic neem liquids or approved insecticides before the pests multiply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu o-cabbage lɛ he kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ organic neem nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ dani kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ayi afa.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and rot on the ground when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Tomato branches become heavy once fruit grows, and the plant stem cannot support the weight alone. Staking your tomatoes with wooden sticks lifts the fruit off the damp soil, preventing rot and keeping pests away.
ga: Tomato niji lɛ feɔ mlɛo beni aduawai lɛ daa lɛ. Ni tsɔne lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ muji lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ŋmɛ tomatoi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni eshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Flowers drop off pepper plants mainly due to stress caused by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil moist during hot spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔi ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. You can prevent it by pruning tree branches to let in light and clearing weeds so air can dry out the pods after rain.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ooofolɔ sɛɛ koni eha la aba kɛ jwɛi ni ooojie koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest produce smaller cobs when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛji midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Most modern farm seeds are hybrid varieties bred for a single strong harvest. When you save and replant those seeds, the crop loses its vigor, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs compared to buying fresh hybrid seeds.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui babaoo ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afɔɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni mli wa kome. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Can I spray weedkiller on my farm without destroying the crops I already planted?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni mifiteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu momo lɛ?

english: Yes, but only if you use a 'selective' weedkiller designed specifically for your crop type, or apply 'non-selective' weedkillers carefully between crop rows using a shield on your sprayer so the chemical never touches your plant leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tsu nii pɛ. ‘Halamɔi’ ni afee pɔtɛɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ‘kaahala’ yɛ tsei akui ateŋ kɛtsɔ shield ni yɔɔ o-sprayer lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ akashɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: How can I find out the exact variety of cocoa growing on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kookooi srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different cocoa varieties have different strengths and weaknesses. Having an extension officer or technical staff inspect your farm can help you identify your specific cocoa variety and understand how it handles disease.
ga: Cocoa henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ bɔjɔmɔi srɔtoi. Kɛ́ oha mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ŋaalɔ ko bakwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oyoo kookoo henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni onu bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ helai anɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Are there certain cocoa varieties that can resist or survive common farm diseases better than others?
ga: Ani kookoo henɔi komɛi yɛ ni nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ loo amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi?

english: Yes, some cocoa varieties are more resistant to specific diseases than others. Consulting technical officers helps you learn which cocoa types are best suited to resist major threats on your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo henɔi komɛi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai komɛi anɔ fe ekrokomɛi. Wɔ ŋaawolɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋaa gbɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ kookoo henɔi ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni okɛteɔ shi awoɔ gbeyeishemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is Cocoa Swollen Shoot, and why is it such a major problem for cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot ni mɛni hewɔ eji naagba wulu kɛha kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot is a severe viral disease affecting cocoa trees. It drastically reduces farm productivity and damages the health of the tree, making it one of the biggest threats to a cocoa farmer's yield.
ga: Cocoa Swollen Shoot ji hela ko ni naa wa ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni yeɔ kookoo tsei anɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔ mli yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa ni efiteɔ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ kome ni woɔ kookoo okwaafoi lɛ aŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbeyei fe fɛɛ.

english: Can I cure a sick cocoa tree by buying chemical medicine at the market?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsa cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ni mahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Buying unverified chemical sprays without expert advice is often a waste of money because not all cocoa diseases, especially viral ones like Cocoa Swollen Shoot, can be cured with chemical medicines.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ hemɔ ni mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ŋaawoo bɛ he lɛ ji shika fitemɔ be fɛɛ be, ejaakɛ jeee kookoo helai fɛɛ yeɔ helai. Titri lɛ, helai ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa, tamɔ kookoo mli fũu lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai atsa.

english: Why do the medicines I buy for my sick cocoa trees fail to cure them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mihe miha mikookoo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ tsaaa mi lɛ?

english: Many chemical treatments cannot cure viral infections like Cocoa Swollen Shoot. Spending money on spray treatments for incurable diseases is wasteful when the true solution requires removing the affected trees.
ga: Tsofai babaoo tsaaa helai ni jɛɔ muawai amli baa, tamɔ kookoo tsei ni efuu. Shika ni afiteɔ kɛshwieɔ hela ko ni anyɛɛɛ atsa lɛ nɔ lɛ ji fitemɔ kɛji akɛ eba akɛ abaajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛtsu naagba diɛŋtsɛ lɛ he nii.

english: Why do agricultural officers insist on cutting down trees infected with Cocoa Swollen Shoot instead of spraying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ afo tsei ni kookoo eyi mli obɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafɔse tsofa lɛ?

english: Cocoa Swollen Shoot has no chemical cure. The only effective way to stop the disease from spreading to healthy trees across your farm is to physically cut down the infected trees.
ga: Tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛtsaa kokoo ni efuu lɛ. Gbɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ ji ni okɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does cutting down a sick cocoa tree help save the rest of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ehere mikookoo ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala?

english: Removing an infected tree gets rid of the source of the disease, preventing Cocoa Swollen Shoot from jumping to nearby healthy cocoa trees and ruining your entire farm.
ga: Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ hela lɛ jɛɛhe lɛ kɛyaa. Tsi Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ naa koni ekaju kɛya kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni okpãtã oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why should I contact technical staff before buying chemical treatments for my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋaa he najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko abɔ dani mahe tsofai ni akɛbaatsa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Getting advice from technical staff before taking action ensures you correctly identify the issue, preventing you from wasting money on ineffective medicines and helping you choose the right solution.
ga: Kɛ́ otao ŋaa kɛjɛ ŋaalɔi adɛŋ dani oya nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oyoo naagba lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite shika yɛ tsofai ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe. ni eye ebua bo ni ohala tsabaa kpakpa.

english: Why should I allow technical officers access to enter and inspect my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋaa nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Giving technical staff access allows them to accurately diagnose disease outbreaks early, inspect your trees, and safely manage threats like Cocoa Swollen Shoot before they destroy your harvest.
ga: Nitsumɔhe nine ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋaa gbɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ haa amɛnaa helai ni baa lɛ jogbaŋŋ mra. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ ni okwɛ gbeyeishemɔi tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is the best first step I should take when I notice signs of disease on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ kɛ́ mina hela he okadii yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: The best first option is to report the issue to an agricultural technical officer or extension staff so they can examine the trees and give you accurate guidance before you attempt any treatment.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ naagba lɛ abɔ okwaayeli he nilelɔ loo sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ ko he amaniɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkwɛ tso lɛ mli ni amɛwo bo ŋaa ni ja dani oka tsofafeemɔ ko okwɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly when the heat is high. The yellowing happens because the plant is stressed from lack of water and cannot absorb essential nitrogen nutrients from the dry soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ kɛji akɛ edɔ. Yellowing baa ejaakɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nitrogen nibii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I plant cassava too close to my maize crop, will one destroy the other?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ tsɔ Ani ebaakpata tso kroko lɛ hiɛ?

english: Yes, planting them too close causes them to compete for the same food, water, and sunlight. Cassava grows tall leaves that block sunlight from maize, while maize roots steal soil nutrients before cassava can establish its tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome he. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ baai kakadaji ni haa hulu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers before they turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed young flowers when they suffer from water stress, sudden heat, or lack of soil nutrients. The tree drops flowers it cannot support to save its energy to keep the main tree alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi bibii yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. hulutsoo trukaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: This usually happens due to bacterial wilt or root rot from overwatering. When root rot attacks, the plant's internal water pipes get blocked, so water cannot travel up to the leaves even if the ground is soaked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Beni shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa Atsiɔ tsei lɛ amli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside corn, they share this free natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for the corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛdara yɛ ŋmãa lɛ masɛi Amɛbaajara adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thin stems but giving me small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo, shi eshishifãi lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: When cassava grows under heavy shade, it uses all its food energy to grow tall stems to reach for sunlight. Because energy is wasted on height, there is little food left to grow big, thick tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo etso lɛ mli ni ekɛ hulu la aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewalɛ laajeɔ kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta. No hewɔ lɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs agboi ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do fall armyworms prefer to eat my young tender maize instead of the old plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-baby corn lɛ moŋ fe tsei momo lɛ?

english: Young maize plants have soft, sweet leaves that are easy for caterpillars to chew and digest. Older maize plants develop tough, fibrous leaves and stalks that are harder for pests to eat.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni ŋɔɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmeii nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni amɛyeɔ amɛmli oya. Abele tsei ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ baai ni wa, fibrous kɛ tsei tsei. ni ewa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye lɛ

english: Why should I cover the ground around my plantain suckers with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Dumɔwui ni jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that stops direct sunlight from drying out the soil. It retains soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn brown and wither right after heavy rainfall starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: High moisture combined with warm air creates the perfect condition for fungal diseases like yam anthracnose to spread. Excess rainwater sitting on foliage allows fungal spores to multiply quickly and damage the leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ sweet potato anthracnose lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ta baai anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ faa oya ni efiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why is it important to pinch off the extra side branches from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing excess side branches prevents the plant from wasting food on unnecessary leaves. This forces the pepper plant to send its water and food straight into producing larger, healthier pepper fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite baa niyenii ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii amaje tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off the extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Removing extra suckers ensures that the parent plant does not have to share its water and soil nutrients, allowing all the plant's energy to go into producing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa lɛ, ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aja nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ plantains ŋmɔji wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen food in the soil, or that waterlogged soil around the roots is preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ ni nu ebɔle he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and fail to make big cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving none of them with enough energy to grow full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwu ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with lots of leaves but producing only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? shi eyɛ yitso bibioo Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their strength into growing top leaves and stems instead of storing energy down in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋwɛi ŋmei lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground and spreads them out in the sunlight, allowing the plant to catch light easily and produce bigger, healthier tubers below.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ la nɔ mlɛo ni ekɛ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or if there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable beds with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry material acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool, preserves water in the soil during hot days, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to wilt even when the rain is falling regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and root space away from your crops before your plants can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ejuɔ sũ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why does my farm land produce fewer crops a few years after clearing the natural forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo yɛ afii fioo komɛi ni mikɛjie adebɔɔ mli kooi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Forest trees drop leaves that rot and continuously feed the soil. When you clear the forest completely, the initial natural food in the soil gets used up quickly, and without shade and tree roots, heavy rains wash away the fertile topsoil.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni fiteɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ ojie koo lɛ mli kwraa lɛ Adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Ni kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo tso shishifãi bɛ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it harmful to burn my bush and tree stumps every year before planting my crops?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui akɛ mashã mi jwɛi kɛ mi tsei akutsei lɛ daa afi dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, frequent burning kills beneficial insects and micro-bugs in the soil, burns away natural plant food, and eventually turns fertile farmland into dry grassland where crops struggle to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, la ni ashãa shii abɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Metabolize plant foods naturally Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaatsɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ etsɔ jwɛi shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ.

english: Why is spear grass taking over my farm so quickly after I cleared the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie tsei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Forest trees block sunlight from reaching the ground, which stops wild grasses from growing. Once you clear the trees, direct sunlight allows aggressive weeds like spear grass to sprout fast and steal nutrients from your crops.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haaa koo mli jwɛi akwɛ̃. Kɛji okɛ tso lɛ shwie shi lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa jwɛi ni wa, tamɔ spear grass lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and grow thin and tall when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs full, direct sunlight to make its food. Under heavy tree shade, the maize stretches high to reach the light, making it weak, thin, and yellow from lack of energy.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ehoo. Yɛ tsei ni tsii lɛ ashishi lɛ, Abɛi shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni eshɛ la lɛ he, ni no haa egbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in a field with no trees or shade at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei loo hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or shade trees to keep them cool and moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall branches and leaves but producing tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much leafy plant food or gets too much water without good drainage, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei niyenii ni yɔɔ baai babaoo loo nu babaoo ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves drop off and the roots turn soft when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the soil for too long, the roots rot from lack of air, causing the plant to drop its leaves and die.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry out and wilt so quickly during the dry season when the soil is left bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsuuu he nii lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water very fast because the hot sun bakes it directly. Leaving dry leaves on top of the soil shields it from the sun and holds moisture around your crop roots much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shwieɔ shi. Otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass and tree leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil acts like an umbrella. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly in the heat, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly breaks down into free organic fertilizer.
ga: Mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni fiofio lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I mix animal manure into the soil compared to using only chemical fertilizer every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa afi lɛ he

english: Chemical fertilizer only feeds the plant for a short time, but animal manure improves the soil itself by helping it hold water, stay soft, and feed crops naturally over several seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii be kukuoo pɛ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu, ehiɔ shi blɛoo, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be babaoo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade from larger plants like plantain trees during their early years to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains adɛŋ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli koni ebu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nutrients like nitrogen in the soil to grow tall and healthy, not just water. Without good soil nutrients or proper fertilizer, heavy rain alone cannot make the crop grow strong.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ. Jeee nu pɛ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa bɛ lɛ, Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa pɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei adara waa.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from feeding properly, resulting in smaller cassava roots underground.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei aye nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do tiny insects keep eating my tomato flowers before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ dani aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Insects like thrips and caterpillars prefer tender leaves and soft flower petals because they are sweet and full of moisture. Once the flower is destroyed, the plant cannot form a tomato.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ thrips kɛ caterpillars sumɔɔ baai bibii kɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo tomato.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and go soft so fast before I take them to the market?
