ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally release a gas that makes them ripen. Heat and direct sun speed up this process, so keeping harvested plantains in a cool, shaded place slows down quick softening.
ga: Plantains jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa amɛshwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ kpo. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee mlɛo oya.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up completely before the harvest season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ egbi kwraa dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves dry up naturally when the underground tuber is fully grown, but if it happens too early, it means the plant roots are suffering from water shortage or disease underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Shi kɛji eba oya tsɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miina nu loo shikpɔŋ shishi hela.

english: Why do my pepper seeds take so many days to shoot up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ gbii babaoo dani amɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds have tough outer shells and need consistent soil moisture and warmth to sprout. If the soil surface dries out or gets packed hard, the seed struggles to break through.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ dɔlɛ daa koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfo mli.

english: How do groundnut plants produce their nuts under the dirt after flowering above the ground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: After the groundnut flower opens above ground and is fertilized, a stem called a peg grows long, bends down, and pushes itself into the soil where the groundnut pod develops safely underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni awo amɛ ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ shishifãi ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, amɛkotoɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do tiny bugs appear inside my bags of harvested maize even when the bags are tied tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii No hewɔ lɛ ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-baagi ni akpa ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akpɛtɛ kotoku lɛ he waa po

english: Weevil eggs are often laid in the grain while it is still in the field. If the maize is not dried completely before storage, the warmth inside the bag allows the eggs to hatch into bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii awoɔ ŋmaa mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does my cowpea farm have plenty of big green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli baa agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen in the soil or are planted too close together, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmeii nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need room underground to swell into large tubers. If you plant them too close, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, which leaves you with thin, small tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji odu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding compost or proper fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off during the hot season without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot, tomato plants get stressed and shed their flowers to save water. High heat also prevents pollen from working properly, so fruits cannot form.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu haa pollen ŋmeii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai efeee.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year when I keep planting the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi be mli ni miyaa nɔ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly. Rotating different crops or adding animal manure puts essential nutrients back into the earth.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ Loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to grab rainwater and soil food faster than farmed crops, allowing them to burst into growth immediately after rain.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni afee amɛ bɔ ni sa koni amɛjie nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha amɛkwɛ̃ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms. They target the tender inner leaves of young maize plants because it provides both a soft food source and a hidden place to hide from heat and predators.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms ji enɛɛmɛi. Amɛtutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli baai bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhaa niyenii ni mli jɔ kɛ he ko ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɛɛ.

english: This is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. The virus stops the leaves from making food properly, causing them to twist and pale.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies plant sap sucker lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ etsilɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the vine leaves above ground turn yellow and completely dry up. This shows that the plant has finished sending all its energy down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo beni wain tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsu ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi kɛtee eyitso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder after keeping them in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda beni akɛto ŋmɔ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow into dried maize to eat the inner core and lay eggs. Over time, their feeding hollows out the grains until only dusty husks remain.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmãa lɛ mli ni amɛwo ŋmãa. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Eniyenii ji akɛ, efoɔ dumɔwui kɛyashiɔ be mli ni sũ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ eshwɛɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or not getting enough water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the plant regain its dark green color and feed the growing corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off when the tree is stressed by hot dry weather, lacks nutrients in the soil, or is attacked by insect pests like mirids. Ensuring your cocoa farm has enough shade trees and applying proper fertilizer helps the tree hold its flowers and form pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutuaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ aná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when the soil holds too much water after heavy rains. Plant your cassava on raised mounds or ridges to help excess water drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Dumɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni eye ebua nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni eho. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die during the hot afternoon sun even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting during hot days often happens when harmful fungi or bacteria in the soil attack the roots, blocking water from reaching the leaves. Mulching around the plants and rotating where you plant peppers each season keeps the soil cool and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ, ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo otsei lɛ amli ni otsake he ni okɛ o-peppers lɛ woɔ lɛ daa be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches against strong winds. Propping the stems with sturdy wooden or bamboo poles supports the heavy weight and keeps the tree standing until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tsei ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni tsii lɛ ni eha tso lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ je shishi ekwɛ̃ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up and start sprouting when the weather gets warm and humid. Storing your yams in a well-ventilated, shady barn keeps them cool and dry, which slows down sprouting and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes wo ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛhe ajɔ ni amɛgbi. Enɛ baaha amɛshweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are small green worms eating holes inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Checking your farm regularly and applying organic sprays like neem leaf liquid or recommended biopesticides early in the morning will protect your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii leebi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to local conditions, so they quickly grab water and nutrients from the soil faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing sunlight and soil nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsɔ amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous plants have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This natural food nourishes nearby maize plants and improves the overall fertility of your land.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: The very first rainfall after a long dry spell can be misleading because the ground is still dry beneath the surface. It is best to wait until you get two or three steady rainfalls so the soil stays deep-moist for the seeds to germinate properly.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Without enough shade trees or plantain plants nearby to shield them, direct sunlight scorches their leaves and drains their moisture, causing them to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛŋkɛ ni baabu amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaajie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray treatments or work on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafɔ tsofa loo matsu nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because temperatures are cooler and wind is low. Spraying in the high heat of midday causes liquids to evaporate too fast before the plant can absorb them, and intense sun can scorch chemically treated leaves.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa shi. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ni akɛ tsofai ewo mli lɛ ashã.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings when planting them on my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa seedlings should generally be spaced 3 meters by 3 meters apart. Planting them too close together forces their roots and leaf canopies to fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients, leading to smaller harvests and high disease spread.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 3 x mitai 3. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo.

english: How long will it take after I plant my cocoa seedlings before I can harvest the first pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe beni midu mi-koko dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ dani manyɛ makpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing their first pods within 2 to 3 years of planting, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties can take between 4 to 5 years before they mature and yield fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees if they are already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ eekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ momo lɛ?

english: Pruning extra or weak branches opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and air to pass through. This prevents fungal diseases from breeding in damp leaf shade and directs the tree's energy into producing flowers and pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã baai ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. ni ekwɛɔ tsei ahewalɛ nɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why do so many tiny flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔi?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to produce thousands of flowers but only turn a small percentage into pods. Flowers drop off naturally due to incomplete insect pollination, high heat stress, or when the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to support many pods.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ cacao tso baawo fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ebaakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kooloi ni feɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ hewɔ. hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii babaoo aye abua lɛ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to suddenly turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni amɛgboi beni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark, and humid weather. It spreads quickly through rain splashes and heavy shade, turning pods black and destroying the beans inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa pod lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain on the same plot of land with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, plantains are great for providing temporary shade to young cocoa. However, deep-rooted crops like cassava should be planted further away from young cocoa stems so they do not steal vital soil nutrients and water from your cocoa roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛha kookoo tsei bibii. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ adu tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ he ko ni kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Enɛ ji koni akaju shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ okokoo shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need food or fertilizer just by looking at their leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mi-cacao tso lɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Leaves give clear warning signs: pale or yellowing leaves often mean a lack of nitrogen, purpling leaf edges suggest a lack of phosphorus, and dry, burnt leaf margins usually show the plant needs potassium.
ga: Foji lɛ haa kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ: bei pii lɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Baai lɛ ahe ni yɔɔ purple lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai ni egbi ni eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium he miihia tso lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster and stronger than my crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive roots designed to soak up rainwater and fertilizer faster than farm crops. They react immediately to rain, so clearing them early prevents them from stealing water and choking your crop's growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa ni afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛhereɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ amɛ mra. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu ni amɛha onibii akakwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if the land on my farm is naturally good for growing rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Rice grows best in flat areas, lowlands, or valley bottoms where soil has high clay content, because clay holds onto water longer than dry, sandy upland soil.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa, shikpɔŋ kplanaa, loo jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some crops like rice need swampy ground to grow well, while my maize dies if water collects around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa, he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ehe.

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes that allow oxygen to reach their roots even underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot when trapped in flooded soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ nu shishi po. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my neighbor's lowland field stay wet long after the rain stops while my hill land dries up immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo nu be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ? Beni mi gɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows down hills into low valley lands, and those lowlands usually have heavy soil that traps water, making them moist for much longer.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ amli kɛyaa jɔɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, nakai shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni haa nu hiɔ shi. Ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be babaoo.

english: How do I know if it is a good idea to try growing a new crop that other farmers in my area are starting to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛduɔ lɛ makwɛ?

english: You should check if your land has similar soil and water conditions as theirs, start by testing a small patch first, and ensure there is a market nearby to sell the harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ekome. Je shishi kɛtsɔ he bibioo ko ni oooka lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni okwɛ akɛ jara ko yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii ni okpa lɛ.

english: Why are so many farmers in my region shifting towards growing rice instead of only traditional crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋmãa nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaadu blema ŋmɔshi nibii kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Local demand for rice is high because more households buy it daily, and modern rice varieties mature quickly while giving strong harvests on suitable moist lands.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ fa babaoo ejaakɛ shia babaoo heɔ ŋmãa daa gbi. Ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni sa ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How many months does it take from the day I plant rice until I can harvest it?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ gbi ni aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa?

english: Most common rice varieties take between three to four months (about 90 to 120 days) from planting to reach full maturity for harvest.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ (aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edara kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my rice plants turn from green to bright yellow when they get closer to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: As rice grains fill with starch and mature, the plant naturally pushes its energy into the seeds, causing the stems and leaves to dry out and turn a golden yellow.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa ni edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tsei tsiɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What will happen to my rice crop if the rain stops early while the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa dani fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shɛ?

english: Rice needs plenty of water during flowering to develop seeds; if drought hits during this stage, the grains will turn out light, empty, or chaffy.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia omɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni enyɛ ewo dumɔwui. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, nɔ ko bɛ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I plant rice on the exact same piece of land where I usually grow cassava or yam?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifɔɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yam and cassava require dry, loose soil to form tubers, so regular swamp rice won't grow well there unless you use special upland rice varieties designed for drier soils.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ cassava biɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni egbɛ eshwa koni amɛfee ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji general peat rice lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. Ja okɛ ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi krɛdɛɛi ni afee aha shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsu nii.

english: Is it better to sow rice seeds directly into the soil or raise them in a small nursery bed first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Raising rice seedlings in a nursery and transplanting them gives young plants a head start against weeds and ensures a more evenly spaced field with higher yields.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ haa anyɛɔ ayeɔ jwɛi anɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni eha he ni yɔɔ lɛ afee ekome pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha yibii babaoo aba

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do caterpillars keep hiding inside the leaves at the center of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars, often Fall Armyworms, hide in the tender inner leaves (the whorl) because it offers protection from heat and predators while giving them the softest tissue to feed on.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbee shi akɛ asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli (whorls) ejaakɛ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer heat stress, lack sufficient water, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with very small roots when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eshishifãi bibii waa yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to create food; when shaded by big trees, the plant wastes its energy stretching upward for sunlight instead of growing thick tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia cassava tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii. Beni eyɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ hulu la nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ bulbs ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I put fertilizer on my farm when the soil is wet rather than when it is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in soil moisture for plant roots to drink it in; applying it to dry soil causes the fertilizer to evaporate or burn the roots under hot sun.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo sũ mli nu mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo eshã shishifãi lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings dry up and die shortly after I move them into the open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ ko ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full sun, so they need fast-growing shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu lɛ shãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo tsei ni hiɛ ka yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I plant four seeds together in one hole instead of spacing them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ amɛ baabɔ he lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for the same water and nutrients in the soil, leaving no single plant with enough food to build large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni no haaa tso ko kwraa aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmei agbo ko akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are fully grown underground without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yams indicate they are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines on top naturally yellow and dry out, showing the plant has finished storing food in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa be mli ni baai kɛ wain tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why does Striga weed keep attached to the roots of my cereal crops even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi ahe beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches underground directly to crop roots to steal food, and its tiny seeds can sleep safely in the dry soil for years until cereal crops are planted again.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛduɔ shishifãi koni eju niyenii. kɛ dumɔwui bibii Ebaanyɛ ewɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ afii babaoo kɛyashi abaadu ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves inward during peak afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping them save water and survive hot weather.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane latsaa be mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tomato ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under the full hot sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have huge, broad leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed nutrients out of the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but giving me small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eshishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or organic waste, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to build thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee tubers nɛ a mi wa nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by very small insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice, or by a plant virus transmitted by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot and smell bad inside the soil before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots for too long, especially in heavy clay soils during the rainy season. The soggy ground creates an environment where small soil fungi attack and decay the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa waa nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ko ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: This is called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree naturally drops young pods when it feels it does not have enough water, sunlight, or nutrients to feed all the pods at the same time.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu mli kɛ́ amɛnu he akɛ nu, hulu la, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ niyenii yɛ be kome mli lɛ bɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures become too high or when dry winds dry out the soil. The extreme heat stresses the plant so it cannot complete pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Maize falls over easily if the seeds were planted too shallow in the ground, preventing deep root support, or if stem-boring insects have eaten away the inside of the lower stalk.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ shɔŋŋ Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ eye tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ kwraa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until after two or three strong, consistent rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting after just the first light rain is risky because a sudden dry spell can kill the germinating seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why does making high soil mounds help my yam tubers grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Building high, soft earth mounds gives yam tubers loose soil to stretch down and expand without fighting hard, compacted ground. Mounds also prevent rainwater from pooling directly around the tuber.
ga: Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato bulbs lɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabɔle yitso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is rice bran useful for anything on my farm, or should I just throw it away?
ga: Mɛni sɛɛnamɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa tsuɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo esa akɛ mashɛrɛ ashwie?

english: Rice bran is very valuable; it can be used as nutritious feed for farm animals like pigs and poultry, or mixed into organic compost to feed your soil.
ga: Omɔ ŋmei jara wa waa. Abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli aha ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tsinai kɛ kooloi. Aloo okɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli koni ekɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: What can I do with all the crop waste left over after harvesting and milling my rice?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa ni migbeɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Instead of burning crop waste, you can collect it to make compost or char it to enrich your soil, which adds nutrients back for your next planting season.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã ŋmɔshi nibii amli jwɛi lɛ Obaanyɛ obua naa ni ofee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ afata he ekoŋŋ yɛ odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can I put fresh rice husks straight onto my soil to help my crops grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Raw rice husks take a long time to break down and can temporarily trap soil nutrients, so it is better to compost or process them before adding them to your fields.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahoo lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani efiteɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli be kukuoo ko. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo atsu he nii dani akɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start harvesting my rice field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa ŋmɔmɔ shishi?

english: You should harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the rice grains turn golden yellow, as harvesting too early or too late leads to grain loss.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa mra loo sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ afite.

english: Why does my field lose its richness and become hard after a heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔji lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kpamɔ babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting removes nutrients from the soil; returning crop leftovers like straw and bran back into the ground helps restore organic matter and keeps the soil soft.
ga: Nikpamɔ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni eshwɛ ni aduɔ tamɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni aku sɛɛ akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall in one part of my field but stay short in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi ebɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil nutrients and water holding capacity are often unequal across a field, which can be balanced by evenly distributing organic waste and soil amendments.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu ni ehiɛɔ lɛ jeee ekome yɛ hei srɔtoi. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ afee ekome kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsakemɔi ni ajaa pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants lack key nutrients like nitrogen or are getting poor water flow, which can be fixed by applying rich organic compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I turn dry farm waste into something that improves my soil fertility?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni egbi lɛ mafee nɔ ko ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo?

english: By learning proper waste-processing methods like slow-burning or composting crop chaff, you create a material that holds water and plant food in the soil.
ga: Kɛtsɔ gbɛi kpakpai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ jwɛi he nii, tamɔ shãa ni yaa nɔ blɛoo loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kasemɔ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ ofeɔ nɔ ko ni kɛ nu kɛ tsei ahe niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What is the best way to clean my field right after harvesting my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsumɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Gather the field leftovers to treat or compost them at the site rather than burning them, so you preserve the valuable organic materials for the next crop.
ga: Bua ŋmɔ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ anaa koni okɛtsa loo okɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ moŋ fe ni oooshã amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni jara wa ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ ato kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What kind of practical skills can I expect to learn if I attend a farmer training program?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋaa ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makase kɛji mikɛ mihe wo okwaafoi atsɔsemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko mli?

english: Training programs teach hands-on methods for post-harvest handling, managing field waste, improving soil health, and boosting your crop yields safely.
ga: Tsɔsemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Jwɛi ni jɛɔ omɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he nitsumɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the nutrition it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the roots underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are packed too closely together, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of tubers. Proper spacing and balanced nutrients ensure energy goes into building large roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa shishifãi wuji afeemɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and dry heat. They need shade trees to protect their leaves from sunburn and to keep moisture in the soil until their root systems grow deep enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main stem. Pruning them down to just one or two shoots allows the main plantain tree to grow faster and produce larger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli kɛyashɛ tsei 1 loo 2 pɛ he lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ ada oya ni efee kuu agbo.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the whorl?
ga: Mɛni haa buji feɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing tips of maize. Spraying early in the morning or late evening when caterpillars are active helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign of a plant virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies with insecticidal soaps or neem oil and planting resistant seeds stops the disease from taking over.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ akɛ samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ye ŋmeii yɛji anɔ, ni adu dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants blossom above ground, but the nuts grow deep under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miikwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they form long stems called pegs that bend down and push themselves into the soil. Once inside the ground, the tips swell to form the actual pods.
ga: Beni ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollen sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ feɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni eyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Naa lɛ fũuɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ ebafeɔ pod diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants before any peppers can start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Regular watering during dry spells and adding compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How does covering the dirt around my crops with dry grass stop the soil from drying out?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from direct sunlight. It acts as a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and prevents heat from baking the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa dɔlɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil healthier for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have natural bacteria on their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air into the soil. When the crop leaves decay, they release this free fertilizer into the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso baai lɛ fite Ebaajie nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crops rely on water to draw essential nutrients from the soil up into their stems and leaves. When rainfall stops, the soil dries out, leaving the plants unable to feed or cool themselves, which causes them to wither and die.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ koni amɛgbala niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ, ni no haa tsei nyɛŋ amɛye nii loo amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji shwiemɔ kɛ gbele.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting enough water from the rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy crops receiving sufficient water will have firm, upright stems and bright green leaves. If they are thirsty, their leaves will droop, curl inward, or start turning yellow, especially during the hottest part of the afternoon.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ. Kɛji kumai ye amɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baagbee shi, ni amɛbaabɔle amɛhe kɛya mli. loo ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Titri lɛ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Is rainwater better for my crops than water I collect from a well?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi fe nu ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ nu bu mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater is natural and covers the whole farm evenly, but well water works just as well to keep your crops growing healthily as long as you supply enough of it when the rains fail.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ji adebɔɔ mli nu ni ehaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shi nu kpakpa hu tsuɔ nii koni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, kɛji akɛ okɛ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ha kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: What can I do to save my farm if the rainy season ends too early?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee mra tsɔ?

english: You can use a system called irrigation, where you intentionally bring water from a nearby river, pond, or borehole to your field so your crops continue getting water until they mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii. He ni ojɛɔ otsuiŋ okɛ nu ni jɛ faa, nu bu, loo nubu ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya nɔ aná nu kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Can I direct water from a nearby stream onto my farm to help my crops grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amaje miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, taking time to divert water from a nearby stream to your field is a practice called surface irrigation, which helps ensure your crops succeed even when there is no rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, be ni ooohe ni okɛ nu ni jɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ atsake kɛya oŋmɔji amli lɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Enɛ haa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ yeɔ omanye kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Is it possible for me to grow crops during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, you can farm during the dry season if you practice irrigation, which means supplying water artificially to your crops instead of relying on rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛji akɛ okɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ okɛ nu ni akɛfee nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni okɛ ohe aaafɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers dig small trenches across their fields before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi tsaa bui bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ dani adu?

english: Farmers dig small trenches or channels to guide water from a river or tank directly to the base of their crops, making sure every plant gets enough water during dry weather.
ga: Okwaafoi tseɔ bu bibii loo ŋmeii. Koni akɛ nu ni jɛ faai loo nu ŋtayaai amli lɛ aya tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I give them too much water when watering by hand?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli fe nine beni mikɛ minine woɔ nu mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills up all the small spaces in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing. This can cause the roots to rot and turn the leaves yellow, damaging the crop.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ hei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ amu. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbó ni eha baai ŋmɔŋ aba, ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops using buckets or hose pipes?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ baagi loo hose baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu?

english: The best time to water your crops is early in the morning or late in the evening when the sun is low, so the water sinks deep into the soil instead of evaporating quickly in the heat.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my crops fail to give a good harvest even when I buy high-quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa yibii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ mihe dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Even the best seeds require a regular and steady supply of water to grow properly. If rainfall is inconsistent and there is no secondary water source like irrigation, the plants will stress and produce a poor yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ po he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be ni nu jɛɛhe ni ji enyɔ tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when floodwater stays on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu afua lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: When floodwater sits on your field, it covers the soil and blocks oxygen from reaching the plant roots. Without air, the roots cannot breathe or take up food, which causes the roots to rot and the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Kɛ nu lɛ eyi oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛye nii. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I protect my crops from drowning when the nearby river level rises high?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nu akabote mli kɛ́ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ tee hiɛ?

english: You can dig shallow drainage channels around your farm to guide excess river water away from your crops, or plant your crops on raised earth ridges so their roots stay above the water level.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛbɔle he. oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ojie nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ onibii amli. Aloo dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ashɛ nu lɛ he.

english: Which crops can survive best on farmland that frequently floods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli hei ni nu afua fɔɔ baa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Crops like rice, sugarcane, and taro (amankani) naturally thrive in very wet soil, whereas crops like cassava, maize, and pepper will quickly rot if left in standing water.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ taro (amangani) kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: What should I do to help my crops recover after floodwater recedes from my field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni maye mabua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ beni nu afua lɛ efo kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: First, clear any debris clogging your field so remaining water drains away quickly. Once the soil dries out a bit, loosen the topsoil gently and apply a light amount of fertilizer to help the plants rebuild their strength.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi ni miitsi oyale lɛ naa lɛ. Enɛ baaha nu ni eshwɛ lɛ atsɔ oya. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi fioo lɛ Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli blɛoo. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo afata he koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crops planted near riverbanks often grow faster and look healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Riverbanks naturally stay moist longer and contain rich nutrients carried down by the river. This gives crop roots easy access to water and food even when rainfall is low.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, faa lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo hoɔ yɛ faa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii oya be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo po.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has too much water in it for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: If water forms standing puddles that do not sink into the ground after a few hours, or if you squeeze a ball of earth and water freely drips out like a soaked cloth, your soil is waterlogged.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ fee nubu ko ni ekã shi ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Aloo kɛ́ omimɔ sũ kuku ko mli lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya tamɔ mama ni afɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain makes the soil very soft and muddy, which weakens its hold on the roots. When winds blow, the weak soil cannot support the weight of the tall maize plants, causing them to fall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee bɔdɔɔ kɛ muji waa. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ shi. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Is it good to water my crops with river water in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ faa mli nu baafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: No, watering under hot sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can absorb it. It is best to water early in the morning or late evening when it is cool.
ga: Dabi, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass help my crops stay fresh during dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves acts like an umbrella, shading the dirt from the direct sun so moisture stays trapped in the soil longer for the roots to drink.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ebuɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani shishifãi lɛ anu nu.

english: Can I channel water from a nearby river to grow vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsu nu kɛjɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli koni mikɛdu aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, by digging small irrigation trenches from the river to your farm, you can direct water to your fields and grow crops all year round as long as you control the water flow so it does not flood your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nu shwiemɔ nubu bibioo ko ni aaafo lɛ nɔ. Kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli kɛya oŋmɔ lɛ mli Obaanyɛ okɛ nu aya oŋmɔji lɛ amli ni odu ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji okwɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nu akaho oŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and intense heat when they are small. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block the harsh sun and hold moisture in the air until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantain loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni akɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi tsei lɛ amli kɛyashi be mli ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops like ginger and turmeric grow better under tree shade instead of open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Ginger and turmeric naturally originated as forest floor plants, so they are built to thrive in soft, indirect sunlight and cool, moist soil. Direct hot sun scorches their leaves and stops the roots underneath from growing large.
ga: Ginger kɛ turmeric jɛ adebɔɔ mli akɛ koo mli tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, ama amɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã ebaa lɛ ni ebaatsi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow from the bottom of the stalk upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food maize needs to stay green and grow fast. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore the dark green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the dirt. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping your maize grow stronger without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits around them in flat, heavy soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jatsui ni tsii yɔɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetable plants with dry bush grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops heat from drying out the ground. It retains water in the soil longer during dry days and prevents weeds from coming up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaaa egbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with green dust inside the leaf center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli ni sũ eŋɔli yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ.

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls deep inside the center leaf funnel to eat the soft new growth. Catching them early and applying approved organic or chemical sprays in the leaf funnel will protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni eda ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that feed on the leaf sap, or viruses spread by whiteflies. Controlling these tiny insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so fruit can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ko ni mikɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce large tubers only when their leaves get full exposure to sunshine. Staking holds the leaves high above the ground and away from weeds, allowing the plant to capture sunlight and feed the growing tuber underneath.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji pɛ kɛji amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ hulu la lɛ ni ehaa bulb ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely high or when soil moisture suddenly drops from wet to very dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and shade cloth during hot periods prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baa shi trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli egbi waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ mama ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantains to protect them, the sun scorches their leaves and dries out the moisture the plant needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la shãa baai lɛ ni egbiɔ nu ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark environments. Clearing weeds, pruning crowded tree branches, and letting sunlight into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. jwɛi ni afoɔ niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small pods even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ani ebaafee po?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or sap-sucking insects like mirids. Ensuring proper shade, moisture, and pest control helps the flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi amli Shade ni sa, hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the new hybrid cocoa seeds yield pods much faster than the old trees my father planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii heei ni akɛfee tsofai krokomɛi lɛ wo ŋmeii oya fe tso momo ni Ataa du lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties are specially bred by agricultural scientists to grow quickly and resist common stresses, allowing them to flower and bear fruit within two to three years instead of waiting five years.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi etsɔ hiɛ amɛkwɛ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛte shi amɛwo haomɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaamɛ afii enumɔ.

english: Why does my young maize turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛwo baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts alongside maize naturally enriches the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and trapping it in the ground, which feeds your maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmeii duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa oŋmei tsei lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan wind affect the growth of my crops?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of the air and soil very quickly, causing leaves to wilt, flowers to drop early, and crop growth to slow down as plants try to conserve water to survive.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi be mli ni tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: When cassava plants are packed too tightly, their roots fight each other for limited soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight, leading to thin plants with small tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra branches from my old cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to flow through the tree canopy. This prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to direct its energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Why do some farmers leave dead grass on top of the soil after clearing instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ beni amɛjie jwɛi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛashã lɛ?

english: Leaving cut plants as mulch acts like a blanket over the dirt. It traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the soil cool, and slowly decays into rich organic food for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ni ji niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is the price I get for my cocoa fixed ahead of time instead of changing every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atoɔ kookoo jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ momo moŋ fe ni eeetsake daa gbi lɛ?

english: Cocoa is sold on a forward-price system where prices are agreed upon in advance with foreign buyers. This protects farmers from sudden market price drops before harvest time.
ga: Akɛ cocoa hɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni akɛyaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ, ni akɛ maŋsɛɛ jarayelɔi lɛ kpɛlɛɔ jara lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Enɛ buɔ okwaafoi ahe kɛjɛɔ jara ni baa shi trukaa dani ŋmaakpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do buyers take my cocoa beans overseas instead of making chocolate right here in the village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa maŋsɛɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee tsokolate yɛ akrowa lɛ mli biɛ lɛ?

english: Making chocolate requires specialized machinery and large-scale industrial processing facilities, so most raw cocoa beans are exported to factories abroad that turn them into finished products.
ga: Tsokolate feemɔ biɔ tsɔnei pɔtɛɛi kɛ nitsumɔhei wuji ni feɔ nibii nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ ateŋ babaoo yaa maŋsɛɛ nitsumɔhei koni akɛtsu nii ni afee nibii ni agbe naa.

english: Why do my cocoa beans need to be fermented under banana leaves before I sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee cocoa ŋmeii yɛ banana baai ashishi bɔni afee ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans to kill the seed inside, removes bitter flavors, and creates the rich chocolate aroma that overseas buyers look for.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni egbe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do cocoa buyers reject my beans when they are moldy or damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ kpooɔ mi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛ́ amɛhe ewo ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛhe ewo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Moisture causes mold to grow, which spoils the flavor of the cocoa and makes it unsafe for foreign processors to turn into chocolate.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ kookoo lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ. ni ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha maŋsɛɛ nibii afeelɔi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ tsokolate

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Mature pods change color from green or red to a bright yellow or orange, and make a hollow sound when you tap them gently.
ga: Pods ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ. ni efeɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ ota he fioo

english: Why should I be careful not to scrape the bark on the main trunk when removing cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ koni mikafolɔ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ nɔ beni mijieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers and future pods grow out of special spots on the trunk called flower cushions. Damaging the bark at these spots stops new pods from growing there in the next season.
ga: Wɔsɛɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ hei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akumɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ yɛ hei nɛɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akakwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight, so taller trees provide shade and keep the air cool and moist around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do some of my small green cocoa pods shrivel up and die before growing large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ So mine lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ dani edaa lɛ.

english: This is called cherelle wilt, which happens naturally when the tree does not have enough nutrients or water to support all the pods growing at the same time.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni miida yɛ be kome mli lɛ.

english: Excessive wetness and shade allow fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread quickly across the wet surface of the pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe nibii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees give me fewer pods than when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their root systems become less active at taking up nutrients from the soil, leading to fewer flowers and lower pod production.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ heɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii fioo pɛ baa, ni pod ni afeɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Keeping large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains shields young cocoa leaves and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo baai bibii ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen is the primary nutrient crops need to produce healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny yields when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?
