english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with one another for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and grow thick stalks with bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the bare soil around their vegetable crops with dry straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔleɔ amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry straw or leaves is called mulching. It traps water in the soil on hot days, prevents dry heat from damaging roots, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. Tsi la ni mli egbi lɛ naa koni ekafite shishifãi lɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: What is causing small holes in my corn leaves and dark waste sitting inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ amaga lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It burrows inside the growing shoot of the maize plant to feed on young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Standing water in flat or heavy soil starves cassava roots of air and leads to fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily.
ga: Nu ni ekã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield if I do not clear them early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal fertilizer, groundwater, and sunlight away from your main crops during their crucial early growth stage, starving the crops before they can mature.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli yɛ amɛ mra be mli dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: It is safest to wait until the ground receives two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the earth. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and die if hot, dry weather returns.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the soil while the fruit is forming. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can crops get sick and pass diseases to each other like people do in a village?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aná hela ni amɛgbɛ hela amɛshwã amɛhe tamɔ bɔ ni mɛi ni yɔɔ akrowa ko mli lɛ baanyɛ aná lɛ?

english: Yes, plants can fall sick from tiny germs, fungi, and viruses just like humans and animals do. If an infected plant stays close to healthy ones, wind, rain splash, or insects can carry the sickness from one crop to another.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei baanyɛ aná hela kɛtsɔ muawai bibii, ŋmeii, kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anɔ, tamɔ bɔ ni adesai kɛ kooloi yeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ ajie hela lɛ kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ.

english: Why did some of my cassava roots rot in the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need to breathe air inside the soil just like animals need air to live. When soil stays flooded with water for too long, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown, suffocate, and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa kooloi koni amɛhi shi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do young plantain suckers die if I plant them immediately after cutting without letting the cut dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo amɛ ni mihaaa amɛniji lɛ agbi lɛ?

english: A fresh cut on a plant stem is like an open wound on human skin. If you place a wet cut directly into damp soil, soil germs easily enter the wound and rot the sucker from the inside before it has a chance to heal.
ga: Tso hee ko shishifã ni afoɔ lɛ tamɔ pilamɔ ni agbele yɛ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ. Kɛ okɛ pilamɔ ko ni mli efɔ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Mulai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli oya ni ehaa nɔ ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ emli dani enáa hegbɛ ni etsaa.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants sweat water into the air through their leaves when it gets hot, just like people sweat. Maize leaves curl up to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the burning sun, helping the plant save moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ latsaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ́ amɛhe edɔ. Taakɛ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ latsaa lɛ. Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ akashɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: When a plant experiences severe stress from heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, it drops its flowers to save energy. The plant chooses to preserve its own life first rather than spending strength on raising fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei na haomɔ ni naa wa kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Tsei halaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines try to climb up wooden stakes instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɔ tso ko nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb stakes to lift their leaves higher into the sunlight, where they make food to feed the tuber below. Raising the leaves off the ground also keeps them dry and safe from damp soil rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Biɛ ji he ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛyeɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do dry seeds need water and warmth to wake up and start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ he hiaa nu kɛ latsaa koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ?

english: A dry seed is like a sleeping animal resting in deep sleep. Water softens the outer shell and activates chemical signals inside, while warm soil signals to the seed that the weather is safe for it to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwu ni egbi tamɔ kooloo ni ewɔ, ewɔ. Nu haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ okadii. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ, etsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ shihilɛi yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha kwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do old cocoa trees stop producing as many pods as when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: Just like humans and animals age and lose energy over time, crop plants also grow old. As a cocoa tree ages, its internal channels for carrying water and food slow down, making it less energetic and less productive.
ga: Taakɛ adesai kɛ kooloi daa ni amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu miidara. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda Gbɛi ni yɔɔ mli ni akɛ nu kɛ niyenii yaa lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haaa amɛná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow and dying off first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant lacks enough food in the soil, it sacrifices its oldest lower leaves to feed the fresh green leaves growing at the top. The old leaves turn yellow and die so the rest of the plant can keep growing.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ekɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ shaa afɔle koni eye baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ. Baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce mostly leaves and very few pods when I give them strong fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ baai babaoo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have natural microbes on their roots that make their own nitrogen food. Giving them extra chemical fertilizer confuses the plant, making it put all its energy into growing big leaves instead of making pods.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen niyenii. Tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afutu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii.

english: Why shouldn't I spray insect chemicals on my farm if I don't see any insects on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli hu?

english: Spraying chemical insecticides when there are no pests wastes your money and exposes you and your land to harmful chemicals unnecessarily. Chemicals should only be applied when pests are actively threatening your crop to protect both your health and useful insects like bees.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ be mli ni kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ bɛ lɛ baaha ofite shika. ni ekɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni he ehiaaa lɛ woɔ bo kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai atsu nii pɛ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai miiwo oŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbeyei. Koni abu ohewalɛ kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do insects prefer attacking the soft green leaves of my cowpea plants instead of the older ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ moŋ fe baai ni edara lɛ?

english: Younger leaves are tender, full of water, and packed with soft nutrients that insects can chew easily. Older leaves are tougher and harder for insects to digest.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni kooloi baanyɛ aye mlɛo Baai ni egbɔ lɛ mli wa ni ewaa kɛha kooloi akɛ amɛaaye.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I remove all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Big trees act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Cassava leaves curl and droop to protect themselves from losing water in strong heat. It is the plant's natural way of resting and saving water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ nu toɔ he kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli hulutsoo baa.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant takes nitrogen from its older lower leaves and sends it to the top so new leaves can keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi koni baai heei lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why do my pepper plants yield smaller fruits when I plant them in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni miduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting pepper in the same soil repeatedly drains the specific nutrients pepper plants need. It also lets pepper-specific pests and soil diseases build up in that ground over time.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni pepper tsei taoɔ lɛ kpo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ pepper he lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my yam crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to suck up water and plant food instantly after rain. Yam roots take longer to settle into the soil, so weeds win the race for nutrients early on unless you clear them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛnu nu ni amɛdu niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ mra. Ja ojie kɛjɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when water is inconsistent. If the plant feels stressed by intense heat or dry soil, it sheds flowers to save its own strength.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ ejaaa. Kɛji tso lɛ miinu he akɛ edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miihao lɛ, Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take almost a year to produce fruit while my maize produces in three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani mi dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain is a large plant that needs many months to build a thick trunk and deep roots capable of holding heavy fruit bunches, while maize is a fast-growing grass designed to complete its cycle quickly.
ga: Plantains ji tsei wuji ni heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ahiɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ji jwɛi ni daa oya ni afee lɛ koni egbe esɛɛkuu lɛ naa oya.

english: Why do my pawpaw fruits ripen so fast on the tree during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pawpaw yibii lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures speed up the natural gases inside the pawpaw fruit that cause it to soften and color, making the fruit mature much faster than during cooler months.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli la ni yɔɔ pawpaw tso lɛ mli lɛ aya oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ su. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ oya kwraa fe nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the same crop on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: When you grow the exact same crop on the same plot continuously, it drains specific nutrients from the soil and attracts pests that favor that specific plant. Rotating different types of crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Beni oyaa nɔ oduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbalaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy green growth. Applying compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ kpakpa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation. It helps the plant conserve moisture until the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Should I clear all large shade trees from my land before planting my new crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu tsei heei?

english: Clearing all trees leaves young crops exposed to harsh sun and wind. Leaving some shade trees helps keep the soil moist, protects young crops like cocoa from intense heat, and prevents heavy rain from washing away the soil.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough resources to produce a strong stem and larger fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ba tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa anáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji aba.

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants with deep root systems adapted to steal water and nutrients quickly. Clearing weeds early prevents them from starving your main crops of the resources they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛfeɔ basabasa ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi otso titri lɛ naa koni nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ akaho.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Keeping the soil consistently moist and avoiding excessive chemical spraying can help fruits form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye abua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves above ground look very green and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on growing big green leaves above ground instead of expanding its storage roots below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a haa sisifãhi nɛ a to ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ wa.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more during the dry season than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, wild bushes dry up, forcing pests to move directly onto irrigated farm crops for food. Additionally, warm temperatures cause insect populations to multiply much faster.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Koo lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ mli egbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aya ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ nu awo mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii. Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why do my harvested grains rot or get infested with bugs in storage even after drying them under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fite loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bote mli yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ beni mikɛ hulu lɛ wo mli po lɛ?

english: Grains often retain hidden moisture inside the kernels even when the outside feels dry. Storing them before they are completely dry creates a warm, moist environment where mold and storage insects thrive.
ga: Dumɔwui sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ato. Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi po. Kɛ́ akɛto dani egbi kwraa lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ

english: If animals stray into my farm and eat the tops of my young cassava plants, will the plants die or can they still grow back?
ga: Kɛji kooloi Kpã kɛtee miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛye mi-cassava bibioo lɛ yiteŋ. Ani tso lɛ baagbo loo ebaanyɛ eda lolo?

english: Cassava is very resilient. As long as the stem and roots remain healthy in the soil, the plant will sprout new green leaves from the nodes on its stem, though harvesting might be delayed by a few weeks.
ga: Cassava lɛ nyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe waa. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ baanyɛ asɛɛ afo otsii fioo komɛi moŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the soil on my farm becomes very hard and packed down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil traps rainwater on top and prevents roots from breathing or spreading to absorb nitrogen. When roots cannot access nitrogen, the leaves lose their deep green color and turn yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nu yɛ nɔ. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu loo amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛŋɔ nitrogen. Beni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aná nitrogen lɛ Baai lɛ hu laajeɔ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Can I plant hedge bushes around my vegetable farm to keep livestock away, or will the bushes steal food from my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ he koni kooloi akabote mli? Aloo jwɛi lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Living fences like vetiver grass or jatropha protect your farm without harming crops. As long as you plant them a few feet away from your crops and trim them occasionally, their roots will not steal nutrients from your food crops.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni hiɛ ka tamɔ vetiver loo jatropha buɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Shii abɔ ni obaadu lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi fioo komɛi ni ofoɔ lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ. Eshishifãi lɛ juŋ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ oniyenii tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which helps them save water during intense heat. It is a natural self-defense response to prevent drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛ shwie he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu baa shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛtsi hewolo lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant many seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crowded roots and stalks fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak plants that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi ni mli eyi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ dumɔwui bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily when I leave tall weeds growing inside the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mishiɔ jwɛi kakadaji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act as safe hiding spots and breeding grounds for insects. When weeds are allowed to grow thick, pest populations multiply rapidly and easily move over to feed on your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ hei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli kɛ hei ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ. Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Pest yibɔi lɛ baagbɛ oya ni efee mlɛo koni amɛye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Excess water and cool, humid shade create the perfect condition for black pod disease to spread. The fungal spores live in the moist soil and splash onto low-hanging cocoa pods when rain drops hit the ground.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa. Fungal spores lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni amɛshwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme weather, improper watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like potassium and calcium required to convert flowers into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa mli baa lɛ he. nu ni esaaa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium kɛ calcium, ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully ripe and ready to be pulled out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnut plants signal maturity when their lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. You can test by pulling one plant; if the inside of the shells has dark veins and the seeds fill the pod tightly, they are ready.
ga: Peanut tsei tsɔɔ dalɛ kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ nii ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli obɔ lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my land before planting maize make the maize grow much greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil. This enriches the soil with free natural fertilizer that feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji legume weku lɛ mli bii, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers put paper bags or tags on the ears and flowers of maize plants in seed fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ woji kotokui loo okadii woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui aŋmɔji amli lɛ atoii kɛ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ?

english: Bags and tags are used to control pollination. They cover the female flower to prevent wind or insects from bringing pollen from unwanted plants or closely related plants, ensuring the resulting seed stays pure and strong.
ga: Akɛ baagi kɛ tags tsuɔ nii koni akɛkudɔ pollination. Ha fɔfɔi yei lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi akaŋɔ fɔfɔi ni jɛ tsei ni ataooo loo ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ahi shi akɛ hetsemɔ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my own harvest produce weaker crops when I replant them the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Replanting seeds from hybrid crops causes inbreeding, where closely related genes mix together over time. This makes the plants weaker, less uniform, and lower-yielding compared to buying fresh certified hybrid seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofafeemɔ baa. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ futuɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: If I plant sweet yellow corn right next to white corn, will the two crops mix together?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ ni ji yellow sweet corn yɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ masɛi Ani tsei enyɔ lɛ baafɔ amɛhe?

english: Yes, corn is wind-pollinated, meaning pollen from yellow corn will blow onto the silks of the white corn. This results in ears that have a mix of yellow and white kernels on the same cob.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaatswa pollen ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awo ŋmãa yɛŋ lɛ siliki lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa toi ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ eyɛŋ ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmei kome mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruit begins to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or nutrient deficiencies. The plant sheds flowers to save energy and protect itself when conditions are too harsh to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply high-nitrogen fertilizer once my tomato plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo woɔ mli beni mi-tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ?

english: High nitrogen encourages the plant to grow leafy green branches rather than flowers and fruit. Applying too much nitrogen during flowering can cause the plant to drop its blooms and lower your harvest.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo aba shi.

english: Why am I advised to pinch off the small shoots growing between the stem and main leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, consume nutrients and water that should go into fruit production. Removing them helps the plant focus energy on making larger tomatoes and improves air flow to prevent leaf diseases.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers nɛɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii kɛwo aduawai. Tomatoi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ tomatoi wuji feemɔ he nii. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akafoli helai aba.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and can burn easily. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the living shade and moisture young cocoa trees need during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing starting at the bottom leaves usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize moves available nitrogen from its older lower leaves to support new, developing foliage at the top of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ baa heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do fall armyworms hide deep inside the central funnel of my maize leaves during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-corn baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the leaf funnel (whorl) to protect themselves from intense sunlight, heat, and birds, while feeding on soft, tender young leaves where moisture remains high.
ga: Asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ amli (rings) koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa, dɔlɛ, kɛ okpoi ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to cut for planting my next farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni mafo koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old and show no signs of disease like mosaic virus. Use the firm middle section of the stem with well-formed buds for the best germination.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni ejieee hela tamɔ mosaic virus lɛ he okadi kpo lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ atsu nii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What kind of soil is best if I want to start a plantain farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi plantain ŋmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Plantains thrive best in deep, rich, well-drained loamy soil high in organic matter. They do not grow well in waterlogged soil because standing water rots their root system.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant plantains on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The ideal time to plant plantains is at the beginning of the major rainy season. This allows the young suckers to establish strong root systems with abundant natural moisture before any dry spell.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa gbekɛbii lɛ toɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni adebɔɔ mli nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain suckers when planting them in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo banana tsei lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting suckers about 3 meters by 3 meters apart gives each plant enough space to absorb soil nutrients, receive direct sunlight, and spread leaves without crowding neighbor plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii. Na hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni ogbɛ baai lɛ oshwã ni okɛ ohe wooo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli

english: Should I remove the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mihe? Nɔ ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, you should practice desuckering by leaving only 2 to 3 healthy shoots of different ages per plant. Removing extra shoots prevents them from stealing nutrients and water from the main fruit-bearing stem.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okase niji ahe nitsumɔ, ni oshi tsei bibii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ tso kome mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during heavy rain or strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and become top-heavy as fruit bunches grow. Supporting the stems with strong wooden or bamboo props helps keep the plants upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What should I do with the big purple bell hanging at the tip of the plantain bunch after the fruits appear?
ga: Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ je kpo lɛ, ani ŋmɛlɛ agbo ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ fĩɔ tso lɛ naagbee?

english: Cutting off the male flower bud a few inches below the last group of fruits allows the plant to redirect its energy into making the remaining plantain fingers bigger and fuller.
ga: Kɛ́ afo fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli inchi fioo komɛi yɛ naagbee aduawai akuu lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ kroko nɔ koni eha plantain niji ni eshwɛ lɛ afee wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up from the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and drying leaf edges usually indicate leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka or a lack of nutrients like potassium. Pruning affected leaves and applying organic manure or fertilizer helps keep the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hela tamɔ Sigatoka loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa tamɔ potassium. Baai ni ena hela lɛ ni aaafolɔ ni akɛ humus loo humus woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my new plantain shoots from insect pests living in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmeii heei ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Peeling the roots clean and dipping young plantain suckers in warm water or approved organic treatments before planting kills hidden pests like banana weevils and harmful soil worms.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ wo nu ni mli edɔ mli loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ afee lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaagbe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ banana ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my farm producing small and thin fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Small fruits happen when plants lack sufficient water or organic nutrients while developing flowers. Adding well-rotted manure and mulching around the base keeps soil moist and nutrient-rich.
ga: Yibii bibii baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: How can I tell the right time to harvest my plantains so they do not spoil before getting to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains lɛ koni amɛkafite dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the individual fingers become plump and rounded, losing their sharp edges, while still remaining dark green. Harvesting at this stage ensures a longer shelf life during transport.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji akɛ inchi fɛɛ inchi mli eyi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni haa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ laajeɔ Be mli ni eyɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lolo lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava plants rot when heavy rains flood my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like people do. When flooded water sits on the land for too long, it pushes out all the air, causing the roots to drown, rot, and die underground.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu afua lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help the crops stay green when the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Manure acts like a sponge in the soil. It holds onto rainwater during heavy downpours and slowly releases that water to plant roots long after the rain has stopped.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ejieɔ lɛ fiofio koni shishifãi akwɛ̃ be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves curl up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing moisture. By folding up, less leaf surface area is exposed to the harsh sun, helping the plant hold onto its water until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. kɛtsɔ folding up nɔ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛɛɛ baa lɛ nɔ he fioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When the heat is too strong and water is low, the tomato plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to save energy so the main plant can survive.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ faaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs during its first years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I put too many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same small amount of water and food in the soil, leaving every plant malnourished and weak.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso yeɔ niyenii ni esaaa ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Maize eats the same nutrients out of the soil every single season. If you do not change crops or add nutrients back, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed the new maize properly.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be. Kɛji otsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efo ni anyɛɛɛ aha ŋmãa hee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal fertilizer, sunlight, and soil water away from your crops before your crops can drink or eat them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani onibii lɛ baanyɛ anu loo amɛye.

english: Why is it helpful to cut off the old, yellow leaves at the bottom of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaafolɔ baai momo ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ?

english: Bottom yellow leaves no longer feed the plant and easily catch soil diseases from rain splashes. Removing them allows clean air to flow around the stem and sends energy up into growing healthy tomatoes.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua tso lɛ dɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ baa amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse lɛ bɔleɔ tso lɛ he ni ehaa hewalɛ yaa tomato ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize seeds rot inside the bag when I leave them in a humid room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli lɛ?

english: Damp air tricks stored seeds into thinking they have been planted in wet soil, so they try to wake up. When they cannot grow properly inside a closed bag, they quickly die and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ he ŋaa lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe, ni esusuɔ akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, a bɔɔ mɔde kaa a maa hwɔɔ. Beni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ kotoku ni aŋã mli lɛ Ebaagbo ni ebaafite oya.

english: How do I know how big one hectare of land actually is when planning my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni shikpɔŋ hectare kome da ha diɛŋtsɛ beni miito miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: One hectare is equal to about two and a half standard acres, or roughly the size of a full football field. Knowing your land size in hectares helps you accurately calculate seed, fertilizer, and expected crop yields.
ga: Hectare kome kɛ aaafee acre enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii, loo aaafee bɔɔlutswaa he ni eyi obɔ lɛ dalɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ da ha yɛ hectares mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ obaaná lɛ he akɔntaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do agriculture extension officers measure crop output in hectares instead of traditional acres?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ susuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ he yɛ hectares mli yɛ blema acres najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Measuring in hectares is standard practice for estimating farm yields accurately. It allows extension officers to give standard advice on how many tons or units of produce a field should produce.
ga: Hectare mli susumɔ ji nifeemɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ koni akɛbu ŋmɔ mli yibiiwoo he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ehaa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋaawoi ni sa yɛ nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ ayibɔ he. Tɔn loo unit enyiɛ esa akɛ afee?

english: How much total harvest can I expect to get from one hectare of pasture grass?
ga: Yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ maná kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi hectare kome mli lɛ falɛ enyiɛ?

english: With good management and timely gathering, one hectare of pasture grass can yield between 2.5 to 3.2 units (or tons) of harvested produce.
ga: Kɛtsɔ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa kɛ nibii ni abua naa yɛ be naa lɛ nɔ. Hectare kome ni akɛyeɔ kooloi lɛ baanyɛ aha yibii ni ji 2.5 kɛyashi 3.2 units (loo tɔn).

english: How do I determine if my harvest output for the season was good or poor?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nibii ni mikɛwoɔ be mli lɛ hi loo ehiii?

english: You calculate your total output based on the size of your land. For example, if you harvest around 2.5 to 3.2 units per hectare, your farm has met a healthy standard yield.
ga: Okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ buɔ onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ he akɔntaa. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛji okpa aaafee 2.5 kɛyashi 3.2 yɛ hectare kome mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ feɔ nibii ni kɛ shishitoo mlai kpakpai kpãa gbee.

english: Does taking proper agricultural advice really change how much crop I harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Ani okwaayeli he ŋaawoo ni sa ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baatsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, following recommended farming advice ensures you use the right field practices, which maximizes your harvest and helps you reach the standard yield expected for your acreage.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ajie yi lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaye abua bo ni okɛ nifeemɔi ni ja atsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni oná yibiiwoo babaoo ni eye ebua bo ni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni sa ni okpaa gbɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can pasture grass be grown and harvested intentionally like regular food crops?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajɛ yiŋtoo mli adu jwɛi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akpa tamɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, pasture grass can be cultivated, managed, and harvested as a valuable crop to feed livestock or produce hay, giving reliable yields per hectare when properly cared for.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ atsu prairie jwɛi lɛ ahe nii, atsu he nii ni akpa amɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni akɛhaa kooloi niyenii loo akɛbaawo jwɛi. Ehaa yibiiwoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ hectare kome mli kɛji akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to gather all the cut grass immediately after harvesting the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abua jwɛi ni afo lɛ anaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Gathering all cut grass right away prevents it from drying out too much, rotting, or blowing away, ensuring you capture your full yield of 2.5 to 3.2 units per hectare without waste.
ga: Jwɛi fɛɛ ni afo lɛ ni ooobua naa oya lɛ haaa egbi fe nine, ekafite loo efo, ni ehaa onine shɛɔ yibii ni fa fe nine ni ji 2.5 kɛyashi 3.2 nɔ yɛ hectare kome mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ni fiteɔ.

english: What happens to my total yield if I leave part of the cut grass on the ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi ni mifo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cut grass scattered in the field reduces your total harvested produce, meaning you won't achieve the maximum potential output your land can offer.
ga: Jwɛi ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onine shɛɛɛ yibii babaoo ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best way to handle my pasture grass in the field to get the highest yield?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ kooloi alɛɛhei anɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni aná yibii babaoo?

english: To get the best yield, follow extension guidelines on field management, cut the grass at full growth, and gather every bit of the produce systematically from the field.
ga: bɔni afee ni aná nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ Nyiɛmɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ kpokpaa nɔkwɛmɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛ́ ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni abua nibii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa

english: How does proper gathering of harvested crops affect the weight of my final output?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ nibii ni mibua naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa mi naagbee ŋmaa lɛ tsiimɔ he?

english: Thorough gathering ensures all produced plant matter is counted in your final weight, directly helping you reach the targeted 2.5 to 3.2 units per hectare.
ga: Nibii ni abua naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ akaneɔ tsei fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yɛ onaagbee shwiili lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo tɛ̃ɛ ni oshɛɔ otii ni okɛma ohiɛ akɛ obaaná 2.5 kɛyashi 3.2 yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ he.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the young, upper leaves to keep growing, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eha baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my rice turn brown and look burnt even when there is water standing in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ? Ni nu ni damɔ shi lolo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: This is often caused by a common fungal disease called 'rice blast' or by damaged roots that cannot drink water properly. Even if water is around the plant, a diseased stem or root stops water from reaching the upper leaves, making them dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Rice blight’ loo shishifãi ni efite waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu jogbaŋŋ Kɛji nu yɛ tso lɛ he po lɛ, ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. ni eha baai lɛ agbi

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. When tree canopies are too dense or weeds are high, moisture stays on the pods and allows the fungus to grow and destroy the crop.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Beni tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli eyi tsɔ loo jwɛi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Fɛ̃i baanyɛ ahi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni eha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if I do not harvest them quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains soak the ground for days, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the tubers and causing soil bacteria and fungi to attack and rot them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ gbii babaoo. Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi Ni enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Yam vines need to catch direct sunlight to produce energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from pests and shade, allowing the plant to make maximum food which goes down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaa gbee kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni niyenii lɛ yaa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots near the surface. When the bunch of plantains gets heavy, or if soil insects damage these shallow roots, strong winds can easily push the heavy plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi ku we nɛ e kɛ nyu ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Kɛ́ plantain tsei lɛ akuu lɛ mli tsii Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛ tsei ni tsii lɛ ahe oya.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant is stressed by irregular watering. High temperatures heat up the pollen inside the flower, preventing fertilization from taking place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ mli dɔɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa

english: Leaf curling is usually brought by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices and spreading a virus. The virus disturbs the leaf's growth, making it wrinkle and stop expanding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus tsiɔ baa lɛ adalɛ naa. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɛɛ eshwaaa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few nuts under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the soil for the pods to fill up with seeds. If the soil lacks calcium or has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow lush leaves while leaving the underground pods empty.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ dumɔwui. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo eyɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ afee efolo.

english: Cowpea roots work with friendly soil microbes to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the cowpea plant dies and decays, it releases this trapped nitrogen into the soil, which feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ naanyo lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsina tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi Ejieɔ nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food for green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed nutrients away or drowned the roots so they cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laaje loo ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie shi kɛyashɛ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛna niyenii.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow big and bushy, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the plant puts all its strength into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that provide living shade and trap soil moisture until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I grow cowpeas or beans on the land before them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mihiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the farm for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize cobs very small when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This leaves less energy for the plant to form large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ aná tso lɛ ni ekɛma ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants fold their leaves in intense heat to block the sun and slow down water loss, helping the plant stay hydrated until the cool evening.
ga: Cassava tsei kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni ekɛtsi hulu la naa ni ekɛha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i baa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water, dropping flowers to save energy and survive the stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Gbalamɔ fɔfɔi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite ni ojo haomɔ naa foi.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies spreading a disease, or by the plant trying to protect itself from extreme heat and dry air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam tubers rot when rain water sits in the mound without draining properly, creating wet dirt where fungi and bad organisms grow and attack the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ bote gɔji amli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ekɛ muji ni mli efɔ baa he ni ŋmeii kɛ nibii gbohii daa yɛ ni amɛtutuaa ŋmeii lɛ

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are ready for harvest since they grow under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the main leaves on top begin to yellow and drop off, and the inside of a test pod turns dark brown instead of white.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni baai titrii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni kaa pod lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow strong, green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients that help your maize grow better without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture in the soil to dissolve so crop roots can absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry ground can burn the plant's roots and waste your money because the crop cannot use it until rain falls.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Cassava root rot happens when the soil stays waterlogged for too long during heavy rains. The excess water stops air from reaching the roots, allowing fungal diseases in the wet soil to infect and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ fungal hela baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni ekɛ hela baa ni ekɛ tuber rot baa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in cool, overly damp conditions. If your cocoa farm has too much shade or overgrown trees, moisture stays on the pods and helps the rot spread faster.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo loo tsei eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i baakã ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ egbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips hiding under the leaves. They suck the sap out of the plant and transfer viruses that make the leaves twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛkɛ helai ni tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ yaa.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too hot or when the soil shifts suddenly from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat stresses the plant so much that it cannot successfully turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ waa aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsake fɔfɔi amɛwo yibii amli yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against drought. By curling its leaves inward, the maize plant exposes less leaf surface to the hot sun, which helps it save water and survive the heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ he tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu baa shi ni ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions in local soils. They greedily steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing them early is critical.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. It also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible to make food. Lifting the leaves off the ground also keeps them dry and prevents soil diseases from rotting the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee amɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ hu ni amɛgbiɔ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea around the base of the plants can bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This is a common sickness called Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that bite the leaves. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems from an agriculture officer is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ cassava mosaic hela. Flɔfoi yɛŋ bibii ni ŋmɔɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni nyɛɔ helai ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ duɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: How does planting groundnuts make my land better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special because their roots can trap invisible plant food from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped food stays behind to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Akpɔlɔi ji nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ tsei aniyenii ni anaaa kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: The heavy rain creates cold, wet conditions that allow a tiny fungus to grow and cause Black Pod disease. Trimming extra tree branches to let sunlight and wind reach the pods helps keep them dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii daraa ni ekɛ black pod hela baa. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni mifeee pepper ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants get stressed when the sun is too hot or when the soil gets too dry, causing them to drop their flowers to save energy. Giving them enough water regularly and a little shade during heatwaves helps the fruit form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ aha amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa, ni aha amɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai aba.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the top funnel of the corn plant. Checking your field early and spraying recommended pest remedies directly into the center funnel will stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ aŋwɛi gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Onibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni oooshwie mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plants with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, works like a protective blanket. It stops the sun from baking the soil, keeps moisture trapped near the roots longer, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why should I peel the roots and dark skin off a plantain sucker before planting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie shishifãi kɛ hewolo ni tsuɔ yɛ plantain suckers lɛ nɔ dani madu?

english: Peeling the bottom of the sucker removes hidden pests, like tiny worms and rot-causing insects, that live in the old roots. Cleaning it first ensures you carry only healthy plant tissue into your clean soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sucker lɛ shishi lɛ, ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ ni hiɔ shishifãi momoi amli lɛ. Kɛji otsu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, tso mli fãji ni hi jogbaŋŋ pɛ okɛbaawo shikpɔŋ ni he tse lɛ mli.

english: Where is the best place on my farm to store chemicals so they do not harm my family or my crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ato? Bɔni afee ni mikaye miweku lɛ loo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui.

english: Farm chemicals should always be kept in a locked, well-ventilated shed built far away from your family home and water sources. Storing them far from living areas prevents accidental poisoning, breathing in toxic fumes, and contaminating household drinking water.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ato tsũ ko ni atswa mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli, ni kɛ weku lɛ shia kɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ hei ni mɛi hiɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee nɔ ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ oshara mli. lasu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amuɔ kɛ shia nu ni anuɔ lɛ mli mujiwoo.

english: Why is it bad for me to mix farm chemicals close to my household living space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai baafutu he ni bɛŋkɛ mishia shihilɛhe lɛ?

english: Mixing chemicals near your home risks spilling toxic liquids on the ground where children and animals walk. Fumes can also drift into living spaces, so chemical mixing should always happen directly in the field away from the house.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ oshia lɛ baanyɛ aha nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ashwie shikpɔŋ ni gbekɛbii kɛ kooloi nyiɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Lasu baanyɛ atsɔ shihilɛhei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ aya nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɛ shia lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I use random sticks from the farm to stir chemical solutions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tso ni afee lɛ random ni jɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma stirrer ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii?

english: Using random sticks can cause chemical splashes onto your skin or eyes, and contaminated sticks left lying around can be picked up by children or livestock. Always use dedicated, long-handled measuring tools meant specifically for chemical preparation.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsei tsu nii trukaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai afɔ ohewolo loo ohiŋmɛii anɔ, ni gbekɛbii loo kooloi baanyɛ ajie tsei ni mli ewo muji ni ekã shi lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, kɛ susumɔ nibii ni hiɛ nine kakadaŋŋ atsu nii pɔtɛɛ kɛha tsofa he saamɔ.

english: What happens to my soil if I spill concentrated farm chemicals directly onto the ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Spilling concentrated chemicals damages the soil by killing beneficial earthworms and microorganisms that help crops grow. It can also scorch crop roots and leave long-lasting toxins in that portion of your farm.
ga: Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ ni amɛgbeɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi hu ni eshi tsofai fɔji ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nakai oŋmɔ lɛ fã lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to use chlorine in the water I use to wash my harvested vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ chlorine ni yɔɔ nu ni mikɛfɔ̃ɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, adding a small, properly measured amount of chlorine to wash water kills bacteria and fungi on the surface of harvested crops. This helps keep vegetables clean, reduces rot, and makes them safe for buyers at the market.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ chlorine fioo ko ni asusu he jogbaŋŋ fata he koni akɛjie nu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ anɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai ahe tseɔ, ehaa fitemɔ baa shi, ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mɛi ni heɔ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: How does washing my harvested crops with sanitized water help them stay fresh longer in the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni mli tse miifɔ mikpamɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua lɛ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Sanitizing wash water with approved treatment agents removes germs that cause soft rot and mold. Cleaned produce stays fresh longer during transport and commands better prices from buyers.
ga: Nu ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ nu mli lɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ helai lɛ jieɔ helai ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. Yibii ni atsuu he lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ, ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ biɔ jara kpakpa.

english: Can I use chlorine-treated water to irrigate my vegetable farm during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni chlorine yɔɔ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Low levels of chlorine in irrigation water can help prevent waterborne plant diseases without harming your crops. However, you must follow exact dosage guidelines, as too much chemical in irrigation water can burn delicate roots.
ga: Chlorine ni fa fioo yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ tsei ahelai ni jɛɔ nu mli baa lɛ anaa ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ atsu nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai babaoo ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Where should I pour out leftover chemical water after treating my crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mashɛ tsofa nu ni eshwɛ lɛ mafɔ̃ beni mitsu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii migbe naa lɛ?

english: Never dump chemical water near homes, rivers, or active crop roots. Dig a dedicated soakaway pit in an unused, fenced part of your farm so the liquid can safely filter into the deep soil without harming living plants or water supplies.
ga: Kaashi tsofa-kɛ-ŋma nu yɛ shĩai, faai, loo tsei ni hiɛ ka shishifãi ahe. Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni nu yɔɔ mli, kɛ́ ebaahi lɛ, yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fã ko ni akɛtsuuu nii ni atswa gbogbo awo he lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ shweshweeshwe ni eyeee tsei ni hiɛ ka loo nu jɛɛhei lɛ awui.

english: How should I clean my equipment after applying chemical treatments to my crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsumɔ minitsumɔ nii lɛ ahe beni mikɛ tsofai etsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rinse your spraying equipment and containers three times with clean water out in the field. Pour the rinse water back onto the treated field area rather than washing tools near family water wells or household compounds.
ga: Okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ shii etɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ. Okɛ nu ni akɛjieɔ nu lɛ aku sɛɛ awo helatsamɔhe lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ fɔ ní tsumi ní ɔmɛ a he nɛ e kɛ weku nubu ɔ aloo we ɔ tsu ɔ he.

english: How far away from my home should I keep chemical treatment activities to protect my family?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee mi tsofafeemɔ nitsumɔi lɛ kɛyashi tɛŋŋ koni mabu miweku lɛ he?

english: Keep all chemical preparation, storage, and disposal activities at least 30 meters away from homesteads and animal pens to ensure toxic fumes and runoff do not reach your family.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ha tsofafeemɔ he saamɔ, nitoo kɛ shwiemɔ nitsumɔi fɛɛ afee mitai 30 kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tsũi kɛ kooloi atsuji amli koni lasu ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ akashɛ oweku lɛ he.

english: If my pepper plants get a disease, will the plants cure themselves or will the sickness stay in my farm permanently?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ Ani tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baatsa loo hela lɛ baahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa?

english: Some short-term crop sicknesses clear up on their own when the weather changes, but long-term viral or fungal diseases stay inside the plant or soil permanently and require you to completely remove infected plants to protect the rest of your farm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ ahe helai ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ baaho amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ. Shi helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa. Ni esa akɛ ojie tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni obu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees slowly produce fewer pods each year even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miida fiofio lɛ? Ha pods fioo daa afi kɛji mikɛ fɔ wo mli po.
