english: Your cocoa trees may have a long-term viral infection like Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease, which slowly destroys the plant's internal tubes over time so nutrients can no longer reach the branches.
ga: Ekolɛ o-cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ hela ko ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, tamɔ cocoa bloat, ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. Niyenii mli nibii nyɛŋ ashɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ahe dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly dry up and die within just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: This fast death is usually caused by an acute bacterial wilt infection that rapidly multiplies and blocks water flow inside the stem, causing the plant to collapse quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni haa mɔ gboɔ oya nɛɛ baa. ni haa amɛyibɔ ​​yaa hiɛ ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ oya yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun, so fast-growing plantains use their large leaves as living umbrellas to give young cocoa the shade and moisture needed to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni shwereɔ oya lɛ kɛ baai wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo koni amɛha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Cassava leaves curl and turn yellow when infected by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and stops the plant from growing healthy leaves and tubers.
ga: Kasava baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ emɔ lɛ. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ni ehaa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daalɛ kpaa.

english: Why do the young leaves of my maize plants look like they were shredded by insects overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii efolɔ amɛmli lɛ? Gbi kome?

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants during the day and chew through the rolled leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall caterpillars lɛ teɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni okɛ baai ni abɔle lɛ atsu nii dani ojie lɛ kpo.

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to local soil conditions, allowing them to aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil food before your crops can use them.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even when rain falls well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Farming the same land continuously drains essential plant food from the soil over time, creating a long-term nutrient loss that rain alone cannot fix without adding manure or fertilizer.
ga: Okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. ni nugbɔ pɛ nyɛŋ atsu he nii kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he.

english: Can my maize plants recover if they wilt during a short week without rain?
ga: Ani mi-abele tsei lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji amɛgboi yɛ otsi kuku mli? He ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, if the water stress is short-term, maize plants will bounce back once rain falls, but long periods of drought cause permanent damage to plant tissue.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ nu he haomɔ lɛ ji be kukuoo pɛ. Abɛi tsei lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Shi hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ahe fãji fiteɔ daa.

english: Why do my stored seed yams rot before the next planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miifite dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Rot-causing fungi enter seed yams through small cuts made during harvest, and storing them in warm, unventilated conditions allows the infection to spread rapidly through the tuber.
ga: Fuŋ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ boteɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛtsɔ amɛ ni efoɔ mli bibii bibii lɛ nɔ. yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Ni kɛ́ aha edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛtsɔ yitso lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Heavy rainfall can also wash these nutrients deep into the soil where the plant roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: If I add a lot of extra fertilizer to my plantain suckers, will they produce fruit faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ Ani amɛbaawo yibii oya?

english: No, using too much chemical fertilizer can burn the roots and kill the plant. Excess fertilizer causes the plant to grow too many soft leaves without strengthening the stem, making it weak against wind and diseases.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ baai bibii babaoo ni ewaaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ helai nyɛɔ wɔyeɔ oya.

english: Why is my cassava taking over a year to harvest when my neighbor harvested theirs in eight months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani akpaa lɛ? Be ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kpaa yɛ nyɔji kpaanyɔ mli lɛ?

english: Different varieties of cassava mature at different speeds. Improved high-yielding varieties are bred to mature early in 6 to 9 months, while older traditional varieties naturally take 12 to 18 months to fully form large roots.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Hoɔ oyaiyeli srɔtoi Afɔɔ henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya tamɔ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9, yɛ be mli ni kusum henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi wuji kwraa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extreme heat, lack of water in the soil, or damage from tiny pests like thrips that feed inside the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nibii bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ fitemɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot afternoons as a self-defense reaction to reduce surface area and conserve water. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is simply protecting itself from heat.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ latsaa lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and shrivel on my trees while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, humid, and overly shady conditions. It spreads quickly during heavy rainy seasons when air cannot circulate freely through the cocoa branches.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ tsɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ kookoo niji amli kɛho oya lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin above ground while producing small, poor-quality tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ehiii kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Does burning my plot of land before planting damage the soil for my crops?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛshãa dani miduɔ nii lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yes, high heat from burning destroys organic matter and kills helpful earthworms and microbes that keep soil healthy. While ash provides a temporary nutrient boost, the soil becomes weak and dries out much faster over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa ni jɛɔ shãa mli lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbi oya yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ edu lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to thrive in poor soil and dry conditions. They are aggressive feeders that absorb fertilizer and water much quicker than cultivated crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ni mli wa waa ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: What causes small round holes in the leaves of my young cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa?

english: Tiny holes in cabbage leaves are made by insects such as caterpillars or diamondback moth larvae feeding on tender foliage. They often hide under the leaves or inside the cabbage head during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo diamondback moth larvae ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛfɔɔ amɛhiɛ amɛtee yɛ baai ashishi loo yɛ kaabe yitsei amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin with tiny ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of developing thick stems and large corn ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ ngma tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ ngma a bumi nguahi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start carrying big bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots like woody trees. As the heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs a wooden prop stick for support against the wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwereɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ tsei afi sɛɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant groundnuts or beans on the land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the land for the next crop like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ abele.

english: Why do my yam plants produce huge leafy vines but very small yams underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei wuji ni baai yɔɔ mli shi sweet potato bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving yams too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on growing top leaves and vines instead of sending energy down to build big underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ wain tsei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miifee ŋmɔŋ ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are strong competitors that steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, starving the crops and stunting their growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni he wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight in hot weather dries out their soft leaves faster than their young roots can soak up water from the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ haa baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon even if the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can pull it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli latsaa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil quickly in the soil when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. Excess water fills up air spaces in the ground, causing the roots to drown, stop breathing, and rot quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛkpaa mumɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why does my maize plant produce yellow powder from the top before the corn ears form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miifee powda ni ji yellow kɛmiijɛ ŋwɛi dani abele toi lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: The top part (tassel) produces pollen powder that must drop down onto the sticky threads (silk) of the ear below for seeds to fertilize and form corn grains.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ (tassel) lɛ feɔ pollen powder ni esa akɛ ashwie toi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli kpãa ni shwieɔ shi (silk) lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of leaves or spreading a plant virus that distorts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo tso mli helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ dalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil is waterlogged, which prevents roots from breathing and absorbing nitrogen nutrients. Creating simple drainage channels in your field helps water flow away so the plants can absorb nutrients again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ooofee Yɛ otsu lɛ mli lɛ, enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to plant my cassava so the tubers grow big?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei koni aná ŋmeii wuji?

english: Planting cassava at the start of the main rainy season allows the stem cuttings to develop strong roots and leaves early, giving them enough energy to build large, starch-rich tubers later in the season.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ aná shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa oya. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi ni starch eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall with lots of leaves but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo shi amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes tomato plants to spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Switching to fertilizers rich in potassium and phosphorus encourages plenty of fruits to form.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai babaoo aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that shields the cocoa from severe heat and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What makes my pepper plants drop their flowers before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, dry soil, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Mulching the soil to hold moisture and using simple organic sprays like neem water helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Mulching koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite kɛ organic spray ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ neem nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem varieties stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do worms attack my maize plants right inside the middle of the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitutua mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which feed on tender central leaves. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended natural bio-pesticides or neem liquid into the central funnels kills the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my field yield smaller yam tubers every time I replant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams take a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Planting yams repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil, so rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas restores fertility naturally.
ga: Sweet potatoes jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it harmful to burn the weeds on my farm before I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ aaashã jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu dumɔwui?

english: Burning damages the topsoil by destroying good organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops. Clearing weeds manually or letting them decompose back into the soil creates rich natural manure.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ niji jieɔ jwɛi lɛ loo ahaa amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa baa.

english: Plantain suckers need proper root preparation, organic manure, and clear space around them to thrive. Clearing competing weeds and removing excess side-shoots directs all the soil nutrients into fast fruit production.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia shishifãi ahe saamɔ kpakpa, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko ni ebɔle amɛhe. kɛha dalɛ Jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yeɔ ehe koni ewo yibii oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the primary food crops need for green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei taoɔ kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with no taller trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that scorch easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them creates a living umbrella that protects the cocoa while it gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛfata tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if heavy rains leave water sitting on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When land stays soaked with water, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why do the leaves on my corn plants have tiny ragged holes in them when they are only a few weeks old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baai amli beni ŋmãa tsei eye otsii fioo pɛ?

english: Tiny ragged holes on young corn leaves are usually caused by early-stage caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that feed inside the plant funnel before the leaf unrolls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mra be mli, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli dani baai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce better maize after I have grown cowpeas or groundnuts on it the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni midu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly microbes on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants yield very small tubers if I leave the vines to crawl on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs bibii waa kɛji mishi wain tso lɛ koni efo shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ staking baawo lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for building big tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the light so the plant can make more energy to swell its underground roots.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Nɔ ni fata staking he ji baai lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛyashɛɔ la lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ afee hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛha eshishi shishi shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without producing any fruits during very hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages their pollen, causing the plant to drop its flowers as a survival mechanism rather than setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin, tall, and fall over easily when I plant too many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo, amɛlɛ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya lɛ? Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil food. This competition forces them to stretch up weak and thin instead of building strong stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛaama tsei ni wa.

english: Curled and wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that feed on the soft leaf undersides and spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary to weed my farm early while my crop seedlings are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mra lɛ? Be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crop seedlings and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your young crops have a chance to grow strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Dani odumɔwui lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ,

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and fall off when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: The dry, dusty Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of plant leaves faster than roots can absorb water from the dry soil. Plants shed their leaves to conserve water and prevent total dehydration during this dry period.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛtsi nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ naa yɛ nɛkɛ hɔmɔ bei nɛɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crop seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until rains become steady for at least two weeks rather than planting right after the very first rain shower, because an unexpected dry spell right after early germination can destroy young seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ shi kɛ hoo lɛ otsii enyɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, hɔmɔ be ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ mra lɛ baanyɛ akpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster during the rainy season compared to the rest of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli kɛ akɛto afi lɛ mli bei krokomɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Rainwater carries natural atmospheric nitrogen into the ground, and the steady soil moisture combined with warm sunshine allows roots to absorb nutrients rapidly, driving fast stem and leaf growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ashishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ daraa oya.

english: What simple step can I take to stop the soil around my crops from drying out quickly in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii bibii komɛi ni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ akakwɛ̃? Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: You can place dry leaves, grass, or crop residue around the base of your plants (mulching). This shades the soil from direct sunlight, traps soil moisture, and keeps the root area cooler.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (mulch). Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe jɔɔ

english: Why do my crops suffer from root rot and leaf diseases when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ baa hela yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil starves roots of oxygen, making plants weak, while persistent moisture on leaves creates perfect conditions for fungi and bacteria to multiply and infect the crop.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. gbɔjɔmɔ tso lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛye tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I put dry fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry and no rain is expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni akpaaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers require moisture to dissolve so roots can absorb them. Applying dry fertilizer to bone-dry soil can concentrate salts around roots and scorch or burn the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo sũ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmei abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshã loo eshã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains turn moldy and spoil quickly if I harvest them during a rainy week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa yɛ otsi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops harvested in high humidity retain too much wetness inside the seed. High moisture encourages mold growth and attracts storage pests, so crops must be properly dried in the sun before storing.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo be babaoo ahi dumɔwu lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo haa ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ yaa hiɛ ni egbalaa kooloi ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto.

english: Which types of crops are better able to survive long dry periods without dying?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli ni amɛgbooo?

english: Deep-rooted or drought-tolerant crops like cassava, cowpeas, and millet are naturally equipped to survive low rainfall because their root systems reach deep water sources or their leaves limit water loss.
ga: Nibii ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. loo ebaai lɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does heavy rainfall hurt the quality of the soil on my farm?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the fertile top layer of soil (soil erosion) and wash soluble plant nutrients deep down into the ground past the reach of shallow roots (leaching).
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni baa nii lɛ kɛyaa. (shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi) ni ekɛ tso mli niyenii ni haa nu shwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ (leaching).

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow when there is a long dry spell during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plants need soil water to transport nutrients from the earth into their leaves. During dry spells, water movement stops, leaving plants nutrient-starved and causing leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Tsei hia nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya baai lɛ amli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nu lɛ nyiɛmɔ baakpa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naaa niyenii kpakpai ni eha baai lɛ eŋɔli su lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How can I tell if my plant is sick from a disease or just thirsty?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ mitso lɛ loo kumai miiye lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: A thirsty plant usually droops during the hot afternoon and recovers after watering. A diseased plant often shows unusual yellow spots, dark patches, or twisted leaves that do not fix themselves even when the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe feɔ shoo kɛ́ awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejaaa, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni tsuɔ, loo baai ni etsake ni nyɛɛɛ asaa amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: What causes my maize leaves to get dark spots and dry up early?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ oya?

english: These spots are usually caused by microscopic germs like fungi that live on the leaves and feed on the plant. Removing infected crop leaves and planting resistant varieties helps keep your field healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai bibii tamɔ ŋmei ni hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ helai nɛɛ baa. Tso lɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ hela lɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔji lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some plants die completely from a disease while others on my farm survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai gbeɔ tsei komɛi kwraa lɛ? Be mli ni tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo lɛ?

english: Just like people, some plant varieties are naturally stronger and can fight off disease germs, while weaker plants easily get overpowered and destroyed by the infection.
ga: tamɔ gbɔmɛi Tsei komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwu amɛshi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ amɛnɔ oya ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: How do tiny disease germs get inside my crops in the first place?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni helatsɛmɛi bibii boteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ shishijee mli?

english: Germs can enter plants through tiny natural openings on the leaves, through damage made by insects or cutlasses, or directly through the roots from infected soil.
ga: Helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii bibii amli abote tsei amli. adebɔɔ mli yɛ baai lɛ anɔ Etsɔɔ nɔ ni kooloi loo dadei kɛbaa lɛ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela lɛ emɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why do some of my seeds die in the soil before they even grow into seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa po ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Harmful germs living in damp soil can attack seeds as soon as you plant them, causing them to rot underground before they can sprout above the ground.
ga: Helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua dumɔwui kɛji odu amɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot from the inside even when the outside looks healthy at first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Certain bacteria enter the tomato through the flower or stem early on and multiply inside the fruit, causing the inside to decay even before the outside skin turns bad.
ga: Muawai komɛi boteɔ tomato mli kɛtsɔɔ fɔfɔi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ mra. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa aduawai lɛ amli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, emli lɛ fiteɔ dani kponɔgbɛ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Can a crop disease stay in my soil and attack the next crop I plant?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, many plant germs survive in the soil or in old crop remains for a long time. Changing the type of crop you plant in that spot next season helps starve the germs.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli helai babaoo baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ nakai he lɛ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hɔmɔ aye helatsɛ lɛ.

english: Can crop diseases spread from one plant to another through irrigation water?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, water flowing across your farm can carry disease germs from sick plants directly to healthy ones, spreading the infection across the whole field.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni jɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ

english: Is it safe for my farm animals to drink water flowing out of a field with sick crops?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ni tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: No, water coming from fields with decaying, diseased crops or chemical sprays can carry germs and toxins that make goats, cows, or chickens sick if they drink it.
ga: Dabi, nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji amli ni tsei ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai kɛ tsofai fɔji ni baanyɛ aha tooi, tsinai, loo kooloi hela amɔ amɛ kɛji amɛnu lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow, crumpled leaves are a common symptom of cassava mosaic disease, which is caused by a virus carried by small insects called whiteflies that feed on the plant's sap.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ cassava mosaic hela he. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei nu lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. They need temporary shade from larger plants like plantains to protect their tender leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil or that too much water is sitting around their roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ebɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa anyɛ aha amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil lacks water, or when the plant is missing essential soil nutrients needed to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni tsei bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What is making small ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in corn leaves are often caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center funnel of the plant to feed on new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni boteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the dirt during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water logging in the soil starves roots of air and allows harmful fungi to attack and rot the cassava tubers before they can be harvested.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛtutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger yield at harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛ́ akpa?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small, weak harvests.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa bibioo ko.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly steals the same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests and diseases that like that specific crop to build up in the field.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni tamɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist after a light rain so the roots can absorb it, and never during heavy downpours that wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛyashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaho.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly even after I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, effectively starving your farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did the seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were stored in hot or damp conditions, which damages their internal life or encourages mold and insects to destroy them.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ wala ni yɔɔ mli lɛ loo ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii hewalɛ koni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which it needs to stay green and produce healthy, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni esa akɛ ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mli wa

english: What will happen to my maize if I plant many seeds very close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo? Dumɔwui bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ he kome

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, weak stems with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui bibii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does my maize plant grow flowers at the very top before the cobs show up on the side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi dani ŋmeii jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: The flower at the top is called a tassel, and it produces pollen that must fall onto the soft hair silks of the lower cobs to form actual corn kernels.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ akɛ tassel. ni ekɛ pollen ni esa akɛ egbee shishigbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ lɛ aba koni efee ŋmei ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high, when they lack water, or when bees are not visiting to help pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, kɛ́ nu faaa, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii bɛ ni baaye abua ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap underneath the leaves or spreading a plant virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ loo helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow so many green leaves but very few pods when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ hiɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive moisture and rich nutrients during heavy rains encourage cowpeas to spend energy growing leaves and stems rather than producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cowpea ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their yellow flowers down into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts develop their pods underground, so after the flower is fertilized above ground, the plant grows a long stem called a peg that pushes into the soil to grow the peanut.
ga: Peanuts feɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii akwɛ̃.

english: Staking yams lifts the leaves high into the sunlight so the plant can make more food, which leads to larger underground tubers.
ga: O-sweet potato lɛ ni okɛwoɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to be harvested underground without digging them up first?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi ni okɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and split into strips during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baa lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ fiber yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves that lose moisture quickly in heat, so the leaves shred and brown to protect the main trunk from drying out.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ, ni kɛ́ edɔ amɛ lɛ, amɛmli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, atseɔ baai lɛ amli koni amɛkagbi tso titri lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and retain soil moisture while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer, feeding the nitrogen-hungry maize plant and keeping the soil healthy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ nitrogen lɛ niyenii. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant moves available nitrogen from older lower leaves to newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei jieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of flowers and fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the stem during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, heavy shade. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and airflow helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo, shade ni mli wa mli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni hulu la kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and uneven watering causing environmental stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaaa ni kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ baa lɛ mli

english: Is it better for my crops if I clear my farm land without burning the weeds?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni mishãaa jwɛi lɛ?

english: Clearing without burning allows cut vegetation to rot into organic mulch. This mulch feeds the soil, keeps it cool, and preserves moisture for your crops during hot dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa tsei ni afo lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ onibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my ginger roots rot underground when the rains become heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Ginger roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Planting ginger on raised soil ridges helps rainwater flow off and keeps oxygen around the roots.
ga: Ginger shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Ginger ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves drop off naturally and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi bɔi fãmɔ.

english: How do I stop insects from destroying my harvested maize grain in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Weevils attack grain that contains moisture. You must dry your maize thoroughly in the sun until it is hard before storing it in sealed, airtight bags or storage bins.
ga: Moŋ lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo kotoku loo ŋmãa ni atsĩ naa mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can I use decomposed cassava peels and chicken manure to feed my crops instead of store-bought chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei ni egbo kɛ tsina ŋmei aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Yes, well-rotted compost feeds the soil naturally, helps it hold water longer, and releases steady food to your crops over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni ojie niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plants without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the midday sun gets too hot or when soil water drops suddenly, causing stress that stops the fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ shwane mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbee shi trukaa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa aduawai kpaa feemɔ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even after staying in the farm for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ tsei eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nɔ ni fe afi ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell if the soil is packed too tightly for the roots to expand or if the ground lacks potassium, which helps store food underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekpɛ tsɔ kɛyashɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and skinny with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, leaving none of them with enough strength to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwu ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and shriveling up right on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions when trees are not pruned to let air move through.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ni akpaaa tsei lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up into tight balls during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to protect themselves from losing water in high heat, but it can also mean tiny insects called thrips or mites are sucking the juice from the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Shi ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ kooloi bibii hu. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ thrips loo mites lɛ miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds from around my crop roots when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi tso lɛ shishifãi He ni tso lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal most of the water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil before your main crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers under the ground when I give them tall wooden sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni mikɛ tsei kakadaji haa amɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to create food, and lifting them off the damp ground protects them from leaves rotting and diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe koni akɛfee niyenii. Ni kɛ́ owó nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ahe.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plantain stems with dry grass keep the ground wet for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: A layer of dry grass acts like an umbrella over the soil, blocking the harsh sun from evaporating moisture and keeping the crop roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Why do some groundnut farmers hold onto their harvest and sell it bit by bit instead of selling everything immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii okwaafoi komɛi kpaa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ fãi bibii amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahɔ̃ɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Holding onto your harvested groundnuts and selling them gradually allows you to avoid low harvest-season prices and sell when market demand is higher, giving you a steady income and better profits throughout the year.
ga: Ni oootsu ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ he nii blɛoo Nihɔɔmɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa be mli jara ni baa shi lɛ he. ni ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni jara nɔ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa babaoo Enɛ haa onáa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my groundnuts are fully dried and ready to be stored for a long time without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ mahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee?

english: Groundnuts are fully dry when the pods crack easily under thumb pressure, the inner seeds rattle inside the shell when shaken, and the moisture level is low enough to prevent mold and rotting.
ga: Peanuts lɛ egbi kwraa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ oshishifa lɛ fã mlɛo. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hosoɔ yɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli kɛji akpokpo. kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi bɔ ni sa ni baatsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce yellow flowers above the ground, but the actual nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have a unique behavior called pegging; after flowers are pollinated above ground, tiny stalks called pegs grow down into the soil to safely form and ripen the groundnut pods underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ subaŋ krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pinning. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my groundnut plants turn yellow and produce small nuts when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When groundnuts are crowded, their leaves compete for sunlight and their roots fight for nutrients, which prevents the pegs from pushing easily into the soil to form full, healthy nuts.
ga: Beni ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo koni ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Can I save some of the groundnuts I harvest this season to plant as seeds for the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmeii ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ato koni mikɛdu akɛ dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, you can keep some of your harvested groundnuts as seed for next season, provided you select healthy, mature pods, dry them thoroughly, and store them intact in their shells in a cool, pest-free place.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Esa akɛ ohala pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara jogbaŋŋ. Hang koni egbi jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛto ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ.

english: How does growing groundnuts in my field help make the soil better for other crops like maize?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil with free fertilizer for the next crop planted in that field.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my groundnuts are mature enough to be pulled out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves begin to yellow and drop off, and the inside lining of the shell turns from white to a dark brown or blackish color when you crack open a pod.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eyɛŋ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ mli kɛ́ ogbele ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my groundnuts and leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii akpamɔ sɛɛ tsɛ ni mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If you leave groundnuts in the soil past their maturity, the stems holding the pods weaken and snap, leaving many nuts buried in the ground where they can sprout or rot.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛdara kwraa lɛ, Tso ni hiɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni efoɔ. Enɛ haa afuɔ ŋmeii babaoo awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi yɛ lɛ.

english: What causes my stored groundnuts to turn dusty and get small holes in them after a few months?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ sũ kɛ bu bibii? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: That damage is caused by storage insects like weevils and beetles; keeping groundnuts dry, storing them in airtight bags, or using approved grain protectants will stop insect attacks.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji kooloi ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. ŋmeii ni egbi Okɛwo vacuum kotoku mli. loo okɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ebaakpa kooloi bibii lɛ atuatsemɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my stored groundnuts develop a bitter taste or moldy smell that buyers complain about?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ wieɔ amɛshiɔ lɛ?

english: This happens when groundnuts are stored while still damp, causing mold to grow and produce dangerous poisons called aflatoxins, which make the nuts unsafe to consume or sell.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii to be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxins lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii loo jarayeli.

english: Why does my harvested maize smell bad and develop a white powdery dust when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ sũ yɛŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Storing maize before it is completely dry allows tiny fungi or mold to grow inside the bag. These fungi produce a bad smell and toxins called aflatoxins, which can make people and animals sick if they eat the spoiled grain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa bibii aba. Ebaanyɛ eda yɛ kotoku lɛ mli Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ jieɔ ŋmeii fɔji kɛ tsofa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin. Enɛ baanyɛ aha gbɔmɛi kɛ kooloi aná hela kɛji amɛye dumɔwui ni efite.

english: What causes the white powdery coating on my pepper leaves, and why are they drying up?
ga: Mɛni Kɛ Powder Eyɛŋ ni Akɛwoɔ Mi Pepper Baai lɛ Anɔ lɛ Baa? Ni mɛni hewɔ egbi lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. The fungus grows on the surface of the leaf and steals nutrients from the plant, causing the leaves to dry out, curl up, and fall off prematurely.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Fuŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛkpãa shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and smell rotten while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet weather and heavy shade. The fungus enters the pod, rots the husk and beans, and gives off a bad odor as the pod decays.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Fuji lɛ boteɔ pod lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋhosomɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi Ni ŋmeii gbohii ko baa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ egbo.

english: How can I stop my tomato seeds from rotting in the soil before they grow into seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tomato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui?

english: Seeds rot in the soil due to fungal damp-off, which happens when the soil stays too wet and lacks good airflow. Planting seeds in well-drained soil and avoiding overwatering keeps the fungus from destroying young seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akafite dumɔwui bibii lɛ.

english: Why do I see a thick white foam on the stems of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That foam is produced by young spittlebug insects to protect themselves from the sun while they suck sap from your plant. Sucking the sap weakens the plant and slows down the growth of the cassava roots underneath.
ga: Ladybugs bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ foam lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he beni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ. Nu ni anuɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa oya.

english: Why are there tiny bite marks and holes on my cabbage leaves as if something is scratching them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ he okadi bibii kɛ bu, tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko efo amɛhe lɛ?

english: Insects like caterpillars or beetles visit your field at night to feed on soft leaf tissue. These leaf-chewing pests reduce the plant's ability to catch sunlight and make food for itself.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii baasara he ni oyɔɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ baai nɛɛ baa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii lɛ shi.

english: Why are my plantain leaves covered in a sticky liquid and black dust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni shãa kɛ sũ diŋ ehà mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like mealybugs suck sap from the leaves and leave behind a sticky liquid called honeydew. A black fungus then grows on top of this liquid, which blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mealybugs lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛshiɔ nu ko ni mli tse ni atsɛɔ lɛ honeydew yɛ amɛsɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ diŋ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu nɛɛ nɔ. ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe

english: Why do my okra leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon sun even when the soil is slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops lose water rapidly through their leaves in strong heat, so they droop to reduce sun exposure and save moisture. If the leaves recover by morning, it is a normal protective behavior, but if they stay wilted, root rot or pests may be damaging the roots.
ga: Tsei laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu hulutsoo be lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ he wa lɛ leebi lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji hebuu subaŋ ni sa. Shi kɛji egbo lolo lɛ Shishifãi ni egbo loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ.

english: When a maize plant lacks nitrogen food in the soil, it moves stored nutrients from its old bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die off early.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why are the roots of my yam plants soft, wet, and bad-smelling when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe efɔ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Soft, smelly roots are caused by root rot fungi, which attack yams when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Without air in the soil, the roots drown and decay.
ga: Shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa lɛ jɛɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni tutuaa sweet potatoes kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni enyɛɛɛ efo kɛya lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: If I want to expand my farm to plant more acres of crops next season, how do I know if my soil is rich enough?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni magbɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nii babaoo?

english: Rich soil usually has a dark color, feels crumbly, holds moisture well without becoming swampy, and contains earthworms. An extension officer can test a sample of your soil to tell you exactly which nutrients it needs before you clear more land for planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ mli tseɔ, enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ nubu. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔwui krokomɛi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight during their first couple of years. They need temporary shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stems when planting so they don't fight for food in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ miidu lɛ, ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ abɔ he koni amɛkaye niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava about 1 meter apart in straight rows gives each plant enough space for its roots to expand and collect water and soil nutrients without choking neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome yɛ ŋsɔɔdoi ni ja mli lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛbua nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if insects are eating my maize crop or if the plants are just suffering from lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miiye mi-ŋmãa lɛ loo kɛji nugbɔ bɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Drought makes maize leaves curl inward and wilt across the whole farm evenly. Pest damage usually shows as visible ragged holes, chewed leaf edges, or small dark droppings inside the funnel of the leaf.
ga: Hɔmɔ lɛ ha ŋmãa baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛgboi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ bu ni etse ehe. ŋmɔɔ baa lɛ naa loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli

english: Why do my crops yield heavily during the major rainy season but produce very small fruits during the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The major rainy season provides continuous soil moisture and cooler weather, allowing plants to build deep root systems and big fruits. The minor season has shorter, less predictable rains, causing plants to save energy just to survive rather than growing large crops.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji. Be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Enɛ haa tsei toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ tsei wuji.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their flowers before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil constantly moist with mulch helps protect the flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant or spread it in the soil nearby?
ga: Ani esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo akɛshwie shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and damage the plant. It is best to dig a small ring a few inches away from the stem where the feeding roots can safely drink up the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tso lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsa ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Niyenii shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops survive dry weather?
ga: Te baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) stops the sun from drying out the soil, keeps root temperatures cool, and slowly decays into natural food for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baaha Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛgbalaɔ fiofio amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops even after I spend time clearing the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ be efo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep seed reserves in the soil that can sprout with very little water. Clearing them early while your crops are still small ensures your planted crops get first access to sun, space, and water.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni dumɔwui yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛ nu fioo pɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii mra Be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ, enɛ haa otsei ni miida lɛ naa hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ nu mra.

english: Can I save seeds from the corn I harvested this year to plant next season, or should I buy fresh certified seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa afi nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: High-yielding hybrid corn seeds give a great harvest in the first year, but seeds saved from that harvest will produce weaker plants with smaller yields. Buying fresh, certified seeds each season guarantees strong crop growth.
ga: Abɛi ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baawo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni abaahere kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ aba, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii adaa waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen hunger. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, and when the soil does not have enough, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji nitrogen hɔmɔ he okadi. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure. High nitrogen makes cowpeas spend all their energy building big leaves and stems instead of flowering and setting seeds.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ dumɔwui awo mli lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into tight little balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee bɔɔlu bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. When sap is sucked out, the leaf leaves buckle and curl up tight.
