ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛji akɛ ajie mliki lɛ Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe waa.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into white powder after keeping them in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ beni akɛto ŋmɔ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That powder is caused by small insects called grain weevils. They bore inside dry maize grains to lay eggs, and their larvae eat the grain from the inside out, leaving behind dusty waste.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ powda lɛ. Amɛfoɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛkɛwo amɛwui lɛ. Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni mli ewo muji ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and shrink before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a condition called cherelle wilt or by black pod disease. The tree naturally drops pods it cannot feed due to water stress, or fungal diseases attack the young pods during wet weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel wilt loo black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa. Taakɛ eji lɛ, tso lɛ baashwie ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ aye yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ lɛ. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be baa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When the sun gets too hot, tomato pollen dries out and becomes sterile. Because the flower cannot get pollinated properly, the plant drops the bloom to save water and energy.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside when rain falls heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee blɛoo ni egbo beni nugbɔ enɛ waa gbii komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the ground for long periods, water displaces all soil air, causing the roots to drown and rot from rot-causing fungi in the mud.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni haa sũ fiteɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam tubers twist when they hit hard, compacted soil or rocks underground as they expand. Building high, loose mounds helps the tuber grow down smoothly without obstacles.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ tɛi ni wa loo shikpɔŋ shishi tɛi beni amɛmli lɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa bulb lɛ daa kɛyaa shi jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when I leave all of them attached to the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni mishiɔ amɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and plant food. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems to feed the fruit fast.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii 1 loo 2 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛye aduawai lɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit buried in the dirt for years waiting for light. Clearing the land exposes these dormant seeds to sunlight and rain, giving them a head start before crop seeds can fully establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ la. Kɛ́ ajie he lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akwɛ̃. Hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ enɛɛmɛi. Enɛ haa amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi kwraa.

english: I am planning to start a new farm, so which cocoa variety should I plant first to get the best harvest?
ga: Miito gbɛjianɔ koni maje ŋmɔ hee shishi. Mɛɛ kookoo henɔ esa akɛ madu klɛŋklɛŋ koni maná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Agricultural officers usually recommend modern hybrid cocoa varieties because they grow faster, produce higher yields early, and have better natural resistance to common cocoa diseases compared to older varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli he onukpai jieɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli lɛ he ŋaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya. Ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa oya ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ kookoo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ kɛ akɛto henɔi ni etsɛ fe tsutsu lɛ ahe.

english: Does the specific variety of cocoa I choose to plant affect how easily my farm gets sick?
ga: Ani kookoo henɔ ni mihala akɛ makwɛ lɛ baaná hela nɔ hewalɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, older cocoa varieties are much more vulnerable to diseases like the swollen shoot virus. Planting modern, certified disease-tolerant varieties gives your farm a much stronger defense against die-offs.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai tamɔ bud swelling virus lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ waa. Kɛ́ odu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni ana akɛ helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔ lɛ waa ni ekɛtsi dieback naa.

english: What is this cocoa swollen shoot disease I keep hearing about, and what does it do to cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni miyaa nɔ minuɔ he lɛ, ni te enáa kookoo tsei anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa swollen shoot is a destructive viral disease that causes swelling on stems and roots, discolors leaves, reduces pod production, and eventually kills the infected cocoa tree within a few years.
ga: Cocoa Top Swollen ji hela ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli fũuɔ, ebaa lɛ tsakeɔ, ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ cacao tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ afii fioo komɛi amli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are healthy or if they are catching a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: Healthy cocoa trees have vibrant green leaves, smooth bark, and regular pod growth. Signs of disease include strange leaf discoloration, swollen stems, dieback of branches, or sudden leaf dropping.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ, amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Hela okadii lɛ ekomɛi ji baa lɛ su tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni efuu, tsei niji ni egboi, loo baa lɛ ni elaaje trukaa.

english: Why is it so important for me to pay close attention to cocoa tree health right from the first day of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahewalɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term investment. Protecting tree health early ensures young plants survive, mature properly, and yield high harvests for decades without being ruined by preventable viral outbreaks.
ga: Cocoa ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he buu mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi. Dalɛ ni sa ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo eba afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Ni helai ni anyɛɔ atsiɔ naa lɛ ni baa lɛ ekpataaa amɛhiɛ.

english: Why did so many cocoa farms in Ghana, especially in the Eastern Region, lose their trees back in the 1930s?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji babaoo yɔɔ Ghana lɛ? Titri lɛ yɛ bokagbɛ No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ laaje yɛ 1930 afii lɛ amli?

english: In the 1930s, large areas of cocoa in the Eastern Region were wiped out because of a major outbreak of the cocoa swollen shoot virus, at a time when farmers didn't have disease-resistant varieties or knowledge on how to stop it.
ga: Yɛ afi 1930 afii lɛ amli lɛ, akpata kookoo hei wuji ni yɔɔ bokagbɛ lɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni ji bloat virus lɛ ni gbɛ eshwa babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ okwaafoi lɛ bɛ kookoo henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ loo nilee ni kɔɔ bɔ ni aaafee akpa lɛ he.

english: Why did cocoa farming move or spread to different regions in Ghana over the years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii efã loo egbɛ eshwa kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ lɛ? yɛ Ghana yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli

english: As older cocoa areas suffered heavy losses from soil exhaustion and devastating disease outbreaks like swollen shoot, farmers expanded into new regions where the soil was fresh and free of infected trees.
ga: Beni kookoo ŋmɔji ni etsɛ lɛ fiteɔ nii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli lɛ, okwaafoi miiya hei heei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ehee ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does cocoa swollen shoot disease spread from one farm or tree to another?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni cocoa bud swelling hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ loo tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ?

english: The virus is spread primarily by tiny insects called mealybugs, which feed on the sap of infected trees and then carry the virus to healthy neighboring cocoa trees.
ga: Koolooi bibii gbɛɔ helai amli. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. ni yeɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛkɛ hela lɛ yaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: If cocoa swollen shoot destroyed crops in the past, how can I prevent it from attacking my farm today?
ga: Kɛji kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi lɛ, amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enaa koni ekatutua miŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: You can protect your farm by planting approved disease-tolerant cocoa varieties, inspecting your farm regularly, and cutting out infected trees immediately to stop insects from spreading the virus.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ kookoo henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa Ni ofolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni kooloi bibii lɛ akagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã.

english: If cocoa trees on my land died from disease a long time ago, is it safe for me to plant new cocoa trees there now?
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela gbe kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ be saŋŋ ni eho lɛ, Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu kookoo tsei heei yɛ jɛmɛ bianɛ?

english: Yes, it is safe to replant as long as all old infected stumps and wild host plants are completely removed, and you plant new, disease-resistant cocoa varieties recommended by extension officers.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ekoŋŋ shweshweeshwe kɛji ajie tsei ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kwraa. Ni oduɔ kookoo henɔ hee ko ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ yɛ ŋaawoo ni extension nɔkwɛlɔ ko kɛha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize heat up and sweat when I pack it into sacks right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔɔ ni eyɛ latsaa beni mikɛwoɔ kotokui amli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize still contains moisture inside the grains. When packed immediately into sealed sacks without proper sun-drying, the grain continues to 'breathe,' trapping moisture and heat, which creates the warm environment where mold quickly grows.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni hulu lɛ eshɛɛɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ baaya nɔ ‘amɛmu’, ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii baanyɛ adara oya yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast if I leave them lying in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that continue to breathe after being harvested. Direct sunlight overheats the yam, causing it to lose water rapidly and weakening its skin, which allows rot-causing fungi to enter and break down the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli adɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehaa hewolo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantains turn soft and yellow so quickly when transported on long journeys to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛji akɛ akɛtee he ko ni jɛkɛ kɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally release a ripening gas called ethylene. Heat and rough handling during transport stress the fruit, causing it to produce even more gas and speed up its own ripening before reaching buyers.
ga: Plantains jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Dɔlɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa. Enɛ haa gas babaoo baa ni ehaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshweremɔ yaa oya dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why does damaging the skin of my sweet potatoes while digging them up cause them to spoil in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ahewolo ni mifiteɔ beni mifoɔ lɛ haa amɛfiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: The outer skin of a sweet potato acts as a natural shield against germs. Cuts and scrapes from farm tools create open wounds where soil bacteria and fungi enter, leading to decay while in storage.
ga: Sweet potato hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa. Nibii ni afolɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ haa pilamɔi ni agbele naa ni haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ebaagbo be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How do small insects like weevils manage to ruin my stored beans even when I tie the bags tightly?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii afite mi-beans ni mikɛto lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevils often lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the bean pods while the crop is still growing in the field. When you store the dry beans, those hidden eggs hatch inside the tied bag and the young insects feed on the beans from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ bean pod lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii miida lolo yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Beni obua ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ anaa lɛ Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku ko ni akɛfi lɛ mli. Ni kooloi bibii lɛ baaye ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my harvested fresh vegetables wither quickly when kept in light plastic bags instead of open baskets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa ehee lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo plastic kotokui ni mli tse mli moŋ fe ni akɛwo tsɛnsii ni agbele mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plastic bags trap the moisture and warm air that freshly picked vegetables give off. Without air circulation, this trapped heat causes the vegetables to steam, lose their crispness, and decay rapidly.
ga: Plastic kotokui lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni ajie ehee lɛ amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni hoɔ nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ la. ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ oya

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready to dig up before they go bad under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa dani amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. If left too long in the ground after reaching maturity, the roots become tough, woody, and lose their starch quality, making them spoil faster after harvesting.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa egboɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I harvest my ripe cocoa pods immediately instead of leaving them on the tree until buyers arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Overripe cocoa pods left on the tree attract diseases like black pod disease, and the seeds inside can begin to sprout naturally. Sprouted or diseased seeds ruin the quality and flavor of the cocoa beans.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa helai tamɔ black pod hela, ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fiteɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe fɛo kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do the new high-yielding tomato varieties soft and spoil faster than our old local tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato henɔi heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya fe wɔ maŋ lɛ mli tomato henɔi momo lɛ?

english: High-yielding tomato varieties are bred to produce larger, juicier fruit with high water content, which naturally gives them thinner skins. While they yield more, their thin skin makes them softer and more sensitive to handling and storage heat than local thick-skinned varieties.
ga: Akwɛ tomato henɔi srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo koni amɛwo yibii ni da ni mli ewo muji. ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli Enɛ baaha tomato lɛ hewolo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ejieɔ babaoo moŋ Shi amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hu haa amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛnuɔ he jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii ni amɛhiɛ dɔlɛ mli fe maŋbii ni yɔɔ hewolo ni mli tse lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested pepper pods turn dark and dull when I dry them in deep piles instead of spreading them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper pods ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ migbi amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Peppers need plenty of air circulation and direct heat to preserve their red color. Stacking them in thick piles traps moisture inside the heap, causing the natural red pigments to break down and turn dark due to slow rotting.
ga: Chili peppers he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli kɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhiɛ su tsuru lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to ŋtayaai ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋtayaai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ tsuru lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ duŋ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ blɛoo lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do farmers call plantains the 'bodyguards' of young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi tsɛɔ plantains akɛ ‘bulɔi’ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and easily scorched by direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that act as protective shade trees, sheltering the young cocoa until it is strong enough to survive on its own.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo, ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Can I plant maize or cassava on the same land where I just planted my plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu plantains nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop plantains with fast-growing crops like maize or vegetables during the first few months. However, as the plantain leaves grow large and block sunlight, lower crops will struggle to get enough light.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai awo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Shi, akɛni plantain baai lɛ dara ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa hewɔ lɛ, Low-end ŋmɔshi nibii baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoot to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these are young shoots with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base. They grow faster and yield bigger bunches than shoots with broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tseee, ni tamɔ lance, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli tse. Amɛ daa oya ni amɛ woɔ kui wuji fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain plants when setting up a field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi plantains lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miitsu nii?

english: Plantains should typically be spaced about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Esa akɛ plantains lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 3 x mitai 3. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: What should I do to the plantain suckers before burying them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee dumɔwui lɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: You should trim off old roots and damaged parts of the sucker base to remove hidden pests like root weevils before planting them in moist, organic-rich soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo shishifãi momo kɛ hei ni efite yɛ sucker shishi lɛ koni ojie kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ shishifãi amli ŋmeii, dani okɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How many months does a plantain stem take to bring out a bunch of fruit?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ ni plantain tso ko woɔ yibii?

english: Under good weather and soil conditions, a plantain stem usually flowers around 9 to 12 months after planting and takes another 3 to 4 months for the bunch to mature fully for harvest.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa shishi lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Ni ebaahe nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani ŋmeii lɛ adara kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or it could be caused by root damage from pests or fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka during heavy rains.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Aloo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ahe helai, tamɔ Black Sigatoka yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha eba.

english: Why do some of my plantain trees fall over before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi miigbee shi dani aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems. When heavy bunches form, strong wind or soft soil after heavy rain can easily pull them down. Supporting the fruit-bearing stem with a branched wooden pole helps keep it standing.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Beni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ feɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛba shi mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛ tsei niji yɔɔ mli lɛ fiɔ aduawai lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔɔ shi.

english: How many shoots should I allow to grow around one main plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei bibii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he?

english: Keep only one main stem producing fruit, one medium shoot growing behind it, and one tiny shoot starting out. Pruning extra shoots prevents them from stealing food from the main plantain bunch.
ga: Ha tso titri kome pɛ ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahi shi. Ayɛ tso kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ ni miida yɛ esɛɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ plantains akuu titri lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land is naturally suited for growing plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ji he ko ni sa kɛha plantain ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Plantains thrive in rich, deep soil that drains water easily without flooding, and in areas that receive good rainfall spread throughout the year.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ oya ni nu afua baaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea gives the maize the food it needs to grow dark, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ baai ni tsuɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the strong sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and their delicate leaves burn easily in full sunlight before their roots grow deep enough to find water. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates living umbrellas that protect the young cocoa from heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Dani shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛna nu Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the soil when heavy rains fall in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain sits on flat land without draining, it chokes the soil and starves the roots of air, allowing rot-causing fungi to grow. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to run off so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ babaoo. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the center leaves of my young corn crops?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing center of the corn plant. Spraying early in the morning with recommended biopesticides or applying neem leaf extract destroys the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from hot dry weather, uneven water supply, or lack of key soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and feeding it well helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into full peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ ahe haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. aloo niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with tiny ears when I plant many seeds in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ toi bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients like people competing for a small bowl of food. Planting seeds with proper spacing ensures every single stalk gets enough nutrients to produce large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ tamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi bibioo mli lɛ he akaŋ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tso fɛɛ tso lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly even when I give my farm water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that drink up water and steal fertilizer from the soil much faster than your crops can. Removing weeds while they are still small ensures all the water and nutrients go directly into feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ehaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my farm getting smaller and smaller every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi lɛ?

english: As a plantain tree grows, it produces many young sucker shoots around its base that suck energy away from the main fruiting stem. Pruning off the extra suckers so that only two or three strong shoots remain allows the mother plant to produce huge, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ebaawo ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. shishitoo koni ekɛjie hewalɛ kɛjɛ yibiiwoo tso titri lɛ mli Afoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo plantain ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and soft during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and crowded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods right away stops the disease from spreading to healthy cocoa.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã kookoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so the rain does not wash it away from my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii koni nugbɔ akafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is damp right after a light rain, rather than during heavy downpours that wash it down the hills. Making a small ring around the plant stem and covering the fertilizer with a little soil keeps it in place for the roots to soak up.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni kɛ muji baa gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ mli lɛ. making small rings Obɔle tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ fioo ko aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do some crops grow better in the Northern Region of Ghana while others thrive in the Middle Belt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: The Northern Region has a single, drier rainy season with lower humidity, making it ideal for grains like millet and sorghum. The Middle Belt enjoys two rainy seasons and richer forest soils, which better support moisture-loving crops like plantains, cocoa, and root vegetables.
ga: Kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli egbi ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Teŋgbɛ bɛlt lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei enyɔ kɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ plantains, cocoa, kɛ shishifãi aduawai jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland has good enough soil to support a high harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ babaoo?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to the touch, retains moisture well after rain, and contains earthworms or organic matter, showing it has the natural fertility needed to nourish crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni he hiaa koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it so important for me to plant my seeds quickly after the first rain season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting immediately allows young crops to make full use of the entire rainy period to establish strong root systems before the heat and dry spells set in.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ haa amɛnáa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa dani hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ baa.

english: What happens to my crops if a sudden dry spell hits right when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ba beni amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive growth stage; extreme heat or lack of water during this time causes flowers to drop off, resulting in fewer fruits or grain heads.
ga: Fɔfɔii lɛ ji be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ yɛ dalɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa aduawai loo dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ faaa.

english: Will burying my seeds deeper into the ground protect them and help them grow better?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛbaafu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baabu amɛhe ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, planting seeds too deep starves them of sunlight and energy before they reach the surface. Seeds should generally only be planted at a depth two to three times their width.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ hewalɛ aye amɛ hɔmɔ dani amɛshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ fe amɛlɛɛmɔ lɛ toi 2-3 pɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out small when I plant the stems very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their root systems compete with each other for space, soil nutrients, and water, leaving little energy to form large, full tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ni akɛfeɔ bulbs agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is missing key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead during the hot afternoon, but recover in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it during peak sunshine. Drooping is a natural mechanism to reduce surface exposure and conserve moisture until temperatures cool.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Drooping ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ shi ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Is it helpful for my farm if I mix legumes like groundnuts with my grain crops?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii futu miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: Yes, legumes naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, which helps fertilize companion crops like maize or sorghum.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afɔɔ nanemɛi tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger on my land than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants highly adapted to local conditions, allowing them to rapidly absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmaŋ lɛ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central part of the maize plant (the whorl) to feed on tender leaves, which can destroy the plant before it matures if not treated early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei (rings) lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tso lɛ hiɛ dani eshɛ shweremɔ he kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ oya.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and dry while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and dark shade. Pruning excess canopy branches to let in light and removing infected pods helps keep your healthy pods safe.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni su yɔɔ diŋŋ lɛ. Afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni la abote mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni o-pod ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Keeping weeds down and spraying recommended soaps or insecticides controls the insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni okɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ koni akɛkudɔ kooloi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily in full sunlight. Planting plantain trees next to young cocoa creates a living canopy that provides shade, retains moisture, and protects the young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni obu tsei bibii ahe

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground exposes them to maximum sunlight for food production while keeping them away from hot soil and wet ground diseases, resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ enaa koni ekafee hulutsoo fe nine kɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the ground when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain in flat or heavy clay soil creates waterlogging, which suffocates roots and causes fungal root rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds allows excess water to drain off easily.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi ni ji fungal lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year even though I plant maize on the same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same soil every season drains specific nutrients out of the earth. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough after the first rain to plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: Dig down into the soil to a hand's depth; if the soil is moist all the way down and forms a soft ball in your hand, it is ready. If only the top surface is wet, seeds may germinate and then die if rain pauses.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔ ni onine baanyɛ ashɛ he; Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ onine mli lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo. Kɛji ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over when the fruit bunch starts growing large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be easily weakened by soil pests like root nematodes. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo or wooden prop takes the weight off the roots so the bunch can fully ripen safely.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ gbɔjɔɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei fi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ baa shi. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow early instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant stay strong and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or sudden changes in soil nutrients. The plant sheds flowers to save water and energy until weather conditions become favorable again.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsake trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants curl their leaves up tight during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. Tomato plants curl their leaves in high heat to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which keeps the plant from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tomato tsei kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa tomato tsei lɛ afite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and large fruits, the plants spend all their energy stretching upward to reach light.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nguahi. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ kɛ e he wami tsuo tsuɔ ní kɛ gblaa e he konɛ e ná la.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so fast when I stack them inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛto ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams need continuous airflow and cool temperatures to stay fresh. If yams are bruised during harvest or stacked tightly in hot, unventilated rooms, rot-causing fungi easily enter the cuts and decay the tubers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ sweet potato mli lɛ he miihia daa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ koni ehi shi ehee. Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes lɛ fã yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo kɛji akɛ ato amɛ yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Fuŋ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ abote pilamɔ lɛ mli oya ni eha bulb lɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots go bad just two or three days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike crops with thick protective skins, cassava roots undergo rapid chemical breakdown as soon as they are detached from the plant. Exposure to air triggers decay rapidly unless the roots are processed or kept buried in damp soil.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ tsei lɛ, cassava shishifãi yɛ hewolo ni mli tse, ni buɔ mɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli pɛ kɛkɛ ni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha fitemɔ aba oya. Ja atsu shishifãi lɛ ahe nii loo afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: How does drying my harvested maize thoroughly help it remain good for a long time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Drying removes internal moisture that mold spores and insects need to survive. Well-dried grain creates an dry environment where fungal decay cannot take hold, keeping the harvest intact for months.
ga: Gbimɔ jieɔ mligbɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa ni ŋmei kɛ kooloi bibii ahi shi lɛ. Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli egbi ni ŋmei lɛ nyɛŋ ashi ŋmei lɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni adu lɛ fiteee nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my plantains turn soft and spoil fast if they get bumped or bruised on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ mikɛ mihe wo mli loo mikɛ mihe wo mli yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bruising breaks the plantain's skin cells and triggers the rapid release of natural ripening gases. The damaged skin also creates open wounds where mold enters, causing the fruit to rot before it can be sold.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko fã lɛ, efiteɔ plantain lɛ hewolo nɔ wala yibii lɛ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo oya. Hewolo ni efite lɛ hu kɛ pilamɔi ni agbeleɔ yɛ he ni ŋmeii boteɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii lɛ baagboi dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea beans get full of tiny holes and brown powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Storage pests like weevils lay tiny eggs on the beans before or after harvest. Once hatched, the young insects eat through the inside of the seed, but storing properly dried beans in airtight containers suffocates the pests and protects the crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ ŋmeii anɔ dani akpa loo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ Kɛji efɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ to tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight and strong winds. Planting shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from harsh heat and retains moisture around the roots until the trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ mli waa

english: Why do produce buyers reject my crops if I harvest them when they are still very green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpooɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikpa amɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lolo lɛ?

english: Buyers reject deep green produce because it usually contains too much water and is not fully ripe or dried. High moisture makes the crop spoil quickly during transportation and storage.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ nu babaoo yɛ mli. ni ehooo kwraa loo egbiko La ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko kɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What causes buying companies to turn away bags of produce at the buying shed?
ga: Mɛni haa nitsumɔhei ni heɔ nii lɛ tsakeɔ nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ akotokui yɛ nitsumɔhei ni amɛheɔ nii lɛ?

english: Buying centers turn away produce if it is still wet, improperly dried, or deep green. Produce must meet specific dryness standards, which officers often check using special testing machines.
ga: Nihɔɔmɔ he lɛ baakpoo nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Egbiŋ jogbaŋŋ loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ Esa akɛ Produce lɛ ashɛ ŋmɔlɔ he mlai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe. ni onukpai lɛ fɔɔ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni akɛkaa mɔ lɛ akwɛɔ lɛ

english: Why do officers at the buying station use small machines on my crops before accepting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ nihɔɔmɔ he lɛ kɛ tsɔnei bibii tsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ dani amɛheɔ lɛ?

english: Officers use testing machines to check the hidden moisture levels inside your crops. This ensures the produce is properly dried and ready for safe storage or processing.
ga: Amralofoi kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkaa nibii akwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ fa ha. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli egbi jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo kɛha nibii ni akɛtoɔ loo atsuɔ nii yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: What should I do if my crops drop from the tree to the ground before they turn brown?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛba shikpɔŋ dani ebatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Produce that falls to the ground while still green should not be sold right away. You need to gather it and dry it thoroughly in the sun until its color changes to brown.
ga: Esaaa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ nibii ni adu ni egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Esa akɛ obua amɛnaa ni ogbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛhe su lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does the color of my crop need to change from green to brown after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The color change from green to brown is a key sign that moisture is leaving the produce. A brown color shows that the crop is properly dried and stable enough for long-term storage.
ga: Su ni tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji okadi ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ miishi nibii ni adu lɛ mli. Su ni ji blɔfo tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can drying green crops in the sun make them acceptable to buyers who previously rejected them?
ga: Ani tsei eŋɔli ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni tsutsu lɛ amɛkpoo amɛ lɛ akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, drying green crops lowers their moisture content and changes their color to brown, which brings them up to the quality standards buyers look for.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni agbiɔ lɛ haa amɛmli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi ni ehaa amɛhe su feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa anáa shishitoo mlai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to pack green crops into sacks right after picking them off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baawo kotokui amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Packing green or wet crops traps moisture inside the sack. This causes mold to grow, spoils the whole batch, and leads to buyers rejecting your entire harvest.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji loo ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baamɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ. fiteɔ set muu lɛ fɛɛ ni oha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akpoo okpamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Does produce that falls onto the soil spoil faster than produce picked directly from the tree?
ga: Ani nibii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya fe nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, produce on the ground absorbs moisture from the dirt. If it remains green and wet on the soil, it rots faster unless collected quickly and spread out to dry.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ muji mli. Kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaafite oya ja ekɛ ehe babɔ he oya ni egbɛ eshwa koni egbi.

english: How do I know that my harvested produce is dry enough for sale without using a machine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ni mikɛ tsɔnei tsuuu nii?

english: While buyers use testing machines for accuracy, a clear visual sign for farmers is the complete color change from deep green to a uniform brown across the entire crop.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hɔlɔ lɛ kɛ kaa tsuɔ nii koni ena nɔ ni ja moŋ. Shi nɔ ni okwaafoi yɔseɔ ji bɔ ni su lɛ tsakeɔ kwraa kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa eŋɔli ni tamɔ ekome nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers insist on drying crops until the color changes completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ agbi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyashi amɛhe su lɛ baaje shishi lɛ?

english: Officers insist on full color change because residual green areas mean water is still trapped inside. Trapped water lowers the quality and market value of the crop.
ga: Amralofoi lɛ ma nɔ mi akɛ amɛbaatsake su lɛ kwraa ejaakɛ he ni eshwɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ehi mli lolo. Nu ni atsĩ naa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ jarayeli jara baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing small ragged holes and looking like something is eating them inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko miiye tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant. Catching them early with recommended biopesticides or neem extract keeps them from destroying the growing point of your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up into strange shapes with yellowish-green patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and by using stem cuttings from sick plants. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by the ministry is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Aduɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni sɔɔmɔ nitsumɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ amɛnaa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before the fruit can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called Blossom End Rot, and it usually happens when the soil lacks calcium or when the soil moisture changes drastically from very dry to very wet. Keeping regular watering schedules and adding calcium-rich soil amendments prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot ni bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ calcium. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni calcium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a field with no big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunlight because their delicate leaves burn easily. Planting plantains or shade trees beside them creates a cool environment and protects them until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ebuɔ tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, weak bunches when I let all the tiny shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main plant. Removing most of the extra shoots and leaving only one strong follower shoot allows the main tree to put all its energy into making a big bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome pɛ ni he wa ni nyiɛɔ esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to manufacture food for the growing underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air, prevents leaf diseases from warm soil, and helps the crop produce larger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Tsi tso helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni oye obua tsei ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Tsoi ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil water quickly, prevents weeds from growing, and keeps the plant roots cool during dry weather.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers onto the ground instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miishwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving them steady moisture and balanced nutrients keeps the blossoms attached so they can grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of farm land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the soil of the exact same nutrients every season and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves turn light yellow and stay small even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and slow growth often mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build leafy green growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a high-nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color and help them head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha yitso lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha yitso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants need standing water in the field while my corn crop dies if the land stays flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their roots that allow them to breathe underwater, whereas corn roots suffocate and rot when trapped in water without oxygen.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ amɛbote nu mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad for me to put fertilizer on my crop when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ani no ehiii kɛha mi?

english: Crops cannot eat dry food; they drink their nutrients dissolved in water. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can actually burn the crop's roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii ni egbi. Amɛnuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛwo nu mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves use to stay green and build energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛsu eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛha hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with very few fruits when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plants use sunlight to make their food. When shaded by big trees, they stretch unnaturally high to search for light, leaving them too weak to produce heavy fruit.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. Beni eyɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Eshɛɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ gbɛ ni jeee adebɔɔ naa nɔ koni etao la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant my seeds very close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant malnourished.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal the water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops, effectively starving your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, drought, or insect attacks, because they do not have enough energy to mature the fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe haomɔ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo koolooi tutuamɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ adara kwraa lɛ bɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my rice before the grains start falling off?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa dani ŋmãa lɛ aje shishi egbee shi?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when roughly 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the head turn golden yellow and the firm grains hard enough to crack between your teeth.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ.

english: Why should I not plant cassava on the exact same spot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ naa shia ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ yɛ daa.

english: Why do seeds I save from my own harvest produce weaker crops than certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds naturally lose their strength and resistance over generations, whereas certified seeds are specially bred and treated for high yield, disease resistance, and uniform growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient maize needs to build green foliage, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛwo baai eŋɔli Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and develop yellowish spots?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This is typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects that feed on the sap of the cassava plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni yeɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli nu lɛ

english: Tomato flowers often drop off during very hot days because extreme heat prevents the flower from pollinating itself properly, stopping the fruit from forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. ni ekpaa aduawai adalɛ

english: Yam tubers become bent when the soil is too hard, compacted, or full of stones, which creates physical barriers that prevent the tuber from growing straight down.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni tsiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the inner leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ mli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed inside the central funnel of young maize plants where the tender leaves grow.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ he ni baai bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to save moisture and usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is my orange tree dropping unripe green fruits onto the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ shĩɔ aduawai eŋɔli ni eshɛko shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit when they suffer from sudden dry spells or lack sufficient nutrients to nourish all the fruits currently growing on the branch.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna piŋmɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli loo amɛbɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why is my land producing smaller crop harvests every year even though I clear it properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mikɛjie mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Growing crops continuously on the same plot depletes the natural soil nutrients. Without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer, or letting the land rest, the soil becomes tired and yields decline.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ohaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dropping off when exposed to too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out their moisture fast. Planting shade crops like plantains provides a natural umbrella that protects young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la fɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very slowly when I plant them under mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ kookoo tso ni eda shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require direct, bright sunlight to make energy and produce heavy fruit bunches. When planted beneath large cocoa trees, the thick canopy blocks the sunlight, causing the plantains to starve for energy and grow poorly.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ ni ewo yibii ni tsii. Kɛ́ adu yɛ kookoo tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the small water shoots growing out of the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ

english: Water shoots (also called chupons) suck away valuable water and soil nutrients from the main tree trunk without producing pods. Removing them ensures the tree directs all its food and energy into making large, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nu mli ŋmeii (ni ale amɛ hu akɛ chupons) lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is there a strange bush growing on my cocoa branch, and why is that branch starting to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ yɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni mɛni hewɔ amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: That strange bush is a parasite called mistletoe. It sinks its roots directly into the branch of your cocoa tree to steal water and food, which eventually starves and kills the branch if you do not cut it off completely.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mistletoe. Eshishifãi woɔ kookoo niji amli tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha yɛ naagbee lɛ, hɔmɔ aye tso lɛ nine lɛ ni egbo kɛji ofooo lɛ kwraa.

english: What happens to my cocoa harvest if I allow tall weeds to cover the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikookoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji miha jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ha miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Tall weeds act like thief plants that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your cocoa trees. They also trap moisture around the tree trunk, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases and pests thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu ebɔle ehe. tso shishi Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease known as Black Pod, which spreads through water drops in high humidity. Pruning overgrown branches helps sunlight and fresh air pass through the farm, drying out the moisture so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃.

english: Trees drop flowers naturally when they do not have enough water or soil nutrients to support full pods, or when there are not enough tiny insects in the soil to pollinate them. Proper soil care and keeping leaf litter on the ground helps protect pollinators and holds flowers on the tree.
ga: Tsei baajie fɔfɔii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbe naa. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii yɛ Shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha pollination bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ baai ni afo lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe ni ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods from the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: A cocoa pod is ready for harvest when its skin changes color completely from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting only at this stage guarantees that the beans inside are fully developed, sweet, and ready for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhewolo lɛ tsake kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli pɛ ji nɔ ni haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edara kwraa, amɛhe ŋɔɔ, ni amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce smaller pods now even though the leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli lolo?

english: Over many years, cocoa trees pull essential nutrients out of the earth to produce pods, leaving the soil tired and weak. Even if the tree stays green, it lacks the extra nutrients needed to make big pods unless you feed the soil with compost or cocoa fertilizer.
ga: Afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sũ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egbɔjɔɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji lolo moŋ Shi ebɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee ŋmɔji wuji. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my yield if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting trees too closely makes their roots fight over water and nutrients, while their leaves block out air movement. This overcrowding leads to smaller harvests and makes it very easy for pod diseases to spread quickly from tree to tree.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ahe baai tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa lɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɔmɛi ni eyi obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa nikpamɔ bibioo baa. ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's life helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my farm so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii koni mikafite nii?

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain, because water helps the roots absorb the nutrients. Avoid applying it right before heavy rain, which will wash it away, or during severe drought when roots cannot take it in.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ nu yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii kpakpai. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he. ni baaho loo yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote mli lɛ.
