english: Can I use chicken manure together with chemical fertilizer on the same crop?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei afata tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ he kɛha tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, mixing them works very well. Chicken manure improves the soil structure so it holds water better, while chemical fertilizer gives the plant a quick boost of essential nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, amɛ ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Kooloi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni ehiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during hot afternoons even when the wet soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ, nu baahi.

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The plant temporary wilts to protect itself from the heat, but it will stand back up once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi ebaadamɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a shortage of plant nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil helps flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo tsei amli niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crops give me very small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space allows it to feed well and produce bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eye nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they aggressively drink the water and eat the fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops all the food and light they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I change the crop I plant on my plot every season instead of planting cassava every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmei daa afi lɛ

english: Planting the same crop every year builds up specific pests and diseases in the soil and drains the same nutrients. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans breaks disease cycles and restores natural food to the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Enɛ haa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I cut off the small extra branches growing on the sides of my tomato stems?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Ani nakai nɔ ni miida yɛ tomato tso lɛ masɛi ni ajie lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming those extra side shoots (called suckers) directs the plant's water and energy into growing larger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, nakai sɛɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ afolɔmɔ. Akɛ tso lɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii) tsuɔ nii koni akɛdu tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do shop-bought seeds grow better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from agro-dealers are specially selected and bred for high yields and resistance to local pests and diseases. Seeds saved from past harvests naturally lose these strong traits over time, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, intense sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside them provides shade and holds soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ adumɔ yɛ he kome. Ebaaha hulutsoo be aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and yellow starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the plant base restores leaf color and crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he lɛ he. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ebaa lɛ su kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field help my soil for the next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots with the help of beneficial soil organisms. When these plants die, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aye abuamɔ nɔ. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains stay on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when roots sit in standing water because waterlogged soil blocks oxygen from reaching the underground roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upward and shrinking into tight knots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miihoso ni ekɛmiifee ŋmei ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck juices from under the leaves and spread viruses. Neem oil spray or insecticidal soap helps control these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ebuɔ baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant before any tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop without setting fruit when the plant faces extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Keeping soil moisture steady and shading nursery beds during extremely hot afternoons helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛmɔhe lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my small vegetable seedlings collapse and die at the stem right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni ji Mine lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ shishi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This problem is caused by fungal diseases that thrive when nursery beds are kept too wet and crowded. Spacing seeds out and watering gently around the base without soaking the stems keeps fungal rots away.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ kɛ́ gbekɛbii ashihilɛhei lɛ amli edɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojara dumɔwui lɛ amli ni okɛ nu awo shishigbɛ lɛ he blɛoo ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ akawo mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why is my plantain tree bearing very small bunches even though I water it regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miida bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ daa?

english: When too many young sucker shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients meant for the fruit. Removing excess suckers and leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main tree produces large, full bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa yibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to produce energy that builds large tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the shaded soil surface into direct sunlight, resulting in much bigger harvested yams.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa hulutsoo be wuji baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: What is the best time of day to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cooler and soil is slightly moist. Applying fertilizer under strong afternoon sun can burn plant roots and cause the fertilizer nutrients to evaporate into the air.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli niyenii lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do imported hybrid seed varieties grow faster than our traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hybrid dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ daa oya fe wɔ shishijee dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Imported hybrid seeds are specially bred in laboratories for rapid growth and uniform crop development under proper management, whereas traditional local seeds have adapted over generations to survive tough local conditions at a slower, steady pace.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ anɔ yɛ laboratorii amli koni amɛdara oya ni amɛkwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, akutsoŋ dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ etsake amɛhe kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛtee yinɔ kroko mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ akutsoŋ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yaa nɔ daa nɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from the imported vegetables I buy at the market to plant on my farm next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ aduawai dumɔwui ni mikɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended because seeds from hybrid imported crops often produce weak plants or inconsistent yields in the next generation. It is better to buy fresh certified seeds each season for predictable harvests.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo yibiiwoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli be fɛɛ be kɛha kpamɔ ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ.

english: Is it safe to mix local cow dung with the chemical fertilizer I buy from the agro-dealer?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ baafutu maŋ lɛ mli tsina ŋmei?

english: Yes, mixing organic manure with chemical fertilizer is very beneficial. Manure improves the soil structure and holds moisture, while chemical fertilizers provide quick nutrients that crops need to grow rapidly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ he. Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni tsuɔ nii oya ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara oya.

english: Cassava sheds its leaves naturally during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to conserve water and survive until the rainy season returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat. They need temporary shade plants, like plantains, to shield their delicate leaves from burning and to retain soil moisture until they grow strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the day to reduce their surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which helps the plant conserve water.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he.

english: Why do pests attack my newly introduced crop varieties more than my old local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsei srɔtoi ni mikɛba ehee lɛ fe mimaŋ tsei momo lɛ?

english: Local crop varieties have developed natural chemical defenses against native pests over a long time, whereas foreign or exotic varieties often lack these natural protections against local insects.
ga: Tsei sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ efee tsofai ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ maŋsɛɛ loo maŋsɛɛ srɔtoi lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi bibii ahe.

english: Why does my pepper plant drop its flowers before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or poor nutrients. Maintaining consistent moisture in the soil helps the plant keep its flowers and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni esaaa ni amɛyeɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when there is a short rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots cannot grip the ground tightly, which happens if seeds are planted too shallowly or if the soil lacks proper depth and organic structure.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ mlibotemɔ ni sa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow long and skinny instead of big and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee agboi ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become thin when planted in hard, compacted soil because the root cannot expand easily. Loosening the soil into mounds or ridges allows the tuber to expand freely into a larger size.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ awoɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii amli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya.

english: What is hand pollination, and why should I do it on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another using your hands or a small brush instead of waiting for insects. It helps your cocoa trees produce significantly more pods than natural pollination alone.
ga: Hand pollination ji be mli ni okɛ oniji loo brɔsh bibioo ko tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kooloi bibii lɛ Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni baa lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but very few of them turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers need to be pollinated by tiny insects called midges to turn into pods. If there are not enough insects or if weather conditions are unfavorable, unpollinated flowers naturally fall off after a day or two.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ bafeɔ pod. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ ehiii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baagbee shi yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ sɛɛ.

english: What work do I need to do on my farm before starting hand pollination?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mabɔi fɔfɔii ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Before hand pollination, you need to weed around the base of the trees and prune unnecessary leaves and branches so flowers get enough light, air, and space to grow into healthy pods.
ga: Dani nine baafee pollination Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni ofolɔ baai kɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni fɔfɔi lɛ ana la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Is it good to carry out hand pollination while it is raining on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ mi nine baawo pollination be mli ni nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, heavy rain washes away the pollen from the flowers and destroys the delicate flower parts. It is best to pollinate on clear, dry mornings when the flowers are fresh.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee pollination yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi, be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ yɔɔ ehee lolo lɛ.

english: Why is cocoa farming described as a daily commitment rather than something I can check on once a month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii amli akɛ eji daa gbi shiwoo moŋ fe nɔ ko ni manyɛ makwɛ mli shikome yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require regular attention because pests, fungal diseases, and unwanted shoots grow quickly. Daily or frequent visits help you catch problems early before they damage your yield.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa ejaakɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ daa oya. Saramɔi ni afeɔ daa gbi loo shii abɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onáa naagbai mra. Dani ebaafite onitsumɔ lɛ

english: What is a 'chupon' on my cocoa tree, and why must I cut it off?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘chupon’ ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: A chupon is a fast-growing vertical shoot that sprouts from the trunk or branches. It steals nutrients and water away from the main tree and flowers, so removing it helps the tree focus energy on pod growth.
ga: Chupong ji tso tso ko ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni jɛɔ tso lɛ tso loo nine mli. Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ maa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are stressed or not getting enough attention?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cocoa tso lɛ miihao loo akɛ hiɛdɔɔ bɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa?

english: Stressed cocoa trees usually show yellowing leaves, drooping branches, excessive flower loss, or stunted growth, which signals that they need shade management, fertilizer, or pest treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni haoɔ lɛ jieɔ baai ŋmɔŋ, niji ni egbee shi, kɛ fɔfɔi ni elaaje fe nine lɛ kpo. loo edalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ni ená hulutsoo, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How long does a cocoa flower take to grow into a fully mature pod ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Once a cocoa flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about five to six months for it to grow from a small green cushion into a mature, fully ripe cocoa pod.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani ejɛɔ jwɛi bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli edaa. Etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eda kwraa.

english: Why do some of my young, tiny cocoa pods turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani eda lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' a natural process where the tree drops pods it cannot feed, or it could be caused by fungal diseases like black pod due to excessive dampness and shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘cherel wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ni tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni jɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer pods even though the trees are huge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni egbɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ miiya hiɛ moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age, overcrowded branches block sunlight and exhaust the soil's nutrients. Pruning the tree and feeding the soil with fertilizer encourage new flower cushion growth and bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ, niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa leaves will curl up, turn yellow, or get burnt edges if they receive too much direct sun. Healthy young cocoa needs shade from companion crops like plantains to keep the leaves broad, green, and moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baabɔle amɛhe. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Aloo eshishigbɛi lɛ baashã kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo shɛ enɔ. Cocoa gbekɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ he miihia ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata ehe tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eŋɔli ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛshwere kwraa lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Can I immediately plant cocoa on land that was previously excavated for illegal mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajie kɛha shika tsuru ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, because mining strips away the fertile topsoil and leaves behind dangerous chemicals and compacted earth. The land needs to be cleared of toxic waste, leveled, and treated with organic manure or cover crops before it can nourish cocoa again.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa lɛ baajie ŋwɛi sũ ni baa nii lɛ. ni eshiɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, afee lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ atsu he nii dani akɛ kookoo awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil, and how can I protect my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Bare soil has no roots to hold it together when heavy rain falls. Planting cover crops like leguminous plants or leaving crop residues on the ground creates a shield that slows down rainwater and keeps the nutrient-rich soil in place.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni baaha ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ Loo nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How often should I harvest my cocoa pods during the main season to get the best quality?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii yɛ be titri lɛ mli koni ehi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should harvest every 2 to 3 weeks. Gathering ripe pods regularly prevents them from over-ripening on the tree, reduces pest attacks, and keeps disease from spreading to untouched pods.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 3. Kɛ́ obua ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anaa daa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni otsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing much smaller harvests than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 30 years, their natural productivity drops and they become more vulnerable to soil exhaustion and disease. You can restore your yield by grafting improved varieties or gradually replanting young trees.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Obaanyɛ okɛ yibiiwoo aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni oookɛwo mli loo ni oookwɛ amɛ fiofio lɛ nɔ. dumɔ tsei heei

english: How do weeds growing around my cocoa trees harm my crop yield?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cocoa trees for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. They also trap damp air around the tree trunks, creating an environment where fungal diseases can easily grow.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu. tso shishi Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: What causes crop leaves to turn yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or waterlogged soil that is choking the roots. Adding compost or the right fertilizer restores the green color and helps the plant absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni miitsi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cocoa crop if I cut down all the large forest trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mifo koo mli tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Removing all large trees exposes your cocoa to severe sun heat, strong winds, and rapid soil drying. Keeping a few permanent shade trees protects the cocoa from harsh weather and extends the lifespan of your farm.
ga: Tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ooojie lɛ haa o-cocoa lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be mli, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ oya lɛ mli. Tsei fioo komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ baabu o-cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe, ni ebaaha oŋmɔ lɛ wala aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and dry up prematurely during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and large leaves that lose water very quickly in heat. Spreading dry grass or crop leaves around the base of the plantain acts as mulch, holding moisture in the soil through dry periods.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji ni kɛ́ edɔ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Jwɛi loo tso baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Plantain shishitoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why are some of the crops on my farm growing very small while others reach full, heavy sizes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa bibioo kwraa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi daraa ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Crops grow to different sizes based on nutrient distribution, water availability, and plant spacing. Ensuring uniform soil fertility and giving plants adequate space helps all crops reach healthy, natural, and heavy sizes.
ga: Tsei daa kɛyashɛɔ dalɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ bɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ mlijaa yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Nu ni yɔɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni ahaa tsei lɛ hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi, nɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli, kɛ nɔ ni tsii.

english: How can I make my maize grains heavier so that I get a better market price when selling by weight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-abele ŋmaa lɛ afee mlɛo koni maná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ beni mikɛ shwiili lɛ hɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grains gain weight during the grain-filling stage after pollination. Providing balanced fertilizer (especially nitrogen and potassium) and ensuring adequate water while the cobs are forming increases grain density and overall weight.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ naa tsiimɔ yɛ be mli ni awoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni sa (titri lɛ nitrogen kɛ potassium) ni akwɛ koni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers and small fruits drop off before they can grow into full sizes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii Ani minɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani edaa kɛyashɛɔ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Flowers and young fruits drop mainly due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients like calcium. Consistent watering and balanced soil feeding prevent premature dropping and help fruits mature fully.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ tso yibii lɛ ahe shwiemɔ naa oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: If I plant my crops very close to each other, will I get a bigger overall harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani mawo yibii babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants with small, light fruits. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to develop full, heavy yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni tsii.

english: What kind of help do crop booster products or liquid fertilizers actually give to my plants?
ga: Te nɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Crop boosters deliver essential nutrients directly through the plant leaves, allowing faster absorption. This helps plants overcome environmental stress, grow stronger, and produce heavier, larger crops.
ga: Tso boosters haa niyenii ni he hiaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ tsei baai anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyeɔ shihilɛ mli haomɔi anɔ kunim. amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: When is the right time to feed my crops fertilizer so that they grow fast and produce big fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii wuji?

english: Crops need nutrients most during early vegetative growth to build strong stems, and just before flowering to build heavy fruits. Feeding them at these specific stages maximizes fruit size and yield.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo he miihia tsei yɛ amɛ dalɛ shishijee mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa. ni dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛfee aduawai ni tsii Niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ nɛkɛ fãi pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni eha elɛɛmɔ kɛ ebɔɔ babaoo aya hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks vital soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are suffering from poor soil conditions. Applying compost or the right fertilizer restores green growth and crop strength.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ sũ shihilɛ kpakpa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants staying short and refusing to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Stunted growth in tomatoes happens when soil lacks organic nutrients or when underground pests damage the roots. Improving soil fertility and protecting roots allows plants to grow tall and set heavy fruit.
ga: Tomato lɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ kɛ shishifãi ahe ni abuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees curl up and dry out during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during dry weather as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss. Planting shade trees alongside cocoa and mulching the soil surface preserves moisture and keeps the crops healthy through dry spells.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ ohi shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛfata kookoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafite ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do insects and pests stop my crops from reaching their natural heavy weight?
ga: Te kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni tsii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Pests suck sap and destroy leaves, stealing the food and energy the plant needs to develop its fruits. Protecting crops from insects ensures that energy goes directly into growing bigger, heavier yields.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ. Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo yibii. Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni dara ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide crucial shade and retain soil moisture, acting as protective covers while the young cocoa trees establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Kɛtsɔ nitsumɔ akɛ hebuu tsɔne nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ agbe naa lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen, leaving the ground weak. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the new top growth to survive, causing the older lower leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii heei anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does adding dried poultry manure make my vegetables grow better than just planting in plain soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ haa mi-aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Poultry manure acts as a rich, slow-release plant food that improves soil structure, helps the ground hold water longer, and feeds essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus directly to plant roots.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii ni jara wa, ni jieɔ ehe blɛoo. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward full sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes increases food production for the plant, leading to larger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni tso lɛ feɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops give smaller yields when I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every individual plant enough room to feed and grow to its full potential.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni eda kɛyashɛ he ni ebaanyɛ eshɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show a white powdery substance during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ powda yɛŋ beni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by tiny pests called mealybugs or spider mites that suck sap from the underside of leaves during hot weather, causing the plant to lose water and stress out.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs loo spider mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa nu ni amɛhaoɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ mli edɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant usually brought on by irregular watering. It is a physiological issue rather than an insect attack or infectious disease.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Eji gbɔmɔtsoŋ naagba fe kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ loo hela ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young pepper plants so much more than when the plants are older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ awui waa fe beni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young pepper seedlings have shallow, delicate root systems and small leaves. Weeds quickly outgrow them, stealing water, fertilizer, and light before the seedlings can build strong stems.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii. Jwɛi lɛ daa fe amɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ la dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly during short dry spells even after heavy rain fell earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa mra moŋ.

english: Heavy rains often wash over hard topsoil without soaking deep into the ground. Mulching your farm with dry grass helps trap rainwater deep in the soil where roots can reach it during hot days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa ekwɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ha oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ.

english: When lower maize leaves yellow in a V-shape from the tip inward, it usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves, showing it needs compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, amɛfeɔ V su kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen awo mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed their leaves and look weak when the dry harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ harmatta be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees lose leaves in the dry season to save water because dry winds and hot sun dry up the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from direct sun and reduces water loss.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi

english: How do I know when cassava tubers are mature enough for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready 8 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves naturally yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni egbeeɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why is it helpful to leave dry grass or plant leaves on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, prevents weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the soil as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni oná nu fioo Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: No, heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away from your crops before the roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or when only light rain is expected.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ onibii amli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ fioo pɛ.

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot every season drains the specific nutrients tomatoes need and allows soil pests and diseases to build up, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree grows large, healthy bunches of fruit.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso yibii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the hot ground into the sunlight, which helps the leaves make food to grow bigger tubers and prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ aba hulu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhoɔ koni bulb lɛ agbo. ni etsi helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee baai ni fiteɔ

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden during the early morning or in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo ooowo hulu lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane mli?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture before the hot sun causes it to evaporate, giving your vegetables enough water to handle the heat of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kwɛmɔ ni o-vegetables lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsu hulutsoo be lɛ he nii nakai gbi lɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in the leaves and center whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the center whorl of the plant and eat the tender growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fãa yɛ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying when they get full sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ ye amɛnɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense direct sunlight, which scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil before their shallow roots can absorb enough water. Providing shade trees or growing plantains alongside them creates a cooler microclimate and protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shade ni akɛhaa loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ni mli ejɔ baa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn pale yellow starting from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center vein of older maize leaves usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the essential nutrient plants need to produce chlorophyll and grow green, leafy foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee klorofil ni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, will I harvest more cassava tubers?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani wɔbaakpa ŋmei shishifãi babaoo?

english: Planting cassava too closely forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin stems with very small tubers rather than a smaller number of healthy plants with large, thick roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yitsei bibii waa. Mohu ɔ, tso bɔɔ ko nɛ a he wa nɛ a sisi agbohi nɛ a mi wa ngɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves higher toward sunlight, which allows the plant to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ, ni amɛkwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and drop leaves after heavy rains leave standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates plant roots by cutting off the air pockets in the soil. Without oxygen, root tissues die and can no longer absorb water or nutrients, causing the plant to wilt even in wet conditions.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifã lɛ gboɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ po mli.

english: What causes tiny holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants along with small brown droppings?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the leaf whorl during the day to feed on the growing tip of the plant and leaves droppings behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ ni amɛshi ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when extreme heat or lack of water stresses the plant, preventing successful pollination. Without pollination, the plant sheds the flower instead of developing a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Enɛ haaa anyɛ afee pollination yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baafɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ tomato.

english: Should I leave all the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii yɛ mi plantains lɛ shishi?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal water and food from the main mother plant, resulting in small bunches. It is better to remove most suckers and keep only one or two healthy ones for the next crop cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli, ni no baaha ŋmeii akui bibii aba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni okɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ato kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Growing maize repeatedly on the same plot rapidly drains the specific nutrients maize needs and gives soil pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply season after season.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ afite oya. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ aná shia ni baahi shi daa ni amɛfɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why should I wait for my crop seeds to sprout before putting chemical fertilizer near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo amɛhe?

english: Seeds carry their own stored energy to germinate, and delicate young sprouts do not yet have strong roots. Applying fertilizer too early can burn the new roots and waste expensive inputs before the plant is ready to absorb them.
ga: Dumɔwui eto hewalɛ kɛha kwɛ̃mɔ. Ni tso bibioo ni waaa lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni wa lolo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi heei ni efite nibii ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ dani tso lɛ afee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ amɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and helps them grow tall, so adding fertilizer or compost restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli nibii aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my farmland better for next season's maize?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does adding animal manure and dried leaves to my soil help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Manure and dry leaves decompose into organic matter, which acts like a sponge. It holds moisture deep in the dirt so plant roots can still drink during dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu lolo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp conditions. Pruning heavy branches lets sunlight and air dry out the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ni tsii lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: How can I tell if my cassava leaves are infected with cassava mosaic disease?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ emɔ ŋmei baai lɛ?

english: Infected cassava leaves look twisted, crumpled, and faded with yellowish-green patches. Using stem cuttings only from healthy plants prevents the disease from starting in your new farm.
ga: Cassava baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etsake, ekpɔtɔ, ni egbo kɛ ŋmɔŋ-eŋɔli he tsɔi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akaje shishi yɛ oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli.

english: This is often caused by bacteria in the soil that enter the roots and block water from moving up the stem. Rotating your field with non-vegetable crops like maize helps starve those soil bacteria.
ga: Bei pii lɛ muawai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ nu gbɛ koni ekaya tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee aduawai, tamɔ ŋmãa tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas while the cocoa establishes root systems.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo feɔ shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo ko.

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss through evaporation. Keeping shade trees in the farm shelters the cocoa from harsh winds and keeps the soil cooler.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops much more than my mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awui babaoo fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak root systems that easily get overwhelmed by fast-growing weeds stealing their light and food. Once crops grow tall, their own leaves shade out weed growth.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ la kɛ niyenii. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baaha jwɛi ni eda lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water around the roots. Nitrogen acts like food for green leaf growth, and without enough of it, the crop cannot feed itself properly to produce a strong yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before they turn into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Peppers shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or inconsistent watering. When the plant feels too stressed by dry soil during flowering, it drops its blossoms to save water and protect itself.
ga: Peppers baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Beni tsei nuɔ he akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miigba amɛnaa tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tsei baagbee shi koni amɛhere nu ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the ground was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoon days, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw water from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to close its pores and conserve moisture, usually recovering when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread a plant virus. Controlling whiteflies early stops the virus from spreading and damaging your whole harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei amli Early Whitefly Control Ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder after keeping them for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils burrow inside dry maize to eat and lay eggs. If the grain is not dried completely before storage or treated properly, weevils multiply quickly and consume the inside of the cobs.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛye nii ni amɛwo ŋmeii. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Weevils lɛ faa oya ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the tender cocoa trees can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tso bibioo ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing thin and weak when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The maize stretches thin and tall to reach light instead of building a thick stalk and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abele lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ kakadaŋŋ koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso nɛ e hyi.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer in the soil. Because weeds are often hardier, they steal those essential nutrients away from your crops, leaving them weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ kaa fe tsutsu lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nakai niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. ha egbɔjɔ

english: Why should I alternate planting maize with beans or groundnuts in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every season. Beans and groundnuts add vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally, which refreshes the earth for your next maize crop.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Beans kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are starving for nitrogen, which acts like food for plant leaves, or that water is sitting in the soil and drowning the roots. Adding a bit of NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure can help them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei ahe baai Aloo nu ko yɛ ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fioo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cassava alongside groundnuts help keep my land good for farming?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ni akɛfataa ŋmeii ahe lɛ adumɔ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like cassava and keeps the soil fertile for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmei, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously sucks out the exact same nutrients from the dirt every season and lets crop-specific bugs build up in the soil. Rotating with different crops lets the soil recover and starves out pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. kɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe kooloi abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi ni ejieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Check your plants early in the morning before the sun gets too hot; if the leaves are already curling or drooping, the soil is too dry. You can also dig a few inches into the dirt—if it feels dry and dusty, your crops need watering immediately.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli leebi dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe momo loo amɛmiigbee shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ inchi fioo komɛi hu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji enu he akɛ egbi ni eyɛ sũ lɛ Ehe miihia ni awo otso lɛ nɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What causes the roots of my crops to rot and turn soft and smelly after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Root rot happens when excess water sits in the soil without draining away, which suffocates the roots and encourages soil diseases to attack. Building raised soil beds or digging simple drainage gutters helps rain water flow away from the roots.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ saatso ni awó nɔ ni afee loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni aaafo lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my farm heavily right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars and other bugs multiply quickly when warm weather follows rain because crops sprout fresh, tender leaves for them to eat. Checking under leaves regularly lets you catch tiny eggs early before a full infestation takes over.
ga: Kplukai kɛ kooloi krokomɛi Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji nugbɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ. ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo ŋmeii heei kɛ baai bibii ni amɛbaaye. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ ŋmeii bibii. Na kɛjɛ shishijee dani hela lɛ je shishi

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up with tiny insects hiding underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni kooloi bibii komɛi kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites that drink the sap from the underside of leaves. Spraying a mild mixture of neem oil or soapy water under the leaves knocks them off and protects the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie nɔ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashwie shi ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus in the soil. Keeping soil moisture steady and feeding the plants properly helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oookwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni sa ni okɛhaa otsei lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if I do not clear them early in the season?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your young crops the space and food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni mli wa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops shade each other and waste energy stretching upwards to reach the sun instead of developing thick stems and good fruit. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each one gets enough light and air.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni shɛɔ hulu la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii kpakpahi. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa.

english: Why is the spray I use for plant diseases no longer killing the disease on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ tsei ahe helai anɔ lɛ egbeee helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you use the same chemical spray over and over again, the disease-causing germs adapt and become resistant to it. To fix this, you need to rotate and switch to different types of farm medicines.
ga: Beni okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ. Helai ni kɛ hela baa lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ mɛi ni nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ. Bɔni afee ni otsu naagba nɛɛ he nii Ehe baahia ni otsake ni otsake kɛya ŋmɔ mli tsofai srɔtoi anɔ.

english: What causes a plant disease to keep coming back to my farm every few years even after I treat it?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ahe helai yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Afii enyɔ komɛi nɛ beni mitsa po sɛɛ.

english: Disease spores can hide in the soil, weeds, or old fallen leaves. When weather conditions become favorable again every few years, the disease wakes up and attacks the crops once more.
ga: Helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ, jwɛi, loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bafee fɛo ekoŋŋ daa afii fioo komɛi lɛ, hela lɛ teɔ shi ni etutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does a crop disease refuse to go away even after I apply the medicine recommended to me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso hela lɛ sɛɛ efooo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ mikɛtsu nii lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: A disease may persist if the medicine is applied at the wrong time, mixed incorrectly, or if the disease has developed resistance to that specific chemical.
ga: Hela lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ kɛji akɛ aye tsofa lɛ yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ejaaa loo kɛji hela lɛ bafee nɔ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ nakai tsofa pɔtɛɛ lɛ

english: Is it safe for me to keep spraying the exact same chemical on my crops every season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa be?

english: No, using the same chemical repeatedly weakens its effectiveness over time and can build up harmful chemical residues in your farmland soil.
ga: Dabi Tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ Ebaaha bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eshwɛ yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba.

english: Can using too many farming chemicals spoil my farmland soil over time?
ga: Ani okwaayeli mli tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, continuous heavy use of chemical sprays can kill beneficial soil organisms, increase soil acidity, and make the soil less fertile over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ehaa sũ lɛ mli acid yaa hiɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli

english: How do I know if my soil has reached a point where it needs special care due to past chemical use?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he ko ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsofai ni akɛtsu nii be ko ni eho lɛ hewɔ?

english: If your crops grow weakly even after applying standard chemical sprays, or if the soil becomes hard and dry, it shows the soil's natural health has been broken down by chemical buildup.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ sɛɛ po. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai ni ebua shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to catch diseases more easily as my farm gets older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni helai baanyɛ aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli oya be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As a farm ages, pests and diseases accumulate in the environment, and the soil loses its natural nutrients, making older crops weaker and more vulnerable to sickness.
ga: Beni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shihilɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Enɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe feɔ oya kɛha helai.

english: Does a young cocoa tree need the same amount of fertilizer as an old cocoa tree?
ga: Ani cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: No, young cocoa trees need smaller amounts of fertilizer focused on root and leaf growth, while mature, pod-producing cocoa trees require larger amounts of fertilizer to support fruit production.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Cocoa tsei ni woɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ biɔ ŋmeii babaoo koni eye ebua ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does the amount of fertilizer I give to my cocoa trees change as the trees grow older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛhaa mi-kokoo tso lɛ tsakeɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow bigger, their root systems expand and they produce more heavy pods, which means they consume more nutrients from the soil and need higher fertilizer amounts.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: At what stage in my cocoa tree's life should I start increasing the fertilizer I give to it?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛfatamɔ he yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shihilɛ mli?

english: You should start increasing fertilizer application when the cocoa trees enter their full bearing age—usually around 3 to 5 years old—when they begin producing flowers and pods heavily.
ga: Esa akɛ oje ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shishi kɛji kookoo tso lɛ eshɛ afii ni ekɛbaawo yibii lɛ he. Ebaa beni eye afii 3 kɛyashi 5 beni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo feemɔ.

english: Why does my cassava crop still survive and grow even when there is no rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni eda eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko be kakadaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Cassava is a naturally drought-tolerant crop. Its deep root system allows it to store water and nutrients underground, and it can drop its leaves during dry spells to conserve water until rain returns.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa enyɛɔ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshɛrɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwie shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does rice need so much more water to grow compared to my maize or cassava crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ fe ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice naturally thrives in wetland environments. It requires constant soil moisture or shallow flooding during its growth stages to control weeds, transport nutrients, and support its specialized root system.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ebiɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo nu aba mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ koni enyɛ eye jwɛi lɛ anɔ. ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa eshishifãi krɛdɛɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants take much longer to produce food than my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ niyenii fe mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ?

english: Maize is a fast-growing annual grain crop that completes its life cycle in 3 to 4 months. Plantain is a perennial crop that needs 9 to 12 months to build a thick pseudostem and broad canopy before flowering and growing fruit bunches.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmaa ni yaa hiɛ oya daa afi. Egbeɔ ewala be lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli. Plantains ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛfeɔ pseudostems ni mli tse kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ aduawai akui.

english: Why does my maize crop turn yellow and stop growing when rainwater collects and stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?
