english: Maize roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe and absorb nutrients. When water sits on the field, it suffocates the roots, preventing nitrogen uptake and causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. etsĩɔ nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ naa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during strong wind storms compared to my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli kɛ akɛto mi yucca tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy top growth with broad leaves that catch the wind like a sail, whereas cassava stays lower to the ground and anchors itself with deep root tubers.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋwɛi dalɛ ni mli wa. Eyɛ tsɔne ni mli kwɔ ni mɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛlɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe lɛ.

english: How come I have to buy and apply fertilizer every season for my maize, but my cassava keeps growing without much fertilizing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa daa be lɛ? Shi ani ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ ni ŋmei babaoo bɛ mli?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that quickly extracts nitrogen and minerals from the topsoil during its short growth cycle, whereas cassava has an expansive root system that efficiently extracts nutrients from deep or poor soil over a longer period.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛ mineral kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya yɛ be kukuoo ni ekɛdaa lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava in poor, tired soil where my maize crops fail to produce well?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni nɔ efite yɛ he ni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cassava is very tolerant of poor or low-nutrient soils. It can produce decent yields where crops like maize fail, though adding organic matter or fertilizer will still increase your cassava harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei baanyɛ akpɛlɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kwraa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eha yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ bei ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa nyɛɛɛ aba mli lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha o-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ lolo moŋ.

english: Why do birds attack and destroy my rice farm so much more than my plantain or cassava fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ babaoo fe mi dumɔwui loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice forms small, exposed grain heads at the very top of the plant that are soft and easy for birds to eat. Cassava grows underground as hidden tubers, and plantains have thick outer peels that protect the fruit from birds.
ga: Omɔ baaná dumɔwui bibii. ejeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ Amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ oya. Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Ni plantain lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli tse ni buɔ aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ okpoi ahe.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural survival behavior to prevent water from evaporating into the air. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts new green leaves from its stems.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala su ni kɔɔ ŋmei he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli oya kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: What makes lowland fields better suited for planting rice than upland dry fields?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni egbi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland fields naturally hold and retain water from rain or nearby rivers, creating the wet, swampy soil conditions that rice plants require to grow efficiently and suppress weed growth.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ buaa nu naa kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ loo faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa, ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much rain early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away nitrogen from the topsoil and waterlogs the ground, cutting off oxygen to the roots and preventing the maize from absorbing the nutrients needed to stay green.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli Ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before planting my cassava instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu ŋmei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often wets only the top surface of the soil and is followed by hot dry spells that dry out the ground, which will scorch and kill newly planted cassava stem cuttings before they can grow deep roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Ni nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji hulutsoo be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ. Enɛ baashã ni egbe ŋmei niji ni adu ehee lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing fruit when it gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries up the pollen inside the blossoms, causing the tomato plant to drop its flowers to save energy rather than produce weak fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin but yield very little food when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, forcing the plants to stretch upward for sunlight instead of spending energy making fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ akpã amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui.

english: Why is it good to plant beans in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen and leaves the soil tired, while bean plants naturally take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, restoring fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked even though the leaves on top look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, well-drained soil to expand downward; if the soil beneath the surface is hard, stony, or clay-heavy, the tubers cannot spread out properly even if the vine looks good.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shikpɔŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ Bulbs lɛ hu nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and spoil right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded farms where air cannot flow freely between trees to dry off moisture.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Biɛ ji he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and look small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni etamɔ nɔ ni efee bibioo ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies feeding on young sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack and eat my young maize stalks from the inside during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm multiply quickly in warm, dry weather and burrow into the central funnel of the maize stalk to hide from the sun and heat while feeding on soft inner leaves.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ faa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi mli. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo hulu kɛ dɔlɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots rot in the ground if I do not harvest them before heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting in the soil during heavy rains starves the tubers of air underground, causing naturally occurring soil bacteria and fungi to rot the water-soaked cassava roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ yitsei lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni akɛwo nu mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia to block excessive heat and keep moisture in the soil, the leaves overheat, lose water quickly, and dry up.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ bɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo gliricidia atsu nii ni akɛtsi dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Baai lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egbiɔ

english: This yellowing pattern is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and fast growth, so when the soil lacks it, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves, but produces tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or water early on, it puts all its energy into growing stem and leaf biomass above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ mra lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmeii, kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit mainly due to extreme heat, uneven watering, or poor pollination. When temperatures get too hot, the pollen becomes sterile, causing the plant to shed the blossom to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii, titri lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen lɛ ji sterile. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How does mixing animal manure into my soil help my crops survive dry spells better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Animal manure adds organic matter to the soil, which acts like a sponge. It helps the soil hold on to rainwater much longer during dry periods while slowly releasing nutrients for crop roots.
ga: Manure kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, Slowly jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli

english: Why do I find small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ.

english: This is damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the tight growing center of the maize plant where it eats tender leaves and leaves behind its waste, which looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo lɛ ateŋ. Eyeɔ baai bibii ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in a field where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpaa ŋmei tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them naturally replenishes the soil fertility that heavy-feeding crops like maize exhausted.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ akwɛmɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kooloi aniyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on leaf sap, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. The feeding causes the leaf tissue to pucker and deform as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Niyenii haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne ko yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural survival mechanism to conserve water. By curling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to the hot sun and dry wind, slowing down the rate at which water evaporates from its tissue.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ amɛbɔle amɛhe lɛ, hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe yɛ he ko ni faaa kwraa. Enɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ fãji lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi blɛoo.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the developing crops compete with one another for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and soil water. This results in thin, weak stalks, low yields, and restricted airflow that encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni miiya hiɛ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ oya ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas gives the soil time to recover and naturally restores nutrients.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Abele tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ ehe baawo mli ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ ebɔɔ nii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant groundnuts or cowpeas to improve the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that nitrogen remains in the earth to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bigger when I give the vines tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa waa kɛ́ miha amɛ wain tso kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the soil, allowing them to capture more sunlight and preventing leaves from rotting on damp ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the small suckers around my main plantain tree instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni bɔle plantain wulu lɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete for the same food and water in the soil. Keeping only the main tree and one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ atsa tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off before turning into fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause pepper plants stress, forcing them to shed flowers to save energy and stay alive. Regular watering and providing light shade during very hot spells help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ pepper tsei lɛ. Anyɛɔ enɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ehi shi. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do young cocoa trees require shade trees like plantains planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the ground instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings can rot if planted upside down, if taken from old or diseased stems, or if planted in waterlogged soil. Planting healthy stems upright or at a slant with the growth buds facing up helps them sprout quickly.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛji akɛ atsɔ hiɛ akwɛ nɔ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ loo ni atsɔ hiɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell that dries out the topsoil. Waiting until the rains are regular ensures tender seedlings have continuous moisture to survive and establish roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛtswa shishifãi.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding and feeding inside the leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft inner leaves of maize to feed and hide from birds. Checking plants early and placing ash, neem leaf extract, or targeted pesticides into the plant center helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe. Nibii ni akwɛɔ tsei amli mra ni akɛ sũ lɛ awo mli Neem tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ mli Aloo, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why would an agricultural officer tell me to cut down my crops when they get sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mifo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: When a severe disease infects your crops, keeping them on the field allows the sickness to spread to healthy plants nearby. Clearing infected crops stops the disease from destroying your entire farm or spreading to neighboring farms.
ga: Beni hela ko ni naa wa gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii amli Tsei ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, no haaa hela lɛ akpata oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ loo egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli.

english: Why am I getting a much lower harvest from my farm this season even though I did not change my farming routine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni minine shɛɛɛ nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ fioo kwraa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsakeko bɔ ni mifeɔ okwaayeli lɛ moŋ?

english: When diseases enter a farm, they steal energy and nutrients from plants. This prevents crops from developing properly, causing fruits or pods to fail to grow, which drastically reduces your total harvest.
ga: Kɛ hela bote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ejuɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai loo pod lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada. Enɛ baaha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi waa.

english: How does a crop disease move from one part of my farm to the rest of my crops?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ amli?

english: Diseases can easily spread across a farm through wind, rain splashing water, contaminated farm tools, or insects moving from sick plants to healthy ones.
ga: Helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ oya. nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi Okwaafoi adɛŋdadei ni mli ewo muji loo kooloi ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I know if a disease on my farm is bad enough that I need to clear the land instead of treating it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kwraa bɔ ni ehe baahia ni ajie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni matsa lɛ?

english: If a disease has spread widely, caused a severe decline in crop quality, and drastically reduced your yield, chemical treatment is often ineffective and expensive, making clearing the land the best option.
ga: Kɛji hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ Ekɛ tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni baa shi waa baa. Ni enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsaa helai lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛjara hu wa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why is the produce I harvest looking different and lower in quality than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto ni ebɛ sɛɛnamɔ fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Plant diseases disrupt how a crop grows and feeds itself. This often leads to damaged, smaller, discolored, or deformed produce that lacks the original quality you used to see.
ga: Tso helai haaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ada ni ena niyenii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa nibii ni efite, ni feɔ bibii, ni amɛhe su tsakeɔ, loo ni efite ni bɛ shishijee su ni ona tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do buyers pay me lower prices for my crops when disease affects my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi jara ni baa shi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni hela miigba miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Buyers offer less money for diseased crops because damaged or poor-quality produce spoils faster, tastes worse, and yields less usable material for cooking, selling, or processing.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ shika fioo pɛ haa tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni efite loo nɔ ni ehiii lɛ baafite oya, eŋɔɔɔ waa, ni ebaafee nɔ ko fioo kɛha nihoomɔ, jarayeli, loo nitsumɔ.

english: How does the age of my farm trees affect the total harvest I get each year?
ga: Te afii ni tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eye lɛ saa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ daa afi lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: As crop trees grow very old—such as over thirty years old—their capacity to absorb nutrients and produce fruits naturally slows down, leading to a permanent drop in your annual yield.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ daraa (akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, amɛye fe afii 30 lɛ), nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ daa afi lɛ baa shi daa.

english: Is it normal for a farm that is over thirty years old to stop producing as much as it used to?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni sa akɛ ŋmɔji ni eye fe afii nyɔŋmai etɛ lɛ baakpa nibii babaoo ni amɛfeɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Yes, it is completely normal. Just like humans, plants weaken as they grow old, making them produce fewer crops and become more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa. tamɔ adesai nɔŋŋ Tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ faaa, ni helai hu baa.

english: Why should I clear and replant my old farm if the trees are still giving me a small harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ lɛ? Be mli ni tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Keeping very old trees costs time and labor for very little return. Clearing the old farm and planting young, healthy seedlings will eventually give you much higher yields and better quality crops.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ heɔ be kɛ nitsumɔ ni nɔ ko fioo pɛ anáa kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmɔji momoi lɛ amli ni odu dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii babaoo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best thing to do when my farm yield drops because the crops are too old?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mi okwaayeli nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ba shi ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔ tsɔ?

english: When crops become too old to yield well, the best solution is to clear the land, let the soil prepare, and replant with fresh, disease-resistant seedlings.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ asaa ehe. ni okɛ dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and thin bark that burn easily in direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade plants like plantains to act as living umbrellas, providing moisture and shade while the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam plants high off the ground with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei aha mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaves from rotting and helps them catch light easily.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ebaaha la ashɛ amɛhe oya.

english: When maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, the plant starves for food. It moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ. Ejieɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help my soil for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and leaves decompose, that nitrogen stays in the soil to fertilize the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni baai lɛ fite lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plant leaves have ragged holes eaten through them with dirt inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli eyi kɛ muji yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the young shoot of the maize plant during the day, eating the soft leaf tissue and leaving behind tiny piles of waste that look like dirt.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii amli fãji ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi bibii ni abua naa. ni tamɔ muji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests. This makes the leaf grow unevenly and curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe tsɔnei lɛ anɔ Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Black Pod is caused by a soil fungus that thrives in damp, cold, and dark conditions. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from the soil onto the pods, causing black rot that spreads quickly across the farm if pods are not removed.
ga: Sũ mli ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ duŋ baa ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hela ko ni ji black rot baa ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya kɛji ajieee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground if I leave them buried during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots. Without air, soil bacteria and fungi attack the tubers, causing them to turn soft, watery, and rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Bacteria kɛ fungi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo, amɛfeɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or the soil dries out completely, tomato plants drop their flowers to save water and energy so the plant itself does not die.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. koni tso lɛ akagbo

english: Why shouldn't I allow too many suckers to grow around one main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he lɛ?

english: Every new sucker feeds on the same water and nutrients in the ground as the main tree. Allowing too many suckers causes them to fight for food, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers heei fɛɛ yeɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow starting from the leaf tips in a V-shape, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. The maize plant is pulling nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni eje shishi kɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni tamɔ V lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei miigba nitrogen kɛmiijɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when we get heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil without proper drainage, it suffocates the roots and creates ideal conditions for soil-borne fungus to cause root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni efee shihilɛi ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers instead of turning them into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers if they experience drought stress, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack from pests like mirids. Keeping the field shaded and watered helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛna hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuamɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha tsei lɛ ni awo amɛ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses, or by severe dry heat during the Harmattan season which stresses the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni mli egbi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli ni haa tsei lɛ haoɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does removing extra suckers from my plantain plant help me get bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi plantains lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmeii wuji?

english: When a plantain tree produces too many suckers, they all fight for the same soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the main plant and one strong successor, concentrating food into producing large fruits.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui wo ŋmeii babaoo Amɛbaawuu koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso titri lɛ kɛ esɛɛyelɔ kome ni he wa pɛ eshwɛɔ. Niyenii nɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ koni akɛfee aduawai wuji.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy to build large tubers underground while keeping leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly collapse and die right at the soil line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbee shi trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal condition called damping-off, which happens when the seedbed stays too wet and warm. The fungus attacks the weak stem at ground level and cuts off water flow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping out, ni baa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ asa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ lolo. Fuji lɛ tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I leave dry leaves or plant cover on my farm soil during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Mulching shades the ground from direct sun rays, keeping the soil cool and retaining moisture. As the plant material breaks down, it adds organic manure back into your farm soil.
ga: Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Kɛji tsei ahe nibii fite Ebaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he ekoŋŋ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why is water so important for my maize crop right when the tassels start showing at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa mi ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miije shishi ejie ehe kpo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Tasseling is the pollination stage when maize grains are formed. If the plant lacks water during these few days, the pollen dies and you end up with empty cobs missing kernels.
ga: Brushing ji bɔ ni afeɔ pollination kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ je kpo. Kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ gbii fioo nɛɛ amli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gboɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Planting seeds too closely forces them to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and plant nutrients. Giving each crop correct spacing allows roots and leaves to spread and grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young leaves at the top, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before they can produce any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani enyɛ ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get too hot, lack water, or have too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant gets stressed, it sheds its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ, nu faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo amɛyɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ tsei miihao lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to breathe in the soil. When the land stays flooded for too long, water displaces the soil air, causing the roots to drown, die, and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nu afua lɛ mli nui lɛ damɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow on land where the dark topsoil was scraped off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The dark topsoil contains almost all the natural manure and food crops need. When topsoil is removed, you are left with deep subsoil, which is packed hard, lacks nutrients, and cannot hold air or water properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Beni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ Oshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will my vegetable crops grow normally if I use muddy river water from areas near mining sites to water them?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa kɛji mikɛ nu wo faa ko ni mli ewo muji ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsaa shika tsuru lɛ yɛ lɛ mli?

english: Heavy mud in water blocks plants from taking in nutrients through their roots, and toxic metals from mining can poison the crop roots, causing stunted growth or complete crop failure.
ga: Muji ni tsii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni dade ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni jɛɔ shika tsuru tsaa mli lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei shishifãi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ edaaa kwraa loo ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Why do cowpea plants make my soil better for next season's maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tsei baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil microbes to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, leaving natural plant food in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Large shade trees protect seedlings from burning up, lower the surrounding temperature, and help the soil retain moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la he. Ha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and thin with very little fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When tomatoes are planted too close, they shade each other out and compete for limited sunlight, making them stretch tall and weak instead of spending energy making heavy fruit.
ga: Beni Adu Tomato He ni Ebɛŋkɛ Tsɔ Tomato haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛjie yibii ni tsii kpo lɛ

english: Why does elephant grass invade and spread through my crop fields so quickly after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shwuɔ jwɛi lɛ boteɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Elephant grass has deep root systems that store extra food energy underground, allowing it to shoot up faster than sown seeds as soon as rain falls.
ga: Shɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kroko toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui ni adu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the growing tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the light and keeps them off the hot, damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ la lɛ hiɛ, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants grow strong and green leaves. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the plants regain their green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ baai ni wa, ni eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my crops growing very short and slow even though I planted them at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa kuku ni amɛyaa hiɛ blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ?

english: Crops grow slowly when the soil lacks basic plant food (nutrients) or when weeds are stealing their food and water. Adding farm inputs like NPK fertilizer and keeping the land clear of weeds gives plants the energy to grow tall and healthy.
ga: Tsei daa fiofio kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa waa (nutrients) loo kɛ́ jwɛi ju niyenii kɛ nu. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo kɛ he ni jwɛi bɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits on the farm for too long, it drowns the roots and encourages diseases that rot the tubers, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain water away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo helai ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so quickly just a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast when exposed directly to the hot sun. Covering the ground around your crops with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts as a blanket that traps soil moisture and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji hulu la shɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni akɛhaa he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Nibii ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt in the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the plant and feeds on young leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide early in the morning or late evening targets these pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread diseases between plants, or by extreme heat and lack of water. Protecting plants with insecticides and keeping the soil evenly wet helps prevent leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa mli Tsei ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ abuɔ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ feɔ ekome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool environment young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha wala. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kooloi bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my plantain trees growing thin and falling over whenever strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ ni egbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight and grow tall, weak stems to reach the light. Proper spacing (about 3 meters apart) allows each plant to build a thick stem and strong roots that can hold against wind.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Plantains kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋshii mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ koni amɛná la. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ (aaafee mitai 3) haa tso fɛɛ tso shishifã ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or dry soil, which stresses the plant. Watering your crop regularly during dry spells and mulching the soil helps the plant hold onto its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ye amɛnɔ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my planted yam seeds take so long to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go through a sleeping phase called dormancy after harvest during which they will not grow. They only sprout once this rest period is complete, but storing seed tubers in a cool, shaded place helps them sprout predictably.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. ni kɛ bɛ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛ kɛji hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee. Shi kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bɔ ni atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantain or cassava during their first few years to retain moisture and survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains loo yucca mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause tomato plants to drop their blossoms to save energy. Providing shade netting or watering consistently during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ shade netting loo nu ha amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellowing along the center of lower maize leaves means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow green leaves and healthy cobs.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpea or groundnut on the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnut capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps the land fertile without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ awo mli.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my maize so it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni ekafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil when the maize is at knee-height, as the roots are active enough to absorb the nutrients before heavy rain can wash them away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahoɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from under the leaves, which causes the plant leaves to warp and stunts its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa edaaa.

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when water stays trapped around them in flat, compacted soil. Planting them on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when they start bearing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep in the ground, making the heavy plant top-heavy. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden fork or bamboo pole prevents the wind from knocking it over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ náa tsiimɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli loo ŋmei tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Does my yam plant really need a tall stake to climb, or can I let the vines crawl on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato tso lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛkwɔ. Aloo manyɛ mashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to swell and produce large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfuu ni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even if I used good seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil water, and nutrients away from your plants, leaving the crop starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunshine. They require shade trees or plantains nearby to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil cool while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ anaa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which maize feeds on heavily to grow tall and green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. He ni akɛ ŋmãa niyenii babaoo haa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɔmpost loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ su kpakpa baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need well-draining soil to breathe. When water sits around the roots for too long, fungal rot sets in and destroys the tubers before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Rot fungus lɛ boteɔ mli ni efiteɔ bulbs lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Why are my pepper plant flowers dropping off before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop without setting fruit when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of visits from pollinating insects like bees.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to capture sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground prevents diseases and allows the plant to produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are there ragged holes inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu ni etse amɛhe lɛ? yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: Ragged holes in the center whorl of maize are a key sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the plant leaves during the day to feed.
ga: Bu ko ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmãa tso ko teŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛyatao niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot support heavy bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo or wooden prop keeps the tree upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ aye abua ŋmɔlɔ ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled, twisted leaves on tomato plants are usually caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit leaf-curl viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni kɛ baai ni etsiɔ helai lɛ yaa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni etsilɛɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean leaves droop down in the hot afternoon but stand up straight again by evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bean plants temporarily wilt during the hottest parts of the day to reduce water loss through their leaves. Once the temperature drops in the evening, they recover their posture.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe.

english: Why are the green leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Healthy cocoa leaves need key nutrients like nitrogen to stay green and manufacture food for the tree. Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nutrients, or the tree is getting too much harsh sun or standing water.
ga: Cocoa baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo niyenii aha tso lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tso lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ loo nu ni ekã shi.

english: Why is it bad for me to strip off too many green leaves from my cocoa tree at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafo cacao tso ko baai eŋɔli babaoo shikome lɛ?

english: Green leaves act as the food factory for the cocoa tree. Removing too many green leaves at once starves the tree, stops it from building energy, and weakens pod production.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ cacao tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. Kɛ́ ajie baai eŋɔli babaoo shikome lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Kpaa hewalɛ feemɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ pod feemɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like shade trees or plantains around them to shield their leaves until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la fɛɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ hulutsoo tsei loo plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa

english: How does keeping the leaves on my cocoa tree healthy help me get bigger cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ akwɛ kookoo baai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Healthy green leaves catch sunlight and turn it into energy that feeds the growing pods. The more healthy green leaves a tree keeps, the more food it sends to make larger, heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ heɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ hewalɛ. Babaoo ni tso lɛ yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ, babaoo ni ebaaná hewalɛ. Niyenii babaoo ni akɛmajeɔ koni akɛfee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni tsii lɛ.

english: What causes black spots to spread across the leaves of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Black spots on cocoa leaves are usually caused by fungal leaf diseases. Fungi thrive when the farm is too wet, overly shady, or lacks good airflow between the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ kookoo baai lɛ anɔ. Fungus lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli edɔ tsɔ. ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ tsei ateŋ

english: Can a leaf disease on one of my cocoa trees spread to the rest of my farm?
ga: Ani baa hela ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ eko nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, fungal and viral leaf diseases spread easily from tree to tree through wind, rain splashes, or contaminated pruning tools if infected leaves are left unchecked.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baa mli helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ oya. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ loo nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni mli ewo muji Kɛji akɛ ashi baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ,

english: When is the right time for me to apply crop medicine or spray to protect my cocoa leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ atsu nii koni mikɛbu mi-kookoo baai lɛ ahe?

english: It is best to apply preventive sprays early in the wet season before pests and fungal spores build up, rather than rushing to spray after the leaves are already heavily damaged.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baatsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli, dani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooya oya ni okɛshwie nɔ beni baai lɛ efite waa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I make my own natural spray using plant leaves to protect my crops from pests?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ahe baai afee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛbuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Yes, crushed plant extracts such as neem leaf mixtures can act as natural remedies to repel pests without harming your cocoa leaves when extracted and applied correctly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli nibii ni atswa tamɔ neem baa ni akɛfutu mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eyeee o-cocoa baa lɛ awui kɛji ajie ni akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take so much time to produce pods even when the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Cocoa trees spend their first few years building strong roots and branches. Even with healthy green leaves, the tree needs time to mature before it has enough stored energy to produce flowers and pods.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani etswaa shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa. Eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa po. Tsei hu he miihia be dani amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: How can I safely share a crop treatment method I tested on my farm with other farmers in my village?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ agba ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikaa mikwɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe sane shweshweeshwe?

english: It is best to test any treatment on a small test area first and have an extension officer inspect the results before sharing the practice with neighbors so everyone avoids crop damage.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka tsofafeemɔ lɛ okwɛ yɛ kaa he bibioo ko klɛŋklɛŋ ni oha nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ akwɛ nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ mli dani okɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ agba nifeemɔ lɛ he sane. Bɔni afee ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ anyɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees create a cooler climate, retain soil moisture, and shield fragile cocoa leaves from burning while the young trees build strong root systems.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli jɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni obu kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. Beni tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa baa lɛ.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus damages the leaves, preventing the plant from making food through sunlight and drastically reducing root yields.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ fiteɔ baai, ni ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ayibiiwoo baa shi waa.

english: Yellow lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant steals remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to keep growing new leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi juɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with tall, weak stems that fall over easily and produce very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shi oya ni amɛwoɔ tsei bibii waa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Without steady moisture and moderate temperatures, the plant sacrifices flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛfɔfɔi baasha afɔle koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up like tubes during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a natural survival defense. By curling its leaves, the plant hides part of its leaf surface from direct sunlight to stop water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ amɛwala he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ebaa lɛ ekomɛi teeɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches small even though rain is falling heavily on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ?

english: When too many young suckers grow around a main plantain stem, they steal food and nutrients from the mother stem. Pruning away extra suckers ensures the primary stem gets all the nourishment needed to grow large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are fully grown and ready to be harvested from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up completely. This signals that the vine has stopped growing and has transferred all its stored energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are my vegetable seeds failing to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep where air cannot reach them, if the soil dries out, or if the ground is so waterlogged that the seeds rot before they can push out shoots.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu aahu akɛ dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani anyɛɔ ashwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjeɔ kpo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important food nutrient for growing plants. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea around the base helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ni miida lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant beans or groundnuts on my land after I finish harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni migbe miŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but leguminous crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil naturally. Planting them restores the soil's strength for your next crop.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Which way should I point cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei nine lɛ atsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should always plant cassava stems with the small raised buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow properly, leading to very low tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ odu cassava tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tsoi lɛ baawa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the dead weeds and bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys the rich, natural food in the topsoil and kills useful earthworms. Leaving cleared weeds to rot back into the land feeds the soil and helps it hold water during dry periods.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni atsuu he lɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die if I remove all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains next to them protects the young cocoa from heat and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaabu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he. ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to build big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up off the damp ground so leaves get full sun and don't rot from moisture.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ wain tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkafite kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry suddenly. Water your tomatoes regularly at the roots early in the morning so the plant stays cool enough to hold its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ trukaa. Okɛ nu awo o-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ daa leebi koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little cups during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the pepper plant's natural defense to protect itself from losing water in intense heat. Providing mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and reduces this stress.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni tsiɔ pepper tso lɛ naa koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why are caterpillars eating deep holes into the central leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye bu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by small moths. Catching them early and applying approved local treatments like neem oil or recommended insecticides protects the growing point of the maize.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ he.

english: Why is my harvested maize turning black and moldy inside my storage barn?
