ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots when it is put into storage while still wet inside. Drying your harvested corn under the sun until the grains are very hard stops mold and insects from ruining your crop in storage.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ emli. Abɛi ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa waa. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clean my seeds before planting them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsumɔ dumɔwui amli dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cleaning seeds removes dirt, weed seeds, and diseased or damaged grains. Clean seeds germinate much better and prevent crop diseases from spreading into your soil.
ga: Kɛ́ atsumɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ejieɔ muji, jwɛi dumɔwui, kɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ loo efite lɛ. Kɛ́ atsumɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kwraa, ni ebaatsi tsei ahe helai anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I stored after harvest are still good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ hi lolo akɛ adu?

english: Good seeds are clean, full, and free from insect holes or mold. You can test them by placing a few in a bowl of water; healthy seeds usually sink to the bottom while bad or damaged ones float.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai ahe tse, amɛmli eyi obɔ, ni kooloi abu loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛyaa shishi, yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni efite loo efite lɛ nyiɛɔ nu hiɛ.

english: How deep should I cover my seeds with soil when I plant them in the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ sũ aha midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: Seeds should be covered with a light layer of soil or sand, usually about twice their size in depth. This protects them from birds and direct heat while still allowing air and moisture to reach them so they can sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ sũ bibioo ko loo ŋã aha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ mli kwɔ aaafee shii enyɔ. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ okpoi kɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu shɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds directly into hard, dry ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Seeds struggle to settle and grow in hard soil because water cannot penetrate easily and young roots cannot push through. Loosening the soil before planting helps the seed absorb water and sprout quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ejaakɛ nu nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii hu nyɛŋ abote mli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why do some farmers mix sand into the soil when covering their seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋã futuɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ amɛmiiha amɛdumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing fine sand into the topsoil creates a soft, light cover that holds moisture well without becoming too hard, making it easy for young shoots to push through to the surface.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋã kpakpa futu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha efee bɔdɔɔ kɛ mlɛo. Amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in plastic nursery bags instead of planting them straight on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ plastic ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds in nursery bags allows you to give fragile seedlings special care, protecting them from heavy rain, pests, and strong sunshine until they grow big enough to survive in the main farm field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kotokui amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do seeds planted in nursery bags need to be watered more often than those in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ nu shii abɔ fe dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: The small amount of soil in a nursery bag dries out much faster under the hot sun, so regular watering is needed to keep the soil moist so the seed doesn't dry out and die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ bibioo ni yɔɔ grow bag mli lɛ baagbi oya kwraa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔse nu daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ gĩii ni amɛgboii.

english: How do I make sure the soil inside a seed nursery bag stays healthy for growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui kotokui lɛ amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dalɛ?

english: You should fill the bag with clean topsoil mixed with loose sand or dark compost so water drains easily and roots have enough space and nutrients to settle and grow.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni he tse awo kotoku lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋã ni mli tse loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ diŋ afutu mli. koni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi lɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛto amɛhe shi ni amɛdara.

english: What actually causes a seed to wake up and start growing after I plant it?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A seed wakes up when it absorbs moisture from wet soil, which triggers the young plant inside to expand, settle its roots into the earth, and shoot up toward the light.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi kɛ́ amɛjie nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ekɛ shishifãi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ oyaiyeli aya la lɛ he

english: Are there different types of seed growth that I should expect when my crops sprout?
ga: Ayɛ dumɔwui adalɛ henɔi srɔtoi. Ani esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Yes, crops sprout differently based on their seed type. Some crops, like beans, push their seed leaves above the ground, while others, like maize, keep the seed below the soil and send up a single green blade.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ dumɔwu henɔ lɛ naa. Nibii komɛi ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmei, tsiɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsuɔ baa eŋɔli kome kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: How do I know if the chemical I am spraying on my farm is actually working to kill pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbemɔ mli?

english: If the chemical is working, you will notice fewer live insects on leaves within a day or two, leaves will stop showing fresh bite marks, and your crops will start showing healthy green regrowth.
ga: Kɛji tsofa lɛ tsu nii Obaayɔse kooloi bibii ni hiɛ ka yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ fioo ko pɛ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli. Baai lɛ baakpa ŋmɔlɔ he okadii heei ni amɛjieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ. Ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpojiemɔ.

english: How often should I spray weedkiller on my farm so it doesn't harm my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Weedkiller should generally be sprayed before planting or when weeds are young, using selective crop-safe chemicals. Over-spraying can build resistance, damage the soil, and stunt crop growth.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ dani adu loo be mli ni jwɛi lɛ darako lolo. Tsofai ni ahala ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ni teɔ shi ewoɔ mɔ lɛ aba. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ etsĩ tsei adalɛ naa

english: Why do I see small caterpillars chewing my maize leaves early in the morning but not during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye ŋmãa tsei leebi shi minaaa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like fall armyworms hide in the soil or crop whorls during the hot sun to avoid heat, and come out early in the morning or at night when it is cool to feed on fresh foliage.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei akui amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Amɛjeɔ kpo leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni amɛbaye baai heei.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or that excessive water is choking the roots. Adding fertilizer or improving farm drainage helps leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and droopy in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. They droop to reduce sun exposure and conserve moisture, usually recovering by evening.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛgbeeɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Dark spots in rainy weather are usually caused by fungal diseases like Black Pod, which thrive in damp, cool air and spread through rain droplets splashing from soil to pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji, ni shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baa. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ

english: Will my cassava crops grow well if I plant them under big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Ani mi-cassava lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛdu tsei wuji ashishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava needs direct, full sunlight all day to create energy and swell its roots. Planting under dense shade trees causes long, weak stems and small tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni ená hewalɛ ni eha eshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii aba.

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce lower overall yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Tomatoes drop blossoms when temperatures get too high, when water supply is uneven, or when there are no bees or insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi bɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava put all its energy into growing tall stems and thick leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do I get new cocoa seedlings from the local Agric officer in my district?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná kookoo dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ mimaŋ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ?

english: Local agricultural extension officers (often referred to by farmers as the 'Agric woman' or officer) register farmers and distribute improved, disease-resistant cocoa seedlings during the early planting season to help farmers start or expand their farms.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi (Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ okwaafoi akɛ ‘kwaafoi yei’ loo onukpai.) Ŋmaa okwaafoi lɛ agbɛi awoɔ mli ni amɛjaa kookoo dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli. Koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛje amɛŋmɔji lɛ shishi loo amɛgbala mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa plants drying up and dying when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that easily burn under intense heat. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantain or shade trees during their first two years to protect them while their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛɔ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Should I clear away all the big trees on my farm before planting my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: You should not remove all trees. Leaving selected tall forest trees creates natural shade, retains soil moisture, protects young cocoa from strong winds, and keeps the soil cooler and more fertile.
ga: Esaaa akɛ ojieɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Koo mli tsei kakadaji ni ahala lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Buu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo

english: What is the best time of the year to put my cocoa seedlings into the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛ kookoo dumɔwui woɔ shikpɔŋ?

english: The best time to plant is at the beginning of the major rainy season, usually around May or June in Ghana. Planting in wet soil gives the young roots enough water to establish deeply before the dry Harmattan period arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ May loo June mli yɛ Ghana. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani Harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ baashɛ.

english: How do I keep my seedlings alive after picking them up from the extension officer before I put them in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ extension staff lɛ mli dani midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Keep the seedlings in a shaded, cool spot near a water source, water them daily to keep the soil bag moist, and plant them within a few days so their roots do not get root-bound or dry out.
ga: Ha dumɔwui lɛ ahi he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe. Nu daa gbi koni shikpɔŋ kotoku lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni odu yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli koni shishifãi lɛ akamɔ shi loo amɛkagbi.

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together causes them to compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin trees, high humidity that encourages fungal diseases like black pod, and lower yield per tree.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei komɛi ni mli edɔ waa Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni feɔ diŋ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ tso kome mli baa.

english: Can I grow cassava or plantain on the same farm plot where I just planted cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava loo plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo nɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping young cocoa with food crops like plantain or cassava is beneficial because it gives the farmer food and income while providing crucial temporary shade for the growing cocoa seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ni akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain loo cassava duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ shika. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni he hiaa haa kookoo dumɔwui ni miida lɛ.

english: If some of my old cocoa trees die, can I plant new seedlings in those empty spots?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei momo komɛi gboi Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, this practice is called 'gapping' or replanting. You can clear out the dead wood, prepare the soil with organic manure, and plant a fresh seedling to ensure your farm remains fully productive without leaving open spaces.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ‘gap’ loo dumɔ ekoŋŋ. Obaanyɛ ojie tsei ni egboi lɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. ni odu dumɔwui heei koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ ni oshiŋ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting before my new cocoa trees start giving me pods?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani kookoo ŋmeii heei aje shishi akwɛ̃?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties distributed by extension officers usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years of proper planting and care, compared to older traditional varieties which took 5 years or longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrid henɔi ni mɛi ni woɔ he hewalɛ lɛ woɔ he hewalɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the soil under my cocoa trees stay wet longer when I leave fallen leaves on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves act as a natural mulch layer. They cover the dirt to stop the sun from evaporating water directly from the soil, keep the roots cool, and eventually break down into rich organic fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, amɛgbalaɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen or when waterlogging prevents the roots from breathing. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed animal manure will help restore the dark green color and boost growth.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ haaa emu. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ fataa he. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni tsuɔ waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same plot after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize restores lost nutrients and improves soil fertility naturally for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Ejɛɔ adebɔɔ mli emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves and transmitting viruses. Controlling these insects early using neem oil or recommended sprays prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in humid, overcrowded, and overly shaded environments. Pruning heavy cocoa branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight and air move through the farm, keeping the pods dry and reducing rot.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi Ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Kookoo niji ni tsii ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa fitemɔ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks from insect pests like thrips. Ensuring consistent watering and protecting plants from extreme heat or pests helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ he miihia waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: It is best to keep only two or three suckers at different growth stages around one main plantain stem. Leaving too many suckers forces them to compete for water and nutrients, resulting in small bunches and thin stems.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi tso lɛ dalɛ fãi srɔtoi amli yɛ tso lɛ he. single main seedling stem Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii babaoo shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei niji bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Yam vines need to reach direct sunlight so their leaves can manufacture food efficiently to enlarge the underground tubers. Staking also lifts the foliage off the damp ground, reducing exposure to soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ baa shi

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when the heavy rain season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges creates channels for heavy rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots safe from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ kɛyaa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: When is the best time of day to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer is best applied in the cool early morning or late afternoon when the soil is moist. Applying fertilizer during the high heat of midday can burn the plant leaves, while applying right before a heavy downpour will wash the nutrients away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã. Yɛ be mli ni akɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaje mli.

english: Why do insects destroy my stored maize grains so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils multiply quickly in stored maize if the grain contains too much moisture. Thoroughly sun-drying the seeds until they are completely hard before storing them in airtight bags starves the pests of air and moisture.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo baa oya yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Agbiɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa dani akɛwoɔ vacuum kotokui amli. Ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo akabote mli.

english: Is it better to leave fertilizer on top of the soil or cover it with dirt near my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo maha nɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Covering fertilizer with dirt near the roots works best because sunlight and heat can destroy fertilizer left on top, while rain can wash it away before the plant gets to use it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: What is the best way to put fertilizer around my cassava plants so I do not destroy them?
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ he ŋmɔshi nibii Mɛni ji bɔni afee ni akafite lɛ?

english: Place the fertilizer in a small circle or line about a hand's width away from the main stem, then cover it lightly with soil so the roots can drink it safely without burning the plant.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo kooyigbɛ bibioo ko mli. aloo yɛ linei ni tamɔ nine nine mlilɛɛmɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni shãaa tso lɛ.

english: If I put extra fertilizer on my crops, will they grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Ani ebaada oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer can actually burn the roots of your crop and turn the leaves yellow, which harms the plant instead of helping it grow.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ yeɔ tso lɛ awui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni eda.

english: Should I clear all the weeds from my farm before I put fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you must weed first because weeds grow very fast and will steal the fertilizer and water away from your crops if they are left in the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before applying fertilizer to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mawo mi-ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so that crop roots can absorb it; placing fertilizer into dry soil can heat up and damage the crop roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ edɔ fe nine ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Why are some crops on my farm growing bigger while others in the same row stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu miiya hiɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai sɛɛkuu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, bibioo ko yɛ lolo

english: Crops grow unevenly when some roots get more water or nutrients than others, or when the soil in certain parts of the field is harder or poorer.
ga: Tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ shishifãi komɛi ná nu loo niyenii babaoo fe ekrokomɛi. aloo be mli ni sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ mli wa loo ebɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are actually taking in the fertilizer I put in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: When crops take in fertilizer, their leaves turn a darker, richer green color and you will see new green shoots growing within one to two weeks after rain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ awo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaai lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Ni obaana ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni miida yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: What happens to the fertilizer on my farm if heavy rain falls right after I apply it?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛwo mli sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash loose fertilizer off the surface of the soil into ditches, which is why burying the fertilizer slightly in the soil keeps it safe for your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya nubu lɛ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni ooofu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why does water collect on top of the soil in some parts of my farm instead of sinking in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu miibua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo lɛ?

english: Hard or clay soils prevent water from sinking in quickly, which means you need to loosen the soil with a hoe so water and nutrients can reach the roots.
ga: Sũ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ sũ haaa nu lɛ aya shi oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋtayaa atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii koni nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow even after I have already put food in the soil for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ niyenii fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he mihaa amɛ moŋ?

english: Leaves can turn yellow if heavy rain washed the plant food away, if the soil is too dry for roots to feed, or if water is sitting around the roots and suffocating them.
ga: Baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa jie tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye nii, Aloo kɛji nu damɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the growing tip of the maize plant and chew the leaves. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem leaf extract early in the morning can help control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early using neem oil or recommended sprays stops the spread and keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa tsei amli Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ehaa egbɛɔ eshwaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear my farmland without burning the cleared bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi ni ajie lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills beneficial soil organisms that help crops grow. Leaving cut bushes and grass to decompose on the soil acts as natural fertilizer and helps the ground hold moisture during dry periods.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ, ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei kɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an important food for crop growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizers like Urea or NPK at the right time supplies the nutrients needed to keep leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads fast during rainy and humid weather. Regularly removing affected pods from the tree and pruning extra branches to allow sunlight and air inside reduces the humidity that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa ni afee ŋmeii krokomɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ahi mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my tomato stems rotting and causing the whole plant to suddenly fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ trukaa ni ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil-borne fungi or bacteria when the ground stays too wet. Planting tomatoes on raised soil mounds and avoiding planting them in the exact same spot every year helps prevent these soil diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Tomato ni aaadu yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ ni aaadu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa nɛɛ anaa.

english: Spacing maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures every stem gets enough sunlight, water, and soil food to produce large cobs without crowding each other out.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 75 ni ŋmãa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 40, ni ehaa ŋmãa ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji aba ni ekɛ ehe ebɔko amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps flowers turn into fruits successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo beni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko edara kɛ́ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have thin, sensitive leaves that burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them provides moisture and shelter while the young cocoa plants establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ ehe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ wɔɔhe aba. yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry weather to conserve water and protect themselves from strong dry winds. Once the rains return, the stems will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and twist into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Twisted or curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Sprinkling or spraying the leaves with neem oil solution helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ loo okɛshwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for green growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni yɔɔ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does growing cowpeas before planting maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plant foliage decays after harvest, it leaves natural fertilizer in the soil for the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when rainwater sits on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When water stays pooled on the field for too long, it pushes out all the air, causing the roots to drown, decay, and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I lift them with wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso tso woɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking keeps yam leaves high off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the roots. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Tsi fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many side shoots compete with the mother plantain tree for soil nutrients and water. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Lateral shoots ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantains yeɔ akaŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when soil water changes drastically from very dry to soaked. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the bare dirt around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi baye ebua.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or straw, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating soil water, keeps plant roots cool, and smothers weeds before they can grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni hulu lɛ mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ akafee lasu. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if fertilizer is actually making a difference on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miifee tsakemɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When fertilizer works, you will notice the crop leaves turning from pale yellow to a deep, dark green within a few weeks, and the plant will grow taller with thicker stems.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii Obaayɔse akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli. ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaaná ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: What is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is moist. The rain helps dissolve the fertilizer so the tree roots can easily drink in the nutrients.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is tired and needs plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni aye tsei niyenii?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, have weak stems, yellowish leaves, or produce much smaller fruits than usual, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa lɛ Na ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii bibii fe nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer burn or kill my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo efite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, using too much fertilizer can burn the roots and cause the leaf edges to dry up and turn brown, which can harm or even kill the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ agbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ afee oshara loo egbe tso lɛ po.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your tree is starving for essential nutrients in the soil, such as nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by a lack of water, bad weather, poor soil nutrition, or because tiny insects have not pollinated the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii eshɛko fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lolo hewɔ?

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet, and overgrown farms where air cannot flow freely between trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct hot sun. Shade trees act like umbrellas to protect them from heat, keep the soil cool, and prevent moisture from drying up.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akagbi.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if I do not clear them regularly?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ daa?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil before your crops can get them, which starves your plants and slows down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa edaaa oya.

english: Why do I need to prune or trim branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or sick branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree, which prevents diseases and helps the tree focus its energy on growing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela mɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand intense direct sunlight. Big trees act as natural shade canopy, keeping the air cool and soil moist; removing them completely causes the delicate cocoa leaves to burn and dry out before roots establish.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ kwraa lɛ, ebaaha kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashã ni amɛgbi dani shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over at the roots even when there is no heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛyashɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: When plantain trees fall easily, tiny soil worms called nematodes or banana weevils are likely eating and destroying the underground roots. Treating planting suckers with hot water or using clean planting material strengthens the root base.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ gbee shi mlɛo lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ hu akɛ nematodes loo banana moths lɛ, bei pii lɛ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ tsu nii kɛtsa tsei ni adu lɛ loo akɛ nibii ni he tse ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shishitoo lɛ mli awa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of older maize leaves is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and grow heavy ears, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea will solve this.
ga: Abɛi ni egbɔ lɛ ahe fãji titrii lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ toi ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall with lots of dark leaves but refusing to produce peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ babaoo shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer or placing plants too close together causes pepper plants to focus all energy on leaf growth instead of fruiting. Reducing nitrogen, spacing plants properly, and ensuring full sunlight will encourage flower and pepper production.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine loo tsei ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei ni ji pepper lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe aduawai. Nitrogen ni baa shi lɛ Shi gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei ateŋ. Ni hulu la ni fa babaoo ni anáa lɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after planting maize to apply fertilizer instead of putting it all in the seed hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmãa ni midu lɛ sɛɛ koni mikɛ ŋmãa awo mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ fɛɛ baawo dumɔwui akuu lɛ mli?

english: Placing strong fertilizer directly with seeds can burn and kill the young seedling before it starts. Waiting until roots develop ensures the plant is ready to absorb nutrients safely and efficiently without wasting fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ ni egbe amɛ dani amɛje shishi. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or through infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties stops this virus from ruining your harvest.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli fãi ni afolɔ mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, dry spells, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch helps the flowers stay healthy and form tomato fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ anáa hewalɛ kɛ tomato ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why are there small holes in my cowpea pods with tiny caterpillars inside eating the beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii Hiɔ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Pod borer caterpillars lay eggs on flowering cowpea plants, and the hatched worms eat into the young pods. Spraying organic pesticides like neem seed extract right when flowers appear prevents caterpillars from destroying the beans.
ga: Pod borers woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsina tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi anɔ. Ni gɔgɔmɛi ni baa lɛ baaye tsei bibii lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu lɛ baashwie nɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when rainwater stays on the land for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field, roots suffocate and rot-causing fungi thrive; planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and becoming soft quickly while stored in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi oya ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ akɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout quickly when exposed to heat and trapped humidity because they think it is time to grow again. Storing yams in a cool, dark, well-ventilated raised barn slows sprouting and keeps tubers firm.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ amɛ lɛ he ejaakɛ amɛsusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potato ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm stop producing as many pods after a few years of big harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni ekɛkpaa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afii fioo komɛi ni eho lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees pull nutrients from the soil to produce pods. If you harvest heavily for several years without putting nutrients back into the dirt through manure or fertilizer, the soil gets tired and exhausted, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji okpa nii babaoo afii babaoo ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he feɔ shoo ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: What happens to the soil if I keep planting crops on the same piece of land without giving it a break?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Continuous planting drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt year after year. Over time, the soil loses its strength, and crop-specific pests and diseases build up, making it harder for anything to grow well.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. ni tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ nɔ ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is becoming exhausted and needs extra nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji ni ehe miihia ni akɛ niyenii krokomɛi afata he?

english: Signs of tired soil include leaves turning yellow, plants growing very slowly, cocoa pods remaining small, and a natural drop in total harvest compared to previous years.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ ahe ji baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ hu ji bibii. ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ ba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe.

english: What can I do to bring life back to my farmland when crops no longer grow well on it?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ beni ŋmɔshi nibii ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: You can restore exhausted soil by letting the land rest for a season or two, planting leguminous crops like beans or mucuna that put nitrogen back into the dirt, and adding compost or organic fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ be kome loo bei enyɔ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo mucilaginous tsei ni kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he

english: Young cocoa plants are like small children—they cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and heat. They need shade from larger trees or fast-growing plants like plantains to keep them cool and moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ gbekɛbii. ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cocoa trees too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. Overcrowding also traps moisture and stops fresh air from flowing, which makes it easy for diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. ni haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrition, or insect attacks. Giving the tree enough nutrients, keeping moisture in the soil, and controlling pests help the flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hɔmɔ miigba tsei anaa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees when I want them to grow big and produce pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ? Akɛni miisumɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo pods hewɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or useless branches so the tree does not waste water and food on them. This allows sunlight and air to reach the tree and directs energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. koni tsei lɛ akafite nu kɛ niyenii Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in cold, wet weather and high humidity. Clearing weeds around the base and pruning dense branches allows air and sunshine in to dry out the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are ready to pick, and why shouldn't I leave ripe ones on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their color changes from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange. Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long makes the beans inside sprout or rot, destroying the quality of your cocoa.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. ni fiteɔ bɔ ni kookoo lɛ hi ha lɛ

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves and soft dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji fioo ko yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves. They hide inside the central shoot of the maize plant where it is dark and moist to protect themselves while feeding.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ, ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ amli, koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves and passing a virus to the plant. Treating the insects early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa hela lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kplukai ahe tsamɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil lacks water. The heat stress prevents the flower from forming fruit, so the plant drops it to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings get scorched and yellow when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains around them creates protective shade that keeps the seedlings cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant many maize seeds very close together in the same small plot?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo kome nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This leaves you with tall, weak stalks and very small corn cobs instead of a larger yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa yɛ ŋmãa ni fa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same piece of soil every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows maize pests to live in the ground permanently. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rotten in the ground when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil loses oxygen. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I avoid putting granular fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve into the soil so plant roots can drink them up. Dry fertilizer sitting against plant roots under the sun can burn and kill the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso shishifãi amli yɛ hulu la mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ ni egbe lɛ.

english: How does leaving dry grass and weeds around the stems of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te tsei ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the soil quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents new weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do extension workers tell me to cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mifolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow inside the tree canopy, which reduces fungal diseases like black pod and directs energy into producing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves and build sturdy stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni etswa tsei ni wa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers but end up with empty shells under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the soil for the pods to fill up with nuts. Without enough calcium, the plant forms pods, but the seeds inside fail to develop, leaving empty shells.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ayi obɔ. Kɛji calcium faaa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee pods. Shi dumɔwu ni yɔɔ emli lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmei ko feɔ efolo.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my corn crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele lɛ mli?

english: Corn usually needs fertilizer at two main stages: first when it is about knee-high to build strong leaves, and a second time just before it flowers to help fill out the ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ, kɛji akɛ aaafee tsitsi nɔ lɛ, ji ni afee baai ni wa. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni eye ebua ni eha toi lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny worm-like pests called nematodes or banana stem borers weaken the roots, making the plant unable to support the weight of a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii eyi amɛmli. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo banana tso lɛ mli ŋmeii, ni amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ aduawai akutsei ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by whiteflies—tiny white insects that feed on the sap of the plant leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai amli nu lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water without proper drainage, allowing soil-borne fungi to attack and decay the tubers during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers often drop because tiny insects like thrips or pod borers feed on the young buds, preventing the flowers from setting pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsina fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo pod borers yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔii kwɛɛɛ

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from dry weather stress or lack pollination from tiny midges, which are insects that live in damp organic litter around the trees.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli loo gbekɛbii lɛ ni amɛhaaa amɛhe ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni hiɔ sũ ni mli efɔ ni bɔle tsei ahe lɛ mli.

english: Hot weather causes heat stress, which forces pepper plants to shed flowers as a defense mechanism to save moisture and stay alive.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting in the storage barn before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout early when storage areas are too warm or exposed to light, which tricks the tuber into thinking it is time to grow new roots and shoots.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo la shɛɛɛ he. Enɛ lakaa yitso lɛ ni esusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow strong. It can also happen when the soil is overly wet and the roots cannot breathe to take up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck the juice out of the leaves and spread plant diseases, or by the plant reacting to severe heat and dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni feɔ amɛnii yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds very close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight underground for water and soil food, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Spacing them properly gives every plant enough room to produce big yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee nibii babaoo.

english: The first rain of the year is often a 'false start' followed by a hot dry spell. If you plant too early, the young seeds will sprout and then dry up and die before the regular rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ ji ‘Apasa shishijee’ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away. Heavy rains combined with hard or clay soil trap water around the roots, causing them to suffocate and decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ sũ fataa he lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do people spread dry leaves and grass around the base of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It stops heat from drying out the soil quickly, keeps moisture in the ground, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ebaatsi la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why should I apply fertilizer when the soil is moist instead of when it is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works like sugar in water—it must dissolve before plant roots can drink it. If you put fertilizer on dry soil, the plant cannot absorb it, and the chemical can burn the dry roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sugar ni yɔɔ nu mli lɛ. Esa akɛ efo dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ. Ni tsofai lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛshã.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough rain for everything on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain isn't the only thing crops need. Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal nutrients from the soil, block sunlight, and harbor harmful insects that will jump onto your crops.
ga: Jeee nugbɔ pɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa, ni amɛhaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ atsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ahiɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat, too little water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to protect itself from dying.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni tsoɔ trukaa lɛ he. nu fioo tsɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashi fɔfɔi yɛ esɛɛ koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees turn brown in the dry season because they lack shade and moisture. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them from direct sun heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plant. Keeping only 2 or 3 healthy suckers of different sizes ensures the main plant grows strong and produces bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ mli tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni dalɛi srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛ plantains wuji aba.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves with yellowish dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni muji ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying recommended neem treatments or approved extension pesticides early in the morning destroys the pests before they eat the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ ajieɔ lɛ kpo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I stop my cassava roots from rotting inside the ground before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa?

english: Cassava rots when water collects around the roots in heavy soil. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground away from weeds and exposes them fully to the sun.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe ni ehaa hulu la lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from intense heat, dry soil, or a lack of calcium. Mulching the soil with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist so the plant can hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo calcium bɛ mli. Mulch ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ fɔfɔii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus they spread. Spraying organic neem leaf extract early controls these insects and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Ni akɛ organic neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra Ekudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni etsĩɔ baa heei adalɛ naa.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year when I plant it on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns valuable nitrogen back into the land naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen ni jara wa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In hot weather, leaves lose water faster than roots can pull it up from dry surface soil. Covering the exposed ground around the crops with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and prevents quick water loss.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha hei ni agbele ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya.

english: Why is maize so necessary when I am feeding my chickens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa he hiaa beni mikwɛɔ kooloi lɛ?
