english: Maize is a vital source of high energy for chickens. It gives them the strength to grow well, stay active, and maintain good body weight.
ga: Abɛi ji nɔ ko ni he hiaa ni haa kooloi hewalɛ babaoo. Ehaa amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ, amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛ shwiili kpakpa mli.

english: Can I feed my chickens yellow maize, or must I use white maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha kooloi niyenii ni ji ŋmɔŋ? Aloo esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ atsu nii?

english: You can feed chickens both white and yellow maize. Both types give chickens the energy they need, so you can use whichever is available to you.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ fɛɛ aha kooloi. Henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ haa kooloi hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Should I grind maize before giving it to my chickens?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmãa dani mikɛha kooloi?

english: Yes, grinding maize breaks it into small, manageable pieces that are easier for chickens to swallow, digest, and extract nutrients from.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni agbɛɔ lɛ fãa lɛ bibii bibii. ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi akɛ amɛmiɔ, amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is feeding my chickens ground maize alone enough to keep them healthy?
ga: Ani ŋmãa pɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ?

english: While maize is essential for energy, chickens also need clean water and other balanced nutrients to protect them from health problems and poor growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa he miihia kɛha hewalɛ moŋ, shi nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni ja hu he miihia wuji. Koni abu kooloi ahe kɛjɛ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai kɛ amɛdalɛ ni ehiii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my chickens developing leg weakness and having trouble standing up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikooloi lɛ naji bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnaa naagba yɛ shidaamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Leg weakness often occurs when chickens do not get properly processed feed or lack essential nutrients during their early growth stages.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, naji ni gbɔjɔɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ahaaa kooloi niyenii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ bɛ amɛmli yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee be mli.

english: What happens if I suddenly stop grinding maize for my growing chickens?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmãa ni akɛbaakwɛ kooloi lɛ trukaa?

english: Stopping proper feed preparation can cause severe physical issues in young chickens, such as leg deformities, stunted growth, and failure to walk properly.
ga: Niyenii he saamɔ ni sa ni akpaa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ naagbai ni mli wa aba kooloi bibii anɔ, tamɔ naji ni egbɔjɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. ni enyɛɛɛ enyiɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is high water content or wetness in my chicken feed bad for my flock?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mikooloi aniyenii lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha mitooi lɛ?

english: High water content makes feed spoil easily and creates a breeding ground for mold and germs that can make your chickens sick.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii fiteɔ oya. Ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baanyɛ aha okɔɔji lɛ aná hela lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Is raising chickens an easy business for a beginner farmer like me?
ga: Ani kooloi akwɛmɔ waaa kɛha okwaafonyo ni eje shishi tamɔ mi?

english: Chicken farming requires careful daily work. It involves managing moisture levels, preparing proper feed, and handling various health challenges to succeed.
ga: Kooloi akwɛmɔ biɔ nitsumɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, daa gbi. Nɔ ni fata he ji bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ. Niyenii he saamɔ ni sa kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai srɔtoi anɔkwɛmɔ. koni eye omanye

english: How fine should I grind maize when preparing feed for my birds?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmãa bibii aha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ miito okpo niyenii?

english: Maize should be ground down into small, uniform grains so that even young birds can easily swallow and digest it without choking.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmãa nɔ afee ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ekome bɔni afee ni okpoi bibii lɛ anyɛ ami ni amɛye amɛhe oya ni amɛkafo amɛhe.

english: Can I plant maize on my farm specifically to supply feed for my poultry?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii aha mikooloi lɛ?

english: Yes, growing maize is a great way to secure affordable, high-quality feed for your chickens, whether you choose to plant white or yellow maize varieties.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni jara waaa kɛhaa okɔɔji lɛ. Ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji ohala akɛ obaadu ŋmãa yɛŋ loo ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even when there is enough rain in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Leaves often turn yellow due to a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen or because of a root infection. While rain supplies water, plants still need proper nutrients and crop medicine to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shishifãi amli hela hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ lɛ haa nu moŋ, shi niyenii ni sa kɛ tsei tsofai he miihia tsei lolo koni amɛhiɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa.

english: This blackening is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in moist weather. Spraying the pods early with the recommended crop fungicide creates a protective shield that prevents the fungal rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: How can I tell if my wilting crops are sick with a disease or just reacting to heat from the hot sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ miipiŋ loo amɛmiitsu hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he nii kɛkɛ?

english: Crops affected by heat typically droop during the hot afternoon and recover by morning, whereas plants sick with a disease remain wilted, develop yellow spots, or rot regardless of the time of day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni dɔlɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ leebi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo fitemɔ, ni gbi lɛ mli be kɔɔɔ he eko

english: What will happen to my maize plants if I cannot find the right medicine to spray for armyworms?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mana parasite spray ni sa?

english: Fall Armyworms eat the growing center of young maize plants. Without spraying the right pesticide in time, the plant leaves become ragged, growth stalls, and the plant fails to form full cobs.
ga: Fall Armyworms yeɔ he ni ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yɛ be naa lɛ, tso lɛ baai baagbala ni ebaakpa amɛdalɛ. ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: This curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny sap-sucking insects called whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from growing broad and healthy, which reduces root growth under the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii mosaic hela. Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa shi.

english: What should I do to protect my crops if the agro-dealer shop runs out of the exact pesticide I usually buy?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mifɔɔ hemɔ lɛ efo yɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli?

english: You can check the bottle label for the 'active ingredient' and buy a different brand that uses the same active ingredient, or consult an extension officer for a safe alternative chemical with a similar effect.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ nɔ ni aŋma yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni ona. "active ingredient" ni ohé tsofa kroko ni kɛ tsofa ni tsuɔ nii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii Aloo oyabi extension official ko koni ona tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Are there natural ways to keep insects from destroying my crops if farm medicine is scarce or hard to find?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli gbɛi komɛi yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nibii? Kɛji tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ faaa loo ewa akɛ aaana?

english: Yes, spraying a mixture of crushed neem leaves boiled in water or soapy water on soft-bodied pests can act as a natural insect repellent and reduce crop damage when synthetic chemicals are unavailable.
ga: Hɛɛ, neem baai ni akpɔtɔ ni ahoo yɛ nu loo nu mli ni akɛ samla efutu mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi bɛ.

english: How can I protect my field from plant diseases if government-supplied chemicals do not reach our village on time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mihe kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ahe? Ni kɛji akɛ tsofai ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ baaa wɔ akrowai lɛ amli yɛ be naa hu?

english: You can plant disease-resistant seed varieties, clear away and burn infected plants early, and practice crop rotation to stop pest and disease cycles naturally while waiting for chemical supplies.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oshã amɛ mra. ni amɛkase ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ koni amɛkpa adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ tsofai lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I mix two different crop medicines together because I don't have enough of one?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ futu mli ejaakɛ mibɛ tsofa ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals can cause a severe reaction that burns leaf tissue, causes flowers to drop, or cancels out the strength of both medicines, damaging your crops instead of protecting them.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko ni naa wa aba ni shãa baa lɛ mli fãji. ha fɔfɔii agbo loo eha tsofai sɔrɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahe nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ ayaje Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ moŋ fe ni eeebu amɛhe.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with many green leaves but fail to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: This usually happens when plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer and not enough phosphorus or potassium, causing the plant to put all its energy into leaf growth rather than flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ ni enáaa phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai adalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green leafy growth. Heavy rains can wash nutrients away from roots, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea can help bring back their bright green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants compete for light, water, and nutrients. Proper spacing gives the tubers enough space under the ground to grow large and prevents wet conditions that promote root rot.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ bulb lɛ he lɛ haa bulb lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara. ni etsĩ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo lɛ naa.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds around the base of the cocoa trees helps air circulate and keeps pods healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji krokomɛi koni hulu la aba ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Cacao tso lɛ shishi haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on the land where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil. Rotating them with maize restores soil nutrients without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmã tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: It is best to wait until the rain becomes steady and the soil stays moist for several consecutive days. Planting after just one isolated rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Blossoms fall off when pepper plants face stress, such as dry soil, extreme heat, or receiving too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil damp using grass mulch and avoiding excessive fertilizer helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does removing weeds around my crops make them produce a better yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow. Regular weeding eliminates this competition, allowing your main crops to feed fully and grow faster.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa akaŋshii nɛɛ baa shi. Ha otsei titrii lɛ aná niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots go bad so quickly after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start to spoil within two to three days after harvest because cuts expose them to air, triggering natural decay. It is best to harvest cassava only when you are ready to process or sell it immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ afo lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa ŋmei pɛ kɛji ofee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi mi-tomato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, which spread viruses to the plant, or by water stress. Controlling pests early and maintaining steady watering helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tomato tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ mli Mra Be mli nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe Ni nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and retains moisture during heat stress.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ baa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ shi, ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually shows that the plant is short on nitrogen. When food in the soil is low, the maize plant moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the fresh, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with thin stems and tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to capture light instead of building strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛshwereɔ koni amɛmɔ la, ni moŋ amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei wuji.

english: Why do improved maize seeds give a better harvest than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved maize seeds are carefully bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry weather, and use soil nutrients more efficiently. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, leading to weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry hot spell. If you plant too early, the soil can dry out completely before the next rain, killing the newly sprouted seeds underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my maize a few weeks after planting instead of putting all of it in the soil on planting day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ awo mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ awo mli yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young sprouts only need a little food at the start. Applying fertilizer in stages ensures that the maize gets nutrients right when it is growing rapidly and forming cobs, rather than letting heavy rains wash the fertilizer away early on.
ga: Tsei bibii biɔ niyenii fioo ko yɛ shishijee mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii ni sa beni edaa oya ni efeɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe mra lɛ,.

english: Why do weeds harm my young maize plants much faster than they affect mature crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ oya fe bɔ ni amɛtutuaa tsei ni eda tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Young maize has shallow roots and weak early growth, so nearby weeds easily steal its water, light, and nutrients. Mature cassava has deep, established roots that can hold their own against weeds.
ga: Baby corn lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni edaa blɛoo. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaju nu, la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kasava ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni baanyɛ ate shi awo jwɛi.

english: Why do small ragged holes appear in the leaves of my young maize with dark droppings inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center of the plant. The ragged holes are where it has been chewing, and the droppings show that the pest is actively feeding inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni kɛ ehe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Spotty holes ji he ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ. Ni ŋmeii tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii miitao niyenii yɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my harvested maize cobs have missing grains and empty gaps along the core?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when drought or extreme heat occurs during flowering. If wind cannot move pollen to every single silk strand on the cob, the unpollinated spots will remain empty.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji hɔmɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atswa pollen lɛ kɛya siliki fiber fɛɛ fiber ni yɔɔ cob lɛ nɔ lɛ, He ko ni pollen bɛ lɛ baakã he ahi shi efolo.

english: Why do weevils still destroy my stored maize grains even after I have dried them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miifite mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ lolo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ

english: Sun drying lowers moisture and kills adult insects, but tiny insect eggs hidden inside the grains can survive the sun. Once stored in normal bags, those eggs hatch into fresh weevils unless stored in airtight hermetic bags or treated.
ga: Hulu la ni shɛɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ haa fɛ̃i baa shi ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ. Shi kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ akɛto kotoku ni sa mli lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii heei. ja akɛwo vacuum kotoku mli loo atsa lɛ

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps leaves stay green. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea can feed the plant and restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall with many leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, the cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves and tall stems instead of tubers. Balanced soil nutrients help the plant direct energy downward into swelling the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ tsei kakadaji yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ afuu.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when soil moisture changes suddenly, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ trukaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel while they are still small on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in very humid, dark, and wet conditions. Pruning shade trees and removing dead leaves lets sunlight in and air flow through to stop the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ waa, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ afolɔ ni ajieɔ baai ni egboi lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni ekpa ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why are my garden egg plants wilting even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil usually means the plant's roots are suffocating or rotting from too much water. Roots need air in the soil to breathe; if water sits too long, waterlogging damages the roots so they can no longer absorb water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ loo amɛmiifite kɛjɛ nu babaoo ni eho lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu ni hoɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in hot sun to reduce the amount of surface exposed to the sky, saving moisture. If leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, it is normal heat defense, but if they stay curled, it could be caused by tiny pests like mites.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba bɔ ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi kpeɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Abuɔ enɛ akɛ eji hulutsoo hebuu ni sa. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lolo lɛ Ekolɛ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to grow rapidly in poor soil with very little water. Because they are so aggressive, clearing weeds early gives your planted crops a fair chance to get sunlight and food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ nu fioo pɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ eyɛ basabasa waa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I put several seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young sprouts must fight each other for limited sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every seed its own room to develop thick, strong stalks.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni hulu la ni faaa, shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa dumɔwui fɛɛ dumɔwui náa tso ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Will my maize plants grow stronger roots if I plant the seeds deep into the ground?
ga: Ani mi-abele tsei lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too deep makes it hard for the young shoot to break through the heavy soil surface before running out of stored energy. Planting seeds 3 to 5 centimeters deep gives them the best balance of moisture and fast germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa. Ewa dani hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni mli kwɔ sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ shweremɔ ni yaa oya.

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can check maturity by carefully digging up two or three sample plants across the field. Open a few pods; if the inside lining of the shell has turned dark brown or black and the seeds are full, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji oyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni oookwɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Gbelemɔ pods fioo komɛi. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ.

english: Why is the government asking us to cut down our cocoa trees when they are still producing a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ biɔ ni wɔfolɔ kookoo tso lɛ be mli ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Diseased trees, especially those affected by Swollen Shoot disease, cannot recover. Keeping them on your farm allows insects to spread the virus to nearby healthy trees, eventually destroying the entire farm.
ga: tso ni hela emɔ lɛ Titri lɛ tsei ni ŋmeii efuu. unable to recover Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: If I cut down my old tree crop to replant, how long will it take before the new trees start giving me fruit?
ga: Kɛji mifo tso momo ko koni madu ehee Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani tso hee ko baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Most modern hybrid tree crops like cocoa or oil palm begin bearing fruit between two to three years after planting, provided they receive proper weed control, shade, and water.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he, tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso lɛ ateŋ babaoo jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha jwɛi, aha amɛ hulutsoo ni aha amɛ nu.

english: How am I supposed to feed my family during the two years after cutting down my main tree farm to replant?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miweku lɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ beni mifo mitso wulu lɛ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: You can plant quick-yielding food crops like plantain, cassava, maize, or cocoyam between the young seedlings. These crops provide food and immediate cash income while your new trees grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa loo kookoo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ be mli ni otsei heei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Is it better to clear my whole farm all at once to replant, or should I do it section by section?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi akɛ aaajie ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome koni adu ekoŋŋ? Aloo esa akɛ mafee lɛ fã kome yɛ be kome mli?

english: Replanting in sections allows you to keep earning money and harvesting food from the mature parts of your farm while waiting for the newly replanted section to start producing.
ga: Dumɔ hee yɛ hei srɔtoi Ehaa onáa shika ni okpaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni eda lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ hei heei ni adu lɛ koni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do my young tree seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in strong sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my farm soil get so hard and dry after I cut down all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbi beni mifo tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Large trees shield the ground from direct heat. When they are removed, bare soil loses moisture rapidly under the sun; spreading dry leaves or planting cover crops helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa shi oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: If I cut a tree trunk close to the ground, will the tree die completely or will it sprout back?
ga: Kɛji ofo tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni obɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ani tso lɛ baagbo loo ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: Many tree roots remain alive after the trunk is cut and will sprout new shoots. To stop growth completely, you must dig out the main root system or repeatedly remove new shoots as they appear.
ga: Tso shishifãi babaoo hiɔ shi yɛ wala mli beni afo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ sɛɛ, ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei heei. Bɔni afee ni okpa dalɛ kwraa Esa akɛ Otsi shishifãi titri lɛ shii abɔ loo ojie ŋmeii heei beni amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why does my old cocoa farm yield fewer pods every year even when I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli moŋ?

english: As tree crops get older, their internal transport systems weaken and roots can no longer absorb fertilizer efficiently. At that stage, fertilizer cannot replace the need to cut and replant young trees.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda Tso lɛ mli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi. Ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, Fertilizer nyɛŋ atsake hiamɔ ni yɔɔ tsei bibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni aduɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Can crop diseases move from my neighbor’s diseased tree farm into my clean farm?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ajɛ mikutsoŋnyo tso ŋmɔ ni hela emɔ lɛ mli kɛya miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli?

english: Yes, insects, wind, rainwater, and shared farming tools easily carry diseases across farm boundaries. Planting a barrier row of non-host plants along the edge helps stop diseases from crossing over.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ nu, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ anɔ oya. Tsei ni jeee maŋ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli akɛ gbɛtsii nii lɛ baaye abua ni helai akafo mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land right after I clear old trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie tsei momo lɛ?

english: Clearing the canopy allows direct sunlight to reach weed seeds buried in the dirt, causing them to sprout all at once. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing soil nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. ni haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ he kome Jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize plants lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much standing water is choking the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or clearing water pathways helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ni miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo nu ni mli tse ni hoɔ baafata he. Ebaaye ebua ni aku sɛɛ aha su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli awa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the crop suffers from extreme heat, dry soil during flowering, or poor soil nutrients like lack of phosphorus. Keeping the soil moist and well-nourished helps the plant keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open, cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby provides a living shield that keeps the young cocoa cool and moist while it gets established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaafee gãimlibii ni hiɛ ka ni baaha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops very close together on my small plot?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives every crop room to grow strong and produce fully.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa shweremɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ feɔ shweremɔ tsu fɛɛ shweremɔ tsu.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when rainwater sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater cannot drain away, it displaces the soil air and drowns the roots, causing rot. Creating shallow drainage channels lets stagnant water escape easily.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni anyɛɛɛ ajie nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ Ebaajie kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. cause decay Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni ekã shi lɛ hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo mlɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer right at the base of my pepper plant's stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem burns the tender plant tissue and damages it. Placing fertilizer in a ring a few centimeters away allows the fine feeding roots to safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni efite lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi amli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the leaves and central shoots of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ayeli he?

english: Ragged holes in young maize are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf whorl. Catching them early and applying neem extracts or recommended insecticides protects the crop's growth center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baa ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and touch the dirt once fruits start appearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato vines become heavy as fruit grows and cannot support their own weight. Tying the stems to wooden stakes keeps the plant upright, preventing fruit rot from soil contact and reducing plant diseases.
ga: Tomato wain tsei lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ shishitso lɛ fĩ tso ko he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Etsiɔ aduawai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ he ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baa shi.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off. You can test maturity by carefully digging around the base of one plant to check tuber thickness before harvesting the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni edara ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome shishigbɛ ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ha dani okpa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why don't seeds saved from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest perform as well when I plant them the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nɛkɛ beni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first planting generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their original strength, leading to uneven growth and much smaller cobs in the second season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛshishijee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: I have a piece of land that has been sitting idle for years, so how do I prepare it properly before planting my first crop?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii afii babaoo nɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu mi klɛŋklɛŋ tso lɛ?

english: Idle land often has hard soil and overgrown weeds. Clearing the brush without burning, breaking up the topsoil with a hoe or tractor, and mixing in organic manure brings life and nutrients back into the soil so your new crop roots can grow easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ yɛ sũ ni wa, ni jwɛi eyi nɔ obɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ ni okɛshãaa amɛ. Okɛ ŋmei loo trakta atse shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, ehaa wala kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha otso hee lɛ shishifãi lɛ ada oya.

english: Does burning the dry grass on my farm before planting help or harm my soil?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mikɛshãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: While burning cleared bush seems easy and gives a temporary layer of ash, it actually burns away organic matter and kills beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops. Clearing and leaving the vegetation to rot into mulch builds much healthier soil over time.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni jwɛŋmɔ bɛ mli ni ehaa sũ baa shi be kukuoo ko moŋ, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ni ashi amɛ koni amɛgboi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it good practice to plant cassava and maize together in the same farm plot?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together is a great practice called intercropping. Maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the space later, allowing you to harvest two different crops from the same land without them competing.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa ni atsɛɔ lɛ intercropping. Abele daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra, yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ mli, ni no haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛyeee akaŋ.

english: Should I buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer or just plant seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ loo madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected to yield more produce, resist common local diseases, and withstand unpredictable weather better than saved seeds. Spending a little on certified seeds usually results in a much bigger harvest.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ afite shika fioo yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe lɛ, no haa anáa yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential plant food, or are choked by too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa loo nu babaoo efo mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl in intense heat to prevent moisture from escaping into the dry air. If they recover by early morning, the plants are managing, but placing dry grass mulch around the base keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture longer.
ga: Shi oyitsɔi lɛ ni ebɔle ehe yɛ la mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje kpo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Kɛji ohe wa bo leebi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant pepper on the exact same farm patch every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in the exact same spot allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil season after season. Rotating pepper with legumes like groundnuts breaks the disease cycle and restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ akwɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tso pɔtɛɛ ko he tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii lɛ haa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa, ni ehaa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes into the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on young corn leaves. You can protect your crop by checking the farm regularly and applying recommended organic measures or approved pesticides directly into the center funnel of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ daa ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when there is plenty of rainfall for everyone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshinii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ náa nugbɔ kpakpa moŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, sunlight, and space that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early—especially during the first four to six weeks after planting—ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ he ni ehe hiaa ni otsei lɛ adara lɛ mli. Ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra Titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4-6 ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so that it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when crops are actively growing and the soil is moist. Apply a first round about two to three weeks after planting when roots are ready to feed, and a second round when the plants begin flowering or setting fruit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Okɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha niyenii. kɛ kpokpaa ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ loo amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, humid conditions and heavy shade. Pruning unnecessary branches to allow sunlight and air into your farm, along with applying recommended fungicides, helps stop the rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛfata tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa fitemɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods have small holes in them with sticky liquid leaking out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli bu bibii lɛ? Ni nu ko ni mli tse miiho kɛmiijɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by mirids (also known as capsids), which are tiny insects that pierce and suck nutrients from cocoa pods and young shoots. Spraying your farm with approved insecticides during peak pest seasons will protect your pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ capsid), ni ji kooloo bibioo ko ni boteɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ shwieɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: How long will it take for my newly planted cocoa trees to start producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe ni mi-cacao tso ni midu ehee lɛ aje shishi ewo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties commonly planted in Ghana typically start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older, traditional cocoa varieties can take between 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome ni afɔɔ dumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing many flowers, but most of them fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee pods?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they lack soil nutrients, suffer from drought, or if there are not enough tiny insects called midges to pollinate them. Proper soil fertilizing and keeping moderate shade helps more flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni kɛ hɔmɔ he naagbai kpeɔ loo kooloi bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ pollination baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo hewalɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and start dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔi shwiemɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean the plants are exposed to too much harsh direct sunlight or lack nitrogen in the soil. Plantain trees planted nearby can provide gentle shade while fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo be blɛoo. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii baaha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow very tall and thin with weak stems when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight and stretch upward rapidly, resulting in thin, weak stems. Giving each crop the recommended spacing ensures they get enough light to grow strong and sturdy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ ha lɛ, ehaa enáa la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni etswa shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during the hottest part of the day as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is fine, but if they stay curled, the crops need urgent watering.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Bɔni afee ni nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi Kɛji baai lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ hi, shi kɛji baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni awo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu oya.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants turn pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on young maize are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogged soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea around the plants will help restore full green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from taking away the food your crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni he hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers taste bitter after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava turns bitter when the plants experience prolonged dry weather or are harvested too late, causing natural chemical compounds called cyanogenic glycosides to build up in the roots.
ga: Cassava lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ loo akpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni atsɛɔ amɛ cyanogen glycosides lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo tsei bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very sensitive leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh heat, keep the air humid, and help the soil stay moist so the cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ fɛ̃i mli bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and grow tall. It usually means your soil is tired and needs compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen, it puts all its food and energy into growing big stems and leaves above the ground instead of sending energy down to swell the roots into thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ Ebaaha lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo eshishifãi wuji kɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a haa he wami kɛ baa si konɛ e ha nɛ sisije ɔmɛ nɛ a gblɛɛ kɛ pee bulb nɛ mi wa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have helpful microbes on their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in the dirt. This naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow better without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-ŋmã lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my plants grow thin and fall over easily when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch out tall and thin to steal light from their neighbors, making their stems weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo koni amɛju la kɛjɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ adɛŋ. ha tso lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when heavy rain sits on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the ground for days without draining, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and killing the crop.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii gboiɔ.

english: Why are the inner leaves of my young maize plants drying up and breaking off even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ egbi ni egbɛ eshwa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by stem borer insects that hatch inside the stalk. They eat the inside of the plant stem, blocking water and food from reaching the top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi ni fɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ koni nu kɛ niyenii akashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce very small yields even if I put fertilizer down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will drink the soil moisture and eat the fertilizer you put down before your crops get a chance to take it in.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ebaaŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ni eye ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛwo mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil. The plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I trim off some of the extra branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming removes useless leafy branches that drain nutrients from the plant. This forces the plant to send all its energy into developing large, healthy tomatoes instead of more leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni woɔ yibii ni jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji ni mli wa moŋ fe ni ebaabi baai babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as the main food for leaf growth, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil holds too much water without draining well, allowing waterborne diseases to enter and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni etsɔɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa helai ni jɛɔ nu mli baa lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is mostly caused by tiny invisible pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus carried by insects.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ mli shwiemɔ babaoo baa ji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli loo tsei amli helai ni kɛ kooloi bibii baa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or dry because the heat stresses the plant and prevents flower pollination.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all big trees off the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunshine; they need shade from larger trees or plantain plants to protect their tender leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no plant with enough energy to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially if tiny soil worms called nematodes have damaged their roots.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kpata amɛshishifãi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why does growing maize on the exact same plot every single year lower my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? afii ni no hewɔ lɛ eha minitsumɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer right before a big downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater sweeps away loose fertilizer from the topsoil into gutters and streams before the plant roots have a chance to absorb it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli. dani tso shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ lɛ

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them during hot periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket that shades the ground, keeps the soil cool, and slows down water evaporation so roots stay moist longer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and dry heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava around them to block the harsh sun and retain soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca, ni ebɔle amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, fight with the mother plant for food and water in the soil. By leaving only one or two healthy shoots, all the soil nutrients go straight into making large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛfeɔ tso wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant steals food from its bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, showing that it needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Atsɔɔ akɛ enɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo urea.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans helps make my farm soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have small nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the earth. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground to act as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it best for me to apply fertilizer during the heavy downpours of the rainy season?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Applying fertilizer during heavy rainfall washes the nutrients away before the crop's roots can drink them in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not flooded, usually right when light rains begin.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu efooo mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ.

english: Why do we cut cassava stems into sticks to plant instead of using the seeds from the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔfoɔ ŋmei tsei wɔwoɔ tsei amli koni wɔkɛdu yɛ tso lɛ mli dumɔwui ni wɔkɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava seeds grow very slowly and produce tubers of unpredictable size and taste. Planting stem cuttings ensures that the new plant matures quickly and produces the exact same large tubers as the healthy parent stem.
ga: Cassava dumɔwui lɛ daaa blɛoo waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso hee lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji tamɔ fɔlɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground away from pests and rot, letting them catch sunlight easily.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ebaaha kooloi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli. Okɛ amɛ awo hulu la mli mlɛo.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and shrinking during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves to suck out the sap. Spraying with appropriate organic or recommended chemical controls stops these pests and helps leaves grow normal again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni sa loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akpa ni eha baai lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young oil palm trees drop their first flowers without forming fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso bibioo lɛ woɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ ni ekɛ aduawai akuu ko efeee lɛ?

english: Young oil palm trees produce mostly male flowers first as a natural way to build strength before they can bear heavy fruit. Once the tree matures and receives proper fertilizer, it will start forming female flowers that develop into fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei bibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛtswa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ amɛma shi dani amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Kɛ́ tso lɛ eda ni enine shɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaaje fɔfɔi yei ni feɔ aduawai akui lɛ afeemɔ shishi.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow better when there is shallow water sitting in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat rice lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni eta ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water blocks wild grass and weeds from growing and competing with your rice. It also keeps the ground soft so the rice roots can easily suck up water and plant food.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baatsi koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi bibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ o-rice lɛ akabɔ akaŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni omɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu oya ni amɛkwɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no larger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Larger trees or plantain plants provide living shade and keep the air humid, protecting the young cocoa until its leaves grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei wuji loo dumɔwui haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi baai lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my yam plants produce very small tubers when I leave the vines to grow on the bare ground instead of using stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs bibii waa beni mishiɔ wain tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ moŋ fe tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight. When left on the ground, the leaves crowd together and get shaded, which prevents the plant from making enough energy to build big tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛfeɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulb agbo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The maize plant starves its older bottom leaves to push whatever nitrogen it has left to the fresh green leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Abɛi tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛtsi nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii dani midu ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the dirt, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ helai ni haa mɔ feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry during a warm period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wooo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can safely absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil concentrates harsh minerals around the roots, which can scorch and destroy the plant's root system.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa sũ mli nibii ni mli wa waa lɛ feɔ ekome kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards like small bowls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe tamɔ tsɛnsii bibii lɛ?

english: Upward curling is a defense response or reaction caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Curling up ji hebuu hetoo loo nifeemɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ kɛbaa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruit develops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or drought. When temperatures get too hot, the pollen dries out, preventing fertilization, so the plant drops the flower to conserve water.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ kpe. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pollen lɛ baagbi. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu.

english: Why do my young green oranges drop off the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tangerine bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop excess young fruit if they don't have enough water or nutrients to feed them all, or when tiny fruit flies pierce the skin to lay eggs inside, causing the baby fruit to spoil and drop.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baawo yibii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. Aloo kɛ́ aduawai bibii fo lɛ Efoɔ hewolo lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmeii awo mli. Ehaa aduawai bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot quickly in the soil if heavy rain falls just before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa lɛ?

english: Roots need oxygen from air pockets in the soil to stay alive. Excess rain floods these air spaces with water, suffocating the roots and creating a wet environment where rot-causing bacteria quickly grow.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui nɛɛ amli nu hoɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni helai ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ adara oya yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees collapse and fall over so easily when a small storm blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum bibii amli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have a deep taproot, relying instead on shallow surface roots. As the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, microscopic soil worms or wet rot can easily weaken those shallow roots until the tree tips over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ e hɛ fɔ sisi nɛ mi kuɔ we nɔ. Beni plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ aba. Nomɛi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ oya kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers, but many of them fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Shi tsei enyiɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers need successful pollination—usually carried out by tiny insects like midges—to turn into pods. If there are not enough beneficial insects or if weather conditions prevent pollination, the flowers simply drop off without growing fruit.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ ni amɛye omanye yɛ pollination mli. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii feɔ enɛ koni amɛtsake amɛ amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ faaa loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsiɔ pollination naa lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: How do small insects actually help my crops grow more fruit?
