ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Insects move from flower to flower carrying pollen, which fertilizes the flowers. This natural process allows the plant to form seeds and pods instead of shedding empty flowers.
ga: Kplukai fãa kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi krokomɛi anɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɔmɔ nii lɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ nɛɛ haa tsei feɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooŋmɛ fɔfɔi ni bɛ nɔ ko mli lɛ

english: Does heavy rain help or hurt my crops when they are flowering?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui kɛ́ amɛwo fɔfɔi?

english: While crops need water to grow, heavy rain during flowering can wash away pollen and tiny pollinating insects, which reduces successful pollination and leads to fewer fruits forming.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tsei he hiaa nu koni amɛdara lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi kɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe, ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ aye omanye ni eha aduawai ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I start treating my cocoa farm like a business instead of just a daily routine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabɔi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he nitsumɔ tamɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni afeɔ daa kɛkɛ?

english: Treating your farm like a business means tracking your expenses on inputs like fertilizer and labor, calculating expected yields, and consistently investing back into crop health to ensure a steady profit year after year.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ tamɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaakwɛ shika ni ofiteɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nitsumɔ he lɛ nɔ. Yibiiwoo ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ he akɔntaabuu kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛnamɔ mli ekoŋŋ daa koni sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aba afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why is it important for me to plan for crop production year after year rather than just focusing on this season's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mato ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ o juɛmi kɛ ma be nɛ ɔ mi ní kpami ɔ pɛ nɔ.

english: Perennial crops like cocoa require continuous investment in soil health and tree maintenance; taking care of your trees today ensures they remain productive and profitable for decades, protecting your long-term livelihood.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo biɔ ni akɛ shika awo shikpɔŋ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ mli daa. Otsei lɛ akwɛmɔ ŋmɛnɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ amli. Buu oshihilɛ he yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: How does investing in proper farm management lead to higher profits at the end of the year?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni shika ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha sɛɛnamɔ babaoo aba yɛ afi lɛ naagbee?

english: Proper management—such as regular weeding, pest control, and timely pruning—improves flower survival and pod development, resulting in a larger yield to sell for more money.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa, tamɔ jwɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe nitsumɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni afoɔ yɛ be naa lɛ Haa fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi kɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa anáa nibii babaoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ shika babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods as the farm gets older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Over time, soil loses essential nutrients, trees become overgrown, and shade becomes too thick, which lowers pollination rates and reduces the tree's energy to produce new pods.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Sũ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite. Tsei lɛ etsɔ tsɔ. ni hulutsoo lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Enɛ haa pollination rate lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii heei lɛ baa shi

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my crops produce better yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Pruning removes unproductive or dead branches, allowing more sunlight and airflow through the farm. This encourages healthy flowering and makes it easier for pollinators to reach the blossoms.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii loo ni egboi lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ fɛo, ni ehaa fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds in my farm reduce the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds take those resources away, your crop trees lack the energy needed to successfully form and ripen pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ kpata nakai nibii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Otso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee eshishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: What causes cocoa pods to stop growing and turn black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is often caused by fungal infections like Black Pod disease, which thrive in damp, overly shaded farms with poor air movement. Proper tree spacing and clearing extra shade help prevent this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa, tamɔ black pod hela, ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo kroko ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick my cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava cuttings upside down will delay growth or cause weak, scattered roots. Make sure the buds on the stem point upward towards the sky so the shoot can grow straight up easily.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo ebaaha shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ aba. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ. mlɛo

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leafy shade to protect young cocoa from sunburn and keep moisture in the soil during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa baai wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for me to dig up and transplant to a new plot?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker tso ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mafo mli ni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Choose 'sword' suckers with narrow, spear-like leaves rather than suckers with broad leaves. Sword suckers have strong underground corms and produce healthier, higher-yielding plantain trees.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Mohu ɔ, hla tso ɔmɛ nɛ a bami ɔmɛ a mi tsɔ. Sword suckers lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves the soil too waterlogged, preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off without fruiting when daytime heat gets too intense or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells followed by heavy watering, which causes extreme stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Aloo beni tomato tsei lɛ gĩɔ trukaa ni nu babaoo nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap out of young leaves, or by viral diseases carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth, while keeping the leaves away from wet soil where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: What benefit do I get if I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi mana kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps soil cool, traps moisture during hot dry spells, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crop immediately when planting or wait a few weeks?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji midu loo esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: It is usually best to wait 2 to 3 weeks after germination or transplanting because very young plant roots can be burned by strong fertilizers before they are established enough to absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ loo ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi ni darako waa lɛ. Dani abaama bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: How do I know the right time to start planting after the first rainy season weather begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains before planting, rather than planting after the very first light drizzle which might be followed by a long dry heat wave that kills seeds.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa dani okɛdu. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se, nɛ la nɛ mi wa be gagaa nɛ ma nyɛ maa gbe dumɔwu ɔmɛ.

english: How long does it actually take for a cocoa pod to grow and mature on the tree before I can harvest it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: A cocoa pod usually takes about 5 to 6 months to grow from a pollinated flower into a fully mature, ripe pod. However, the main harvesting period across a farm in Ghana can last over several months due to continuous flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛdaraa kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi ni awo mli ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni eda kwraa lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, kpamɔ be titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ ahé nyɔji babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi ni yaa nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do we have two different harvest seasons for cocoa in Ghana during the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔyɛ kookoo kpamɔ bei srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ Ghana yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ghana experiences two distinct rainy seasons each year. The major harvest season runs from October to February following the main rains, while the minor harvest season occurs from May to June following the smaller rains.
ga: Ghana yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ daa afi. Nikpamɔ be wulu lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ October kɛyashiɔ February ni nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ asɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kpamɔ be bibioo lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ May kɛyashiɔ June ni nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi bibii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How many years after planting my cocoa seedlings will I see the trees start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ? Ani obaanyɛ ona kookoo tsei lɛ ni miibɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take about 3 to 5 years to start bearing fruit, but newer hybrid cocoa varieties developed in Ghana can start producing pods within 2 to 3 years if given proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi yinɔ hee ko ni ji cocoa hybrids ni afee yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to drop up to 95% of its flowers. The tree produces thousands of flowers, but only those pollinated by tiny insects like midges will successfully turn into pods.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei ni fa fe 95% baawo fɔfɔi. Tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ pɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my cocoa pods are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when they mature, turning from green to bright yellow, or from purple-red to orange. Tapping a ripe pod gently with your knuckles will also produce a hollow sound because the beans inside have loosened.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo kɛjɛ magenta kɛya ŋmɔŋ Okɛ oniji atswa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ blɛoo. Ebaaha gbee ni mli ewo muji aba ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbee shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high humidity and heavy rain. Keeping the farm clear of weeds and pruning dense branches helps air circulate to prevent this.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni afo tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ekɛtsi enɛ naa.

english: Can a single cocoa farm keep producing pods for my children over many decades?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ afee pods aha mibii lɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa trees are long-term perennial crops that can remain productive for 30 to 40 years or more if they are properly pruned, weeded, and protected from diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ awo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛji akɛ afolɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, jwɛi kɛ helai tsiɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade from bigger trees when crops like maize grow best in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa ni tsei wuji lɛ aná hulutsoo lɛ? Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa naturally originated under tall forest trees. Young cocoa leaves dry out and burn easily in direct sunlight, so shade trees help regulate heat, maintain moisture, and protect young cocoa trees.
ga: Cocoa jɛ koo mli tsei kakadaji ashishi. Kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ dɔlɛ nɔ. Ha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni obu kookoo tsei bibii ahe

english: Will trimming branches off my cocoa trees reduce my harvest or increase it?
ga: Ani niji ni mifoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ yibii lɛ aba shi loo ebaaha mi-koo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Pruning actually increases your crop yield. Removing dead, diseased, or excess branches allows sunlight and air to reach the tree, reduces disease risks, and directs the tree's energy into making bigger pods.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa otso lɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ helai ni baanyɛ aba lɛ shi ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni okɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: What kind of nourishment do my cocoa trees need most while the pods are filling up with beans?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa mi cacao tso lɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii eyi ŋmeii amli lolo lɛ?

english: When pods are growing, cocoa trees need high amounts of potassium to help the beans develop fully, alongside nitrogen for healthy leaf growth and phosphorus for strong root development.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ miida lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ biɔ potassium babaoo koni eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara. Kɛfata nitrogen he kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni mli wa. kɛ fɔsfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ shweremɔ

english: Why are deep roots so important for my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Deep roots act like long straws that reach deep under the ground to find hidden water and nutrients, helping your crops stay green and survive even when there is no rain.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni tsaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How does applying fertilizer help my newly planted crops get a strong start?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mitso hee lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni ejeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer feeds the soil with essential nutrients that encourage early root growth, making young plants strong enough to establish themselves quickly and resist harsh weather.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shishifãi lɛ daa oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛto shi oya ni amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anaa.

english: Why do my crops fall over easily when strong winds and rain hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops usually fall over because their root systems are shallow or weak. Strong, deep roots anchor the plant firmly into the soil, keeping it standing upright during heavy wind and rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛhe waaa. Shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ fiɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ha ehi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli.

english: Can fertilizer actually help my crops develop better roots in hard soil?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛná shishifãi kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ?

english: Yes, certain fertilizers provide specific nutrients like phosphorus that stimulate root spreading, helping roots push through tough soil to reach water and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii.

english: How do my crops actually take in the fertilizer that I spread on the soil?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops use their fine roots to absorb water from the soil that has dissolved the fertilizer nutrients, which then travel up through the stem to nourish the leaves and fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi kpakpai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala nu ni jɛɔ sũ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa gbɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ koni eyaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young seedlings struggle to grow right after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Transplant shock happens when fragile roots get damaged during moving; helping the plant build new roots quickly allows it to absorb water again and recover fast.
ga: Transplant shock baa kɛji shishifãi ni waaa lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni atsakeɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aye abua tsei ni amɛná shishifãi heei oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu ekoŋŋ ni amɛhe feɔ oya.

english: Should I apply root-boosting fertilizer at the time of planting or wait until the plant grows bigger?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni mikɛwo shishifãi lɛ ahe hewalɛ kɛ́ midu loo mamɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Applying a fertilizer that supports rooting right at planting gives young roots immediate food to expand early, which prepares the plant to grow bigger faster.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni amɛkɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni asaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: What happens to my crops if the soil around their roots is too hard and compacted?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe?

english: Compacted soil starves roots of air and prevents them from expanding, leading to stunted crops that cannot reach hidden moisture or nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why does having a bigger root system lead to a better harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni da ni anáa lɛ haa anáa ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: A bigger root system covers more ground to gather food and water, giving the crop the energy it needs to produce larger and healthier yields.
ga: Shishifã ni da lɛ haa he babaoo ni akɛbuaa niyenii kɛ nu naa. Ehaa tsei hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks nutrients or has a weak root system that cannot absorb food properly from the soil, despite receiving enough water.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo eyɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, kɛji enine shɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po nɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well during the dry season even when there is a stream near my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ faa ko yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Crops need regular water to absorb soil nutrients. Even if a stream is nearby, plants cannot reach it on their own unless you actively pump or channel the water into the farm through simple irrigation.
ga: Tsei hia nu daa koni amɛ nu niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ faa ko yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ moŋ, shi Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he kɛkɛ. Ja okɛ nu miiwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo okɛmiiwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ.

english: How can using water from a nearby stream help me grow crops all year round?
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Te ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ tsei afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Using stream water for irrigation keeps the soil moist when the rains stop, allowing you to harvest crops continuously and sell them when market prices are high.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ faa mli nu tsu nii kɛshwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyaa nɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ kɛ́ jara lɛ nɔ wa.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too little water during the hot sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miináa nu fioo tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When plants get too little water, their leaves wilt, curl inward, or turn yellow to conserve moisture, which slows down their growth and reduces fruit yield.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu fioo tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi. tsɔ mli loo etsɔ ŋmɔŋ koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Can I grow enough healthy vegetables in the small space behind my house to feed my family?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he bibioo ko. Ani manyɛ mikɛ shia lɛ sɛɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ miweku lɛ?

english: Yes, small backyard gardens can produce high yields if you use practical methods like raised beds, regular watering, and good soil compost in that small space.
ga: Hɛɛ, abɔɔ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ okɛ nifeemɔi tamɔ saatsoi ni awo nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa tsu nii. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ nakai he bibioo lɛ mli.

english: What are some simple, low-cost things I can do on my farm that will make a big difference in crop yield?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni jara waaa ni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha srɔtofeemɔ kpele aba ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Small habits like keeping correct distance between plants, removing weeds early, and adding crop mulch to keep the soil wet make a huge positive difference without costing much.
ga: Sui bibii tamɔ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa srɔtofeemɔ kpakpa kpele baa ni ekɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Why are my backyard pepper plants producing many leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishia sɛɛ pepper tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer which pushes leaf growth, or when the plant isn't getting consistent water and sunlight to form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo, ni no haa baai lɛ daa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu kɛ hulu la ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: I have been farming for many years, so why should I bother attending farm demonstrations?
ga: Mikɛ afii babaoo etsu okwaayeli he nii. Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mihe awo ŋmɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Farm demonstrations show practical, modern techniques in action so you can see new ways to save labor, protect your crops, and get higher yields than traditional methods allow.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnii ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai ni miitsu nii No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ona gbɛi heei ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ nitsumɔ atsu nii Buu onibii ahe ni oná yibiiwoo ni fa fe bɔ ni blema gbɛi lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant them in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, while making it much easier for you to weed and care for them.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi ni okwɛ nakai tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: What do buyers look for if I want to sell my vegetables to bigger markets outside my village?
ga: Mɛni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baatao kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ aduawai mahã jara wulu ko ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Big buyers look for clean, unblemished, and uniform vegetables that were grown with clean irrigation water and harvested carefully to avoid bruising.
ga: Mɛi wuji ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ aduawai ni he tse, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he, ni yaa nɔ daa ni akɛ nu ni mli tse ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ duɔ. ni okpa jogbaŋŋ koni akafite.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani anyɛɔ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops during the hot afternoon heat or leaving them directly under the sun causes them to lose moisture and rot fast; picking them early in the morning keeps them fresh much longer.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo oshi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafite oya. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again and boosts your crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibi lɛ ji ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ yɛ bu ko ni etse. Yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young leaves and growing points. Spotting them early and applying approved biological or chemical treatments saves your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ baai bibii kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaahere okpamɔ lɛ yiwala.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and lacks good drainage during heavy rains. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the large trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct intense sunlight dries out their leaves and soil quickly. Retaining some canopy trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai anɔ loo odu tsei ni haa ŋwɛi ŋtayaai shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋtayaai bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking exposes leaves to sunlight and keeps them off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain yibii ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaaa sũ ni mli ewo fɔ, ni ji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving seeds proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stems and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ shi ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of key nutrients stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to survive. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plant helps flowers set into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if I give my crop plants enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from your plants' root zones. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and moisten the soil deeply, rather than planting right after the very first rain. Planting after a single rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji latsaa ni naa wa ba.

english: Why are the branches and stems of my cocoa trees swelling up in some parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ aniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Swelling on cocoa stems and shoots is usually a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD). It is spread by small insects called mealybugs, and because it is a virus, infected trees must be removed to prevent the disease from spreading to healthy trees in your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei kɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ji kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahe okadi (CSSVD). Kplukai bibii ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Ni akɛni eji hela ko hewɔ lɛ Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes sticky liquid or fluid to ooze out of cuts on my tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni haa nu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Aloo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ pilamɔ ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Fluid or gummy liquid oozing from a tree trunk usually indicates a fungal or bacterial bark infection called a canker or gummosis. This happens when germs enter through physical cuts or insect damage, and it can be treated by scraping off the bad bark and applying a protective copper fungicide.
ga: Nu loo nu ni shwieɔ shi ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso shishi lɛ fɔɔ kaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi loo bacteria mli baa ni atsɛɔ lɛ cancer loo gummosis. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ bote pilamɔi loo kooloi ni efite lɛ amli. Ni abaanyɛ atsa lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ehiii lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni akɛ akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Is it harmful to my crops if I accidentally scrape or cut the stems while weeding with a cutlass?
ga: Ani ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ dade shwie jwɛi lɛ nɔ loo mifo amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ oshara mli?

english: Yes, open wounds on a plant act like cuts on human skin, allowing disease-causing fungi and bacteria in the soil or air to easily enter and cause internal rot or stem decay.
ga: Hɛɛ, pilamɔ ni agbele yɛ tso nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ pilamɔ ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ boteɔ mli oya ni ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli fãi lɛ fiteɔ loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the edges of my tomato leaves look soggy, swollen, and rotten after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efɔ, efuu, ni egbo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soggy, rotting leaf edges during wet weather are a classic sign of fungal blight. Fungi thrive in excess moisture, so pruning lower leaves to improve airflow and applying fungicide helps stop the rot from destroying the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ ahe ni efɔ ni egbo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji fungal leaf blight he okadii ni ale waa. Mold lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔmɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: How do I stop black rotten spots from spreading across my cocoa pods during the wet season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi black spot rot lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black rotten spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly through rain splashes. Removing infected pods from the tree immediately and spraying copper-based fungicide keeps the rest of your harvest safe.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ oya ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ akɔɔble fee lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaf edges of my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry, brown leaf edges during hot or windy periods mean the young plant is losing water faster than its roots can absorb it. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava shields young trees from harsh sunlight and dry winds.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: Why are my pepper plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by root rot or bacterial wilt, where infected roots rot away and can no longer pump water up to the leaves. Improving soil drainage and avoiding planting peppers in flooded areas helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni egbo loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ shwiemɔ baa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛpomp nu kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni abaafee jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn soft and rotten in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Soft tuber rot happens when water gathers around the tubers in the soil, allowing rot-causing fungi to attack them. Plant your yams on high mounds or ridges so rain drains away easily.
ga: Tuber rot ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ tuber lɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ atutua amɛ. Dumɔ sweet potatoes yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ koni nugbɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ oya.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have holes in them with dark waste inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Holes and dark waste inside the center of maize plants are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Spraying recommended treatments early into the center of the plant destroys the pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ bu kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ tsui lɛ mli lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofa lɛ afɔse mra. Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ekpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly collapse at the stem and die right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seedlings falling over at the base are suffering from a condition called 'damping off,' caused by soil fungi in overly wet conditions. Using well-drained soil nursery beds and avoiding overwatering protects fragile new stems.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbee shi kɛtee shishi lɛ miina naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping’, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine mli lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Does plowing my farm with a tractor help crop roots grow better than clearing the land by hand?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ trakta baatsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ niji baatsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii?

english: Plowing loosens hard, compacted soil, making it much easier for young crop roots to spread out, drink water, and reach nutrients deep below the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã, amɛnu nu, ni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if the tractor scrapes off the top dark layer of my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji trakta lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top layer of soil contains most of the natural plant food and decomposed matter; removing it leaves behind hard infertile soil that starves young plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛ nibii ni egboi babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni wa ni wooo yibii ni baaha tso bibioo lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Does burning the dry grass after clearing my farm help or hurt my soil before I plant?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ashãa beni ajie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui dani aduɔ nii?

english: While burning leaves behind ash that gives a brief boost, hot fires destroy essential soil organisms and burn away organic food that keeps crops healthy over time.
ga: Beni etswaa lɛ, eshiɔ sũ ni haa enáa hewalɛ be kukuoo ko. Shi la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ kpataaa nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni eshãa niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I leave cut weeds on top of my cleared farm, will it choke my new crop seeds?
ga: Kɛ mishi jwɛi ni afo yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni ajie mli lɛ mli Ani ebaatsi midumɔwui heei lɛ anaa?

english: Leaving dry cut weeds on the surface acts as mulch, which keeps the soil cool, holds moisture, and gradually turns into good plant food without choking your seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni fiofio lɛ, etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii kpakpa ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieee shi.

english: Why is it important to pull out tree stumps from my land before planting root crops like cassava or yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei bibii kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu shishifãi tamɔ yucca loo sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Old tree stumps rot underground and attract pests like termites and root fungi that can easily spread and destroy your new crop roots.
ga: Tsoi akutsei momo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni egbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi amli ŋmeii. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite otsei heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ oya

english: Why should I plant my seeds in neat rows instead of scattering them across the cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets equal sunlight, air, and space to feed, while making it easier for you to weed and care for them.
ga: Row planting haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyeli he ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is too wet for tuber crops like yam and cassava to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If water sits on top of your land after rain without draining quickly, tuber crops will drown and rot underground because their roots need air to breathe.
ga: Kɛji nu ta oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni efooo oya. Tubers lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛshishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu.

english: If I clear all the big trees from my farm, will the bright sun damage my young crops?
ga: Kɛ mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baafite mitsei bibii lɛ?

english: Full sun helps crops like maize grow fast, but delicate young crops like cocoa or coffee will get scorched and dry out unless you keep some shade trees.
ga: Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo loo kɔfe baashã ni amɛbaagbi. Ja okɛ tso lɛ ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Is it better to prepare my land during the dry season or right when the first rains start?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaasaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli loo klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Preparing your land late in the dry season allows you to plant immediately when the first rains fall, giving your crops a head start before weeds take over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooosaa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to rebuild, causing crops to weaken over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛma ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my maize farm in just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kpata mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ trukaa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hatch quickly from eggs laid by moths and feed aggressively as they grow. Within a few days of hatching, young caterpillars grow larger and can consume entire fields rapidly if not controlled early.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ fɔɔ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii waa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli beni amɛfɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye he ko muu fɛɛ oya kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives and spreads quickly in wet, humid conditions. Rain drops splash the fungus onto pods, so clearing weeds and removing infected pods early helps stop the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why does Striga weed only show up in my maize field after my crop has already started growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ beni mitsei lɛ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Striga seeds stay hidden in the soil until they smell chemicals released by growing maize roots. Once maize roots grow near them, the seeds wake up, attach to the roots, and steal water and food from the crop.
ga: Striga dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnuɔ tsofai ni ŋmãa shishifãi ni miida lɛ jieɔ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa shishifãi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ Dumɔwu lɛ baate shi ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi ahe ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too wet. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving field drainage will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cassava plants if I plant the cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow thin stems and produce very small tubers underground instead of big, heavy roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I save and replant seeds from my hybrid maize harvest for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ hybrid corn dumɔwui lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the new crops will produce much smaller yields and uneven growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso hee lɛ baaha yibiiwoo fioo kwraa kɛ dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: How do I know if my groundnut farm is getting too much water from the rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli?

english: If groundnuts get waterlogged, their leaves turn pale yellow and the roots start to rot. Groundnuts prefer well-drained soil, so standing water around the stems is a sign of danger.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu eyi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Peanuts sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ ji oshara he okadi.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains develop mold even when I dried them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Grains can absorb moisture from damp air or humid storage rooms even after sun-drying. Storing grains off the ground on wooden pallets and using airtight bags keeps external moisture and mold away.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli ni mli edɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ eshɛ amɛhe po sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ to tsei anɔ ni akɛ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my local rice plants turn yellow when water stays standing in the field for too many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Even though rice needs plenty of water, the roots still need oxygen to breathe. When water stays completely still and flooded for too long without fresh flow or drainage, the roots choke, rot, and can no longer take up food from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa moŋ, shi shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lolo koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi kwraa ni eyi obɔ kɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehooo loo efooo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my rice stalks fall over easily right when the grains start to grow big and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Rice plants usually fall over (called lodging) when they are planted too close together, or when too much chemical fertilizer is used early on. This makes the stems grow tall and weak, so they cannot support the weight of heavy grain heads when wind or rain hits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ shĩa) kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii mra Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ, no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying small and thin even though the green leaves above ground are huge and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often from over-using certain fertilizers—the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches up top instead of storing food in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ mli. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: How can I tell if my soil is running out of food for my maize without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa eshwɛ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: Watch the bottom leaves of your maize. If the lower leaves start turning yellow in a 'V' shape starting from the tips while the top leaves stay green, your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow.
ga: Kwɛmɔ o-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli kɛjɛ baa lɛ naagbee, yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ adu lɛ

english: Should I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season arrives in my area?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ebashɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: It is usually better to wait until the rains become steady. The very first rain is often followed by a hot, dry period of several days, which can scorch young germinating seeds before their roots grow deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa kɛ gbii babaoo sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu baakpe lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any tomatoes during hot sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When daytime temperatures get extremely high, the pollen inside tomato blossoms gets damaged by heat and fails to make seeds. The plant then sheds the useless flowers to save its water and energy for survival.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, latsaa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, ni enyɛɛɛ efee dumɔwui. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin like sticks with very few fruits when planted close to large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsei niji ni woɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ahe lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their food. When shade from large trees blocks the light, the crop stretches upward as fast as it can to find sunshine, leaving no strength to build thick stems or heavy fruits.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji tsei wuji amli hulutsoo lɛ tsi la lɛ naa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ yaa oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ena hulu la. No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baaha tso ni mli tse loo aduawai ni tsii aba.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after I clear the land and rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are already adapted to local soil and weather conditions. Their seeds lie hidden in the soil waiting for moisture, allowing them to wake up and grab nutrients faster than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛfee nɔ ni sa shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ etee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛmiimɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa amɛteɔ shi ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting together tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves to suck out sap, or viruses spread by these insects that disturb normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my vegetable leaves during cool mornings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: That white powder is a plant fungus called powdery mildew. It breeds when nights are cool and moist, but days are warm and dry, feeding on the leaves and blocking them from getting sunlight.
ga: Nakai powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tso mli ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Amɛfɔɔ bii gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ. Shi gbii lɛ mli edɔɔ ni edɔɔ. Ye baai lɛ ni okɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. This often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients deeper into the ground or when surrounding weeds steal the crop's nourishment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Aloo be mli ni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli

english: Why do my maize crops grow better when I plant cowpeas or beans right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special organisms on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the earth. This acts as free, natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly when I clear all the weeds and leave bare soil around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni mishi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ he lɛ?

english: Bare soil is hit directly by the sun, causing soil moisture to evaporate rapidly. Covering the ground with dried leaves or grass acts like a protective shade that keeps the roots cool and holds water in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When the ground stays soaked with excess rainwater for too long, air is pushed out, causing the roots to suffocate and rot from soil fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ, abaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛje kpo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before setting any pods during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, a cocoa tree enters survival mode. It drops its fragile flowers to conserve its remaining water and energy just to keep its main leaves and stem alive.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Cacao tso lɛ baaya wala shihilɛ mli. Ekɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he koni eha baai titrii lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi kɛkɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft before they get a chance to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil to build the fruit tissue, usually caused by uneven watering or long dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee aduawai amli fãji. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too tightly together, their roots and leaves fight with neighboring plants for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because each plant gets fewer resources, they cannot grow large ears.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nibii fioo pɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ adu tsei ni toii wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does cutting off small extra branches on my pepper plants cause them to bear larger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ haa amɛwoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Removing weak side branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on unnecessary stem growth. The plant then redirects its water and plant food straight into producing bigger flowers and stronger fruits.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni he ehiaaa lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli koni ekɛ fɔfɔii wuji kɛ aduawai ni mli wa aba.

english: How do seeds resting under the dry dirt know when it is the right time to start sprouting?
ga: Te dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ be ni sa ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Seeds remain asleep until water thoroughly penetrates their outer shell. Moisture triggers internal chemical signals inside the seed, telling it to break open and send roots down into the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu lɛ eboteɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i haa tsofa okadii ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi. Ekɛɔ dumɔwu lɛ akɛ etswa ni ekɛ shishifãi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do worms hide deep inside the leaves of my maize during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the funnel of the maize stalk during hot hours to shade themselves from sunlight and hide from birds. They crawl out to feed on the crop when temperatures cool down.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Koni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe Amɛfoɔ kɛyaa koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli bawo wu.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to make food. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the field, which prevents roots from taking up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii yɔɔ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look small and weak even when I water the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal fertilizer, sunlight, and soil moisture directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong roots and produce larger yields.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains to protect them while their roots establish during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off the extra side branches growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra side shoots prevents the tomato plant from wasting vital energy on excessive stem and leaf growth, directing that energy into producing bigger and healthier fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nakai hewalɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rain for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, the roots drown and harmful fungal rot quickly develops.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baagboi oya.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the stems of my crops help them during the dry season?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, shields the soil from direct sunlight. It traps moisture in the ground longer, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Hay ni aduɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by intense heat, prolonged dry spells, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees needed to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases to build up, leading to smaller harvests every season.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and can carry hidden diseases from previous seasons, whereas certified seeds are specially bred for disease resistance and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ helai anaa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How long does a coconut seedling usually take to grow in the nursery before it is ready to be planted in my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmei ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Coconut seedlings usually take between 6 to 10 months in the nursery. They are ready to plant in the main field when they have grown 3 to 4 strong, healthy green leaves and developed a thick base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 10 yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛfee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli beni amɛyɛ baai 3 kɛyashi 4 ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shishi ni mli tse.

english: How do I select the best coconut nuts from my farm to start my own nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛje mi diɛŋtsɛ mi ŋmeii akwɛmɔ shishi?

english: Choose fully mature, brown coconuts from healthy, high-yielding mother trees. Select nuts that are medium to large, round, and still have water sloshing inside when you shake them.
ga: Halamɔ akooshi asasu ni eda kɛjɛ nyɛ tsei ni wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Halamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyashi agbo, ni yɔɔ kokroo, ni nu yɔɔ emli lolo kɛ́ otsi amɛ.

english: Plant coconut trees about 7 to 9 meters apart in a square or triangular pattern. Proper spacing gives their large fronds enough room to open and capture sunlight without shading each other.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 9 yɛ sqɛɛ loo triangle su mli. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa baai wuji lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbele amɛhe ni amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsĩii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: How many years will it take after planting before my coconut trees start producing fruits?
ga: Kɛ́ adu agbe naa lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ko jeɔ yibii womɔ shishi?

english: It depends on the variety you plant. Dwarf coconut varieties start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional Tall varieties take 6 to 8 years to start fruiting.
ga: Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Kokooi ni kɛlɛ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni akusum kooloi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young coconut trees turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign of drought stress during the dry season, lack of nutrients like potassium or nitrogen in the soil, or poor water drainage around the roots.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee hɔmɔ he haomɔ he okadi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Can I plant crops like maize or cassava between my coconut trees while the trees are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop food crops like maize, cassava, or groundnuts between coconut trees for the first 3 to 4 years while the coconut leaf canopy is still small and lets sunlight reach the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa baa lɛ ŋtayaa lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi bibioo ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my coconut trees shed their small flowers before they turn into full coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei yɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ ŋmei tso ni eyi obɔ?

english: Flower shedding happens when the tree experiences sudden weather changes, severe drought, poor soil fertility, or attack by pests like bugs and mites that damage young flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na tsakemɔi trukaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. hɔmɔ ni naa wa Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Can I use the same coconut tree for fresh drinking water and for making coconut oil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nakai ŋmei tso lɛ nɔŋŋ afee nu ni anuɔ ni he tse ni mafee ŋmei fɔ?

english: Yes, but it depends on when you harvest. For fresh drinking water, harvest young green nuts at 7 to 8 months. For oil processing, leave the nuts on the tree until they turn fully brown at 11 to 12 months.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi edamɔ be ni obaakpa lɛ nɔ. kɛha nu kpakpa ni anuɔ Kpaa mung ŋmeii bibii ni eye nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 8 kɛha mu nitsumɔ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii beni amɛye nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12 lɛ.

english: How do I know when a coconut is mature enough to yield plenty of oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie fɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: A coconut is ready for oil extraction when the husk turns completely brown, the nut feels heavy, and you hear a sharp sloshing sound of liquid when you shake it.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii kwraa. Beans lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ tsiimɔ. Ni obaanu nu lɛ mli gbee ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ okpokpo.

english: What other useful products can I make or sell from my coconut farm apart from selling fresh drinking nuts?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii krokomɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ manyɛ mafee loo mahɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Kɛ ajie ŋmeii heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Beyond fresh water nuts, you can produce copra (dried coconut meat) for oil extraction, sell coconut shell charcoal, process coconut husk fiber into peat for nurseries, or grow and sell healthy seedlings from your own nursery.
ga: Kɛfata nu-ŋma mli ŋmeii ahe lɛ Obaanyɛ ofee ŋmeii loo ni egbi hu. (ŋmei loo ni egbi) koni akɛjie mu Mli ŋmei ŋmei ni ahɔ̃ɔ Aŋmei ŋmei tsɔji ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfee ŋmei kɛha dumɔwui ni akwɛ̃ɔ. Aloo dumɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ o-nursery lɛ mli lɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in full sunlight, so they require shade trees overhead to shield them and keep the soil moist during hot weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ amɛyiteŋ koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Can I just leave any wild tree standing on my farm to provide shade for my cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi koo mli tsei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛha mi-kokoo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: No, not every tree is suitable because some wild trees harbor pests and diseases that attack cocoa, while others absorb too much water from the soil; you need specific, recommended shade trees.
ga: Dabi, jeee tso fɛɛ tso sa ejaakɛ koo mli tsei komɛi hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa kookoo. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi shwieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Osumɔɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ amɛyi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods stay small and thin instead of growing big and fat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agboi ni amɛhe ewo fɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require extra nutrients, especially organic matter in the soil, to build large, heavy pods; without proper fertilization, the tree lacks the energy to mature full-sized pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he. Titri lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Is chicken manure actually good for my crops, or is chemical fertilizer always better?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii, aloo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Chicken manure is excellent for crops because it is packed with rich organic nitrogen and nutrients that improve soil structure and hold moisture, whereas chemical fertilizers only feed the plant temporarily.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli pɛ.

english: What is the main difference between organic fertilizer and normal chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Organic fertilizer builds up the soil over time and releases nutrients slowly without washing away easily in rain, while chemical fertilizer gives a quick boost but does not improve long-term soil health.
ga: Organic fertilizers lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kpo fiofio. ni nugbɔ lɛ efɔɔɔ he mlɛo Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ oya lɛ, amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How does adding organic manure to my soil help my crops survive long dry spells?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic manure acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto water longer so your crop roots can continue drinking even when rainfall stops for days.
ga: Organic fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ anu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo po.

english: Will using organic manure on my cocoa farm really increase my total harvest yield?
ga: Ani organic fertilizer ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, organic manure constantly feeds the soil with vital nutrients, helping cocoa trees produce more flower buds and retain more maturing pods through every harvest season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa be fɛɛ be. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo. ni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be fɛɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?
