english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen in the soil; adding nutrient-rich organic fertilizer like chicken manure will restore their dark green color and energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has run out of power to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efo?

english: If your crops grow slowly, produce thin stems, or give very low yields despite good rainfall, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs organic matter added to restore its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ miida blɛoo, amɛshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli ekoŋŋ koni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some trees on a farm help nearby crops grow better instead of competing with them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛ baabɔ akaŋ lɛ?

english: Certain beneficial trees drop leaves that rot into rich natural plant food, protect crops from damaging winds, and pull nutrients up from deep underground to share with surrounding surface crops.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai ni egboi lɛ amɛshwieɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii ahe ni egbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agba he sane.

english: Why should I ferment my harvested cocoa beans before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ dani magbi lɛ?

english: Fermentation develops the rich chocolate flavor inside the beans and stops them from sprouting. Without proper fermentation, buyers will consider the beans poor quality and pay a lower price.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ haa tsokolate mli ŋɔɔ waa, ni ehaaa amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ehiii ni amɛwoɔ jara ni baa shi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick my cocoa pods off the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready to harvest when they turn fully yellow or orange depending on the variety. Harvesting green pods leaves the beans underdeveloped, while waiting too long causes beans to germinate inside the pod.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa, ni enɛ damɔ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do some cocoa farmers get many bags of cocoa every season while my farm produces very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi komɛi nine shɛɔ kookoo kotokui babaoo nɔ daa afi yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: High yields come from doing consistent field management such as regular pruning, weeding, pest control, and proper bean treatment after harvest. Skiping these tasks starves the trees and reduces pod output.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ daa tamɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ mli. jwɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitsumɔi nɛɛ ahe lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tsei lɛ ni ebaaha pod yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Can I dry my harvested cocoa beans directly on the bare ground or concrete floor?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbi mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ loo kɔnkrit nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Drying cocoa directly on the ground ruins the beans because they collect dirt, absorb moisture from the earth, and can develop mold. Spreading them on raised bamboo mats lets air flow freely underneath for clean, even drying.
ga: Cocoa ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ kɔfe ŋmeii lɛ ejaakɛ ebuaa muji naa. shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Okɛwo ŋmei ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛha hetsemɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by excessive moisture and heavy shade on your farm. Pruning your trees to let sunlight in and removing infected pods immediately stops the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ nakai baa ji hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Will cutting branches off my cocoa tree reduce the amount of cocoa I harvest?
ga: Ani kookoo tso lɛ niji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Cutting unwanted branches actually increases your yield. Pruning allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the lower branches, which reduces diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa helai baa shi ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad to pull cocoa pods off the tree with my bare hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ niji folo baagbala kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pulling pods tears the flower cushion on the tree trunk where future pods grow. Using a sharp harvester or knife leaves the cushion safe so the tree can produce more flowers and pods in upcoming seasons.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii akutso ko baa tso lɛ shishi he ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii loo tsɔne ni mli wa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha kushɛŋ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds around my cocoa trees lower my final crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ miiba mi naagbee ŋmaa lɛ shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa roots for nutrients, fertilizer, and soil water. Keeping the farm clean ensures all the nutrients in the ground go into feeding your cocoa trees instead of unwanted grass.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa niyenii yɛ o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli yɛ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does applying fertilizer help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ cacao tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer replaces essential food nutrients that cocoa trees take out of the soil over time. Well-fed trees grow stronger, hold flowers longer without dropping them, and yield more heavy pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni cacao tso lɛ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná hewalɛ. Ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli be kakadaŋŋ ni egbeeee shi. ni amɛfeɔ pods ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled, yellow leaves are usually a sign of insect attack like mirids (capsids) sucking sap from young shoots. Identifying these pests early allows you to spray appropriate treatments before they destroy the tree's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi, tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni miinu nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Ni ooona nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra Enɛ haa okɛ tsofai ni sa ni akɛbaatsa tso lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act as a natural shield, reducing heat stress and keeping the air humid so the tender leaves do not lose water faster than the young roots can absorb it.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Ha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i Enɛ ji koni baai bibii lɛ akafite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. The maize plant automatically moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newest top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves starving.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Abɛi tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni eya nɔ eda. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains last for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ enɛ waa gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the ground, water fills all the air pockets, suffocating the roots and creating ideal conditions for rot-causing fungi to attack.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ atuatsemɔ baa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon heat even though I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo tsei lɛ anɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot afternoons, water evaporates from leaf surfaces faster than the roots can draw water up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing too much moisture, but it will recover as temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ baa lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni efiteɔ lɛ he. Shi ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards into tight, twisted bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛtsi amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Their feeding damages the leaf tissues, causing them to shrink and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe

english: Why do small holes appear in my maize stems with tiny powdery sawdust coming out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei fioo ko pɛ miije kpo?

english: This damage is caused by stem borers, which are caterpillars that hatch from moth eggs and bore into the stem center. The powdery material is the waste product the caterpillar pushes out of its tunnel as it feeds inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui amli ni amɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Nibii ni akɛfee powda lɛ ji jwɛi ni ŋmei lɛ tsiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli beni eyeɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops unfertilized flowers to conserve energy rather than trying to produce weak fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii bibii.

english: How do my harvested seed yams start shooting sprouts while stored inside a dry barn without any soil or water?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ aje shishi akwɛ̃ be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni egbi ni sũ loo nu bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams have an internal biological clock regulated by plant hormones. After a natural resting period (dormancy) post-harvest, these hormones trigger sprouting using energy and moisture stored inside the tuber itself.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni yɔɔ mli ni tso mli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kudɔɔ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be (dormancy) sɛɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ tsofai nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛtsɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ato yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during storms once they develop heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli beni eyɛ kui babaoo mli lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have a deep taproot; instead, they have shallow surface roots. When a heavy bunch grows near the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for strong winds to pull the shallow roots out of wet soil.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ nu sisi nɛ mi kuɔ we. Beni kuu agbo lɛ bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya

english: Why does my harvested corn develop mold and spoil quickly if I bag it right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmãa baa oya ni efiteɔ kɛji mikɛwo baagi mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn grains contain high amounts of internal moisture. When sealed inside bags immediately, this trapped moisture creates heat and high humidity, which are perfect conditions for mold spores to grow.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛji akɛ atsĩ kotoku lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off before the tubers are big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves yellow early due to diseases like cassava mosaic virus or a lack of soil nutrients like nitrogen. When leaves drop too early, the plant cannot feed itself to grow thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Kasava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya yɛ helai tamɔ kasava mosaic virus lɛ hewɔ. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ́ baai lɛ shwie shi oya tsɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aha ehe niyenii koni eha bulb lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: If I leave my yam tubers in the ground after the vines dry up, will they spoil or keep growing?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ beni wain tsei lɛ egbi sɛɛ hu? Ani ebaagbo loo ebaaya nɔ eda?

english: Yams stop growing once the vine dies. Leaving them in the ground too long makes them easy target for soil pests like termites and can cause rot if heavy rains arrive.
ga: Sweet potatoes kpaɔ kwɛ̃mɔ kɛji wain tso lɛ gbo. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small and light even after I harvest them at the normal time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikpaa amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Small maize cobs usually happen when the crop does not get enough water during flowering or if the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus during grain filling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa bibii baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus yɛ be mli ni akɛ dumɔwui woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my rice crop fall flat on the ground just when the grains are turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Rice falls over, or lodges, when the stems are weak from applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, planting seeds too close together, or from sudden heavy rains pushing down heavy seed heads.
ga: Omɔ shwieɔ shi loo efoɔ kɛ́ eshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ kɛjɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa ni tsiɔ dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa pods turn black because of Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during cool, wet weather and in dark, overly shaded farms.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Ni yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is completely ready for harvest so buyers don't reject it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa bɔni afee ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ akakpoo amɛ?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the individual fingers become full and rounded, losing their sharp edges, and the dried flowers at the tip of the fruit fall off easily.
ga: Plantains efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ nine fɛɛ nine eyi ni ebɔle ehe. ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ laaje Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ naagbee lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my tomato fruits start rotting at the bottom right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Bottom rot in tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happens when there is inconsistent watering or when the soil lacks calcium while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo kɛ́ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers instead of turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus on leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, loo kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why are my garden egg fruits very small and full of tiny holes when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni ŋmeii bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Be ni mikpaa lɛ

english: Tiny holes and undersized fruit are caused by pests like fruit borers that eat into the crop early on, draining the plant's nutrients before the fruit can mature properly.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ aduawai ni dalɛ faaa lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fruit borers lɛ kɛbaa. ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii mra Ehaa tso lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai lɛ hoɔ dani aduawai lɛ baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits split open on the farm before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ tswaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelons split open when there is a sudden heavy rainfall after a long dry period, causing the inside of the fruit to fill with water and expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelon lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli eyiɔ kɛ nu ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do all my tomato plants produce fruit at the exact same time, making it hard for me to sell everything before it spoils?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ dani egbo.

english: Certain crop varieties are 'determinate,' meaning they grow to a fixed size, flower, and set fruit all at once. If you plant them on the same day, they will ripen together. To spread your harvest across several weeks, you can stagger your planting dates or choose 'indeterminate' varieties that bear fruit continuously over a longer period.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ‘ehi shi’, ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdaraa kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii shikome. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ, amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli. koni okɛgbɛ okpamɔ lɛ oshwã otsii babaoo mli Obaanyɛ otsake gbii ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ loo ohala srɔtoi ni ‘atsɔɔɔ’ ni yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do market buyers often prefer onions imported from Burkina Faso over the ones grown locally in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ sabala ni akɛjɛɔ Burkina Faso lɛ fe nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Onions grown in drier, hotter climates typically have lower moisture content and thicker skins. This makes them firmer and allows them to last much longer during transport and storage without rotting, compared to crops grown under high humidity.
ga: Sabolai ni adu yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi, ni mli edɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi kɛ hewolo ni mli wa. Enɛ haa ewaa ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko kɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ni efiteee. kɛ akɛto tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ he.

english: What happens inside a sealed sack of freshly harvested vegetables if I leave it sitting under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni baa mli yɛ aduawai heei ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli? Ni kɛji mishi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi hu?

english: Harvested crops continue to breathe and release heat and moisture. When trapped inside a hot, enclosed bag, this creates a warm, humid environment that rapidly speeds up rotting, softens the produce, and encourages mold growth.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ baaha fitemɔ aya oya. ni haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa

english: Is it safe for me to harvest and sell my garden eggs immediately after spraying them with chemicals to kill pests?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni mikɛbaahɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, every crop chemical requires a specific waiting period known as a 'pre-harvest interval' (PHI). You must wait a set number of days after spraying so the chemical can break down safely before the produce is picked and consumed by people.
ga: Dabi Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ biɔ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Pre-harvest period’ (PHI) biɔ ni omɛ gbii babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsofai lɛ anyɛ afite shweshweeshwe dani gbɔmɛi abaŋɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ ni amɛye.

english: If all the farmers in my area plant cabbage during the same rainy season, how will that affect my crop?
ga: Kɛji okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ du kaabe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Te ebaasa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe eha tɛŋŋ?

english: While your cabbages will grow normally, having the same crop across many neighboring fields allows pests and diseases to multiply and spread very fast from farm to farm. Additionally, harvesting at the same time creates an oversupply in the market, driving selling prices down.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cabbage lɛ daa bɔ ni sa po lɛ, Ni ooona ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe. Amɛyi fa babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ kroko mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, ŋmaa ni akpaa yɛ be kome too mli lɛ haa nibii ni fa fe nine baa jara nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava roots when I plant cassava on the exact same farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shishifãi bibii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava absorbs large amounts of specific nutrients from the soil, especially potassium. Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts these vital nutrients without giving the soil time to replenish, leading to weaker plants and smaller yields over time.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ potassium Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaafite niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants during very hot and dry weather without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa ni egbiɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: When pepper plants experience extreme heat and lack of water, they undergo heat stress. To save their own lives and preserve energy, the plants shed their flowers (a process called blossom drop) instead of spending resources to grow fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kpe lɛ, Amɛkɛ hulutsoo he haomɔ baakpe. Koni okɛhere bo diɛŋtsɛ owala ni okɛ ohewalɛ akafite. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ. (nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fɔfɔi) lɛ kɛ nibii tsuɔ nii moŋ ni ekɛduɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my stored cowpeas turn into powder after a few months even though I dried them well in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ hulutsoo be mli egbi amɛ moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils often lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the seeds while the crop is still standing in the field. After harvest, these eggs hatch inside your storage bags, and the larvae eat the inside of the grain, leaving behind powdery waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anyɛɛɛ ana nakai yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baafɔ yɛ onitoo kotoku lɛ mli. ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. kɛtsɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni eshiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up with strange patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe mfoniri ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow, wrinkled leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the leaves from capturing sunlight properly, which severely reduces root growth beneath the ground.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ aba shi waa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into narrow tubes when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni shwane hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism maize uses to conserve water. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight and dry air, slowing down the amount of water escaping from the plant.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he. Tsei haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni baa amɛbai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted beside them to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make green leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color so they can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eŋɔlii lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to put into storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo baagi mli?

english: If you bite or press a maize grain with your thumbnail and it leaves a dent, it still holds too much water. Properly dried grains should be hard and break with a sharp click; storing wet grain causes mold and pests to quickly ruin your crop.
ga: Kɛji okɛ otsitsi bibioo lɛ ŋmɔ loo onyɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ko nɔ ni efolɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ yɛ nu babaoo lolo. Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni egbɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afite onibii oya.

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots compete heavily with each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from neighboring plants. Giving each crop enough space allows it to feed well and produce bigger fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the soil when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When continuous rain waterlogs the farm and water cannot drain away, the roots drown from a lack of air, which allows rot and fungi to destroy the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, anyɛɛɛ ajie ŋmɔji kɛ nu kɛya. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii afite shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my maize plants during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These pests, known as Fall Armyworms, feed heavily on young leaf tissue. They hide deep inside the funnel of the maize stem during the hot daytime to escape heat and predators, coming out when it is cool to chew on the leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii babaoo. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni amɛjo hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ anaa foi Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei niji awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight, which creates the energy needed to expand the tuber under the ground. Staking the vines keeps the leaves lifted into the sun and off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and boosting tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛgbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ baa. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ ŋwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni ehaa yitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Plants shed their flowers when they experience severe heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of soil food. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of conserving energy to survive unfavorable weather until conditions improve.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii amli kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look droopy in the hot afternoon but stand up fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛfeɔ ehee ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: Under hot sun, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can draw it from the dry soil, causing the plant to temporarily wilt to conserve water. During the cooler night, the roots catch up on absorbing water, making the plant firm again by morning.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Gbimɔ tsei yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu akafite. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ nu. Ha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and turning wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat and dry soil. The plant curls its leaves to reduce surface exposure and cut down on water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize plants need to build strong green leaves and produce good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni amɛwo toi kpakpai.

english: Why does putting fertilizer right against the stem of my crop burn the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haa tsei lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is full of strong salts. When it touches the soft stem directly, it draws water out of the plant tissues and causes chemical burns that can kill the crop.
ga: Fertilizer eyi kɛ ŋmei ni mli wa. Kɛji ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsofa shãa ni baanyɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade from temporary nurse crops like plantain trees to keep them cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow. If tiny soil pests like nematodes damage the roots, or if the soil is too loose, the heavy stem cannot support itself in strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nematodes lɛ kpata shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse tsɔ Tso ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: What causes small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the leaf funnel of young maize and chew the growing leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress, because the plant lacks the resources to turn the bloom into a heavy fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous plants trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural food supplier for the nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers remain very small if I leave weeds around the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ gɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight away from the yam leaves, leaving the vine with no energy to swell the tuber under the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ sweet potato baai amli. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready to harvest without digging them up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛtsuuu nii?

english: When cassava is ready for harvesting, the plant leaves naturally start turning yellow and dropping off, leaving mostly bare stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baaje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. Ni tsɔne lɛ mli fã ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko pɛ eshwɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the afternoon sun even if the ground was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi po.

english: Hot afternoon air makes leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can drink it up, so the plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from losing too much moisture.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They need shade trees or plantains around them to block strong sunlight and keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yam plants are vines that grow best when they can climb toward the sun. Staking holds the leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to form large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɔ kɛya hulu la mli. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small plantain shoots growing at the base of my main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: If too many young shoots grow around one main tree, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, resulting in larger and heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, tso titri kome Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain lɛ feɔ agbo ni etsiiɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem starts to crack open due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient it needs to build green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni afee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil-based pests and diseases to build up and attack your future harvests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛtutuaa onibii ni obaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does putting animal manure into my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts as natural plant food that slowly releases essential nutrients into the ground while helping the soil hold onto rainwater longer during dry spells.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni yaa hiɛ fiofio. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni ajieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant does not get steady amounts of water, causing the plant stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu babaoo be fɛɛ be. Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ

english: What is making holes in the leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋ lɛ baa?

english: Holes in the inner leaves of maize are typically caused by armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves to feed on the tender young growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your plants starved of the basic things they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, otsei lɛ bɛ shishijee nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on my land before or at the same time as my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani loo kɛfata kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as temporary shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa plants and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close to each other so I can fit more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ bɔni afee ni adu tsei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak trees that yield fewer pods and make it easier for diseases to spread from tree to tree.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kwɔlɔɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ hela lɛ baajɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko nɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and fresh air can pass through the tree canopy. This prevents damp conditions that breed diseases, keeps the tree manageable in height, and forces the plant to direct its energy into producing large cocoa pods instead of just leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tsei lɛ akutsei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ni onyɛ tsei anɔ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji moŋ fe baai kɛkɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to let tall weeds grow around the base of my cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle he? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ oshara.

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients meant for your cocoa trees. They also trap excess humidity at ground level and create hiding places for pests like rodents and insects that damage cocoa pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ mli lɛ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ hu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ amɛhe.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, cool, and dark environments. Clearing weeds, pruning branches for air movement, and picking off affected pods quickly will stop the fungal spores from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, jɛmɛ ejɔ, kɛ duŋ. Jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ oya. Ehaa fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: What is causing small black burn spots on the stems of my young cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni kɛ shãa diji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi kookoo nine bibioo lɛ nɔ

english: Those dark patches are damage caused by mirids (also called capsids), which are tiny insects that suck sap from young stems and pods. Their toxic saliva kills the plant tissue, which can dry out whole branches if not treated early.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni mirids (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ fiteɔ. Muji ni yɔɔ gbeyei gbeɔ tso mli fãji. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the plant is stressed, usually because the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or because the seedling is getting too much direct sunlight without enough water. Adding manure or fertilizer and providing proper shade helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni aha hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do so many small flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can support, dropping the extras. However, excessive flower drop happens when the tree is under stress from dry weather, poor soil fertility, or pest damage.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ laajeɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ haomɔ shishi kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ

english: How does a long Harmattan dry season affect my cocoa trees, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Harmattan brings dry winds and heat that dry out the soil and cause cocoa leaves to drop. You can protect your trees by retaining permanent shade trees on the farm and spreading dry leaves or mulch around the tree bases to hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbiɔ ni ehaa kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu otsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni oookwɛ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie tso lɛ shishi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cassava inside my mature cocoa farm to get extra food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda mli koni maná niyenii kroko?

english: It is not recommended to plant cassava inside mature cocoa farms. Cassava roots are heavy feeders that aggressively steal water and nutrients from the soil, which starves the cocoa roots and lowers your cocoa yield.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ amli. Cassava shishifãi ji niyenii ni tsii ni kɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kookoo shishifãi lɛ, ni ebaaha kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: My farm land has a lot of small stones and rocks, so can crops still grow well on it?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi kɛ tɛi bibii babaoo. Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Yes, crops can grow on stony land because small stones help trap soil moisture and hold warmth. While you need to clear large rocks so roots can expand, crops like cassava, yam, and legumes can thrive in gravelly soil if given enough organic matter.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ lɛ ejaakɛ tɛi bibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa edɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe baahia ni ojie tɛi wuji koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã moŋ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmei shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji amɛná nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Which specific crops survive best if my soil is hard and full of stones?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ?

english: Hardy root crops like cassava and tough grains like sorghum or millet handle rocky soil best. Their roots are strong enough to push through hard ground to search for nutrients and water deep underground.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ dumɔwui ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsuɔ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ amɛtao niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is it true that I should remove every single stone from my farm field to get a good yield?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ esa akɛ majie tɛ fɛɛ tɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: No, you only need to remove large boulders that block planting. Leaving small gravel and tiny stones on top of the ground actually protects your soil from baking in the hot sun and prevents heavy rains from washing away your good topsoil.
ga: Dabi, ehe miihia ni ojie tɛi wuji fɛɛ ni tsiɔ dumɔwu lɛ naa lɛ kɛkɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tɛi bibii kɛ tɛi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does water wash away all my topsoil and crop seeds whenever it rains heavily on my rocky ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hoɔ mishikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa yɛ mishishi tɛsaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain rushes down hard or sloping land quickly because the soil cannot absorb water fast enough. Building low rows of stones or soil ridges across the slope acts like a dam, slowing down the water so it soaks into the ground to feed your crop roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo gɔŋji anɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Tɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni afeɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ dam. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya bɔni afee ni enyɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and look tired when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Maize rolls its leaves inward during hot hours as a survival trick to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This stops water from escaping into the air too quickly, helping the plant hold onto moisture until the soil cools down.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How do deep-rooted crops help my land become better for future crops?
ga: Te tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Deep roots act like natural pickaxes that punch holes through hard underground layers. When those deep roots rot after harvest, they leave open channels in the earth that help air, rainwater, and future crop roots penetrate deeper into the soil.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shɔvel, ni amɛfoɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ shishigbɛ tsũ ni wa lɛ mli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ Amɛshiɔ gbɛi ni agbele yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ nu, kɛ wɔsɛɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when I plant them in untreated, hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni asaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Hard or poor soil lacks decayed leaves and organic matter, so plants cannot get the food they need until you feed the ground with manure or compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ehiii lɛ bɛ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛyashi obaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my crops hydrated during dry spells if I don't have pipe water or irrigation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ nu ni hoɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ hu?

english: You can cover the bare ground around your crops with dry grass, straw, or old crop leaves. This practice, called mulching, acts like a blanket that shades the soil, stopping the hot sun from evaporating the groundwater.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo tso baai momoi akpã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans alongside my main crops help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take invisible food from the air and store it in their roots as nitrogen. When planted near other crops, they share this natural plant food and feed the surrounding soil without you having to buy expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ niyenii ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nitrogen gbɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi Amɛbaajara tsei niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What can I add to hard, low-quality soil to produce a large abundance of food like rich farms do?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ehiii lɛ he koni maná niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmɔ ni baa nii?

english: Adding animal manure, composted leaves, or crop waste turns hard soil into rich, spongy ground. This organic material holds water longer, feeds soil organisms, and provides continuous food to crops so you get much higher harvest yields.
ga: Koolooi aŋmei ni akɛ baai ni edɔ Loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ fata he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ haa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ onine shɛɔ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ babaoo nɔ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when the soil has too much water around the roots. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green so the plant can grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abɛi baai lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off the plant before making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiihao. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap, or by a virus carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why does my cassava produce big bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted in rich shaded soil, it puts all its energy into growing top leaves to search for sunlight instead of storing energy in the underground roots.
ga: Beni ŋmãa nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ena hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food that builds the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they can get maximum sun and prevents leaves from rotting on the wet soil.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ yɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni ehaaa baa lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and aggressively steal the nutrients and fertilizer from the soil, leaving your crops weak even if there is enough rainwater.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: How does putting dry leaves or grass around my crop roots help them survive hot weather?
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents sunlight from drying out the ground water too quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate root systems and lose water quickly through their leaves under harsh sun and dry winds. They need temporary shade trees, like plantains, to shield them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees lean over and fall when they start bearing heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛwo yibii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are soft and fibrous, so the weight of a heavy bunch easily pulls the plant down. Using strong wooden poles (propping) supports the stem and protects the plant from snapping in strong winds.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyɛ tsɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji ni tsii lɛ ahe tsiimɔ gbalaa tso lɛ kɛbaa shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Tso ni mli wa (nibii ni fiɔ sɛɛ) ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni ehaaa tso lɛ akumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees get sunburned and stressed when exposed to strong sunlight without cover. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides canopy shade and retains soil moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hulu shãa amɛ ni amɛhaoɔ amɛhe kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I select healthy plantain suckers to start my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' with narrow leaves and a solid stem base. Ensure the underground corm is clean, firm, and free of dark rot marks or holes, which indicates pest infestation like stem borers.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante tso’ ni baai lɛ mli etse kɛ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe tse, amɛhe wa ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii diji bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers eba.

english: Why does my maize produce small, incomplete cobs even when the stalks grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeee emuu eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall but produce poor cobs when planted too close together or when they lack sufficient nitrogen during early growth. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough sunlight and nutrients to fill out the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ daa shi ewooo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli eyi.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many lush green leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fix their own nitrogen from the air into the soil. Adding extra high-nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing foliage instead of flowering and setting seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas saa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni miida lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji baawo mli lɛ

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my yam vines as soon as they start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɔ pɛ.

english: Yam vines need full sunlight and soil nutrients to feed the developing tuber underground. Weeds quickly choke young vines and steal water, leading to thin stalks and small yam tubers at harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii. Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ wain tsei bibii lɛ anɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ nu. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji akpa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by small sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites, which also spread plant viruses. Spraying neem seed extract or insecticidal soap early keeps these insect populations down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips loo mites, ni amɛ hu amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Neem dumɔwui amli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaha kooloi nɛɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why are the lower fronds on my young oil palm trees drying out and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Lower fronds brown prematurely when the tree experiences prolonged dry spells or potassium deficiency in the soil. Applying balanced fertilizer and keeping the base mulched helps maintain green, productive fronds.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ mra kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when soil moisture swings rapidly between dry and wet, or when day temperatures get extremely high. Regular watering at the root level keeps soil moisture steady so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nɔ ni edɔ teŋ. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi baanyɛ afee aduawai.

english: Why are my watermelons splitting open right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ mli gbalaa dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons split when a heavy rain or sudden watering follows a dry spell. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the rind can stretch, causing it to crack open.
ga: Watermelon mli gbalaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu ho trukaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot within three days of harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ gbii etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots deteriorate quickly after harvest because exposure to air triggers rapid oxidation and spoilage. Leaving roots unharvested in the ground until you are ready to sell or process them preserves their quality.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa oksided ni fiteɔ oya lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ oshi shishifãi ni akpaaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ loo obaatsu he nii lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize eats that natural food left behind and grows much better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa baaye adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ kwraa ni ŋmãa ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let in sunlight and air helps keep the pods dry and free from the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ŋmeii bɛ mli.

english: Why do I keep finding tiny holes chewed through the leaves of my young corn crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Be fɛɛ be lɛ, mikɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yeɔ nii?

english: Small holes in corn leaves are typically caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding on the tender foliage. Inspecting the center funnel of the plant early in the morning helps you catch them early before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ mra. dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy and wilted in the hot afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil, causing temporary wilting. As long as the soil has moisture, they will recover and stand straight again in the cooler evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ he okadii baa Be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Ebaatsa ehe ni ebaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and light shade during extreme heat help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and blocks weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests specific to that crop to multiply. Rotating with different crops keeps the soil balanced and starves out crop-specific pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa nakai tso pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cassava tubers staying thin and small even after growing for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nɔ ni fe afi etsu nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand into thick tubers. If the soil is too hard or compacted, or if the land lacks nutrients, the plant spends its energy surviving instead of growing big tubers.
ga: Kassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei bibii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ bulb agboi.

english: Why do certified seeds bought from an input dealer produce better crops than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ amlijalɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and treated to resist common local diseases and withstand dry spells. Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller harvests and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa. Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa yibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight when they are small. Planting quick-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa leaves from scorching while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to return to a healthy green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛfee baai ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eku esɛɛ etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around my crops help them survive the dry season?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry leaves or straw acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and retains water longer after it rains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with tiny fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops have to fight for sunlight, space, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to absorb what it needs to grow thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ abɔi hulu la, ŋwɛi, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward into the sunlight to make food. Staking gets the vines off the ground, ensuring maximum sun exposure and preventing soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves, which helps the yam tuber grow big.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ aná babaoo ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: What causes tiny holes in my corn leaves and white powder inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworm caterpillars that feed on tender plant shoots. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil protects the corn before the leaves are destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ ŋmãa mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni ji bio-insecticide loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmãa lɛ he dani baai lɛ afite.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks water tubes inside the plant's stem. Once blocked, water cannot travel up to the leaves, making the plant look dry even in moist soil.
