ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ anaa. Kɛji akɛ atsĩ gbɛ Nu lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ po nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting quickly if left in waterlogged soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the soil remains soaked with water for too long, oxygen gets cut off, allowing soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without producing peppers during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ni amɛwooo pepper yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall and cloudy weather reduce sunshine and prevent bees from pollinating flowers. When plants get stressed by too much water and cold, they drop their flowers to save energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ atatu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa hulu la lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii. Beni nu babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i haoɔ tsei lɛ. Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest yield less than newly bought certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and are more likely to carry diseases or weak traits. Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to produce uniform, strong plants with high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli, ni ekolɛ amɛhiɛɔ helai loo sui ni egbɔjɔ. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Which way should I point the buds on my cassava stem when planting it in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, te esa akɛ otsɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ oha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should always plant the cassava stem with the small buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant the stick upside down, the plant spends too much of its energy turning its new shoots around, which leaves you with weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ odu cassava tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji okɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ shwie shi Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii heei. Enɛ baaha odalɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni oyitso hu afee bibioo.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: When too many small shoots grow around one plantain tree, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil. Removing the extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough nourishment to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ ni bɔle dumɔwu kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashiɔ niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under the strong sun. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide big leafy umbrellas that keep the young cocoa cool and moist until they are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves. This often happens after heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil away from the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny natural partners in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the dirt. When those plants die, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground as natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eyɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi bibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ nakai tsei lɛ gboi lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the base of my pepper plants during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a blanket that shades the soil. It stops the hot sun from drying out the earth quickly, keeps the roots cool, and reduces the amount of watering your peppers need.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just crawling on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for growing big tubers. When the vines trail on the hot ground, they can easily rot from soil moisture and produce small tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awó sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la babaoo aná bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni eha niyenii aha bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ. Kɛ wain tsei shwie hei ni mli edɔ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛfee bulbs bibii.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before any small tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly very wet. Heat stress causes the plant to protect itself by shedding flowers it cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ haomɔ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baa lɛ miifee bu ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides deep inside the center fold of the maize plant during the day, eating the soft leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii ni ayeɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up tightly toward the sky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from under the young leaves, or from a virus spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaf tissues twist as they try to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Baai lɛ amli fãji ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients that help the maize grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural shade trees, giving young cocoa the protection and moisture it needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hebuu kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why will my crops produce smaller harvests if I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves every plant weak and small, reducing the total crop yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I leave them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain makes heavy soil soggy, which prevents air from reaching the cassava roots. Waterlogged roots suffocate and attract fungi, causing the cassava tubers to rot underground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa ŋmeii. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny black droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-corn baai kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii amli lɛ baa? Yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize stem. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening reaches the caterpillars effectively.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes too drastically. Heat stress prevents the flower from forming fruit, so the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake tsɔ. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to lift and stake my yam vines high off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ ni mikɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light while preventing fungal diseases caused by soil splash.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ la ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sũ mli shwiemɔ kɛbaa lɛ ni atsĩɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil. It holds water in the ground longer, reduces soil heat, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rain soaks the soil deep enough that a handful of earth from a few inches down stays together when squeezed. Planting too early in lightly moist soil can dry out and kill the germinating seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi ni jɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ fioo lɛ aba ekomefeemɔ mli kɛji akɛ afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees or plantains growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct heat and sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains protects them from getting scorched, keeps the soil moist, and helps the young trees survive their early stages.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la fiteɔ amɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shãa naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shishijee mli

english: How do I know the best time of the year to plant my cocoa seeds or seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo ŋmeii loo dumɔwui?

english: The best time to plant cocoa is at the start of the major rainy season, usually around April or May in Ghana. Planting when the rains begin allows the seedlings to establish deep root systems before the dry harmattan season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April loo May mli yɛ Ghana. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani harmatta ni egbi lɛ baashɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely forces them to compete for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak trees that produce fewer pods. Proper spacing also lets air flow through the farm, which prevents diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kokoo tsei kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu he. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akamɔ mɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the trees are suffering from a lack of nutrients in the soil, severe dry weather, or damage from pests like capsids sucking the juices from the leaves and stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa loo nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ capsids ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree does not get enough water, if the weather is extremely hot, or if there are not enough tiny insects (midges) around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rotting is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shady, and overcrowded farms during heavy rains. Regular pruning and picking off infected pods helps keep it under control.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji blackpod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei lɛ ahe daa ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees instead of letting them grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tso mli moŋ fe ni maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or unnecessary branches so the tree can focus its energy on growing healthy pods. It also opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air, which stops humidity from causing fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ hu koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ kpaa.

english: How do weeds growing under my cocoa trees hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil nutrients away from your cocoa roots. They also create a damp hiding place for harmful pests and diseases that can attack your cocoa pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ amli. Amɛfeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ hu kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atutua o-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm needs fertilizer to help my cocoa grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua mi-kokoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your cocoa trees grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves, or produce very few pods even when rainfall is good, it means the soil lacks essential nutrients and requires organic or inorganic fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa tso lɛ miida blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo ewoɔ pods fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa nɛɔ moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii.

english: How can I keep the soil on my cocoa farm from drying out too quickly during hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaving fallen cocoa leaves and natural plant waste on the ground acts as mulch. This ground cover shields the soil from direct sunlight, holds moisture in the dirt longer, and slowly decays into rich plant food.
ga: Kookoo baai ni egbee shi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: How do I choose between planting Sugarloaf pineapples and MD2 pineapples on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala Sugarloaf Pineapple kɛ MD2 Pineapple ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Sugarloaf pineapples are very sweet, juicy, and popular in local Ghanaian markets, while MD2 pineapples are firmer, have a longer shelf life, and are preferred for international export. Your choice depends on whether you plan to sell locally or send your harvest overseas.
ga: Sugarloaf Pineapple lɛ ŋɔɔ waa, eyɛ nu ni ehe gbɛi waa yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni MD2 pineapple lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Eyɛ shihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni asumɔɔ kɛha majimaji ateŋ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ. Nɔ ni obaahala lɛ damɔ kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli loo okɛ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ amaje maŋsɛɛ.

english: Why do different pineapple varieties taste different even when grown on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ srɔtoi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ po lɛ?

english: Each crop variety has its own natural genetics that control how much sugar, juice, and fiber it produces. Even in the same soil, a Sugarloaf pineapple naturally builds higher sweetness, whereas varieties like MD2 build a balance of acid and sweetness designed for transport.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii ni kudɔɔ bɔ ni sugar, nu, kɛ fiber ni ekɛbaa lɛ fa ha. Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ po lɛ, Sugarloaf pineapple lɛ hu feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi tamɔ MD2 lɛ feɔ acidity kɛ sweetness ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha gbɛfaa lɛ.

english: Why do my pineapples sometimes taste sour even though they look ripe on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ mli ŋɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Pineapples do not continue to get sweeter after they are picked. If you harvest them too early based on skin color alone before the natural sugars build up inside while attached to the plant, the fruit will stay sour.
ga: Pineapple lɛ efeŋ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ dɔŋŋ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ okpa mra tsɔ yɛ hewolonɔ su pɛ nɔ Enɛ ji dani adebɔɔ mli sugars lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ mli be mli ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he. Yibii lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does the timing of my harvest affect the sugar level in my fruits?
ga: Te kpamɔ be lɛ saa sugar ni yɔɔ aduawai amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fruits build up their sweetness during the final stages of growth on the plant. Timing your harvest correctly allows the crop to fully absorb sunlight and nutrients, ensuring the sugars reach their highest peak before picking.
ga: Yibii lɛ naa ŋɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ naagbee fãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ato be ni sa ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa sugar lɛ shɛɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Can heavy rain right before harvest change the taste of my crop?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani akpaa nii lɛ baanyɛ atsake miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ?

english: Yes, excessive water taken up by the plant right before harvest can dilute the natural sugars inside the fruit, making the harvest taste watery or less sweet than expected.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ baanyɛ aha adebɔɔ mli sugars ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ afee bibioo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ baafee nɔ ni nu loo nɔ ni ŋɔɔ bɛ mli fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ.

english: Why is the quality of water I use so important for my crop health?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ lɛ?

english: Water carries nutrients into the plant's roots. If the water contains harmful chemicals, high salts, or filth, it can block nutrient absorption, stunt plant growth, or damage the internal development of the crop.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ nu lɛ mli, ŋoo fa yɛ mli, loo eyɛ muji lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlibotemɔ naa. etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa loo efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli shweremɔ

english: How can I tell if the water source near my farm is safe to water my crops with?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu jɛɛhe ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ?

english: Safe farming water should be clear, free from foul smells, and free from visible oil or scum on top. To be sure, you can consult an extension officer to test for hidden chemical pollutants or bacteria.
ga: Esa akɛ nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ afee nɔ ni mli tse. Ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo ni mu loo muji ni anaa bɛ mli. koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ Obaanyɛ oyakwɛ extension official ko koni eka tsofai loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ akwɛ.

english: What happens to my fruits if my farm water becomes polluted by nearby activities?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nifeemɔi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ fite nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Polluted water carries harmful substances that can seep into plant roots, leading to diseased plants, poor fruit quality, off-flavors, or crop yields that are unsafe for human consumption.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ abote tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ yɛ nu fɔŋ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ hela. Yibii ni ehiii, ŋɔɔmɔ ni ehiii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha gbɔmɔ niyenii

english: How do I secure a clean and reliable water supply if I want to farm year-round?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nu ni mli tse ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni matsu okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can identify a reliable water source by digging a protected well, constructing a water storage tank for rainwater, or using a river supply that is situated away from washing areas and chemical runoff.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu bu ni abuɔ he lɛ ni oootse lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ nutoohe kɛha nugbɔ nu. Aloo okɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni kɛ he ni afɔɔ he kɛ tsofai ni hoɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do some of my crops grow well while others right next to them look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Crops can react differently due to minor variations in water access, root strength, or subtle soil differences. Ensuring uniform watering and proper land preparation helps all plants grow at the same pace.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ tsakemɔi bibii ni baa yɛ nu ni anáa lɛ mli lɛ he. shishifãi ahewalɛ loo srɔtofeemɔi fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ oyaiyeli kome mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow starting from the bottom leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This yellowing is usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. When maize does not get enough nitrogen from the ground, it takes nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋmãa ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmãa heei anɔ lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my cowpea field have thick green leaves but very few beans inside the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ pod lɛ mli?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes leguminous crops like cowpeas put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowering and producing pods. Cowpeas fix their own nitrogen from the air, so they require very little added nitrogen.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi ni amɛfee ŋmeii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa amɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen fioo ko pɛ he hiaa ni akɛfataa he.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a soil-borne fungus that spreads rapidly through rain splashes and high humidity. Clearing excess shade branches and harvesting ripe or infected pods regularly helps keep humidity down and prevents the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shi ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or thrips sucking the plant sap and transmitting viral infections. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or targeted sprays protects the new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo thrips kɛ chili baa baa, ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ muawai amɛshwãa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo spot spray ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai heei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, flat, rotten patches at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot and happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium. Irregular watering often prevents roots from absorbing calcium properly, so maintaining consistent soil moisture helps solve the problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ haaa amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baatsu naagba lɛ he nii.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without forming small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or when the tree is stressed by intense heat and dry winds. Keeping moderate shade trees in the farm protects midges and reduces temperature stress on cocoa flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo be mli ni latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ dwarfism he, ni ebaaha hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni baa kookoo fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil remains waterlogged for too long, depriving roots of air and allowing soil fungi to attack. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fãa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light winds when bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa beni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are easily weakened by root-knot nematodes or banana weevils eating the root base. Propping up fruit-bearing trees with sturdy wooden forks gives them physical support against light winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishifãi amli ni ji nematodes loo banana ŋmeii ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa wo aduawai tsei ahe fɛo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua amɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa lɛ akatswa amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots inside my yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔŋ yɛ mi-sweet potatoes ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their dormancy and sprout when exposed to warmth, light, or rising humidity. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded barn on raised racks slows down sprouting and preserves tuber quality.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ wɔɔhe ni ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛwo dɔlɛ, la, loo fɛ̃i ni yaa hiɛ. Too atomo yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, shade, kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli yɛ adekai ni awó nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into fine powder and get tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda kpakpa mli ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: This damage is caused by maize weevils that bore into the seeds to feed and lay eggs. Drying your maize properly until it is hard and storing it in airtight containers or hermetic bags smothers the pests and prevents damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmãa ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli koni amɛye nii ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni akɛto tsɛnsi loo kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaajie ŋmeii kɛya ni ebaatsi nɔ ni efite lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to stay green and grow fast. This often happens when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni esa akɛ ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli.

english: How come my cassava roots stay small even though the leaves on top look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛji ŋmeii moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the plant puts all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to expand the tubers in the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní konɛ e kɛ bulb nɛ wo zugba a mi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from intense heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ ŋtayaa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ ŋtayaa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture stress pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy and protect themselves from drying out completely.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛtsi amɛhe gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil each time and allows specific pests and diseases to permanently live and grow in your field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi hiɔ shi daa ni amɛdaraa yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker when I leave weeds to grow around them during the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛji mishi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from young crops when the crops need those resources the most.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli yɛ be mli ni nakai nibii lɛ he hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack and eat my maize leaves so quickly during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Warm and dry weather helps pests like armyworms multiply much faster, while young maize leaves remain soft and easy for them to chew.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi tamɔ armyworms ni amɛshwereɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny invisible pests, like aphids or mites, are sucking the sap from the underside of the leaves or spreading a plant virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahe okadi. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Amɛmiinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli loo amɛmiigbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my mature maize plants fall over easily when strong winds bring heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ha nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over if its root system is shallow, which happens if the soil is too hard for roots to dig deep or if seeds were planted too close to the surface.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji akɛ eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsa kɛya shɔŋŋ. aloo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ

english: Why do my bean plants produce lots of green leaves but very few pod beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ miiwo baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: If bean plants receive too much water or rich fertilizer early on, they spend all their energy making leaves instead of producing the flowers that turn into pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo loo ŋmeii babaoo mra lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee fɔfɔi ni bafeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Can I save groundnut seeds from my last harvest to plant next season, or should I buy new ones from local experts?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli nilelɔi adɛŋ?

english: While you can save seeds from your own harvest, buying certified seeds from local agricultural experts ensures high germination rates, strong resistance to local diseases like groundnut rosette, and much better yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ ohere dumɔwui kɛjɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli moŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nilelɔi adɛŋ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai tamɔ ŋmei rose. ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ kwraa

english: If I want to start a business growing high-quality seeds to sell to other farmers in Ghana, where do I get the right starting material?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi nitsumɔ ko ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ, nɛgbɛ maná shishijee nibii ni sa?

english: To grow seeds for commercial sale, you must source certified foundation seeds from recognized agricultural research institutions or approved seed dealers in Ghana to guarantee the seed quality, purity, and legality of your business.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni odu dumɔwui kɛha jarayeli. Esa akɛ oyahe shishijee dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ loo dumɔwui jarayelɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. hetsemɔ kɛ mla naa nitsumɔ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ

english: Why do groundnut flowers bloom above the ground, but the actual nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi ŋmei diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a unique growth process called pegging. After the yellow flowers on top of the plant are pollinated, long stems called 'pegs' grow downwards, push into the soil, and develop into pods under the ground.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛdaraa ni atsɛɔ lɛ pinning. Beni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ daa kɛyaa shishi, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my groundnut crop turning yellow and curling up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are often symptoms of Groundnut Rosette Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny insects called aphids that suck sap from the plant stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji Rosette Groundnut Disease, ni ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids ni nuɔ tsei ashishifãi amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi.

english: How does heavy rain during the flowering stage affect the way groundnut plants grow?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa ŋmei dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains during flowering can wash away pollen and make the topsoil compact or waterlogged, which stops the growing pegs from penetrating the soil to form nuts.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo nu shwieɔ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: What kind of soil is best for groundnuts so the crop can produce full pods easily?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmeii koni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ mlɛo?

english: Groundnuts thrive best in loose, well-draining, sandy loam soil. Loose soil allows the pegs to sink into the ground easily and gives the pods enough room to expand without rotting.
ga: Peanuts daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo. Ni ehaa pod lɛ hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni egbɛ eshwa ni efiteee.

english: Do groundnut plants need the same amount of chemical nitrogen fertilizer as corn crops do?
ga: Ani tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ he miihia ŋmei tsei tamɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means they can capture nitrogen directly from the air and feed themselves through their root nodules, requiring very little added nitrogen.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛye amɛhe niyenii. Enɛ biɔ nitrogen fioo ko pɛ.

english: What happens to groundnut crops if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-peanut tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the plants to compete for sunlight, ground moisture, and nutrients, leading to weak stems, smaller pods, and higher risks of leaf diseases due to trapped moisture.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite hulu la ni tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ŋmɔtɔ bibii kɛ baa helai ahe oshara ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully matured and ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You can check maturity by digging up a few sample plants and cracking open the pods; if the inside shell has dark brown or black markings and the seeds fill the pod completely, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni ooofo mli ni ooofo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How should I store groundnuts after harvest to keep them from rotting or getting spoiled by pests?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmeii ato beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite loo ŋmeii akafite amɛ.

english: Groundnuts should be dried thoroughly until the moisture content is low, left in their shells for protection, and stored in clean, breathable bags kept off the ground in a cool, dry place.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛmli nu lɛ baa shi. Shi yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli koni ebu he. ni okɛto kotoku ko ni mli tse ni mumɔ baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Okɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective shield against heat and helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip and moving down the middle vein indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to produce green leaves and healthy ears, which can be fixed by applying nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yaa shishi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni etoi lɛ hu ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for my next corn crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into natural plant food in the soil. When the leaves and roots rot, they leave behind rich nutrients for maize to feed on.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ sɛɛ koni ŋmãa lɛ aye.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves with tiny brown droppings inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This pattern of damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center of maize plants and eats the leaves before they fully open.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up off the soil so they can catch maximum sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy the plant generates to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la lɛ naa baai lɛ, Babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ lɛ, babaoo ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ e-bulbs wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot and smell bad underground when water stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nu ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Waterlogged soil cuts off air to the roots, causing them to suffocate, rot, and get infected by soil fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ, fitemɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it a bad idea to plant pepper on the exact same plot where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ ooodu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot consecutively allows diseases to build up in the soil and destroy the new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Why should I cut off the extra young stems growing around the base of my main plantain shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, food, and light away from the main stem. Removing most of them leaves only the main plant to put all its strength into producing a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo kɛjɛ mli, ni ashi tso titri lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaahe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee tso agbo ko.

english: Extremely high temperatures dry up the pollen in tomato flowers, preventing them from being fertilized. When pollination fails, the plant naturally drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops small and weak even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your main crops can reach them, starving your crops and lowering harvest yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baashɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick if I cannot see any bugs or worms on them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ minaaa kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii komɛi hu?

english: Crops can get sick from microscopic germs like fungi, bacteria, and viruses that you cannot see with your eyes. You will know the crop is sick by watching for changes in its leaf color, spots appearing on the stems, twisted growth, or sudden wilting.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ aná hela kɛjɛ helai bibii tamɔ fungi, bacteria, kɛ virus ni onyɛŋ ona kɛ ohiŋmɛii amli. Obaale kɛji hela mɔ onibii kɛtsɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Spots jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. shweremɔ ni ejaaa loo shwiemɔ ni baa trukaa

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow when I am giving them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the plant is suffering. If you are watering them enough, it usually means an invisible root disease is stopping the plant from taking up food, or the soil is missing key nutrients.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ. Kɛji okɛ nu ha lɛ bɔ ni sa Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ hela ko ni shishifãi ni anaaa lɛ miitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the sunny day even though the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When a plant wilts in wet soil, tiny germs inside the stem are blocking water from flowing up to the leaves. The plant droops because it cannot drink the water that is right there in the soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, helai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli. Tsei gboiɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What does it mean if dark brown spots start spreading on my pepper leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ je shishi egbɛ eshwa mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Dark spots on leaves are visible warning signs of fungal or bacterial sickness. These spots destroy the leaf surface, preventing the plant from making food and reducing your harvest.
ga: He ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni anaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ baa shi.

english: How can I know if my cassava roots are dying underground before I harvest them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ?

english: Even though cassava roots are hidden under the ground, the leaves on top will show you if there is a problem. If the upper leaves curl, show yellow mosaic patches, or dry up prematurely, the roots underground are likely rotted or sick.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ehiɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ, Shi nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baatsɔɔ bo kɛji naagba ko yɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Mosaic okadii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ. loo egbi mra Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi baanyɛ agbo loo hela aba amɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees have a disease in their roots under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã hela?

english: Root diseases prevent the tree from feeding properly. You can tell the roots are sick if the branches start dying back from the top down or if green leaves suddenly fall off the tree.
ga: Shishifã hela haaa tso lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shishifãi lɛ hela mɔ amɛ kɛji niji bɔi gboimɔ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi kɛtee shishi, loo kɛji tso lɛ baai eŋɔlii lɛ gbee shi trukaa.

english: What signs show that my yam tubers under the ground are rotting?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii komɛi ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Although the yam tuber grows hidden underground, the vine above ground will give you clues by wilting, turning yellow early, or decaying at the base where the stem meets the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ, shi wein tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ole nɔ ko kɛtsɔ amɛshwiemɔ nɔ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ oya loo egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ he ni tso lɛ shishi kɛ sũ lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my plantain trees fell over because of sickness or just wind?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo kɔɔyɔɔ hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi lɛ?

english: Strong wind snaps healthy stems, but invisible root diseases or stem borers weaken the plant from inside first. If the roots are dark and rotted, or the trunk breaks easily and looks hollow inside, the plant was sick before the wind blew.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fiteɔ tsei ni mli wa. Shi shishifãi helai ni anaaa loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛjɛ emli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ ediŋ ni amɛmiifite Aloo tso lɛ shishi lɛ fãa oya ni etamɔ nɔ ni mli ewo muji. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa.

english: How can I tell if my garden egg plants need fertilizer or if they are sick with a leaf disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nii loo hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ miipiŋ lɛ?

english: When plants lack fertilizer, the whole field usually turns a pale, even yellow. Sickness usually shows as uneven brown spots, twisted leaves, or patches that spread from one plant to neighboring plants over time.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii Bei pii lɛ ŋmɔji fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ. baai ni etsilɛ loo hei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Can disease stay hidden in my soil and attack new crops I plant later?
ga: Ani hela ko baanyɛ ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etutua tsei heei ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, many microscopic crop diseases stay alive in the soil long after the crop is harvested. If you plant the same crop in that dirty soil, the hidden disease will attack the new crop's roots as soon as they grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai bibii babaoo hiɔ shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ lɛ, Helai ni yɔɔ Teemɔŋ lɛ tutuaa tsei heei ashishifãi lɛ kɛji amɛdara pɛ.

english: Why does a white, watery liquid come out when I cut my cassava stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu yɛŋ ni tamɔ nu jeɔ kpo kɛ́ mifo ŋmei tso lɛ?

english: That white liquid is plant latex or sap. It is a natural substance that helps the crop protect itself against insect pests and seal up wounds on the stem.
ga: Nu yɛŋ lɛ ji latɛs loo mliki. Eji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ehaa pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe.

english: What does it mean when a milky white ooze comes out of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ mliki ni tamɔ mliki je mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli?

english: A whitish or watery ooze coming from maize stalks usually signals a bacterial stalk rot infection, which happens when too much moisture enters wounded plant tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu yɛŋ loo nu ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ emɔ ŋmãa tsei amli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu babaoo bote tso lɛ fãji ni epila lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots look watery inside instead of dry and white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni nu yɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee futafuta lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become watery inside when harvested too early or during heavy rains, because the plant has absorbed a lot of water but has not yet built up solid starch.
ga: Nu yɛ ŋmei shishifãi amli kɛji akpa mra tsɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo shi efeee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa lolo.

english: Why is there a dark, swollen ring around the base of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ ni efuu yɛ mi-cacao lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: A dark ring around the base often means collar rot or a fungal attack caused by waterlogging or burying the stem too deep under moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ tsitsi ni egbo loo ŋmei ni nu ni hoɔ loo ŋmei ni afuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ shishi lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us not to tie tight ropes or bands around young tree trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkafi kpãai loo kpãai ahe waa yɛ tsei akutsei ahe lɛ?

english: Tying a tight band around a trunk chokes the plant's food pipes, stopping nutrients made in the leaves from reaching the roots and eventually killing the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ fĩ tso lɛ tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ niyenii paipii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni abɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbe tso lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves above a brown ring on my pepper plant stem turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: A brown ring on the stem shows that disease has damaged the plant's internal water tubes at that spot, preventing water from getting to the top leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela lɛ efite tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli, ni no haaa nu ashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop in the hot afternoon but stand up fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Plants lose water faster than their roots can drink during hot afternoons, so they wilt to conserve moisture, then recover overnight when temperatures cool down.
ga: Tsei fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni ehiɛ baa shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do I see clear water drops on the tips of my maize leaves early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa nu ni mli tse ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Those morning drops are caused by guttation, a normal process where healthy roots absorb water at night and push the extra water out through leaf tips.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ leebi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ji gutting, ni ji gbɛ ni afɔɔ nɔ ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu gbɛkɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjeɔ kpo.

english: How can I tell if my yam plants need more food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi he miihia mi-sweet potato tso lɛ?

english: If yam leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and the vines stay thin and weak, the crop is short on nitrogen and needs extra plant food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Ni wain tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni tso niyenii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Can I put fresh poultry manure directly on my vegetable crops as food for them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã hee awo mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛha amɛ niyenii?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and hot because of high ammonia levels, which can burn root tips; it must be dried or composted first before feeding it to crops.
ga: Manure hee lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ yɛ ammonia ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ agbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani adu.

english: Why do the new white hybrid maize seeds from the agricultural store sprout faster and more evenly than the grains I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hee ni ji white hybrid ŋmãa ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ oya ni ehi shi daa fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high vigor and uniform growth. Seeds saved from previous harvests naturally lose these strong genetic traits over generations, leading to uneven sprouting and slower early growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ daa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: What is the main difference in growth between planting red cowpeas and white cowpeas in my field?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titri ni yɔɔ tsina tsuru kɛ tsina yɛŋ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dalɛ mli?

english: Red and white cowpeas are distinct varieties with different traits. White cowpeas generally mature faster and are ideal for quick harvesting, while red cowpea varieties often show higher tolerance to wet conditions and insect pests during storage.
ga: Cowpeas tsuru kɛ eyɛŋ ji ŋmeii srɔtoi ni amɛyɛ sui srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, tsina ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ daa oya ni ehi kɛha ŋmaa oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, red cowpeas lɛ nyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: If I buy vegetable seeds that were imported from cold countries like France, will they grow properly in our hot Ghanaian soil?
ga: Kɛ mihe aduawai dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maŋ ko ni mli ejɔ tamɔ France mli lɛ. Ani amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ Ghana shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Some imported crops struggle in tropical heat, but many varieties are specifically bred as heat-tolerant hybrids. To get good yield, you must choose certified tropical varieties that can handle high heat and humidity without drying out.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ miiwuu. Shi atsɔse henɔi babaoo pɔtɛɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa. bɔni afee ni oná nibii kpakpai Ehe miihia ni ohala tropical henɔi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa naa ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are my corn seeds taking more than two weeks to shoot up out of the soil after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe otsii enyɔ dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require adequate moisture, warm air, and loose soil to break open. If the soil is planted too deep, pressed down too hard, or lacking moisture, the seed remains dormant or struggles to push through the hard ground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ, atswa lɛ waa tsɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. loo ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ

english: Why did only about 50 percent of the seeds I planted in my nursery bed come up as healthy seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ mi-nursery lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 50 pɛ bafeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: A low germination rate usually occurs when seeds are old, damaged by insects during storage, exposed to high heat before planting, or buried in soil that is either too dry or waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ. Kplukai fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Na la ni mli wa dani odu. Aloo ofu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my pepper plants stay sharp and healthy while neighboring ones get twisted leaves and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baai etsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted or stunted leaves are a common sign of attack by tiny insects like mites or thrips, or a virus they transmit. Plants that remain healthy usually have better natural resistance or were not fed upon by pests early on.
ga: Baai ni etsake loo egbɔjɔ lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips tutua amɛ. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Bei pii lɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lolo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai yeee amɛ mra.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many bright flowers, but the flowers fall off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni kpɛɔ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme midday heat, sudden dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than setting fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Gbimɔ trukaa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my bean plants produce lots of thick green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive excess nitrogen from chemical fertilizers or rich manure, they put all their energy into leafy growth above ground. To produce pods, crops need balanced nutrients, particularly phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náa nitrogen ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Niyenii ni ja he miihia tsei koni amɛfee pods. Titri lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium.

english: Why do white yam varieties take much longer to mature for harvest than yellow yam varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ heɔ be babaoo dani akpaa fe ŋmeii ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: White yams and yellow yams have different genetic growth cycles. White yams require a longer rainy season—usually 8 to 10 months—to accumulate maximum starch in the ground, whereas yellow yams mature faster but store differently.
ga: Sweet potato yɛŋ kɛ sweet potato yellow yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Ehe miihia ni ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ aná nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ, nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10, koni enyɛ eshɛ ŋmeii ni abua naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sweet potatoes ni ji yellow lɛ daa oya shi akɛtoɔ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with thick leaves during heavy rains but leave me with small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: During intense rains, cassava uses available water and nutrients to build big leaves and tall stems to capture sunlight. It only shifts its energy to filling and expanding tubers underground as the rain slows down.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ tsei kakadaji ni ekɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Etsakeɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It often happens when the soil is exhausted or when heavy rains wash nutrients deeper down past the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or by a plant virus they spread. These insects feed on the leaf sap, causing the leaves to twist, dry up, and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ yeɔ baa nu, ni no haa baa lɛ tsɔɔ, egbiɔ, ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. When it is too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo egbi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell while the soil is still hot underneath. If you plant immediately, the seeds may sprout but will quickly dry up and die before the regular rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo yɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The sunlight allows the plant leaves to make food, which is sent down to help the yam root grow large and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ahe baai ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni akɛmajeɔ shi koni eye ebua sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsii

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Growing fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates living umbrellas that give young cocoa plants the shade and cool moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Why does letting weeds grow near my crops make my crops weak and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe feɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, soil food, and sunlight directly from your crops. When weeds crowd your field, your crops starve and stretch tall and thin as they fight for light.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni jwɛi bɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaafee shwiili ni amɛbaafee shwiili be mli ni amɛyeɔ la he akaŋ lɛ.

english: Why does placing dry grass around the base of my vegetable plants help them during dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks the sun from drying out the ground, keeping water in the soil longer so your plants don't wilt.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ gbooo.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot of land every year reduce my yield each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa miŋmãa lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize takes the same specific food out of the soil every single season. Repeatedly planting it in one spot drains those nutrients completely and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in that soil.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa nakai nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava is generally mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving larger trees provides shade to keep the young cocoa cool and preserves moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji ni ashi amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba koni eha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow while the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help bring back the healthy green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to become soft and rot inside the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛkpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long, especially in heavy clay soils during the rainy season. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and drop their leaves even when I water the soil regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi trukaa ni amɛbaai miiho eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease that lives in the ground and blocks the stems from carrying water to the leaves. To clear it, avoid planting tomatoes or peppers in that same spot for a few seasons and rotate with maize or cassava instead.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ nu aya baai lɛ amli. Kɛji oosumɔ ni otsi ohe Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ he be fioo komɛi ni odu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa moŋ.

english: Why do I need to put long wood stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up into the light and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni eshɛ amɛbaa lɛ he koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ hiɔ la mli ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. baanyɛ atutua

english: What is eating small holes inside the top centers of my young maize leaves, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant. You can control them by putting a little dry sand, wood ash, or recommended botanical sprays directly into the plant funnel early in the morning.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ ŋã ni egbi, tso mli sũ, loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fioo ni okɛbaafata dumɔwui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ nɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or fallen leaves around the base of my crops help them grow better?
