ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwaa Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It stops the sun from drying out the earth quickly, keeps weeds from growing, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehãaa hulu lɛ agbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same farm as my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a family of plants that can pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it into the soil. As the groundnut roots grow and decay, they release this natural fertilizer, which feeds the nearby maize without you having to buy extra chemicals.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛgboi lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei. Akɛ enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers can start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat or unequal watering. Watering your plants consistently at the base early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the bottom of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: The small shoots, called suckers, steal water, light, and soil food away from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree grows strong and produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, juɔ nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow starting from the bottom leaves going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the lower leaves, it means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaves to stay green and healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick stems and lots of green leaves, but the tubers underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo. Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen in the soil or too much rain, it puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots to make large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei agboi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why does my land yield much better maize when I plant cowpea or groundnuts on it first before planting the maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ kwraa kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free plant food behind that feeds the next crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn and soil moisture evaporates quickly; they need shade from larger trees or plantains during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei bibii adɛŋ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I drop four or five maize seeds into a single hole to get more maize on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli koni maná ŋmãa babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the seedlings to crowd each other out and fight for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin stems and small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why is it so important for me to clear weeds during the first four weeks after my crops emerge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eje kpo lɛ?

english: Young crop plants grow slowly at first, so if weeds grow beside them in the early weeks, the weeds steal most of the water and soil nutrients, permanently stunting the crop's growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ shishijee Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Enɛ baatsi tsei lɛ adalɛ naa kwraa.

english: Why do my crop roots stay short and weak when the farm soil becomes hard and dry like stone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbi tamɔ tɛ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil blocks roots from pushing deep into the ground to find moisture during dry spells, which prevents the plant from drinking enough water to grow tall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the center funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Eyɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize plant during warm periods and feeds on the soft new leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or viruses spread by these insects, which suck sap and stunt leaf development.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni nuɔ nu ni haa baai lɛ daraaa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the air is too hot and dry or when rainfall is unpredictable, because the plant gets stressed and tries to save its energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ miihao ni amɛmiitao ni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How does covering my soil with dry leaves help my crops during the hot season?
ga: Te baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that traps soil moisture, blocks weed growth, and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to produce healthy, dark green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni mli wa, ni ji eŋɔli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam plants with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb. Staking lifts their leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to feed and expand the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ akwɔ. Staking baawó amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni tsei kɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni amɛbaagbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli amɛshwã

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture shifts drastically between very dry and very wet, causing stress to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa teŋ. Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting when water sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess water from flooding pushes oxygen out of the soil, causing the buried roots to suffocate and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nu afua mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni afu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars eating the inside of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mibi lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the tender center leaves of young maize to feed on the growing tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa bibii amli koni eye fãji ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting maize in that same spot later allows the maize to use that stored nitrogen to grow strong.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so the roots can absorb them. Applying fertilizer to dry soil concentrates the chemicals and can burn or destroy the plant's roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afee ekome ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why do many farmers in Ghana plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miidu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing vital shade and cool soil moisture while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hia kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do plantain trees produce new plants if they do not grow from regular seeds?
ga: Te dumɔwu ko baafee tɛŋŋ ewo tso hee kɛji akɛ ejɛɛɛ dumɔwu ni sa mli?

english: Plantains grow from an underground bulb called a corm. As the main plant grows, it shoots up young offspring from its base called suckers, which farmers dig up and replant to start new trees.
ga: Plantains jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ tubers lɛ amli. Kɛ tso titri lɛ da Ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛɔ shishitoo ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. ni okwaafoi shwieɔ shi ni amɛduɔ ekoŋŋ koni amɛkɛje tsei heei shishi lɛ.

english: What are creeper plants, and how do they help keep my farm soil healthy?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni kwɔɔ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Creepers are ground-covering plants that spread quickly across the soil. They block direct sunlight to prevent weed growth, protect the earth from rain erosion, and naturally add nitrogen nutrients to feed surrounding crops.
ga: Ivy ji tso ko ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ oya. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he ni oha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen niyenii aya hiɛ koni eha tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the tree trunks and cleared brush after clearing a new plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashãa tsei akui kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ beni ajie shikpɔŋ hee lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving cut timber and leaves to rot naturally on the soil acts like slow-release fertilizer. It protects topsoil from washing away in heavy rains and helps the soil hold moisture during dry periods.
ga: Tso kɛ baai ni afo lɛ ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi blɛoo. Ebuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: Does a single plantain tree yield fruit multiple times, or do I need to cut it down after harvesting?
ga: Ani dumɔwu kome woɔ yibii shii abɔ loo esa akɛ mafolɔ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Each individual plantain stem flowers and yields a bunch of fruit only once in its life. After cutting it down during harvest, the energy goes into the young suckers growing at the base to produce the next crop.
ga: Plantain fɛɛ plantain baafɔ fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ eshihilɛ mli. Beni afo lɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli sɛɛ lɛ Hewalɛ lɛ yaa tsei bibii ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: What time of the year is best to plant plantain suckers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant suckers is at the start of the major rainy season around April or May. This ensures the roots develop strongly with steady rainwater before dry spells begin.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli, aaafee April loo May. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Will wild vines and creepers choke my young plantain plants if I let them grow on the farm?
ga: Ani koo mli wain tsei kɛ tsei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baaha mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, if left unchecked, climbing vines will wrap around young plantain stems and compete for sunlight and nutrients. Clearing a clear ring around the base of each tree keeps them protected.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ wein tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛbɔleɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Ajieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni bɔleɔ Tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ buɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do strong windstorms easily push over my plantain trees when they carry heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shwieɔ mi plantains lɛ anɔ oya beni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems instead of deep taproots. When the heavy fruit bunch forms at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy and requires wooden props or bamboo poles for support against high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji aduawai akui ni tsii fee yɛ ŋwɛi Tsei lɛ tsii yɛ ŋwɛi ni ebiɔ tsei ahe nibii loo ŋmei tsei ni akɛfiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain tree turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turn yellow naturally as the plant matures and directs energy to younger leaves and fruit. However, widespread yellowing can indicate a lack of soil nutrients, drought stress, or leaf spot diseases.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ hewalɛ haa baai bibii kɛ aduawai lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ loo baai amli hela mli baa

english: How quickly can I expect to harvest plantains after planting them?
ga: Te manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa plantains lɛ etsɛ tɛŋŋ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most plantain varieties take between 11 to 15 months from planting the sucker to harvesting a mature bunch, making them a good source of quick food and income while longer-term tree crops mature.
ga: Plantain henɔi babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe kpakpa yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant only one type of vegetable like cucumber on my whole farm or mix it with other crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu aduawai henɔ kome, tamɔ kukumba yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo mikɛ tsei krokomɛi afutu mli?

english: Planting a single crop makes farm work simpler, but it is riskier. If a disease or pest attacks that specific crop, or if market prices drop, you could lose all your income. Mixing crops helps protect your farm because different plants attract different pests and use soil nutrients differently.
ga: Nibii kome ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo. Shi osharai babaoo yɛ. Kɛji helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo kɛji jara nɔ jara ba shi Obaanyɛ ofite shika fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi kɛbaa ni amɛkɛ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Proper spacing depends on how wide and tall the crop grows when fully mature. If you plant crops too close together, they will fight for sunlight, water, and plant food, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛto tso lɛ he lɛ damɔ tso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ kɛ ekɛlɛ nɔ beni edara lɛ. Kɛji odu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: How should I transport young tree seedlings to my farm so they do not die before I plant them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui bibii aya miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkagboi dani madu?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and easily damaged by heat and wind during movement. Keep their soil moist, cover them to protect them from direct sunlight and harsh wind during transport, and plant them early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ amɛ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha nɔ ko nɔ koni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsɔne lɛ yaa lɛ. ni aduɔ yɛ leebi loo shwane mli

english: Why do some extension officers advise planting shade crops alongside young tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shweremɔ he nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings have tender leaves that burn under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops beside them acts like a natural umbrella, protecting the young plants and keeping the soil moist until the tree roots grow deep enough.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetable crops droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When the afternoon sun is very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it from the soil. The drooping is a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss, and the leaves usually stand back up once temperatures cool down.
ga: Beni shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛte shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning light green or yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow or pale leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients in the soil, especially nitrogen, or the plant is receiving too much or too little water. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer can help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to walk around and inspect my farm regularly instead of just leaving the crops to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ manyiɛ? ni okwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Regular farm visits help you catch problems early, such as insect invasions, leaf diseases, or weed growth, before they spread to the whole farm. Early action saves money and prevents crop loss.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mli saramɔi daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oyoo naagbai mra, tamɔ kooloi ni baa, tso lɛ mli helai loo jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Dani naagba lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli Nifeemɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ekɛ shika toɔ ni etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds lower the yield of my crops if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and will steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your plants. Keeping the farm clean gives your crops full access to the resources they need to produce well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛbaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: The best time to water crops is early morning or late evening. Watering during the middle of the day causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my vegetables are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa mi-aduawai lɛ?

english: Every crop shows specific physical signs when mature, such as reaching a standard size, changing color, or becoming firm to the touch. Harvesting at the right time ensures the produce stays fresh longer and fetches better prices at the market.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi akpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ amɛshɛɔ bɔ ni sa, amɛsu tsakeɔ, loo amɛfeɔ nɔ ni wa akɛ aaata he. Nibii ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa nibii ni akpaa lɛ hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa jara ni hi fe fɛɛ baa jara nɔ.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer talks about crop varieties, and why does it matter for my farm?
ga: Mɛni amɛtsɔɔ kɛ́ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wie tsei srɔtoi ahe? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A crop variety is a specific type of plant within a crop family that has unique traits. Some varieties mature quickly to beat short rains, while others yield bigger harvests or resist local pests. Choosing the right variety ensures your seeds suit your land and weather.
ga: Tso henɔ ji tso pɔtɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ tsei aweku mli ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi. Henɔi komɛi daa oya koni amɛye nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ nɔ kunim. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii babaoo loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kɛ́ ohala tso ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni odumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ.

english: How do I decide whether soya bean or rice is the better crop to invest my money in this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji akɛ soybeans loo ŋmãa ji shika ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be nɛɛ?

english: Your choice depends on your soil type and water supply. Rice thrives in lowlands or valley bottoms that hold a lot of water, while soya bean prefers well-drained soil and actually adds natural nutrients to the soil, requiring less synthetic fertilizer.
ga: Nɔ ni obaahala lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ kɛ nu ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishi loo jɔɔ lɛ amli he ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Shi soybean lɛ, esumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni esumɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ebiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do some rice seeds produce a harvest much faster than other rice seeds planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa komɛi woɔ yibii oya fe ŋmãa krokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties are bred with different growth cycles. Early-maturing varieties complete their life cycle in about 90 days to avoid dry spells, while late-maturing varieties take 120 days or longer to build up larger grains.
ga: Omɔ henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ bɔ ni edaraa ehaa. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ gbeɔ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa yɛ aaafee gbii 90 mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo bei ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ gbii 120 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛwoɔ dumɔwui wuji.

english: How does growing soya beans help make my farm soil richer for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soybeans ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soya bean plants work with good bacteria in the ground to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvested, that nitrogen stays in the soil, feeding whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Soybean tsei kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa tsei lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eha tsei fɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I plant rice on regular dry land, or does it always need to grow in water?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ nu mli be fɛɛ be?

english: There are two main types of rice: upland rice, which grows on well-drained dry land using regular rainfall, and lowland rice, which requires flooded fields or swampy soils to grow properly.
ga: Omɔ henɔi titrii enyɔ yɔɔ: ŋmɔ mli omɔ, ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ; kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni biɔ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo ŋmɔtɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my soya bean plants turn yellow and fall off right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani abakpa lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural sign that the soya bean plant has finished its life cycle. It sheds its leaves to direct all remaining energy and moisture into fully drying out the seeds inside the pods.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ soybean tso ko eshɛ ewala be lɛ naagbee. Ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why do my soya bean pods burst open on their own if I leave them in the field too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbalaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As soya bean pods dry under hot sunshine, the outer shell tightens and cracks open to naturally spread its seeds. Harvesting promptly when pods turn brown prevents your grains from spilling onto the ground.
ga: Kɛji soybean ŋmeii lɛ gĩ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatswa ni amɛgbala koni dumɔwui lɛ agbɛ ashwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmaa lɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmaa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ.

english: What happens to rice plants if the field dries up completely while they are flowering?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩ kwraa be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Rice plants need steady water especially during the flowering stage to form grains. If the field dries out completely at this time, the flowers will produce empty husks with no rice grains inside.
ga: Omɔ tsei hia nu daa, titri lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli, koni amɛfee omɔ ŋmaa. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baafee ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmaa bɛ mli.

english: How can I fund and manage a crop farm successfully if I cannot be on the land to do the daily work myself?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika ni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye lɛ anɔ? Kɛji mi diɛŋtsɛ minyɛɛɛ mahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni matsu daa gbi nitsumɔ lɛ.

english: You can operate as an absentee farmer by providing financial capital for land preparation, quality seeds, and inputs, while paying hired farm workers or a trusted supervisor to execute the field tasks on schedule.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsu nii akɛ okwaafonyo ni bɛ shia kɛtsɔ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛha shikpɔŋ he saamɔ nɔ. dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni haa anáa nii Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ni aŋɔɔ amɛ loo nɔkwɛlɔi ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nyɔmɔ koni amɛtsu ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to level my farm field before planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Leveling the field ensures that rainfall or irrigation water spreads evenly across the land. This prevents water from collecting in deep spots and drowning some plants while leaving other plants dry.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mlijaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ ji koni nu akabua ehe naa yɛ hei ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ tsei komɛi awo nu mli yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei krokomɛi hu gĩɔ.

english: How should I clear my farm land before planting cocoa for the first time?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu mi klɛŋklɛŋ kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Clearing land for cocoa requires removing heavy weeds and brush while leaving selected large trees to provide overhead shade. You should avoid burning all the cleared bush because burning destroys organic matter and essential nutrients in the topsoil that young cocoa seedlings rely on.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ tsei wuji ni ahala koni amɛha amɛyiteŋ hulutsoo. Esa akɛ okpa jwɛi fɛɛ ni ajie lɛ shãa ejaakɛ shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni cacao tsei bibii damɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: What kind of soil is best for growing cocoa on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha kookoo dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa thrives in deep, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic matter that holds moisture without staying waterlogged. Hard clay soils that trap standing water will cause root rot, while overly sandy soils dry out too fast during the dry season.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni hiɛɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ tsɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How do I know how many cocoa trees my piece of land can support?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male cacao tsei enyiɛ ni mihe lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ?

english: Every hectare of land has a limit to how many crops it can feed. For cocoa, standard recommended spacing is about 3 meters by 3 meters, which allows roughly 1,100 trees per hectare so roots and branches have enough space to access sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Hectare fɛɛ hectare yɛ husu yɛ tsei ayibɔ ni abaanyɛ adu lɛ he. Kɛha kookoo lɛ, gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ mli lɛ ji aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3, ni haa anáa tsei aaafee 1,100 yɛ hectare kome mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi kɛ tsei niji lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛna hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Overcrowding forces cocoa trees to compete fiercely for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Trees planted too close together grow tall and thin with fewer pods, and the lack of airflow between overlapping leaves makes it easy for diseases like black pod to spread.
ga: Mɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaafee mlɛo ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Ni bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ baai ni tsɔɔ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, intense heat rapidly dries out the soil and scorches the young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni eshãa tsei bibii.

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin producing their first pods within two to three years of planting if properly cared for, whereas older traditional varieties can take four to five years to mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai krokomɛi lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani ekwɛ̃.

english: Why is it so important to give intensive care to cocoa trees during their first two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ ni mli wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa waa lɛ?

english: The first two years are when the young plant establishes its main taproot and branch framework. Protecting the crop from pests, weeds, and sun damage during this early stage ensures the tree grows strong enough to yield pods for 20 to 30 years.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ ji be mli ni tso bibioo lɛ feɔ eshishifã titri kɛ eniji ahe gbɛjianɔtoo. Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, jwɛi, kɛ hulu ni fiteɔ nii ahe yɛ nɛkɛ shishijee be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii afii 20 kɛyashi 30.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or plantain together with my new cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo plantain kɛ cacao tsei heei?

english: You can plant plantains because their big leaves provide beneficial shade and moisture for young cocoa. However, you should avoid planting cassava near young cocoa because cassava roots feed aggressively and steal water and nutrients from the young cocoa plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ejaakɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okpa ŋmei dumɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi yeɔ nii waa ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli.

english: Why do leaf-eating insects attack my fresh cocoa seedlings right after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ tutuaa mi-kokoo dumɔwui heei lɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you clear wild bushes from your farm, you remove the natural food sources of local insects, prompting them to attack the fresh, tender leaves of your new cocoa seedlings. Regular farm monitoring helps catch and control these pests early.
ga: Kɛji ojie koo mli jwɛi kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli Obaajie adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi amli lɛ kɛyaa. Wo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtutua o-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe baai bibii heei lɛ. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: How much farm labor do I need to prepare and manage a large cocoa farm?
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ enyiɛ he baahia mi koni manyɛ masaa ni makwɛ kookoo ŋmɔ agbo ko nɔ?

english: Land preparation and seedling planting require more labor—typically 2 to 4 workers per hectare—to clear brush and dig holes. Once the cocoa trees are established, ongoing weeding and maintenance require significantly fewer hands.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ dumɔwui adumɔ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo. (bei pii lɛ nitsulɔi 2 kɛyashi 4 yɛ hectare kome mli) koni amɛjie jwɛi ni amɛfo bu Beni kookoo tso lɛ ema shi Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ fioo kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or drown the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo ekɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli.

english: How can I stop my tomatoes from getting squashed and rotting on the way to the Techiman market?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa tomato ni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa Techiman Jarayelihe lɛ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly when packed in soft bags or stacked heavily. Pick them early in the morning while cool, pack them gently in firm, wooden, ventilated crates, and lay straw at the bottom to absorb shocks during transport.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui ni yɔɔ blɛoo amli loo akɛto amɛhe babaoo. Kpɔ̃ɔ amɛ leebi maŋkpa, be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, ni okɛ amɛ awo tso adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni mli wa mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni akɛ jwɛi fɔɔ shishigbɛ koni ekɛjie shoofeemɔ kɛjɛ mli beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant have plenty of big leaves but very tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing bushy leaves on top instead of sending energy down to build big roots. Cassava needs potassium to make heavy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai babaoo yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji lɛ, Cassava he miihia potassium koni ekɛfee yitsei ni tsii.

english: Will planting groundnuts together with my maize help or harm my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye miŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: Groundnuts help your maize because groundnut roots grab natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt. This enriches the soil and helps the maize grow strong without exhausting the land.
ga: Peanuts yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ejaakɛ peanut shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and wrinkle?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant sap, or by viruses spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait to plant my yam seeds instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni madu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain only wets the top layer of earth and makes the ground hot. If dry weather follows, the hot soil will burn and rot your yam seed pieces before the real rainy season sets in.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã ni eha sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ agboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so fast when I stack them together in a pile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ato ŋmeii ahe lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still breathing roots. Stacking them tight traps heat and moisture, which creates the perfect warm, wet environment for fungal rot to spread fast from bruised yams to healthy ones.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni muɔ lolo. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ mɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ baa. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmei ni egbo lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ amli kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or when bees and insects are not present to carry pollen from flower to flower to form the fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi bɛ ni kɛ pollen baajɛ fɔfɔi amli kɛya fɔfɔi amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my farm land dry out faster and turn hard after I burn the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ewaa beni mishã mi jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the natural layer of dead leaves and organic matter that covers the soil. Without this protective cover, sunlight bakes the soil hard and makes water evaporate very quickly.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ bɛ Hulu la lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya waa.

english: Why are my young cashew trees dropping their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cashew trees shed leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to save water, which prevents the tree from drying out completely and helps trigger its flowering cycle.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ agbi kwraa, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any other crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside them provides cover, keeps the soil cool, and retains moisture so the cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize grow much taller and healthier when I plant cowpeas on the plot first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ da ni ehiɛ hewalɛ beni midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this natural soil fertilizer to grow strong and yield larger cobs.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Eyeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmãa wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the underground tuber. Staking holds the vines off the damp ground, exposing more leaves to light and preventing rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa wain tso lɛ jeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay alive during dry spells while my maize dries up completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiye wala yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmei lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that reach water deep underground, and it sheds its leaves during dry periods to conserve moisture, allowing it to survive drought far better than shallower-rooted crops like maize.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. ni ebaashwie baai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he Koni ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants turn black and rot when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crowding tomato plants prevents air from moving between them, keeping the leaves wet from dew and rain. Moisture traps fungal diseases on the leaves, which quickly spreads from plant to plant.
ga: Tomato tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Ha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nugbɔ mli. Fɛ̃i lɛ mɔ̃ɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which the crop needs to make green chlorophyll. Applying compost or rich manure restores nitrogen so the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii afee klorofil eŋɔli yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing new leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa baai heei adalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense reaction caused when tiny insects like thrips or aphids suck the sap out of young leaves, or when those insects spread a leaf-curl virus to the plant.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu nifeemɔ ko ni baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids miinu nu ni jɛɔ baabii bibii amli lɛ. Aloo beni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ eshwaa tsei lɛ.

english: Why does my rice farm produce small, empty grains if I leave weeds growing around the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ toi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. When rice plants have to compete with weeds, they lack the energy needed to fill out full, heavy grain heads.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hia kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Beni esa akɛ ŋmãa tsei kɛ jwɛi abɔ akaŋ Ebɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni ekɛbaawo dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off the dry, brown leaves from my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbi ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning dead leaves forces the plantain tree to focus its water and nutrients on growing fresh leaves and heavy fruit bunches, while also removing places where pests and fungal diseases hide.
ga: Baai ni egboi ni afoɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ yɛ baai heei ni miida kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jiemɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant cashew or oil palm trees along the edges of their land instead of short season crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ cashew loo oil palm tsei yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ naa moŋ fe ni amɛaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kuku lɛ?

english: Tree crops live for decades and establish permanent roots in the soil. Planting them along farm edges creates clear, living boundaries that signal long-term farm use while producing valuable harvests every year.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni hiɔ shi daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ haa husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, ni yɔɔ wala mli baa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii be kakadaŋŋ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu nibii ni jara wa ni anáa daa afi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need protection from intense direct sunlight while their root systems establish. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create temporary living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa be kukuoo mli hɔɔŋ baa. Ehaa kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, and when it is missing, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from older leaves to newer leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. Ni kɛ́ etee Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai heei amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, or viruses transmitted by them. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or approved sprays prevents damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants instead of growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the crop suffers heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and balanced plant feeding helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihe dɔlɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it depleted. Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa efiteɔ. Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting maize in straight rows produce better yields than scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures proper spacing so that each plant gets enough sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa anáa gbɛ ni sa bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough to grow good yam mounds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai anɔ?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark in color, loose, rich in decayed plant matter, and drains water easily without becoming waterlogged. Clay soils that trap water make yam tubers rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ mli ewo duŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni tsei ni egboi eyi mli obɔ. ni ejieɔ nu oya ni ehaaa nu lɛ afee nɔ ni ekã shi Shikpɔŋ sũ ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes waterlogged soil, which cuts off oxygen to the cassava root zone and encourages fungal root rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni baafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my sweet orange trees shed many of their green fruits before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiwo aduawai eŋɔlii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop in citrus trees is often triggered by sudden dry spells after heavy rains, nutrient deficiency, or attacks by fruit flies. Mulching around the base and regular watering helps retain fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ yibii ni shwieɔ mra yɛ citrus tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ trukaa. niyenii ni esaaa loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa mɔ Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my harvested cowpea grains develop small holes and turn to dust in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ebatsɔ sũ yɛ nitoohe

english: Holes in stored cowpeas are caused by cowpea weevils laying eggs inside the seeds. Drying the seeds thoroughly and storing them in airtight hermetic bags suffocates the pests naturally.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli lɛ baa ji tsina ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Applying poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ su kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get soft black patches at the bottom before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and uneven watering while the fruit is forming. Regular watering and adding lime or organic compost to the soil prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ lime loo organic compost ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in full open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the seedlings cool and retains soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my cassava mounds instead of putting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need enough underground space to swell into large tubers. When mounds are too close, the plants fight for soil nutrients and water, producing small, thin roots instead of thick ones.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji gɔŋ lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide in the soft center of maize plants to feed. Detecting them early and applying approved treatments saves the growing tip from being destroyed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsitsii ni miida lɛ akafite.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant pepper on the exact same bed every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ saatso kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows soil diseases and pests that attack peppers to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like maize or beans breaks this pest cycle and improves soil quality.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy branches from my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra branches, called pruning, lets sunlight and air flow through the tree canopy. This keeps fungal diseases like black pod from spreading in damp shade and directs energy into pod growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei niji ni afoɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ akɛ pruning. koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ shishi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches after two harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ feɔ bibii bibii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As plantains grow, new sucker shoots sprout around the main stem and steal its water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one strong stem ensures large plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ, tsei heei baakwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe. tso titri lɛ ni ejuɔ emli nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tso kome pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It acts like a shield that stops the sun from baking the soil, keeping it cool and moist so vegetable roots do not dry out.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɛŋ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akagbi

english: Why do my vegetable leaves drop and look weak in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa be mli ni amɛdaraaa lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it up. Drooping is their natural defense to reduce heat surface area, and they usually bounce back by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie. Drooping ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni baaha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning under direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from taller plants like plantains because strong sunlight burns their delicate leaves and drains moisture from the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ejieɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow poorly if I do not give them wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mihaaa amɛ tsei ni akɛkwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their leaves can spread out to catch sunshine, which provides energy to grow big yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni akɛduɔ yam tsei wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom of the stalk even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient that maize uses to grow green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa baadu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize crop and improves the soil for future planting.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In waterlogged soil from heavy rain, water fills all the soil spaces, suffocating and rotting the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ, nu lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, which prevents the flowers from turning into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which attack young maize by hiding inside the central leaf funnel where it is moist and sheltered while they feed.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmei bibii kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛnáa hebuu yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads easily when heavy rain leaves constant moisture on the pods in humid weather.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the top leaves of my tomato plants curling up and slowing down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdaraa fioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, which feed on leaf sap and weaken the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Removing extra suckers prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from the main stem, allowing the main plant to produce a bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil cool and moist for the cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛha kookoo dumɔwui.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same soil food and water, and their leaves block light from each other, resulting in thin, weak plants with small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts and maize together in the same field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil, which feeds the maize crop and leaves the soil healthier for future planting without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil or are sitting in too much stagnant water. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after a good rain so the plant roots can absorb it, usually a few weeks after germination and again when the crop is growing fast.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ, koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni tso lɛ daa oya lɛ

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from hot direct sunlight, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weed seeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui akwɛ̃

english: How do I know if a farm chemical or medicine bought at the market is safe for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Check that the bottle has an official label approved by agricultural authorities, follow the mixing instructions carefully, and observe the recommended waiting period between spraying and harvesting.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ tɔ lɛ yɛ wolo ko ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ. Nyiɛmɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ futumɔ he lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni kadimɔ be ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ amɛmɛ yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ teŋ lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the young leaves to feed. Checking your farm early and applying approved crop protection early stops them from destroying the cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ baai bibii amli koni eye niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ akafite ŋmei lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked soil that cannot drain water away, causing the roots to drown. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps extra rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. drowning the roots Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too hot, suffers from a lack of water, or lacks nutrients. Regular watering during hot spells and keeping the soil healthy prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ fe nine, nu faaa yɛ emli, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Nu ni oooha amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: If I let my chickens walk around my plantain farm, will they destroy my plants?
ga: Kɛ miha tsina lɛ nyiɛ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ Ani amɛbaafite mi tsei lɛ?

english: Free-roaming chickens generally do not harm growing plantain plants. In fact, they help your farm by scratching the soil to eat harmful insects, grubs, and weed seeds without disturbing the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛhe lɛ yeee plantain dumɔwui lɛ awui. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa oŋmɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ koni amɛye kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni amɛgbaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa lɛ nɔ.

english: I found tiny insect eggs hidden in dark spots under my plantain leaves, how do I handle them?
ga: Miyana kooloi bibii komɛi awui. Ekɛ ehe ewo hei ni yɔɔ duŋ yɛ plantain baai lɛ ashishi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu he nii?

english: Pests often lay eggs in dark, shaded crevices under leaves to shield them from the sun. You should gently scrape them off or apply a mild neem-based spray before they hatch into leaf-eating caterpillars or borers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ amli yɛ baai ashishi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ ajie lɛ blɛoo. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni akɛ neem ni mli ejɔ ewo mli lɛ atsu nii. Dani amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai

english: Why is it important to clear weeds and dark bushy spots around the base of my plantain stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni bɔle mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Clearing dense weeds around the base removes cool, dark hiding places where pests like weevils and snakes like to settle, while allowing light and airflow to keep the plant healthy.
ga: Ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishitoo lɛ jieɔ hei ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Biɛ ji he ni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ onufui sumɔɔ ni amɛhi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow and dry up even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: As plantains grow taller, the older bottom leaves naturally die off so the plant can send energy to new green leaves and developing fruit. You can simply cut off the dry leaves to keep the farm clean.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ gboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ ajie hewalɛ kɛya baai eŋɔli heei kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ baai ni egboi lɛ koni oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need consistent soil moisture to wake up from dormancy. Planting them in rich soil and keeping mulch around the base traps moisture and speeds up new root sprouting.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛte shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe mli. Dumɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ ni okɛ sũ awo amɛhe. Shishitoo lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eye ebua shishifãi heei ni amɛdara oya.

english: What causes my plantain stems to bend or fall over before the fruit bunches are ready?
ga: Mɛni haa plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi dani aduawai akuu lɛ feɔ klalo?

english: Heavy fruit bunches combined with strong winds or stem-boring insects inside the trunk weaken the stem. Supporting your plants with sturdy wooden or bamboo props prevents them from snapping.
ga: Yibii akui ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fataa he lɛ haa tso lɛ mli gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi otsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkakumɔ.

english: I see small dark spots appearing on my plantain leaves, does this mean my plant is sick?
ga: Mina he ko diŋ fioo ko. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ plantain baai anɔ Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Dark leaf spots are usually a sign of Black Sigatoka, a common fungal issue caused by moisture trapped on leaves. Pruning off the affected leaves helps stop the fungi from spreading to healthy parts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ ji Black Sigatoka, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɛɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Is fresh chicken manure safe to throw directly at the base of my plantain stems?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ashɛrɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee ashwie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is very strong and can burn plant roots. It is best to let the manure dry out and rot (compost) for a few weeks before placing it a small distance away from the stem base.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni egbo (compost) otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛto he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field with my plantains without them killing each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ plantains ni migbeee mihe?

english: Yes, intercropping plantain and cassava works well because plantains grow tall to capture upper sunlight, while cassava roots spread below, provided you leave enough space between rows.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ plantains lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shishi Kwɛmɔ ni oshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ.

english: How do I know when a plantain bunch is mature enough for me to cut and harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni plantains kuu ko da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afo ni akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp edges, fill out to become round, and the dry flower ends at the tips rub off easily.
ga: Plantain tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ efo, ni eyiɔ obɔ ni efeɔ kokroo, ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. When the soil lacks nitrogen or becomes waterlogged, the plant pulls energy from its lower leaves to keep growing, causing them to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ Tsei lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy and store starch. When heavy rains leave water standing in the field for too long, it drowns the roots and creates conditions for harmful soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ni amɛkɛ starch ato. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afite lɛ aba.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any young pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii bibii baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they experience sudden stress, such as a long dry spell, harsh sunlight, or insect attacks. Dropping flowers helps the tree conserve water and energy to survive harsh conditions.
