ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ, hulu la ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: How does delaying weeding for just two weeks hurt the growth of my crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water from your crops. Delaying weeding gives weeds time to crowd out young plants, making your crops thin, weak, and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni jɛɔ onibii amli oya Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ baahã jwɛi lɛ aná be ni ekɛye tsei bibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: The first rain often wet only the top surface of dry, hot soil. If a long dry spell follows immediately, the intense sun cooks the soil and dries up the tender emerging seeds before their roots can reach deeper moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baahoo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ akwɛ̃. Egbiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do fall armyworms hide and eat deep inside the central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛboteɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms crawl into the inner funnel of the maize plant because it provides soft, nutritious young leaves and protects them from predators and hot direct sunlight.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhaa baai bibii lɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni haa mɔ he waa, ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture so the seedlings do not dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and stopping the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by viruses spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by extreme heat. Curling helps the plant reduce water loss, but it limits the plant's ability to make energy for growing large fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ tomato mli. Curling yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Shi ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛbaafee hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ aduawai wuji lɛ naa wa.

english: Leguminous crops like cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer. This enriches the soil and provides extra nutrients for neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to produce larger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need their leaves spread out high in the air to trap as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves healthy and exposed to the sun, allowing the plant to produce more energy to swell the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ ni biɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo haa koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are insects constantly eating the leaves of my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender, soft, and rich in nutrients, making them an easy food source for pests like caterpillars, beetles, and mirids. When insects destroy these leaves, it reduces the tree's ability to absorb sunlight and grow healthy.
ga: Cocoa baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii nɛɛ fite baai lɛ, amɛhaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the damage on my cocoa leaves is caused by insects or a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo helai ji nɔ ni kɛ nɔ ni efite yɛ mi-kokoo baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ba?

english: Insects typically leave visible holes, chewed edges, or stripped leaf skeletons behind. Leaf diseases usually show up as discolored spots, yellowing, or powdery growths without physical bite marks on the leaf.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi shĩɔ bu ni anaa, ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ, loo baai wuji ni etse amɛhe lɛ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baa hela jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsake. Ayɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni dalɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ he okadii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn brown and dry up after insects bite them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji kooloi ŋmɔ mi lɛ?

english: When insects chew on leaves or suck their sap, they break the veins that carry water and nutrients. The damaged leaf rapidly loses moisture, turns brown, dies, and eventually drops off so the tree can save water.
ga: Kɛji kooloi ŋmɔɔ baai loo amɛnuɔ nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ lá fãji ni hiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Baai ni efite lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Etsɔɔ blɔfo, egboɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeeɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ato nu he.

english: What kind of chemical should I buy to kill the pests eating my cocoa leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofai esa akɛ mahe koni mikɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ?

english: You should use an approved, cocoa-specific insecticide recommended by agricultural authorities. Because different chemicals target different insects, an extension officer must first inspect the pest to identify the exact chemical that will kill it safely.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ kookoo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ pɛ atsu nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai srɔtoi lɛ yeɔ kooloi srɔtoi anɔ. Esa akɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛna tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni baagbe amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: If I spray chemical on my cocoa farm once, will it completely wipe out all the pests forever?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai shwie kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ shikome pɛ lɛ, Ani ebaajie tsɛŋemɔ helai fɛɛ kɛya naanɔ?

english: No chemical eliminates pests forever. A single spray may kill current insects, but new pests can fly in from neighboring farms or hatch from eggs left behind, requiring regular farm management.
ga: Tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ agbe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛya naanɔ. Spray kome pɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ. Shi tsɛŋemɔ helai heei Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli loo amɛfɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni ashi yɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: How do I know if the pest control chemical I sprayed on my cocoa farm actually worked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will know it worked if you find dead insects on the ground or under leaves within a day or two, and if new, undamaged green leaves begin to sprout without being eaten.
ga: Obaale akɛ etsu nii kɛji ona kooloi bibii ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ loo baai ashishi yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli. Ni kɛji akɛ baai eŋɔli heei lɛ Mɛi ni efiteee lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ ni ayeee amɛ.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me when insects attack my cocoa trees?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua mi-kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: An extension officer can visit your farm to examine the damaged leaves, identify the specific insect causing the harm, recommend the right chemical treatment, and teach you how to spray safely.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ aya oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyakwɛ baai ni efite lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ kooloi bibii pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ awui baa lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he ŋaa ni otsɔɔ bɔ ni afeɔ ashwieɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why is it important for an extension officer to come and inspect my farm in person instead of me just describing the problem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni extension officer lɛ diɛŋtsɛ abakwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, ha nɛ ma tsɔɔ nyagba ɔ mi kɛkɛ.

english: Many cocoa pests and leaf diseases look similar to an untrained eye. An extension officer needs to physically inspect the farm to see the actual insects, assess the extent of the damage, and prescribe the correct solution.
ga: Kookoo mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai babaoo tamɔ hiŋmɛi ni atsɔseee lɛ. Esa akɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛ ŋmɔji amli koni ana kɛji kooloi bibii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni nɔ ni efite lɛ fa ha lɛ mli ni okwɛ tsabaa ni ja.

english: How often should I check my cocoa trees after spraying them with insect killer?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ sɛɛ?

english: You should inspect your farm at least once a week after spraying. Regular checks help you see if pests are returning, if hidden eggs have hatched, or if the trees are producing healthy new growth.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli beni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛba. Akpɔlɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ efɔ. Aloo ani tso lɛ miiwo shweremɔ hee ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Can I bring samples of damaged cocoa leaves or insects to an extension officer to get advice?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo baai loo kooloi bibii ni efite lɛ eko aba koni mikɛ extension officer lɛ asusu he?

english: Yes, collecting fresh damaged leaves and placing any insects you find in a clear container helps the extension officer identify the exact problem and give you the right treatment plan quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ abua baai ni efite kɛ kooloi ni ana lɛ anaa yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛyoo naagba lɛ oya ni amɛto tsamɔ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes and green waste inside the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mɔ ni etse ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm feeding. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaf funnel where it is moist and shaded, eating the young leaves before they unfold, which leaves ragged holes as the leaf grows.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm niyenii he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋshɔi lɛ amli he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii lɛ ni ayeɔ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha buji amli agbala be mli ni baai lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips that carry a virus. As they feed on the underside of the leaves, they transmit the virus, which disrupts the leaf's normal growth and causes it to wrinkle and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni hiɛ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ Amɛbaagbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ ada bɔ ni sa. ni eha etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under full sunlight. Shade trees block excessive direct sun and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa tsɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The maize stretches upward to reach light, using up energy that should have gone into growing bigger cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abɛi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa kane lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ eya kɛyashi ebatsɔ ŋmei agbo lɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: Too many suckers around one plantain stem share the same root water and nutrients. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems to feed, resulting in larger and heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Akɛni ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle tso lɛ he hewɔ lɛ, tso kome pɛ kɛ shishifãi amli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ falɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ayeɔ, ni no haa aduawai akuu ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push tiny stems into the soil after the yellow flowers drop off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi etso bibioo lɛ kɛmiijɛ mli lɛ? kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ lɛ egbee shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: This natural behavior is called 'pegging.' Groundnut flowers grow on the stem above ground, but once pollinated, the plant grows pegs down into the soil where the actual pods can safely grow and mature underground.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ 'fixation.' Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ pollination wo mli lɛ, akɛ tsei lɛ fĩɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant and dries out the pollen inside the flower. When pollen cannot fertilize the flower properly, the plant sheds the flower to save its water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollen nyɛɛɛ aha fɔfɔii lɛ afee fɛo jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines grow much better when I give them tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ha amɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Akɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛduɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground when there is too much rain on my flat farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ? Ani nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli tsɔ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen from the air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain sits on flat land without draining, water fills the soil gaps and drowns the roots, allowing fungal rots to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ Nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbo ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpea on my land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu cowpea dani wɔdu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea is a legume crop that works with natural bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in its roots. When the cowpea plant breaks down, it releases this natural plant food into the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji cowpea tso lɛ gbee shi Ejieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does using a drip hose to water my crops help them grow better than using a bucket?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ drip hose ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ baagi tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Drip hose watering slowly delivers water directly to the plant's roots without wasting it through evaporation or runoff. It keeps the soil consistently moist without over-soaking the plant leaves, which helps prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Abaakɛ drip hose awo nu mli fiofio. Ha nu lɛ aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ni okɛ nu ni hoɔ loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ akafite. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my crops start wilting and turning yellow even when there is plenty of water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely waterlogged, plant roots cannot breathe in air and begin to rot. When roots rot, they lose the ability to drink water and take up nutrients, causing the leaves above ground to yellow and wilt as if they were thirsty.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu ni amɛye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kumai miiye amɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with few fruits when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food through their leaves. When shaded by big trees, the plants stretch upward trying to reach the sun, spending all their energy growing tall instead of producing strong stems and healthy fruits.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ ohewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii koni oda lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my crops instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Plants growing too close together fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and air movement around its leaves to grow big and resist diseases.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ ehe lɛ nɔ. Baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ afee agbo ni helai nyɛŋ amɔ lɛ.

english: What actually happens to my crops when I apply store-bought fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizers act like nutrient-rich food for the soil. Once dissolved by moisture, plant roots absorb these nutrients (like nitrogen and phosphorus) to build stronger roots, greener leaves, and heavier fruits.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwie shi lɛ Tse shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii nɛɛ (tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus) koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni wa, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why is it important for me to clear and loosen the hard soil before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli ni mafo mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil creates air spaces and makes it easy for tender young plant roots to spread out deep into the ground. It also allows rain and water to soak into the root zone instead of washing away over the hard surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui baa, ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa nugbɔ kɛ nu hu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeho yɛ hei ni wa lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of poor soil or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ?

english: Yellowing caused by poor soil usually shows up evenly across older leaves first as the plant starves for nutrients. Yellowing from disease often appears as irregular spots, patches, or rotting areas on specific leaves regardless of age.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ejaakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hela ni haa mɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo hei ni egbo yɛ baai komɛi anɔ, ekɔɔɔ afii ni mɔ lɛ eye lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds hurt my main crops if they are just growing next to them in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. This starves your crops, leading to lower yields during harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do insects and animals seem to attack my crops more when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ babaoo kɛ́ amɛbɔi fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers and young fruits produce sweet smells, rich sugars, and soft plant tissues that attract insects and animals looking for food. Protecting your crops right before and during flowering is critical to saving your harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii jieɔ muji ni ŋɔɔ waa. sugar ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei amli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni miitao niyenii lɛ. Onibii ni ooobu he dani fɔfɔii lɛ baawo kɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia waa koni okɛto oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use the same chemical spray I bought at the shop on all the different crops on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: No, because different crop varieties react differently to chemicals. A spray designed to kill weeds in corn might destroy broadleaf crops like tomatoes or beans, so each crop requires specific chemicals used at the correct dosages.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ tsofai ahe. Spray ni afee koni akɛgbe jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ hu baanyɛ afite tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo tamɔ tomato loo ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso biɔ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko ni sa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that provide vital shade and keep the soil moist, helping the tender cocoa trees survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Staking yam vines spreads the leaves out so they can catch more sunlight and air. This allows the plant to make more food, which goes down into growing larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ gbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo. Je shishi kɛtsɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when they experience high heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moist and mulching around the plants helps cool the soil and protects the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ he ko ni edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Tsei lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that bakes the soil. If seeds sprout and the rain stops, the seedlings will dry up and die before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: Too much rain fills the air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the roots and creating moist conditions where rot-causing fungi thrive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to ruin my maize farm overnight without me seeing them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-corn ŋmɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ kome ni minaaa amɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the central funnel of the maize leaves during the hot day to stay cool, and they come out to feed aggressively at night when it is cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Ni amɛbaaje kpo kɛyatao niyenii kɛ hiɛdɔɔ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow close to my pepper plants make the peppers small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa pepper lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, light, and soil nutrients directly from pepper roots, leaving the pepper plants with too little food to grow big, healthy fruits.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hia kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ náa niyenii fioo tsɔ ni enyɛɔ ewoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra shoots allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree, reducing high humidity that causes black pod disease and helping the tree focus energy on making pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. Tsɔɔmɔ hulutsoo ni fa ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why did my crop leaves dry up and die after I placed chemical fertilizer right against the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ewo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very concentrated and draws water out of plant stems and roots if placed directly against them. It should always be placed a few inches away in a ring around the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli be fɛɛ be, ni ekɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to give each of my maize plants so I don't destroy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa? bɔni afee ni akafite lɛ

english: Using a standard measuring container, like a specific bottle cap or small tin for every plant, ensures each crop gets the exact right amount without burning the roots or wasting fertilizer.
ga: Kɛtsɔ nɔ ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ tɔ mli tsɔne loo tsinsii bibioo ko nɔ. kɛha tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nɔ ni sa nɔ ni eshãaa shishifãi lɛ loo efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it necessary to spread my fertilizer evenly across the field instead of putting big piles around a few plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ moŋ fe ni aaabua naa yɛ tsei fioo komɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading fertilizer evenly allows all plant roots to access nutrients equally, preventing some plants from getting burnt by excess while others starve.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haaa la ashɛ tsei komɛi ahe fe nine, yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ yeɔ ekrokomɛi hu.

english: Is it better to measure manure in buckets before applying it to my vegetable beds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ masusu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baagi mli lɛ he dani mikɛwo mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, measuring manure with a bucket gives you a consistent amount per bed, ensuring your whole field has equal soil fertility so crops grow uniformly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ okɛ baagi susu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni falɛ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ saatso fɛɛ saatso nɔ. Enɛ haa okpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ baaná shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant too many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants and very low yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when planting on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Spacing cassava about 1 meter apart gives the roots enough room underground to swell into large tubers without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Aaafee mita kome ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why are the crops on one side of my farm growing tall while the ones on the other side remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when soil nutrients, sunlight, or water are not equal across the land, or when fertilizer is applied inconsistently.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, hulu la, loo nu lɛ jeee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. aloo kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ

english: How can I make sure all my tomato plants mature and produce fruit around the same time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-tomato tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii yɛ be kome too mli?

english: Planting seeds on the same day, giving every plant the same measured amount of fertilizer, and watering them equally helps all plants grow and ripen at the same pace.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ Ha tso fɛɛ tso ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa. kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛyeɔ amɛbuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ oyaiyeli kome mli.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce big leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen makes leaves grow large, but balanced nutrients are needed to send energy down into growing thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛbaa lɛ afee wuji. Shi niyenii mli nibii ni sa jogbaŋŋ he miihia koni akɛ hewalɛ amaje kɛya ŋmeii ni mli edɔ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some cocoa pods stay small and dry up while others grow large on the same tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi ji bibii ni amɛgbi lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi daa agbo yɛ tso kome nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees produce small or withered pods when the tree lacks enough nutrients or water to feed every pod, or when pests damage them during early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Aloo egboɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ nii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: How can I accurately measure if my harvest this season is bigger than last season's harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛji akɛ mikpamɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ fa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmaa lɛ?

english: You can measure harvest by weighing dried beans or counting standard bags and measuring tins filled, giving you a clear quantity to compare year after year.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu okpamɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni ooosusu loo kotokui ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ akanemɔ kɛ tsɛnsii ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ susumɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa onáa yibɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni okɛtoɔ afi kɛ afi he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil, stopping the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the ground to nourish whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kɛji okpa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent rotting and helps the plant produce larger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafite ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: When planting cassava, does it matter which way up I stick the stem cutting into the ground?
ga: Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ akɛ tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, direction matters a lot. You must plant cassava stem cuttings with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky; if you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to emerge and your root yield will be very small.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ he miihia waa. Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmeii bibii adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu lɛ ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ Tsobii lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ baafee fioo kwraa.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in tall, thin, weak stalks with very small corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa anáa ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my crop right before a heavy rain storm or after?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa loo yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain. Applying fertilizer right before a heavy downpour will cause the rain to wash the food away before your plant roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ lɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers actually start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo tsei niyenii ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔi amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: What is causing small ragged holes and green droppings inside the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? No ekumɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's growing leaves. Catching them early with recommended treatments stops them from destroying the center stalk of the maize.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Tsamɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ baaye abua ni ekafite ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants wilting even though the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Wilting in wet soil usually means a soil-borne disease has attacked the plant's stem or roots, or that the roots have rotted from sitting in water. Damaged roots cannot pull water up to the leaves, so the plant wilts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ etutua tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ. loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni amɛwoɔ lɛ Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ gbiɔ.

english: If I spray chemical weedkiller on my land, will it stop my crops from growing there in the future?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii akakwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ wɔsɛɛ?

english: Chemical weedkillers break down over time in the soil, but using too much or the wrong type can stay in the ground and harm sensitive seeds. If you spray, you must wait a specific amount of time before planting new crops so the chemical disappears from the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ awui. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko dani okɛ tsei heei adu. koni tsofai lɛ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do some farmers let specific bushy plants completely cover their farmland without planting crops on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ŋmɛɔ tsei bibii komɛi gbɛ ni amɛduuu amɛŋmɔji lɛ?

english: These plants are cover crops that protect the soil from heavy rains washing away the good topsoil. They also stop unwanted weeds from growing and add natural nutrients back into the earth while the land rests.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ ji shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he. Amɛhaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ hu shwereɔ ni amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔ ehe lɛ.

english: How long should I leave my farmland to rest after farming on it for many years?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni miyajɔɔ mihe beni mitsu okwaayeli afii babaoo sɛɛ?

english: Resting your land for one to three years allows wild plants to grow and fall back onto the earth. This returns rich organic matter and nutrients to the tired soil naturally before you plant on it again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ afii kome kɛyashi afii etɛ baaha koo mli tsei akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ dani odu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when there is too much water sitting in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When excess water sits in the soil for too long without draining, it drowns the roots, stopping them from taking up plant food and causing them to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haaa amɛye tsei aniyenii, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: How does leaving dry leaves on top of my farm soil help my crops stay healthy in hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from baking the earth directly and keeps soil moisture from evaporating quickly so roots stay cool and hydrated.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya Koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has too much water underground before I plant maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa?

english: You can dig a small hole about two feet deep in your field. If water quickly fills the bottom and stays there even on dry days, the soil is waterlogged and needs drainage channels before you plant maize.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo bu bibioo ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee ninetalɔi 2 yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji nu eyi ŋshɔ lɛ shishi oya ni ehi jɛmɛ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ po nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee nɔ ni nu baatsɔ mli ni ehe baahia ni okɛ nu atsɔ mli dani odu ŋmãa.

english: Can putting a wire fence around my farm protect my crops from being damaged?
ga: Ani ŋtayaa ni akɛ ŋtayaai ebɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite?

english: A wire fence creates a strong physical barrier that keeps farm livestock and large wild animals from stepping on or eating your crops, though you will still need other methods to control tiny insect pests.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni akɛ waya fee lɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni mli wa ni tsiɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi kɛ koo mli kooloi wuji anaa koni amɛkanyiɛ onibii anɔ loo amɛkaye. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ gbɛi krokomɛi atsu nii lolo kɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii anɔ moŋ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and burning after I spray them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying pesticides during the hottest part of the day or mixing them too strong can burn tender leaves. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when the sun is cool.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ mli waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ. Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu la lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than the food crops I carefully plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local soil and harsh weather. Because they are stronger, they quickly steal water, sunlight, and nutrients away from your cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni wa ni ekɛ ehe ewo jɛmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli wa lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ amɛhe wa fe amɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ amli oya.

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce their own food. When shaded by big tree leaves, the crops stretch unnaturally high searching for light, making them weak and unable to produce good yields.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Kɛji tsei wuji ahe baai lɛ ha amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baashɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa ni eyatao la. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to make high soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and deep soil so the tubers can expand easily underground. High mounds also allow excess water to drain away, stopping your seed yams from rotting during heavy rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ he miihia sweet potato koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hu haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants drop off when the dry harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and protect itself from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will naturally grow fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Tso lɛ baaná ebɔɔ su ni ji eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over by itself when the fruit bunch starts to grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ ehe nɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and weak compared to the weight of a full bunch of fruit. You need to prop up the heavy stem using a strong, branched wooden pole so the wind does not pull it down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ akɛto aduawai akuu ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiimɔ he. Esa akɛ okɛ tso ni wa ni niji yɔɔ mli lɛ afi tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ akagbala amɛ kɛba shi

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree is stressed by hot, dry weather, if the tree lacks nutrients, or if tiny insects like mirids damage the flowers before they can form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ glase ni mli edɔ lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms eating the tender leaves hidden inside the center shoot of the maize plant. They must be sprayed early before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fallworms ni yeɔ baai bibii ni akɛtee ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Esa akɛ ashwie nɔ mra dani efite he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading a virus, or by extreme sun heat stressing the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. aloo kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil lacks calcium or when the plant receives uneven amounts of water while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid burning the bushes on my land before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms in the soil. Leaving cleared weeds to rot naturally into the soil keeps the ground moist and fertile for a longer time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my maize plants turn thin and light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee mlɛo ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal nitrogen, sunlight, and water from the soil that your maize plants need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nitrogen, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa o-abele tsei lɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Forest trees act as natural umbrellas that keep the ground cool and moist, protecting tender young cocoa leaves from scorching until the crop canopy develops enough to shade itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Buu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ he kɛyashi tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rainfall often washes nitrogen down beyond the reach of young plant roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen ni tsei bibii ashishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaf vegetation on top rather than storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete with the parent plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, helping the main plant produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the soil exposes them to maximum sunlight needed for growth, while keeping them dry and away from wet soil fungi that cause leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kɛ tsei ahe helai baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without growing into fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from being fertilized. When pollination fails, the plant drops the flower to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize help the soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into natural fertilizer in the soil, helping nearby crops grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes the exact nutrients that plant needs while giving crop-specific soil pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ náa shia ni hiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why is it better for me to water my pepper plants early in the morning instead of late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering in the morning gives plants the moisture needed to handle heat during the daytime. Evening watering leaves leaves wet overnight, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do small insects destroy my stored maize even after I tie the bags tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotokui lɛ fĩ shi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Insects or tiny eggs often come from the field inside the grain, or remain hidden in regular woven sacks. Standard bags allow air to pass through, allowing pests to breathe and multiply unless grain is dried properly and stored in sealed, airtight bags.
ga: ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli. loo akɛtee kotokui ni akpɛ lɛ amli Standard kotokui lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ muɔ ni amɛshwereɔ. Ja agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto vacuum kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli.

english: Can I grow my crops successfully without using any chemical fertilizer at all?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, you can grow crops without chemical fertilizer if you choose organic farming using compost or manure. However, for large-scale commercial farming, organic methods usually result in smaller or slower yields compared to using commercial fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ, kɛha jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo fioo loo amɛwoɔ nii blɛoo fe jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is the main difference in how crops behave when grown for family food versus growing for commercial sale?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsei asubaŋ mli kɛji akɛ adu kɛha weku niyenii kɛ nɔ ni adu kɛha jarayeli?

english: Crops grown just for the family can rely on natural soil nutrients even if yields are modest. However, crops grown for commercial sale need high yields and uniform size, which requires feeding the plant regular nutrients through proper fertilizer application.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ahaa wekui pɔtɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo lɛ faaa moŋ, shi ehe miihia ni tsei ni aduɔ yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ aná yibii babaoo ni amɛdalɛ afee ekome. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aha tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ nɔ.

english: Is organic farming better for my crop production than using store-bought fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Organic farming improves long-term soil health using natural plant and animal waste, but crops grow more slowly and yield less. Store-bought commercial fertilizers provide immediate food to crops for high production, but you must choose one path clearly based on your farm goals.
ga: Organic okwaayeli haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei kɛ kooloi ahe jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Shi tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi esa akɛ ohala gbɛ kome ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni damɔ otii ni okɛma ohiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I decide to switch completely from fertilizer to organic farming?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ matsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ kɛya okwaayeli ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli kwraa lɛ nɔ?

english: When you switch completely to organic farming, your crop yields may drop initially because natural fertilizers release nutrients to plants much slower than commercial fertilizers do.
ga: Kɛji otsake kwraa kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ Onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aba shi yɛ shishijee mli ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa tsei amli blɛoo kwraa fe jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly and stay small when I don't apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops need essential plant food from the soil to grow. When soil loses its natural nutrients from repeated farming, plants become stunted and weak unless extra fertilizer is added to feed them.
ga: Tsei he miihia tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ edebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ okwaayeli ni afeɔ shii abɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he koni akɛha amɛ niyenii.

english: Will applying special commercial fertilizer damage my crops or make them unsafe?
ga: Ani jarayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii loo ebaaha amɛfee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: No, special commercial fertilizers contain clean plant food designed to make crops grow strong. As long as you follow the correct measurement instructions, fertilizer will improve crop health rather than harm it.
ga: Dabi, tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli lɛ amli tsei aniyenii ni he tse ni afee koni ekɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni obaanyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja ni kɔɔ susumɔ he lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye amɛ awui.

english: How can I tell by looking at my crops that they are in urgent need of fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛ́ mikwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia amɛ oya?

english: When crops lack fertilizer, their leaves often turn pale yellow instead of deep green, their stems remain thin, and they struggle to produce healthy flowers or fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. Ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná fɔfɔi loo aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Why should I spend money buying special fertilizer for my crops instead of letting nature grow them for free?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ahe kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha adebɔɔ akwɛ lɛ yaka

english: While nature can grow plants, natural soil often lacks enough nutrients for heavy harvests. Investing in fertilizer feeds the crops properly so you harvest enough quantity to make a good profit when selling.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ baanyɛ akwɛ tsei moŋ Shi bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ shikpɔji lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ shika wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni okpa babaoo bɔ ni sa ni oná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛ́ oohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my neighboring farmers get much bigger harvests than me when we planted the exact same crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi yɛ be mli ni wɔduɔ nibii ni wɔduɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Farmers getting larger harvests are likely feeding their crops with special fertilizers during key growth stages, which allows their plants to produce much more fruit than unfertilized crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi ni kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi haa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛtsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe tsei ni anáaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Should I feel discouraged if my farm requires costly fertilizer to produce a good crop yield?
ga: Ani esa akɛ minijiaŋ aje wui kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he miihia mi koni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: No, you shouldn't be discouraged. Needing fertilizer is a normal part of commercial farming because high-yielding crops take up a lot of plant food from the soil that must be replaced.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ onijiaŋ jeɔ wui. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ jarayeli okwaayeli mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ tsei niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni esa akɛ atsake lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata cacao tso he lɛ moŋ fe ni maŋmɛ gbɛ ni eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Removing excess branches allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, which helps the remaining branches concentrate energy on producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa niji ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know which branches to cut when trimming my cocoa tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei niji ni esa akɛ mafo kɛji mifolɔ kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Focus on cutting weak, overcrowded, crisscrossing branches, and shoots growing from the trunk, while keeping the main structural branches intact.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni eyi obɔ, ni efo amɛhe kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsɔne lɛ niji titrii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often in a year am I supposed to trim my cocoa trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ yɛ afi mli?

english: Trimming is usually done twice a year, especially before the main rainy seasons, to prepare the trees for flowering and prevent disease build-up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afoɔ tsei lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Koni asaa tsei lɛ ahe kɛha fɔfɔi ni baa ni helai akabua amɛhe naa.

english: What should I do if I notice black or rotting spots on some branches of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii ni egbo yɛ kookoo niji komɛi anɔ?

english: You should cut off those infected branches slightly below the diseased part to stop the sickness from spreading to the rest of the tree and neighboring crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli fioo yɛ fã ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ shishi koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa tree branches keep drying up and getting sick during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ egbi ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture and low air circulation create a perfect environment for fungal diseases to grow. Pruning helps air dry the trees quickly after rains.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ fioo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ. Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: If I cut off a diseased branch, can it grow back healthy again?
ga: Kɛji ofo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Ani ebaanyɛ eda ekoŋŋ ni efee hewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Once a branch is diseased, that specific branch cannot heal, but removing it allows the tree to sprout new, healthy shoots that can bear good fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ hela mɔ tso nine lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsa. Shi niji ni aaajie lɛ baaha tso lɛ akwɛ̃ niji heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are some of my mature cocoa trees not producing any pods at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ ekomɛi wooo ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Trees often fail to bear fruit due to lack of sunlight, overcrowding, or nutrient loss caused by feeding too many unnecessary branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei wooo yibii yɛ hulu la ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ayeɔ amɛ fe nine loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Will cutting off unproductive branches really help my cocoa tree produce more fruit?
ga: Ani niji ni wooo yibii ni afoɔ lɛ baaye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, removing branches that take up plant food without yielding pods redirects water and nutrients to healthy branches that can produce cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni yeɔ jwɛi ni ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ ni aaafo lɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ afee kookoo lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clean up dead leaves and cut branches from my farm floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ baai ni egboi kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing farm debris removes hiding places for destructive pests like insects and stops fungal spores on dead branches from jumping back onto healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Okwaafoi amli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛyaa kookoo tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it safe to leave pruned cocoa branches under the trees to rot naturally?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi kookoo niji ni afolɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi koni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: It is safer to gather cut branches away from tree bases, especially if they are diseased, because leaving infected wood near tree trunks can spread illness back into the soil and roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooha tso lɛ niji ni afo lɛ ahi tso lɛ shishi. Titri lɛ kɛji hela mɔ nine lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ ashi tso ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help make the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the groundnut plant dies, this captured nitrogen remains in the dirt, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni amɔ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests and diseases that attack maize a permanent home to multiply. Rotating with different crops, like legumes, gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa abɛi akɛ shia ni baahi shi daa koni amɛshwere lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ amɛhe Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How do groundnuts produce nuts under the ground when the flowers open above the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After the groundnut flower is pollinated above ground, it forms a long stem called a peg. This peg grows downwards, bends toward the earth, and pushes itself deep into the soil, where the tip swells up to form the groundnut pod.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pin lɛ baafee. Pin nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ shishigbɛ. Ekoto shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Eshishigbɛ lɛ baafu aahu kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmei ŋmei.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam plants to make them climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei awo sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in full sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which is then sent down into the root system to build thick, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in full sunlight and dry out fast. Plantains grow very quickly and have large leaves that create living shade, protecting the delicate young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to stand the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to harvest without digging up my entire field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Look for the leaves to start turning yellow and shedding, then dig up two or three sample plants. Open the pods; if the inside of the shell has dark brown or black veins and the nuts tightly fill the shell, the groundnuts are ready to harvest.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii fioo komɛi, ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ amli; Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛwo ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ amli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ eshɛ he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that your maize is starving for nitrogen. The plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves and sends it to the top to keep the young growth and ears alive, causing the lower leaves to die off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen. Tsei heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha tsei bibii kɛ toi lɛ aya hiɛ. ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ agboi

english: Why does my cassava crop stay green and survive long dry seasons when my maize dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni mi-ŋmei lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, strong roots that store water and nutrients deep in the ground, and it can drop its leaves during dry spells to conserve water. Once the rains return, it quickly recovers and continues growing.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni toɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni abaanyɛ ashɛrɛ baai lɛ ashwie yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu akafite. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, ebaatsa oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow during the hot months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to reduce water loss when it is too hot or dry, but yellowing leaves often mean tiny insects like whiteflies have infected the plant with a virus. Keeping weeds down and protecting plants from insects reduces leaf curl.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ loo egbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloo bibioo ko tamɔ whitefly kɛ hela ko ewo tso lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ haa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds in my farm make my crops yield smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because the weeds steal these essential food sources, your crops cannot get what they need to produce large fruits, grains, or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo aduawai wuji, ŋmaa, loo ŋmeii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so I don't pick it too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? koni akabua naa oya tsɔ

english: Maize shows clear physical signs when mature, such as the outer husks turning pale brown and a small black layer forming at the tip of the grain kernels, usually around 90 to 120 days after planting.
ga: Abɛi baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni edara lɛ, tamɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ diŋ. Efeɔ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ naagbee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some fast-growing vegetables take only a few weeks to harvest while other crops take many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ heɔ otsii fioo pɛ dani akpaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi heɔ nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Leafy vegetables like spinach grow rapidly because they only build soft leaves, whereas cereal and root crops like maize and cassava need several months to store energy in heavy grains or tubers.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ spinach lɛ daa oya ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ baai bibii pɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmaa kɛ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Eheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani hewalɛ toɔ dumɔwu loo ŋmãa ni tsii mli.

english: Can I harvest my cassava early if I just want to cook and eat it at home?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makpa ŋmei mra. Ani ehi kɛji miisumɔ ni mahoo ni maye yɛ shia?

english: Yes, you can harvest cassava early at around 6 to 8 months for soft tubers to eat, but waiting up to 12 months allows the roots to grow much larger and produce more starch.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa ŋmei lɛ mra kɛjɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli koni oye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Shi kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi nyɔji 12 lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Is it bad if I leave mature vegetables on my farm for too long without harvesting them?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mishi aduawai ni edara yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa amɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field past their harvest time causes them to overripe, turn tough or rot, and makes them easy targets for insects and diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛho kpamɔɔ be lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔ fe nine, amɛwa loo amɛgboi, ni ebaaha amɛfee nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: What is the difference between crops I harvest once and crops that keep producing food over time?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tso ni mikpaa shikome kɛ tso ni woɔ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Single-harvest crops like maize finish their life after producing seed once, while continuous crops like tomatoes or peppers keep flowering and fruiting as long as the plant stays healthy and watered.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa shikome pɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, gbeɔ amɛwala naa beni amɛwo dumɔwu kome pɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yaa nɔ tamɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ Ebaaya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni enine shɛɔ nu nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants dry up completely after yielding once, while my neighbor's climbing beans keep giving pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ egbi kwraa beni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kome sɛɛ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ ŋmeii

english: Bush beans are programmed to mature all at once for a quick, single harvest, whereas climbing bean varieties continue growing longer vines and producing pods over several months.
ga: Ato tsina ŋmeii ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛshwere shikome koni amɛkpa oya yɛ be kome mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kwɔɔ lɛ Yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ wain tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants take a break from flowering after I harvest the first fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ heɔ hejɔɔmɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe beni mikpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After producing a big harvest, pepper plants temporarily use their energy to build fresh branches and roots before starting a new round of flower and fruit production.
