ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛkɛfee tsei niji kɛ shishifãi heei dani amɛje fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei ni yɔɔ kpokpaa nɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do the newer seed varieties mature much faster than the seeds my elders used to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ kwɛ̃ oya kwraa fe nɔ ni mi onukpai lɛ du lɛ?

english: Modern improved seeds are specially bred by agricultural scientists to complete their growth faster, helping farmers harvest early before dry spells or late-season pest attacks occur.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi ekwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛdara oya. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii oya dani hɔmɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa.

english: How come my neighbor's tomatoes are ready for market so quickly while mine are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tomatoi lɛ efee klalo kɛha jara nɔ mra be mli ni minɔ̃ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Your neighbor is likely growing an early-maturing hybrid tomato variety, which is bred to set fruit and ripen days or weeks ahead of traditional varieties.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ duɔ tomato ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra. Atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni amɛshwere gbii loo otsii komɛi mra fe blema tomatoi.

english: Does picking my tomatoes before they are fully red affect how long they stay fresh after harvest?
ga: Ani tomatoi ni abaakpa dani amɛfee tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa lɛ baaná bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Harvesting tomatoes at the 'mature green' or early pink stage actually helps them last longer during transport, whereas picking them fully soft and red shortens their shelf life.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tomato to ‘eŋɔli ni egbɔ’ loo mra be mli pinki mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ tomato ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kwraa ni eyɛ tsuru lɛ toɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshihilɛ be lɛ afee kuku.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible so that I can harvest more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the maize plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stalks and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni he wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside crops like maize naturally feeds the soil and helps your main crop grow bigger without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni oye obua otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛdara ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat, which scorch their soft leaves. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains next to young cocoa creates a safe environment that retains moisture and shields seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã. Shi tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔ tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. Kakao tso lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛɔ nɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the leaves and branches from around the base of my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie baai kɛ eniji kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing the base allows fresh air to flow through the tree canopy and reduces dampness. Excessive moisture around the trunk creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases like black pod disease to spread.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is exhausted and needs manure or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji, ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia mi?

english: Exhausted soil causes plants to grow slowly, produce small leaves, turn pale yellow instead of dark green, or yield small harvests. Adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer replaces vital nutrients that previous crops took from the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo, amɛnáa baai bibii, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataa he lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ náa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the harsh sun from evaporating soil water, keeps root systems cool, and gradually breaks down into food for the soil.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants developing ragged holes and pale yellow strips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on young shoots, while yellow strips indicate a nutrient deficiency. Inspecting crop leaves early helps you spray appropriate remedies or apply fertilizer before damage spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni baa ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa. Tso lɛ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ tsofa ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nɔ ni efite lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if I do not harvest them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store food for the plant, but when left past maturity during heavy rains, water builds up around the roots. Excess soil water starves the roots of air and allows destructive soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Shi kɛ́ oha egbɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato wooo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away flower pollen and creates high humidity that causes fungal blights. Without proper pollination and with weak plant stems from excessive dampness, tomato flowers naturally fall off before fruit can form.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ pollen lɛ ni ehaa hulutsoo ni naa wa ni kɛ fungal leaf blight baa lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to mount wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into the air, preventing leaf disease and allowing the plant to direct its energy into expanding the root tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Tsi baa helai anaa ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛkudɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh, direct sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Leaving larger canopy trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a cooler environment that keeps the seedlings alive until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adumɔ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a survival trick to conserve water and keep the roots beneath the ground alive. Once the rains return, the plant will quickly sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkwɛ amɛshikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help restore the plant's healthy green color and build strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔlii lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ su eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. Planting them alongside or in rotation with maize acts as a free natural fertilizer that improves the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi loo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot, which lives in damp soil and blocks the water pathways inside the stem. To stop it from spreading to other plants, you must pull up and destroy the affected crops and avoid planting tomatoes in that spot next season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa Enɛ ji koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei krokomɛi anɔ. Esa akɛ ojie ŋmɔshi nibii ni ena hela lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tomato ni ooodu yɛ nakai he lɛ he yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap out of leaves and spread viruses. Spraying the leaves with an organic neem oil solution or an approved insecticide will clear the pests so the plant can grow normal leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ baai ni sa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible, which gives the leaves energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp wet soil, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoot sprouts growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: When too many young shoots grow around the main plantain stalk, they steal water and plant food away from the main stem. Removing the extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, which allows the parent plant to produce a bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ Ejuɔ nu ni ekwɛɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, competing directly with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your crops get all the food they need to yield large fruits and healthy cobs.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ aduawai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer when the ground is completely dry and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so that crop roots can safely absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil under high heat can scorch and burn the plant roots, causing more harm than good.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛshã. Ekɛ awuiyeli babaoo baa fe kpakpa.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight for growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where fungal diseases spread easily, helping the plant direct its energy into growing big underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛshwere. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava stem cuttings have tiny raised buds or 'eyes' where the leaves will sprout, and these buds must always point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the plant to waste energy trying to grow downward first, resulting in weak roots and lower yields.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋmei tso lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii, loo ŋmeii, ni baa lɛ baajɛ mli aba, ni esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yitso lɛ shwere kɛtee shishi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda kɛya shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my neighbor farmers cut off extra small shoots growing around the base of a plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ shwieɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, sunlight, and water. Pruning them away so only one or two strong suckers remain allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Plantain titri lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant maize and cassava together in the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping them works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly over a full year. You can harvest the maize early without disturbing the cassava, getting two crops from the same land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ okpa ŋmãa mra ni ogbalaaa ŋmãa lɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmãa enyɔ ni ooona kɛjɛ he kome lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and helps form full, heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Maize drains a lot of nutrients from the ground, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When you rotate them, they naturally feed the soil so your next crops grow better without needing as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji otsake amɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa atsu nii.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, shields the earth from the hot sun. It keeps water from evaporating too fast, protects root systems from extreme heat, and gradually breaks down into rich organic food for the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ akashwie oya tsɔ. Ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings dry up and burn under full daylight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and have small roots that cannot handle direct, scorching sunlight without drying out fast. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains near young cocoa keeps the soil cool and moist while the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshishifãi bibii yɔɔ. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaaa egbi oya Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hidden in the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? ni akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats the soft growing center of maize plants. Inspecting your fields early and using recommended bio-pesticides or approved sprays controls them before they destroy your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before the fruit can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black rotting bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when plants cannot get enough calcium or when watering is uneven during dry spells. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering helps the plant pull up the calcium it needs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato nɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ená calcium ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under intense full sun. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves, acting like living umbrellas that provide crucial shade and keep the soil moist around the young cocoa roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from drying out the earth. This keeps the ground cool and locks in soil moisture so roots can drink even when rainfall is low.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo po.

english: Maize takes heavy nutrients like nitrogen out of the ground. Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny root organisms that pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. No baajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it bad for me to spread fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ani no ehiii kɛha mi?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for plant roots to safely take it in. When placed on dry soil, the raw fertilizer creates heat and heavy salts that burn and damage crop roots.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre shweshweeshwe. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ Ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni shãa ni efiteɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: Why should I leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them very close together to get more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and ground food, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough resources to grow large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni atswa lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to produce energy for the tuber growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground helps them absorb sun better and protects them from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛheɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally as a defense mechanism to survive drought. By losing leaves, the plant reduces the amount of water lost into the air, keeping itself alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Ehaa ehe hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollination stresses tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than spending resources to grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Black pod is caused by a mold-like fungus that thrives in wet conditions. Heavy rain splashes the fungus spores from the ground onto the trees, where moisture allows it to rapidly attack and ruin the cocoa pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji ŋmei ko ni tamɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa amɛtutuaa kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ oya ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stem share the same water and soil food, making all of them weak. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot to get all the energy needed to produce a massive bunch of plantains.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ tsei bibii babaoo ni ebɔle plantain tso kome he lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛwo plantains babaoo lɛ aha.

english: How do I know if my maize crops are getting enough water during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water, their leaves roll up tightly like a drinking straw during the afternoon heat to trap moisture. If you notice the leaves stay rolled up even in the cool early morning, your crops are severely stressed and need water right away.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Kɛji oyɔse akɛ baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe lolo yɛ leebi maŋkpa fɛ̃i be mli po lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao waa ni nu he miihia amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow when water sits on my farm after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain creates standing water around your plants without draining away, it drowns the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb food from the soil. This root suffocation causes the leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ he fɛɛ he. otsei lɛ ni okɛ nu shwieee amɛnɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ hãaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛmɔmɔ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ shishifãi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How does digging small water channels or gutters through my vegetable farm help my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋshɔ bibioo ko loo nu ŋshɔ ni mikɛfoɔ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Digging small channels directs excess water away from your plant roots so they do not rot during heavy rains, while guiding the water gently across the farm so the roots can drink without topsoil washing away.
ga: Bu bibioo ko ni aaafo Ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli. Koni tso shishifãi akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛfɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my yam vines bending and stretching towards one side of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpã kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally bend and grow toward whichever direction receives the most sunlight. The leaves reach for light so they can produce the energy needed to grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi ni amɛdaraa yɛ he fɛɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Baai lɛ náa la koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much leafy fertilizer (nitrogen) but lacks root-building nutrients (potassium), the plant puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of feeding and expanding the cassava tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ baai ahe tsofa (nitrogen) babaoo shi ebɛ niyenii ni haa shishifãi maa shi (potassium) lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii ni amɛdu lɛ,.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cover the soil around our tomatoes with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ mulch awo he ni ebɔle wɔhe lɛ? Tomato kɛ jwɛi?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass acts like a protective blanket that keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth. It keeps the roots cool, holds soil moisture much longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon heat becomes too intense or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. The plant panics from stress and sheds its flowers to protect itself from losing too much water.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ sheɔ gbeyei kɛjɛɔ haomɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu ehe koni nu babaoo akafite.

english: If maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots will fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves will block sunlight from one another. This competition results in weak, thin stalks with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do caterpillars and worms seem to destroy my cabbage leaves much faster when the weather is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ oya kwraa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Warm weather speeds up the body processes of insects, making caterpillars eat much faster and lay eggs more rapidly. Heat allows a small pest population to multiply quickly and strip leaves in a short time.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nibii ni yaa nɔ yɛ kooloi agbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii mra. Dɔlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii akui ni amɛhiɔ shi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ebaanyɛ ejie baai yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: What does an extension officer mean when they tell me a crop has different 'varieties'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ beni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baa yɛ ‘srɔtoi’ amli lɛ?

english: A crop variety is a specific type within a plant family that has been bred for special qualities—such as growing faster, resisting diseases better, or producing larger and sweeter fruits than normal wild plants.
ga: Tso henɔ ji tso pɔtɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ tso weku ko mli ni atsɔse lɛ koni ená sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ ni eda oya. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ loo ewoɔ aduawai ni dara ni ŋɔɔ fe koo mli tsei krokomɛi.

english: Why are there multiple improved varieties of the same crop available for me to buy instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ babaoo moŋ fe ekome pɛ lɛ?

english: Agricultural researchers develop different varieties to suit different farmer needs, such as varieties that handle dry weather better, ones that mature quickly, or ones that yield extra oil or food for processing.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi feɔ srɔtoi srɔtoi. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ okwaafoi srɔtoi ahiamɔ nii akpã gbee, tamɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ. Srɔtoi ni daa oya loo henɔi ni haa mu loo niyenii krokomɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii.

english: Is it better for me to keep planting my traditional local crops or switch to newly developed varieties?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei loo matsake kɛya tsei srɔtoi ni afee ehee lɛ anɔ?

english: Local crops are familiar and often taste good, but newly developed varieties from research centers are bred to give you higher total harvests and better protection against common pests and droughts.
ga: Ale akutso lɛ mli tsei ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi atsɔse ŋmeii heei ni afee kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ koni eha oná yibii fɛɛ ni fa fe tsutsu lɛ. kɛ hebuu ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hɔmɔ ni baa lɛ he.

english: If I harvest fruits from an improved variety on my farm, can I plant those seeds for next season?
ga: Kɛji mikpa aduawai kɛjɛ tso ko ni atsake lɛ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ madu nakai dumɔwui lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: It is best to buy fresh certified seeds or seedlings each time because seeds taken from harvested hybrid plants often lose their high yield strength and will not grow as well as the parent plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei loo dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ, ni amɛdaŋ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ.

english: What makes Tenera oil palm seedlings special compared to the wild palm trees growing in my area?
ga: Mɛni haa Tenera oil palm dumɔwui lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto kɛ akɛto koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Tenera is a special cross-bred oil palm that has a thin shell and thick, fleshy pulp, which produces much more palm oil per bundle than wild or unselected traditional palms.
ga: Tenera ji tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛ mu fee ni eshishifã lɛ mli tseee ni eshishifãi lɛ mli tse. ni jieɔ ŋmei fɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmei kome mli fe adebɔɔ mli ŋmei loo blema ŋmei ni ahalaaa lɛ.

english: Why do some fruits on my plants change color from green to yellow or red as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As a fruit matures, the plant breaks down the green pigment (chlorophyll) and produces natural sugars and new colors to signal that the fruit is ripe, sweet, and ready to be harvested.
ga: Kɛji aduawai lɛ eda kwraa Tso lɛ gbálaa ŋmɔtɔ ko (chlorophyll) mli ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars kɛ sui heei baa koni ekɛtsɔɔ akɛ aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: How can two crop plants of the same type produce fruits that look different in color or size?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei enyɔ ni ji henɔ kome lɛ awo yibii ni sui loo amɛdalɛi sɔrɔtoi yɔɔ mli?

english: Just like children can look different from the same parents, different varieties inherit specific genetic traits that determine whether their fruits grow large, stay small, or turn red, yellow, or green.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛbii ji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Abaanyɛ aná sui srɔtoi kɛjɛ fɔlɔ kome mli Sui sɔrɔtoi lɛ yeɔ fɔmɔ su pɔtɛɛ ko ni tsɔɔ kɛji amɛyibii lɛ daa, amɛhiɔ shi bibii, loo amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ, ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if a fruit is ready to harvest if the variety stays green even when it is ripe?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ aduawai lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa kɛji akɛ srɔtoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ ekwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Besides color, you can tell a crop is ripe by checking its size, how soft or firm the fruit feels, how easily it detaches from the stem, or by testing the taste of a few sample fruits.
ga: Kɛfata su he lɛ, obaanyɛ ole be ni ŋmɔshi nibii ekwɛ̃ kɛtsɔ bɔ ni edara ha lɛ nɔ. Yibii lɛ amli bɔ ni eyɔɔ blɛoo loo eyɛ shiŋŋ ha Te ejɛɔ tso lɛ shishi mlɛo eha tɛŋŋ? aloo kɛtsɔ aduawai fioo komɛi ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ akamɔ nɔ.

english: How do researchers in agricultural labs develop new plants before bringing them to farmers?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni niiamlitaolɔi ni yɔɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔhei lɛ afee tsei heei dani amɛkɛyaha okwaafoi lɛ?

english: Scientists carefully select parent plants with the best traits—like big fruit, good flavor, or disease resistance—and cross-pollinate them in controlled environments to create stronger seedlings for field testing.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi halaa fɔlɔi tsei ni yɔɔ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ aduawai wuji, ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa loo helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ cross-pollinate yɛ shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ mli koni ekɛfee dumɔwui ni he wa kɛha ŋmɔ mli kaa.

english: Why do some crop varieties start producing fruit quickly while others take several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Every variety has a natural growth timeline written into its traits; early-maturing varieties spend energy producing flowers quickly, while late-maturing ones spend more time building strong roots and branches first.
ga: Henɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ be ni aŋmala akɛ eji su. Tsoi srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo fɔfɔi oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies and burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains around them creates living umbrellas that protect the delicate leaves and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ Tsei lɛ ahe koni afee ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize stems mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and healthy so the plant can grow big cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abele tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes happen when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding lime or organic manure helps the plant build strong, healthy fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ tsei lɛ amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the soil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow off, keeping the roots in dry soil where they can mature safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if the soil is wet enough to plant my corn seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of moist soil from your farm into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping wet water and easily crumbles when you poke it, the soil has the perfect balance of moisture for seeds to sprout.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo ko ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni sa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and squeezing like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiimi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices. Spraying the leaves with natural neem oil water or safe insecticides removes the insects so the foliage can spread flat again.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu, adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ, loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are holes appearing in the leaves and stalks of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually made by fall armyworms or stem borers eating the crop. Checking the plant centers early and applying approved insecticides or targeted ash keeps these caterpillars from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cutworms loo stem borers ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa baa lɛ mli. Nibii ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo sũ ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I cut down extra shoots growing around the foot of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots causes them to fight for the same water and food in the soil. Removing extra shoots and leaving only one strong main stem ensures all the plant's energy goes into producing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔi babaoo haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashiɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ ni wa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear small weeds around my crop roots even when my crops are taller than the grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi bibii lɛ? mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ

english: Even small weeds steal nutrients, fertilizer, and water from the soil that your main crops need. Keeping the base of your plants clean ensures your crops get all the soil food to yield a rich harvest.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni otsei titrii lɛ taoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ shishi he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing heavy tubers underground. Training the vines up wooden stakes spreads the leaves out to catch sunlight and prevents leaf rot from wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ atsɔse wein tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaagbɛ etso lɛ efoji lɛ eshwa koni ehere hulu la lɛ atuu, ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekafite kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my tomato seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes too close forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller fruits. Giving them space allows air to circulate, which keeps leaf diseases away and helps the plants produce larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛwu amɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. He ni akɛhaa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows fast and is harvested within a few months, while cassava grows slowly underground and takes over the space after the maize is cleared, giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Beni ŋmãa lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehiɔ jɛmɛ beni ashã ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn dark green so the plant can grow big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni eha tso lɛ toii wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots during hot days helps the flowers stay on the plant and form healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs animal manure before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ashikpɔŋ ni miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia dani madu?

english: If your soil feels light, dry, or sandy and crops grew poorly last season, it lacks nutrients and organic matter. Mixing animal manure into the soil before planting improves its fertility and helps it hold onto water longer.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo, egbi loo ŋã yɔɔ mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaha ewoɔ nii babaoo, ni ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crops so it doesn't wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkaho?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist a day after a light rain, rather than right before a heavy downpour. Placing the fertilizer near the plant roots and lightly covering it with dirt prevents rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, gbi kome yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛha he fioo koni nugbɔ akafɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and look patchy yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems from the agricultural extension office keeps your farm healthy and secures a good crop.
ga: Cassava baai ni shwieɔ shi Ekɛ cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Agricultural Extension Office lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How do weeds hurt my yam crop even when the yam vines are growing very tall?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daraa waa moŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and space underground from the yam roots. Even if your yam vines look strong, weeds beneath them will cause the tubers to stay small and thin.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he kɛjɛɔ sweet potato shishifãi amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ, shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baaha bulb lɛ afee bibii ni efee mlɛo.

english: Why should I wait for the steady rains before planting my main season maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu be mli abele?

english: Planting in dry soil before steady rains begin can cause seeds to rot or sprout early and wither under the hot sun. Waiting for reliable rain ensures seeds germinate quickly and build deep, healthy roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛgbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni abaamɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa.

english: How can I keep insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni fiteɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ naa be mli ni akɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive on moisture in stored grain. Drying your maize fully under the sun until the grains are hard, and storing them in airtight sacks or clean silos, stops insects from breeding and spoiling your harvest.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Okɛ ŋmãa agbi yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni okɛto kotoku loo ŋmãa ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa ni amɛkafite onibii.

english: No, not all insects are bad. Some are beneficial insects that help pollinate cocoa flowers into pods or hunt down harmful pests that destroy your crop.
ga: Jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ ehiii. Ekomɛi ji kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ mli loo amɛtaoɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni miifite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do some insects live on my farm without damaging my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii komɛi hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfiteee mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Those insects are usually beneficial bugs. They stay on your crop to eat destructive pests or help pollinate flowers, naturally protecting your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nakai kooloi lɛ ji kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Amɛhiɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛye kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo amɛye amɛbua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination. Koni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: What helps my cocoa flowers turn into healthy pods on the tree?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Tiny beneficial insects like midges carry pollen from flower to flower. Protecting these good insects from harsh sprays is crucial for getting a rich harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii woɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi kpakpai nɛɛ ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni mli wa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he lɛ he miihia waa koni aná ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How do I make sure the spray I use on my cocoa doesn't kill the good bugs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ egbeee kooloi kpakpai?

english: Use only specific chemicals approved by agricultural officers at the correct doses, rather than harsh sprays that destroy all insects blindly.
ga: Kɛ tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ atsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni kpataaa kooloi srɔtoi fɛɛ ahiɛ lɛ baatsu nii shwilafoi.

english: How can I tell if a farm chemical with a COCOBOD mark on it is genuine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛ COCOBOD ekadi lɛ ji anɔkwale?

english: Some sellers put fake logos on unapproved chemicals. Always buy inputs from authorized distributors or verified officers to ensure the product is real and safe.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi komɛi kɛ amale kadimɔi woɔ tsofai ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ anɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ saji kɛjɛ mɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jaa nibii lɛ loo mɔ ko ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɛŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ nibii lɛ ji anɔkwale ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I check with an extension officer before buying new sprays at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ extension nitsulɔ ko agba sane dani mahe spray hee yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Extension officers know which products are officially tested and safe for cocoa, protecting you from buying fake chemicals that damage your farm.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ le nibii ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha kookoo. Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ tsofai amalei ni fiteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ hemɔ he.

english: Can applying the wrong chemical actually harm my cocoa trees instead of helping them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-cacao tsei lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: Yes, unapproved or fake chemicals can cause harsh side effects like burning leaves, damaging pods, and destroying the beneficial insects that protect your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo amalei baanyɛ ekɛ naagbai ni mli wawai tamɔ baa shãa kɛ pod fitemɔ aba. ni okpãtã kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ onibii ahe lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Is it better to use a strong chemical that destroys every single bug on my farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: No, wiping out every bug kills the beneficial insects that pollinate your flowers and eat pests, which can lead to worse pest problems later.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni agbeɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛyeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai ni ehiii fe tsutsu lɛ aba sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods dying even after I sprayed my farm with pest chemical?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miigboi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Using fake or unapproved chemicals often fails to control real pests and can cause toxic side effects that stress and damage the cocoa tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni ji amale loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diɛŋtsɛ. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ naagbai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa mɔ haoɔ ni efiteɔ cacao tso lɛ aba.

english: Why do some chemicals cause my cocoa leaves to burn and turn brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi haa mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Unapproved chemicals or improper chemical mixtures contain harsh ingredients that act like poison to the plant's leaves rather than treating pest problems safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni esaaa lɛ yɛ nibii ni mli wa ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ poison yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagba lɛ he nii shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over once they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep in the soil, making the plant top-heavy when fruit develops. Propping the main stem up with strong bamboo or wooden stakes gives the plant extra support against wind and weight.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ kɛ́ ewo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ kroko ni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ muji.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is its main food for leafy growth, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa Aloo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cowpeas in my field before I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpea yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you plant them first, they naturally fertilize the soil so the next crop, like maize, grows better.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni odu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. tamɔ ŋmãa nɔŋŋ

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess rainwater collects around the roots in heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads crack open right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ miihoso dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when they get a sudden heavy watering after a dry period. The inside of the head absorbs water and grows faster than the outer leaves can stretch, forcing the head to burst.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu babaoo mli trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. gbee yitso lɛ mli

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding on the underside of the leaf, or by a virus carried into the field by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. The plant sheds its blossoms to conserve energy and survive the harsh conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why is it important to clear tall weeds around the stakes of my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he miihia.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers underground. Tall weeds smother the vine, competing for light, water, and nutrients, which results in smaller yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Jwɛi kakadaji haa wain tsei lɛ ahe, ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa anáa ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why should I space out my watermelon seeds wide apart when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala watermelon dumɔwui amli kɛ́ midu?

english: Watermelon vines spread out wide along the ground to produce large fruits. Wide spacing ensures each plant gets enough soil space, sunlight, and nutrients without fighting neighboring vines.
ga: Watermelon wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo koni amɛwo yibii wuji. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa shikpɔŋ he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ wain tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akawu.

english: Cassava naturally sheds leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive. However, if yellowing happens with web-like spots under the leaf, it could be caused by green spider mites.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ je kpo yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, Ekolɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ hu kɛbaa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs fertilizer before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If your previous crops grew very slowly, had weak stems, or turned pale green instead of dark green, your soil is low in nutrients like nitrogen and requires fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo waa lɛ, eyɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ loo etsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow plenty of green leaves but fail to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil or heavy watering during flowering causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Small holes are usually caused by caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae feeding on the leaves. Handpicking them early or using neem-based sprays can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ daimondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Amɛ ni oooŋɔ mra Aloo okɛ tsofa ni akɛ neem fee lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, which can also spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips loo mites, ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ hu ashwã tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when the soil retains too much water without proper drainage, allowing fungi or microscopic worms called nematodes to attack the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Maize is ready for grain harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and a small black layer forms at the base of the kernels.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Afee yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, during extreme dry spells, or when the plant lacks sufficient phosphorus and water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the plants absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, and the foliage dries quickly, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Ni baai lɛ baagbi oya koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main nutrient for green growth, or when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a plant virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, creating wet conditions where soil fungus and bacteria attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch sunlight with their leaves, which helps the plant create energy to grow big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ amɛbaai lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa tsɔnei wuji ni tsii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off if the tree lacks water, if insect pests like mirids attack them, or if the soil lacks sufficient nutrients to support fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji kooloi tamɔ mirids tutua amɛ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many extra shoots steal water and food from the mother plant, which results in small plantain bunches instead of one large, healthy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii shwieɔ shi. Yɛ kuu agbo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer when the soil is completely dry during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve so root systems can drink it in; putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the crop roots and go to waste.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if I leave them growing together in the same field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Weeds actively steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops, which weakens crop growth and invites pests into the farm.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni efɔ̃ɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ nine kɛbaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do tiny insects appear in my harvested maize bags after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kotokui amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insect eggs often hide inside grains from the field. If the maize is not completely dried before bagging or kept in airtight storage, the eggs hatch into grain-eating weevils.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani awo kotoku mli loo akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli. Wɔlɔi lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from faster-growing crops like plantain or cassava to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca amli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act like natural umbrellas over young cocoa plants. This temporary shade protects the tender cocoa seedlings from scorching heat and keeps the soil damp so the young trees can survive.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo nɛɛ buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei bibii anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and produce energy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure will help the plants regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛha hewalɛ aba. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the plant and pass on a sickness called cassava mosaic disease. Removing infected plants early helps stop the insects from spreading the sickness to your healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cassava mosaic disease lɛ baa. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akagbɛ hela amɛshwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by high heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and placing dry grass around the base of the plant helps lower soil temperature and keeps flowers attached.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ he Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, damp, and shady environments. Pruning excess shade tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing away infected pods stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ kɛ diŋ pod rot baa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la abote mli ni ejie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop black spots on the bottom of the fruit as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛyibii lɛ ashishi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom end rot, happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to uneven watering. Keeping a consistent watering schedule prevents the bottom of the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ oto be ni akɛhaa aduawai lɛ daa lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why will my harvest be smaller if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots and leaves to spread out and produce bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the soil, prevents the sun from drying out the ground, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and turn yellow when there are no tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees or plantains act as natural shields, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting young leaves from drying out and burning.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shweshweeshwe shihilɛhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkashã.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but giving me small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much leafy-growth food like nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa baai lɛ daa lɛ babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Crops planted too close together fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, which leaves every plant weak and leads to a smaller harvest overall.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɔjɔɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Excess moisture and damp air allow the fungus that causes Black Pod disease to spread fast on cocoa pods, especially when sunlight and air cannot pass through overcrowded branches.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do people say burning my field before planting harms my soil in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmɔji ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ baaná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys dead leaves and good microorganisms in the dirt that naturally rot down into rich food and help the soil hold onto water during dry times.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ baai ni egboi ni nibii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ ni fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii babaoo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer on my farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so roots can drink it up; putting chemical fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots or sit unused until wind carries it away.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛta shi ni amɛfee nɔ ko. Kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa kɛya

english: Why does cutting off extra branches help my fruit trees give me larger fruits?
