ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Removing weak or unneeded branches stops the tree from wasting water and energy on them, allowing the tree to focus its strength on making bigger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ fiteee nu kɛ hewalɛ yɛ niji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your main plants, effectively starving them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land is ready and good enough before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can check your soil's condition by looking at its color, texture, and drainage. Dark, loose soil that holds a bit of moisture without becoming waterlogged usually means the land is fertile and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛtsɔ esu, bɔ ni eyɔɔ, kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni nu bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii, ni esa akɛ adu nii.

english: Why are my crops failing to grow on one part of my farm while another part produces very well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli yɛ be mli ni fã kroko lɛ woɔ yibii waa lɛ?

english: Land conditions can vary across the same farm due to differences in soil depth, nutrient levels, or water drainage. Areas that collect standing water or have hidden rocks under the surface can stunt plant growth compared to deeper, well-drained soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ hewɔ lɛ Nutrient level loo drainage sɔrɔtoi Hei ni buaa nu ni damɔ shi loo tɛi ni akɛtee shishi lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Akɛ enɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety I brought from another area will thrive on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ni mikɛjɛ he kroko kɛba lɛ baashwere yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Before planting a new crop across your whole farm, set aside a small test patch. Observing how a few plants handle your local rainfall, sunshine, and soil for a season shows you if the crop can thrive on your land.
ga: Dani obaadu tsei heei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Ha kaa wolo bibioo ko ahi odɛŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni tsei komɛi tsuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii kɛjɛɔ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from a mild sickness or if it is completely ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela mɔ miŋmɔshi nibii fioo loo efite kwraa?

english: A mild sickness usually shows as light leaf discoloration or small spots while the main stem remains firm and new shoots continue to open. If the roots are still white and firm, the plant can often recover with proper care, water, or mild treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni waaa lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ baai ni etsake fioo loo ŋmɔtɔ bibii. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ yitso lɛ kã shi shiŋŋ ni ŋmeii heei yaa nɔ amɛgbeleɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ futafuta lolo ni amɛhe wa lɛ, bei pii lɛ Tsei lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, afɔ amɛ nu, loo akwɛ amɛ blɛoo.

english: Leaf yellowing and curling are common signs of plant stress, often caused by small insect pests like whiteflies feeding on the sap, a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or prolonged dry weather.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsei ahe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to get dark spots and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya?

english: Dark spots and early leaf drop are usually signs of a fungal or bacterial leaf disease. These sicknesses tend to spread quickly during warm, rainy weather when air cannot flow easily between crowded plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, he ni edɔɔ kɛ baa ni fiteɔ mra lɛ ji fungal loo bacteria baa hela he okadi. Helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ateŋ mlɛo

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much direct sunlight and heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ babaoo tɛ̃ɛ?

english: When crops suffer from sun heat, their leaves will wilt during the middle of the day, dry out at the leaf edges, or drop their blossoms before setting fruit as a way to save water.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná dɔlɛ kɛjɛ hulu la mli lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ŋmɔlɔ ni bɔleɔ baai lɛ ahe Aloo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii bɔni afee ni nu akafite.

english: Why do my crop leaves look pale and weak after a few days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash essential soil nutrients deep below where the roots can reach. Excessive water also fills the air gaps in the soil, briefly suffocating the roots and causing the foliage to turn pale.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences environmental stress, such as sudden hot spells, inconsistent watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo, ni haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Overwatered crops will have soft, yellow leaves, soil that stays wet and smells sour, and roots that turn brown and soft instead of staying firm and white.
ga: Tsei ni nu babaoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baaná baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eŋɔɔɔ. kɛ shishifãi ni tsɔɔ blɔfo ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaashwɛ yɛŋ.

english: How long does cassava usually take before it is ready to be harvested?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Depending on the variety, cassava usually takes between 8 to 12 months (around 32 to 48 weeks) to fully mature and produce strong tubers rich in starch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 (aaafee otsii 32 kɛyashi 48) dani ekwɛɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmei babaoo yɔɔ mli. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers very small when I dig them up, even though the leaves grew well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ shwie shi lɛ? He ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Small tubers usually happen if the soil is too hard for roots to expand or lacks potassium, which causes the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves instead of roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo potassium faaa yɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe shishifãi.

english: Is cassava farming profitable enough for me to expand from a small backyard plot to a large commercial farm?
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛ cassava ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ mli lɛ ba bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ majɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ migbɛ mihe. Shia sɛɛ kɛyaa jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji amli?

english: Yes, cassava is highly profitable when scaled up because of rising market demand for food staples, gari processing, animal feed, and industrial starch.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ babaoo baanyɛ aba kɛjɛ ŋmei mli kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ kpo. Enɛ jɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni ataoɔ yɛ jarayelihe lɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ hewɔ. Gari, kooloi aniyenii kɛ nitsumɔhei ashikiŋsha nitsumɔ

english: How do I select the best cassava stems to plant for a high yield?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni adu koni aná yibii babaoo?

english: Choose clean, pest-free stems from mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old, cutting them from the thick middle section of the main stalk where the buds are strong.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ mli tso ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ, ni ofolɔ kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli tse lɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: What kind of soil do I need to make my cassava stems grow strong roots?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ he hiaa koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adara waa?

english: Cassava thrives best in loose, well-drained sandy loam soil that allows root tubers to swell easily without rotting in stagnant water.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbooo yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: What should I do if my cassava leaves start turning yellow and twisting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellow, twisted leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease spread by whiteflies; the best solution is to plant certified disease-resistant stem varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etse ehe lɛ baa. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ofee ji ni odu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds from my cassava farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeding is critical during the first 3 to 4 months after planting; once the cassava plants grow tall and form a dense canopy, their shade naturally blocks weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ he hiaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 ni adu sɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ da ni eyɛ ŋmei ni mli ewo wu lɛ, E-susuma lɛ hu baatsi jwɛi ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Can I plant other crops like maize or groundnuts between my cassava rows?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava with quick-maturing crops like maize or legumes during the first few months makes full use of your land before the cassava leaves cover the space.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani ŋmãa baa lɛ aha nɔ.

english: Can cassava survive if the dry season lasts longer than expected?
ga: Ani ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ?

english: Cassava is extremely drought-tolerant; during dry spells, it drops its leaves to conserve water and resumes growing strong as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa waa. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Ebaashwie baai lɛ koni ekɛto nu he ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba kɛ hewalɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Signs of maturity include the bottom leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the ground around the base of the stem cracking as the expanding tubers push the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ egbɔ lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ mli gbalaa beni tso lɛ mli ŋmei ni eda lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no bigger trees or plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda loo plantains bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil, which young roots need to stay alive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Esa akɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil or are getting too much water, which stops the roots from taking in nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛmiiná nu babaoo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I grow groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans put nitrogen back into the soil naturally, which enriches the land for your next crop without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: How does putting animal manure or rotted leaves around my crops help them yield more?
ga: Kooloo ŋmei loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha amɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Organic manure improves the soil so it holds rainwater better and slowly releases nutrients that keep crops strong throughout the season.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo koni nugbɔ nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes through the leaves of my young corn crops?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young crop leaves; early detection and spraying with approved pesticides or neem extract can protect your farm.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ tsei bibii ahe baai lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ ni anaa mra ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔ lɛ he

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I wait too long to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb excess water if left in wet soil past maturity, making them soft and inviting fungi or insects that cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ nine.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even after I have already applied fertilizer?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, light, and water before your crops have a chance to feed on them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kane, kɛ nu dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the soil lacks water, as extreme heat stresses the plant during flowering.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize roll up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to cut down on water loss through its leaves during intense heat, showing that the plant is thirsty.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa nu ni baa yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient. When heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil, the leaves start turning yellow from the bottom up, showing that the soil needs fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow lots of big leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi e-pods lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes bean plants to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Beans naturally capture their own nitrogen from the air, so adding strong nitrogen fertilizers makes them bushy without yielding food.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii ni niyenii bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to give me a good cocoa yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha kookoo kpakpa aba?

english: Healthy soil for cocoa is dark, soft, and crumbly, holds water without becoming soggy, and is full of earthworms and decaying leaves. Dark, spongy soil provides a continuous supply of moisture and food to cocoa tree roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo lɛ yɛ ediŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni egboi eyi mli obɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and get dark spots after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ diŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dark spots and curling leaves are signs of fungal disease encouraged by wet weather. Rain splashes disease spores from bare soil onto lower leaves; placing dry grass mulch on top of the soil stops water from splashing dirt onto the foliage.
ga: Helai diji kɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Nugbɔ shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni egbi fɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu akashwie muji nɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves have small holes chewed all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani ooye nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Small holes in cowpea leaves are caused by leaf-eating insects like beetles and caterpillars. Damaged leaves cannot catch sunlight efficiently to feed the plant, which leads to smaller harvests and fewer pods.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ hulu la jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni pods hu baa shi.

english: Maize stalks fall over when they are weakened by stem-boring insects eating the inside or when roots lack firm support. Mounding soil around the base of the stems during weeding strengthens the plant against wind and pests.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ni yeɔ amɛmli lɛ ha amɛgbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ nɔ ko ni fiɔ shi shiŋŋ. heaping dirt around Tso lɛ shishigbɛ yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe; long periods of flooding cut off air and allow rot-causing fungi to attack the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu afua ni hoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by intense hot sun, long dry spells, or extreme water changes. Dropping flowers helps the plant save energy to survive rather than spending it on growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hao amɛ. hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ loo nu tsakemɔi ni naa wa Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika yɛ aduawai akwɛmɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants take so long to produce a bunch compared to my neighbor's field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛ akɛtoɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains grow slowly when too many shoot suckers grow around the main stem, stealing water and soil nutrients. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing main bunches to mature faster.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa fiofio kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni bɔle tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baahi shi, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ adara oya.

english: Yam tubers become twisted when grown in hard, stony, or compacted soil that prevents them from growing downward. Building tall, loose soil mounds gives tubers space to expand easily into smooth, large yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, ni no haaa amɛkwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help my crops grow better than planting them directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe ni amɛduɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made of clear plastic or glass that creates a protected climate for crops. It guards plants against harsh sun, heavy rains, and pests, allowing crops to grow faster, stay healthier, and produce much higher yields.
ga: Greenhouse ji ŋwɛitsu ni akɛ plastic loo glase ni mli tse fee ni haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni buɔ he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ koolooi ni yeɔ amɛ awui ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni owo yibii babaoo babaoo

english: Why do vegetables imported from overseas often look larger and smoother than the ones I harvest from my open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni aduawai ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ dara ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe nɔ ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ ni migbele mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Imported vegetables are typically grown in controlled greenhouse environments where water, temperature, and nutrients are carefully regulated. This steady care prevents disease spots and stunted growth, resulting in larger, cleaner, and uniform crops.
ga: Aduɔ aduawai ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ hulutsoo be. Akwɛɔ nu lɛ, latsaa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ kwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ahe tsɔi kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa, amɛhe tseɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ekome.

english: Why do my tomato plants stop producing good fruits during the dry season, and how can I keep harvesting all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa nii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air during the dry season cause tomato flowers to drop off before setting fruit. Using protected structures like greenhouses keeps the air moist and cool enough for the plants to continue flowering and fruiting continuously throughout the year.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ he, tamɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do insects destroy my vegetable farm so easily when I plant on open land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ oya kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Open fields leave crops fully exposed to flying insects looking for food. Growing vegetables inside covered structures creates a physical barrier that keeps destructive pests away from your plants, reducing the need for chemical sprays.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele naa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni miitao niyenii lɛ kpeɔ kwraa. Aduawai ni ooodu yɛ tsũ ko ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akashɛ otsei lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi.

english: How does intense sunlight in Ghana affect delicate crops like sweet peppers?
ga: Te hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ saa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmeii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive heat and direct sunlight stress delicate crops, causing flower loss, leaf scorch, and small, sun-damaged fruits. Providing shade or growing them inside ventilated greenhouse structures lowers the temperature so plants can focus energy on producing healthy fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei ni nuɔ he waa lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii ni egbee shi, baai ni shãa, kɛ aduawai bibii ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ aha hulutsoo loo tsei ni akɛwo ŋwɛitsu ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do crops grown inside covered plastic structures grow and mature faster than crops in open soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ plastic ni akɛha he lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ lɛ?

english: Inside a protected house, crops enjoy balanced temperatures and direct root feeding without wasting energy surviving heavy winds, scorching heat, or pest attacks. This stress-free environment allows plants to grow and fruit much quicker.
ga: Yɛ shia ni abuɔ he lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ náa hulutsoo ni ja kɛ shishifãi niyenii tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfiteee hewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. la ni tsoɔ waa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuamɔi Shihilɛ ni haomɔ bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya kwraa.

english: How can I produce a large amount of vegetables to sell if I only have a small piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo aduawai babaoo ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ miyɔɔ?

english: Greenhouse farming allows you to plant crops closer together and train them to grow upward instead of outward. Because almost every plant survives and yields heavily in a controlled environment, you get maximum harvest from a very small footprint.
ga: Greenhouse okwaayeli haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe. ni amɛtsɔse tsei koni amɛdara babaoo moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ kponɔgbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tsei fɛɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni akudɔ amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ onine shɛɔ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ he bibioo ko ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: Why do heavy downpours cause my crop leaves to turn yellow and rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes mud containing fungal diseases onto plant leaves and keeps the foliage wet for too long, encouraging rot. Shielding crops under a greenhouse roof keeps the leaves dry and stops soil-borne diseases from spreading.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa muji ni fungal emɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ. ni baai lɛ ni oooha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa Nibii ni abuɔ he yɛ ŋtayaa shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Can I successfully grow foreign vegetable varieties in Ghana instead of relying on imported ones?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ maŋsɛɛ aduawai yɛ Ghana moŋ fe ni makɛ mihe afɔ̃ aduawai ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, foreign crops like sweet peppers, cucumbers, and cherry tomatoes can thrive locally if you recreate their ideal mild climate using greenhouses, which protect them from Ghana's extreme weather conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, kukumba, kɛ cherry tomato baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ greenhouse tsu nii ni okɛfee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli wa ni sa jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do crops grown in protected greenhouse structures need specialized drip feeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsũi ni abuɔ he lɛ amli lɛ biɔ ni aha amɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛ ko ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ?

english: Because greenhouse crops are sheltered from natural rain and natural soil water movement, they depend entirely on the farmer. Drip feeding delivers water mixed with exact plant nutrients directly to the roots, ensuring steady growth without waste.
ga: Enɛ ji akɛ, abuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni nyiɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ damɔ okwaafoi lɛ anɔ kwraa. Drip feeding kɛ nu ni akɛ tso mli niyenii efutu mli lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni fitemɔ bɛ mli.

english: Officer, if I plant rubber trees on my land, how long will it take before I can start harvesting latex from them?
ga: Ofisa Kɛji midu rɔbɔt tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mijeɔ latɛs ŋmɔshi nibii ashishi?

english: Rubber trees typically take about 6 to 7 years of growth before their trunks become thick enough to be safely tapped for latex without damaging the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛtso lɛ mli shwereɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtswa rɔbɔt lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteee tso lɛ.

english: Why do my young rubber seedlings dry up and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔbɔt tso bibioo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young rubber trees have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep groundwater, making them vulnerable to heat and intense sunlight unless they receive temporary shade and adequate watering during their early months.
ga: Rɔba tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ atswa bo oya. Ja aha amɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli.

english: Officer, why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a signal that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abɛi bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔlii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even when the leaves on top look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil is too hard or contains too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing upper leaves instead of expanding its storage roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shishifãi ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Officer, why do my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight; they need shade trees like plantains or shade timber to protect their leaves from sun damage while their roots grow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my trees turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly when there is too much wetness and poor airflow around crowded cocoa branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ ehiii. kookoo niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ

english: Officer, why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any peppers grow out of them?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, sudden dry spells, or a sudden shortage of food in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa loo niyenii ni faaa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it necessary to put tall sticks next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsei niji kakadaji woɔ sweet potatoes ahe koni amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to produce the food needed to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Officer, how can I know if my farm soil has enough moisture for planting without using expensive equipment?
ga: Te onukpai lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii ni akɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can test your soil moisture by squeezing a handful of earth from a few inches deep; if it forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping water, it is ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni oootsi kɛjɛ inchi fioo komɛi amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋmɛɔ shi ni nu shwieɔ shi lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the crops I carefully plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, aggressive roots that allow them to steal water and plant food from the soil much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa amɛjuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does rice grow better in standing water compared to crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels in their stems and roots that allow them to breathe underwater, whereas crops like maize drown because water blocks oxygen from reaching their root systems.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa shwieɔ nu mli ejaakɛ nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Do rice plants need full sunshine to make good grains, or can I plant them under big tree shade?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛdumɔwui kpakpai akwɛ̃? Aloo obaanyɛ odu yɛ tso agbo ko hɔɔ shishi.

english: Rice plants require full, direct sunlight for most of the day to produce energy and heavy grains; shade from trees will cause them to grow tall, weak, and produce empty grain heads.
ga: Omɔ tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii. Tsei ahe hulutsoo baaha amɛkwɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is good for growing valley rice in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Land suitable for lowland rice usually sits in low areas where rainwater collects naturally and has sticky clay soil that holds water for long periods without letting it drain away quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ dumɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni baanyɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa eho oya.

english: Why do my crops produce less food every year if I keep planting on the exact same land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ he kome ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, causing the soil to become tired and nutrient-poor.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant seeds too close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mikɛ he ko akafite?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and a much smaller harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds planted deep in the dirt fail to grow while seeds planted near the surface sprout quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Seeds need warmth and oxygen from the air to wake up and sprout; if planted too deep, they run out of stored energy before their green shoots can break through the soil into the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baa shi dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛbote hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen—a key food element in the soil—or that too much water around the roots is suffocating the plant and preventing it from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu yɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ Shishifãi babaoo haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa eye niyenii.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wilt quickly even when there was rain just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: On hot, sunny days, plants lose water rapidly through their leaves; if their root systems are short or damaged, they cannot pull up soil moisture fast enough to replace what was lost, leading to wilting.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji shishifã lɛ yɛ kuku loo efite lɛ, enyɛŋ ejie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto nɔ ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ebaanyɛ egbo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than the crops I intentionally planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from your crops faster than the crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya fe bɔ ni tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: If insects attack my neighbor's farm field, will those same insects move over to destroy my crops too?
ga: Kɛji kooloi bibii tutua okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ Ani nakai kooloi bibii lɛ baabote mli ni amɛfite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu?

english: Yes, crop pests move easily across nearby farms looking for more food, especially if you are growing the same type of crop as your neighbor without protective barriers or treatments.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ akutsoŋnyo ko du ni gbɛtsii nii loo tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he bɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sun exposure. They require partial shade from larger trees or plantain plants to protect them from drying out and overheating during their first two years of growth.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo dumɔwui adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips that spread down the center of maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa baa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ kpakpa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Holes and chewed edges on young corn leaves are commonly caused by pests such as the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying recommended organic or chemical sprays early prevents major crop damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ ŋshɔŋ ni ashɛreɔ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when I stick them into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ matsɔɔ ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Yes, stem orientation matters because the small buds on the stem must point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down delays leaf sprouting and causes low root yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he hiaa yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Esa akɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Cassava ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha baai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee bibioo.

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need to lift their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight. Proper staking allows the leaves to make more food, which leads to bigger, healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ wo tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaving too many young shoots, or suckers, forces them to steal water and soil nutrients from the main tree. Pruning them down to leave only two or three strong shoots helps the main plant produce larger bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛju nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo tsei babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting due to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent soil moisture and light shade during the hottest parts of the dry season helps flowers set fruit properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do dark patches and rotting leaves appear on my pepper plants during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates excess moisture on plant leaves, creating perfect conditions for fungal diseases to spread. Spacing plants further apart improves airflow so leaves dry faster after rainfall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine baa tsei ahe baai anɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Tsei ni akɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, no hewɔ lɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows field pests to build up. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass on top of the soil around their crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or straw, known as mulching, traps soil moisture during hot weather, prevents weed growth, and adds organic material to enrich the soil as the grass decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential for plants to produce green leaves and grow tall. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ afee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves curl up and turn brown during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves curl and dry out when the plant loses moisture faster than its roots can pull water from the soil. Providing shade trees like plantains or shade nets helps shelter young cocoa trees from intense direct sunlight and dry winds.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ fite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo ŋtayaai ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring regular watering and balanced feeding keeps the flowers attached so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops just once or split it into multiple applications?
ga: Ani esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli yɛ be kome mli loo aja mli awo nibii babaoo amli?

english: Splitting your fertilizer application into two or three smaller doses throughout the growing season is usually better. It prevents heavy rains from washing all the food away at once and ensures plants have continuous nutrients as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooja ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli bibii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ shikome. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ be fɛɛ be beni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: How long does it usually take to see green growth after I put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani minaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: For quick-acting chemical fertilizers, you will generally see leaves turn darker green and grow faster within one to two weeks, provided the soil has enough moisture to dissolve the nutrients.
ga: Kɛha tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii oya lɛ Bei pii lɛ obaana akɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to mix manure into the soil before planting instead of just leaving it on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu nii moŋ fe ni aaashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing manure into the soil places the nutrients deep near the root zone where plants can easily feed, while keeping the manure moist so heat and sun do not dry it out and burn off its nutrient value.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe he ni tsei baanyɛ aye nii yɛ mlɛo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la akagbi ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open due to expanding tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the right week to harvest my maize for dry grain store?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male otsi ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni akɛto ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ he?

english: Dry grain maize is ready when the husk leaves covering the cob turn completely light brown and papery, and the silk at the tip becomes dark brown and dry.
ga: Abɛi ni egbi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ŋmei ni ha ŋmei lɛ he lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee tamɔ wolo kwraa. ni siliki ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi.

english: Why should I mix beans or cowpeas with my cereal crops in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii afutu ŋmãa nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. Planting them alongside crops like maize feeds the soil naturally and helps reduce overall weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow very slowly compared to others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow unevenly if some were taken from weak parent plants or planted in shallow, hard soil. Using healthy 'maiden' suckers and planting them deep with organic compost ensures fast, uniform growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji akɛ ajie ekomɛi kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso ni egbɔjɔ mli loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni wa nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ‘gbekɛ yoo’ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii ni akɛ organic compost du amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara oya, ni amɛdara po.

english: Why is my maize struggling to grow on land where my rice is doing very well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice and maize have very different water and soil needs. Rice thrives in low-lying, wet, or flooded soil, but too much standing water suffocates maize roots, causing the corn leaves to turn yellow and stunt its growth.
ga: Omɔ kɛ ŋmãa yɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ he hiamɔ nii sɔrɔtoi kwraa. Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni efɔ loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why does my soil seem to produce good yams but my corn on the same field stays small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ? Shi mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: Yams feed deep in the soil and prefer loose ground for their tubers, while corn feeds near the surface and needs high amounts of nitrogen. Soil can have plenty of nutrients deep down for yams while being depleted of nitrogen near the surface.
ga: Sweet potatoes shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛsumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse kɛha amɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yeɔ nii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni ebiɔ nitrogen babaoo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ kɛha sweet potatoes yɛ be mli ni nitrogen lɛ faaa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: What causes my corn plants to stay very short and pale instead of growing tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee kuku ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Stunted, pale corn is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, waterlogged ground that starves roots of air, or early competition from weeds that stole the soil's food before the corn could take root.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni mli tse ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shikpɔji ni nɔ edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ loo mra be mli akaŋshii ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my corn crop perform poorly when I plant it on a plot that failed a few years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ beni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii afii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Land that failed previously often has depleted nutrients, hard compact soil, or soil-borne pests and diseases remaining from past seasons. Without adding manure or compost to restore the land, new crops will continue to struggle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ efite lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ wa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ mli. Nibii heei ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fataaa he koni ekɛha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I keep planting corn on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting corn repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients corn loves, especially nitrogen, and allows corn pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts food back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baajɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen ni ehaa ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is too tired and needs to rest before I plant yams or corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grow slowly, leaves turn yellow early, yields get smaller each harvest, or weeds like spear grass take over easily, your land is tired and needs organic matter, cover crops, or a season of rest.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ dara blɛoo lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. Yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ kpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ mli loo jwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi yeɔ nɔ oya. Ani oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii, loo hejɔɔmɔ be he miihia lɛ?

english: Why do my crops planted in low valleys grow differently from the ones planted on higher land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe nɔ ni miduɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Low valleys collect rainwater and washed-down soil nutrients, making them great for water-loving crops like rice. Higher ground drains quickly, which prevents root rot in crops like cassava and yams but can dry out maize during dry spells.
ga: Jɔɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ buaa nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ mli nu hoɔ oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mli lɛ akafite. Shi ebaanyɛ eha ŋmãa agbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn turn yellow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash key nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil beyond the reach of young roots, or waterlog the root zone so the plant cannot breathe and absorb food properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. aloo nu ko yɛ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant yams and corn on the same piece of land without them hurting each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome ni miyeee mihe awui?

english: Yes, intercropping yams and corn works well if spaced properly. Yams feed deeper in the soil while corn feeds near the surface, but you must ensure the corn doesn't shade out young yam vines before they climb their stakes.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potatoes kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ayeɔ atomo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, yɛ be mli ni ayeɔ abele yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni ŋmãa lɛ akaha ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ dani okwɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to plant rice early in the rainy season or wait until the rains become heavy?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli loo ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa baaje shishi?

english: Planting rice early allows the roots to establish so the crop can take full advantage of the heaviest rainfall during its grain-filling stage when it needs water most.
ga: Omɔ ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe fɛɛ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni awoɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni nu he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food responsible for green leaves and fast growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or NPK helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni haa amɛbaai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my sweet pepper plants stop producing fruits after the first few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper tso lɛ kpa yibiiwoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants stop fruiting when they exhaust the nutrients in the soil or experience water stress. Adding well-rotted compost or fertilizer and pruning old stems encourages the plant to grow new branches and fruit again.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo amɛna nu he haomɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he ni afolɔ niji momo lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ niji heei ni ewo yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot in flooded or heavy waterlogged soil because the excess water cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing them to suffocate and allowing fungal diseases to easily attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Amɛhaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni amɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during severe heat as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce their surface area, which slows down water loss and protects the plant from drying out.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni ebuɔ tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers if they are stressed by drought, lack adequate nutrients, or if there are not enough tiny insects like midges present to properly pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hɔmɔ ha amɛhao. Niyenii ni sa ni bɛ Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ teŋgbɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my yams grow very thin and long instead of big and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli tsɔi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow thin and long when planted in hard, unloosened soil where the tuber struggles to expand sideways, or when the soil lacks balanced nutrients like potassium.
ga: Atomɔ shwereɔ bibioo ni etsɛɔ kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli tse nɔ. Tuber ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kɛya sɛɛgbɛ. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni sa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow slowly when planted in poor soil or too close together. They require rich organic matter, adequate space, and plenty of moisture to develop quickly and yield heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa blɛoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo he miihia amɛ. he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛha shweremɔ oya kɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akui wuji.

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Removing weeds early gives your main crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: In the dry season, natural wild bushes dry up, so farm crops are often the only fresh, green food source available. Pests gather on your irrigated or surviving crops to feed and survive.
ga: Yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli mli nibii pɛ ji niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jɛɛhe. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛye nii ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are tiny black insects crawling all over the leaves of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji miiho yɛ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Those tiny black insects are aphids that suck the sweet sap out of cowpea stems and leaves, causing the leaves to dry up and leaf growth to stunt if not controlled early.
ga: ŋmeii diji bibii Nomɛi ji ŋmeii ni nuɔ wuo kɛjɛɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ baai amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni baai lɛ baaje kpo kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why do my crops suffer even when we get a lot of total rain in a season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu eyɛ mli akɛ wɔnáa nugbɔ babaoo yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Crops need water continuously throughout their growth. If all the rain falls in a few heavy storms and then stops, the land dries out and the crops cannot use that water effectively over the rest of the season.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli shii fioo komɛi ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ nu atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better for my farm to receive light rain regularly instead of one big downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nugbɔ miiho lɛ? Da yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nugbɔ ni naa wa shikome pɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Regular, well-spaced rainfall allows the soil to absorb moisture gradually so crop roots can drink steadily. A massive downpour often just runs off the hard surface of the land without soaking in where the roots need it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ ehe kpaa gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ fiofio Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu efɔɔɔ hei ni shishifãi lɛ he hiaa yɛ lɛ.

english: What does it mean when people say rainfall needs to be properly distributed for crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ aja nugbɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Proper distribution means that rain falls in steady intervals across the entire growing period. This ensures plants never go too long without water and can grow without constant drought stress.
ga: Jajemɔ ni sa tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. yɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nu bɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara ni hɔmɔ ni baa be fɛɛ be lɛ he haomɔ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops look weak even after a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpeteŋkpele ko sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: If a long dry spell came before the rainstorm, your crops may already be stressed or damaged. A single storm cannot make up for weeks of poor rain distribution.
ga: Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ba dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ lɛ Ekolɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehao loo efite. Ahum kome pɛ nyɛŋ atsu otsii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he nii.

english: How do crops react when the rainy season stops unexpectedly for a few weeks?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kpa trukaa otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Crops do not like sudden dry breaks mid-season. They respond by wilting, dropping flowers or young fruits, and slowing down their growth because they depend on reliable moisture.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ sumɔɔɔ ni egbi trukaa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ. Amɛhaa hetoo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdaraa fioo ejaakɛ ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the rain falling on my land is actually benefiting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Rain is beneficial when it soaks gently into the dirt around the roots without flooding the land or washing away topsoil, keeping the root area moist for several days.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ nugbɔ he kɛ́ ebote shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. shishifãi lɛ blɛoo ni okɛ nu efɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ Ha shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee fɛ̃i gbii babaoo.

english: Why does the timing of rainfall matter so much to my crops' growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ?

english: Crops require water at specific critical moments, such as when seeds are sprouting or flowers are forming. If rain misses these key stages, the water is much less useful to the crop's development.
ga: Tsei hia nu yɛ bei ni he hiaa waa amli, tamɔ be mli ni dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ loo amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, atsɔko gbɛi ni he hiaa nɛɛ anɔ. Nu he baahiaa kwraa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ.

english: Why do crops dislike long dry gaps between rains during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sumɔɔɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni kã nugbɔ bei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Long dry gaps cause soil moisture to vanish. When plants run out of water repeatedly, their tissues get damaged, making it hard for them to recover even when rain returns.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli egbi kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ laajeɔ. Kɛ tsei bɛ nu shii abɔ Amɛ fãji lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaná hewalɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ po.

english: How can I tell if my crops are unhappy with the weather and rain pattern this year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ miishɛɛ yɛ afi nɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he?

english: Crops show distress through yellowing leaves, stunted growth, rolled leaf edges, or failing to produce fruits properly when rainfall patterns are bad.
ga: Tso lɛ miitsɔɔ haomɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ahewɔ. Dalɛ bibioo, baai lɛ anaa, loo yibii ni sa wooo kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain sometimes do more harm than good to my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ mi tsei lɛ awui fe bɔ ni ehi lɛ?

english: Excessive rain in a short time can wash away nutrients from the soil and drown plant roots by removing air from the dirt, leaving crops struggling despite the plenty of water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni ekɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ awo nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow root systems that easily dry out in harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides temporary shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ egbiɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do tomato flowers drop off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to stress caused by intense heat, lack of water, or insufficient soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying mulch around the base helps the plant retain flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni abɔle shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to convert light into food, which expands the underground tuber. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground so leaves capture maximum sunlight while staying safe from soil rots.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni etsake la lɛ ewo niyenii mli. ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni baai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Yellowing leaves are a sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy foliage growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will restore their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni mli wa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on land where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nitrogen, leaving the ground tired. Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it back into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I place fertilizer right near the plant root instead of scattering it on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the base allows the plant's roots to absorb nutrients quickly before weeds can steal them or heavy rains wash them away.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani jwɛi lɛ juɔ amɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the hidden central part of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miitutua mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like Fall Armyworms hide in the central whorl of young maize because the leaves there are soft, tender, and nutritious. Catching them early prevents them from destroying the growing core of the plant.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai lɛ amli ejaakɛ baai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa mɔ he waa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ mli fã ni miida lɛ.

english: Weeds steal vital resources like water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell before full rains arrive. If seeds germinate during that brief wet period, the young sprouts may dry up and die during the subsequent dry weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ baa shi kwraa. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be kuku mli lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ otsii ni hulu enyɔ shi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the base of the stem develops small cracks. Digging up one test plant lets you check if the tubers are full and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baaná ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ otsa tso kome ni akɛkaa mɔ lɛ, ehaa okwɛɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ.

english: If I invest extra money to buy fertilizer for my maize field this season, will it actually increase my harvest enough to cover the cost?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ shika babaoo wo ŋmɔshi nibii ahemɔ mli kɛha mi ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Ani nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo shika he nyɔmɔ?

english: Yes, applying the right fertilizer provides key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, which can increase your overall crop yield by 30 percent or more compared to unfertilized soil, easily paying back your investment at harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus aba. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ oha mlijaa 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nɔ lɛ he. ni ekɛ shika ni ekɛwo mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba mlɛo kɛji akpa

english: Why does my cassava crop take almost a full year in the soil before I can harvest big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Cassava plants spend their first few months growing stems and leaves to capture sunlight, and only begin storing large amounts of starch in their underground roots after 8 to 12 months.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ yeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛná hulu la. ni ejeɔ shishi ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to have an extension officer test or investigate my soil before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ loo amɛkwɛ mli dani amɛje dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Testing your soil reveals which specific nutrients are missing and whether the ground is too acidic, allowing you to buy only the exact inputs your crops need to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ mli lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oheɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the plot before planting my maize?
