ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well when I let weeds fill up the space between the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miha jwɛi eyi tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your plants, choking their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ waa. tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves compete against each other for nutrients and light, leaving less energy for the plant to build big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛ la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing pollen to dry up so the flowers cannot be fertilized, leading the plant to shed its flowers to conserve water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ bɔni afee ni nu ahi amɛmli.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and transmitting viruses that disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛhaa muawai ni tsiɔ baa lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get eaten by insects so quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite loo ŋmeii miiye lɛ oya yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains stored with too much moisture attract molds and pests like weevils; thoroughly sun-drying your grain before storage stops insects from multiplying and prevents decay.
ga: Nibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ; Gbimɔ ŋmãa ŋmaa dani okɛto koni kooloi akafɔ ni amɛkafite.

english: Why should I leave space between my cocoa trees instead of planting them very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in smaller trees and fewer pods. Proper spacing also allows air to flow through the farm, which keeps the trees dry and prevents diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Cocoa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni no haa kookoo tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to shelter them, the direct sun burns their young leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while they are still growing on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, cool, and overly shady conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and trimming extra tree branches helps air and light enter the farm, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baakpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ?

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to produce more flowers than they can feed, shedding many naturally. However, if too many fall off, it usually means the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or lacks tiny beneficial insects like midges that transfer pollen between flowers.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua. ni ebaagbee shi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi, kɛji akɛ egbee shi tsɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midges ni kɛ pollen yaa fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree reduce the amount of pods I harvest?
ga: Ani mi cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: No, proper pruning actually increases your harvest. By cutting off unwanted side shoots, dead wood, and crowded branches, the tree directs its energy into producing healthy flowers and large pods instead of wasting energy on useless foliage.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛtsɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei ni egboi lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism that cocoa trees use to protect themselves when water is scarce. By shedding leaves, the tree loses less water through evaporation, allowing it to keep its root system and main stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni cacao tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛji nu bɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu fioo kɛyaa latsaa mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm needs fertilizer or if the soil has lost its strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ miigbɔjɔ?

english: If your cocoa trees grow slowly, have pale leaves, or yield small and weak pods despite receiving good rainfall, the soil is likely low on nutrients. Applying recommended fertilizers replenishes key nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to boost pod growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium lɛ aba mli ekoŋŋ. Koni eha pods lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why is it important to heap fresh cocoa beans under plantain leaves for a few days right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato kookoo yibii heei ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ plantain baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Covering wet cocoa beans under leaves creates natural heat that starts fermentation. This essential process stops the bean from germinating, releases the rich chocolate flavor, and changes the bean color from purple to deep brown.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛhaa baai ashishi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni jeɔ ŋmɔlɔ shishi lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni he hiaa nɛɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Ejieɔ tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kpo ni etsakeɔ ŋmeii lɛ su kɛjɛɔ purple kɛyaa asasu mli

english: Why is it not recommended to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava plants have very aggressive roots that absorb large amounts of soil water and nutrients, taking them away from young cocoa trees. Cassava also casts heavy shade that can smother young seedlings instead of giving them balanced light.
ga: Cassava tsei yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa waa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Ha amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ cacao tsei bibii ahe. Yucca hu haa hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha la ni sa aba.

english: How does switching from cutlasses to motorized weeders help my cocoa trees grow better?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni mitsake kɛjɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi kɛtee tsɔne ni akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ ye ebua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Motorized weeders allow you to clear aggressive weeds much faster and more thoroughly before they can steal water and fertilizer from your crops. It also saves your time and physical effort, allowing you to focus on crucial tasks like pruning and pod inspection.
ga: Motor ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ojieɔ jwɛi ni wa lɛ oya ni okɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. dani obaaju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ onibii amli Ehaa obei kɛ omɔdɛŋbɔɔ hu baa shi. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ maa nitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. Leaving some big trees or planting plantains beside them provides shade and traps soil moisture, helping the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves are usually a signal that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient it needs to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure near the base helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: What is eating small holes in the fresh leaves inside the central funnel of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by pest caterpillars like fall armyworms that hide in the growing center of the plant. Checking your field early and applying targeted controls into the plant's funnel will stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli koni okpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to lift up high mounds or ridges of soil before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil to expand and grow big, and they rot quickly if standing water collects around them. Mounds keep the soil loose for large tuber growth and let heavy rain drain away safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara. Ni shishifãi lɛ baagboi oya kɛji nu ni damɔ shi ebua amɛhe naa. Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi koni ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃. ni oha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need their leaves spread high in the air to catch sunshine to make food. Supporting the vines on tall wooden stakes gives them maximum sunlight, resulting in bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Wein tsei lɛ ni akɛfiɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small suckers growing around the main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow together, they fight with the main plant for food, water, and space, leading to small bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strong main stem and one successor, ensuring larger plantain fruits.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Ekɛ tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ he ko, ni ebaafee kui bibii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ esɛɛyelɔ kome pɛ. Enɛ baaha plantain lɛ agbo.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by a plant virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early and choosing resistant seed varieties keeps your tomato plants growing strong.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii eyɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ kudɔmɔ mra Ni dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooohala lɛ baaha o-tomato tsei lɛ adara waa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when plants cannot take up enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding wood ash or lime helps solve this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on my farm after harvesting a crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but groundnuts are legumes that naturally add nitrogen back into the dirt through their roots. Rotating these crops restores soil fertility naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my dry fertilizer on the field when the ground is completely dry and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for crop roots to absorb it, and hot, dry conditions can cause the fertilizer to burn the roots or evaporate into the air. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã shishifãi lɛ loo efo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: If I plant my local seeds now, will I be able to harvest and sell them within this same year?
ga: Kɛji midu maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui komɛi bianɛ Ani manyɛ makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ afi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Certain traditional seeds take over a year to yield fruit. If you need a harvest within the same year, you must plant short-duration or improved fast-maturing seed varieties.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui komɛi heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa nii yɛ afi kome mli lɛ Ehe miihia ni odu yɛ be kukuoo mli loo ofɔ dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya.

english: Why hasn't my crop produced any food even though I planted it earlier this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewooo niyenii ko beni midu yɛ afi nɛɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Some crop varieties naturally take longer than twelve months to complete their maturity cycle, so planting them will not yield any harvest within the first year.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsei komɛi heɔ be fe nyɔji 12 dani amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli.

english: How can I ensure that I get a harvest before the year ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ minine baashɛ mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ dani afi lɛ aba naagbee?

english: To harvest within the same year, you should select certified short-term seed varieties, such as 6-month crops, which are bred to grow and produce quickly.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa nii yɛ afi kome mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni awo he odaseyeli, tamɔ tsei ni eye nyɔji enumɔ, ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii oya.

english: What happens to my farm planning if I plant a crop variety that takes more than a year to mature?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: You will have to maintain and protect the crop across dry and wet seasons for over a year without receiving any income from that farm plot during that period.
ga: Abaabi ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni obu he yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ nɔ ni fe afi ni onine shɛɛɛ shika ko nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nakai be lɛ mli.

english: What is a 6-month crop variety, and why should I plant it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei srɔtoi ni eye nyɔji 6 ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A 6-month variety is an improved seed that matures and produces a full harvest in half a year, allowing you to harvest food and make money in the same year you plant.
ga: Nɔ ni eye nyɔji 6 lɛ ji dumɔwu ni atsake lɛ. ni baakwɛ̃ ni ebaawo yibii ni fa yɛ afi fã mli Ehaa okpaa niyenii ni onáa shika yɛ afi ni adu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise us not to plant certain traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkadu kusum dumɔwui komɛi lɛ?

english: Extension officers advise against some seeds because they take too long to yield, leaving farmers without food or income for over a year when faster options are available.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akakɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi atsu nii ejaakɛ amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ. Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, okwaafoi lɛ bɛ niyenii loo shika nɔ ni fe afi beni gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii oya lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to buy certified seeds from an extension officer or use seeds saved from my harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ extension nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ? Aloo okɛ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Buying certified seeds ensures you get predictable, fast-maturing crops like 6-month varieties, whereas saved seeds may take much longer to grow and yield less.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ haa onine shɛɔ tsei ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba lɛ anɔ, tamɔ tsei srɔtoi ni eye nyɔji enumɔ, yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ ahe be babaoo dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii fioo.

english: How do I know if the seeds I am buying will yield quickly or take a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baaje kpo oya loo ebaahe be babaoo?

english: You can ask your agricultural extension officer for the exact maturity period of the seed; they will guide you to short-duration varieties meant for quick harvesting.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ he sane. Amɛbaawo bo ŋaa yɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni heɔ be kukuoo lɛ ahe kɛha ŋmaa oya.

english: Why do some seeds mature in six months while others take more than a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi heɔ nɔ ni fe afi lɛ?

english: Agricultural researchers breed specific seed varieties to grow faster so farmers can avoid dry season risks and get a quicker return on their investment.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlipɛilɔi fɔɔ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. Bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ ajie osharai ni baa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛná shika ni amɛkɛwo mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo oya.

english: Can I plant seeds that take a long time to mature alongside fast-growing seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, but you must remember that only the fast-growing seeds will give you food to harvest within the same year, while the long-term seeds will take longer to produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okai akɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya pɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛha kpamɔ lɛ yɛ nakai afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the new top leaves, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmã lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baa hee lɛ nɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. Water droplets carry tiny fungal spores onto the pods, causing dark spots that expand quickly and destroy the beans inside.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu lɛ mli nui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni shwereɔ oya ni efiteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. The damaged leaves roll up to protect themselves from further stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Baai ni efite lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ kroko he.

english: Cassava root rot happens when the soil stays too wet for long periods, creating a breeding ground for soil fungi and bacteria that attack the roots. Poorly drained heavy clay soils trap excess water around the tubers and suffocate them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ baamɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. yitso ni efo

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperature or moisture stress occurs. If the weather gets too hot or if the soil dries out completely while flowering, the plant panics and drops its blossoms to conserve energy and water.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be hao amɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, Tsei lɛ sheɔ gbeyei ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my crops grow tall with many big leaves but fail to produce large tubers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji waa shi enyɛɛɛ ewo bulbs loo aduawai wuji lɛ?

english: This happens when plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer and not enough phosphorus or potassium. Nitrogen encourages leafy green growth, but potassium and phosphorus are needed for strong roots, heavy tubers, and healthy fruits.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛnáaa phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nitrogen haa baa eŋɔli lɛ daa. Shi potassium kɛ phosphorus he hiaa waa kɛha shishifãi ni wa, bulbs ni tsii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the top layer of soil. If the roots are weakened by soil pests like nematodes or stem borers, or if the soil is too loose, the heavy weight of a fruit bunch easily pulls the root system out during strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse tsɔ Yibii akui ni tsii lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When planted next to maize, they naturally feed the soil with nitrogen, acting like a free fertilizing partner.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Amɛkɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry spell often warms up the soil surface temporarily, but the ground below remains hot and dry. If no follow-up rain comes within a few days, the seeds germinate briefly, run out of moisture, and dry out underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ be kukuoo ko. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lolo. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, amɛbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines turn brown and dry out early before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi oya dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Premature browning of yam leaves is often caused by Yam Anthracnose, a fungal disease that attacks leaves and stems during high moisture conditions. It stops the leaves from making food, which reduces the final size of the tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ anaagbee dalɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow leaves and stems. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough for crops without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛyaaa laboratori lɛ?

english: Dark, moist soil that crumbles easily in your hand and has earthworms is usually very fertile. If wild weeds on the land naturally grow tall and dark green, it shows the soil has good nutrients for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ ni fiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ baa waa. Kɛji koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dara ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛha onibii.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when rainwater sits on my farm without flowing away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejooo foi lɛ?

english: When water collects on your farm without draining, it blocks air from reaching the roots. Root systems need oxygen from the soil to breathe, so standing water causes the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi.

english: Why should I dig small trenches or gutters around my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nubu loo nubu bibioo ko? Miŋmɔji ni miduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Digging trenches creates drainage paths that allow excess rainwater to flow off your land. This keeps the root area from becoming waterlogged and prevents soil diseases.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni atsaa lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu akabote shishifãi lɛ amli, ni helai akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Does trapped, standing water on my land cause diseases in my plants?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ hela baa mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, stagnant water that cannot flow creates a wet environment where harmful fungi and bacteria thrive, leading to fungal leaf spots and root rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi ni nyɛɛɛ atsɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa lɛ Ekɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ baa.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow during dry spells when the groundwater gets warm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ?

english: When sunlight heats up standing water or topsoil, high temperatures damage delicate roots. Warm water holds less air, making it harder for roots to drink and take up nutrients.
ga: Beni hulu la lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ hiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Can hot soil during the dry season burn the roots of my young crops?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ashishifãi?

english: Yes, direct heat from the sun bakes exposed soil, which can scorch fragile root tips. Covering the soil with organic matter like dry grass shields the soil from high temperatures.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã shikpɔŋ ni hulu lɛ eshɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ni waaa lɛ ashã. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around my crop stems protect them from extreme heat?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Placing dry leaves or straw on the ground acts like a shade cover. It keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and prevents soil moisture from overheating.
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekafee nɔ ni mli edɔ tsɔ

english: How do air and water work together inside healthy farm soil?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Good soil contains tiny spaces that hold both water and oxygen. This balance lets roots absorb water while breathing oxygen, which keeps the plant strong and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ji hei bibii. Nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni akɛtoɔ Nɛkɛ tsɔne ni akɛtoɔ he nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ nu yɛ be mli ni amɛmuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad to irrigate my crops with warm, still water from a shallow pit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli edɔ ni ekã shi ni jɛ bu ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ baafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Warm, still water lacks the dissolved oxygen that fresh rain provides. Using fresh, cooler water helps root systems stay healthy and absorb plant nutrients effectively.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ ni ekã shi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ mli. Nu kpakpa ni mli ejɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛŋɔɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crops when fresh rain does not fall for a very long time?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Without fresh rainwater to refresh the soil, groundwater dries up or gets warm, nutrient movement stops, and crops wilt because their roots cannot absorb proper food.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu kpakpa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ he ajɔ lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baagbi loo ebaadɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nyiɛmɔ kpaa. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii hu gboɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni sa.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my land instead of sinking down to the roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ taa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo kɛyashɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, packed soil prevents water from sinking in or flowing through. Loosening the soil allows water to penetrate deep down to where roots can drink it safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabote shishi loo ekatsɔ mli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ, nu lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: If my cocoa trees get diseased and have to be cut down, how long will it take for new seedlings to produce pods?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ hela mɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ ni ehe miihia ni afo lɛ hu? Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani dumɔwui heei lɛ afee ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, unlike older varieties that took up to 5 years, allowing your farm to recover faster after replanting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 5 lɛ, enɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ he waa oya yɛ dumɔ hee sɛɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to cut down and destroy cocoa trees that show signs of severe disease instead of just trimming them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni jieɔ hela he okadii ni mli wa kpo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofolɔ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus infect the whole internal system of the tree; cutting down infected trees completely is the only way to stop the virus from spreading to neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ anɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafolɔ ashwie shi lɛ pɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant temporary food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ be kukuoo mli. Ani abaanyɛ akɛfata kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside young cocoa provides vital shade to protect the seedlings from harsh sunlight while giving you food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting cocoa or if I should choose a different crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ loo esa akɛ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Cocoa thrives in deep, fertile, well-drained soils that hold moisture well; if your soil is overly rocky, sandy, or stays waterlogged for long periods, food crops like cassava or rice will perform much better.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛi, ŋã, loo nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out during the intense harmattan season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ harmatta be ni mli wa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Mulching—covering the soil around the base of your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—helps trap moisture in the ground and insulates roots from extreme heat.
ga: Mulching—ni ji shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or overwatering which prevents roots from absorbing oxygen properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest every year even though I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing crops continuously on the same plot drains nutrients from the soil; without adding organic compost, using fertilizers, or rotating crops, the soil loses its fertility over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: If bushfires or bad weather destroy my farm, how should I restore the soil before planting new crops?
ga: Kɛji koo mli la loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii kpata miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsake shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu tsei heei?

english: After clearing burnt vegetation, add organic matter like farmyard manure or compost to restore lost nutrients, and plant temporary cover crops to protect the bare soil from erosion before planting new main crops.
ga: Kɛji ajie tsei ni eshã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii titrii heei.

english: What kind of assistance can smallholder women farmers access when trying to start or restore a farm?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ yei okwaafoi bibii baanyɛ ana kɛji amɛmiitao ni amɛje ŋmɔ shishi loo amɛtswa ŋmɔ ko shi ekoŋŋ?

english: Women farmers can access support through local agricultural extension offices and cooperatives, which offer subsidized seedlings, training on modern farming techniques, and access to farm rehabilitation programs.
ga: Yei okwaafoi baanyɛ ana yelikɛbuamɔ kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ nitsumɔhei kɛ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ ekome lɛ anɔ. ni haa dumɔwui ni akɛyeɔ abuaa Tsɔsemɔ yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaai kɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa ŋmɔshi nibii asaamɔ nitsumɔi

english: Why are tree crops like cocoa so important for sustaining our families compared to short-season food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo he hiaa waa kɛha wɔwekui lɛ niyenii kɛ akɛto niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Tree crops provide a reliable, long-term source of seasonal income for decades once established, while annual food crops provide immediate short-term food security and quick cash returns.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni akɛnáa shika yɛ be mli afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛjɛ be mli ni ato shishi lɛ. yɛ be mli ni niyenii ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii ni anáa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛ shika ni anáa oya.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient corn needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kompost loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow big bushy stems but produce very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips that feed on the leaf juices underneath. Spraying neem oil or organic pest control helps get rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily in light wind, even when they don't have heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa lɛ? No bɛ hewalɛ ni tsii?

english: Underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers eat inside the base of the plantain, destroying the root structure so the plant loses its firm grip on the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers yeɔ plantains shishigbɛ. kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ nɔ Ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he dɔŋŋ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the pods and reduce the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni amɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets the yam vines off the damp ground and spreads the leaves out to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant produce food faster and grow larger tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ajie ehe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ni egbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii oya ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why is it bad to water my vegetable crops in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli nu ni akɛhaa aduawai lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Watering in hot sun causes most of the water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and water droplets left on leaves can burn the plant by acting like small magnifying glasses.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei kɛtsɔ nifeemɔ tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant before any fruit shows up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Extreme daytime heat or dry winds stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to save water instead of setting fruit.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are my groundnut shells empty inside when I harvest them, even though the green leaves looked healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔji lɛ amli efee efolo kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa po

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the top layer of the soil to fill out their pods. Without enough calcium, the outer shell grows normally, but the seed inside fails to develop.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni ekɛwo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa. Shi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ waaa.

english: Why do seeds planted right after the very first rain of the season sometimes fail to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ lɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up the ground without soaking deep into the soil. If heat returns quickly, seeds swell up, run out of moisture, and dry out before true steady rains establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji latsaa lɛ ku esɛɛ oya lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baafu, amɛhe baajɔ, ni amɛbaagbi dani nugbɔ lɛ baaya nɔ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How can I keep my crops from dying when the rains suddenly stop in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass (mulching) to trap moisture in the ground, and choose certified drought-tolerant seed varieties suited for your region.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ohala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni sa kɛha okpokpaa lɛ.

english: What kind of machine can I get to water my crops when the rainfall is not enough?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɔne esa akɛ mikɛwo mitsei lɛ amli nu kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: A small motorized water pump connected to a shallow well or river, paired with simple drip hose pipes, allows you to feed water directly to plant roots without relying solely on rainfall.
ga: Nu pɔmp bibioo ko ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛtsaa nubu loo faa ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko mli. Akɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ fata he. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu haa tɛ̃ɛ koni okɛdu shishifãi ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops still look thirsty even after a short, heavy afternoon shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kumai miiye amɛ lolo yɛ shwane mli nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa fioo po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fast heavy rains often wash over the surface and run off without soaking deep down where roots live, and hot sun right after causes the surface water to evaporate quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ oya kɛhoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ kɛyaa ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ eboteee shihilɛhe lɛ mli. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though the sun is shining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ hulu lɛ miitso moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffocating because too much water is trapped underneath without draining.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ ejaakɛ nu babaoo efo amɛshishi ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli.

english: How do I know what fertilizer my farm soil needs before I spend money buying one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani mafite shika yɛ he?

english: You can ask an extension officer to test your soil or look at past crop performance; soils missing nitrogen need organic manure or specific NPK blends tailored to that crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi extension nitsulɔ ko ni eka oshikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛ loo ekwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii eha yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Shikpɔji ni nitrogen bɛ mli lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK pɔtɛɛ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my vegetable plants flower too early and give very small fruits when the heat increases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ?

english: When crops experience extreme heat and dry air, they get stressed and hurry to produce flowers to reproduce before dying, resulting in small, poor-quality produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he lɛ, Amɛhaoɔ ni amɛyaa oya koni amɛwo fɔfɔi koni amɛfɔ dani amɛgboi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa, ni amɛhe ehiaaa tsɔ.

english: Why do my harvest yields keep dropping every year even when I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and breeds pests. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps rebuild the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will grow well on my farm before I replace my old seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ dumɔwui momoi awo najiaŋ?

english: Different seed varieties are bred for specific climates and soil types. You should consult local agricultural officers and try planting a small test patch before planting your whole field.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi. Esa akɛ oyabi maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ ni oka shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni okɛkaa okwɛ lɛ okwɛ. Dani abaadu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: How does using a tractor to plow land help my crops survive dry periods better than digging by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ traktɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baatsu nii?

english: Tractors loosen hard, compacted underground soil deep down, allowing roots to grow deeper where ground moisture stays preserved longer during dry spells.
ga: Traktɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni eshwɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow thick stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni emɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that create shade, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Too much water standing in the soil cuts off oxygen to the cassava tubers and creates conditions where soil fungi thrive, leading to root rot.
ga: Nu babaoo ni etse shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni efee shihilɛi ni baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ adara Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afite.

english: Why are there small worms eating holes in the middle of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that burrows into the growing funnel of maize plants to feed on young leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii dani ŋmãa lɛ afee.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus transmitted by whiteflies that damages the leaf cells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa ni fiteɔ baa mli wala yibii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the temperature gets too high or when there is sudden heat stress, because the plant cannot successfully pollinate or support fruit growth under extreme conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna hulutsoo be mli haomɔ trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛŋ afee pollination loo amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa waa amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil. When the heavy fruit bunch matures, the plant becomes top-heavy and easy for wind to uproot.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná ŋwɛi tsiimɔ babaoo ni ebaafee mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baajie amɛ.

english: The first rainfall of the season is often followed by a brief dry spell. Seeds planted too early will sprout but may die from heat and lack of follow-up rain.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ latsaa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce much smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, space, and nutrients in the soil, effectively stealing the food your crops need to produce big yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, he ko, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná niyenii babaoo lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a vital plant food. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea early in the plant's life helps it regain its green color and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei, tamɔ urea fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli su lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry periods to conserve water. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or permanent shade trees keeps the farm cool and protects cocoa leaves from hot winds and burning sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing loose leaves but refusing to form a tight, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ebɛ yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form heads when they receive too much nitrogen, experience high heat, or don't get consistent water. Giving them balanced fertilizer and steady watering encourages the center leaves to wrap tightly.
ga: Kaabe nyɛŋ afee yitsei kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ. nine shɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɔ loo nine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baawo baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee ekome yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying with neem oil solution or an appropriate insecticide protects new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai heei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I see small holes and fine sawdust inside the tops of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ayiteŋ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the central leaf whorl. Applying recommended treatments or a pinch of dry sand mixed with ash into the leaf center early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ loo ŋã ni egbi ni akɛ sũ efutu mli lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ko wo baai lɛ ateŋ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools around the roots without draining, creating soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to run off, keeping the tubers safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. shishifãi ni nu bɛ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Koni oyitso ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Mulching the soil with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist, helping flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii

english: Groundnut plants bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the stem grows downward into the soil where the actual peanut pod develops safely beneath the earth.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee lɛ pollination lɛ, tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu lɛ nɔ ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: How do I choose the right plantain sucker to plant so I get big bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains ni mikɛdu koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji?

english: Look for 'maiden' suckers that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves rather than broad leaves. These suckers grow faster, establish stronger roots, and produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘maiden’ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Nɛkɛ sukpɔi nɛɛ baadara oya. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi ni wa ni ofee plantain tsei wuji

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves yellow in a V-shape from the tip inward, your maize is starving for nitrogen. Heavy rains can wash this key nutrient away, leaving the plant unable to build healthy green leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, amɛfeɔ V su kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the roots under the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ato tuber lɛ mli yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant sheds the flower to protect itself.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Heat haomɔ tsiɔ fɔfɔii amli pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing very small fruits that drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa ni egbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Early pepper drop happens when the plant lacks sufficient water or essential nutrients like calcium and potassium during fruit setup, or when pest attack weakens the flowering branches.
ga: Pepper ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ potassium yɛ yibiiwoo be mli. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ

english: Why do my cabbage plants form soft, loose leaves instead of tight, hard heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ yɛ yitsei ni mli wa ni wa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages form loose heads when temperatures are too high or when watering is uneven. Constant moisture and cooler weather are needed for the inner leaves to pack tightly together.
ga: Kaabaji baafee yitsei ni etse ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ he miihia koni eha baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee ekome.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop when I clear all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle mihe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Without shade trees to filter the sun and keep the air humid, intense heat burns their sensitive leaves and dries out their roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha hulu lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã ebaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split and droop during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split and fold down during dry spells to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This natural defense mechanism helps the plant conserve water until the rains return.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the vines on my yam plants turn black and die back long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi be saŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dying early is usually caused by leaf spot diseases like anthracnose, which thrive in high humidity and spread quickly across crowded, un-staked yam fields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbele mra baa ji leaf spot helai, tamɔ anthracnose, ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds and insects grow so much faster on my farm during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi bibii daa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Abundant rain and warm air create ideal conditions for weed seeds to germinate and pest eggs to hatch rapidly, allowing them to multiply much faster than in dry weather.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jwɛi dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafɔ oya. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ oya fe shihilɛi ni mli egbi.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant the same crop on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in that field.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow starting from the tip in a V-shape, your maize is lacking nitrogen. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or poultry manure helps the plant stay green and grow strong ears.
ga: Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛyaa V su mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo kooloi ashishifãi tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛtoi lɛ hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my plot after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but leguminous crops like groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to apply chemical fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: No, fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so crop roots can drink it in. Applying dry fertilizer to bone-dry soil can scorch and burn the plant roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tamɔ wui lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot, wet ground, preventing leaf rot and encouraging the plant to grow bigger underground yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai akabote hei ni mli edɔ ni edɔ. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil evenly damp and providing light shade helps the plant hold onto flowers so fruit can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa la kpɛɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi aha hei ni agbele ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground, or mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating under the sun, and stops weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Mulching, loo mulching, tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsĩ nu naa koni ekatsɔ hulu la shishi. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to trim off small branches and water sprouts from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Ni nu ni jɛɔ kookoo tso ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak branches that waste plant energy and opens up the tree so air and sunlight can flow through, which stops black pod disease from spreading and increases crop yields.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. ni ogbele tsei lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha black pod hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: How do I choose the right part of a cassava stem to cut and plant in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select the middle portion of strong, healthy stems that are at least eight months old. Avoid the soft green top parts which dry out quickly and the very hard bottom parts which sprout slowly.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ eye nyɔji kpaanyɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse ni gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ shishi ni wa waa ni daa blɛoo lɛ he.

english: Why should I select sword suckers with narrow leaves instead of broad-leaf suckers when planting new plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala klante tsei ni baai lɛ mli etse lɛ fe nɔ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ beni miduɔ plantains heei lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have a large bulb with deep roots and strong food reserves, which helps them establish faster in the field and yield heavier fruit bunches than broad-leaf suckers.
ga: Sword shoot lɛ yɛ tuber agbo ko ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: What is eating the soft inner leaves inside the whorls of my young maize plants?
ga: Te eji tɛŋŋ akɛ ayeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ a-rings lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late in the evening reaches the worms before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkpãtã hei ni amɛdara lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Does the type of cocoa seed I buy really change how much I harvest later?
ga: Ani kookoo yibii ni miheɔ lɛ baatsake bɔ ni mikpaa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, planting high-quality crop varieties ensures faster growth, stronger resistance to diseases, and a much larger harvest compared to using low-quality or wild seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa oya. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai Ni kpamɔ lɛ da kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni baa shi loo koo mli dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: How do I know if a crop variety is good enough for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ ko hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Good crop varieties are specifically bred to give high yields, withstand local weather conditions, and fight off common crop diseases far better than traditional varieties.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ewuɔ eshiɔ tsei ahelai ni afɔɔ namɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shishijee henɔi lɛ

english: Can I plant my cocoa trees in a forest area under bigger trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ kooi amli hei yɛ tsei wuji ashishi?

english: Yes, cocoa grows very well under forest trees because the large canopy provides natural shade, protecting young crops from harsh sunlight and keeping soil moisture rich.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ tsei ashishi yɛ kooi amli ejaakɛ ŋwɛi ŋta agbo lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees seem to prefer growing in forest soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ sumɔɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Forest soil is rich in organic nutrients from fallen leaves and is naturally shaded, which creates the ideal moist and protected environment cocoa trees need to thrive.
ga: Koo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli babaoo, ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli ejɔ ni abuɔ he ni he hiaa cacao tsei koni amɛshwere lɛ baa.

english: What happens to my cocoa harvest if I do not clear weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi tsuuu nii daa?

english: If you don't tend to your farm through regular weeding and care, pests and weeds will steal vital soil nutrients from your crop, drastically reducing your yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okwɛɛɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ daa lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: What basic steps must I take on my farm to get a large cocoa yield?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná kookoo babaoo?

english: To get a big yield, you must combine good quality crop varieties with regular farm maintenance, such as weeding, pruning, and protecting the plants from pests.
ga: koni onine ashɛ yibii babaoo nɔ Ehe miihia ni okɛ tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ ni afeɔ daa, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ afata he. tsei ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe

english: Which months of the year am I supposed to harvest my cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ esa akɛ makpa kookoo?

english: In Ghana, the main cocoa harvesting period runs from September to March, which is when the majority of the pods mature and ripen.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, kookoo kpamɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ September kɛyashi Otsokrikri. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwereɔ ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce ripe pods mainly between September and March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ September kɛ March teŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow a natural flowering and fruiting cycle linked to the weather and rainfall patterns, causing the pods to fully ripen during these specific months.
ga: Cacao tsei nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo ni kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ yɔɔ tsakpaa lɛ sɛɛ. Ha kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ nyɔŋ nɛɛ mli.

english: Can I harvest cocoa pods at any time of the year?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be manyɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii?

english: While a few pods may ripen outside the main season, the bulk of your harvest will only happen during the major season from September to March.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ pods komɛi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be titri lɛ sɛɛ moŋ. Shi ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli babaoo baa yɛ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ kɛjɛɔ September kɛyashi March lɛ mli pɛ.

english: How does the time of year affect my cocoa crop's behavior?
ga: Te afi lɛ mli be lɛ saa bɔ ni miduɔ kookoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops naturally flower and produce fruit based on annual weather cycles, meaning cocoa trees concentrate their pod ripening into the major September to March window.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ daa afi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, cacao tsei lɛ feɔ amɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ September kɛ March teŋ.

english: Why are the maize stalks in one part of my field tall and dark green, but in another part of the same field they are short and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ waa lɛ? Shi nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ fã kroko hu yɛ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Soil nutrients and water are rarely spread equally across a field. Areas where topsoil has washed away or where soil is rocky lack nitrogen, causing short yellow plants, while low-lying areas with rich soil allow maize to grow tall and green.
ga: Ajaraaa shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii mli nibii lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ hei lɛ hoɔ loo nitrogen bɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa su kuku ni ji ŋmɔŋ. yɛ be mli ni hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow thick stems while others stay thin and fall over easily during windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stems stay thin and weak if plants are planted too close together or hidden under heavy shade. Proper spacing gives each plant full sunlight and soil nutrients to build strong stems that can withstand strong winds.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛtee hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni afee tsei ni mli wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: If rain delayed for weeks after I planted my corn, will adding extra fertilizer now help them catch up to normal size?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ otsii komɛi yɛ be mli ni midu ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ Ani ŋmãa kroko ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa lɛ ni eshɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer helps, but it cannot fully fix early drought damage. Lack of water early in the plant's life stunts root growth, which permanently limits how well the plant can absorb nutrients and produce yield later.
