ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua, shi enyɛŋ ekɛ nɔ ni shishijee hɔmɔ lɛ efite lɛ aku sɛɛ kwraa. Nu ni bɛ tso ko shihilɛ shishijee mli lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ naa baa shi kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my wilting crops just need water or if they are suffering from a root disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu kɛkɛ he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi lɛ loo amɛyɛ shishifãi hela?

english: If your plants droop in the hot afternoon sun but look fresh again in the cool morning, they simply need water. If they remain wilted early in the morning, their roots are likely damaged or rotting from a disease under the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ gbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi etamɔ nɔ ni ehiɛ ejɔ ehe yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, Nu hu he miihia amɛ. Kɛji amɛgboi lolo leebi Amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afite loo amɛfite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi helai amli.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates living umbrellas that protect young cocoa trees until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the line instead of giving them wide spacing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ aaabɔ he shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil, while their leaves block light from each other, leading to weak plants and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why is my pepper farm producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Consistent watering and adding manure or compost helps flowers stay on the stem and form healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some cocoa pods on my tree big and healthy while small ones beside them turn black and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa waa lɛ? Beni pod bibioo ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Small black pods can be caused by Black Pod disease or natural pod shedding, where the tree drops extra fruit it lacks energy to feed. Removing black pods immediately stops fungal spores from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ aba ji ŋmeii diji hela loo ŋmeii lɛ adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ. Tso lɛ baawo yibii babaoo fe nine kɛyashi be mli ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaahã niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii diji lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape from the leaf tip inward is a clear sign of nitrogen hunger. The plant steals nitrogen from older lower leaves to nourish new top leaves and growing ears.
ga: V-shaped yellowing ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mligbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ miiye. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei kɛ baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does water collect and stay on top of the ground in one part of my farm after rain while other parts dry quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni fãi krokomɛi hu gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Areas with heavy clay or compacted soil trap water because soil pores are too tight for water to sink in, while loose or sandy soil lets water drain away rapidly.
ga: He ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ lɛ Emɔɔ nu ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ mli etsii tsɔ ni nu nyɛŋ abote mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni etse loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides shade and traps moisture in the air, giving the young cocoa trees time to develop strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing maize leaves are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen, which crops need to make green leaves and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small worms inside the plant shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ Yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on young corn leaves and central shoots. Catching them early and using appropriate organic treatments or recommended sprays will help protect your crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni sa loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin, weak stalks with small cobs, whereas proper spacing lets each plant produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains in flat or hard soil can cause water to pool, which smothers cassava roots and stops them from breathing. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, preventing fungal root rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nu afee ekome. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ ni amɛmuɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ fungal shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for root growth. Staking also keeps the foliage away from damp soil, reducing the chance of fungal leaves diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa hela ni ŋmei kɛbaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts before maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots rot after harvest, they release natural nitrogen into the soil, feeding the next crop like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekɛ niyenii aha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your main crops full access to the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha otsei titrii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to plant my seeds right at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early lets seeds take advantage of warm soil and predictable moisture. This gives young plants a strong head start to grow deep roots before heavy storms or sudden dry spells occur later.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ lɛ he sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi waa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ dani ahum ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ baa sɛɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my rice when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ?

english: Rice seeds need consistent water at the early stages, so waiting until the main rains fully establish prevents the seeds from drying out and dying in unpredictable dry soil.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ daa yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ nɛ kwraa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekagbi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing when we get unpredictable heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ wɔna nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during heavy rain usually mean waterlogging, which drowns the roots and prevents the plant from taking up nitrogen from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ tsɔɔ nu ni hoɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can I keep my vegetables from drying up when a sudden dry spell hits during the growing season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kɛji hɔmɔ ba trukaa yɛ be mli ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or straw keeps the ground moist for longer and protects the roots from harsh heat.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he

english: Why are insects eating holes in my young cassava leaves right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii baayeɔ bu yɛ ŋmei baa mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The fresh leaves that sprout after early rains attract tender-leaf pests like grasshoppers, which need to be controlled early before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ gbalaa baabii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ni ehe hiaa ni akudɔ amɛ mra lɛ. dani ekpata tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ

english: Why does my swamp rice farm get overgrown with weeds even after I cleared the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi eyi mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ? Ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weed seeds in the soil germinate quickly in wet land, but keeping a controlled, shallow layer of water over the field smothers most weeds while helping the rice grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Shi nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ be kome mli. kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ

english: Is it better to plant my crops close together so I get more plants on my land?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ madu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small, weak plants with very low yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: Why does my soil produce good crops in the first year but weak crops in the second year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops consume nutrients from the soil as they grow, so without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot support a second harvest well.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmaakpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my harvested rice grains to break easily when I thresh them?
ga: Mɛni haa mikpamɔ ŋmaa lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ miikpa ŋmaa?

english: Rice grains break easily if they are left in the field too long to dry out completely or if they are dried too fast under direct, harsh sunlight instead of in the shade.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ kɛyashi amɛgbi kwraa. aloo kɛji egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi moŋ fe ni eeefee yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the seeds from my high-yielding maize harvest from last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni wo yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ lɛ?

english: Improved seeds lose their special strengths after one season, meaning saved seeds often produce weaker plants and much smaller cobs in the next generation.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kroko lɛ yɛ be kome sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ awoɔ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer heat stress or a sudden lack of water, which stops the plant from producing fruit to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tomato tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii ni ekɛkwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is too much sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them creates a cool protective cover that keeps the soil moist and shields the young plants until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ ni aduɔ Ehaa fɛ̃i ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the proper food it needs to make lush green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the remaining space to mature underground later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko ni eshwɛ koni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when they suffer from sudden changes in soil moisture or extreme heat stress. Keeping the soil consistently watered around the roots helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakemɔi trukaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi ni yɔɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does spreading dry cow manure on my farm help my yam crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure and retains water while slowly releasing essential nutrients, giving yam tubers soft, rich soil to expand and grow large.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio Haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my pepper seeds very close to each other in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants grow too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems and very small peppers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have small holes in them even after I clear all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ po sɛɛ.

english: Weeding removes competing plants, but insects like caterpillars feed directly on cabbage leaves. You need targeted pest control, like neem oil sprays, to stop insects from chewing the crop.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ, shi kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ kaabaji baai tɛ̃ɛ. Ohe miihia ni okɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii, tamɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Koni kooloi akaye ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my cowpea plants creep along the ground instead of growing tall like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miihoso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally spread out to cover the soil surface, which acts as a living mulch to shade the earth, lock in moisture, and suppress weed growth.
ga: Cowpeas gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in heavy soil and cannot drain away. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it better for me to move my oil palm seedlings into the field late in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mu tso dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting in the cool afternoon prevents the seedling from wilting under hot afternoon sun, allowing the roots to settle in the cool soil overnight.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and leafy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants produce smaller harvests when I plant many seeds very close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow strong and yield big fruits or cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I spread dried grass or palm leaves on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried plant material, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil too quickly, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no plantain trees or shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in full sunshine. Plantain trees grow fast and provide living umbrellas that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding air moist until the cocoa becomes strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even if the soil was damp in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. Wilting is the plant's way of curling its leaves to reduce water loss until the sun cools down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi hulu lɛ baaha amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves and center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and eats the young leaves. Early detection and applying natural remedies like wood ash or targeted spraying can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ tso mli sũ loo shwiemɔ ni akɛtoɔ mɔ ko he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cultivated crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local climate, so their seeds sprout instantly and absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to be dug up and harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and cracks start appearing on the ground around the base of the plant where the growing tubers are pushing the soil open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Eshi tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni eshwɛ Ni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ, he ni ŋmeii ni miida lɛ miitsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination by wind and bees. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not soaking wet, and avoid putting it right before a heavy downpour. Putting fertilizer in small split doses during the plant's active growth allows the roots to absorb it before rain carries it off.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi edɔɔɔ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata he yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on my farm before putting down young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to hot sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my maize seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin plants with small cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and space to grow large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the same plot where I just harvested maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. Since maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients, planting groundnuts afterwards restores fertility to your land naturally.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear all the weeds on my land before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will consume the fertilizer before your plants can reach it. Clearing the weeds first ensures your crops get all the nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛbaaye ŋmɔshi nibii dani otsei lɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or transmitting a plant virus. Spraying your plants with neem oil or an approved pesticide can clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo egbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwa tsei amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, usually from extreme heat, lack of water, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots during hot weather helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose as many leaves to sunlight as possible. The leaves use sunlight to make food, which travels down to build large, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛha hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Covering the soil with dry organic material, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating in the heat, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil directly around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when the weather gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to save water and keep the main tree alive. Providing shade or adequate water helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they can turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso titri lɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni sa ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni efeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi.

english: How does water affect how big my cocoa pods will grow?
ga: Te nu saa bɔ ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ baadara aha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water carries nutrients from the soil up into the cocoa plant. When cocoa trees get enough water during pod development, the pods grow large and healthy, but lack of water causes pods to stay small or dry up completely.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kookoo tso lɛ nɔ. Beni cacao tso lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ be mli lɛ Pod lɛ da ni ehe wa. Shi nu ni bɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii loo amɛgbi kwraa.

english: Why is my mango tree producing only leaves instead of fruits after I water it a lot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ awo mango tso nɔ nu babaoo lɛ, ewoɔ baai pɛ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Giving a mango tree too much water right before its flowering season encourages it to produce fresh green leaves instead of flowers. Mango trees actually need a short dry period to stress them into producing flowers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo omango tso lɛ nɔ fe nine dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ baawo lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Mango tso diɛŋtsɛ ni ehe miihia ni egbi be kuku koni ema fɔfɔii anɔ mi

english: How far apart should I space my mango trees so they get enough ground water?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ko yɛ mango tsei lɛ ateŋ koni shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shi.

english: Mango trees have wide root systems that spread out to find water. Spacing them about 10 meters apart ensures that their roots do not compete with each other for water and nutrients in the soil.
ga: Mango tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa nu lɛ mli. Ha amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 10 koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akashi akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why is it important to clear clear paths between my rows of cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo gbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ yɛ mi cacao tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Creating clear paths between tree rows improves airflow and allows sunlight to reach all sides of the plants. This reduces humidity that causes fungal diseases like black pod and makes farm work much easier.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni afeɔ yɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young mango trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mango tsei lɛ ateŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, you can plant short crops between young mango trees during their first few years. This makes good use of land and water, as long as the temporary crops do not grow tall enough to block sunlight from the young mango trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji yɛ mango tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ kɛ nu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ eshɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa ni baatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ mango tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ naa lɛ,.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too little water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miináa nu fioo tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves will curl, turn dull or yellow, and wilt in the afternoon sun. If the leaves do not bounce back and stand fresh by early morning, the crop is stressed and needs water immediately.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tso ko mli lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. ni egbo yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ sɛɛ efooo ni efee ehee leebi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni nu he miihia lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to pour water directly on crop leaves in the middle of a hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Water droplets sitting on leaves during intense sunlight can heat up quickly, causing burns on the leaf surface. It is best to water crops at the base near the roots early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ adɔ oya. Ekɛ shãa baa baa lɛ nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ nu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ leebi loo shwane mli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crop turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant lacks nutrients or water, it automatically shifts its remaining energy to feed the young leaves at the top. The older leaves at the bottom turn yellow and fall off because the plant is sacrificing them to survive.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu Ebaatsake hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ esa akɛ akɛ tso lɛ ashã afɔle koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my young tree saplings grow slowly even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for fast growth; plants also need healthy soil with organic nutrients. Additionally, overwatering can drown the roots by blocking oxygen, which stunts the plant's overall growth.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha dalɛ oyayaayai. Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli lɛ hu he miihia tsei. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ naa.

english: If I clear a fresh piece of land to farm, will my crops grow well immediately or does the soil need special treatment first?
ga: Kɛji mijie he hee ko ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Newly cleared land often has rich topsoil, but removing trees strips away natural cover. Crops usually grow well right away, but you need to clear deep roots and add organic matter so the soil stays fertile and retains moisture for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ sũ babaoo. Shi tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei daa jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni ojie shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to dry out faster after I clear all the trees and bushes off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya beni mijie tsei kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trees and natural bush provide shade and trap ground moisture. When you clear the land completely, direct sunlight reaches the dirt, causing water to evaporate quickly from around your crops' roots.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsei kɛ tsei bibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli.

english: Should I burn the weeds and bush after clearing my land, or will that harm my crops later?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ? Aloo no baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Burning leaves behind ash that gives crops a quick nutrient boost, but the high heat kills beneficial soil organisms and burns away organic matter, making the soil harder for crop roots to penetrate over time.
ga: Shãa shĩɔ sũ yɛ sɛɛ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds sprout so much faster than my crops right after I clear new farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie he hee ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant under the soil for years. Clearing the bush allows direct sunlight and rain to hit the ground, triggering those hardy weed seeds to germinate before your planted crops can grow leaves.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ada.

english: If I buy a much larger piece of land to expand my farm, will my crops need a different type of care?
ga: Kɛ mihe shikpɔŋ ni da kwraa koni mikɛgbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he baahia ni akwɛ amɛ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ?

english: On larger land, crops face higher risk of pest outbreaks and nutrient competition. You need proper spacing and consistent weed management, as pests and diseases spread much faster across big, continuous fields.
ga: yɛ he ko ni da nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ osharai ni fa babaoo ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa kɛ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he lɛ kpeɔ. Ohe miihia ni okɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa yɛ hei wuji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I plant my seeds very close together on my land so I can harvest more food from a small space?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko?

english: Planting crops too close together makes them fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with very small yields instead of healthy, food-bearing crops.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops like maize grow better and yield more in regions like Bono Ahafo compared to drier areas in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ kpokpai tamɔ Bono Ahafo kɛ akɛto hei ni egbi yɛ Ghana lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Crops respond to climate and soil quality. Regions like Bono Ahafo have deep, fertile soil and longer rainy seasons, which give crops a steady supply of nutrients and water throughout their growth cycle.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ahe nii. Kpokpai tamɔ Bono Ahafo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, kɛ nugbɔ bei ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu daa yɛ amɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if a new piece of land I want to buy has good soil for growing crops like cassava or plantain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ni misumɔɔ ni mahe lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abaanyɛ adu nɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Good crop soil feels crumbly, looks dark from rich organic material, and drains water easily. Cassava and plantain need deep soil where water does not pool, as standing water rots their roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ duŋ kɛjɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. kɛ nu ni hoɔ oya Cassava kɛ plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu shwieee nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What happens to food crops if I plant them at the very start of the rainy season under government initiatives like Planting for Food and Jobs?
ga: Mɛni baa niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ nɔyeli nifeemɔi tamɔ Niyenii kɛ Nitsumɔi Adumɔ shishi?

english: Planting at the first rains allows seeds to soak up moisture early, establishing strong root systems before major dry spells occur and giving them a head start over competing weeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu oya. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifã ni mli wa dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba. ni ehaa dumɔwui yeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops after I cultivate and harvest from it for several years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa yɛ be mli ni midu ni mikpa nɔ afii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every harvest removes nutrients from the soil. If you plant the same crops repeatedly without adding manure, fertilizers, or resting the land, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed new plants properly.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ, Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔɔ lɛ fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. It can also happen when too much water drowns the roots or during intense drought.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi loo yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: This is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally shed young pods when they get stressed by sudden dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or pest attacks, because the tree is trying to save its strength.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuamɔ Enɛ ji akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when I water them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a soil disease called bacterial wilt. Microscopic germs enter the stem from the soil and block the plant's internal water tubes, so water cannot travel from the roots up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ bacteria wilt lɛ kɛbaa. Helai ni gbeɔ mɔ bibioo lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, nu nyɛɛɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and wrinkle when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat, or because tiny insects like thrips and aphids are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite babaoo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ aphids kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain stays in the soil without draining away, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to grow fast.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ daa oya.

english: Beans and groundnuts are part of the legume family. They have special tiny organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen fertilizer directly from the air and store it in the soil for future crops to feed on.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛji bɔɔ nii bibii. Nɔ krɛdɛɛ lɛ damɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni okɛto shikpɔŋ koni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii aye.

english: Why do my crops grow much greener and taller near the place where my goats sleep?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛkwɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ he ni mitooi lɛ wɔɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure contains rich nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus from the food they eat. When droppings mix with the soil, they act as powerful natural fertilizer that feeds the crops.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus, jɛɔ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ mli yɛ kooloi ashishifã mli. Kɛ kooloi ashishifã kɛ shikpɔŋ futu Amɛbaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil where leaves can easily rot or get shaded by weeds.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baanyɛ agbo oya loo jwɛi baaha amɛ shade.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in harsh conditions. Their seeds wake up instantly after rain and their roots grow very fast to grab water and plant food before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Ni eshishifãi lɛ daa oya waa koni amɛjie nu ni amɛdu niyenii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abashɛ.

english: Yes, planting fast-growing food crops alongside young cocoa provides necessary shade to protect seedlings from strong sunlight while giving you food and income before the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ oya yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ baaha aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani cacao tsei lɛ daa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take several years before they start giving me fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to establish strong root systems and sturdy branches to support heavy cocoa pods, which usually takes 3 to 5 years depending on the variety.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa ni baaye abua cacao tsei ni tsii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa.

english: Is it safe to spray the same chemical on my food crops that I use on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baashwie niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, chemicals are formulated for specific crops and pests. Using cocoa chemicals on food crops can be toxic and unsafe for consumption.
ga: Dabi, afee tsofai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Cocoa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ehiii kɛha niyeli.

english: How do I know if my crops need chemical fertilizer to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops have pale or yellow leaves, grow very slowly, or produce small fruits, it usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients that targeted fertilizer can restore.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aku sɛɛ aha lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches and shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so air and sunlight can reach all parts of the tree, which lowers disease risk and helps the tree send energy directly to growing pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa helai baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees very close together to get more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mafee tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trees planted too closely compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak trees, higher risk of disease spread, and fewer cocoa pods overall.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Oshara babaoo yɛ ni helai baagbɛ ashwã. kɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo pɛ yɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, space, and sunlight from your crops, which weakens your plants even if water is sufficient.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, ŋwɛi, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Clearing weeds and removing infected pods helps keep the air dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do so many small flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but naturally drop most of them because the tree can only support a limited number of pods based on its strength and available water.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi bɔ ni eji lɛ, amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi anɔ yɛ ehewalɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: Dropping leaves during hot, dry weather is a natural self-defense mechanism for the tree to conserve water and survive drought.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Nitrogen is like food that helps plants build green leaves, so when it is lacking in the soil, the leaves fade and growth slows down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Nitrogen tamɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ebɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ gboɔ ni amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leaves above the ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or cassava plants are spaced too closely together, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall green leaves to reach sunlight instead of storing food below ground in big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ŋmei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛná hulu la. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ niye ní toɔ zugba sisi ngɛ ngmɔkɔ nguahi a mi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in an open field with full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle strong direct heat. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to keep them cool and preserve soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up on instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to prevent diseases and allows the leaves to trap solar energy, which feeds the tuber growing under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hela akabote mli. Ni ehaa baai lɛ toɔ hulu hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds fail to come up out of the soil even after I pour plenty of water on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli waa moŋ?

english: Seeds need air just as much as water to wake up and grow. Planting seeds too deep in the dirt or flooding them with water suffocates them from lack of oxygen, causing them to rot before they can sprout.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo he miihia dumɔwui tamɔ bɔ ni ehe hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu ni akɛteɔ shi ni ekwɛɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo ni akɛ nu woɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when they lack consistent water. Extreme heat stresses the plant, making it drop flowers to protect itself rather than spending energy making fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Gbalamɔ fɔfɔii ni okɛbu ohe Yɛ hewalɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii ni okɛfee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why are the leaves at the top of my pepper plant curling up and stopping the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Curled top leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaf, or a virus they spread. They drain the plant's juices, causing new leaves to grow twisted and stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋwɛi baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Amɛjieɔ aduawai amli nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baa heei ni efite ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and bigger than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native to the land and naturally adapted to take up water and soil nutrients very quickly. Because they grow faster, they will steal light and food from your young crops unless you clear them early.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya. Amɛbaaju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Ja otsi mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to produce fruit when I leave many suckers growing around one mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɛ tso kome he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain tree, they act like too many children sharing one small meal. Cutting away extra suckers leaves all the soil nutrients for one main stem to grow fast and produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii babaoo ni miija niyenii bibioo ko. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ jeɔ kpo koni tso titri kome adara oya ni efee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why does my okro plant drop its small green pods before they grow into big okro?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Green dani eda ni etsɔ okra agbo?

english: Okro plants drop young pods when the soil runs out of water during flowering or when tiny fruit borer insects damage the young pods. Giving the plant enough moisture and checking for pests helps the pods grow to full size.
ga: Okro tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu faaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ aduawai lɛ fite ŋmeii bibii lɛ, tso lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akwɛɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛdalɛ he.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting at the lower leaves, it usually means the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives leaves their deep green color and helps plants grow tall.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize make the soil richer for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans belong to a family of crops called legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting like a natural fertilizer for crops planted beside or after them.
ga: Beans fata ŋmãa weku ni ale lɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ he. Emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni adu yɛ emasɛi loo esɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and easily dry out. Leaving tall shade trees provides cover and protects young cocoa from sun damage while keeping moisture in the air.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ aha kookoo bibii ahe ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, hulutsoo ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mlihiɛmɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and tiny fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is scarce, pepper plants drop flowers and young fruits to conserve energy and survive the harsh weather.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu faaa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii bibii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains last for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Standing water fills all the small air pockets in the earth, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal diseases to cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and straight only when the soil is soft and deeply tilled; hard, compacted soil or underground rocks block the tubers and force them to grow twisted.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛfite.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by small pests like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by intense heat causing the leaf to roll up to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite lɛ mli

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily right before the bunches are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by tiny soil worms called nematodes or stem borers, leaving the heavy tree without strong anchors against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ. Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni tsii lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but fail to form pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen between flowers; without these insects or proper moisture, flowers simply drop off without turning into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ No lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted to be extremely tough, allowing them to suck up water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhe wa waa. Enɛ haa amɛnáa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Fast-growing shade crops like plantains act as living umbrellas, protecting the tender cocoa leaves from scorching during the hot dry season while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots fight underground for water, nutrients, and space. This competition results in thin, woody tubers instead of large, heavy cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii agboi ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. When temperatures get too high or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight, which powers the growth of the tubers underground. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi fungal helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil, feeding the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and twisting into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on tender young leaves and pass a virus to the plant. The sucking action damages the leaf tissue, causing it to distort and curl.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni yeɔ baai bibii ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ nɔ Suction haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ sɛɛkuu kɛ ŋmɔlɔ aba.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring you get large, full bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Ejuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha oná plantains ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot, dry spell before the real rainy season starts. If seeds germinate in wet soil and the ground suddenly bakes under dry heat, the young sprouts die and rot underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa kɛ la ni mli egbi. Tso bibioo lɛ baagbo ni ebaagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into mounds or ridges before planting sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ lɛ naa kɛfee gɔji loo ŋmeii dani madu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need soft, loose soil to push outward and expand into thick tubers. Building raised mounds loosens hard earth and prevents water from pooling around the roots, keeping them from rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekɛtsi kɛya kponɔgbɛ ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa nu abua naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa amɛfite.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide large leaves that create shade, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops too close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak plants with small yields instead of strong plants with big harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Flowers often drop off when the weather is extremely hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or if small pests attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo, kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stems at a slant or straight down in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo madu yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree slant makes it much easier to harvest the tubers later because they form closer to the surface, whereas planting them straight down makes the tubers grow deep and hard to dig up.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45-degree lɛ, ebaaha sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmei lɛ akpamɔ afee mlɛo kwraa ejaakɛ amɛbaabɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. be mli ni aduɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shɔŋŋ ni ewa akɛ abaafo.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food for building large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaf decay and increasing yields.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my garden vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the intense heat. It keeps the roots cool, conserves water, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ehaaa nu ahi shi, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Rotating them restores soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young crops have short roots and can easily be overwhelmed by aggressive weeds that steal their light, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds early gives young plants a strong start before they get choked out.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni juɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye nɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani amɛfo.

english: Why should I pinch off some of the small side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? yɛ tomato tso lɛ nɔ

english: Removing small side shoots, or suckers, forces the tomato plant to direct its water and food into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni ooojie lɛ nɔ lɛ, onyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under intense sunlight and dry Harmattan winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil, protecting the seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii ewo mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.
