Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛŋmɛɔ hulu la naa.

english: Why should I remove some of the young suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a plantain tree, they compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to small bunches. Pruning back excess suckers so that only two or three strong ones remain ensures the main stalk gets enough food to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee panicles agboi ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to build green leaves, so when soil nutrients run low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth, signaling that it is time to add fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ ashishi ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he.

english: What is eating ragged holes into my young corn leaves and leaving green dirt inside the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ muji eŋɔli yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel (whorl) of the young corn plant during the day. Treating the central funnel early with safe insecticidal soaps, neem extract, or approved pesticides kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi, neem mli nu, loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi bibii lɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ naa.

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the node buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If stems are planted upside down, the roots and shoots will struggle to grow in the wrong directions, causing delayed sprouting, weak stems, and significantly lower tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji lɛ esa akɛ odu amɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu tso lɛ shishi lɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the blossoms drop off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly during hot weather prevents the plants from dropping their flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ nu shwie nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akafɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi.

english: Curled and wrinkled pepper leaves are caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips that feed on leaf sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these pests early using neem oil sprays or insecticidal soap helps young leaves open up normally and keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni baai bibii lɛ agbele amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant peppers or garden eggs on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ abaadu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting crops from the same plant family on the same plot repeatedly allows specific soil diseases and pests to build up in high numbers in the ground. Rotating peppers with legumes like cowpeas breaks the disease cycle and naturally restores fertility to the soil.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ tsei akuu kome mli lɛ ni aaadu shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Ebaaha helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni kooloi bibii komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peppers ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry animal manure or poultry dung on my land make my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi loo kooloi ŋmeii ni mikɛshwãa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure like a sponge, helping sandy or hard soils hold onto water during dry periods while slowly releasing essential plant nutrients into the roots over time.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Ejieɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow poorly even if I applied fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and will aggressively steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's growth stage ensures your crops get all the food and water they need to yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe shia tsei. Ni ejuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, sũ mli nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ be mli lɛ, ekwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my maize crop fail to produce full cobs when there is a short dry spell in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Maize needs a steady supply of water, especially during the flowering stage when the cobs are forming. If a dry spell hits at that critical time, the plant gets stressed and cannot pollinate properly, leaving you with empty spaces on the cob.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa daa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli, beni ŋmeii jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba yɛ be ni he hiaa waa mli lɛ Tso lɛ haoɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onáa gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do farmers in hot, dry countries manage to harvest good corn while my crops suffer during dry periods here in Ghana?
ga: Te okwaafoi ni yɔɔ maji ni mli edɔ ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkwɛɔ ŋmãa kpakpa nɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ hɔmɔ ni yeɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Farmers in dry regions use drought-tolerant crop seeds and water-saving methods like drip irrigation and mulching, which keep the plant roots hydrated even when rain is scarce.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa kɛ gbɛi ni akɛbuɔ nu he tamɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How can I keep my soil moist for my crops even when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa po?

english: You can cover the soil around your crop roots with dry grass, leaves, or crop stalks—a practice called mulching. This acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tso shishifãi, nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ko ni tsiɔ nu ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are market women buying imported farm produce instead of buying what we harvest here in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei hɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni wɔkpaa yɛ Ghana biɛ lɛ?

english: Market women often buy imported goods because foreign farms sometimes produce cleaner, standard-sized crops in consistent quantities due to modern storage and processing facilities.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yei ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ heɔ nibii ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei komɛi lɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔji woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse ni dalɛ ji nɔ ni sa lɛ babaoo be fɛɛ be. Yɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kɛ nitsumɔ hewɔ lɛ

english: What crops can I grow on my land to replace the expensive imported food sold in our local markets?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛto niyenii ni jara wa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ wɔmaŋ jarayelihe lɛ najiaŋ?

english: You can grow high-demand staples like maize, rice, onions, and tomatoes. Using certified seeds and proper land care allows local Ghanaian soils to produce yields just as good as imported crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tomato. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa Ghana maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Does weather in far away countries affect how well my crops grow or sell here in Ghana?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ maŋ ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ saa bɔ ni miduɔ loo mihɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana lɛ he?

english: While weather overseas does not change how your crops physically grow, droughts in other countries reduce global food supplies, making your local crops more valuable and higher in demand in the market.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ po tsakeŋ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ. Shi hɔmɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ eha niyenii ni anaa yɛ jeŋ fɛɛ lɛ eba shi. Ha tsei ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa ni mɛi sumɔɔ waa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Can Ghanaian soil naturally support crops that we usually assume can only be grown overseas?
ga: Ani Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni bei pii lɛ wɔsusuɔ akɛ maŋsɛɛ pɛ abaanyɛ adu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Yes, Ghana has diverse soils and climate zones that can support crops like onions, Irish potatoes, and specific grains, provided you select the right seed variety and plant in suitable regions.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ghana yɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, Irish ŋmei. kɛ ŋmaa pɔtɛɛi Kɛji ohala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa ni odu yɛ kpokpaa ni sa nɔ.

english: If I take a high-interest loan to farm, which fast-growing crops will help me harvest and pay back quickly?
ga: Kɛji ofã shika ni nyɔmɔwoo babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya baaha awo nyɔmɔ oya kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ?

english: Short-cycle crops like leafy vegetables, okra, pepper, or early-maturing maize varieties allow you to harvest within two to three months, giving you quick sales to repay debt.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai, okra, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ oya koni owo nyɔmɔ.

english: Why do some corn fields produce big yields while my field yields very little even though we plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ? ni wɔfeɔ ekome kɛduɔ?

english: Differences in crop yield depend heavily on seed quality, proper soil feeding, and planting distance. Using improved high-yielding seeds and applying organic or mineral fertilizers at the right times gives crops maximum strength to produce heavy yields.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ damɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛ ni sa, dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I make my harvested corn last longer without spoiling so I can sell it when prices rise?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee koni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ kɛji ejara tee hiɛ?

english: You must thoroughly dry your corn until the kernels are hard before storing them in sealed, airtight storage bags (hermetic bags). This keeps moisture, mold, and destructive grain beetles away from your harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbi o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ mli. (Vacuum bags) Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ okpamɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same plot with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ mikoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which crops need for leaf growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away, so adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen lɛ shwiemɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil so quickly if I leave them out for just two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni akpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled from the ground, its tissues react to air and begin a rapid natural decay process. Cassava stays fresh longest while left unharvested in the ground, so it is best to pull up only what you can sell or process immediately.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajieɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ efãji lɛ hereɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛjeɔ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ shishi oya. Cassava hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe fɛɛ kɛ́ akpaaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ obaajie nɔ pɛ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo otsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the earth, while legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. Rotating them naturally restores soil fertility for your next main crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to make raised soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand into large tubers. Raising the soil into mounds gives the roots room to push downward easily and prevents water from pooling around the roots, which causes the tubers to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ owó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔ gɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo aha shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaatsi amɛhe kɛya shi. ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: What causes small holes to appear in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the center of the plant and eat the soft leaves. Detecting them early allows you to use neem extracts or recommended sprays before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa bibii lɛ amli. mra be mli ni anaa Enɛ baaha okɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo spray ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together to get more yield from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stems and full fruits, resulting in a bigger total harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ aduawai ni eyi obɔ baakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away some branches from my mature cocoa tree when it looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji ni eda lɛ amli be mli ni tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive branches so the tree can send its energy directly into growing cocoa pods. It also allows sunlight and breeze to pass through the tree, which prevents fungal diseases like Black Pod from spreading.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ akudɔ hewalɛ kɛya kookoo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually reduce my final harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te fee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ ba shi?

english: Weeds act as thieves in the farm by stealing light, water, and fertilizer away from your main plants. When crops don't get enough of these essentials, they grow smaller and produce fewer grains or roots.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, Ebaafee bibioo ni ebaawo dumɔwui loo shishifãi fioo.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant them immediately after a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Extremely wet, waterlogged soil loses the air bubbles that seeds need to breathe. Without air, seeds suffocate and rot in the ground before they get a chance to sprout, so it is better to wait until excess water drains off.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ laajeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛmu lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaho.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings die inside my nursery shade when the afternoon sun gets too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ miigboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni shwane hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heat gets trapped inside a shade structure without good airflow, the temperature rises rapidly and cooks delicate roots and leaves. Good ventilation lets hot air escape and keeps the environment cool enough for seedlings to survive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ emɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ oya ni ehooɔ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil and get moldy inside my storage bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ efite ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested grains still release moisture. If there is no air movement to carry away trapped heat and dampness, mold and fungi grow quickly, causing the grains to rot inside the bag.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni tsiɔ ehe koni ejie dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ, Mold kɛ mildew daa oya ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave enough space between my tomato plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: Leaving space allows breeze to flow between plants, which reduces heat and moisture buildup that causes fungal diseases, while ensuring each plant gets enough air and light.
ga: He ko ni ashiɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce smaller tubers when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ bulbs bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight throughout the day to produce energy through its leaves and store it in root tubers. Big trees block sunlight, causing the plant to grow tall and thin without forming large roots.
ga: Hulu la he miihia cassava tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa Ehaa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miitswa be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense full sun. Temporary shade crops like plantains protect delicate cocoa leaves from extreme heat and sunlight until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa

english: Why do tomato leaves curl and wilt during the hottest part of the day even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up from the soil. Curling leaves is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from excessive sun exposure.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why should I sort my harvested yams by size before taking them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdalɛ ji lɛ naa dani mikɛwo jara nɔ?

english: Sorting yams by size prevents large, heavy tubers from crushing smaller ones during transport, reduces spoilage, and helps you sell uniform batches to buyers for better prices.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni ajara mli yɛ amɛdalɛ naa lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ beni amɛkɛ amɛ yaa he kroko lɛ. Ha nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni eye ebua bo ni okɛ batch ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to spread out my cocoa beans on raised mats to dry instead of keeping them in a thick heap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋtayaa ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ koni egbi moŋ fe ni mabua amɛnaa yɛ ŋtayaa ni mli wa mli lɛ?

english: Spreading cocoa beans in a thin layer allows fresh air to circulate around them so sun heat can dry them evenly, preventing mold and bitter flavor buildup.
ga: Okɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii bibii amli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɔleɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe, no hewɔ lɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops stop growing when weeds take over my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ beni jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. When weeds surround your crops, they steal the food plants need to grow and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it important to sort and transplant nursery seedlings of the same size together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ ni adu amɛ ekomekomei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seedlings of equal size together ensures bigger plants do not shade out smaller ones, allowing all crops in the field to get equal sunlight, air, and soil nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tso agbo lɛ shwieee tso bibioo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the tip downward in a V-shape, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient that keeps leaves green and helps maize produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi kɛbatsɔ V su Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that scorch easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cooler environment and holds soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow mature and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ehe waa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small ears when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to stretch upwards to reach sunlight instead of putting energy into developing big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push against the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I leave dry leaves and crop leftovers on top of my soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Covering the soil with plant waste creates a protective layer that traps ground moisture during sunny days, keeps the roots cool, and gradually breaks down into natural plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Excess rain and cool moisture allow a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread quickly between trees. Cutting overgrown branches lets air and light into the farm to dry out the trees and prevent the mold from growing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsei ateŋ. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha tsei lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes turn black and rot before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, which happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is forming rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo amɛnáa nu ni ejaaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee oya lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to stress, such as intense midday heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaf growth rather than fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni amɛbaawo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow forces the main plantain tree to share its nutrients and water, leading to smaller bunches. Removing extra shoots ensures all energy goes into making a large bunch on the main stem.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaanyɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ aha. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ feɔ bibii. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground where leaves could rot, giving them maximum sunlight to produce bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni baai lɛ baanyɛ agbo yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ he babaoo koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: I have a very small plot of land, so how can I increase my harvest without buying more land?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni miheee shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: You can practice integrated farming by combining different activities on the same plot—such as growing crops, raising small farm animals, and keeping fish. This allows you to use your limited space efficiently as the waste from one activity helps feed or fertilize another.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ nifeemɔi srɔtoi ni okɛaafee ekome lɛ nɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ kɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli kɛ loo ŋmɔ mli Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ he ni faaa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi ni jɛɔ nitsumɔ kome mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii haa nitsumɔi krokomɛi.

english: What does integrated farming mean, and why are extension officers recommending it to us?
ga: Mɛni ji okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome lɛ shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ jieɔ wɔyi lɛ?

english: Integrated farming means running crops, livestock, and fish farming together on one piece of land. Officers recommend it because it reduces your spending on fertilizer and animal feed, protects you from total loss if one crop fails, and brings in income throughout the whole year.
ga: Okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi kɛ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Amralofoi lɛ woɔ enɛ he ŋaa ejaakɛ ebaaye ebua ni shika ni afiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi aniyenii ahe lɛ aba shi. Tsi nibii ni laajeɔ lɛ anaa kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite. ni ekɛ shika aba yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: If my land size is limited, what fast-yielding farm activities can I add to get extra income quickly?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ faaa Mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni woɔ yibii oya manyɛ mikɛfata he koni maná shika kroko oya?

english: Adding activities like mushroom growing, poultry keeping, or small fish ponds takes up very little land space and yields products faster than traditional food crops, giving you quick income while you wait for seasonal harvests.
ga: Nitsumɔi tamɔ ŋmeii akwɛmɔ kɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ ni yaa hiɛ. Aloo loo ŋshɔ bibioo ko heɔ he ko fioo pɛ ni ewoɔ yibii oya fe blema niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa shika oya yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ.

english: Can I grow mushrooms on my farm, and do they need a large piece of land like maize or cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni ani he ko ni da he miihia ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: No, mushrooms do not require large farm fields or regular soil. They grow indoors or inside simple shaded structures on bags filled with sawdust or farm waste, making them ideal if you have very little land.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii biɔ ŋmɔji wuji loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shia mli loo yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kotokui ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmɔ mli jwɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko pɛ oyɔɔ.

english: Why are agricultural extension officers encouraging smallholder farmers to try mushroom farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi bibii hewalɛ koni amɛka ŋmeii akwɛmɔ amɛkwɛ lɛ?

english: Extension officers encourage mushroom farming because mushrooms grow very quickly, sell for good prices in local Ghanaian markets, and use agricultural waste like corn cobs or sawdust instead of expensive inputs.
ga: Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii akwɛmɔ he hewalɛ ejaakɛ ŋmeii daa oya waa. Akɛ jara kpakpa hɔ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. ni akɛ okwaayeli mli jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atswa lɛ atsu nii. yɛ nibii ni akɛfeɔ nibii ni jara wa lɛ najiaŋ

english: How can keeping pigs on my farm help my food crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsinai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pigs produce large amounts of manure, which is rich in organic nutrients. When you collect and compost pig dung and apply it to your crop field, it improves soil fertility and crop growth without needing expensive synthetic fertilizers.
ga: Kplotooi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli. Beni obua tsina ŋmɔshi nibii anaa ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: If I keep chickens or poultry near my vegetable crops, will they help or harm my farm?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ kooloi loo kooloi to mi aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ Ani amɛbaaye amɛbua loo amɛbaaye miŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: If you keep poultry in enclosed coops or beds, you can collect their droppings safely. Poultry manure is very high in nitrogen, which makes leaf crops grow green and healthy when properly applied to the soil.
ga: Kɛji okɛ kooloi to kooloi atsu loo saatso ni agbe naa lɛ mli Obaanyɛ okɛ o-droppings lɛ ato shweshweeshwe. Nitrogen babaoo yɛ kooloi ashishifã mli waa. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I use waste from my food crops to feed my farm animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ niyenii ni efite lɛ aha ŋmɔ mli kooloi niyenii?

english: Leftover crop parts like cassava peels, maize stalks, and bean husks can be processed and fed to pigs or small livestock, saving you money on commercial animal feed.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa, ŋmãa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa he nii ni akɛha tsinai loo kooloi bibii. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli niyenii he nyɔmɔwoo mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it possible for me to start fish farming on the same small land where I grow crops?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mabɔi lookwɛmɔ yɛ he bibioo ko? Nɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ mi dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, you can dig small earthen ponds or set up tarpaulin fish tanks on a small area of your farm. Fish farming does not take up much room and can be easily fitted alongside crop fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsa shikpɔŋ nɔ nubu bibioo ko loo oto ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛ tarpaulin fee lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ he ko bibioo. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli Loo ŋmɔ lɛ heee he ko babaoo ni abaanyɛ akɛwo ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko masɛi mlɛo.

english: Why is water from a fish pond beneficial for watering my food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ loo nubu mli nu lɛ he hiaa kɛha mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu lɛ?

english: Water from fish ponds contains natural fish waste and organic matter, making it rich in natural fertilizers. Using this water to irrigate your crops provides both moisture and extra plant food at the same time.
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ loo ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ loo mli jwɛi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni no haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu nɛɛ tsu nii ni okɛshwie onibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii krokomɛi yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why is my soil requiring expensive chemical sprays before planting nowadays when my father never used them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni jara wa afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu kɛji akɛ Ataa kɛtsuuu nii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Over many years of continuous farming, natural soil nutrients wash away and stubborn weed seeds accumulate in the soil. Chemical sprays clear these aggressive weeds quickly, but you can also restore your land naturally by leaving it to fallow, planting cover crops, or applying organic compost.
ga: Okwaayeli tee nɔ afii babaoo. Akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni jwɛi dumɔwui ni wa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɛɛ anɔ lɛ gbeɔ oya. Shi obaanyɛ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa hu kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni oooshi lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ adumɔ loo akɛ organic compost atsu nii

english: What cheap natural alternatives can I use on my farm if I cannot afford chemical weed killers before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii krokomɛi ni jara waaa, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii krokomɛi manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi dani aduɔ nii hu?

english: You can plant cover crops like mucuna or cowpea during the off-season. They cover the ground like a carpet to choke out stubborn weeds while adding free nitrogen back into your soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ mucilagina loo cowpeas yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛɛɛ lɛ. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti koni amɛgbe jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ amɛwoɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid planting the same crop on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients every year and lets crop-specific pests build up in the ground. Alternating with legumes like beans or peanuts refreshes the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eha tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than the maize I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tougher and better at stealing light, water, and soil nutrients than farm crops. Clearing them early in the first three weeks gives your young maize the advantage it needs to grow tall and shade out new weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ baaha obi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ akɛ ebaada ni ekwɛ jwɛi heei anɔ.

english: Why do my young crops turn pale yellow when I do not apply chemical fertilizer early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mikɛwooo amɛmli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow green leaves. If soil lacks natural organic matter, crops struggle early on unless fed with compost, manure, or early fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji nitrogen bolɔmɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ mra. ja amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii oya

english: How do pests keep multiplying on my farm even when I buy expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mihe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ ni jara wa po?

english: Using the same chemical repeatedly can make pests resistant to it, meaning it stops working over time. Mixing up your control methods by burning infected plant waste, clearing field borders, and rotating crops keeps pest populations low naturally.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ Baanyɛ aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anyɛ atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai lɛ baakpa nitsumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ gbɛi ni otsɔɔ nɔ okudɔɔ nii lɛ afata he kɛtsɔ tsei ahe jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oooshã lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa ni otsake ŋmɔshi nibii Naturally haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ baa shi

english: Why do my crops dry up and fail to yield well during the minor rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The minor rainy season is shorter and the rains can stop suddenly before crops finish forming seeds or tubers. Using fast-maturing or drought-tolerant seed varieties ensures your crop reaches harvest before the water runs out.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ be lɛ faaa ni nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa trukaa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe dumɔwui loo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ naa. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ abaakpa onibii lɛ dani nu lɛ baaho.

english: Why do my crops look weak and stressed during hot afternoons even when the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhaoɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko po.

english: In intense sun, crop leaves lose water faster through evaporation than their roots can pull from the soil. Mulching around the base of plants with dry grass keeps the soil cool and prevents precious water from evaporating into the air.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tsei ahe baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How can I prevent my harvested vegetables from spoiling quickly while I wait for market prices to go up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mikpamɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni jara nɔ jara aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting during the cool early morning and storing your produce in well-ventilated, shaded areas prevents heat damage. For grains, keeping them in dry, airtight hermetic bags protects them from insects without needing expensive sprays.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni okɛ onibii lɛ to he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo akafite nii. Kɛha ŋmaa lɛ, kɛ́ akɛto vacuum kotokui ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa afɔ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops look small and unappealing to market buyers even after I put in a lot of hard work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi feɔ bibii ni egbalaaa mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ jara nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops produce small fruits when they have to compete heavily with weeds for nutrients or suffer from irregular watering. Giving plants proper spacing during planting ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, food, and room to grow big and attractive for buyers.
ga: Nidumɔ nii lɛ baawo yibii bibii. Kɛji akɛ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi miitswa akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ loo amɛmiipiŋ yɛ nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa kpãa shi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, niyenii, kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaadara ni eha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ aná he miishɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and turn yellow when they are in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and quickly dries out soil moisture, causing the seedlings to heat up, wilt, and turn yellow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baadɔ, amɛbaagbi, ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do shade trees help my cocoa plants survive the dry season?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees lower the soil temperature and slow down water evaporation from the ground, helping your cocoa plants retain moisture and stay healthy during long dry periods.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa o-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How do I know how much space to leave between cocoa trees when planting my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ mawo kookoo tsei amli kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ?

english: Leaving recommended spacing (about 3 meters by 3 meters) ensures each cocoa tree gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to produce pods without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Shi gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ekɛ ehe awo mli lɛ (aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3) koni ekwɛ akɛ kookoo tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekɛfee pods ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Is it better for me to clear my entire farm land at once or cultivate it in sections?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ shikome loo matsu nii yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli?

english: Clearing and planting in sections allows you to properly care for and weed young plants without getting overwhelmed by labor or leaving exposed soil vulnerable to erosion.
ga: Fãi ni ajieɔ kɛ dumɔwui Ehaa okwɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni otsu nii waa loo oshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ oshara mli akɛ ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the branches without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop due to excessive heat, insufficient rainfall, or a lack of tiny pollinating insects like midges, which are required to turn flowers into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa kɛha pollination, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni ehe hiaa ni amɛtsake fɔfɔi lɛ amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: How long does a new cocoa seedling usually take to produce its first crop?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ woɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years, while traditional varieties usually take around 4 to 5 years before producing their first cocoa pods.
ga: Kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa trees to get food while waiting for the cocoa to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni maná niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava heavily drains water and nutrients from the soil, so it is better to intercrop with plantain or cocoyam, which provide temporary shade without starving the cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ plantains loo kookoo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hɔmɔ yeee kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afata he.

english: Why are the leaf tips on my young cocoa plants turning brown and brittle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Brown, dry leaf tips usually mean your plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or a shortage of essential soil nutrients like potassium.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ eshɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, nu efo emli, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium bɛ mli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark, and excessively cool conditions, especially when trees are overgrown or not pruned.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, duŋ, kɛ fɛ̃i, titri lɛ kɛji tsei lɛ dara fe nine loo afolɔko amɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is rich enough to grow healthy cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, crumbly, and allows rainwater to drain easily without pooling on the surface for long periods.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. Clearing surrounding weeds and applying neem oil or insecticidal spray helps protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing lots of green leaves, but the tubers underground remain very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When sweet potatoes receive too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below. Using less manure or low-nitrogen fertilizers encourages larger tuber growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo loo nitrogen fioo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo adara.

english: Why do the tips of my young cocoa tree leaves burn and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight or harsh dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa shelters the leaves from direct sun and keeps humidity around the roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ atsu hulu la ni tsoɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ he nii. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing consistent soil moisture and light shade during the hottest part of the afternoon helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Black pod is a common fungal disease that spreads fast during wet, rainy conditions when air cannot flow around the trees. Regularly plucking infected pods and pruning thick cocoa branches to let sunlight in stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle tso lɛ he lɛ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ofolɔ kookoo niji ni mli tse lɛ. daa koni hulu la lɛ akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully grown and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava roots are typically mature when the leaves start yellowing and dropping off (around 9 to 12 months after planting), and when the soil around the base of the plant cracks open due to swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava shishifãi lɛ daa kɛji baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi (aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ) kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli etse yɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and deformed instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe efee shoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when the soil underneath is too hard, rocky, or compacted for the root to push through smoothly. Digging deep, loose soil mounds or high ridges gives the tubers room to expand downward cleanly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo ebɔle amɛhe waa aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ejɔ loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni akuɔ lɛ baaha tuber he lɛ alɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛya shi.

english: Why does my maize fall flat on the ground whenever a strong rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni ahum ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root system is shallow or when seeds are planted too close together. Mounding soil around the bottom of the stem (hilling) as the plant grows gives the roots extra support against strong winds.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (mound) he be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get covered in a white powdery dust during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ yɛŋ ehà mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That white dust is a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which thrives in crowded, shady fields where air doesn't move well. Spacing your cowpea seeds further apart allows sunlight and breeze to dry the leaves and prevent the fungus.
ga: Nakai sũ yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa mli jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ atse tsina dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛya shɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do the newer seed varieties yield more maize than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ woɔ ŋmãa babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified new seed varieties are specially bred for high yield, fast growth, and disease resistance. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength over generations, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ amli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛdara oya, ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do early-maturing crop varieties need fertilizer earlier in the season than my older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli fe mi tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Early-maturing crops complete their life cycle in a shorter time frame, so they consume nutrients much faster in their early weeks to build roots and stems before flowering.
ga: Tsei ni shwereɔ mra lɛ gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa yɛ be kukuoo mli, no hewɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kwraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. koni ekɛma shishifãi kɛ shishifãi dani ewo fɔfɔi

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air humid and the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do extension officers suggest planting plantains alongside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mi-kookoo tso hee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa plants from the hot sun, while also giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa bo yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are turning yellow from lack of rain or lack of soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves roll up or wilt during the dry afternoon heat. When crops lack soil nutrients, the leaves turn yellow or purple steadily, even when the soil is wet.
ga: Beni tsei bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ŋmãa dumɔ he afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot strips the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ajieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall with small yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and produce full yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Will removing extra side branches from my tomato plants help me get bigger fruits?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni mijie kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Yes, trimming extra side shoots directs the plant's food and energy straight into growing larger, healthier fruits instead of wasting energy on excess stem and leaf growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ,

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and get yellow patches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the leaves from making food, causing small or weak tubers.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo loo egbɔjɔɔ

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight from heating the earth, keeping the soil cool and locking in moisture so the plant roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ebaatsi jeŋ muu fɛɛ dɔlɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why can't I just plant the seeds saved from my last maize harvest instead of buying new seed bags every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduuu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui kotoku hee daa afi lɛ

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give high yields in their first planting, but seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in smaller yields and uneven plant growth in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Shi dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How much of my harvest should I set aside to re-plant for the next season so I don't run out of money to buy planting material?
ga: Esa akɛ ato ŋmɔshi nii lɛ mlijaa enyiɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? No hewɔ lɛ, mifiteee shika kɛheɔ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii?

english: Setting aside about 10 to 15 percent of healthy crop stems or grains ensures you have reliable planting material for the next season, reducing your cash burden when planting time arrives.
ga: Too tsei loo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ oha mlijaa 10 kɛyashi 15 he gbɛjianɔ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oyɛ dumɔ nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Enɛ haa oshika he jatsu lɛ baa shi kɛ́ be shɛ ni obaadu nii.

english: Why do some of the seeds I buy from local vendors fail to sprout at all after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds can lose their vitality if they are stored in hot, humid conditions or if they are past their shelf life, which is why buying certified seeds from recognized agricultural dealers is safer.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ afite shihilɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ, fɛ̃i yɔɔ loo kɛteke amɛ shihilɛ be. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko ni ale lɛ dɛŋ lɛ.

english: If someone does small-scale mining or uses heavy machinery on my land, can I still grow food crops on it afterwards?
ga: Kɛji mɔ ko miitsu shika tsuru ŋmɔ bibioo ko he nii loo ekɛ tsɔnei ni tsii miitsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Heavy machinery destroys the rich topsoil layer and leaves behind compacted subsoil and dangerous chemicals, making it extremely difficult for crops to grow without expensive land restoration.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ. ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni mli edɔ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni heɔ shika babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil; rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil, and how does that affect my crop yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te enáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Topsoil contains essential organic matter and nutrients crops need to feed; when rain washes it away, plants struggle to root properly and harvest yields decrease significantly.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, efoɔ tsei lɛ kɛyaa. Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ shishifãi ni sa lɛ ahe. ni nikpamɔ yibii lɛ hu baa shi waa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees drying up after I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ miigbo beni mifo tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants require shade protection from larger trees to shield them from intense sunlight and moisture loss while their roots are still developing.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer pods even when I clear the weeds around them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso ni etsɛ lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo komɛi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ ehe moŋ? Cocoa tsei daa

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural productivity drops; replacing old trees gradually with newer high-yielding varieties is needed to restore high pod yields.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ atsake tsei momoi lɛ fiofio koni akɛ pod ni fa babaoo aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if an agricultural chemical or fertilizer seller is offering me a genuine product or a scam?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ okwaayeli mli tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ kɛ nibii diɛŋtsɛ loo shishiumɔ nibii miiha?

english: Genuine agricultural inputs carry official registration seals from regulatory authorities, clear batch numbers, and accurate labeling; buying from accredited extension outlets helps avoid fake products.
ga: Okwaayeli mli nibii diɛŋtsɛ hiɛ woloŋmaa stamp kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ. clear batch number kɛ correct labeling Kɛ́ ohe nii yɛ shwapo ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ ekɛ nibii krokomɛi baatsu nii lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ amale nibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though I get enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of essential plant nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, showing that crops need proper fertilizer feeding in addition to water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛfata nu he.

english: If my plants are growing too close together in the field, is it okay for me to remove some of them?
ga: Kɛji mi tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani manyɛ majie ekomɛi kɛjɛ mli?

english: Yes, removing extra plants (called thinning) gives the remaining crops enough sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil so they can grow big and strong instead of fighting each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ thinning) haa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe baawu.

english: How can I tell if my crops are overcrowded and need more space?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo ni ehe miihia ni maná he ko babaoo?

english: If your plants look thin and weak, lean heavily to find light, or if their bottom leaves are turning yellow because sunlight cannot reach them, they are likely planted too closely together.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ Ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shi waa koni ena la lɛ Aloo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe. tsɔɔ akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too far apart from each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ?

english: While plants with lots of space will grow very well, planting them too far apart wastes farm space and leaves empty ground where weeds can easily take over.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ he ko babaoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ moŋ, shi tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔ mli he ni eshiɔ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni jwɛi baanyɛ aŋɔ he lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are there strange spots and discolored patches showing up on my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ sui ni tsakeɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ miije kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spots on leaves are usually signs of fungal or bacterial diseases, often caused by too much moisture or poor airflow between overcrowded plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji fungal loo bacteria hela ko he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo babaoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Is it helpful to cut off leaves that look damaged or sick from my growing crops?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba akɛ mafolɔ baai ni efite loo ni tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ mi lɛ kɛjɛ mitso ni miida lɛ mli?

english: Yes, carefully removing sick or dying leaves helps stop diseases from spreading to the healthy parts of the plant and keeps the crop clean.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni hela mɔ amɛ loo ni miigboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haaa hela akagbɛ ashwã tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tseɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning light green or yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the plant is not getting enough nutrients from the soil, such as nitrogen, or when the roots are getting too much or too little water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tsei lɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji shishifãi lɛ naa nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ.

english: How much yield should I expect to get from a single healthy cassava plant at harvest?
ga: Yibii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ maná kɛjɛ ŋmei tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: A well-cared-for cassava plant in good soil can yield between 5 to 10 kilograms (about 11 to 22 pounds) of healthy roots.
ga: Cassava tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 5 kɛyashi 10 (aaafee pound 11 kɛyashi 22).

english: Why are my neighbors getting more produce from their crops than I am getting from mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa babaoo kɛjɛɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii amli fe minɔ lɛ?

english: Higher crop yield usually comes from giving plants proper spacing, removing weeds regularly, using good fertilizer, and protecting them from pests and leaf diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni akɛtoɔ he kroko lɛ mli baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai tsuɔ nii kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ahe

english: Why is my crop growing very tall and bushy but not producing many fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji shi amɛwooo ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: When plants put all their energy into growing tall—often because they are competing for sunlight in crowded conditions—they may not have enough energy left to produce good fruits or roots.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsu nii koni amɛdara—bei pii lɛ, ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la yɛ shihilɛi ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ—ekolɛ amɛnaŋ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo yibii loo shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my crops are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show clear signs when mature, such as leaves drying up and changing color, stems falling over naturally, or fruits reaching their full size and proper color.
ga: Tsei baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni egbi kɛ amɛhe su tsakemɔ. Tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. aloo aduawai lɛ dalɛ fa ni eyɛ su ni sa.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow and stop growing whenever the water in my field dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ be fɛɛ be ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli baagbi lɛ?

english: Rice plants need consistent soil moisture to absorb essential nutrients from the ground. When the field dries out completely, the roots cannot take up fertilizer or soil nutrients properly, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stall.
ga: Omɔ tsei hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my rice in straight lines instead of just scattering the seeds everywhere on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives each rice plant proper spacing, sunlight, and airflow. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier compared to scattering seeds, which causes plants to crowd and fight for space.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso naa he ni sa, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ. Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa. Enɛ haa tsei buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛshiɔ he ko he akaŋ.

english: Why do my harvested rice grains break into tiny pieces when I take them to the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli fãi bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Grain breakage usually happens when paddy rice is dried too fast under extremely hot sun. Drying your harvested rice slowly in thin layers—preferably in mild sunlight or partial shade—prevents internal cracks, keeping the grains whole during milling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa mligbalamɔ baa kɛji ŋmaa gĩ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Omɔ ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ blɛoo yɛ ŋmãa bibioo mli, titri lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ mligbɛ ŋmeii anaa. ni ogbe ŋmãa lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival trick crops use to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which stops moisture from evaporating too quickly from the leaves.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many green leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil and not enough potassium. Excessive nitrogen causes the plant to spend all its energy growing big leafy stems above ground instead of sending energy down to swell the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni potassium lɛ faaa. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ, moŋ fe ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛwo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: If I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more on my land, why do I end up harvesting less food?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná he ko babaoo hu? Mɛni hewɔ mikpaaa niyenii fioo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Instead of getting many big, healthy plants, you end up with weak, crowded plants that yield smaller fruits or grains.
