ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, o náa tso nguahi nɛ a he wa fuu. Etsɔɔ tso ko ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer bags of grain every year even though I plant on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa kotokui fioo daa afi lɛ? ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ

english: Crops feed on specific nutrients in the soil to grow. When you plant the same crop on the same piece of land year after year without adding organic manure, fertilizer, or rotating with leguminous crops like beans, the soil becomes exhausted and loses its fertility.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my planted crops after the first rains of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil and are naturally tough, adapted to sprout immediately at the light of the first rain. Clearing your land early and removing weeds when they are still young prevents them from stealing light and nutrients from your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Atsake koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ ekɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ kpe. Shikpɔŋ ni oootsi mra Ni jwɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why are dark brown spots spreading across my crop leaves during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves create the ideal environment for fungal diseases to grow. Raindrops splashing from leaf to leaf spread the fungal spores across your field, creating dark spots that damage the foliage.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii adalɛ. Nugbɔ ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ baa.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my farm crops more heavily during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, green vegetation becomes scarce, so hungry insects migrate from dry wild bushes directly to green farm fields looking for food and sap. Additionally, heavy rain naturally washes small insect pests off plant leaves.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baafee nɔ ni faaa. Kplukai ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ koo mli jwɛi ni egbi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu hoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛyaa. kɛjɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli hu

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dry at the tips during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct intense sunlight or dry winds. They get heat-stressed easily, so planting temporary shade plants like plantains nearby protects them until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛhaoɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aka akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains akui wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to spread fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo kɛha mi akɛ mafɔse ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the top layer of fertilizer away off the farm or washes it too deep into the ground where the plant's roots cannot reach it, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe loo efoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground if I leave them after the wet season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil stays soaked with too much rain, air cannot reach the plant's roots. This lack of oxygen, combined with wet soil fungi, causes the mature cassava tubers to decay quickly.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Oxygen ni bɛ ni akɛfataa ŋmeii ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines off the ground using stakes or sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso loo tso awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need full sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into small tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by insects that disturbs leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without ever growing into tomatoes when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato kɔkɔɔkɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the sticky pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot pollinate themselves. Unpollinated flowers die and drop off because the plant cannot form seeds or fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeee pollination. Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui loo aduawai.

english: Why does putting dry grass and leaves on the soil around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai baawo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minibii ni miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps soil moisture, keeps root temperatures cool during hot days, suppresses weed growth, and eventually decays into natural manure.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans on my field improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top ones are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving its limited nitrogen up to nourish the younger leaves at the top, showing that your soil needs manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Beni baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen fioo ko kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every time I plant on the same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Crops like maize consume specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting the exact same crop repeatedly drains those specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up; planting beans or groundnuts in rotation restores nitrogen back to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsuɔ nii daa be. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Beans loo peanuts ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry out and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight and heat. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool microclimate and protects their tender leaves until they grow strong enough to endure full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko baa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young pepper plants with dry grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-baby pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that stops sunlight from baking the bare soil. It prevents irrigation water from evaporating quickly, keeps the roots cool, and slows down weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ egbi. Tsi nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: How should I cut and place my cassava stems in the ground so they grow strong cassava tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oha tɛŋŋ koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ awa?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be about 20–30 cm long with healthy buds pointing upward. Planting them at an angle or horizontally buried beneath 5–10 cm of moist soil ensures proper root formation and strong tuber development.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ni afo lɛ afee aaafee 20–30 cm ni ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo afuɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi 5–10 cm yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground away from fungal diseases and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, ni agbɛ amɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruit bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants often fall over because invisible pests like microscopic worms (nematodes) or weevils eat away their shallow roots underground, destroying the plant's anchor during strong winds or heavy fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii bibii (nematodes) loo ŋmeii yeɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo yibiiwoo ni tsii mli.

english: How can our farming group store our harvested maize together for months without insects eating it all?
ga: Te wɔ okwaayeli kuu lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛha ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ afee ekome nyɔji babaoo ni kooloi bibii lɛ eyeee fɛɛ?

english: Insects need air and moisture to survive. Drying maize completely until it cracks between your teeth and storing it in airtight hermetic bags or clean sealed drums starves pests of oxygen and keeps the grain safe without chemicals.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i he miihia koolooi koni amɛhi shi. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashi ebaagbala onyanyɔji ni okɛto vacuum kotoku ni mli tse loo baagi ni atsĩ naa mli. Ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa ni eye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni tsofai bɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when pollinators like bees are absent. Ensuring steady watering during hot afternoons keeps the plant calm enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ kpoo bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops. They aggressively steal soil nutrients, fertilizers, water, and sunlight that your main crop needs to grow thick and tall.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛdara.

english: Why do I need to cut my seed yam into pieces before planting instead of planting the whole tuber?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afo sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli bibii bibii dani adu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu tuber muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cutting a large yam tuber into smaller pieces (seed setts) allows you to plant many more crops from a single harvested yam. It also stimulates dormant buds on the skin of the cut piece to sprout into fresh, strong new vines.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii wuji amli bibii bibii (dumɔwui akui) lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akpaa shikome lɛ mli. Ekanyaa ŋmeii ni ewɔ lɛ hu. Yɛ he ni afo lɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ, wain tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What will happen to my cut yam pieces if I put them straight into the ground without letting them dry first?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potatoes ni mifo lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛwo shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ ni mihaaa amɛgbi klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Freshly cut yam pieces have wet, open wounds that easily attract soil bacteria, insects, and fungi, causing the seed to rot before it can sprout. Letting the cuts dry in the shade or dusting them with wood ash seals the wound to protect the seed.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni afo ehee Pilamɔi ni agbele ni efɔ ni gbalaa helatsɛmɛi, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Ha pilamɔ lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo okɛ tso sũ afɔ pilamɔ lɛ he koni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I clear all the weeds and bushes off my field before making my yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mafee sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing the field removes hidden pests and prevents old plants and weeds from stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your young yam plants when they begin to grow.
ga: He ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa tsei kɛ jwɛi momoi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ mra be mli sweet potato tsei lɛ amli beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do yams need high soil mounds to grow well instead of just being planted on flat soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Mounds provide loose, soft soil that allows the expanding yam tuber to push easily downward without hitting hard earth. High mounds also keep the roots safe from drowning in heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ ji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akabote nu mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the top of my planted yam mounds with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi aha mi sweet potato ŋtayaa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the mounds—a practice called mulching—protects the delicate buried seed piece from harsh sun heat, keeps moisture in the soil, and prevents heavy rain from washing the soil mound away.
ga: Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni afu amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers under the soil. Wooden stakes lift the leaves high into the light and keep them off the wet ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Tso ko woɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ kane lɛ akpee. Ni ha amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if I am planting my crops too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If crops are planted too close, their leaves shade each other from the sun and their roots fight over water and food in the soil, causing thin vines and small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai tsiɔ hulu la naa ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa wain tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Why does planting my crops right at the start of the rainy season make such a big difference?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa nɛkɛ?

english: Planting at the start of the rains ensures young plants get steady moisture while their roots are developing, allowing them to establish deeply before any unexpected dry spell arrives.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ aduɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani hɔmɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant yams on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting yams repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients yams need to grow and lets yam-loving pests and diseases accumulate in the soil over time.
ga: Sweet potato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa sweet potato koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. ni eha kooloi kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ sweet potato lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like maize or beans in the same space as my yams, or will they harm my main crop?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni sweet potato lɛ yɔɔ lɛ? Aloo ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui?

english: You can grow them together through intercropping. Legumes like beans naturally add nitrogen into the soil which nourishes the yams, while fast-growing crops like maize maximize your land use without harming the tubers below.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua ni okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo ni eyeee bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ awui.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting at the tip and moving down the central vein of older lower leaves, usually means your maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay dark green and grow strong stems.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ, titri lɛ, jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naa ni eyaa shi kɛyaa baa ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná su ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little cups and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni etsake?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny, invisible pests like thrips or mites sucking the juice from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying organic neem oil or appropriate insecticides early helps protect the young shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Mra be mli ni akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii bibii ahe.

english: Tomatoes shed their blossoms when temperatures get too high during the day or night, or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Without uniform soil moisture, the flowers dry out and drop before pollination can turn them into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani pollination baanyɛ atsɔ amɛ aduawai.

english: Why are my watermelons rotting from the bottom end while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rot is called 'blossom-end rot' and happens when the plant cannot transport enough calcium to the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent helps the plant move calcium continuously to the fruit tips.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ‘Blossom end rot’ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium yaa aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the cassava roots I harvested small, thin, and woody this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni mikpaa lɛ ji bibii, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni tamɔ tsei yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell when the soil is too hard and compacted, when weeds compete heavily for nutrients in the first three months, or when plants are spaced too close together. Softening the soil beds and early weeding allow tubers room to swell.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe. Enɛ ji be mli ni jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when a strong wind blows, even before the bunch matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or root-weevil grubs eat away the underground roots, leaving the tall plant without a anchor. Planting clean, treated suckers keeps the root system strong and anchored.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo weevils lɛ ye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Ha tso lɛ akwɔ ni ŋwɛi ŋta bɛ he Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishifãi ni he tse ni atsa amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly through rain splashes and high humidity. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and air circulate through the canopy keeps the pods dry and reduces fungal growth.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cabbage plants form soft, loose leaves instead of folding into a hard, tight ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɔle ehe ni efee kui ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head properly if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or experience high heat. Excessive nitrogen forces rapid leaf growth without giving the plant time to form a tight center head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ atsɔ yitso nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa waa nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa baai lɛ daa oya ni ehaaa tso lɛ be ni ekɛfee bulb ni mli wa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ.

english: Is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Alternating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the soil is moist enough to plant my seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛdu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to germinate; if you plant after just one short rain, a sudden dry stretch can kill the sprouted seed underground. Squeeze a handful of topsoil—if it holds together in a ball without dripping, the soil has ideal moisture for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔ kuku ko sɛɛ shikome pɛ Trukaa lɛ, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli nine kome kɛji ekɛ ehe ebɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or Gliricidia planted beside them to block strong heat and hold moisture in the soil while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo glicidia ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he, ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the central vein is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the correct stage helps leaves stay green and boosts grain size.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni etsɔɔ fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Muji ni etse ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Applying recommended organic remedies like neem leaf extract or approved insecticides directly into the funnels early in the morning destroys the pests before they kill the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛgbe he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction the buds point when I push cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ cassava nine ko wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the node buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down delays leaf sprouting and causes roots to grow poorly, resulting in much smaller tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji lɛ esa akɛ odu amɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ ehiii kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tuber ni anáa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil plant food through small nodules on their roots. When you harvest them, this natural nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ okpa amɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to clear land and cut tall sticks to stake my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafolɔ tsei aniji kakadaji koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture energy for big tubers. Keeping leaves off the ground also prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from spreading onto the foliage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛ bulb agboi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop mainly when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying mulch around the roots keeps the soil cool so flowers stay on to produce peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi koni amɛfee chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Mi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly during dry weather, suppresses weed growth, and turns into rich organic manure as it decays.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛji efite

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Tight leaf curling is usually caused by Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies feeding on the sap. Controlling whiteflies with soapy water or botanical sprays early in the season stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ye ŋmeii yɛji anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the main rainy season settles in. Planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then wither away from lack of moisture during the heat gap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer. When the soil runs out of nutrients, the plant moves whatever food it has left to its upper leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen directly out of the air and fix it into the soil. When the leaves and roots break down in the ground, they leave behind free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ lɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips. As they suck the sap from under the leaves, they spread viruses and cause the foliage to warp.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ Amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn soft and black before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the fruit, which is usually triggered by uneven watering during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or attacks by insects like mirids. Dropping flowers helps the tree save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii Aloo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ tamɔ atatui, fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to grow bigger tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food for the tubers below. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and protects them from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo aba ni ekɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily lose their grip on the soil when heavy bunches grow. Tiny pests called nematodes can also eat away the root system, making the tree unstable.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo kɛji jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ kwɛ̃. ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ hu baanyɛ aye shishifãi lɛ. ha tso lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ

english: Why do my crops grow much slower when I leave weeds in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. They steal the food meant for your plants, causing your crops to grow weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the soil stays soaked for too long, water fills all the air gaps, suffocating the roots and causing rotting fungi to multiply.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ he lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture to plant maize after the first rains?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball and then press it gently. If it holds its shape without dripping water and crumbles easily when touched, it has just enough moisture for seed germination.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu ni onyɛ nɔ blɛoo. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ ata he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains beside them blocks harsh light and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees are mature enough to survive on their own.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ, ebaatsi la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete with the main plant for water and nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe Plantain kome Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plant the food it needs to turn green and grow heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Planting maize on the same field continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does leaving dry grass on top of the ground help my vegetables during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi aduawai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that prevents the sun from evaporating soil moisture. It keeps the ground cool, saves water, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ, ehaaa nu ahi shi, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves of growing maize. You can control them by checking your farm early and applying recommended pesticides or localized organic treatments into the leaf funnels.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli baai bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra nɔ. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ awo baai lɛ amli.

english: This black rotting is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the tomato roots absorb calcium and produce clean, healthy fruit.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa, ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to push tall wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight, which powers the growth of the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and maximizing crop yield.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni hulu la aba amɛnɔ. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How do I select the best cassava stems to cut and plant for my next farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Choose thick, mature stems from strong plants that showed no signs of leaf diseases during the season. Cut pieces from the middle part of the stem containing at least three to five healthy nodes for quick root growth.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko bɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ahe tsei ni mli tse ni eda. Kpɔ̃ɔ fãi kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3-5 yɔɔ mli koni ewo shishifãi lɛ adalɛ oya he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow when I plant them immediately after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often wet only the surface layer of soil, followed by several hot days. If the deeper soil is still dry, planted seeds will absorb just enough water to open and then dry out and die before sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbele. No sɛɛ lɛ, egbiɔ ni egboɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. Leaving selected forest trees or planting plantains around them provides necessary shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni ajieɔ yɛ koo ni ahala lɛ mli loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Tsei lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my green maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso ni ji eŋɔli lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rains fall heavily for many weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, air cannot reach the cassava roots, causing root rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away quickly.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to eat holes inside the center of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ye bu ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the central growing leaves of corn. Applying approved organic pesticides or neem leaves extract early in the morning helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɔ dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Propping up the main stem with strong bamboo poles or wooden stakes gives the tree physical support against wind until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. cause a lot weight Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eshi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn black and rotten before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani tomato lɛ daa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which occurs when the plant does not get enough calcium or experiences uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for next season's maize crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plants decay, this natural nitrogen enriches the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper bushes curling upwards and preventing the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that transmit leaf curl virus. Spraying the leaves with soap-water solution or recommended insecticides kills these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to weed around my yam mounds while the vines are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi abɔle ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he be mli ni wain tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that young yam vines need to grow strong. Keeping the mounds clear allows the plant to send all its food down to form large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ha gɔŋ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsuɔ eniyenii fɛɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee bulbs agboi.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into fine powder and get filled with tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda kpakpa ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: This damage is caused by storage pests called weevils that bore into dry grains to eat and lay eggs. Properly sun-drying the seeds and storing them in airtight bags or treated storage bins prevents weevil attacks.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ nii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi koni eye ni ekɛwo ŋmeii Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni atsa mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akatutua amɛ.

english: What does 'lining and pegging' mean, and why should I do it before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘lining kɛ riveting’ shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee enɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Lining and pegging means using ropes and wooden pegs to measure and mark exact spots on your farm before planting. Doing this ensures your crops are neatly spaced in straight lines, which gives each plant enough sunlight, air, and room for roots to gather nutrients without overcrowding.
ga: Lining kɛ pinning tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ kpãa kɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baasusu ni okadi hei pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani okɛdu. Enɛ haa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa ni ehiɛɛɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear old roots and stump debris before I peg and plant my new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie shishifãi momoi kɛ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ dani mahi shi ni madu ŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Clearing old roots and debris prevents pests and fungal diseases from surviving in the soil and attacking your new crops. It also makes it easier to measure straight lines and dig healthy planting holes.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie shishifãi momoi kɛ sũi ni etse lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua onibii heei lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu akɛ aaasusu ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja ni atsa dumɔ bu ni wa.

english: How should I layer or fill soil inside my nursery polybags for young seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ sũ ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ato loo awo polybags amli?

english: Fill the polybag with loose, fertile topsoil mixed with dark compost, leaving about one inch at the top. Topsoil provides the natural nutrients young roots need, and leaving space at the top keeps soil from washing away when you water.
ga: Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ efutu mli lɛ awo polybag lɛ mli. Shi shikpɔŋ aaafee 1 inch yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa shishifãi bibii lɛ. Ni kɛ́ oshi he ko yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ okɛ nu shwie nɔ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings need a shade canopy in the nursery before moving them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are very sensitive like newborn babies. Direct, harsh sunlight can scorch their leaves and dry out their small roots before they are strong enough to handle full sun in the main farm.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ nuɔ he waa, tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbi dani amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my crop seedlings in the nursery are mature enough to transplant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ adu amɛ?

english: Seedlings are ready when they have developed a firm main stem, at least 4 to 6 strong leaves, and a solid root ball that holds the soil together when removed from the nursery bag.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛfee tso titri ni wa. Kɛ hoo lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 4 kɛyashi 6 kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛji ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: If I want to plant plantains and young cocoa together, which crop should go into the ground first?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni makwɛ plantain kɛ cocoa bibii lɛ ekome Mɛɛ tso esa akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: You should plant plantains first or at the same time as the cocoa. Plantains grow faster and produce large broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees from dying under the hot sun.
ga: Esa akɛ odu dumɔwui lɛ dani okɛ kookoo lɛ adu loo yɛ be kome too mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and slender when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward trying to reach light, making them tall and weak instead of thick and healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi, ni amɛmiitao ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Ha amɛfee mɛi ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ekãa kɛ hewalɛ.

english: How deep should I bury my seedling when taking it out of the polybag to plant in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ poly kotokui lɛ amli koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You should plant the seedling at the exact same depth it was growing in the nursery bag. Burying the stem too deep causes it to rot, while planting it too shallow leaves the roots exposed to heat and wind.
ga: Esa akɛ odu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni adu amɛ yɛ grow bags lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ofu tso lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha egbo. Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baaná dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Should I place animal manure at the bottom of the hole before putting in my seedling?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii awo bu lɛ shishi dani mikɛ dumɔwui awo mli?

english: You should mix the manure with topsoil first rather than putting raw manure straight at the bottom. Fresh or unmixed manure gets very hot as it breaks down and can burn the tender roots of your young seedling.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afutu sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ awo shishi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei loo ni akɛfutuuu mli lɛ mli edɔ waa kɛji efite ni ebaanyɛ eshã otsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my nursery seedlings turning yellow even when I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving seedlings too much water drowns the roots by filling all the air spaces in the soil, which stops the plant from breathing and turns leaves yellow. Only water when the top layer of soil feels dry, and make sure your nursery bags have holes at the bottom for drainage.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo dumɔwui lɛ amli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni eeewo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nu pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nu he akɛ egbi. Ni kwɛmɔ ni okwɛ akɛ o-grow bag lɛ yɛ bu yɛ shishigbɛ koni nu atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight rolls during a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water, their leaves roll up tightly to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and survive dry heat until the next rainfall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ koni ŋmãa lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ baa.

english: Can I rely only on rainfall to grow cassava, or do I need a backup water source?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ okɛ nugbɔ pɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu ŋmei? Aloo esa akɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ahi shi?

english: Cassava is a tough crop that grows well with normal rainfall once its roots are set. However, planting early in the rainy season is essential so young cuttings get enough moisture to form strong root systems.
ga: Cassava ji ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛji ewo shishifãi pɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji bibii lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily by direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that create a shade umbrella, keeping the young cocoa seedlings cool and the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Will planting beans alongside my maize help or harm my maize crops?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ awui?

english: Planting beans with maize helps your maize grow better. Beans act as 'helpers' by trapping nitrogen from the air and feeding it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beans tsuɔ nii akɛ ‘yelikɛbualɔi’ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni emɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to pull out extra seedlings if three or four seeds sprout in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie dumɔwui krokomɛi kɛji dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seedlings grow too close together, they fight each other for nutrients, sunlight, and water. Pulling out the weaker extra plants gives the remaining seedling enough space and food to grow strong and yield big crops.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛkɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu. Tsei krokomɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my crop field as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, fertilizers, and sunlight intended for your plants. Removing weeds early allows your crops to grow strong without competing for survival.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa ni okɛ amɛ akaŋ akaŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I completely uproot and destroy cassava plants that have twisted, yellowish leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie ŋmei tsei fɛɛ ni baai ni etsilɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni akpãtã amɛhiɛ lɛ?

english: Twisted, pale leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which spreads from plant to plant through small insects like whiteflies. Pulling out and burning diseased plants protects the rest of your field from getting infected.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies nɔ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie ni oshã lɛ baaye abua ni ebu he ni eshwɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ hela he.

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up and look crinkled?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects. Spraying early with neem oil can protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ abu baai lɛ ahe

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and sterile, preventing the flower from forming a fruit. Shading the plants or mulching the soil keeps the roots cool enough for fruit to set.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Tsi fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo yibii Tso lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni yibii lɛ anyɛ atswa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent even when the leaves on top look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand downwards easily. If the soil is hard or compacted, or if you use too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of expanding the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni kwɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ bulbs.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water. Once the rains return, the plant naturally sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing its underground roots.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi.

english: Why are my tomato stems growing very tall and thin instead of bushy and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants grow tall and thin, or 'leggy', when they are planted too close together or shaded, causing them to stretch upward in search of sunlight.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo loo ‘naji’ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli tsɔ. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛyatao hulu la.

english: Maize leaves curl inward during hot periods to reduce their surface area exposed to the sun, which stops moisture from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani eyibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face stress, such as intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil needed to hold the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow flowers directly on their thick trunks instead of on young branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔii yɛ tsei ni mli tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on their main trunk and thick branches so that tiny pollinating insects like midges can reach them easily, and so the heavy cocoa pods have strong support as they grow.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ amɛtso wulu lɛ kɛ amɛniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe mlɛo. Ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsii hewɔ lɛ, amɛfiɔ amɛsɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my young watermelons turn black and rot before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon gbekɛ lɛ shishi ji ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eda lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually triggered by uneven soil moisture or prolonged dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni ejaaa loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs become very bitter even when they look ripe and fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ ŋɔɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ehee moŋ?

english: Garden eggs become bitter when they are harvested too late or when the plant experiences severe heat and drought stress while the fruit is forming.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akpa amɛ sɛɛ tsɔ. aloo beni tsei naa latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ be mli ni aduawai miifee lɛ.

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up completely, showing the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsakeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ naa.

english: Why does my plantain stool produce smaller bunches when I leave many shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain poop lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one main plantain tree, they compete with each other for soil nutrients, water, and light, resulting in smaller bunches for all of them.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ la mli lɛ he, ni no haa niji bibii baa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu nɔ.

english: Why are my citrus leaves curling up and covered in a sticky white layer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Sticky white residue on citrus trees is caused by tiny insects like mealybugs that suck plant sap and secrete a sweet substance, which can slow down leaf growth if left untreated.
ga: sticky white residue Yɛ citrus tsei anɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs, ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees away from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Keeping bigger trees or planting plantains next to them provides essential shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop showing holes with small powdery waste inside the top leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani eyɛ wolo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaves of maize plants. Applying recommended control products or clean ash directly into the center funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it ruins the stalk.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛyeɔ hela lɛ nɔ loo sũ ni he tse wo ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmei lɛ dani efite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellowish-green and curling up into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing and leaf distortion is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Using disease-free stems of improved varieties recommended by extension agents prevents this issue.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsakeɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ haa. Kɛ akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni woɔ nibii ahe hewalɛ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ahe tsei ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to maximum sunlight so the vine can produce more energy, which directs food down to grow larger and healthier yam tubers under the soil while keeping leaves off the hot ground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ woɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ kudɔɔ niyenii lɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ebaai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and drop off very quickly during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose moisture quickly when dry winds blow. Covering the soil around the base of the plantain with dry leaves or plant husks (mulching) keeps the root zone moist during dry periods.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswa lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo tsei ahe tsɔi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem can burn the plant tissue and roots due to concentrated chemical salts. It is best to apply fertilizer in a ring a small distance away from the stem where feeder roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli fãji kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ ŋta lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo lɛ mli. ni shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my maize harvest drop if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize uses up specific nutrients like nitrogen quickly. Planting maize continuously exhausts the soil, whereas rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen back into the land naturally.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen tsuɔ nii oya. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ ehe. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and turn pale even when there is regular rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete heavily with crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. If weeds are left uncleared, they steal essential food from the soil before the roots of your crop can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛji ashi jwɛi lɛ ni mli tseee Jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce lots of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi ko gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off due to high dry heat, irregular watering, or a lack of balanced nutrients. Keeping moisture levels steady in the soil during flowering helps the flowers set into healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa ni haa egbiɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni ja ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny insects bore holes into the maize grains I store after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa ni mibuaa naa beni mikpaa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack stored maize if the grains are not thoroughly dried or are stored in unsealed sacks. Sun-drying the maize properly until it is hard and using clean, airtight bags prevents these insects from multiplying.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa loo akɛto kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni akɛ vacuum kotokui ni he tse tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Applying well-rotted manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help your maize regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant my crop during the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli?

english: The ideal time to plant is right after the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains. Planting too early into dry soil causes seeds to dry up, while planting too late causes crops to miss the peak rainfall required for good yields.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ji beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Can withholding water from my pepper plants for a short time actually encourage them to produce more fruit?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛtsiɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anaa yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baanyɛ awo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, mild stress can signal to the plant that it needs to reproduce quickly, triggering it to produce more flowers and fruit. However, this must be done carefully, as severe drought stress will cause flowers to drop off completely.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔnyɛɛ fioo baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ale akɛ ehe miihia ni amɛfɔ oya. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ atsu tsei ni tsirɛɔ amɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hɔmɔ ni naa wa baaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo kwraa.
