english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a disease or just being eaten by insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo kooloi bibii miiye amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Inspect the damage closely: insects leave visible bite marks, holes, or pests on the stems, whereas diseases usually show up as discolored spots, yellowing rings, powdery surfaces, or sudden wilting without any physical chewing.
ga: Kwɛmɔ he ni efite lɛ jogbaŋŋ: Kplukai shĩɔ ŋmeii, bu, loo ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Amɛfɔɔ kpojiemɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni amɛhe su etsake. ŋmɔŋ powder texture loo trukaa ni shwieɔ shi ni niyenii ni ayeee

english: Why should I trim off some of the lower leaves and shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning lower leaves allows more sunlight and air to circulate around the stem, which reduces fungal diseases. It also directs the plant's energy away from growing useless leaves and into producing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ he fɛɛ he. trunk babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: How many times and at what stages should I apply fertilizer to my crops for the best harvest?
ga: Shii enyiɛ kɛ mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Most crops perform best with split applications—usually once shortly after germination to boost root and leaf growth, and a second time just before flowering to support fruit or seed development.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ enɛ shikome pɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ aya hiɛ. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni eye ebua aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Can I use chemical sprays to cure my cocoa trees once brown spots start appearing on the leaves?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ je kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, approved fungicides can control leaf spot diseases, but they work best when applied at the very first sign of infection. Spraying on a regular schedule during humid weather prevents the disease from destroying the farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii. Shi etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo mɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela lɛ eba lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ato tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as temporary shade umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are some of my planted seeds failing to sprout even after rains have fallen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to germinate if they were planted too deep in the soil, if bad storage ruined their viability, or if the soil became waterlogged and suffocated the seeds before they could break through the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni dumɔwu lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛhiɔ shi lɛ, Aloo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage is very delicate. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them protects the seedlings from heat stress until they are established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa kwraa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛbaatswa shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft stem and inner leaves of young maize. Detecting them early allows you to use recommended sprays or traditional treatments like neem extract before they destroy the entire farm.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛtutuaa ŋmãa bibii kɛ amɛmli baai lɛ. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ŋaa loo blema tsofai tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii dani efite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants produce very small roots while others give large ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi shishifãi bibii waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need enough space and loose soil to grow big. Planting stem cuttings too close together forces the plants to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my plant leaves turn pale green or yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate that the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen. Adding animal manure or well-balanced fertilizer gives plants the strength to grow green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or dry soil, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moisture steady and balanced helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. aloo beni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food and water. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to produce a much bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsofɔi krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents the bottoms of the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts or beans together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fata he lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground through their roots. This enriches the soil naturally and helps neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight on all their leaves to build energy and store it underground. Lifting the vines off the wet soil also prevents leaf diseases and leads to larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot soil will dry out and kill the freshly sprouted seeds before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why are my crop plants growing so many big leaves but giving me very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops grow too fast vegetative growth takes over, spending all the plant's energy on producing heavy foliage instead of flowers and fruits. Pruning unneeded branches helps redirect that energy back into growing big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara oya tsɔ Tsei adalɛ baaye egbɛhe. Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni tsii. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Cocoa pods rot when thick, unpruned branches trap damp air and block sunlight around the tree. Letting fresh air and light pass through the canopy dries out moisture and stops black pod disease from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji niji ni mli tse ni afolɔko lɛ mɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni amɛtsi hulu la ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ naa. Kɛ́ oha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la bote ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi black pod hela lɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it dangerous if I allow bushy, low-hanging branches to grow thick on my farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee oshara kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ fee jwɛi ni mli ewo muji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Overgrown foliage creates dark, damp hiding places for dangerous creatures like snakes and scorpions, making farm work unsafe and potentially sending you to the hospital if you step on them.
ga: Baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ haa bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ onufui kɛ ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni mli edɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni ekolɛ ebaaha oya helatsamɔhe kɛji onyiɛ amɛnɔ.

english: How do I know when it is time to trim or prune extra branches off my trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafolɔ loo majie niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You should trim extra branches when the leaves grow so dense that sunlight can no longer reach the main stem or ground below, or when wild shoots begin taking energy away from main fruiting branches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ahe beni baai lɛ dara waa aahu akɛ hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ lɛ. Aloo beni koo mli tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei niji titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does sunlight need to reach the trunk and lower parts of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ hulu la lɛ ashɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi kɛ eshishigbɛ hei lɛ?

english: Sunlight acts as a natural dryer that destroys mold spores and harmful fungi on the tree stem, while helping pods ripen evenly and stay healthy.
ga: Hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei anɔ lɛ fiteɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can giving my crops too much fertilizer actually reduce my yield?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes rapid leaf growth with very few fruits, creating heavy shade that holds excess dampness and leads to crop decay.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baaha baai lɛ adara oya ni aduawai fioo pɛ aba. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ baa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ.

english: Why do insects like mirids and capsids attack dark, bushy cocoa farms more than open ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids kɛ capsids tutuaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔji yɔɔ mli lɛ fe ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in cool, humid shade created by dense leaves because direct sunlight dries them out. Thinning out thick leaves removes their hiding spots.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ ni tsei ahe tsei lɛ feɔ lɛ ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ. Kɛ́ afee baai ni mli tse lɛ mlɛo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why is good breeze or airflow important inside my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ he hiaa yɛ miŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Flowing air quickly dries rain and morning dew off leaves and stems, preventing moisture build-up that fungal rot needs to grow and infect crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ kɛ leebi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ oya. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ naa.

english: What happens if I leave young shoots growing out from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ shwie shi?

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main tree stem. Removing them keeps the main tree strong so it can produce plenty of pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaawaje tso titri lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: How does clearing thick leaves and weeds under my cocoa trees stop pods near the ground from rotting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ajie baai kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ni ajie ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ lɛ koni amɛkafite?

english: Fungal rot lives in damp ground soil. Clearing dense growth allows sunlight to dry the soil surface so heavy rains cannot splash wet fungal spores onto your low pods.
ga: Rot fungi hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Nibii ni eda waa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ. No hewɔ lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nyɛŋ ashwie ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ o-pods ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to protect themselves from losing too much water, and they usually bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as a living canopy, protecting the young cocoa seedlings from strong heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crop seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too tightly together, their roots compete for water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them properly allows every plant to get enough food and light to yield well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei waa tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and produce very little yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very aggressively and steal soil food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets all the nutrients it needs to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ agbo ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make the food that grows the tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves high up into the light and keeps them off the wet soil where fungal diseases can easily rot them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ la mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afite oya lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small dark dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ waa mli Yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing tip of the plant and chew the soft leaves. Treating the crops early in the morning or late afternoon when caterpillars feed stops them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Tsumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii leebi loo shwane mli. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ miiye nii lɛ, tsi amɛnaa dani ŋmɔ lɛ akumɔ.

english: Curled, small leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking plant juices and spreading plant sickness. Controlling these insects using neem oil or recommended sprays allows new leaves to expand flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ekɛ tsei amli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ tsu nii kɛye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai heei lɛ ni amɛdara ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers can drop off when weather temperatures get too high, when water is lacking, or when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and balanced feeding encourage flowers to set into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbo kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, kɛji nu bɛ, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can notice cracks in the soil around the base of the stem, or gently clear soil around one root to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli loo okɛ blɛoo ajie sũ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shishifã lɛ yɛ fa kome koni ona kɛji tuber lɛ mli edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight because their root systems are not deep enough to draw enough water. Planting shade crops like plantains overhead protects young leaves from sun damage and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to keep growing, showing that fertilizer or compost is needed.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara, ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: Why should I space my maize seeds carefully instead of planting several seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-corn ŋmeii lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu Dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ.

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the growing plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them gives each plant enough space to grow strong stalks and larger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni ato lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if it rains too heavily near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ beni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes water to collect in heavy soil, blocking air from reaching the roots. Without oxygen in the soil, bacteria and fungi quickly multiply and cause the cassava tubers to decay.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu buaa ehe naa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Bacteria kɛ fungi lɛ faa oya ni amɛhaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or lack of water. Heat stresses the plant and prevents pollination, so keeping the soil moist helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ sũ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: If I cut off some of the lower leaves on my tomato plant, won't that hurt the plant?
ga: Kɛ mifo tomato tso ko shishi baai lɛ, Efiteee tomato tsei lɛ, aloo jeee nakai?

english: Removing lower leaves actually helps the plant by directing food and energy toward growing bigger fruit rather than keeping old leaves alive, while also improving airflow to prevent leaf diseases.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa tso yibii wuji lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha baai momo lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi baai helai anaa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the juice underneath the leaves. Controlling these pests helps new leaves grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai heei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds when the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai akutsei lɛ feɔ shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantains have short, shallow roots that cannot support heavy weight on top. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop stick prevents wind from tipping the heavy tree over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ tsɔne ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food, which flows back down to feed and expand the yam tuber under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ekoŋŋ koni eyaye sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm make the soil better for my next crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil with free fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build food. It can also happen when excess water sits in the field, suffocating the roots and preventing them from drinking up soil nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee niyenii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛnu niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even after spending almost a year in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to swell into thick tubers. If the soil is too hard and compact, or if you used fertilizers with too much nitrogen, the plant spends its energy growing green leaves above ground instead of expanding roots below.
ga: Kassava shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛfuu ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai eŋɔlii lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shishi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly during wet, humid weather and in heavy shade. The fungus travels through splashing rain droplets and destroys the cocoa beans inside the pod.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fuji lɛ tsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ amli ni efiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How does a crop disease reach my farm when my neighbor's infected farm is separated from mine by a road?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai shɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Beni gbɛ ko gbala mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Tiny fungal spores and small insects that carry diseases travel through the air with wind currents, splash through rainwater, or stick to shoes, clothing, and farm tools as people move from field to field.
ga: Fungal spores bibii kɛ kooloi bibii ni hiɛ helai lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, amɛshwieɔ nugbɔ nu mli loo amɛkpɛtɛɔ tokotai, atadei kɛ okwaayeli nibii ahe beni gbɔmɛi fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves and vines of my yam plants drying up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ miiho dani akpa lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is usually caused by leaf spot diseases or insect pests attacking the stem. When the leaves dry up early, the plant loses its ability to make food, resulting in very small yams.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya ji leaf spot hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ gĩ oya Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni miduuu pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Dropping flowers helps the plant conserve energy to survive the stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. loo shikpɔŋ ni fɔsfɔs bɛ nɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ haomɔ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the ground, causing temporary wilting. However, if they do not bounce back by evening, pests or root diseases may be damaging the plant's underground system.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, kɛji amɛkuuuu amɛsɛɛ amɛbaaa gbɛkɛ. Kooloi loo shishifãi helai hu baanyɛ afite tso lɛ shikpɔŋ shishi gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do the edges of my crop leaves look dry and burnt after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ ahe feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni eshã beni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer or placing it directly against the plant stem creates a salty environment that pulls water out of the roots, burning the plant leaves from dehydration.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo akɛwoɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli ŋmei baa. ni baajie nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eha tso lɛ baai ashã yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them with maize feeds the soil and helps the maize grow stronger without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa abɛi lɛ ni edaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops on raised mounds or ridges instead of flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges loosen the soil so root crops like yams and cassava can grow bigger easily. They also prevent excess water from drowning root systems during heavy rains and make harvesting much simpler.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava baanyɛ adara oya. Ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize relies on to grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant stay green and grow bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa damɔɔ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa wuji.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excess water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy stems and leaves above ground instead of expanding the food tubers underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ niyenii yitso ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over after it produces a heavy bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi beni ewo yibii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that cannot easily hold heavy weight. Supporting the stem with a strong bamboo or wooden prop prevents strong winds and heavy bunches from pulling the tree out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ jatsui ni tsii nɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or mild soap water stops these insects from stunting your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea is a legume crop that pulls nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in its roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Black, rotten bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots transport calcium properly into the fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato ni shishigbɛ diŋ lɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds early when my yam vines start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe miihia beni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young yam vines need maximum sunlight and soil nutrients to build big tubers. Weeds shade the vines and steal water during this early growth stage, which reduces the size of your final harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Jwɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa wain tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejuɔ nu yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why do some of my rice plants produce heads with empty grains inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty rice grains happen when plants face drought or extreme sun heat right at the flowering stage, which stops seeds from forming inside the heads.
ga: Nibii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo hɔmɔ loo hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui ni baa bulb lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it up. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves (mulch) keeps roots cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Mulch) shwie tsei ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to stay healthy and grow. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away or if the soil stays waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil retains too much water without proper drainage. Wet conditions allow harmful fungal water molds to attack the buried tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ haa nu mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni afu lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut flower stems push themselves into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but once pollinated, the plant stems naturally grow downward into the soil. This buries the seed pod so the peanut can develop safely underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee lɛ pollination lɛ, tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ futuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in direct sunlight to make energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent leaf diseases and gives you bigger tubers at harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni akafoliar hela aba ni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba kɛji akpa.

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) creates competition for water and food. Pruning back excess shoots so only two or three remain ensures the mother plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo (tsobii) lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eshi tsei 2-3 pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso nyɛ lɛ awo ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are naturally sensitive to harsh sunlight and high heat. Big shade trees protect young cocoa leaves from sun damage and keep the soil moist during dry seasons.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei wuji haa hɔɔŋ ni amɛbuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their blossoms without making any peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms as a survival mechanism when temperatures get too high or soil becomes too dry, preventing the plant from wasting energy when it is stressed.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei akafite hewalɛ kɛ́ amɛmiihao.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers dry up and fall off the tree trunks without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when they are not pollinated by tiny forest insects, or when sap-sucking pests like capsids damage the flower stalks.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ koo bibioo lɛ mli lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ nu, tamɔ capsids lɛ kpata fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up into tight cups and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny whiteflies carrying a virus from plant to plant, or by severe hot weather and water stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli loo kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu mli haomɔ mli.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hidden inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee kone mli?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars eat the soft center leaf funnel where they are hidden from sun and rain.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ wui yɛ baai anɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, he ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hulu kɛ nugbɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cassava using stem cuttings instead of planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmei kɛjɛ ŋmeii amli moŋ fe dumɔwui?

english: Cassava stem cuttings sprout much faster and grow into plants that carry the exact good qualities of the parent crop, whereas seeds grow slowly and give unpredictable crop yields.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afolɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni hiɛ sui kpakpai tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ.

english: Is it healthy for my soil to replant cassava in the exact same spot immediately after harvesting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Replanting the same crop continuously in the exact same spot drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop diseases build up in the soil. Rotating crops gives the land time to recover.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba shi. ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ahe helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut for planting my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from disease-free plants that are 8 to 18 months old, using the strong middle portion of the stem for the highest chance of successful sprouting.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela bɛ amɛhe ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ amli, ni okɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii koni ená hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it so physically difficult to dig up my cassava tubers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi ni atsa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni wa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ lɛ?

english: During dry weather, the soil loses moisture and bakes hard like clay around the roots, making harvesting tough labor and often breaking tubers underground unless soil is softened with water.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ewaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa anyɛɔ akpaa nitsumɔ ni wa. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ja nu eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli efee blɛoo.

english: Why does my farmland produce lower crop yields today compared to how it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Continuous farming year after year without resting the land or adding nutrients drains essential minerals from the soil, causing the land's natural crop-producing strength to decline over time.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔɔ loo akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he lɛ haa sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has become weak or sick before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo hela mɔ lɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Signs of exhausted soil include yellowing leaves on young plants, slow crop growth, soil that forms a hard crust when dry, and water washing away soil easily after light rain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ ahe ji baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ. tso lɛ daalɛ blɛoo Shikpɔŋ ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa kɛji egbi. Ni nu baaho shikpɔŋ lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ.

english: What basic steps can I take to bring nutrients back into tired farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee koni mikɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni etɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore soil vitality by adding compost or animal manure, planting leguminous cover crops like beans that fix nitrogen into the ground, or allowing sections of land to rest.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. aloo ha he ko ahi shi ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe

english: Why do old cocoa trees eventually stop bearing as many pods as they did when young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 30 years, their natural productivity drops due to aging roots, accumulated soil pest pressures, and declining nutrient absorption from old soil.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ewoɔ lɛ baa shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ hewalɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ sũ momo mli lɛ baa shi

english: How can keeping cattle on or near my farm help my crop fields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsinai ni mikwɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cattle produce rich manure that can be collected and mixed into crop soil as natural fertilizer, returning vital organic matter and nutrients that make food crops grow much stronger.
ga: Tsinai woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni abaanyɛ abua naa ni akɛfutu tsei ashishi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa niyenii tsei lɛ daraa waa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly during short breaks in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hejɔɔmɔ kuku ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil lacks organic matter, it loses its ability to hold onto water like a sponge, causing crop roots to run dry and wilt soon after rain stops falling.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ Ebaafee nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaahiɛ nu mli tamɔ sponji lɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ekpa.

english: Why do some farmers build plastic house structures over their vegetable crops instead of planting directly in the open soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa plastic tsũi ni akɛwoɔ amɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: These plastic structures, called greenhouses, protect sensitive crops like tomatoes and peppers from heavy rains, harsh sun, and pests, allowing you to grow healthy vegetables all year round.
ga: Atsɛɔ plastic tsũi nɛɛ akɛ greenhouses. Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni oduɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Won't crops heat up and burn inside a plastic greenhouse under our hot Ghanaian sun?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edɔɔɔ ni amɛshãaa yɛ plastic ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ wɔ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: Greenhouses are built with side vents and special shade nets that allow hot air to escape while keeping moisture inside, creating a warm, humid environment that many vegetables love.
ga: Akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ be mli ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ mli lɛ maa tsũi ni mli tse lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni aduawai babaoo sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: If I read farming instructions from a foreign book, can I apply them directly to my farm in Ghana without changing anything?
ga: Kɛ mikane okwaayeli he ŋaawoi kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ wolo ko mli Ani manyɛ mikɛtsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli ni mitsakeee nɔ ko nɔ ko?

english: Foreign farming books give good starting ideas, but our tropical heat and soil are different, so you often need to adapt those guidelines to fit local conditions through careful practice.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ okwaayeli he woji haa shishijee susumɔi kpakpai. Shi dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ wɔ hulutsoo shikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ ehe hiaa ni atsake nakai nifeemɔi lɛ kɛya shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ nifeemɔi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some foreign tomato seed varieties fail to yield properly when planted directly in my outdoor field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ wooo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ mi kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Many foreign seed varieties are bred for cooler climates and struggle with local outdoor heat and pests, meaning they perform much better when grown inside a protected structure like a greenhouse.
ga: Akwɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui babaoo kɛha hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli ejɔ. ni ehe bahia ni ekɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akpee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he, tamɔ greenhouse.

english: Should I wait until I have full master training before trying a new crop growing technique on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi maná master tsɔsemɔ dani maka ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he ŋaa hee ko makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, farming knowledge grows best by starting small; you can test new methods on a small patch of land, learn from what happens, and make improvements as you expand.
ga: Dabi, okwaayeli he nilee yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ shishijee bibioo nɔ. Obaanyɛ oka gbɛi heei okwɛ. yɛ he bibioo ko nɔ Kasemɔ nii kɛjɛ nɔ ni ba lɛ mli ni ofee tsakemɔi beni ogbɛɔ onitsumɔ lɛ mli oshwaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a new growing method I am testing is actually working for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji gbɛ hee ni mikaa mikwɛɔ lɛ baatsu nii diɛŋtsɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Observe the crop's daily behavior; healthy growth is shown by deep green leaves, steady flowering, and strong stems, while yellowing leaves or wilting signal that you need to adjust your approach.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa daa gbi lɛ. Nɔ ni tsɔɔ dalɛ kpakpa ji baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. fɔfɔii ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ tso ni mli wa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni otsake gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ otsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do crops grown under plastic covers seem to require water differently than crops in open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plastic shishi lɛ he hiaa nu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: In an enclosed space, water does not evaporate as quickly from the soil into the air, keeping the root area moist for longer and reducing how often you need to water.
ga: Yɛ hei ni afo mli lɛ, nu lɛ shwieee oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni ajie nu ni akɛhaa shii abɔ lɛ shi

english: Why do greenhouse tomatoes produce fruits for many more months than those planted out in the open rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii nyɔji babaoo fe tomatoi ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Protecting flowers from being knocked off by heavy rains and keeping soil moisture steady allows the tomato plant to continuously bloom and set fruit over an extended period.
ga: Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Do crops grown under plastic covers completely avoid insect attacks and diseases?
ga: Ani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ plastic shishi lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ helai ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe kwraa?

english: While greenhouse nets block big pests, tiny insects can still enter, and because the enclosed air is warm and humid, diseases can spread fast if you do not check your plants daily.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ greenhouse netting baanyɛ aha kooloi wuji akabote mli moŋ, Shi kooloi bibii baanyɛ aba mli lolo Ni akɛni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli edɔɔ ni edɔ hewɔ lɛ, helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛji okwɛɛɛ otsei lɛ amli daa gbi.

english: Is it fine to build a simple greenhouse using local wooden poles instead of expensive imported metal frames?
ga: Te aaafee ama ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei baatsu nii moŋ fe dade ni jara wa ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ?

english: Yes, using strong local timber with proper farming plastic works well and lets you test and learn protected farming at a much lower starting cost.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni wa ni akɛ ŋmɔ mli plastic ni sa tsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa onyɛɔ okaa okwaayeli ni abuɔ he lɛ okwɛɔ ni okaseɔ yɛ shishijee nyɔmɔwoo ni baa shi kwraa mli.

english: Why do some crops need to start in a nursery before I plant them on my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aje tsei komɛi ashishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seeds are very fragile when they first sprout. A nursery protects them from harsh sun, heavy rains, and pests until their roots become strong enough to survive out in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa kwraa kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. He ni amɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do my young plants look weak and droopy right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. When seedlings are uprooted, their tiny roots get disturbed and struggle to absorb water for the first few days until they adjust to the new soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Kɛji ajie dumɔwui lɛ, amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ gbaa naa ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmu nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli kɛyashi amɛbaatsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young transplanted seedlings need shade during their first few weeks in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii ni adu amɛ lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and thin leaves that lose water very quickly in full sun. Shade keeps them cool and conserves moisture while their roots grow deeper into the ground.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo shɛ amɛhe. Shade lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: What does it actually mean when someone calls a crop seedling a 'hybrid'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mɛi tsɛ tsei amli dumɔwui akɛ ‘hybrid’?

english: A hybrid crop is bred by combining two different strong parent plants to get the best qualities of both, such as producing more yield, growing faster, or resisting diseases better than traditional varieties.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni ji hybrid lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni he wa ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ nɔ koni anyɛ ana tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ahe sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. shwereɔ oya loo enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai jogbaŋŋ fe blema tsofai srɔtoi lɛ

english: Can I save the seeds from my hybrid crop harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended because seeds saved from hybrid plants do not grow true to the parent plant. They usually result in lower yields and unpredictable plant behavior, so fresh hybrid seeds or nursed seedlings should be used each season.
ga: Akɛ enɛ etsɔɔɔ ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ edaaa tamɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ tsei asu ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome loo dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do hybrid crops usually mature faster than our traditional local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya fe wɔmaŋ tsei lɛ?

english: Hybrid varieties are specifically developed to use soil nutrients and sunlight more efficiently, allowing them to grow faster, flower earlier, and produce fruits in a shorter amount of time.
ga: Afee tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni edaa oya, ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Are hybrid crops completely protected from all pests and plant diseases?
ga: Ani abuɔ tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ ahe kwraa kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai fɛɛ ahe?

english: Hybrids are bred to resist common diseases better than local varieties, but they are not completely immune. They still need good weeding, proper watering, and regular monitoring to stay healthy.
ga: Afɔ tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai krokomɛi koni amɛnyɛ amɛye helai ni afɔɔ namɔ anɔ fe tsofai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Shi amɛjeee mɛi ni yeɔ amɛhe kwraa. Ehe miihia ni amɛjie jwɛi kpakpai hu. Nu ni sa kɛ kwɛmɔ daa kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa

english: How do I know if a new crop variety brought to our region will grow well in my soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ni akɛba wɔkpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops perform well when the local soil type, rainfall, and temperature match their preferred conditions. Trying a small plot first helps you see how well the plant adapts to your farm's local environment.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa kɛ shihilɛi ni ataoɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni akɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko atsu nii Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona bɔ ni tsei lɛ etsake amɛhe amɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli shihilɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to crop behavior if I plant my seedlings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui ahe subaŋ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight for the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block light from each other. This causes plants to grow tall, thin, and yield fewer fruits.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why is it important to loosen the soil before putting my new seedlings into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akɛ dumɔwui heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil creates air pockets and softens the earth, making it easy for delicate young roots to spread out deep and absorb water and nutrients quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya.

english: Why do my maize plants produce leaves but no actual corn cobs at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ baai shi ebɛ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants need adequate nitrogen and water, especially during the flowering stage, to produce cobs. Poor soil fertility, severe dry spells, or planting too close together causes the plants to become stressed and fail to form cobs.
ga: Abɛi biɔ nitrogen kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Titri lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli koni ekɛ cob aba. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa Aloo amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni efeee ŋmei.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your soil is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is logging the roots and preventing the crop from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu miibote shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩ tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting maize on the same piece of land every year result in smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply and live permanently in your farm's soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ ni amɛhiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: What causes tiny worms to eat up my young maize leaves overnight, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome. Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: This destruction is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a fast-spreading pest. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts when the plants are young helps stop them before they ruin the entire field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite jɛmɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do insects destroy my stored maize even after I have successfully harvested it from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ omanyeyeli mli moŋ?

english: Storage insects like grain weevils attack corn that is stored with too much moisture or in open containers. Drying your maize completely until the grains are hard and using airtight storage bags prevents pests from breeding.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ ahe kooloi tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmaa ni akɛto yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli loo yɛ tsɛnsii ni agbele mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa, ni akɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ehaaa ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, crowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants weak with small stalks and tiny or missing cobs. Proper spacing yields bigger, healthier crops.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii, loo elaajeɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my previous harvest perform worse than the seeds I buy from certified dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred hybrids designed for high yield and disease resistance. The seeds saved from your harvested crops lose these special qualities in the next generation, leading to weaker growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpaa lɛ amli lɛ baafite nɛkɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Can I grow cassava on the same plot of land with my maize without damaging either crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni mifiteee ŋmãa enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows and matures quickly before the cassava grows large enough to block the sunlight and take over the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ oya dani ŋmãa lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up even when rain falls a few days after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: If the soil lacks organic matter, it cannot hold water for long during hot days between rains. Adding animal manure or compost helps the soil trap moisture longer to keep young roots alive.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, enyɛŋ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough soil conditions and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks gives your crops a fair chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry up when there are no bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without larger shade trees or plantains to block the harsh sun, the young leaves get sunburned, lose moisture quickly, and dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei wuji ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ. Efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya ni egbiɔ

english: Yam plants need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for their leaves to produce energy. Keeping the leaves off the ground also prevents rotting and helps the plant send energy down to form large tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛbaai lɛ aná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no hu haaa egbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall bushes with lots of leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that nitrogen stays in the earth to feed whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha nɔ ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops produce much smaller yields if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously sucks out the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year while allowing specific pests and crop diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to tomato plants, making the flowers drop off before pollen can fertilize them to produce fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look weak in the hot afternoon even if the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Drooping is a survival defense that reduces leaf surface exposure to the sun until the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Defoliation ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ wala he ni haa baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i baa shi.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from under the leaves, or by viral sicknesses spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why does my plantain tree take so long to yield fruit when I allow all the small shoots to grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ? Beni mihaa tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small suckers growing around the main plantain stem steal water and food away from the mother tree. Removing most suckers and leaving just one allows the main stem to flower faster and bear larger bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɔleɔ Plantain tso titri lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmei lɛ fã ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ashi eko pɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei titri lɛ afɔ oya ni ekɛ fɔfɔii akui wuji aba.

english: What crops can I plant directly under my coconut trees to get extra food and income?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmei tso shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni maná niyenii kɛ shika kroko?

english: You can plant shade-tolerant crops like ginger, pineapple, cassava, or cocoa under mature coconut palms because the open canopy lets in filtered light while protecting lower crops from excessive heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei loo kookoo yɛ ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ ashishi. Ejaakɛ ŋwɛitsu ni agbele lɛ haa la boteɔ mli, ni yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why do some small crops grow better when planted in the shade of taller trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ekomɛi daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi lɛ?

english: Tall trees create a favorable microclimate by lowering ground temperature, reducing soil water evaporation, and protecting delicate young plants from harsh direct sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa ni baa shi lɛ nɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he.

english: Is it beneficial to plant multiple species of crops together on the same land?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ ko yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛaakwɛ he kome yɛ he kome lɛ he?

english: Yes, mixing crop species improves soil health, prevents the rapid spread of pests, and ensures you have different sources of food and income throughout the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afɔɔ amɛbii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ naa. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oná niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhei srɔtoi yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning a reddish or purple color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ tsuru loo purple lɛ?

english: Reddish or purplish leaves usually signal a phosphorus deficiency in the soil, which prevents plants from developing strong roots and transferring energy efficiently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai tsuru loo ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tsei aná shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛkatsɔ hewalɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the edges of my crop leaves to turn red or brown and dry up?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ?

english: Red or brown leaf edges are often caused by potassium deficiency or severe drought stress, showing that the plant is struggling to manage its internal water levels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, potassium ni faaa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Healthy cocoa pods change color as they ripen, turning from green or dark purple to a vibrant yellow or reddish-orange, indicating the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: How does covering my farm soil with dead leaves or straw help my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi loo jwɛi shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Mulching creates a cool, protective layer over the soil that slows down water evaporation, stops weeds from taking over, and breaks down into organic food for your crops.
ga: Mulching haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ blɛoo. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛha onibii.

english: Why do my crops wilt quickly during the afternoon heat even if I watered them earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ shwane mli mra eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli mra moŋ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes plants to lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it up from hot soil; shading the soil and retaining moisture helps prevent this heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akatsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa.

english: Do coconut trees take away all the nutrients from small plants growing nearby?
ga: Kokoo tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ani fɛɛ etee loo etee?

english: Coconut trees have deep root networks that feed lower in the soil, but you should still add compost or fertilizer near smaller plants so they do not compete for surface nutrients.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata tsei bibii ahe lolo. Bɔni afee ni akatswa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do tree crops like coconut or oil palm take several years before they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmei kɛ mu tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Perennial tree crops focus their early energy on growing strong root systems and sturdy trunks first so they can support heavy harvests later in their life.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ kɛ amɛ mra be mli hewalɛ lɛ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the center or bottom of the plant, usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build strong green leaves and grow well.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ loo shishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller every year if I plant it on the same farm plot?
