ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava repeatedly on the same land without adding compost or fertilizer drains the soil's natural nutrients, leaving less food for the roots to grow large tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aná kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ faaa.

english: How do crops like cowpea or groundnut help make my farm soil richer?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni efee nii babaoo eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the plant leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ tso baai amli nu lɛ

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod Disease, which spreads quickly in dark, wet, and overly shaded cocoa farms during the rainy season.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni efɔ, ni hulu enyɔ shi fe nine lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the stem without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfeee pod lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, lack sufficient water or nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny pollinating insects in the field.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollin lɛ yɔɔ Nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop making fresh peppers when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei feemɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and the air becomes dry, pepper plants drop their flowers to conserve water and survive, preventing new fruit from forming.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi. Koni yibii heei akafee

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often because the soil dried out too much between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around my plantain trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantains lɛ ahe lɛ eje kpo.

english: Removing excess shoots (suckers) ensures the main plantain stem gets all the water and soil nutrients required to produce a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa plantain tso titri lɛ naa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to direct sunlight so they can produce food for the tubers underneath, while keeping the leaves away from wet soil that harbors rot.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni egbo lɛ he.

english: How can I protect my crop farm from wild animals like monkeys and birds that keep eating my harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ koo mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ okpoi ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Installing scarecrows, physical fencing, or planting border crops like hot chili peppers around your field deters pests and wildlife. The sharp smell and heat of peppers discourage animals like monkeys from entering your main crop area.
ga: Nibii ni haa mɔ he feɔ gbeyei, gbogboi, loo husu tsei tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔji ahe lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ koo mli kooloi akabote mli. Chili ŋmeii lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ haaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii abote he titri ni otsuɔ okwaayeli nii yɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my newly planted young cocoa trees burning and turning brown in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mikoo tso ni midu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ shãa ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily under full direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective living canopy that shelters them from severe sun heat during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli dɔlɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: As a beginner farmer, how do I know if my land has good soil for planting cassava?
ga: Ákɛ okwaafonyo hee lɛ Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmei?

english: Good cassava soil should feel loose, light, and sandy-loam so roots can swell into tubers easily. Heavy clay soil that stays flooded during rains will trap water and cause cassava roots to rot underground.
ga: Esa akɛ cassava shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ŋã yɔɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ bulbs. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen shortage in the soil. Maize plants move stored nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed young growing leaves at the top when soil nutrients run low.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ faaa.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas on the same piece of land alongside my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize improves soil quality. Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the neighboring maize plants while suppressing weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo. Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme temperatures, poor soil moisture, or heavy rains that wash away pollen. Keeping soil evenly moist with mulch helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many green leaves but forming tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to direct all its energy into growing thick stems and lush leaves instead of storing energy underground to form large, starch-rich tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe kɛ baai ni etse lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ toɔ zugba sisi konɛ a kɛ pee tso nguanguahi nɛ a mi mi ɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil and germinate quickly as soon as clearing exposes them to sunlight and rain. Weeds grow fast because they adapt quickly to bare soil, competing with crops for light and nutrients.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui fuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni atse lɛ pɛ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ejaakɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ oya. ni amɛkɛ tsei akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my maize seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait to plant maize seeds until after two or three deep, consecutive rainfall events. Sowing after just the first light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a dry spell follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni odu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are some of my plantain suckers failing to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-banana tsei lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers may fail to sprout if they were damaged by soil pests like root nematodes before planting, or if old roots were not peeled off to encourage fresh root shoots to grow.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ fite amɛ dani adu. Aloo kɛji ajieee shishifãi momoi lɛ koni shishifãi heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important to leave enough space between my crops when planting instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ bɔ ni sa kɛ́ midu nii moŋ fe ni makɛ amɛ abɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, diseases can easily jump from an infected plant to a healthy neighboring plant through contact or air moisture. Proper spacing also ensures each plant receives adequate sunlight, airflow, and soil nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, helai baanyɛ ajɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ hu haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ waa

english: If I notice sick or spotted leaves on one of my crops, should I cut them off or leave them alone?
ga: Kɛji mina baai ni hela mɔ amɛ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko nɔ Ani Esa akɛ mafo mli loo mashi lɛ?

english: You should cut off sick leaves immediately and take them away from your farm. Leaving infected leaves on the crop allows the sickness to spread to the healthy parts of the plant and to neighboring crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ helatsɛmɛi ahe baai amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ojie kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that excessive rain is suffocating the roots. Adding proper fertilizer or compost helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants look twisted and patchy with yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. As these insects fly from plant to plant feeding on sap, they transfer the virus to healthy cassava crops.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Enɛ ji akɛ, kooloi nɛɛ foɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkɛ hela lɛ yaa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp weather. Raindrops splash soil and fungal spores onto lower pods, causing them to rot quickly if the farm is too shady or unpruned.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ sũ kɛ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo afolɔko ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What causes the ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: These holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the tender leaves and growing tip of the plant. Inspecting your field early allows you to treat them before they destroy the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii kɛ amɛyitsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when the soil is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: On hot days, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up from the ground. It can also mean underground root rot is preventing the roots from absorbing available water.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekolɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ shishifãi ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow, small, and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to survive. When weeds surround your crops, they choke the plants and rob them of essential nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle onibii ahe lɛ Ehaa egbɔjɔɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to cut stem cuttings from my old cassava farm to start a new field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maŋɔ tsei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo ko mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: If your old cassava plants carried hidden viruses or pests, using those stems will transfer the disease straight into your new farm. It is best to use certified disease-free stem cuttings for a clean start.
ga: Kɛji o-cassava tsei momo lɛ yɛ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ Nakai tsei lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tso lɛ mli tsei ni hela bɛ mli ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ baatsu nii kɛha shishijee ni he tse.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil where the roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow huge vines with plenty of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ wain tso agbo ko ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes bean plants to focus all their energy on growing tall leaves instead of forming flowers and pods. Beans need balanced nutrients and enough sunshine to produce good yields.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai kakadaŋŋ agboi anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Niyenii ni sa kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmeii koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my cocoa seedling leaves get scorched and turn brown in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need living shade from taller crops like plantains to shelter them and keep the surrounding soil moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the soil is too dry or when the afternoon heat is too high. Without adequate water, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism tomato plants use to keep water from escaping their leaves during hot, dry periods. Once watered or when the afternoon heat cools down, the leaves usually stretch back out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni nu akaje baai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. kɛji akɛ ashɛreɔ nu loo beni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Baai lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboi dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining. Heavy rains combined with hard soil choke the underground roots, allowing soil fungi to infect and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. nu ni hoɔ bɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa fataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn black and wither before the tubers grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani bulbs lɛ miida lɛ?

english: This early drying of yam leaves is often caused by a fungal infection called Anthracnose, which spreads rapidly during hot and rainy weather, stopping the plant from making food for the tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ gbiɔ oya. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain plants falling over on their own even when there is no wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are often eaten underground by tiny pests called nematodes or banana weevils. When roots are destroyed, the plant loses its anchor in the soil and falls over under its own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii yeɔ plantain shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ laajeɔ eshishitoo mla lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbeeɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my okra plants getting sticky with white spots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi gumbo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Sticky okra leaves are caused by tiny pests called whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and secrete a sugary substance. This weakens the plant and lowers fruit production.
ga: Okra baai ni wa lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛbaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni shwieɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni ejieɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sugar mli lɛ kpo Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibii ni ewoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my soil become hard and cracked like stone after harvesting my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa tamɔ tɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Exposing bare soil directly to intense sunlight dries out organic matter and bakes the earth. Leaving crop residue like corn stalks on top of the soil helps shade it and keep it soft and moist.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ agbi ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni edɔ.

english: Why are the rainy seasons in my region starting later than they used to in past years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ fe bɔ ni ebɔi yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weather patterns across Ghana are shifting over time due to climate changes. This means rains no longer follow traditional schedules, so planting times must be based on actual weather updates rather than old calendar dates.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ miitsake yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ nyiɛɛɛ kusum gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ sɛɛ dɔŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ dumɔ bei lɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi diɛŋtsɛ anɔ moŋ fe kusum kalanda gbii.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds when the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives two or three steady rains and stays damp beneath the surface. Planting immediately after the very first light rain is risky because the weather might stay dry afterward and ruin your seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shihilɛi baanyɛ agbi yɛ sɛɛ mli ni efite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves curling up and turning yellow during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating too quickly when the sun is hot and the soil is dry.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a fully cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to shield them from intense heat while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dried leaves or grass around my crop roots help them during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Covering the ground around your plants with organic mulch acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and preserving moisture in the earth longer.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What crops can I plant if I expect the rains to end earlier than usual this season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu kɛji akɛ akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ lɛ baagbe naa mra fe bɔ ni eji daa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Fast-maturing and drought-tolerant crops like cowpeas, sorghum, or early-maturing cassava are best because they require less overall rainfall to mature fully.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛbiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni fa fioo dani amɛshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Should I keep planting seeds saved from my previous harvest or buy certified seeds from extension officers?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato loo mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: Certified seeds are bred to handle current weather challenges, heat stress, and local pests better than traditional saved seeds, leading to higher crop yields.
ga: Afɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛkɛtsu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he naagbai ahe nii. hulutsoo he haomɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hi fe blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why is my farm producing fewer crops each year even though I farm the same way my parents did?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mifeɔ okwaayeli tamɔ bɔ ni mifɔlɔi fee lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: Continuous farming exhausts natural soil nutrients, and rising temperatures dry out the land faster. Modern soil care, like crop rotation and adding organic manure, is needed to restore soil fertility.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Ni hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli Ehe miihia ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why am I seeing more pests like armyworms eating my crops during warm, dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi tamɔ armyworms ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ otsii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Warmer weather speeds up the life cycle of many field pests, causing them to reproduce faster and attack crops in larger numbers during dry periods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔ mli kooloi babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ aya hiɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ oya ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting leguminous crops like beans alongside my main crops help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the soil, acting like natural fertilizer that nourishes neighboring crops while covering the ground to prevent weeds.
ga: Legumes jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ahe nibii ni baa lɛ hewalɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ekɛ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni jwɛi akabote mli.

english: Which crops can I plant on my farm if I need to harvest and get money in just three or four months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa ni maná shika yɛ nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ pɛ mli.

english: Short-term crops like maize, tomatoes, pepper, and beans complete their life cycle fast, allowing you to harvest and earn income within three to four months of planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, tomato, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa oya. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii ni onáa shika yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ be mli ni odu nii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant a long-term tree crop when it takes years before I can harvest anything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei kɛha be kakadaŋŋ be mli ni eheɔ afii babaoo dani anyɛɔ akpaa nɔ ko?

english: While short-term crops give quick money once, long-term tree crops like cocoa or cashew require waiting a few years but will yield harvests every year for several decades once they mature.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii baaha oná shika oya shikome pɛ moŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo cashew amɛmɛ afii fioo komɛi. Shi ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii daa afi kɛyashi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the first two or three years of planting tree crops so difficult for me on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa kɛha mi akɛ madu tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ?

english: In the first few years, young seedlings have small roots and weak stems, requiring constant watering, weeding, and protection from sun and pests until their root system is established.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baaná shishifãi bibii kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Esa akɛ afɔ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be, ajie jwɛi, ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: What happens to my long-term crop if I neglect it during its first two years of growth?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ anɔ kɛji miku mihiɛ mishwie nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni mikɛbaakwɛ nii lɛ mli?

english: Neglecting a young crop stunts its growth or kills it, meaning it will either take much longer to produce fruit or fail completely, wasting your initial investment.
ga: Tsei bibii ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ afee mlɛo loo ebaafite. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ebaahe be babaoo dani ewo yibii loo ebaafite kwraa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, shika ni okɛwo mli shishijee lɛ baafee yaka.

english: Why do my young seedlings struggle and die during the dry season while older trees survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Young plants have short roots near the dry soil surface, whereas older trees have deep taproots that reach subterranean water underground during hot weather.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Is it true that my tree crop farm will require much less daily work after it gets older?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ mi tso ŋmɔ lɛ baabi daa gbi nitsumɔ fioo ko kwraa beni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, as trees mature, their wide canopy blocks sunlight from reaching the ground—naturally preventing weeds from growing and reducing your daily work.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, enɛ baatsi jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebaaha onitsumɔ ni otsuɔ daa gbi lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast around my young crops compared to mature tree farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi tsei bibii lɛ miida oya waa kɛ akɛto tsei ni eda lɛ aŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Young crops are small and leave open space for direct sunlight to hit the soil, which encourages fast weed growth until the crops grow big enough to shade the ground.
ga: Atoɔ dumɔwui lɛ bibii ni ashiɔ amɛ koni hulu la ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ woɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when a crop I plant today will actually start giving me income in the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ baaje shishi diɛŋtsɛ ekɛ shika aba mihe wɔsɛɛ?

english: Every crop has a specific maturity period; fast crops yield in months, while hybrid tree crops usually take two to three years before producing their first harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni ekɛdaa. Nibii ni aduɔ oya lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ heɔ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani amɛkpaa amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ.

english: How can I survive financially during the first three years while waiting for my tree crop to mature?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahi shi yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ tso lɛ ni eda lɛ?

english: You can practice intercropping by planting short-term food crops like plantain, cassava, or legumes in between young trees to provide food and income while waiting for the main crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛyeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains, cassava loo legumes ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika aha yɛ be mli ni emɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ.

english: Why is long-term crop farming described as something that requires advance planning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ kɛ́ oodu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Long-term crops require you to invest money, time, and land care for several years without income before you see your harvest, requiring you to budget for your living expenses in the meantime.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ biɔ ni okɛ shika, be, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ awo mli afii babaoo ni shika ko bɛ mli dani ona yibiiwoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ onɔ ni oto shika he gbɛjianɔ kɛha shihilɛ mli nyɔmɔwoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Why are so many farmers in Ghana choosing to plant rice instead of maize these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miihala akɛ amɛbaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa najiaŋ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Rice has become one of the most eaten staple foods in Ghanaian homes every day. Because local demand is so high, farmers who grow rice can easily find buyers and earn a steady income compared to crops with smaller markets.
ga: Omɔ ebatsɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghanabii ashiai amli daa gbi lɛ ateŋ ekome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa waa. Omɔ okwaafoi baanyɛ ana mɛi ni baahe lɛ oya ni amɛná shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my farmland is better suited for growing rice or growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔ?

english: Maize prefers well-drained upland soil where water flows away easily. Rice, on the other hand, grows best in low-lying valley areas or clay soils that hold water and stay moist for long periods.
ga: Abɛi sumɔɔ delta shikpɔji ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli oya lɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishi loo shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hiɛɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: How can I get support or certified seeds if I want to start a new crop farm this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yelikɛbuamɔ loo dumɔwui ni awo he odase? Kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ hee yɛ be nɛɛ mli

english: You can join a recognized local farmer group or approach agricultural extension officers before the planting season starts. They connect farmers to government programs and outgrower schemes that provide quality seeds, fertilizers, and technical guidance.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyafata okwaafoi akuu ko ni ato ama shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ he loo okɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ko abɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Amɛkɛ okwaafoi tsaa nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛlɔi agbɛjianɔtoi ni haa dumɔwui ni hi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋaa ŋaawoo.

english: Why shouldn't I just save grains from my eating supply to use as seeds for planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mibuaa dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛɔ mi niyenii lɛ mli koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Grains meant for eating often have low germination rates, mixed varieties, or hidden diseases. Certified seeds from extension officers are specifically treated to sprout healthily, resist pests, and produce much higher yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni ayeɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fioo, eji ŋmaa ni efutu, loo eyɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko haa dumɔwui ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Does rice require more water to survive throughout its growth than maize?
ga: Ani ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ yɛ edalɛ be fɛɛ mli fe ŋmãa?

english: Yes, rice naturally requires a continuous supply of moisture, especially during its early growth and flowering stages. Maize can survive on moderate rainfall, but rice plants will stunt or fail if the soil dries out completely.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia ŋmɔtɔ daa. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni edara mra kɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Abɛi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Shi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ loo amɛbaafite kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa.

english: How do I recognize when my maize plants are lacking nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmã lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When maize lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, the lower leaves start turning yellow in a 'V' shape from the tip inward, and the stalk remains thin instead of growing thick and dark green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli etse lolo yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ.

english: Most improved rice varieties in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) to mature, which is very similar to the growth duration of standard maize varieties.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) dani amɛshwereɔ, ni enɛ tamɔ be ni ŋmãa henɔi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do birds attack my rice field much more aggressively than my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ waa fe minɔ lɛ?

english: Rice seeds grow exposed on open heads at the top of the plant, making them an easy target for birds when the grains ripen. Maize grains are protected inside thick husks that birds cannot easily tear open.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ bulbs ni agbele yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa okpoi kɛ́ ŋmaa lɛ ekwɛ̃. Abuɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ahe yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni okpoi nyɛŋ ajie kɛjɛ mli mlɛo lɛ mli.

english: What should I do immediately after harvesting rice to prevent it from spoiling?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ afee koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite?

english: Freshly harvested rice contains high moisture inside the grains. You must thresh and spread the grains out on a clean tarpaulin to dry under the sun immediately so mold and fungi do not rot the crop.
ga: Omɔ ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he ni okɛshwã tarp ni he tse nɔ koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmei kɛ ŋmei akahã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite.

english: When is the correct time to apply fertilizer to my young rice crop so it grows strong?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛhe awa?

english: Apply the first round of fertilizer about 2 weeks after the plants sprout to encourage strong root development, and apply a second boost (nitrogen) when the plants begin to form flower heads inside the stem.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ eje kpo lɛ koni ewo shishifãi ni wa lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Ni okɛ tsofa ni ji enyɔ (nitrogen) afata he beni tso lɛ jeɔ shishi enáa fɔfɔi ayitsei yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specially grown and tested by agricultural experts to ensure high germination rates and freedom from diseases, while seeds saved from previous harvests can carry hidden diseases and produce lower yields over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli lɛ ji nɔ ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi duɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni amɛkaa amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni helai bɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do certified seeds cost more than buying seeds from the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds undergo strict quality control, disease testing, and careful breeding under controlled conditions, ensuring nearly every seed grows into a healthy, high-yielding crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yaa nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa mli, helai akaa kɛ fɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu daa ni etsɔɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: I keep hearing about foundation seeds—what does that mean for a farmer like me?
ga: Miyaa nɔ minuɔ dumɔwui ahe shishitoo he—mɛɛ no ​​tsɔɔ kɛha okwaafoi tamɔ mi?

english: Foundation seed is the pure parent seed produced by plant researchers, which is then grown under strict supervision to produce the certified seeds that farmers buy and plant.
ga: Shishijee dumɔwui ji fɔlɔ dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni tsei ahe niiamlitaolɔi feɔ. ni no sɛɛ lɛ aduɔ yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni ekɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni okwaafoi heɔ ni amɛduɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do some farmers grow their seed plants inside screenhouses instead of out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔji amli moŋ fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Screenhouses act like protective nets that keep harmful insects and harsh weather away from delicate plants, ensuring pure, disease-free seed production.
ga: Filtration plants tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔŋloo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ akaje tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ dumɔwui ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I start my delicate seeds in a sheltered nursery area before moving them to my open farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui ni mli tse lɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, keeping tender young plants in a sheltered nursery protects them from harsh sunlight and heavy rain until they are strong enough to survive open field conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die so quickly if I miss watering them even for one day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji mikɛ nu ha amɛ gbi kome po lɛ?

english: Young plants have tiny, shallow roots that cannot reach water deep in the ground, so missing a single watering causes their soil to dry out and damages the plant fast.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni nyɛŋ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ, nu kome pɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya ni efite tso lɛ.

english: How much water should I give to very small crops in my nursery?
ga: Nu enyiɛ esa akɛ maha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii waa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Very small crops need small, regular amounts of water—just enough to keep the top layer of soil moist without washing away the seeds or drowning the fine roots.
ga: Tsei bibii waa biɔ nu fioo daa. Nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ efɔɔɔ loo ekɛ shishifãi kpakpai lɛ efɔɔɔ nu mli.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are suffering from lack of water before they die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu efo mi dumɔwui lɛ amli dani amɛgboi?

english: Before young plants die, their leaves will start to curl, drop, or turn light green/yellow, and the stems will lose their firmness and begin to bend downward.
ga: Dani tso bibioo lɛ baagbo Ebaai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaagbee shi, loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ/ŋmɔŋ. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ebɔi shwiemɔ kɛmiiya shi.

english: How do I know when my seed crops have reached full maturity?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Crops show maturity when the foliage begins to dry or turn yellow naturally, seeds become firm and fully formed, and the plant reaches the end of its growing cycle.
ga: Tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ mli eyi obɔ ni efee kwraa. ni tso lɛ gbeɔ edalɛ be lɛ naa.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my crops after they mature in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ shwie shi beni amɛdara yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the open field exposes them to weather damage, insect attack, molding, and seed dropping, which significantly reduces the quality of your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi fiteɔ amɛ, kooloi baatutuaa amɛ, amɛbaafee ŋmeii, ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ aba shi waa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that cools the plants and holds moisture in the soil until the trees are mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce food for the crop. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and helping the plant grow much larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ajieɔ staking kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of a maize plant usually show that the soil is running out of nitrogen. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to shrink their surface area under high heat, which prevents water from evaporating too fast. As long as they uncurl in the evening, it is a normal defense behavior against heat stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhiɛ he lɛ afee bibioo kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Eji subaŋ ni sa akɛ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain stays trapped around roots in clay or flat ground, it starves the tubers of oxygen and invites soil fungi to grow. Planting cassava on raised mounds helps water drain away safely.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ sũ mli loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Nugbɔ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oxygen concentrators ni efɔ̃ɔ sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ nine koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Will planting groundnuts between my maize rows help or harm my crop yield?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Groundnuts actually help maize because they pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and manure meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your crops to consume all available food without fighting for it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ amɛ awuu.

english: How do I prevent rain from washing away the fertilizer I apply to my vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a gentle rain rather than right before heavy downpours, and bury it slightly under a small layer of soil near the root zone.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. ni efu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko shishi ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he fioo

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves with powdery dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni muji ko ni tamɔ powder yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage comes from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the plant to feed on fresh growth. Spraying recommended treatments early into the crop leaf funnel controls them.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ amli. Mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli mra ni awo he ŋaa lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ nakai tsofai lɛ.

english: Why do maize seeds saved from last year's harvest yield much smaller cobs than the seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii kwraa fe dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong single-season performance. Seeds collected from hybrid plants lose that vigor in the next generation, producing weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha nitsumɔ ni mli wa yɛ be kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my mango trees produce plenty of flowers, but no fruits actually grow afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi no sɛɛ lɛ efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi kwraa lɛ?

english: When the weather becomes unusually dry or warm during the flowering period, the tree gets stressed. It can still put out flowers, but without enough water and stable weather, those flowers dry up and drop off instead of forming fruits.
ga: Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi loo edɔɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Tso lɛ baahao. Ebaanyɛ efɔ fɔfɔi hu. Shi kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɛ lɛ, Nakai fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops shed their flowers as soon as the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa pɛ?

english: Crops need steady moisture to turn flowers into fruit. When rainfall stops abruptly, the plant enters survival mode and drops its flowers to save water rather than using energy to grow crop fruits.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛtsake fɔfɔi amɛwo yibii. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baaya wala shihilɛ mli ni amɛjie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How does intense sunshine and hot weather affect my maize crop when it is growing?
ga: Te hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaná mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Excessive heat dries out the soil moisture quickly and can damage the maize pollen before it fertilizes the plant. If the sun is too harsh during this period, the cob may end up empty or missing kernels.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli egbiɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmãa mli nu lɛ dani ebaanyɛ ekɛ tso lɛ awo ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛji hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli Ekolɛ cob dumɔwui lɛ etee loo elaaje.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds in the exact same month I used to plant years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ nyɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ni midu afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Weather patterns in Ghana have shifted over time, meaning the rainy season can start earlier or later than before. Sticking strictly to old planting calendars might cause your young seeds to face early dry spells.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe tsutsu lɛ. Kalanda momo ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ nɔ ni oooye nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha odumɔwui bibii lɛ akpee hulutsoo be oya.

english: Why do small fruits fall off my trees before they get a chance to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso yibii lɛ baagbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Fruit dropping happens when a tree faces sudden heat stress, poor soil nutrients, or lack of rain. The tree sheds extra fruits because it does not have enough water or energy to sustain them all.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ. Tsei woɔ yibii babaoo ejaakɛ amɛbɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛhi shi kwraa.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist when the hot season lasts longer than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ mli?

english: You can place dry grass, leaves, or crop remnants on top of the soil around your plants, a practice called mulching. This shades the soil, keeps it cool, and traps moisture so your crops survive hot spells longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebaaha edɔ, ni eha ŋmɔlɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my young crops grow better under the shade of bigger trees during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Young crops can easily burn and lose moisture under full sun. Shade trees block the harshest sunlight, lower the surrounding air temperature, and keep the soil from drying out too fast.
ga: Tsei bibii baanyɛ ashã oya ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ

english: What happens to my vegetable garden if heavy rains fall while the plants are in bloom?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Heavy, hard rainfall can physically knock delicate flowers off the plants and wash away pollen, preventing the plants from successfully making fruits and seeds.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ atswa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii kɛ dumɔwui yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and hard when the weather is very hot for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants store extra water and food in their underground roots to make them swell. During prolonged hot weather, the plant uses all its strength just to keep its leaves alive, leaving nothing to expand the tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo toɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛfuu. Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi. Ni nɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ ni baaha yitso lɛ mli alɛɛ

english: How can I tell if my crops are struggling because of heat and dry weather rather than a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitswa amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi ahewɔ shi jeee tsei ahela?

english: Weather stress usually affects your entire field at the same time, causing widespread leaf curling or flower dropping during hot days. Diseases usually start on a few plants first and spread gradually to others.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ saa oshikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ he yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei fioo komɛi amli yɛ shishijee mli, ni fiofio lɛ, eyaa hiɛ. Egbɛ eshwa tsei krokomɛi anɔ

english: How do I protect my harvested maize from pests when storing it inside a room?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe kɛ́ akɛto mli?

english: You can treat your stored maize with approved grain protectants or storage powders. These treatments stop insects from feeding and prevent them from laying eggs on your grain, keeping your harvest safe for months.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ahebuu loo powda ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he lɛ ato ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he. Tsofafeemɔi nɛɛ baatsi kooloi bibii lɛ anaa ni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ oŋmaa lɛ nɔ. Koni oha onibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do weevils still attack my maize even after I sweep and clean my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmei lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ mihe ewo nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli ni mijie mli lɛ?

english: Insects and their microscopic eggs often travel from the farm right inside the maize husks, or they hide in tiny wall cracks. Cleaning helps, but applying proper storage grain treatment ensures hidden insects cannot survive or reproduce.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii fãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛyaa ŋmãa ŋmeii amli. Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe tee gbogboi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ, he saamɔ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi loo amɛkafɔ.

english: Is it safe to use storage chemicals on maize that my family will eventually eat?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai baatsu nii koni akɛbu ŋmãa ni miweku lɛ baaye yɛ naagbee lɛ he?

english: Yes, as long as you use recommended, food-safe post-harvest chemicals at the right dose and wait the required period before consuming or selling the maize so the chemical breaks down safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi, ni niyenii nyɛŋ ayeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ ayibɔ ni sa baatsu nii. ni omɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni ato lɛ dani oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa bɔni afee ni tsofai lɛ afite shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my maize rot or attract insects if I store it immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ loo egbalaa kooloi kɛbaa kɛji mikɛto beni mikpa nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains moisture. If you store it without drying it properly, the trapped moisture encourages mold growth and creates ideal conditions for pests to lay eggs and multiply.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ okɛto ni ogbiiee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Trapped moisture woɔ ŋmɔtɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃. ni eha shihilɛ ni sa aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛwo amɛwui ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Why do pests lay eggs on my crops, and how does that destroy my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ? Ni te enɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni mitsuɔ nii ehaa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects lay eggs on maize so that when the young larvae hatch, they immediately have food to eat. These hatching caterpillars or grubs eat through the grains, turning your crop into dust.
ga: Kplukai lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa nɔ bɔni afee ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, niyenii aba ni amɛye amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni efɔ nɛɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ onibii lɛ sũ

english: How can I tell if insects are starting to damage my crops before I harvest them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miibɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afitemɔ dani mikpa?

english: Inspect your plants regularly for early signs like small holes in leaves, dark insect droppings, or tiny clusters of eggs under the leaves and near the maize cobs.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ daa kɛha mra be mli okadii tamɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli, kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to attack my maize plants more than other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer grass-family crops like maize because tender young maize leaves and stalks provide the exact nutrients they need to grow rapidly.
ga: Fall cutworms sumɔɔ jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa ejaakɛ baai kɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ haa amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is short on nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to produce healthy green leaves and big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, providing natural food for your maize and helping control weeds.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha o-corn lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ jwɛi anɔ.

english: Why do my maize cobs develop white mold when rain falls right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ dani akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rainwater trapped inside the husks creates high humidity around the grain, allowing fungal spores in the air to grow into white or black mold on the cobs.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni emɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo baa ŋmãa lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect them from direct sunlight and harsh dry winds like the Harmattan. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava shields the young leaves from drying out and burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa ni mli egbi, tamɔ Harmattan lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai bibii lɛ akagbi ni amɛkashã.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies that transmit viruses, causing the leaves to distort and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and nutrients to grow strong stems and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Too many suckers attached to one main plantain stem force them to share nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots and leaving only 2 or 3 strong ones ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce larger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni kpɛtɛɔ tso titri kome he, ni enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛja niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to put all its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of storing starch in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients encourage root swelling.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ.

english: Why does my land give me smaller maize harvests every year when I plant in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility by fixing nitrogen naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ekɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, dry soil, or poor pollination. When the plant experiences high temperatures without enough water, it sheds flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ji nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei na hulutsoo ni naa wa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get dry, hard, and cracked so quickly after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ, ewaa, ni egbɛɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens rapidly when it lacks organic matter like compost or mulch, which acts like a sponge to hold water. Leaving soil bare exposes it to the hot sun, causing fast evaporation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni akɛhiɛɔ nu mli Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ enɔ. Ekɛ la ni hoɔ oya baa

english: Why are there holes in my young corn leaves with small brown dirt inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central whorl of young maize plants and eats the leaves. Early treatment with bio-pesticides or neem extract helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Mra be mli tsamɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu lɛ tsuɔ nii Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants look weak and yellow even after applying fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔ mli po lɛ?

english: Your crop may be attacked by parasitic weeds like Striga (witchweed), which attach directly to the maize roots underground and steal water and nutrients before the plant can use them.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ Striga (witchweed) lɛ baatutua oŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: What is integrated farming, and how can combining crops with farm animals help my yield?
ga: Mɛni ji okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome? Ni te ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni akɛfeɔ ekome lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Integrated farming means combining crops and livestock on the same land so they support each other. Animal manure acts as free, rich fertilizer for your crops, while crop residues can feed the animals, cutting down your costs and improving your harvests.
ga: Okwaayeli ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi afee ekome yɛ he kome koni amɛye amɛbua amɛhe. Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni fa babaoo kɛhaa onibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ aha kooloi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shika baa shi ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the soft cocoa leaves from burning while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cocoa baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant beans or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have roots that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen, so planting legumes feeds the soil naturally and leads to healthier maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: My maize plants are turning yellow from the bottom leaves upward; what is happening to them?
ga: Mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi. Mɛni ba a nɔ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen or that water is pooling around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer and ensuring proper field drainage helps the plants turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ebua ehe naa ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he, ni ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots struggle to swell when planted in hard, tightly packed soil or when the ground lacks potassium. Loosening the soil well before planting allows the roots to expand freely and absorb needed nutrients.
ga: Ewa akɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ baafu kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. aloo be mli ni potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Which fast-growing crops can I plant to get quick food and money while waiting for my main crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni maná niyenii kɛ shika oya be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mitso titri lɛ ada?

english: Short-season crops like vegetables, cowpeas, and maize mature in 3 to 4 months. Planting them in the open spaces between your long-term crops gives you quick food and steady cash flow.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ aduawai, tsina ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei, shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa onáa niyenii oya kɛ shika ni baa shi daa.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my cassava immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The season's first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can scorch delicate young plants. Waiting for regular, continuous rains ensures the soil retains enough deep moisture for cassava stem cuttings to sprout healthy roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni baa daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: If I plant my tomato seeds very close together to fit more on my land, why do I get smaller fruits?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hegbɛ babaoo hu? Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ hetoi bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight one another for water, soil food, and sunlight. Giving tomato plants proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow big, healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la. Tomato tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tomato agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize farm more aggressively during dry spells than during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains physically knock young caterpillars off plants and slow their breeding. In dry weather, pests reproduce faster, and heat-stressed crops are weaker and easier for insects to damage.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii shwieɔ tsei anɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii blɛoo. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, ŋmeii baafɔ oya. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my pepper seedlings after I clear my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants built to rapidly grab open sunlight and nutrients before anything else can grow. Young pepper seedlings grow slowly at first and need regular clearing around them so weeds do not steal their food and shade them out.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa, ni afee amɛ koni amɛgbala hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani nɔ kroko baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Baby pepper dumɔwui lɛ daaa oya yɛ shishijee mli ni ehe miihia ni ajie amɛ daa yɛ tso lɛ he koni jwɛi akaju niyenii ni amɛha nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and turn pale green during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tightly to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, which prevents water from evaporating too fast. Pale leaves indicate heat stress or a lack of moisture and nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ akashɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant plantains or cassava next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain loo cassava yɛ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide living shade to cool the young cocoa plants and preserve soil moisture while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni omɛɛɔ cacao lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big bushy green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to expand the tuber roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha bulb ɔ sisije ɔ mi nɛ wa.

english: What causes my tomato blossoms to dry up and drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tomato lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni egbeeɔ shi ni ewooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the daytime temperatures are too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between overly dry and overly wet, which prevents the flower from pollinating properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and exposes them fully to sunlight for bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ. ni oha bulb tsei wuji lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops during dry spells?
ga: Te jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry vegetation (mulch) acts like a blanket that shades the dirt from the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating quickly and keeping the plant roots cool.
ga: Muji ni akɛ tsei ni egbi (Mulch) woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of young leaves, causing the tissue to grow unevenly and wrinkle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa fãji lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie Plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) causes them to compete with the main plantain stem for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest stem to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers (tso) ni fa tsɔ lɛ haa amɛkɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I pour my fertilizer directly against the stem of my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ aduawai tsei anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw water out of plant tissue. Placing it directly against the stem burns the bark and roots; it should be applied in a circle a few inches away.
