ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ kokroo nɔ ni kɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi.

english: Why are my maize cobs missing grains in some places instead of being full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ bɛ hei komɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Incomplete grain formation happens when dry conditions or extreme heat occur during silk emergence, preventing pollen from reaching every silk thread on the cob.
ga: Nibii ni afee ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ba yɛ siliki kwɛ̃mɔ be mli. Etsiɔ pollen naa koni ekashɛ siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct heat from the sun burns their leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young plants until they are mature enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my crops yield much smaller fruits when I plant many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for the same limited food, water, and space in the soil. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough nutrients to produce full-sized crops.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the maize regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I apply fertilizer to my field right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔji amli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer off the top layer of soil before the roots can absorb it, wasting your money. It is better to apply fertilizer when the ground is damp but heavy rains are not expected immediately.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Shika ni afiteɔ Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I keep planting the same crop on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miyaa nɔ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly without giving the ground time to recover. Rotating different crops, especially beans or groundnuts, puts nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni ahaaa be ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ titri lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Enɛ baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground before I get the chance to harvest them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛkpaa nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays around them without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. without draining out Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam leaves need to climb high on stakes so they can catch direct sunlight to produce energy. Raising the leaves off the ground allows the plant to build bigger, healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ daa, ni ehiɛɔ sweet potato tubers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and becoming small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiifee srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that carry a plant virus. Controlling whiteflies early stops the virus from spreading and damaging your entire tomato harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ tomato ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress or lack of water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost gives the plant enough strength to hold its flowers and grow peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops and choke them if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehaa amɛmuɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally adapt to survive aggressively, taking water, fertilizer, and light faster than cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients and water available for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi kɛtsɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la nɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ aba koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to get cocoa seedlings from a relative's farm in another region to plant on my land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maŋɔ kookoo dumɔwui kɛjɛ miwekunyo ko ŋmɔ mli yɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ ni mikɛdu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: While seedlings from other farms can grow, it is safer to use certified hybrid seedlings from official sources. Seedlings moved from other regions can carry hidden pests or diseases, and they might not be well-suited to the rainfall and soil conditions of your specific area.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ moŋ. Shi eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ maŋ onukpai adɛŋ lɛ baatsu nii. Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni adu kɛjɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Ni ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ esaaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant cocoa seedlings from a nursery instead of putting seeds straight into my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ kookoo dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Nursery seedlings are given extra care, water, and shade when they are young and weak. Planting mature seedlings gives your cocoa a strong head start, resulting in a much higher survival rate compared to planting raw seeds directly in the harsh field.
ga: Nursery dumɔwui lɛ naa kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ, nu, kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdarako ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni eda lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha o-cocoa lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa wala yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ waa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli wa amli lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa seedling in a nursery is healthy enough to move to my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy seedling should have a strong, straight stem, deep green leaves without yellow spots or insect holes, and a firm soil root-ball that holds together without damaged or twisted main roots.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná tsei ni wa, ni ja. Baai eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii bɛ mli. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni efiteee shishifãi titrii lɛ loo efiteee amɛ.

english: What time of the year should I put my cocoa seedlings into the farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: You should plant your cocoa seedlings at the beginning of the main rainy season. This gives the young roots plenty of time to establish themselves deep in the moist soil before the dry season begins.
ga: Esa akɛ odu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ naa be babaoo ni amɛkɛma amɛhe shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How deep and wide should I dig the holes for my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu ni mli kwɔ kɛ elɛɛmɔ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha kookoo dumɔwu hee?

english: Dig holes that are about 40 centimeters wide and 40 centimeters deep. This loosens the soil around the seedling, making it easy for tender new roots to spread out and gather food and water.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni elɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 40 ni elɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 40. Enɛ baaha sũ ni bɔle dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi heei baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbua niyenii kɛ nu naa.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa seedlings when planting them on the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Cocoa seedlings should generally be planted 3 meters apart from each other. Proper spacing ensures that full-grown trees have enough room to get sunlight, airflow, and soil nutrients without crowding each other out.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mitai 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kɛ ehe wooo mli

english: How should I transport young cocoa seedlings to my farm without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ cacao tsei bibii aya miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mifiteee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Keep the root soil moist, avoid stacking seedlings on top of each other, and cover them with a cloth or tarp during transport to protect the young leaves from strong drying winds and harsh sun.
ga: Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he. ni okɛ mama loo tarpaulin aha he yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa egbiɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my newly planted cocoa seedlings turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is experiencing transplant shock, receiving too much direct sunlight, or lacking water. Providing temporary shade and keeping the soil moist will help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo nu ni bɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What basic care do my cocoa seedlings need right after I plant them to make sure they survive?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ he hiaa mi-cocoa dumɔwu lɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi?

english: Young cocoa needs temporary shade (such as nearby plantain trees), regular weeding so weeds do not steal water, and protection from hot afternoon sun during their first year in the field.
ga: Cocoa oblahii kɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo (tamɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ). Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi daa koni jwɛi akaju nu. ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting my cocoa seedlings before I start seeing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi ŋmeii lɛ anamɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa seedlings usually start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting if they receive proper shade, water, and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo, nu kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and slow down growth during the short dry spell in August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo yɛ August mli nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the August dry break, moisture in the topsoil drops quickly, making it hard for maize roots to absorb nitrogen. The yellowing is a sign of temporary water and nutrient stress, which you can reduce by applying mulch around the crop earlier in the season to hold soil moisture.
ga: Yɛ August mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi oya. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nitrogen. Yellow ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Abaanyɛ aba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ sũ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii mra yɛ be lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the roots need air to stay healthy. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly on land that was previously used for galamsey?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ galamsey tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Galamsey activity scrapes away the fertile topsoil where plants feed and leaves behind compacted subsoil. Toxic residue and heavy metals left in the soil prevent plant roots from absorbing water and vital nutrients properly.
ga: Galamsey nitsumɔ lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni tsei yeɔ niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛ kɛ dade ni tsii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to water my vegetable farm with muddy river water from areas where illegal mining happens?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ he ko ni ajieɔ shika tsuru yɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baafɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, water polluted by mining contains fine silt that clogs soil pores and blocks air from reaching plant roots. It may also carry chemicals that stunt crop growth and make the harvested vegetables unsafe to eat.
ga: Dabi, nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ bibii ni tsiɔ sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ tsei shishifãi ahe. Tsofai ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa ni haa aduawai ni akpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ lɛ hu yɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my farm before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the season ends, those roots decay and leave natural fertilizer in the soil, helping your next maize crop grow strong without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ye obua o-abele ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large shade trees off my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and dry out easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving taller shade trees protects the young plants from extreme heat and keeps the soil cool and moist while the seedlings establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How does leaving dried crop leaves and straw on top of my soil help my plants survive hot periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dried plant leaves creates a blanket that shields the soil from direct sun. This prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly and slowly decomposes into rich plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ akafo oya ni efite fiofio ni etsɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and shrink when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants during hot weather is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mites or thrips that multiply rapidly in the heat, or it is a self-defense reaction by the plant to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baa. ni shwereɔ oya yɛ latsaa mli Aloo eji nɔ ko ni tsei feɔ kɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when day or night temperatures get too high, or when the plant doesn't get consistent water. The heat prevents successful pollination, so the plant sheds the flower to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Heat tsiɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of thick green leaves but only produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo nɛkɛ? Mohu ɔ, e woɔ bulb nyafii pɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium, the yam plant uses all its energy to grow green leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli lɛ. Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛba shi koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: My cocoa trees are sick and turning yellow, so why are you telling me to cut them down instead of just spraying medicine?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ okɛɛ mi akɛ mafo mli moŋ fe ni mawo mi mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Some cocoa diseases, like the Swollen Shoot Virus, live inside the tree's system where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down infected trees is the only way to stop the disease from spreading through insects to your healthy trees and destroying your entire farm.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi, tamɔ Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofolɔ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okpa hela lɛ ni ekatsɔ kooloi bibii anɔ kɛya otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. ni okpãtã oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: What are the clear signs I should look for to know if my cocoa tree is completely ruined by disease and needs to be cut down?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni esa akɛ matao koni mana kɛji hela emɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ amli kwraa ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ amɛhe?

english: Look out for swollen stems or roots, red leaf veins, mottled yellow patterns on leaves, and abnormally small, misshapen cocoa pods. When a tree shows these signs, it cannot be cured and will eventually stop producing altogether.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi ni efuu, baa lɛ mli fãji tsuru, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ. kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ su kpakpa ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ jie okadii nɛɛ akpo lɛ Enyɛŋ atsa lɛ kwraa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaakpa yibiiwoo kwraa.

english: Can diseases from a sick cocoa tree jump across the farm to infect my healthy crops?
ga: Ani hela ko ni jɛɔ cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni ekɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs carry viruses from sick trees to healthy ones, and fungal diseases can travel through wind, rain drops, or even contaminated cutlasses. Removing diseased plants quickly protects your uninfected crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ dade ni mli ewo muji po mli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ni hela emɔko amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What is the biggest mistake farmers make that causes them to suffer massive loss from cocoa disease?
ga: Mɛni ji tɔmɔi wuji ni okwaafoi feɔ ni haa amɛfiteɔ nii babaoo kɛjɛɔ kookoo hela mli?

english: The biggest mistake is holding onto sick trees because they still have a few pods left. Leaving diseased trees on your farm allows the sickness to silently infect all surrounding trees, leading to total farm failure later on.
ga: Tɔmɔ ni fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛkpɛtɛ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ eshwɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni ebɔle ohe lɛ anɔ. all quietly Enɛ ha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ fite yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land is actually suitable for growing cocoa or if I should plant another crop like cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ loo esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Cocoa requires deep, rich, well-draining soil that holds moisture without getting waterlogged, along with good rainfall. If your land is very sandy, rocky, or frequently flooded, crops like cassava, potato, or plantains will grow much better there than cocoa.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia kokoo. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu bɛ mli kɛfataa nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa he Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã, tɛi, loo nu hoɔ shii abɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe kookoo.

english: If cocoa keeps failing on a specific patch of my farm, does that mean the soil is useless?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ehiaaa?

english: No, it just means that patch of soil is no longer suitable for cocoa. Different crops need different nutrients; replacing cocoa with food crops like maize, legumes, or root vegetables can restore the soil and give you high yields.
ga: Dabi, etsɔɔ kɛkɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ esaaa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dɔŋŋ. Tsei srɔtoi biɔ niyenii srɔtoi. Niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ kookoo najiaŋ. Aloo aduawai ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I choose the best crop variety to plant if my area experiences very long dry seasons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu? Ni kɛji akɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ naa hɔmɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa hu?

english: You should ask extension officers for modern hybrid varieties that are specifically bred to tolerate drought. Hybrid cocoa seedlings and drought-resistant crop varieties can survive heat and poor rainfall much better than older local seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ obi o-extension agent lɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid srɔtoi ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ahe sane. Cocoa dumɔwui, hybrids kɛ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni etsɛ.

english: If I cut down my diseased cocoa trees today, how long must I wait before I can safely plant new ones?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu tso hee shweshweeshwe?

english: After clearing diseased trees and destroying the infected plant material, you can prepare the land immediately. Planting fresh, disease-resistant hybrid seedlings right away helps you recover your farm's production as quickly as possible.
ga: Beni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ofite tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe nibii lɛ, Obaanyɛ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya bɔ ni ooonyɛ.

english: What kind of seedling should I buy to make sure my new cocoa farm doesn't get destroyed by the same disease again?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mahe koni hela nɛɛ nɔŋŋ akafite mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Always source certified hybrid cocoa seedlings from approved government nurseries. These improved seedlings are bred to resist common diseases, grow faster, and yield more pods than seeds picked directly from old pods.
ga: Hemɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛ odaseyeli ewo mli kɛjɛ maŋ nɔyeli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be. Afɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. edaa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmeii momo amli tɛ̃ɛ

english: What simple steps can I take on my land to ensure newly planted cocoa seedlings survive their first year?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Provide shade by planting plantains around young seedlings, keep weeds cleared so they do not steal soil nutrients, and protect the small plants from harsh sunlight and pests during the dry season.
ga: Ha hulutsoo kɛtsɔ plantains ni ooodu yɛ tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ, ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to make food and grow green leaves. This often happens when the soil is worn out or after heavy rains wash nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii ni akɛbaa eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family. They have tiny swellings on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Amɛyɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and gives pests that feed on maize a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even when the leaves grow tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava soil has too much nitrogen or water, the plant uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ woɔ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nine ni kɛlɛ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves higher into the sunlight to produce food. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf rot and increasing tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main stem. Keeping only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily in direct heat. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from hot sun and dry winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: Why do many farmers plant maize and cassava together in the same farm at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly over a year. Planting them together uses land efficiently and gives you food early while waiting for the cassava.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ afi kome mli lɛ. Hefatalɔi adumɔ kɛ he ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa niyenii oya be mli ni emɛɛɔ ŋmei lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is often caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on leaf juice, or by a virus carried by insects that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden stress, causing the plant to shed its blossoms to survive rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo haomɔ trukaa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my maize crop right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ trukaa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms survive the dry season as pupae in the soil or in nearby weeds. When the rains arrive and young maize sprouts, the adult moths emerge and lay hundreds of eggs, creating a sudden outbreak.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli akɛ pupae yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ba ni ŋmãa bibii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni eda lɛ baawo ŋmãa ohai abɔ. ni kɛ hela ko ni baa trukaa lɛ baa

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids transmitting a virus, or by a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and humid conditions, especially when trees are not pruned to let sunlight and air pass through.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, titri lɛ kɛji afolɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my maize seeds at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the ground receives two or three heavy soaking rains so the soil holds deep moisture; planting too early after just one light shower can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in heavy clay or poorly drained soil after long rains, which starves the roots of air and allows fungal diseases to attack.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ atutua.

english: Why do I need to leave shade trees or plant plantains near my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains act like umbrellas, providing shade and cooling the ground until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when plants experience heat stress, extreme dryness, or sudden flooding, which prevents the flowers from pollinating successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. ŋmɔlɔ loo nu afua ni baa trukaa Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: No, planting seeds too close forces plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks with tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii baa. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when I do not add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mikɛ fɔmɔ wooo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants with deep roots that are adapted to thrive in harsh conditions, making them faster at stealing available water and nutrients than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛshwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during long dry spells as a survival mechanism. Dropping leaves reduces water loss through evaporation, allowing the root under the ground to stay alive and healthy until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Ha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants with dark dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant. It eats the tender green leaves before they unfold, which weakens the plant's ability to make food and reduces your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ niyenii, ni ehaa onibii ni okpaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air so their leaves can spread out and capture full sunlight. Staking prevents leaves from rotting on the damp ground and allows the plant to create enough energy to swell the big tuber under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ. Staking tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special microscopic organisms on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the legume stems and roots decay, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii waa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers fall off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly waterlogged. High heat and uneven water stress cause the plant to lose its flowers before pollination can take place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi aahu akɛ nu shwie nɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu mli haomɔ ni bɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under strong, direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves burn easily. Big shade trees protect cocoa seedlings from excessive heat and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why do weeds make my maize plants turn pale yellow even after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight before your maize crop can use them. If weeds are left in the field, they consume most of the plant food you put down.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ hulu la dani ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii. Kɛji jwɛi komɛi eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaaye tsei aniyenii ni oshɛrɛɔ lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly like drinking straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll inward to protect themselves from intense heat. By curling up, the plant hides its leaf pores from the sun to slow down water evaporation and save moisture until the cooler evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ mli koni akadɔ fe nine. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ato hulu la he koni nu lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to grow out of the soil even after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to come up if they were planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil is packed too hard, or if insects ate the seed underground. Planting seeds deeper than two finger-lengths makes it hard for the weak sprout to reach the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ. loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni mli kwɔ fe inchi 2 lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tight and the whole plant staying small and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: This curling is caused by a plant virus usually carried by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck the plant juices. The virus disrupts the plant's natural growth process, stopping leaves from opening fully and reducing fruit size.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ curling nɛɛ baa ji tso mli hela ko ni bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ kɛbaa. Virus gbalaa tsei adalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbeleee kwraa, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight and dry out quick in strong heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living shelter that protects the seedlings while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni egbiɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa anáa he ko ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛ ŋmeii yɛji lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get destroyed by small insects even inside sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kotokui amli po fiteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Grain weevils and insects often enter stored crops if the grains are not completely dried before storage. Storing thoroughly dried grain in airtight hermetic bags suffocates the pests and prevents them from multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii boteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ amli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha amɛkafɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop produce tall leaves but very small, weak cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ baa kakadaji shi ŋmeii bibii waa ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nitrogen to build strong leaves and phosphorus to produce large, healthy cobs. If the soil lacks essential nutrients, the plant spends energy growing leaves but cannot develop full cobs.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛma baai ni wa, ni phosphorus hu he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji ni wa aba. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai shi enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii?

english: Tired soil often produces pale or yellow crops, slow-growing plants, or noticeably lower yields compared to past years. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or balanced chemical fertilizer helps restore nutrients to the land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally feed the soil and make neighboring crops like maize grow healthier.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: Will I harvest more crops if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close causes the plants to fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every crop room to grow strong roots and yield larger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shĩa fɛɛ shĩa ni daa lɛ náa shishifãi ni wa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i ngɔ dumɔwu komɛ kɛ je ye nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi.

english: Saved seeds from previous harvests often lose their vigor over time, leading to weaker plants and lower yields. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, tolerate dry spells, and produce high harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni gbɔjɔɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni ekɛ yibii babaoo baa

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants without forming fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to tomato plants, making the flowers dry up and fall off before pollination happens. Mulching the soil with dry grass helps keep the roots cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly soak up available rainwater and soil nutrients before domestic crops can. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your main crops the best chance to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya dani shia tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaashwere.

english: Why should I measure and space my crops using lines and pegs instead of just planting anywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ line kɛ pin asusu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni mato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ekome pɛ

english: Proper line spacing gives every plant enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong. It also makes it much easier to walk through your field to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Line ni ato jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji amli koni ayajie jwɛi, awo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa nii lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for light and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, producing smaller yields or smaller fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo fioo loo yibii fioo.

english: Why do I need to completely uproot tree stumps and big weeds before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi wuji fɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Uprooting stumps and deep weeds prevents them from regrowing and stealing nutrients from your young crop. It also removes places where soil pests and diseases like to hide.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei akutsei kɛ jwɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Ejieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe lɛ hu kɛyaa.

english: Why does ploughing and loosening the hard soil help my seeds grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ŋmɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil allows soft young roots to push deep into the ground easily to find water. It also helps air and rainwater penetrate the soil so the roots do not suffocate.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sũ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaabote sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu hu boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akagbɔjɔ.

english: How do I determine the right number of plants to put on my acre of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ayibɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mawo mishikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre lɛ nɔ?

english: The right plant count depends on the specific crop type and its recommended row distance. Having the correct plant population ensures you get the maximum yield without overcrowding your soil.
ga: Tsei ayibɔ ni sa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oyɛ tsei ayibɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha onine ashɛ yibii babaoo nɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ.

english: Why do my young crop plants grow tall and thin when big trees are shading them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ tsei wuji ewo amɛhe shade lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce energy for growth. When shaded, the plant stretches upward as fast as possible to reach the light, making the stem thin and fragile.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha amɛdalɛ. Beni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baatsi ehe kɛya ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and drop off when water sits on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns crop roots by blocking air from reaching them. Without air, roots rot and cannot send water or food up to the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsĩɔ naa koni ekashɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ nu loo niyenii aya baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast during the dry season even when I water the top soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Heat and strong winds cause water to evaporate quickly from the surface soil and leaves. If root systems are shallow, the plant loses water faster than roots can draw it from deep underground.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in that field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young shoots naturally bend toward the sun during the morning and afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi kɛyaa hulu lɛ he leebi kɛ shwane lɛ?

english: Plants naturally bend toward light because sunshine triggers growth hormones in the stem. This movement helps the leaves catch as much sunlight as possible to make food.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ haa tsofai ni haa mɔ daa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ nyiɛmɔ nɛɛ haa baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize crops turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer will give the plants the food they need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantains next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the strong sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool moisture the delicate cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ aha kookoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are there small holes all over my cassava leaves, and will this reduce my harvest under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii eyi ŋmeii baai lɛ amli obɔ lɛ? Ni ani enɛ baaha nibii ni afeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba shi?

english: The holes are made by leaf-eating insects. Leaves act as factories that catch sunlight to make food for the cassava tubers growing underground, so when insects destroy too many leaves, the plant cannot produce large tubers.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ baa ji mɛi ni kɛ bu nɛɛ baa. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso ni nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ koni efee niyenii eha ŋmei shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii kpata baai babaoo ahiɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmei shishifãi wuji.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before any small tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked too quickly. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves clean, prevents diseases from the wet soil from spreading to the plant, and encourages the plant to direct its energy into growing big tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ he tseɔ. Tsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ nɔ. ni ekanya tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje ŋmeii ni miida lɛ

english: What happens to my maize seeds if I push them too deep into the ground when planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its stored food energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the surface. Planting seeds at a shallow depth of about 2 to 3 centimeters gives them the best chance to sprout quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ji sɛntimita 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: How do weeds growing around my pepper plants lower the amount of pepper I harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ mi-pepper tsei lɛ aha pepper ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that drink up the soil water and consume the fertilizer meant for your peppers. When weeds crowd your crop, they also block sunlight, leaving your pepper plants weak and unable to produce many fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi tsei ni nuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-peppers lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle onibii ahe lɛ Amɛbaatsi hulu lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa pepper tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it bad practice to place chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem can burn the outer bark and delicate plant tissue due to the high concentration of salts. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away from the stem in a ring where the underground feeder roots can reach it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fãji kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi inchi fioo ko pɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni niyenii shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny insects appear inside my stored dried maize bags after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa kotokui ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects, called grain weevils, hatch from tiny eggs that were already on the grain in the field or crept in through small openings. Ensuring the maize is completely dry before bagging and storing it in airtight bags suffocates the insects and protects your food.
ga: Atsɛɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ akɛ dumɔwui ŋmeii. Efɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔŋloo bibioo ko mli. ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ momo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛboteɔ mli lɛ Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku mli ni okɛto kotoku mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafo ni ebu oniyenii lɛ he.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts next season where I harvested maize this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nitrogen from the soil during its growth. Groundnuts belong to a plant family that captures nitrogen gas from the air and puts it back into the soil, naturally restoring the land's strength for future crops.
ga: Abele gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ. Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, acting like natural shade umbrellas while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la fiteɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I remove and burn a crop plant that shows signs of disease instead of leaving it in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔɔ hela he okadii lɛ ni mashã amɛ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Diseased plants can harbor pests, fungi, or viruses that quickly spread to nearby healthy crops through wind, water, or insects. Removing and burning the infected plant stops the disease from destroying your entire farm.
ga: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsɛŋemɔ helai, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nu, loo kooloi bibii anɔ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie ni oshã lɛ haaa hela afite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen, a key food element plants need to grow. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant make leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same spot every season, why does my harvest keep reducing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minitsumɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the ground every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients, while alternating with crops like legumes helps the soil recover and maintain its fertility.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpea or beans help make my farm soil richer?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, naturally enriching the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shweremɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so that I get more plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong roots and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my young crops make them grow much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ midumɔwui lɛ haa amɛdaraa oya kwraa.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds ensures all available resources go directly to feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall for a long period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When water sits in the soil without draining, it prevents air from reaching the roots. Without air, the roots suffocate and become vulnerable to waterlogged fungi that cause rotting.
ga: Beni nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu mli ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat stress combined with dry soil causes pepper plants to drop their flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy and survive severe conditions.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops at the very start of the rainy season rather than in the middle of it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu nii yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli fe nɔ ni nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Planting early allows seeds to germinate when soil moisture is consistent and temperature is ideal, giving young roots enough time to anchor deeply before dry spells occur.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yaa nɔ daa ni hulutsoo be lɛ hu ja. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. They need shade from taller trees like plantains or forest trees to protect their leaves and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Which direction should the stem buds point when I am planting cassava cuttings in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: The small buds on the cassava stem must always point upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the plant will waste energy trying to turn around, resulting in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyitsei lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, giving leaves access to light and preventing diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náa la ni ehaa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛbaa lɛ baa.

english: This is a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong cobs. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps fix this.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I avoid planting my maize immediately after the very first rainfall of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell before the main rains settle in. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout and then dry up and die from lack of continuous water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nu ni bɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when the plant has too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and balanced feeding help flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the extra shoots growing around my plantain stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Too many shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only two or three, ensuring the main plant gets enough food to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny root nodes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that nitrogen stays behind, acting as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi bibii. No gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi lɛ Nitrogen baahi shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not wash it off my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Instead of throwing fertilizer loosely on top of the dry ground, dig a small hole a few inches away from the plant stem, put the fertilizer inside, and cover it back up with soil.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko. Kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight or hot winds. Without shade trees or plantains grown next to them to block the sun, the intense heat causes the delicate leaves to dry out, turn yellow, and drop off.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, koni akɛtsi hulu la naa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. The plants spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of developing strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ tsohi agbohi.

english: Why does my cassava produce very thick green leaves above ground but small, thin tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen—often from over-using certain fertilizers or manure—the cassava plant directs its energy into growing leafy branches above the ground instead of storing starch in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ sisi a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die off on their own before the heavy rains end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ gboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ba naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn yellow and die back when the tubers underground have reached full size. This is the plant's natural sign that it has finished growing and is ready to be harvested.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboi kɛji ŋmeii lɛ shɛ amɛdalɛ he. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe dalɛ naa ni esa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot quickly if heavy rains flood my farm just before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground remains waterlogged for days, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing the starch to break down and allowing soil fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa starch lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or a sudden lack of water. The plant sheds its flowers as a defense mechanism to save water and stay alive during stressful weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu bɛ trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling inward and turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and purple colors in tomato plants usually indicate stress from missing nutrients in the soil, such as phosphorus, or a viral disease spread by tiny insects like whiteflies during hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly start eating my young maize leaves right after the first major rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi mi-baby corn baai lɛ yeli trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay hidden eggs in weeds and dry soil just before the rainy season starts. As soon as the first rains fall and fresh, soft maize leaves sprout, the eggs hatch into hungry caterpillars like armyworms.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ woɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛtee jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ ni ŋmãa baai bibii heei lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ asraafoi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves shred into thin strips when strong winds blow across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miigba amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ? Beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Plantain leaves are designed with natural weak lines so they can split easily during high winds. This unique behavior stops the wind from snapping the main stem or uprooting the heavy plant.
ga: Afee plantain baai lɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni amɛgbala mli mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Nɛkɛ subaŋ krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekafo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ loo efolɔ tso lɛ shishi waa.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow so well even when I do not add nitrogen fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which works with natural soil bacteria that live on their roots. These bacteria capture nitrogen gas directly from the air and convert it into food for the plant.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nɛkɛ muawai nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil strips away specific nutrients like nitrogen and lets pests that attack maize build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii komɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ emli. ni amɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.
