Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil is rich enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and has earthworms or decaying leaves in it. Hard, pale, or sandy soil that dries out quickly lacks nutrients and needs animal manure or compost mixed in before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai ni fiteɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli tseee, loo ŋã ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei loo kooloi aŋmei afutu mli dani adu.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Curled and yellow-spotted cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to keep your crop healthy.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛji woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the funnel of young maize plants to eat the soft leaves. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening directly into the leaf funnels helps destroy them before they kill the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni teɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ atsɔnei amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efite amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into tight curls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips that feed on the leaf sap and spread viruses. Keeping weeds away from your farm and spraying organic or recommended treatments early prevents these insects from multiplying.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips. ni yeɔ baa mli nu kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Akɛ jwɛi lɛ tsi ohe kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ ashwie nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafɔ bii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium in the soil. Watering consistently at the roots and providing light shade during very hot weeks helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines stop growing green and naturally dry up to a yellowish-brown color. Digging them up too early when vines are still green leads to small, watery tubers that spoil quickly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛyashɛ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ atsa mra tsɔ beni wain tso lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ aba.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain trees turn brown and droop down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: It is normal for older, lower leaves of a plantain tree to turn brown and die as the plant channels energy to new leaves and the fruit cluster. Pruning off these old, dead leaves keeps the farm clean and prevents fungal spots from spreading.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ plantain baai ni egbɔ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboi be mli ni tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa baai heei kɛ aduawai akui amli lɛ. Baai ni egboi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Is it better to water my vegetables early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plant roots can soak up moisture before the sun gets strong. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most water to evaporate instantly, and watering late at night can encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli awa tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow and look weak after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away essential plant foods from the topsoil and fill up air spaces in the dirt, suffocating the roots. Building raised soil mounds or ridges with proper drainage gutters allows excess rainwater to flow away safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akashɛ he ko shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for crops. When maize doesn't get enough nutrients from the soil, it pulls energy from its lower leaves to feed new growth, causing the older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Can I throw raw kitchen scraps directly onto my vegetable bed to feed my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashɛrɛ niyenii ni ahoko ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋtayaai amli lɛ mafɔ̃ aduawai atsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii?

english: Raw kitchen scraps can rot, attract pests, and produce heat that burns crop roots. Food waste must be composted first so it breaks down into safe, rich organic manure that crops can easily absorb.
ga: Kpataashi nibii ni etse lɛ baanyɛ afite. Egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ baa Esa akɛ afee niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ dani akumɔ mli awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why does my land produce weaker crops when I only use chemical fertilizers every year without organic manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ? Akɛni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli pɛ tsuɔ nii daa afi ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuuu nii hewɔ lɛ.

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the crop quickly, but organic manure feeds the soil itself. Without manure or dead plant materials, the soil loses its ability to hold water and nutrients, eventually becoming hard and tired.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ni egboi bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli dɔŋŋ. ni naagbee lɛ, ewa ni etɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any larger plants nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni kookoo tso agbo ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies and scorch easily in strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides shade and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What happens if I plant several maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight aggressively against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look droopy during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. Cassava plants curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps them save water and survive the heat until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or sudden nutrient stress. The plant drops the flowers to save its own life when conditions are unfavorable.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛ yashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛhere amɛhe kɛji shihilɛi lɛ bafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small branches growing at the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Pruning extra side branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on non-essential leaves. This directs more food and water into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii kɛ nu babaoo aba koni akɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of crawling on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air so they catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe

english: Black pod is a disease caused by excess moisture trapped around the cocoa trees. Clearing heavy shade and pruning lower branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm and protect the pods.
ga: Black pod ji hela ko ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle cacao tso lɛ he lɛ kɛbaa. Ni niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes always get crushed and rot before I reach the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have soft skins and high moisture content. Stacking them too high in heavy wooden woven baskets puts immense pressure on the bottom layers, causing them to burst and rot. Using rigid, shallow crates or containers prevents weight pressure and protects the produce during transit.
ga: Tomato hewolo lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Ni akɛ tsɛnsi lɛ baawo tsɛnsi ni akpɛ́ ni tsii mli tsɔ Ebaaha shishigbɛ tsũi lɛ anɔ aná nɔnyɛɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa efoɔ ni efiteɔ. Kɛ akɛ adeka loo tsɛnsi ni mli wa, ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi shwiili mli haomɔ naa ni ebaabu nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested avocado fruits turn dark and soft inside even though the outside looked clean when I picked them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-avocado ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ mli tse beni mikɛto he lɛ moŋ.

english: Rough handling or dropping fruits during harvest causes internal bruising. Even if the outer skin appears undamaged initially, the inner flesh breaks down from the impact, leading to decay by the time it reaches the buyer.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ tso yibii lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo ekɛshwie shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ekɛ mligbɛ fãji baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni kponɔgbɛ lɛ efite yɛ shishijee mli moŋ, shi mligbɛ nibii lɛ fite kɛjɛ gbee ni etswa lɛ mli. ni ebaafite kɛ́ eshɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: Why should I prune the extra sucker shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to direct its energy into growing a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Sucker krɛdɛɛ ko baaju nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli Kɛ́ ajie tso wulu lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso wulu lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ kɛya ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants developing ragged holes and rolling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl into the central whorl of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upward and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus blocks normal water and nutrient flow inside the plant, causing the leaves to distort and discolor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Virus lɛ tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but yield only tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus its energy on growing top foliage rather than swelling its underground roots. Balanced soil nutrients are required for good root development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ adalɛ he nii moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni efuu lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ he miihia koni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without forming peppers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper efeee yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and low soil moisture place the pepper plant under severe stress. To survive and conserve water, the plant naturally sheds its blossoms instead of spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ kɛ pepper tsei lɛ woɔ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi. Bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi ni amɛbu nu he Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting and shrinking in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni miigbɔjɔ yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally come out of dormancy as temperatures rise. As the sprouts grow, they pull stored moisture and nutrients directly from the tuber, causing the yam to shrivel.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni baa kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ Ejieɔ nu ni ato kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ agbi

english: Why does my stored dry maize turn into fine dust after a few months in the room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ sũ kpakpa beni mihi tsu lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils lay eggs inside dry maize kernels. When the larvae hatch, they eat the grain from the inside out, reducing the harvest to powder unless the maize is properly dried and kept in airtight storage bags.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ woɔ wɔji yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi ni etsɔɔ powda. Ja agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around the roots. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps restore the green color and support proper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas in between my maize rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as natural fertilizer for your maize while suppressing weeds and giving you an extra harvest from the same piece of land.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni etsiɔ jwɛi hu anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo kroko kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving tall canopy trees or intercropping with plantains provides shade, lowers the temperature, and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ loo ni akɛ dumɔwui akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba shi, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal rot and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why is it bad to water my vegetable crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaaha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering under strong midday heat causes most of the water to evaporate before reaching the roots. Drops of water left on leaves can also magnify the hot sun, scorching the foliage and encouraging fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop roots with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with organic material, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, keeps the soil cool during dry spells, prevents weeds from growing, and adds nutrients as it decomposes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viruses carried by whiteflies. Sprayers using neem oil or recommended insecticides help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by sudden heat, inconsistent watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering at the root level and applying balanced fertilizer helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ahiɔ shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready for harvesting without digging up all the roots?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni atsaaa shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking open as the tubers swell beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ edara beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why am I getting very few bags of cocoa from my farm while other farmers get so much more?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ kookoo kotokui fioo pɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi krokomɛi nine shɛɔ kookoo babaoo nɔ lɛ?

english: Low yields happen when trees are old, soil nutrients are low, or pests and diseases are unchecked. Following simple practices like pruning, weeding, applying fertilizer, and spraying against pests can multiply your harvest bags.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ egbɔ. Akwɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛgbe ŋmɔshi nibii. Obaanyɛ oya hiɛ yɛ okpamɔ kotokui lɛ amli.

english: What can I do if my mature cocoa trees look healthy but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tso ni eda lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Trees might be spending their energy on leaves instead of pods, or flowers aren't being pollinated properly. Pruning to let in light, applying proper cocoa fertilizer, and using hand pollination can help the tree switch to producing many pods.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ atsu nii yɛ pods najiaŋ. Aloo afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni la abote mli Okɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa afata he. Ni nine ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛfee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my cocoa trees if I want them to grow more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ aniji kɛji miisumɔ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cutting excess branches allows sunlight and air to reach the main trunk and inner branches. This prevents fungal diseases and forces the tree to direct its food and water into growing heavy cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ kɛ niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ koni efee kookoo ŋmɔji ni tsii. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ baai baafata he

english: Why do flowers fall off my cocoa trees before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree lacks water or nutrients, or when tiny pests attack them. Giving the farm proper shade, plant food, and pest control keeps the flowers attached so they can grow into full cocoa pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii. Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii batutua lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo ni sa, tsei aniyenii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Do my cocoa trees need full sunlight or shade to grow well?
ga: Ani hulu loo hulutsoo be babaoo he miihia mi-cocoa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees need a balance. Young trees need heavy shade to protect them from burning in the hot sun, while adult trees need partial shade and sunlight so they can produce plenty of pods without drying out.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ he miihia ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Ákɛ tso ni eda lɛ, ehe miihia ni ená hulutsoo kɛ hulu la fioo koni enyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba ni egbiŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs fertilizer to help my crops grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crop leaves turn yellowish, branches grow slowly, or pod yields stay low every year, your soil is exhausted and needs nutrients like specialized cocoa fertilizer to feed the crop.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Niji lɛ daaa fiofio. loo pod ni baa shi daa afi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia niyenii, tamɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi, koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and crowded farms. Pruning your trees and clearing weeds lets sunlight dry up moisture, which stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ baaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes the young shoots and leaves on my cocoa trees to look burned and dry?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã ni amɛgbi?

english: This damage is usually caused by insects called capsids or mirids that suck sap from the branches. Spraying recommended insecticides at the right time protects the trees and saves your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo mirids ni nuɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ ashwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baabu tsei ahe ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ akafite.

english: Why is it bad to leave open, broken cocoa pod husks scattered around my farm after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni ekumɔ ni egbɛ eshwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔ ni mifeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ.

english: Rotting husks host harmful fungi that cause diseases like Black Pod. Leaving them near healthy trees allows rain to splash the disease onto your living pods, so husks should be removed or composted far away.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni nugbɔ ashɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: How does letting weeds grow on my farm hurt the amount of crop I harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots. They also hide dangerous pests and trap moisture that leads to plant rot, reducing your total yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu teeɔ, ni emɔɔ nu ni haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ nɔ ni baa shi.

english: What does it mean when experienced farmers talk about using 'fingers' or suckers to plant, and how do I prepare them?
ga: Kɛ́ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ wie ‘niji’ loo tsɔnei ni akɛmuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mihe?

english: In crops like plantains, bananas, or ginger, 'fingers' or suckers are the healthy shoots and rhizomes taken from a strong mother plant. You prepare them by trimming off dead roots and pests before planting them in moist soil so they can grow into high-yielding plants.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains, banana loo ginger mli lɛ, ‘niji’ loo ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni he wa kɛ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli. Osaa amɛ kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni egboi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ dani oduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What key inputs do I need to put into my field before planting to help my crops grow well?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ mikɛfata miŋmɔ lɛ he dani madu nii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Before planting, your crop needs good soil preparation, organic manure or compost to improve soil texture, and a balanced fertilizer to provide essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ asaa jogbaŋŋ. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium baa.

english: How does planting my crops too close together affect how they grow and produce?
ga: Te tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stems, small leaves, and low yield because no single plant gets enough food to thrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii, amɛbaa bibii, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ejaakɛ tsei komɛi nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and make food; when it is lacking in the soil, the plant moves its remaining nitrogen to the newer, top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa niyenii. Kɛ shikpɔŋ bɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plants produce thick green leaves but very small fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi aduawai loo ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When a plant grows lots of big leaves but small fruit, it usually means the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus, which are the nutrients that fuel flower and fruit development.
ga: Kɛ tso ko wo baai wuji babaoo shi ewo yibii bibii lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai daa lɛ

english: How does covering my crop soil with dry leaves or grass help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Te tsei ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It traps moisture beneath it so the sun cannot dry out the roots quickly, helping the plant stay hydrated during dry periods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off without forming fruit when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be Loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii.

english: Plantain plants fall over mainly because root pests like nematodes or weevils have damaged the root system, or because the original planting hole was too shallow to anchor the heavy plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo gboɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo weevils lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. aloo akɛni shishijee dumɔ bu lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ehiɛ tso ni tsii hewɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava crops curling up and developing light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with pale yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease. It is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from healthy plants and transfer a virus.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii anɔ. No shwieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa.

english: How can I tell whether my crops are suffering from insect damage or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi loo helai efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Insect damage usually leaves clear holes, chewed edges, or visible bugs on leaves. Disease damage usually appears as powdery spots, dark rot patches, or yellow patterns without visible insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii ni mli tse, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi, loo ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, helai ni efiteɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ diŋ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their stems back down into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ eshishifã lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants are unique because once their flowers are pollinated above ground, the stalks (called pegs) bend downward and grow into the soil, where the actual pods and nuts develop safely underground away from heat and sun.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ kɛ́ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã (ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg) lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni edaa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ shwereɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni hulutsoo kɛ hulu la bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Cassava leaves curl up during intense afternoon heat to reduce their surface area exposed to the sun. This natural reaction helps the plant conserve water and protect itself from drying out during hot dry spells.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground toward the sun. When the leaves spread out in direct sunlight, they trap energy to manufacture food, which is then stored underground to form bigger and healthier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gbɛ eshwa ni hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ebaamɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛfee niyenii. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛfee bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. The maize plant automatically pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Empty pods, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks enough calcium. Groundnut plants need calcium directly in the soil around their developing pods so the nuts can fill out properly inside the shell.
ga: Pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Peanut tsei lɛ he miihia calcium yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. developing pods Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ calcium afata ŋmeii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my field make my crops grow better than using no fertilizer at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko kwraa fataaa he lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients like nitrogen and organic matter. It improves soil texture, helping it hold water longer during dry days and giving plant roots a steady supply of food.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ

english: Why does my plantain tree grow so many small shoots around its base, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ, ni esa akɛ mafo amɛ?

english: Plantain trees produce extra shoots called suckers to multiply. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight the main tree for food and water, so you should remove most of them and keep only one or two strong ones for the next harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui woɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛkɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ́ ashi suckers babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ojie amɛteŋ babaoo ni okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1-2 pɛ ato kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in full sun. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, protecting the young plants from harsh sunlight and keeping the air moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my pepper plants early in the morning rather than in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ haa nu leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the roots to soak up water before the day gets hot. Afternoon watering causes much of the moisture to evaporate instantly into the air, and hot wet leaves can attract fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni baai ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes and small powdery droppings deep inside the center leaf funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ.

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm pests. The caterpillars crawl deep into the central funnel of the maize plant to hide from predators and hot weather while feeding on the soft, fresh growing leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe, yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni miida ehee lɛ hu.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and wilting after I irrigate them with water from the nearby river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: River water contaminated with mud, oil, or chemicals from upstream land clearing and illegal mining chokes plant roots. It blocks them from taking up clean water and vital nutrients, effectively poisoning the crops and causing them to starve.
ga: Faa mli nu lɛ mli ewo muji, fɔ loo tsofai ni jɛɔ faa lɛ ŋwɛi ŋshɔkei ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei shishifãi ni afoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli. Ehaaa amɛnu nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why does my soil become as hard as stone and fail to hold water after a short dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves, compost, or animal manure. Organic matter acts like a sponge, keeping the soil soft, open, and capable of holding moisture for your crop roots during dry periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, egbeleɔ, ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛhaa tsei shishifãi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and keeps the moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree before they even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, dark, and crowded farms. Pruning heavy cocoa branches allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni ewo duŋ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kookoo niji ni tsii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: What is eating ragged holes in my young maize leaves and destroying the center of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli ni efiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ mligbɛ?

english: This destruction is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They crawl deep inside the growing tip (whorl) of the maize plant to feed, which stops the corn from growing properly unless treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi (rings) lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao niyenii. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ja atsa lɛ mra.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming any actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛfeee pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Mulching the soil around the plant keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ la ni mli wa mli lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Ye obua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves and tall stems, but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil forces the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to expand its root tubers. Balanced soil nutrients are needed for good tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa yucca tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala shishifã lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ he miihia koni tuber lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize consumes high amounts of specific nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients completely and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo tsuɔ nii, tamɔ nitrogen, ni kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough rain and sunshine for every plant on the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that grow faster than crops. They steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and root space underground long before your crops can reach them, reducing your final harvest yield.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛju ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ahe gbɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abashɛ. Enɛ haa onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting when I give them lots of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ beni mikɛ nu babaoo haa amɛ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen from the soil just as much as they need water to sprout. Soaking the soil completely fills all air pockets, suffocating the seeds and encouraging soil fungi to rot them before they germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni amɛtaoɔ lɛ. kɛ nu ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo mli kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ eyi. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees necessary shade and moisture to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer brings back the dark green color and improves growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to drown, decay, and turn rotten.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room to grow strong and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How can my cassava crop stay alive even when the rains stop for months?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nyɔji babaoo po?

english: Cassava stores water and energy inside its thick underground roots. During dry periods, it can drop its top leaves to save water while keeping the roots alive in the soil.
ga: Cassava toɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ ekɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass acts like a protective blanket. It blocks the direct hot sun from drying out the dirt, keeping the soil cool and moist for longer periods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haaa muji agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I keep growing maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to multiply. Switching to beans or groundnuts restores nutrients and starves pest populations.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmeii loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yield even when there is plenty of rain for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients and light meant for your plants. Even with plenty of water, weeds starve your crops of essential food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ waa. Kɛ nu babaoo po yɛ mli lɛ, Jwɛi hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or dry soil stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Why do little insects bore holes into my harvested corn when I store it in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ mli beni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack stored corn if the grains are not thoroughly dried before storage or if the barn is damp. Drying corn completely and storing it in airtight containers prevents insect damage.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli efɔ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ kwraa ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite lɛ.

english: Why must I clear all the weeds and bushes from my farm before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This ensures your young crops get all the food and light they need to grow strong without being choked by wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni kɔɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa otsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni koo mli tsei etsĩii amɛ gbɛ.

english: How do I know the right time of year to start clearing my land for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi midumɔi lɛ ashishijee?

english: Land should generally be cleared just before the rainy season begins so the soil is ready when the rains start. Planting right after the first steady rains gives seeds the moisture they need to germinate.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it better to plant crop seeds directly into my big field or start them first in a small nursery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ agbo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mabɔi yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting delicate seeds in a shaded nursery protects young seedlings from harsh sun and heavy rain, allowing them to build strong roots before you transplant them into the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaaje shishi yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ baabu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi ni wa dani okɛ amɛ yaa saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: How long should I keep my young crop seedlings in the nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ dumɔwui bibii ahi ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Most crop seedlings are ready for transplanting after 3 to 6 weeks, once they have grown a few strong leaves and a sturdy root system that can survive field conditions.
ga: Tsei amli dumɔwui babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ, beni amɛyɛ baai fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi amli lɛ.

english: Why are agriculture officers recommending that I plant Moringa trees on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu Moringa tsei yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Moringa trees enrich the soil with nutrients, act as natural windbreaks to protect other crops, and produce leaves that serve as highly nutritious food and herbal medicine for your family.
ga: Moringa tsei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe. ni okɛ baai ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli waa kɛ tsofa ni jɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma mli aha oweku lɛ aba.

english: Can planting Neem trees near my food crops help protect them from insect pests?
ga: Ani neem tsei ni aduɔ yɛ mi niyenii tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, Neem leaves and seeds contain natural oils that act as organic pest repellents, helping to stop harmful insects from damaging your main food crops without using expensive chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli fɔji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ neem baai kɛ dumɔwui amli. Ye obua ni okpa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛkafite oniyenii titri ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: What does it mean when a crop is described as a beneficial plant for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛ́ atsɔɔ tso ko mli akɛ ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A beneficial plant is one that helps your farm beyond just yielding food, such as adding nitrogen to the soil, providing shade, repelling pests, or offering medicinal uses.
ga: Tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ji tsei ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ fe niyenii ni akɛhaa kɛkɛ, tamɔ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni haa hulutsoo, ni ashwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo tsofafeemɔ he sɛɛ ni akɛhaa.

english: Why do some crops grow better when planted alongside a different type of crop on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Different crops can help each other grow; for example, beans capture nitrogen from the air to feed nearby maize, while taller crops provide shade for low-lying plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi baanyɛ aye abua amɛhe. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hulutsoo.

english: How does leaving trees on my farmland help improve the soil for my crops?
ga: Te tsei ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Deep tree roots pull up water and minerals from deep underground. When the tree leaves drop and decay, they turn into natural fertilizer that feeds your crops.
ga: Tso shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛ tsei gbee shi ni amɛgboi Ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa onibii lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings dry up and die even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ nu ha amɛ po lɛ?

english: Young crops often dry up if the soil loses moisture quickly under strong heat. Putting dry grass or leaves around the base of the plant (mulching) keeps the soil moist and cool.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ fo oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi (mulch) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients or leave the soil waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility by fixing nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ekɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the early rains start in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives steady, wet rain for a few days so the ground is consistently moist deep down. Sowing after just one light rainfall can cause seeds to sprout and then wither quickly if dry weather returns for a couple of weeks.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ Dumɔ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting beans or groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize acts as a natural fertilizer, covers the ground to reduce weeds, and gives you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Mulch koni jwɛi lɛ aba shi ni eye ebua bo ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by long dry spells, lack of shade, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Proper pruning and planting shade trees like plantain help keep the crop cool and hydrated so flowers can turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ, hɔɔ ni bɛ, kɛ niyenii kpakpa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the air where they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber under the ground. It also keeps the leaves dry and off the wet soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Biɛ ji he ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo yɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ mli egbi ni sũ ni mli ewo fɔ bɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and rotting while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It often happens when watering is uneven—dry soil prevents the roots from taking up calcium, so keeping soil moisture steady with mulch helps solve the issue.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná calcium. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsu naagba lɛ he nii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures that your crops get full access to the nutrients you put in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid spraying pesticides on my crop flowers during the warm morning hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe yɛ mitsei lɛ afɔfɔi anɔ yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Spraying during the morning kills helpful insects like bees that visit open flowers to pollinate them. Without pollination, plants like peppers, cucumbers, and tomatoes cannot form good fruit, so spraying late in the evening is safer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni yaa fɔfɔi ni agbele naa lɛ amli koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ pollination bɛ lɛ, tsei tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, kukumba, kɛ tomato nyɛŋ awo yibii kpakpai. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots go bad and turn dark inside within just two days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fite ni etsɔ duŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start a natural chemical reaction as soon as they are cut away from the main plant and exposed to oxygen. Because they spoil so fast, cassava must be eaten, sold, or processed into flour or gari right away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ shishi kɛji afo amɛ kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli pɛ ni akɛ amɛ wo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli. Akɛni efiteɔ oya hewɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ aye Cassava, ahɔ̃ɔ, loo afee lɛ ashikishaŋ loo curry amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some green caterpillars on my vegetable leaves stay in one place all day without moving away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ ahe lɛ hiɔ he kome gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe lɛ?

english: Many leaf-eating larvae cannot fly or run. They conserve all their energy solely for eating and resting on the same spot, which helps them grow as fast as possible.
ga: Lalabii babaoo ni yeɔ baa lɛ nyɛɛɛ afã loo amɛjo foi. Amɛtoɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛye nii ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ he kome pɛ, ni no haa amɛdaraa oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ.

english: Why is it so easy to hand-pick some pests off my maize plants in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa akɛ majie tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi kɛjɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ?

english: Certain pests cannot fly or jump away quickly. After feeding heavily on your crops, they become sluggish and rest right on the leaves, making them easy to spot and remove.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ amɛfo loo amɛho oya. Beni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo niyenii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ Amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana ni ajie.

english: If a pest on my farm cannot fly or run, how does it survive without searching for food?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ afã loo amɛjo foi hu? Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ehi shi ni etaooo niyenii?

english: These pests don't need to search because they spend their whole lives right on their food source. They simply eat the leaf they are on, rest when full, and continue eating.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ atao niyenii ejaakɛ amɛkɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ taoɔ niyenii. Amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ kɛkɛ, amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛye nii, ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛyeɔ nii.

english: How do pests manage to lay so many eggs on my farm leaves without ever leaving the plant?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aaawo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛshiŋ tsei lɛ?

english: When a pest continuously feeds on your crop leaves, its body uses that nutrition directly to form and develop eggs right where it lives on the plant.
ga: Beni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ otsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ Egbɔmɔtso lɛ kɛ nakai niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ he ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I find insect eggs attached directly to the leaves where damage is happening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ anaa kooloi awui ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ baai ni efite lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Insects lay their eggs directly on the leaves they eat so that when the eggs hatch, the new young pests instantly have food available without having to travel anywhere.
ga: Kooloo lɛ fɔɔ ewui lɛ yɛ baai ni eyeɔ nii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. koni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii heei lɛ aná niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛfã gbɛ kɛya he ko.

english: Does a pest need to leave my farm to produce the next generation of insects?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashi miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛwo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: No, many crop pests complete their entire lifecycle—feeding, resting, growing, and forming eggs—on a single plant without ever needing to travel.
ga: Dabi, tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa—amɛyeɔ nii, amɛjɔɔ amɛhe, amɛdaraa. kɛ ŋmeii ni abɔɔ—yɛ tso kome nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni afã gbɛ.

english: Why does a single slow-moving worm cause so much damage to my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kome ni fãa blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai babaoo nɛkɛ?

english: Because these pests cannot travel far, all their daily activity is reduced to just eating and sleeping on your plant, leading to heavy continuous destruction of the leaf.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nyɛŋ aya shɔŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛ daa gbi nifeemɔi lɛ baa shi kɛyaa niyeli kɛ wɔɔ yɛ otsei lɛ amli. Enɛ kɛ baai lɛ akpãtãmɔ ni tsii ni yaa nɔ lɛ baa.

english: What happens inside a pest's body after it finishes eating large parts of my cassava leaves?
ga: Mɛni baa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli beni eye mi-cassava baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo sɛɛ?

english: The food energy the pest gets from eating your leaves immediately goes into forming eggs inside its body, preparing it to multiply on your field.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa kɛjɛɔ obaai lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, saa ohe ni ofɔ bii yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: How can I tell if a pest living on my crop is getting ready to multiply?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaafɔ bii?

english: When you see a stationary pest feeding heavily and resting repeatedly in the same spot, its body is actively using that food to form eggs for reproduction.
ga: Kɛ́ ona kooloi ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni miitao niyenii ni amɛmiijɔɔ amɛhe yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛgbɔmɔtso lɛ kɛ nakai niyenii lɛ feɔ wɔji kɛha fɔmɔ.

english: How can slow-moving pests spread to the rest of my farm if they cannot run or fly?
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yaa blɛoo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã hei krokomɛi. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛjo foi loo amɛfo?

english: While the adult pests stay put, eat, and lay eggs on one leaf, their newly hatched eggs and tiny young can easily be carried across your farm by wind, rain, or farm tools.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi ni eda lɛ baafɔ, amɛye, ni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ baa kome nɔ moŋ, Shi ŋmeii ni afɔ ehee kɛ amɛbii Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, loo okwaayeli nibii anɔ amɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure to the soil will help restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: My cassava plants have big green leafy tops, so why are the tubers under the ground so small?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to put all its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of swollen roots. Using potassium-rich inputs like wood ash or balanced fertilizer helps the plant send food down to form thicker tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Potassium ni fa babaoo tamɔ tso mli sũ loo sũ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii amaje shi koni efee bulbs ni mli wa.

english: Why do I get better crop yields when I plant my maize seeds further apart instead of crowding them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛ́ midu mi-ŋmã dumɔwui lɛ srɔtoi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛaafee ekome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and nutrients to produce big, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct heat from the sun and burn easily. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides shade and holds soil moisture, acting like a protective umbrella for the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshã oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni haa kookoo lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: The very first rainfall usually only wets the surface, leaving the soil dry underneath where seeds sit. Wait until the soil is damp at least hand-deep after two or three rainfalls so your planted seeds do not dry out and die after sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi yɛ he ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi. Mɛɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ onine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui ni adu lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, intense heat, or insect damage. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and planting during favorable weather stops the flowers from falling.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ miihao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli. Ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects. Spraying the leaves with safe neem oil solutions or soapy water helps clear the insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii lɛ ajie amɛhe.

english: What causes my yam tubers to turn soft and rot inside the soil mound before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Yam rot is caused by excess water trapped around the roots or fungal diseases in the soil. Building higher, well-drained soil mounds prevents waterlogging and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa, ni ebaaye ebua ni bulb lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted wild plants with deep roots designed to suck up water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops a head start to grow strong before weeds overpower them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔi lɛ aná hewalɛ waa dani jwɛi lɛ aye amɛnɔ kunim.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that natural fertilizer stays behind to feed the next crop, such as maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out their roots. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby shields them from harsh heat while they establish.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee hulutsoo ni naa wa waa beni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, exposing leaves to sunlight while preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in the middle of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure supplies this essential nutrient to make the leaves green and healthy again.
