ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant beans or groundnuts on land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni wɔkpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but leguminous crops like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot every single year result in smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, which weakens future harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my corn and leaving brown dust behind?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ ni mishiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms, which are caterpillars that nest inside the central whorl of young corn plants and destroy the leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni feɔ amɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just dig up any plantain sucker from an old farm to plant in my new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Older plantain suckers often carry hidden root pests or diseases. Using clean, disease-free suckers prevents spreading pests into your fresh soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain suckers ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ suckers ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã oshikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller yields even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients under the soil, effectively stealing food from your plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii. ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: As cassava plants age past their ideal harvest window, the roots deposit tough fibers and cellulose to support the plant, making the roots hard and difficult to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ho ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sa lɛ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ buaa ŋmeii ni wa kɛ cellulose naa koni amɛkɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewaa akɛ aaaho.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing pollination from taking place. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the unused flower.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa pollination aba. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni yeɔ omanye bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ ashwie.

english: How many bags of maize should I expect to harvest from one acre of land if the crop grows well?
ga: Abele kotokui enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ kɛji tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Under good weather conditions and proper care, one acre of improved maize in Ghana typically yields between 10 to 15 bags (about 1 to 1.5 metric tons) of dried grain.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa shishi lɛ, ŋmãa ni atsake lɛ acre kome yɛ Ghana lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni egbi ni falɛ shɛɔ kotokui 10 kɛyashi 15 (aaafee mɛtrik tɔn 1 kɛyashi 1.5) baa.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and weak without big fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni aduawai wuji bɛ mli beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants spend all their energy growing upward to reach light instead of building strong stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii beni amɛdaraa lɛ koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nguahi.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is fully mature and ready to harvest from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is mature when the husks covering the cob turn dry and brown, and a small black spot forms at the base of each grain where it meets the cob.
ga: Abɛi lɛ eda kɛji ŋmeii ni ha ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi yɛ he ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do cassava roots start to rot if I leave them in the ground for too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living storage organs. Once fully mature, excessive soil moisture and natural aging allow soil bacteria and fungi to break down the roots, causing rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji gbɔmɔtso mli nibii ni kɛ wala yibii toɔ. Kɛji eda kwraa lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ shishifãi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow during periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water fills the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, roots cannot absorb nitrogen from the ground, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my crops stop growing during the hot dry season even when I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo pɛ moŋ?

english: In high heat, crop leaves close their breathing pores to hold onto moisture. This stops food production inside the plant, slowing down growth even if the topsoil gets some water.
ga: Kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ba Tse lɛ baai lɛ ŋaa amɛmumɔ bu lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Enɛ haa niyenii ni afeɔ yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ mli lɛ kpaa. ni ehaa shweremɔ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa nu fioo moŋ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small, young pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? dani eda

english: This is often cherelle wilt, a natural reaction where the cocoa tree sheds extra young pods it cannot feed when it lacks enough soil nutrients, water, or light.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa kookoo tso lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ adu kɛha niyenii beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu loo la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Will planting beans alongside my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for nearby maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. Unfertilized flowers cannot form fruit and fall off the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. tsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and attract insects so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains moisture that attracts pests and molds. Drying the grain thoroughly under the sun hardens the seed skin and prevents insect eggs from hatching.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ amli nu ni gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do these new improved seeds actually help me harvest more crops than my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mikpaa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji fe blema dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, withstand weather changes, and produce bigger yields per acre compared to traditional seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ yɛ acre kome mli kɛ akɛtoɔ blema dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if the crop seed I am buying in town is a real certified seed and not a fake one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni awo he odaseyeli shi jeee amalei?

english: Certified seeds come in sealed bags with official government inspection tags (like green or blue tags in Ghana). Look for intact packaging and buy directly from licensed agro-dealers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo nɔ ni nɔyeli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ eji lɛ mli (tamɔ Green loo Blue Label yɛ Ghana). Taomɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he lɛ ni ohé kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvest of these new improved crops to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ amli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is best to buy fresh seeds each season because saved seeds from high-yielding hybrid varieties lose their vigor, disease resistance, and yield capacity in the next generation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai kɛ nyɛmɔ ni ayɔɔ ni akɛfeɔ nibii yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small yields when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants that produce small or incomplete cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry or flooded, or if soil pests eat them. Plant at the recommended depth when the soil is moist.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. loo kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔ yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ eshɛɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the ground has received two or three heavy rains and stays moist, rather than planting after the very first shower which might be followed by a long dry stretch.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo. Mohu ɔ, mo du ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se, nɛ eko ɔ, be kakadaŋŋ maa ba nɛ nyɛɛ se.

english: How do I know if my crop field needs fertilizer to grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, have light green or yellowish leaves instead of deep green, or produce small fruits, the soil lacks essential nutrients and needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. loo aha yibii bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What can I do to keep my crops from drying out when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass (mulching) holds water in the soil longer and protects plant roots from strong sun heat.
ga: Mulching around Kɛji okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) ha onibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni ebu tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he

english: How can I protect my harvested grain from being ruined by insects in my storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahe koni nitoohe mli kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: Ensure grain is dried completely until it is hard, clean your storehouse, and store the harvest in airtight hermetic bags or treat it with approved grain-preservation dust.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa ni amɛhe wa. Tsumɔ o nitoohe lɛ he ni okɛ nibii ni otsu lɛ ato kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli mli loo okɛ sũ ni akɛ buɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ atsu he nii.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels feel hard. If you push your fingernail into a kernel and it does not leave a dent or release milk, the crop has finished growing and is ready to be picked.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa Kɛji okɛ otsitsi wo dumɔwui lɛ amli ni eshiii ŋmei loo ejieee nu, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why is it important for air to flow through my corn right after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn holds a lot of hidden water inside the cob and grains. Good airflow carries that moisture away; without air movement, the trapped water causes the corn to heat up, rot, and spoil quickly.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni akɛtee ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni tsiɔ ehe Nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ mli adɔ, egbo ni efite oya.

english: Why does my harvested maize shrink and lose weight after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize shrinks because it loses water weight as it dries out. This water loss is a natural and healthy process that hardens the grain, making it safe to store without spoiling.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ nu lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi beni egbiɔ lɛ. Nu ni laajeɔ nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ni haa ŋmaa lɛ mli waɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ amɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteee.

english: Is it better to dry my harvested corn in a ventilated wooden structure or directly on the bare ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaagbi ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ tso ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A ventilated wooden structure is much better because it lets wind dry the crop evenly while keeping it elevated above damp soil, rain runoff, farm animals, and pests that easily ruin corn left on the ground.
ga: Tsoi ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ amɛwomɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ.

english: What will happen to my corn if I pack too much of it into a tight storage space?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa babaoo wo he ko ni akɛ ŋmãa toɔ ni mli ejɔ?

english: When corn is packed too tightly, air cannot pass between the cobs. The trapped moisture creates internal heat, which causes the corn in the middle to mold, rot, or even sprout before you can sell or eat it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abɔ ŋmãa he waa tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa emli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ shwieɔ, egboɔ, loo ekwɛɔ po dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye.

english: If I put my dry corn in the same storage structure as my neighbor's damp corn, will my crop be safe?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni egbi to he ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe?

english: Your dry crop will be at risk. Moisture travels through the air, so damp corn will release humidity into the room, causing your dry corn to absorb water, warm up, and become vulnerable to rot and insects.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ baafee oshara. Fɛ̃i tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni mli efɔ lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛbote tsu lɛ mli. Ha o-corn ni egbi lɛ aŋɔ nu. hulutsoo ni amɛyɔɔ oshara akɛ amɛbaafite kɛ kooloi

english: Should I strip the outer husks off my maize cobs before putting them in storage?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ dani mikɛto?

english: Removing the husks helps the grains dry out much faster because the air can reach the kernels directly. However, if the corn is already very dry, leaving tight husks on can act as a natural blanket against some flying pests.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya kwraa ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi waa momo lɛ, ŋmãa ni mli wa lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa komɛi.

english: Why does my stored corn develop a white powdery coating or black spots after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powda yɛŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: That white powder or black spot is mold, which is a tiny organism that feeds on damp crops. It grows whenever corn is stored before it is completely dry or when stored in a dark place without fresh air.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ loo ŋmeii diji ji ŋmeii. ni ji nɔ ko bibioo ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli efɔ Ekwɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmãa toɔ dani egbiɔ kwraa loo kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni duŋ ewo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why do small insects like weevils appear in my stored corn even if I clean the storage room carefully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mitsumɔ nibii atoohe lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ po?

english: Weevil eggs are often laid inside the corn kernels while the crop is still growing in the field. When you harvest and store the corn in a warm place, those hidden eggs hatch into adult insects that eat the inside of the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛwoɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii miida lolo yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Beni okpaa ŋmãa ni okɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ Nakai ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni eda ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why does heat build up inside a pile of harvested grain even when the sun is not shining on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ? He ni hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Harvested grain is still 'breathing' living tissue. When wet grains are piled together, their natural breathing releases heat and moisture, which gets trapped in the middle of the pile and makes it feel hot to the touch.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ ji fãji ni hiɛ ka lolo ni ‘muɔ’ kɛ́ abua nibii ni efɔ lɛ anaa. Mumɔ jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋtayaa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni enuɔ he akɛ edɔ kɛji eta he.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base will help the plant regain its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients, while cowpeas put natural nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating these crops heals the land so your next crop can grow strong without relying heavily on bought fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, cowpea kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa he ko hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anyɛ adara waa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe lɛ anɔ waa.

english: Why does my soil produce good harvests during the first year but weak yields after two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi ewoɔ yibii ni waaa yɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground every season. If you continuously harvest without adding organic manure or giving the soil time to rest, the land loses its fertility and cannot feed new plants properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji oya nɔ okpaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them and stays in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: What makes my yam tubers grow short and crooked instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ kuku ni ebɔleɔ shi moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadamɔ kɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Hard, stony, or tightly packed soil prevents growing yam tubers from stretching downwards. Digging deep, loose, soft mounds gives the tubers room to expand smoothly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi sweet potato ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anaa koni amɛkashi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni etse ehe, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni akuɔ lɛ baaha tuber he lɛ alɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering stress the tomato plant, causing it to shed its flowers to conserve energy. Keeping the soil evenly moist during flowering helps the blossoms set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni afɔɔɔ amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping them cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of leaves. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or soapy water helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are made by hungry caterpillars or beetles eating the plant tissue. Removing the caterpillars by hand or using natural insect sprays will protect the leaves so heads can form properly.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ladybugs ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmeii lɛ loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are black pods forming on my cocoa trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a water-loving fungal disease that spreads quickly when cocoa farms stay too damp and dark. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air into the farm, drying out the moisture that the fungus needs to spread.
ga: Black pods ji hela ko ni hydrophilic fungus kɛbaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji kookoo ŋmɔji amli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni he hiaa ni ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: How can I get quality seeds and support from my district agricultural office?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná dumɔwui ni hi kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ mi Kpokpaa nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: District agricultural offices run government support programs where they share input costs with local farmers, providing high-yielding seeds and technical advice to boost your farm produce.
ga: Kpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ tsuɔ maŋ yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ahe nii. Abaajara nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ aha maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi lɛ. Ekɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ ŋaawoo ni kɔɔ ŋaa he haa koni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does the extension officer need to measure the size of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ asusu miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ he lɛ?

english: Measuring your farm helps calculate the exact amount of seeds and fertilizer you need, and allows agricultural officers to accurately estimate how much crop yield your farm will produce.
ga: Kɛ́ osusu oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni obu dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he baahia bo lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa. ni ehaa okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ buɔ nibii ni oŋmɔ lɛ baawo lɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and skinny without big cobs when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ? ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of growing strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a plant's natural defense to reduce surface area, helping it save moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly in the heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ehiɛ ni ebaa shi lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems rather than deep taproots, making them top-heavy and easy for strong winds to push over when bearing heavy fruit bunches unless supported with wooden stakes.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni tsii, ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli kɛ́ eewo aduawai akui ni tsii. ja tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: How can I tell if my farmland is healthy and good for crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well, contains earthworms, and naturally grows dark green, leafy vegetation rather than pale or stunted weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ. ni edaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ jwɛi ni mli tse loo ni egbɔjɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow when there is heavy rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rain waterlogs the soil, which suffocates the root system and washes away important nutrients like nitrogen that keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests swarm my cowpea crop as soon as the flowers open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miibɔle mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and bright colors that naturally attract sap-sucking insects like thrips and pod borers looking for food.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu mli nu kɛ sui ni kpɛɔ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers ni miitao niyenii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What will happen if I leave crowded vegetable seedlings to grow without thinning them out?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miha aduawai dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ ni mifeee amɛ bibioo?

english: Leaving overcrowded seedlings forces them to compete for root space and nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stems and very small or low-quality crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashiɔ amɛyiɔ obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa loo amɛhe ehiaaa tsɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting early in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo ekwɛ̃ mra lɛ? Yɛ nitoohe?

english: Yams rot from trapped moisture and heat, while bright light and warmth signal to the tuber that it is time to sprout; keeping them in a cool, shaded, well-ventilated barn prevents this.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ dɔlɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kane kɛ dɔlɛ haa tsɔnei lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Can I feed my maize crop only urea fertilizer, or does it need other plant foods to produce big cobs?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ urea awo ŋmã tsei amli kɛkɛ? Aloo esa akɛ akɛ niyenii ni jɛ tsei krokomɛi amli lɛ atsu nii ni akɛfee ŋmeii wuji?

english: Just like people need more than just one type of food to stay strong, crops cannot thrive on nitrogen alone. Urea helps maize leaves grow green and tall, but the crop also needs phosphorus for strong roots and potassium for big, full cobs; using only urea leaves the plant weak and prone to falling over.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii srɔtoi ni fa fe ekome he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ nitrogen pɛ nɔ. Urea yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa. Shi tsei hu he miihia phosphorus kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ urea pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize turn yellow and dry up even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves is a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. When soil nutrients run low, the crop actively moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new leaves at the top, causing the lower ones to turn yellow and die.
ga: Kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ, ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Is it fine if I keep planting cassava on the same piece of land year after year without adding manure?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ ŋmei fataaa he?

english: Cassava pulls a lot of nutrients out of the earth as its roots grow. If you keep planting it in the same spot without adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes completely exhausted, resulting in much smaller yields each season.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni eshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite, ni no baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kwraa yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their blossoms before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as sudden hot spells, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and rich in organic matter helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa trukaa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why is my cocoa farm dropping many of its small young pods during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ ashwieɔ lɛ? Lots yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees drop young pods as a natural survival response to protect themselves when water is scarce. Keeping shade trees on the farm and spreading dried leaves or grass around the base of the cocoa trees helps hold moisture in the soil and reduces pod drop.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo hetoo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he kɛji nu faaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛshwieɔ amɛhe Cocoa tso lɛ shishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cowpea crops make my main maize crop grow greener when I plant them together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ haa mi-corn titri lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ amɛ feɔ ekome yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special root nodules that pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it directly into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the plot?
ga: Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of getting more harvest, you end up with thin, weak plants that produce tiny ears or roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakpa babaoo lɛ Ebatsɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni toi bibii loo shishifãi yɔɔ mli.

english: Can I save seeds from the high-yielding hybrid maize I harvested last season and plant them again this year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ afi nɛɛ?

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid maize lose their high vigor and disease protection in the second generation. If you replant saved hybrid seeds, the resulting plants will grow unevenly and produce much smaller yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahebuu yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Tsei ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛbaawo yibii bibii kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: Can I just throw my granular fertilizer on top of dry soil and leave it there until it rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji granular lɛ mashwie shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni mashi jɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ?

english: Fertilizer left exposed on top of dry ground gets lost into the hot air or washed away by sudden heavy rains. For fertilizer to work, it should be buried slightly in moist soil near the crop's root zone so the roots can drink it up.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ atsu nii Esa akɛ afu fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and stop producing fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during dry periods partly to save water, but severe curling combined with stunted growth usually means tiny insects like whiteflies have infected the crop with a virus. Treating the insects early and keeping plants well-watered keeps the crop healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛfataa dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ he lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies emɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kplukai ni akwɛɔ amɛ mra Kɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ koni amɛná nu kpakpa lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures they all get enough resources to grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛnáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How does putting dry grass or leaves on top of my crop bed help my plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist by slowing down water evaporation. It also blocks light from reaching weeds, preventing them from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ la hu naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkadara

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which travels down to swell and enlarge the yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eyafutu ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi yam tsei lɛ amli

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist and crops are actively growing. Avoid applying right before heavy rainfall, as running water will carry the nutrients away from the plant roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni tsei miida lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Ejaakɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of specific soil nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli.

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the tender inner funnel of young corn plants where they feed on new foliage before the ears develop.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli he ni amɛyeɔ baai heei dani toi lɛ baa lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot and smell bad in the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot is usually caused by excessive water sitting around the roots in poorly drained soil during heavy rains, which allows destructive fungi to multiply and attack the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu babaoo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni kpataa nii ahiɛ lɛ feɔ babaoo ni etutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when planted in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate foliage and shallow roots that dry out quickly under direct, intense sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them until they establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaawo shishifãi.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot rapidly drains specific soil nutrients and lets maize-specific pests and diseases build up in the soil, leading to weaker harvests each season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi baajɛ mli oya. ni eha ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a plant usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crops need to stay green, and when there is not enough in the soil, the plant pulls it from the older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab natural nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the maize naturally and keeps your soil rich for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni ooodu lɛ baaha abele akwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings get burnt and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like small babies—they cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains growing nearby to protect them, the harsh heat will scorch their leaves and dry out the young stems.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii tamɔ abifabii bibii. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ, koni akɛbu tsei ahe Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ agbi.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops end up fighting for the same sunlight, water, and soil food. Because none of them get enough food, they stretch high for sun but do not have enough strength to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu he akaŋ. Ejaakɛ amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, ekpã ehe koni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Shi hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ bɛ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if I just leave them to grow in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. They also hide pests and diseases that can jump onto your crops and destroy your yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and stays there for too long without draining away. Cassava tubers need loose, well-drained soil; excess water suffocates the roots and causes rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehi jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, usually caused by too much heat, lack of water, or putting too much chemical fertilizer at once.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ babaoo, nu ni bɛ, loo tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell. If you plant too early, the sun will dry out the soil and kill the young germinating seeds before the main rains settle.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark green waste inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls deep into the growing center of the maize plant during the night to feed on leaves before they open up.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ gbɛkɛ koni eye baai lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Tomato leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that carry a disease from plant to plant, or by severe water stress when the plant experiences sudden dry heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni hiɛ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa mli beni tsei naa latsaa ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like cigars when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ sigaret yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll up their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water through evaporation during intense heat and dry spells.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava plants dropping their leaves during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive, and it will sprout new leaves once the rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ekɛto nu ni ekɛha wala ahi shi. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ nɛ lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my young crops refusing to grow tall even though I planted them weeks ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaadara eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ otsii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need water to absorb nutrients from the soil, so without enough rain or moisture, plants stop growing to save energy and protect themselves.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛ nu niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa Koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ebu ehe lɛ, tsei kpaɔ amɛdalɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dried grass help them when it doesn't rain?
ga: Mulching around Te jwɛi yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, blocking direct sunlight so the ground stays cool and keeps its moisture for a much longer time.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be babaoo.

english: It is best to water in the early morning because the water sinks deep into the root zone before the hot afternoon sun can evaporate it away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi ejaakɛ nu lɛ baabote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I collect water on my farm so my plants do not die when the rain stops coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mitsei lɛ akagboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ?

english: You can dig simple water collection pits or build earth mounds called micro-basins around your plants to trap rainwater right on your field for later use.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nutoohe ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Aloo otswa gɔŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ tsɛnsi bibioo ko obɔle he. O tsei lɛ koni okɛmɔ nugbɔ nu ni yɔɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ koni okɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli.

english: Which crops can I plant on my land if my area receives very little rain?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, sorghum, millet, and cowpeas are drought-tolerant because they either have deep roots or require very little water to give a good harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ loo amɛbiɔ nu fioo koni amɛná ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: You should wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked the soil deep down to the depth of your hand, ensuring seeds have enough wet soil to sprout and grow roots.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tamɔ oniji. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi.

english: Why do my tomato plants dry up quickly without water while my yam crops last much longer without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigbo oya kɛ nu bɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɔ shi be babaoo ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have shallow roots and thin stems that dry out fast, whereas yams store nutrients and water underground in their tubers to keep them alive.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu toɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛhi shi.

english: What happens if I plant my crops in dry soil before the rain actually falls?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Seeds planted in completely dry soil will either sit inactive and get eaten by pests or germinate partially and die from heat before the rains arrive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ amɛ loo amɛfã ko kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does planting start earlier in the Southern part of Ghana than in the North?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni aje dumɔ shishi mra yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ fe kooyigbɛ lɛ?

english: Southern Ghana gets its main rains early in the year around March or April, while Northern Ghana has a single rainy season that starts later around May or June. Planting must align with when rain falls in your specific region so the seeds get enough water to grow.
ga: Ghana kooyigbɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli aaafee March loo April. Ghana Kooyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome ni jeɔ shishi yɛ May loo June naagbee gbɛ. Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is the main difference between the major rainy season and the minor rainy season for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji shishijee kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ teŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The major rainy season brings longer, heavier rains which are best for crops that take a long time to grow, like maize. The minor season has shorter, lighter rains, which are better for quick-maturing crops like cowpeas, vegetables, or short-duration maize.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa. Be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waaa. Enɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tsina ŋmei, aduawai loo ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kukuoo.

english: Why do my crops yield so poorly if I plant them late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai kɛji midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Crops planted late run out of rainwater before they finish producing flowers and seeds. When rain stops while the crop is still developing, the plant starves for water, leading to small, dry, or unfilled harvests.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo Nugbɔ nu lɛ ho dani fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ gbe fɔmɔ naa. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tsei lɛ, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi, amɛgbi loo amɛshɛɛɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and traps moisture inside to survive heat stress.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni nu babaoo akafite. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ koni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants during periods of very heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours can physically knock delicate blossoms off the stems. Additionally, saturated, waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing properly, causing stress that makes the plant shed its flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ajɛ tsei lɛ ashishi, ni shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu hu haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi baa.

english: Why do my seeds sprout so quickly after the very first heavy rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds stay dormant in dry soil until moisture wakes them up. The first heavy rain softens the seed coat and supplies the high moisture and soil heat needed to trigger rapid root growth within days.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baate amɛ shi. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ ni he hiaa koni eha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear my land and buy seeds weeks before the rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mahe dumɔwui otsii komɛi dani nugbɔ lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Preparing early ensures your field is ready to capture the very first rains. If you wait until it rains to start clearing and buying seeds, your crop will miss the best soil moisture and lose valuable growing days.
ga: Hesaamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha oŋmɔji lɛ afee klalo kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. Kɛji omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ dani obɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ kɛ dumɔwui ahemɔ. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaafite gbii ni he hiaa ni akɛkwɛɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is wet before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that roots can drink up. If you apply dry fertilizer to dry soil, it cannot feed the plant and can actually scorch and damage the roots when the sun gets hot.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛfee nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi he lɛ Enyɛŋ eha tsei lɛ niyenii. ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ

english: Which crops are best suited for areas in Northern Ghana that experience long dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like sorghum, millet, groundnuts, and cowpeas are best. They have deep root systems or tough leaf structures that allow them to survive with far less rainfall than water-heavy crops.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsina ŋmei ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni mli wa ni haa amɛhiɔ shi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo fe tsei ni nu tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings survive better when I transplant them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo he kroko leebi lɛ?

english: Early morning air is cooler and soil moisture is higher. Transplanting early gives fragile young roots a few hours to settle into their new position before the severe heat of the midday sun stresses the plant.
ga: Leebi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hu fa babaoo. Tsei ni aduɔ mra Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ náa ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi koni amɛyahi he ko hee dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings look very healthy in the nursery, but die shortly after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi beni mijie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ ni amɛgboi.

english: Seedlings experience transplant shock when suddenly moved from a shaded nursery to a sunny field. Slowly reducing shade and water a week before moving them helps the plants adapt and survive in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa beni trukaa lɛ Ajie lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ mli lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ mli lɛ mli. Shade kɛ nu ni ajieɔ lɛ shi fiofio Otsi kome dani ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Is it better to plant my cabbage seeds directly into the farm soil or start them in a nursery bed first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu cabbage dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting tiny seeds in a nursery protects them from harsh sun, heavy rain, and pests. Once they grow strong stems, they can handle the tougher conditions of the main farm field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ashishijee Yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe kɛji amɛná ŋmeii ni wa pɛ. Amɛnyɛ amɛkpee shihilɛ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: If I store my harvested maize seeds carefully in dry sacks, why do some of them still fail to grow when I plant them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ to kotokui ni egbi mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds naturally lose their vigor over time, especially if the air temperature changes often. Even if seeds look good on the outside, internal life reduces the longer they stay in storage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Titri lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ tsakeɔ shii abɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ, Shi mligbɛ wala be lɛ baa shi kɛ be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from the high-yielding hybrid maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for one generation only. If you plant seeds saved from a hybrid harvest, the new plants will grow unevenly and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛhaa yinɔ kome pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ hybrid harvest mli lɛ Tsei heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the dry Harmattan winds start blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture out of young leaves faster than roots can draw water from the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around young cocoa protects them from these harsh winds.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɛɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and dry out even when I water them every day during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes plants to lose water faster than their roots can take it up, making leaves curl to protect themselves. Applying mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: When my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during a dry spell, is the crop dead?
ga: Kɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during drought on purpose to save water and keep its underground roots alive. Once the rains return, the plant will shoot fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ abaato nu he gbɛjianɔ ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: I weed my maize farm regularly and take good care of it, so why are the cobs still very small?
ga: Mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni mikwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Removing weeds prevents competition, but plants still need food. Without enough soil nutrients like nitrogen, maize plants cannot build large, heavy cobs even if the field is clean.
ga: Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ akaŋshii naa. Shi niyenii he miihia tsei lolo. Kɛ́ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa tsei nyɛŋ afee ŋmãa agboi ni tsii. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse po

english: I added fertilizer to my crops just like my neighbor did, so why did my crops turn yellow and burn instead of growing?
ga: Mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔji amli tamɔ bɔ ni mikutsoŋbii lɛ feɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer can burn root stems if applied too close to the plant or when the soil is completely dry. Fertilizer must be placed a short distance from the stem when the soil is moist.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa.

english: Flowers drop off due to high heat, lack of water, or because insects are not visiting to pollinate them. Consistent watering and avoiding chemical sprays during flowering helps fruits stay attached.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo akɛni kooloi bibii baasara amɛ koni amɛbawo amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight without enough shade and moisture. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains nearby keeps the soil cool and provides shade to help the cocoa survive.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ tsei bibii, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down so easily when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems, making them top-heavy when bearing fruit. Supporting the main stem with sturdy bamboo poles or wooden forks prevents wind and heavy fruit weight from pulling the plant down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Ehaa efeɔ tsii kɛji ewo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala tso lɛ kɛba shi.

english: Why are there small holes and ragged edges on my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ amɛhe ni etse lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center leaves of the maize plant. Inspecting the field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a short dry period that can dry out newly germinated seeds. Waiting for the rains to become regular ensures the soil stays moist enough for young crops to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni tsei bibii akwɛ̃.

english: Those bumps are root nodules filled with beneficial bacteria that capture nitrogen from the air and convert it into plant food, which actually enriches your soil naturally.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii, ni no diɛŋtsɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know my cassava is ready to harvest if the tubers grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛmiida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and falling off, and small cracks appear in the soil near the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines off the ground using stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking helps the yam leaves catch maximum sunlight to make food for bigger tubers, while keeping the leaves off hot, wet ground prevents fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulb wuji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus they spread. Spraying organic insecticides or soap solution early helps protect the plant.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo samla ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baashwie nɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit due to uneven watering. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for nitrogen and other essential nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures all soil nutrients go straight to feeding your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehe hia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa otsei titrii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do older farmers advise me not to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How does adding black compost or manure help my crops grow better than relying on chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Compost acts like a sponge in the dirt—it holds moisture during dry spells, softens hard soil so roots can spread easily, and slowly feeds the plant natural nutrients that chemical fertilizers cannot provide.
ga: Kompost tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo, ni fiofio lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aha lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by too much direct sunlight, hot dry winds, or lack of soil water. Maintaining proper shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay attached and mature into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ, loo nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they compete with the mother plant for food and water from the soil. Leaving only one strong sucker ensures the main plant gets enough strength to produce a huge, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Sucker ni mli wa kome ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo dumɔwui wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them past maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji miha amɛdara tsɔ lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots continue to absorb water from wet ground, which makes them soft and vulnerable to soil bacteria and fungi. Harvesting them as soon as they reach full maturity prevents rot and preserves quality.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni eda lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmɔɔ nu kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ pɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛfite, ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually because watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant draw calcium smoothly into the growing fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ awo aduawai ni miida lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain often tricks farmers because the deep soil underneath remains dry and hot. If a sunny dry spell follows right after, your sprouted seeds will dry up and die before their roots can reach deeper moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa okwaafoi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Kɛji hulu la ni mli egbi yɛ lɛ, ebaanyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ he.

english: Weeds steal essential sunlight, rain, and soil food away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early eliminates this competition, letting your crops use all available resources to grow big and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leafy tube of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-insecticides or neem oil into the center leaves prevents them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: I farm around Techiman, what types of food crops are best suited for my land?
ga: Mifeɔ ŋmɔ yɛ Techiman he fɛɛ he. Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Techiman has an excellent climate and soil for growing major grain and legume crops, particularly rice, beans, sorghum, soybeans, and millet.
ga: Techiman yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmaa kɛ ŋmãa ni he hiaa waa, titri lɛ, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, soybeans kɛ ŋmãa.

english: What is this product called Multicroft Treasure and what does it do for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ Multicroft Treasure nɛɛ ni te ehaa miŋmɔ lɛ he baa sɛɛnamɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Multicroft Treasure is a specialized agricultural input designed to support and boost the growth of various staple crops, including grains like rice, millet, and sorghum, as well as legumes like beans and soybeans.
ga: Multicroft Treasure ji okwaayeli he nibii ni he esa waa ni afee koni eye ebua ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji srɔtoi ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ soybeans lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Can I use the same crop treatment for both my grain crops like rice and my legumes like beans?
