ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa fɛɛ?

english: Yes, certain general crop boosters and treatments, such as Multicroft Treasure, are versatile enough to be safely applied across both grain crops like rice and cereal and legume crops like beans and soybeans.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai komɛi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe hewalɛ kɛ tsamɔi, tamɔ Multicroft Treasure lɛ, yɛ srɔtoi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ fɛɛ nɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmaa. kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ soybeans shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it difficult for smallholder farmers to sell crops directly to markets in the European Union?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa kɛha okwaafoi bibii akɛ amɛaahɔ̃ɔ amɛŋmɔshinii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya EU jarayeli hei lɛ?

english: The European Union has strict food safety, chemical residue, and quality control regulations that require specific certifications and high-standard farming practices that smallholder operations are often still working to meet.
ga: Europa Kuu lɛ yɛ niyenii he shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai. Tsofai ni eshwɛ kɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa Enɛ biɔ odaseyeli pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ahe mlai ni nɔ kwɔlɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, jarayelɔi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bɔni afee ni amɛfee nakai

english: Why does planting soybeans or beans in my field help the grains I plant next season grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybeans loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soybeans and beans are legumes, which naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, leaving valuable nutrients behind for heavy-feeding grains like rice and millet.
ga: Soya kɛ ŋmeii ji ŋmeii. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Amɛshiɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmaa ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Why do sorghum and millet stay green during dry spells while rice suffers quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yeɔ amanehulu oya lɛ?

english: Sorghum and millet have deep root systems and natural structures that conserve water, making them naturally heat- and drought-tolerant compared to rice, which requires high moisture levels.
ga: Sorghum kɛ millet yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa nu hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni biɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ he.

english: How can a smallholder farmer improve crop yields on a small plot of land without expensive machines?
ga: Te okwaafoi bibii lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔji bibii ni tsɔnei ni jara wa bɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Small-scale farmers can maximize yields by using supportive crop treatments like Multicroft Treasure, practicing proper crop spacing, and combining nitrogen-fixing crops like beans with staple grains.
ga: Okwaafoi bibii baanyɛ aná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ Multicroft Treasure, ni ji tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ dumɔwui titrii lɛ afata he.

english: How do I tell if my millet or sorghum plants are growing healthily in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy millet and sorghum show strong upright stalks, broad dark-green leaves without yellow streaks, and full, tight head formation during flowering.
ga: Shɔm kɛ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni ja. Baai lɛ dara, eŋɔli diŋŋ, ni ŋmɔŋ bɛ he. kɛ yitso ni mli edɔ ni eye emuu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why do international agricultural buyers care so much about what inputs we put on our grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ okwaayeli he jarayelɔi lɛ susuɔ nibii ni wɔkɛwoɔ wɔŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ he waa lɛ?

english: Foreign markets check crops for chemical residues to protect consumer health; unapproved or overused inputs can cause an entire harvest to be rejected at international borders.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu mɛi ni yeɔ nii lɛ ahewalɛ he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha akpoo ŋmaa fɛɛ yɛ majimaji ateŋ husui anɔ.

english: Do my soybean plants need the exact same care and nutrients as my rice plants?
ga: Ani mi-soybean tsei lɛ he miihia amɛkwɛmɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai tamɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ?

english: No, soybeans make much of their own nitrogen food from the soil air, whereas cereal grains like rice rely entirely on nutrients drawn directly from the soil and added fertilizers.
ga: Dabi, soybeans feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen niyenii lɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa tamɔ omɔ damɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow so tall with many leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are planted too close together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and letting sunlight reach the foliage so the underground tuber can grow bigger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fɔmɔ helai anaa ni oha hulu la lɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or a lack of water. Without enough moisture, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ kpe. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worms hide inside the growing tip of the maize plant during the day and feed on young leaves, leaving behind holes and tiny droppings that look like dark sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni amɛshiɔ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that enters through the roots and blocks the plant's internal water tubes. Because the tubes are blocked, water cannot reach the leaves, causing the plant to wilt rapidly even in wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli kɛboteɔ mli ni etsĩɔ tsei amli nu paipii lɛ anaa lɛ kɛbaa. ejaakɛ paipii lɛ efo No hewɔ lɛ nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei gboɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ po.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun and hot winds. Without shade plants to protect them and keep the surrounding air cool, the leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can absorb it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they compete with it for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones and allows the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, dumɔwu titri lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni ena nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with natural soil organisms to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, this nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains before putting dry fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can take it in. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots or cause the nutrients to evaporate into the air before the plant can use them.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why can rice grow in flooded water while my maize crop rots if water stays on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu afua nu mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu kã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their stems that carry oxygen from the leaves down to the roots underwater. Maize roots lack these channels, so standing water suffocates and rots the roots by cutting off their oxygen.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die between November and May even if I try to water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ November kɛ May teŋ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ mawo nɔ nu moŋ

english: This period is the long dry season (Harmattan) in Ghana. Strong, dry winds and hot sun cause plants to lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Using organic mulch around the plant bases helps retain soil moisture, and creating simple shading structures protects young crops from extreme sun.
ga: Enɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ (harmattan) yɛ Ghana. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi kɛ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ni hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaafee lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in an open field without trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and sensitive to direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing companion crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary living shade, which lowers the air temperature around the young cocoa trees and protects their leaves from sunburn during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nuɔ he waa. Hefatalɔi tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Rainwater often washes nutrients out of topsoil. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Nugbɔ nu hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant four or five seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɛɔ etsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ

english: When too many seeds grow in the same hole, the roots fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil food. Planting fewer seeds per stand and spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough nutrition to grow thick, strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Be mli ni dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ. Shishifãi wuɔ koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli ni akɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse, ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or sudden water shortages. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering or mulching prevents the plant from dropping its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and collapse during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks the internal tubes the plant uses to carry water. Because the plant cannot transport water upward, it collapses under heat. Rotating tomatoes with non-susceptible crops like maize helps stop this disease from building up in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa nu lɛ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ nu aya ŋwɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, efoɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la mli. Tomato ni akɛ tsei ni nyɛɛɛ atswa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela nɛɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and branched instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ niji moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep, stone-free soil to push downward smoothly. Hard or compacted soil forces the growing root to bend and branch out sideways as it tries to find softer soil.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛba shi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baaha shishifãi ni miida lɛ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛje kpo kɛya afã be mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛna shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest every time I plant cassava on the exact same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating cassava with legumes, such as cowpeas or groundnuts, fixes nitrogen back into the soil and restores fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: This pattern is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny flying whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents prevents this virus from damaging your crop yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ mfoniri nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni foɔ loo tsei niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ okɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni o-extension agent lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why does maize planted in the major rainy season grow taller than maize planted in the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ daa fe ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fioo mli lɛ?

english: The major rainy season offers longer periods of continuous moisture and cooler temperatures, allowing plants to photosynthesize and grow steadily. The minor season is shorter and subject to early dry spells, which limits maximum plant height and yield.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni mli ejɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ fotosintɛsis ni amɛdaraa daa. Be ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ kuku ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi mra. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nɔyaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees nearby to cool the air and keep moisture in the soil, the severe heat causes the leaves to burn and dry up.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ Koni kɔɔyɔɔ aba ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha baai lɛ ashã ni amɛgbi.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. If the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the plant's sap and spreading viruses. It can also happen when the plant is trying to protect itself from extreme heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji tsei bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he.

english: These caterpillars are known as Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks maize. They hide deep inside the growing funnel of the plant to feed on fresh leaves, which can destroy the crop if not controlled early.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei adalɛ gbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai heei. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during light rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are often weakened under the ground by tiny pests called banana weevils or nematodes. These pests burrow into the underground stem, destroying the roots that anchor the heavy plant to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni baa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ haa plantain shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ banana ŋmei loo nematode. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei amli. Efiteɔ shishifãi ni ŋmɛɔ tso ni tsii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if rain falls heavily near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave the ground waterlogged for too long, the roots suffocate and harmful fungal diseases quickly set in, causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ yeɔ nɔ oya. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why do agriculture officers advise me to grow groundnuts or cowpeas on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them enriches the ground with natural fertilizer, helping the next crop like maize grow much better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, ni ji ŋmãa lɛ, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer into the soil at the exact same time I plant my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui duɔ lɛ?

english: Strong fertilizer placed directly against a tender seed or fresh sprout can burn the emerging delicate roots. It is safer to wait until the plant has sprouted and formed proper roots to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui heei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwereɔ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni efee shishifãi ni sa koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop black mold inside the bag even after I dried it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ

english: Maize grains can feel dry on the outside while still holding moisture deep inside. If you bag maize before it is completely dried to the core, trapped moisture creates heat and fungal growth, leading to toxic molds like aflatoxin.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa lɛ baanu he akɛ egbi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ emli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Trapped moisture haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmãa baa. Ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ aflatoxin baa.

english: Why do my stored yams become soft, wrinkled, and start sprouting shoots in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ blɛoo, egbɔjɔ ni ebɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally come out of rest after a few months. When they start to sprout, they use up the water and food stored inside the tuber to grow shoots, making the yam soft and light.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Kɛ amɛbɔi shweremɔ Amɛbaafite nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni ato yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii. Ha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee blɛoo ni efee mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to act as living shields, protecting the tender plants from extreme heat and keeping soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ gãimlibii ni buɔ wala he Buu tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the tips instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK will restore their green color and help them produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Look closely at the small raised bumps or nodes on the cassava stem where leaves used to grow. Ensure these nodes are pointing upward toward the sky before pushing the bottom of the stick into the ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, reducing disease risks and improving yield.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha helai ahe oshara aba shi ni oha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ

english: What is eating holes in my corn leaves and leaving fine dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to feed, so inspecting your field early and applying targeted controls into the funnels is necessary.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye niyenii, no hewɔ lɛ kwɛmɔ tsei ni odu lɛ amli mra. Ni ni akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni akɛmamɔ hiɛ atsu nii yɛ funnel lɛ shishi lɛ he miihia waa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady, and humid conditions. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper bushes curling upward and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses. Clearing surrounding weeds and managing insects early stops leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛ kooloi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside other crops, they naturally feed the soil and fertilize neighboring plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or dry leaves around the bases of my crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ashwã he lɛ? Mi tso lɛ shishitoo?

english: Covering soil with organic mulch acts like an insulating blanket. It traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Organic mulch tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before any small tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady by watering consistently at the base helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oooha ehi shi daa kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ nu ni oooha lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do tree crops like rubber or cocoa take several years before they start producing anything I can sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani tsei tamɔ rɔba loo kookoo jeɔ nibii ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ afeemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their first few years building strong roots and trunk structures to support heavy yields later. Just like a child must grow before doing heavy physical work, the tree needs time to mature before it can produce fruit or sap consistently.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ maa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa koni amɛkɛye amɛbua nibii babaoo ni afeɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ. Taakɛ esa akɛ gbekɛ ko ada dani enyɛ etsu nii waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Be he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii loo nu daa.

english: How is it possible to harvest liquid sap from rubber trees every month without killing the tree?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ abua latex naa kɛjɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei amli daa nyɔŋ nɔ ni agbeee tsei lɛ?

english: Rubber trees continuously produce latex as a natural defense system to seal bark wounds. When you make a thin, controlled cut in the bark, the tree safely releases a small amount of latex and heals itself, allowing you to harvest regularly without harming the main tree.
ga: Rɔba tsei feɔ latɛs ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛtsiɔ pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ yibii bibii ni akudɔ amɛ lɛ, tso lɛ jieɔ nu fioo ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni etsaa ehe. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oyeee tso titri lɛ awui.

english: Why do my crops wilt and turn yellow during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: During the dry season, the lack of moisture prevents plants from taking up essential nutrients from the soil through their roots. Without water and nutrients, the leaves lose their green color and droop to save energy and protect the plant from dying.
ga: yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ Fɛ̃i ni bɛ lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why should I plant perennial tree crops instead of only planting quick seasonal crops like maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo moŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa oya, ni yɔɔ be mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai kɛkɛ?

english: Seasonal crops give quick money after a few months, but you have to clear land and replant every season. Perennial tree crops take longer to start producing, but once mature, they yield regularly for many years without needing to be replanted.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ be mli lɛ haa shika oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Shi esa akɛ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni odu ekoŋŋ daa afi. Tsoi ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi kɛ́ eda kwraa lɛ, ebaawo yibii ni yaa nɔ daa afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes black spots to appear on cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a tiny fungus that thrives in cool, wet conditions. When heavy rain splashes water onto the pods and there isn't enough sunlight or airflow to dry them, the fungus grows quickly and spoils the crop.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni hulu la loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛgbi lɛ bɛ. Fuŋ lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my young trees when they are already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mitsei bibii lɛ amli kɛji tsei lɛ etswa shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or unnecessary branches so the plant doesn't waste energy on them. It directs all the tree's strength into growing a sturdy main trunk, developing good canopy shade, and producing healthy fruit or sap.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. koni tsei akafite hewalɛ Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekwɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri ni mli wa. Umbrella kpakpa su ni ekɛ aduawai loo mliki ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa

english: How do crops use fertilizer, and why doesn't putting more fertilizer always mean getting a bigger harvest?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ? Ni nɔ hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ etsɔɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Fertilizer supplies food like nitrogen and potassium that plants absorb through water in their roots. However, if you give too much fertilizer at once, it can burn the roots and kill the plant, just like overeating can make a person sick.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium ni tsei lɛ tsɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli shikome lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baashã ni amɛbaafite tso lɛ. Taakɛ niyenii babaoo ni ayeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ he ajɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted crops and choke them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapt to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because farm crops are cultivated for high yield rather than wild survival, weeds will easily steal their food if you don't clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii koni aná yibii babaoo moŋ fe ni aaahi shi yɛ koo lɛ mli. Jwɛi baanyɛ aju niyenii oya kɛji ojieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do my fruit trees shed their flowers during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and strong winds physically knock fragile flowers off the branches before insects can pollinate them. Excessive water can also stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers to protect its main stem.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ amɛmli. Nu babaoo baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and their leaves block sunlight from each other. This causes them to grow thin, tall, and weak, resulting in a much smaller harvest compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛkwɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick cocoa trees use to conserve water. Leaves lose moisture into the dry air, so shedding them helps the tree hold onto its remaining water until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ cacao tso lɛ he ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he lɛ. Baai lɛ laajeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aŋmɛ baai lɛ gbɛ ni amɛho lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu fɛɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to make green leaves and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: You can look for signs above ground: mature cassava plants usually shed their lower leaves, the main stem turns woody, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao okadii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ: Bei pii lɛ, yucca tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air for maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp ground where rot and fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Ni okɛto hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ he.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm as my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that pull natural nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. This naturally feeds your maize crop and keeps the soil fertile for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-mai lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are tiny holes suddenly appearing on my maize leaves with caterpillar dirt in the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni ŋmeii yɔɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. These caterpillars hide in the center funnel of the plant where it is soft and moist, eating the new leaves before they fully unfold. Catching them early prevents severe crop damage.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli, he ni loo lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Ye baai heei dani amɛje kpo kwraa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ waa lɛ anaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed, usually by extreme heat or irregular watering. When a plant feels thirsty or too hot, it drops flowers to save energy for its own survival instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu kumai he loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow faster than my crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the soil waiting for moisture. Once the rains hit, they shoot up rapidly to capture sunlight and water before your planted crops have a chance to establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni amɛwɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛmiimɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛfoɔ oya koni amɛyamɔ hulu la kɛ nu dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Why should I remove the extra young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, food, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Cutting them back to leave only one or two strong stems ensures the main tree has enough strength to grow a large, heavy cluster of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ koni oshi tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tso titri lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the maize plants to compete with each other for space, soil food, and sunlight. This results in tall, thin, weak stems with small or incomplete cobs instead of strong plants with full ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e tue hyi.

english: Can I still grow rice on my land if there is no river, swamp, or standing water nearby?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmã yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo? Kɛji faa, ŋshɔ, loo nu jɛɛhe ko ni damɔ shi bɛŋkɛɛɛ.

english: Yes, you can still grow rice without a nearby river or swamp by using special seeds called upland rice, which rely strictly on normal rainfall rather than flooded land.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa lolo ni faa loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwu krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ rai ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. ni damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ waa moŋ fe hei ni nu afua eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Why does traditional rice farming require so much water to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kusum mli ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ nu babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Traditional lowland rice varieties are adapted to grow in flooded conditions because standing water helps suppress weeds, regulates soil temperature, and provides the heavy moisture their roots need.
ga: Atsake kusum mli ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kudɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ biɔ lɛ

english: What can I plant on dry farmland during periods when rainfall is very low?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo kwraa lɛ?

english: On dry farmland with low rain, you should plant drought-tolerant crop varieties or upland grains that require minimal soil moisture and mature quickly before the dry spell worsens.
ga: Yɛ okwaayeli hei ni nugbɔ enɛɔ fioo lɛ Esa akɛ odu dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa loo dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ ni biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu fioo ko pɛ ni amɛdaraa oya dani hɔmɔ shihilɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if my dry farmland is good enough for planting crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Most dry land can support crops as long as you select seeds specifically designed for well-drained soils and plant them right at the start of the rainy season.
ga: Hei ni egbi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji ohala dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni odu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Will my rice crop die if my field dries up completely after planting?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ baagboi kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbi kwraa beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties will suffer or die if the field dries out completely, but upland rice varieties are tough enough to survive and yield grain even without continuous water.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baaná amanehulu loo amɛbaagboi kɛji ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbi kwraa. Shi ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ po bɛ mli.

english: What is an upland rice variety and how does it work?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni te etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Upland rice is a special type of rice bred to grow on dry slopes and flat land just like maize or millet, relying only on rain instead of flooded water.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ji ŋmãa henɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni egbi kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛtsɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ moŋ fe nu afua lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the main difference between lowland rice and upland rice seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Lowland rice seeds need flooded, muddy fields to thrive, while upland rice seeds are adapted to well-drained, dry soils and do not require standing water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui biɔ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ muji koni amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe ehiaaa nu ni ekã shi

english: Which type of rice seed should I buy if my farm is located on a hill?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, mɛɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui esa akɛ mahe?

english: You should buy upland rice seeds because water drains quickly off hilly land, and upland rice is made to grow in those exact dry, sloping conditions.
ga: Esa akɛ ohe gɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ejaakɛ nu hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ hei ni gɔji yɔɔ lɛ. Ni aduɔ Khao Don koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ kɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Are there specific crops that do not need continuous watering to produce a good yield?
ga: Ani tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni afɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, crops specifically developed for dry conditions—such as upland rice, sorghum, millet, and certain dryland maize varieties—can give a good harvest with just basic rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afee pɔtɛɛ aha shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ekomɛi ji ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa ni egbi henɔi komɛi. Ebaanyɛ ewo yibii kpakpai kɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ.

english: How do I choose the right crop seed for land that gets very hot and dry quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni sa kɛha mishikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: You should ask your extension officer for heat-tolerant and drought-resistant varieties, like upland rice, which have root systems built to handle dry and hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ obi o-extension officer lɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ naa, tamɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa, ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni ama koni ekɛtsu shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ he nii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps bring back the dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the field for too long, it drowns the roots and allows water fungi to grow, causing the tubers to decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ta ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why do I have to cut long wooden sticks for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ofo tsei kakadaji koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch direct sunlight. When the leaves get enough light, they produce the food needed to swell and grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaafee niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛfutu ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there are no insects to pollinate them. Keeping the soil moist with mulch helps cool the plants so flowers stay on.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I not put four or five maize seeds in one single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ ŋmãa bu kome pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to compete against each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Spacing seeds out ensures each stalk grows thick and produces large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ baaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: What causes small green and brown caterpillars to hide inside the central funnel of my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ mi-ŋmei baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths on the leaves. They hide inside the center leaf funnel where it is dark and moist to eat the tender growing parts of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ duŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni miida lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I place solid fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa woɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are concentrated salts that can burn or damage tender crop stems and surface roots if touched directly. Placing fertilizer in a small ring a short distance away allows the roots to drink it safely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã loo efite tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Kɛ́ ahi he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnu nu shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull water from the soil. The leaves droop to reduce sun exposure and usually stand back up as the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ aba shi. ni esumɔɔ ni ete shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil food available for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and wither during the heat of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sun. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to cover them, the sun scorches their leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni egbiɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they fight with the main plant for plant food and water in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, which helps the main plant grow bigger and produce heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ Ekɛ tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ baawu koni ená tsei aniyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso lɛ niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni edara ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make food and stay green. The maize plant pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the fresh leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Abɛi tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aha.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the roots underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa.

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients. The cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above the ground instead of storing starch in its underground tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo fe niyenii krokomɛi. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes and tiny brown dirt spots packed inside the central leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Akɛwo cone mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the center of the young maize plant, eating the leaf tissue and leaving behind its waste, which looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai amli fãji ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei kpakpa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling tightly upwards and becoming very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the plant. As they suck the sap from the leaves, they weaken the plant and can spread leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ Amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ curling virus lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off to the ground without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or dry soil. If the daily temperature gets too high, the pollen inside the flower dies before it can form a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛji daa gbi latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ dani aduawai baa.

english: Why does my groundnut plant push tiny stems with flower ends down into the soil instead of growing nuts on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi eshishifãi bibii ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts produce flowers on the stem above ground, but after pollination, the plant sends out 'pegs' that bend downward and grow into the earth. The groundnut pod can only develop and mature safely underground.
ga: Peanuts woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ tsuɔ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shi ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Peanut pods baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf rot and helping the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛtso lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my swamp rice plants require standing water in the field while my maize crops die if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi swamp rice plant lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have hollow stems that transport air down to roots underwater. Standing water also stops weeds from growing while keeping the soil wet, whereas maize roots drown because they cannot breathe in flooded soil.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested mangoes spoil so quickly if I don't sell them right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ahɔ̃ɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fresh mangoes have high moisture and spoil fast, but extracting their juice or turning them into concentrate removes water and preserves them for a much longer time.
ga: Mango heei yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni efiteɔ oya. Shi kɛ́ ajie mango nu loo afee lɛ mango mli nu lɛ, ejieɔ nu lɛ ni ehaa ehiɔ shi be babaoo.

english: Aside from eating them fresh, what other valuable products can I get from my mango harvest?
ga: Kɛfata amɛ ni ayeɔ ehee lɛ he lɛ, mɛɛ nibii krokomɛi ni jara wa onine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mango ni akpaa lɛ mli?

english: You can turn mangoes into ready-to-drink juice, concentrate, extract essential oil from the peels, and use the dried leftover pulp as animal feed.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsɔ mango mli ofee nu ni mli ewo muji, ni esa akɛ anu, ni ojie fɔ ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ mli. ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii akɛ kooloi aniyenii.

english: Is there any real value in fruit peels, or are they just rubbish?
ga: Yibii ahe tsɔi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo eji jwɛi kɛkɛ?

english: Fruit peels like mango skins contain valuable essential oils that can be extracted and sold for extra income rather than being thrown away.
ga: Fruit peels tamɔ mango peels lɛ mli mu ni he hiaa waa yɛ mli ni abaanyɛ ajie ni ahɔ̃ɔ koni aná shika babaoo moŋ fe ni aaashɛrɛ ashwie.

english: How does turning my raw fruit into juice help me make more money?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu tsake aduawai ni ahoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi ni maná shika babaoo?

english: Processing fruits into ready-to-drink juice or concentrates allows you to sell higher-value products and prevents losses from fruit rotting before it reaches the market.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso yibii tsu nii ni ofee nu loo nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nɔ ko ni jara wa waa. ni atsĩ yibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa dani amɛya jara nɔ.

english: Can I extract anything useful from the skin of fruits when I press them?
ga: Kɛ́ anyɛ nɔ lɛ, ani abaanyɛ ajie nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛjɛ tso yibii lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pressing or processing fruit peels allows you to collect natural peel oils, which are valuable for cosmetics, flavorings, and secondary markets.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso yibii ahe tsɔi ni ooonyɛ loo otsu he nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuaa mu kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔi lɛ amli. Amɛjara wa kɛha tsofai ni akɛsaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ jarayeli ni ji enyɔ lɛ.

english: Can I feed the leftover skin and pulp from my fruits to my farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ hewolo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ aduawai amli lɛ aha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ?

english: Yes, leftover fruit pulp and skins are full of nutrients and make excellent feed for farm livestock like goats, sheep, and cattle.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso yibii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ehewolo ni eshwɛ lɛ eyi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni eji niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tooi, tooi, kɛ tsinai.

english: Why should I dry fruit waste before giving it to my farm animals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ dani mikɛha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ?

english: Drying fruit residue removes moisture, which stops it from rotting quickly and allows you to store it as animal feed for weeks or months.
ga: Yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekafite oya. Ni ehaa okɛtoɔ akɛ kooloi aniyenii otsii loo nyɔji babaoo.

english: How can I make sure nothing goes to waste on my farm after squeezing juice from my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can practice zero-waste farming by using the juice for drinks, collecting oil from the peels, and drying the solid residue to feed your livestock.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ zero-waste okwaayeli atsu nii kɛtsɔ aduawai amli nu ni okɛnuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Bua fɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. ni ogbi nɔ ni eshwɛ ni mli wa lɛ koni okɛha okooloi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I safely store wet fruit leftovers so they don't rot before my livestock can eat them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ aduawai ni efɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Enɛ ji koni ekafite dani kooloi aye lɛ.

english: The best way to preserve wet crop residues is to dry them thoroughly in the sun or a dryer before storing them in a dry place for feed.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ ahe ji ni agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii amli dani akɛto he ko ni egbi kɛha niyenii.

english: Will feeding dried fruit leftovers to my animals make them sick?
ga: Ani tso yibii ni egbi ni eshwɛ ni mikɛhaa mikooloi lɛ baaha amɛhe ajɔ amɛ?

english: No, as long as the fruit residue is properly dried and free from mold, it provides safe, healthy carbohydrates and fiber for your livestock.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Ebaaha okooloi lɛ aná carbohydrates kɛ fiber ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying out under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage is very delicate. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cocoyams provides living canopy protection, keeping the cocoa cool and retaining soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa kwraa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo cocoa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka lɛ he. Ha kookoo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water rapidly in hot, dry weather. When water is scarce, the plant naturally folds or drops outer leaves to protect its main stem, but spreading mulch like dried grass around the base helps hold water in the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ baafolɔ loo ebaashwie esɛɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ebu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Shi mulching tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle Cones lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hidden in the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee tso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the central growing leaves of maize. Catching them early by inspecting the leaves and applying recommended neem-based solutions or targeted spraying protects your grain yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ tsofa ni neem yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo, tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmaa lɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and showing yellow blotches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral sickness carried by tiny whitefly insects or spread through infected stem cuttings. You can prevent it by planting clean, disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ kɛbaa loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei henɔi ni he tse ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly upwards like cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying early with appropriate organic or chemical insecticides kills the insects and keeps the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Organic loo chemical tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi ni eye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I know if my soil is weak and needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii dani madu nii?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or produced poor yields last season, the soil is short on nutrients. Adding animal manure, compost, or balanced chemical fertilizer feeds the ground so crops grow robustly.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo nibii ni anáa fioo yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ falɛ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen breaks down in the ground, acting as natural food for crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which pushes leaf growth instead of fruit production. Consistent watering during flowering helps the blossoms set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao, ni no haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up off the ground into direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food efficient enough to swell the tubers growing deep under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ehaa bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Why does my stored maize get full of small insects and rot quickly in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Ni fitemɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize rots and attracts seed-boring insects like weevils if it is put into storage while still containing moisture. Thoroughly sun-drying corn until the grains are very hard before storing them in airtight bags prevents mold and insect damage.
ga: Abele fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa kɛ kooloi akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. It can also happen when excessive rain washes nutrients out of the soil or when water pools around the roots and suffocates them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my maize crop fail to produce big cobs if I plant late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo ŋmeii wuji kɛji midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady water and strong sunlight while forming cobs. When you plant late, the rains often stop just as the plant is trying to fill the cobs, leaving it without enough water to build full grains.
ga: Nu kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa he miihia ŋmãa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifee lɛ. Kɛ́ odu sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpaa be mli ni tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha afee dumɔwu ni eyi obɔ lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce flowers at the top before I see any cobs growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi dani manyɛ mana ŋmãa lɛ ni miida lɛ?

english: This is a normal part of the plant's growth cycle. The top flower produces pollen, which the wind carries down to the silks lower on the stalk. Once pollen touches the silks, the cobs begin to form and fill with grains.
ga: Enɛ ji tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ fã ko ni yaa nɔ daa. Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jieɔ pollen ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa shi kɛyaa siliki ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollen kɛ siliki kpe lɛ Cob lɛ baaje shishi efee ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from my previous harvest yield less than the new seeds from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni jɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from agro-dealers are specially bred hybrid seeds designed for high yields. When you save seeds from that crop to plant again, the plants lose those special hybrid strengths and naturally produce smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni afee amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛji obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ hybrid lɛ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my oil palm tree take several years before it starts producing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mi-oil palm tso lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Oil palm is a long-term tree crop that spends its first three to four years building a strong root system and a sturdy trunk. It needs to establish this strong base before it has the energy to produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani ekɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa baa. Ehe bahia ni ama nɛkɛ shishitoo ni wa nɛɛ dani ená hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo aduawai akui babaoo.

english: Why do oil palm seedlings need so much distance between them when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni oil palm dumɔwui lɛ aná gbɛ babaoo yɛ amɛteŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Oil palm leaves spread out very wide as the tree grows. If planted too close together, the trees shade each other out and compete for soil nutrients and water, resulting in poor fruit yields.
ga: Mu tso lɛ baai gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo beni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai ni ehiii.

english: Can I plant maize inside my oil palm farm while the palm trees are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop maize between young palm trees during their first two years. Because the palm trees are still small, they will not block sunlight from the maize, allowing you to harvest food while waiting for the palm trees to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Akɛni tɛŋ tsei lɛ darako lolo hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsĩii hulu lɛ naa koni amɛkashɛ ŋmãa lɛ he. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Weeds are native plants with strong roots that are adapted to grab water and nutrients faster than farm crops. They act quickly to take advantage of rain before your crops can fully establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli ni nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛtsuɔ nii oya koni amɛkɛ nugbɔ lɛ atsu nii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does burning my cleared bush hurt my crop yield over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ brɔshi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: While burning clears land quickly, the extreme heat burns away the natural organic matter that feeds the soil. It kills helpful soil organisms and leaves the earth dry and exposed to rain erosion.
ga: yɛ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ jieɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya. Shi la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to buy seeds and fertilizers together with other local farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi baahe dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Buying inputs as a group allows you to get bulk discounts, share transport costs, and ensure supplies arrive on time before the rainy season starts, so you never miss the best planting period.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ babaoo ni ooohe lɛ haa onine shɛɔ nɔ ni he hiaa waa nɔ. jaa nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo ni amɛha nɔmimaa akɛ nibii lɛ baashɛ yɛ be naa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ dumɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight. This allows the plant to gather light energy efficiently, which helps build bigger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbua la hewalɛ naa jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow heavy cobs. It can also happen if the soil stays too waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni tsii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ.

english: Why does my land yield less crop each year even when I burn the weeds to clear it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mishãa jwɛi koni mikɛjie nɔ lɛ?

english: Burning weeds destroys the natural organic matter and beneficial organisms in the topsoil, gradually stripping the land of nutrients rather than feeding it for future crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ fiofio moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather with high humidity. Pruning overgrown branches helps air move through and reduces moisture buildup.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa lɛ baa shi.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often brought by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a plant virus, or it can be a reaction to excessive heat and uneven watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ko ni jɛɔ la ni mli edɔ fe nine kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ mli baa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant grow stems and leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tsitsii kɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why should I buy fresh hybrid maize seeds every season instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
