ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa heei ni akɛfee ŋmãa daa be mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved hybrid seeds lose their strength and uniformity in the second generation, resulting in smaller cobs, weaker stalks, and lower overall yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii, ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the leaves begin to yellow and drop off naturally, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack from the expanding roots beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni gbɛ eshwa eshishi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good to plant beans or cowpeas between my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that nourishes your main crop while maximizing space on your farm.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii amɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa onibii titrii lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli he lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo.

english: Officer, why do I need to plant plantains next to my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi? Cocoa dumɔwui ni adu ehee?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves. It can also happen when the ground stays flooded for too long after heavy rains, suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What will happen to my corn if I plant too many seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and tall, producing very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛhe yɛ tsɔi ni amɛkwɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii waa loo eko kwraa bɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow giant stems and bushy leaves, but only leaves very tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or very rich organic matter, making the plant spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ he nii, moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Officer, my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers dry up and drop off without forming tomatoes. Why?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato. Maaba?

english: Flowers drop off when temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks key minerals. Irregular watering while the plant is flowering is the most common cause.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ minerals ni he hiaa lɛ Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa fe fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects. It can also happen when the soil gets too dry under extreme heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crops with dead grass or dry leaves during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he? Aduɔ nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi yɔɔ mli yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves—a practice called mulching—keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so it doesn't evaporate into the air, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: It is always best to water early in the morning because the roots absorb the moisture before the sun gets strong. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate quickly into the air.
ga: Okɛ nu awo mli be fɛɛ be leebi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu la lɛ mli wa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help improve the soil for the next farming season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen gas out of the air and traps it in their roots. When the plants die, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli lɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Officer, why do dark spots and white powders appear on my crop leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves create the perfect conditions for fungi to grow. Rain droplets hitting the bare ground also splash microscopic fungal spores from the soil onto the lower leaves of your crops.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii adalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni etswaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ hu shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and scorching at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshã yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted next to them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall, leafy bushes but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ waa shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or overly rich manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering stress the pepper plant. To survive the stress, the plant sheds its flowers instead of using energy to grow pepper fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu pepper aduawai.

english: Yam is a vine that needs sunlight to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground into the air and sun, which helps the plant produce much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni biɔ hulu la koni ehoo. Staking haa baai lɛ holeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why are there small holes torn all over my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji bibii egbɛ eshwa lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf shoot. Catching and treating them early prevents them from destroying the growing point of the maize plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni yeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra kɛ tsamɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: What makes my maize leaves turn purple or dark red instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ purple loo etsuru ni mli edɔ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Purple leaves usually mean the plant is lacking phosphorus in the soil. Phosphorus is an essential nutrient that helps crops build strong roots and process energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Fosforo ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ nifeemɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do black spots appear on my tomato leaves and stems during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji yɔɔ tomato baai kɛ amɛshishifãi anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity, and rain droplets splash fungal spores from the soil onto the leaves. Pruning lower leaves and spacing plants allows air to dry the foliage and prevent leaf rot.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ haa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Seeds planted too close together compete heavily for soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight. This results in weak, thin stalks that yield small ears of corn instead of healthy plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la he akaŋshii mli waa, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa ni haa ŋmɔtɔ toi bibii baa yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Wild weeds are naturally tough and have deep roots adapted to quickly capture available soil water and nutrients before crop seedlings can establish their root systems.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ dani tsei amli dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ato shishifãi ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are yellowing from too much water versus not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ nu babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa mli?

english: If leaves are yellow and soft while the soil stays soggy, the roots are drowning from too much water. If leaves are crisp, curled, and the ground is dry, the plant is thirsty.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ lolo lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛji baai lɛ mli edɔ, ebɔle ehe, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu egbi lɛ, no lɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to trap moisture and protect their soft leaves from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and produce small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji oodu dumɔwui babaoo Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the plants act like hungry children fighting over one small bowl of food. They compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to grow weak instead of strong.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ feɔ enii tamɔ gbekɛ ni hɔmɔ miiye lɛ ni miiwu yɛ niyenii tsɛnsi bibioo ko he. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni amɛhe wa.

english: If too many suckers grow around the mother plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients meant for producing fruit. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces large, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ, tso nyɛ lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa anáa yibii. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to manufacture food for the growing yam tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, giving them maximum sunlight and protecting leaves from rotting.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe babaoo, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas make my farmland better for my next corn crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have special leaves and roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants decay, this natural food stays in the soil, helping the next corn crop grow greener and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Beni tsei fiteɔ Adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ye obua ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when rain washes over my field for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up all the tiny air pockets in the dirt, suffocating crop roots. Without oxygen, root tips rot and can no longer absorb nutrients from the soil, causing the leaves to yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it bad to burn the weeds and dry grass on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the top layer of organic matter that holds moisture and plant food in the soil. Leaving cleared weeds to rot on top of the soil instead creates a natural blanket that keeps the soil cool and rich.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋwɛi fã lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni atsuu he lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no najiaŋ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, usually caused by sudden heat, prolonged dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Aloo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and curl up after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash soil particles containing fungal spores onto the lower leaves of tomato plants. The wet conditions allow fungi to grow quickly, damaging the leaves and causing them to curl.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ daa oya. Efiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if my cassava tubers under the ground are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack as expanding roots push upward.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the seeds very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow big and produce a strong harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on all their leaves to build big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and avoid rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni ekɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the field has too much standing water. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat gets too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Regular watering during hot periods helps flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: What causes tiny ragged holes in my corn leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which are caterpillars that feed on maize leaves and stems. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening helps control them before they destroy the field.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than regular crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil fertilizer before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nutrients go straight into your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei krokomɛi ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground in rainy weather while my rice thrives in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil and drown in waterlogged ground. Rice plants have special internal tubes that send air down to their roots underwater, keeping them alive in flooded fields.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia sũ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛbote sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Ni amɛaaha amɛhi wala mli yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry like concrete after a few weeks of dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like compost or mulch, and when exposed directly to hot sun. Adding organic material keeps the soil loose, spongy, and able to hold water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. ni kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfata he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehiɛ ŋmeii, ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I save maize seeds from my previous harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern improved maize seeds are hybrids designed for a single season. Replanting saved hybrid seeds results in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and weaker plants compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji ŋmãa ni afee amɛ aha be kome. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. Ni tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do some of my seeds float to the top when I put them in a container of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ mikɛwo nu tsɛnsi mli lɛ?

english: Seeds float because they are hollow, immature, or damaged inside by insects. Good, healthy seeds are solid and heavy inside, so they naturally sink to the bottom of the water.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ hoɔ nu lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛmli ewo bu, amɛdarako, loo kooloi efite amɛ. Dumɔwui kpakpai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ wa ni amɛmli tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛboteɔ nu lɛ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I quickly check which of my crop seeds are good before planting them in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ dumɔwui ni hi lɛ oya dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You can do a simple water test by placing your seeds in water. The bad or damaged seeds will rise to the top so you can skim them off, leaving only the healthy, heavy seeds at the bottom for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka nu lɛ okwɛ mlɛo. Anáa enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni efite loo efite lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni onyɛ ojie amɛ. Dumɔwui ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛɔ ni akɛduɔ.

english: Should I throw away the seeds that rise to the surface when I wash them in water?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashɛ dumɔwui ni baa ŋwɛi lɛ ashwie beni mikɛ nu miifɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yes, you should remove and throw away the floating seeds because they lack the strength to germinate properly and will likely fail to grow into healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie dumɔwui fɛɛ ni hoɔ lɛ ni oshɛrɛ ashwie. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. ni ekolɛ edaŋ ni efee tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stir or test my crop seeds in water more than once before selecting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo maka dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ yɛ nu mli fe shikome dani mahala amɛ lɛ?

english: Repeating the water test helps release any light or bad seeds that were trapped under heavy seeds or held down by air bubbles during the first try, ensuring you only plant the absolute best seeds.
ga: Nu mli kaa lɛ ni ooofee ekoŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie dumɔwui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo efite ni ŋmɛ dumɔwui ni tsii shishi loo ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kaa lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ pɛ oduɔ.

english: Why do seeds that sink to the bottom of water sprout much better in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo amɛ nu mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds that sink are full of nourishment and have a complete plant embryo inside, giving them the strength to push through the soil and grow into strong crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ebote mli lɛ eyi kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni fɔmɔ kotoku ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why do some of my seeds look good on the outside but still fail to grow when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi amɛkwɛ̃ɛɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Insects often eat the inside of a seed while leaving the outer shell looking untouched. Putting seeds in water exposes these hidden bad seeds because the hollow inside makes them float.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi yeɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli, ni ehaa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, ebaajie nɛkɛ dumɔwui gbohii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛmli ewo bu, ni no baaha amɛfo nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use ordinary clean water from my well or river to sort good seeds from bad ones?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mli tse ni jɛɔ nubu loo faa mli lɛ atsu nii kɛgbala dumɔwui kpakpai kɛjɛ dumɔwui gbohii amli?

english: Yes, ordinary clean water works very well for seed testing because healthy seeds are naturally denser than water and will sink without needing any special chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli tse ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ dumɔwui akasemɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu. Ni ebaabote nu mli ni ekɛ tsofai krɛdɛɛ ko tsuuu nii.

english: Will putting my seeds in water to select them spoil them if I don't plant immediately?
ga: Ani midumɔwui ni mikɛwoɔ nu mli koni mikɛfolɔ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji miduuu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Soaking seeds briefly for selection is fine, but if you are not planting right away, you must dry the good seeds thoroughly in a shaded, ventilated place so they do not mold or rot.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli be kukuoo ko koni akɛkpa amɛ lɛ hu baanyɛ aba mli. Shi kɛji oduuu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ehe miihia ni ogbi dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Koni akafee ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does sorting out bad seeds with water save me time and money on my farm?
ga: Bɔ ni dumɔwui gbohii ni akɛ nu gbalaa mli lɛ haa mibɛ be kɛ shika yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Sorting ensures every seed you plant grows, so you do not waste labor, land space, or expensive fertilizers on empty spots where bad seeds failed to germinate.
ga: Nibii ni ooohala lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni oduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteee nitsumɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa yɛ he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ he ni dumɔwui gbohii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some damaged seeds take a few moments to rise to the top of the water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni efite lɛ heɔ be fioo dani amɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Air trapped around the seed coat can temporarily hold bad seeds down. Giving the seeds a little time and a soft stir allows the light, damaged seeds to break free and float up.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle Dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dumɔwui fɔji lɛ be kukuoo ko. Ha dumɔwui lɛ be fioo ni okɛfutu blɛoo. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui ni waaa ni efite lɛ agbo ni amɛfo kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunshine during their first few years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living shelter that cools the soil and protects tender leaves from sunburn.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is essential for green leafy growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer around the base helps the plant regain its healthy green color and produce good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ Koji lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa eŋɔli su ni yeɔ emuu kɛ toi kpakpai.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to rotate maize with groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility without needing as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa tsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmãa ni jara wa waa atsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small and thin even after sitting in the ground for a full year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ be mli ni mita shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi muu fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose soil and adequate space to swell properly. If plants are placed too close together or in hard soil, their roots end up competing for water and nutrients, resulting in thin, woody roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfuu jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many maize seeds as possible in one hole to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce small ears or no grain at all.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ toi bibii loo dumɔwui ko kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or dry spells. Mulching the soil around the base and keeping moisture levels steady helps cool the root zone so flowers can form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishigbɛ lɛ he ni okwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during hot afternoons even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji He ni esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Under strong midday sunshine, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it, causing temporary wilt. As the air cools down in the evening, the plant usually recovers its shape.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ tso lɛ naa ehiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes holes that look like tiny ragged windows in the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni tamɔ samfɛji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This leaf damage is commonly caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying recommended pesticides or neem-based treatments early in the morning kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii loo akɛ neem tsu he nii leebi lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Does leaving weeds in my farm really reduce the amount of grain I harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mijieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmaa ni mikpaa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act as aggressive thieves that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to nutrients, boosting your harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni onitsumɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why do certified seeds bought from agro-dealers perform better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred in laboratories for strong vigor, uniform growth, and high yield. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, leading to uneven growth and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ laboratori ko mli koni ekwɛ akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ. shweremɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshɛ latsaa he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade using food crops like plantains protects the leaves from burning while keeping the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but very few turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ tsɔɔ fɔfɔi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny beneficial insects like midges for pollination. If insects cannot reach the flowers or if chemicals kill them off, the flowers dry up and fall off without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ anɔ akɛ amɛji nɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii shɛɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo tsofai gbeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa seedling take before it starts giving me pods to sell?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties typically start producing pods within 2 to 3 years of planting, whereas older traditional varieties can take between 4 to 6 years to yield full harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 6 dani amɛshɛ kpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he.

english: What makes my green cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ niji lɛ anɔ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air flow and sun reach the tree helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are small insects attacking the leaves and young shoots of my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The warm, rainy season creates high humidity and soft young plant growth, which attracts pests like mirids and capsids. Regular field monitoring helps catch and manage these pests before they destroy new growth.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ daalɛ baa. Amɛgbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ blemies kɛ capsids. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni atsa amɛ dani amɛfite nibii heei ni eda lɛ.

english: How does covering the ground with dead leaves help my cocoa trees survive the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Bɔ ni baai ni egboi ni mikɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye ebua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛje Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Mulching with dead leaves creates a protective layer over the soil, trapping moisture beneath it and keeping root zones cool during dry, hot weather.
ga: Ni akɛ baai ni egboi awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi ni oha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ latsaa be mli

english: Signs of nutrient-poor soil include pale or yellowish leaves, thin tree trunks, slow growth, and small crop yields even when rainfall is good.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli lɛ he ji baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. tso bibioo lɛ shishifã lɛ daaa blɛoo ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ faaa yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ

english: Why does cutting off old or overgrown tree branches help my cocoa farm make more money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni mináa shika babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or unproductive wood so the tree spends its food and water energy direct into growing healthy cocoa pods, resulting in bigger yields.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ, niyenii kɛ nu tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛwo kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava and plantains inside my new cocoa farm without damaging the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava kɛ plantains yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ hee mli ni mifiteee kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains provides essential shade for young cocoa trees, but cassava should be spaced carefully away from the tree base so its large roots do not steal water and food from the young cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi wuji lɛ akaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ kookoo bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around the base of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with cocoa roots for soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water. Keeping the tree base clean ensures the cocoa tree gets all the food it needs to grow strongly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo shishifãi yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ shishi he tse lɛ, ehaa kookoo tso lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Officer, what is the best way to prepare my land quickly so my crops grow well?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ oya koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing the surface of the land is the fastest way to get your soil ready and create a good environment for your crops to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ oya fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afee shihilɛ kpakpa ni shweremɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: What should I do with the dry grass and weeds after I finish clearing my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee jwɛi kɛ jwɛi lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not scatter or throw away the cleared material. Instead, gather it and spread it evenly over your soil surface as mulch to protect the ground.
ga: Kaagbɛ nibii ni ajie lɛ ashwã loo oshɛrɛ ashwie. Mohu ɔ, moo bua nɛ o ngmɛɛ o zugba ɔ nɔ kaa nɔ́ nɛ maa po zugba a he.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm, and how can I slow them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya nɛkɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo mli fioo?

english: When the soil is left bare, weeds grow fast. Covering the soil with a layer of mulch prevents weeds from sprouting and taking over your farm quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is there a simple way to stop weeds from taking over my farm without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ nɔ akpa jwɛi ni yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: Yes, you can place a layer of cleared plant material, or mulch, on top of the ground to block weed growth naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ahe nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajie lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Officer, how can I prevent my farm soil from drying out when the sun is very hot?
ga: Official Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Applying mulch on top of the soil surface shields the ground from direct heat and keeps it from drying out.
ga: Mulching baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: How do I make sure the water stays in the ground longer after it rains so my crops can use it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii?

english: Covering the farm surface with mulch helps the soil retain water for longer periods, ensuring your crops have the moisture they need to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my crops suffer from lack of water so quickly even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil surface is uncovered, water evaporates quickly. Placing mulch over the ground traps moisture in the soil so it goes directly to the crop roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbeleee lɛ Nu lɛ baaho oya. Mulching lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɔni afee ni ebote tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What does 'mulch' mean, and how does putting it on my land help my plants?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘muji’ shishi? Ni te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Mulch is plant material spread over the surface of the soil. It protects the ground from drying out, stops weeds from growing, and keeps water in the soil for your crops.
ga: Mulch ji tsei ahe nibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it good practice to just burn or scatter all the clearings from my farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashã loo magbɛ shikpɔji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashwã?

english: No, you should not scatter or burn them. Using cleared plant material as a mulch layer directly on the soil surface protects your ground and helps crops thrive.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ oshwãa loo oshãa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe nibii ni ajie lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaabu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛshwere.

english: How can I protect the top layer of my soil from losing all its moisture during dry periods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he koni eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ akafite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Applying mulch directly onto the top of the soil surface keeps the soil cool and prevents the surface layer from drying out completely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning when there is high sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow root systems and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade plants like plantains planted beside them to act as umbrella crops while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni amɛtsu nii akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb high up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tsei koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food through their leaves. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows leaves to catch more light, which feeds the growing tuber underground to make it bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛhoo kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii koni amɛfee wuji.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize, making the soil richer and helping you get a better yield without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa bo ni onáa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will restore the green color and give the plants the energy they need to grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdara.

english: Pruned branches allow sunlight and air to move freely through the cocoa tree. This keeps the tree dry, stops fungal diseases like black pod from spreading, and encourages the tree to direct its energy into producing more cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa. ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why does my plantain stem produce so many small shoots at the bottom, and should I leave them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Lots yɛ shishigbɛ Ni ani esa akɛ maha eda kwraa?

english: Those shoots are called suckers, and if you leave all of them, they will fight with the main plant for food and water. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures your main plantain stem produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ni kɛji oshi fɛɛ Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ gbɔi lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ojie emli babaoo ni oshi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha o-plantain tsei titri lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving small dirt pellets inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa? ni oshi pellets bibii Yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's leaves. Checking your farm early and spraying recommended organic or chemical treatments directly into the plant funnel will stop them before they destroy your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni oooshwie tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot as soon as the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa pɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in high moisture and damp shade. You can prevent it by clearing weeds around the base, pruning dense branches to let in light, and spraying protective copper fungicide before the heavy rains begin.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ, ni ooofolɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ koni la atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ afɔ shi dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aje shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering or extreme heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and using mulching to cool the ground helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the soil for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the wet ground, which prevents leaf rot and allows the yam tubers to grow much larger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni eye ebua sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do some extension officers advise covering the soil around crops with dried leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves is called mulching. It keeps the sun from drying out the soil, keeps weeds from taking over, and slowly turns into natural manure as it breaks down.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye nɔ ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully grown and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava is ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack. These cracks mean the tubers under the soil have expanded and are fully mature.
ga: Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ Nɛkɛ fãmɔi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli elɛɛ ni egbɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, a crucial nutrient for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that nitrogen stays behind as free, natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ nɔ ni aheee nɔ ko, adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When plants grow too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong and produce large tubers or fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo bulbs loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds when they start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ́ ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and become top-heavy once a large bunch forms. Staking the tree with a strong bamboo or wooden pole supports the extra weight and prevents the shallow roots from snapping in high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ dara. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shwiili ni fa fe nine lɛ atsu nii, ni ebaatsi shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and stay small?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids that suck liquid out of young leaves, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Catching pests early and using target sprays or neem oil keeps new leaves growing broad and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Ni ooomɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua baai heei ni amɛdara babaoo ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave soil soaked in standing water, the roots cannot breathe and become weak, allowing water-loving fungi to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ baanyɛ agbo ni amɛtsɔko tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too hot, when the soil is too dry, or if there are no insects to shake pollination loose. Keeping soil moisture consistent and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bɛ ni baatsi pollination naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do small pods drop off my cocoa trees before they get a chance to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra pods (called cherelle wilt) if the tree is stressed by drought, lacks nutrients, or has too many pods to feed at once. Proper pruning and soil feeding reduce stress so more pods mature.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ cherelle wilt) lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii babaoo ni eyɔɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ yɛ be kome mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa lɛ baaha haomɔ aba shi. Ehaa pods lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: How does leaving dead leaves or dry grass on top of my crop beds help my crops in dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi loo jwɛi ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective shield that blocks hot sunshine, slowing down water evaporation from the soil so your crop roots stay cool and moist longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ha nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ baaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do certified seeds from agro-dealers produce better crops than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are selected and bred for strong traits like disease resistance and high yield, whereas saved seeds slowly lose their vigor over generations and may carry hidden seed-borne diseases from last season.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛná sui ni mli wa tamɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ fiofio kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli Ni ekolɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aba.

english: What is the difference between the local coconut tree and the agric coconut variety?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii tsei kɛ okwaayeli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ?

english: The agric (hybrid) coconut variety grows shorter and produces fruit much faster—usually starting within 3 to 4 years—whereas the local variety grows very tall and can take anywhere from 6 to 10 years to start fruiting.
ga: Okwaayeli mli ŋmeii srɔtoi (hybrid) lɛ daa kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, ejeɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ daa waa ni ebaanyɛ ehe afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting the agric coconut variety instead of our traditional local trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu okwaayeli mli ŋmeii srɔtoi yɛ wɔ maŋ tsei lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Agric varieties are bred to start bearing fruit much earlier, stay shorter so they are safer and easier to harvest, and generally yield a higher quantity of nuts compared to older local varieties.
ga: Akwɛ okwaayeli mli tsei srɔtoi koni amɛwo yibii oya. Amɛhiɔ shi be kukuoo ni haa amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛkpamɔ hu waaa. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii babaoo baa kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting before I can harvest my first coconuts?
ga: Kɛ́ midu migbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ makpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmei lɛ?

english: The waiting time depends on the variety you plant; fast-growing agric varieties can produce fruit in about 3.5 years, while local varieties take much longer, often 6 to 10 years.
ga: Be ni okɛbaamɛ lɛ damɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Okwaayeli mli tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ aaafee afii 3.5 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe nakai. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 10.

english: Why are my coconut trees taking much longer to produce fruit compared to my neighbor's trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Your neighbor might have planted an early-bearing agric variety or has better soil nutrients and water supply. Local varieties and trees planted in poor soil naturally take much longer to mature.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ baadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii oya loo ni niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu mli. Kuu lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi kɛ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔji ni ehiii kwraa nɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa.

english: How can I tell when my coconuts are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-koko lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: If you want fresh coconut water, harvest them while the outer shell is still green and full. If you want mature dry nuts for oil, wait until the husk turns completely brown and you hear water sloshing inside when shaken.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ŋmei nu kpakpa Kpamɔ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ afee fɔ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa. ni kɛ́ ekpokpo lɛ Obaanyɛ onu nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How does the quality of my soil affect how fast my coconut tree grows?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa bɔ ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ daa oya lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rich, well-drained soil gives the tree essential nutrients to grow strong roots quickly. Poor or overly wet soil slows down growth and delays the time it takes for the tree to produce fruits.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ fɛo ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa oya. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ni edɔ fe nine lɛ baaha tso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha be ni heɔ koni tso lɛ awo yibii lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: What is the proper way to plant a coconut seedling so it grows well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ŋmei tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Dig a spacious hole, mix topsoil with organic manure, and place the seedling in a sunny area with good drainage so its roots can spread easily without rotting.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ni mli kwɔ Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara oya ni amɛfiteee.

english: Good coconut land should have loose, sandy-loam soil that drains water easily, receives full sunlight throughout the day, and stays moist without becoming waterlogged.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ aná ŋmei ni mli tse, ni ŋã yɔɔ mli. Easy drainage Na hulu la ni fa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli

english: Do coconut trees need fertilizer and regular watering, or can I just leave them to grow naturally?
ga: Ani ŋmeii kɛ nu he miihia ŋmeii tsei daa? Aloo wɔbaanyɛ wɔha eda yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: While coconut trees can survive on their own, giving them organic manure, weeding around their roots, and watering them during dry periods helps them grow faster and produce far more fruit.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe moŋ, shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ha lɛ Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ nu ni oooha yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmei tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Am I allowed to harvest crops from a tree growing near my farm boundary if I didn't plant it?
ga: Ani aŋmɛ mi gbɛ ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ masɛi lɛ amli? Kɛji miduuu lɛ

english: No, harvesting fruit from a tree that belongs to someone else or sits on land you do not own is illegal and causes community conflicts. Always get permission from the land owner first.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni ji mɔ kroko nɔ loo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni jeee onɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ yibii ni oookpa lɛ ji mlakwamɔ ni ekɛ béi baa akutso lɛ mli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ná hegbɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ dɛŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool protective canopy, keeping the moisture in the soil and preventing the young plants from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni daa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii, yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa dumɔwui lɛ agbi

english: Why do my plantain plants start producing smaller bunches after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii bibii feemɔ lɛ? Afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow new stems called suckers around their base. When too many suckers grow around the main plant, they all fight for the same soil nutrients and water, leaving less energy for the plant to grow large fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tsei heei ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ ebɔleɔ shishigbɛ. Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ hu. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ be mli ni amɛkã shi lolo yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during cold, rainy seasons when humidity is high. The fungus attacks the pod wall, destroying the beans inside before they mature.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli, nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Fungus tutuaa pod gbogboi lɛ. Efiteɔ kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my tall plantain plants fall over so easily during heavy rainfall and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni kɛlɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep woody roots or solid wood trunks; their trunks are made of soft leaf sheaths. When heavy fruit bunches develop at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and root-heavy soil can soften, causing the entire plant to uproot under strong wind.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo tso shishifãi ni wa. Akɛ baai bibii ahe tsɔi fee tso lɛ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ shwere yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ bafeɔ ŋwɛi-tsitsii, ni shikpɔŋ ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ ha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ fã yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do so many tiny young cocoa pods shrivel up and drop off the tree shortly after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So babaoo gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This natural dropping is called 'cherelle wilt.' The tree thins out its own young pods when it realizes it does not have enough stored water or nutrients to feed all of them to full maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ 'cherelle wilt'. Tso lɛ baafee fiofio Amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni amɛnaa akɛ nu loo niyenii ni ato ni baaye abua amɛ kɛyashi amɛdara lɛ bɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain plants turning yellow from the edges and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛmiigbi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign of leaf spot diseases or root damage. When the leaves lose their green color, the plant cannot absorb sunlight effectively to manufacture food for its growing fruit.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee baa lɛ he hela loo shishifãi ni efite lɛ he okadi. Kɛji baai lɛ bɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha niyenii aha aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact color change that shows my cocoa pods are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male su tsakemɔ pɔtɛɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color distinctly—green pods turn bright yellow, and naturally red pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting when fully colored ensures the beans inside have reached peak sugar content for good processing.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Nibii ni akpaa kɛji akɛ ehiɛ su fɛɛ lɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɔ sugar ni fa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he koni akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do fresh cocoa beans need to sit under banana leaves for several days right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii heei hiɔ banana baai ashishi gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans are surrounded by a sweet white pulp that needs to ferment. Covering them under leaves traps heat and natural yeasts, which breaks down the pulp and develops the rich chocolate flavor inside the bean.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ ni esa akɛ atsɔ mli lɛ ebɔle kookoo yibii heei ahe. Kɛ́ okɛha baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ gbálaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli wa baa kɔfi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why must I spread wet cocoa beans thinly on raised mats to dry instead of leaving them in a thick heap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋtayaa ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ fioo fioo koni egbi moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ ŋtayaa ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ?

english: Spreading beans in a thin layer allows sunlight and fresh air to reach every bean evenly. Stacking them in a thick pile keeps moisture trapped inside, which creates mold and spoils the bean quality.
ga: Ni agbɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashwãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ kɔfi ŋmeii fɛɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ ato amɛ yɛ ŋtayaai ni mli tse mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni efiteɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer cocoa pods now than it did when I first planted it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo kookoo ŋmeii fioo fe beni adu klɛŋklɛŋ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull minerals and nutrients out of the earth every season to produce leaves and pods. Over time, without replacing those nutrients using organic compost or balanced fertilizers, the soil becomes tired and exhausted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ shika tsuru kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be koni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Kɛji jeee nakai lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo nakai niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shoo ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green foliage. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my main crops when I plant cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa?

english: Cowpeas and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, which naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants and improves soil fertility.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Egbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ

english: Why do my groundnut flowers push themselves into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts develop underground rather than on top of the branches. After pollination, the flower stem grows downward into the soil where the groundnut pods can safely form.
ga: Peanuts shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe niji anɔ. after pollination Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake up my yam vines on tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves lifted toward the light and away from moist ground where rot and diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ woɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he ni ekɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ akabɔ.

english: Why must I plant my cassava stem cuttings with the small leaf buds pointing upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava buds sprout new stems toward the sky. Planting them with the buds pointing upward ensures the branches grow properly toward sunlight while roots spread below to yield solid tubers.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii heei ni shɛɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni niji lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la mli. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shishi koni efee ŋmei ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into straws during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce surface exposure and conserve water. It is a natural self-defense action to survive dry heat until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ be mli koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu akafite. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do millet and sorghum handle long dry spells much better than my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Millet and sorghum have deep, spreading root systems that reach moisture deep underground, along with special leaf coatings that keep water from escaping during dry periods.
ga: Sorghum kɛ sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Kɛfata he lɛ, nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaje mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the yellow blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when afternoon temperatures get too hot or water levels change suddenly. This heat stress prevents the flowers from pollinating successfully to form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu lɛ mli tsake trukaa. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkaye omanye yɛ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are small worms eating ragged holes inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are pests called Fall Armyworms that hide in the tender center leaves of young maize to feed, which can stunt crop growth if you do not control them early with safe treatments.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii amli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa kɛji okuuu amɛ mra. kɛ tsamɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why does my rice grow better when shallow water stays on top of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ eshwɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns out competing weeds that steal sunlight and nutrients from the rice, while keeping the soil wet and soft so the rice roots can draw food continuously.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni juɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbala niyenii kɛba mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds and tree stumps before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei akui dani madu lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds and stumps removes competition for nutrients, water, and sunlight, allowing your young crop seedlings to grow strong roots quickly without being choked by wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei akutsei ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni kɔɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa odumɔwui bibii lɛ daa shishifãi ni wa oya ni koo mli tsei efiteee amɛ.

english: Why should I loosen or plow hard soil on my land before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo matsu shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Loosening hard soil creates air pockets and allows roots to easily spread and reach deep into the ground. It also helps rainwater soak into the soil rather than washing away your topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui baa ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa nugbɔ nu hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and weak when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?
