english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for limited soil food, water, and sunlight. Giving plants proper space ensures each one gets enough resources to grow thick, healthy stems and high yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ he gbɛ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ tsei ni mli tse, ni wa, ni woɔ yibii.

english: What happens to my seeds if I bury them too deep under the soil during planting?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply use up all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil to reach daylight, which often causes them to die underground or sprout very weak.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛaatsi amɛhe waa koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo tsei bibii waa kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do I need to start delicate crops like tomatoes in a small seedbed before moving them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato yɛ dumɔwui bibii amli lɛ? Dani mifã kɛtee miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli

english: Tiny seeds produce fragile sprouts that can easily be destroyed by heavy rains or insects on an open field. A nursery lets you protect and nourish seedlings until they are strong enough to survive on the main land.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni waaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ahe ni okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing—usually a few weeks after sprouting or during flowering—so the roots can easily drink up the nutrients without getting burned.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ loo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ ni shãaa lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why should I not pour chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing raw fertilizer directly against the stem can scorch and burn the plant's delicate tissues. Placing it a few inches away allows the roots to safely grow toward the food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni kɛ niyenii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe kɛya niyenii lɛ he.

english: Can I use dry animal manure on my crops together with store-bought chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛfata tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, combining them works very well; manure improves the soil's structure and ability to hold water, while commercial fertilizer supplies quick, concentrated nutrients that crops need during rapid growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ amɛ fee ekome lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli wa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or it is stressed by too little water or waterlogged soil. Nutrient feeding helps keep the leaves green and active.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛjɛ nu fioo tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the exact same crop on the same farm field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients that the crop relies on and allows pests that target that plant to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and pest-free.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ nɔ.

english: When maize turns yellow at the bottom in a V-shape, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The plant is moving its remaining nutrients from the older lower leaves up to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I plant them directly in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopies around them for the first two to three years to protect their tender leaves and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli lɛ koni ebu baai bibii ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting seeds too close together actually reduces your yield. The crops will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and tiny, weak cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are given the wrong fertilizer, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dani wɔdu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without forming any fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When daytime temperatures get too high or the air is extremely dry during hot dry spells, tomato pollen dries out and dies, causing the flowers to drop off before fruit can form.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl in intense heat as a defense trick to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and stop water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light rains even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa po bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over easily when tiny microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects destroy the root system underground, leaving the plant without an anchor to hold it in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ ŋshɔŋloo ko ni baaha emɔ lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Does my swamp rice need to stay completely flooded with deep water every day until harvest?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ mi-swamp ŋmãa lɛ awo nu mli waa daa gbi kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli?

english: While rice loves water to block weeds and maintain moisture, it does not need deep flooding all the time. In fact, fields need to be drained a few weeks before harvest so the stalks ripen evenly.
ga: Omɔ sumɔɔ nu, shi kɛlɛ, koni etsĩ jwɛi anaa ni ehiɛ fɛ̃i mli. Shi ehe ehiaaa ni nu lɛ agbɔjɔ be fɛɛ be. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ Esa akɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli otsii fioo komɛi dani akpa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ ahoo pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing shoots and soft roots even when I keep them inside a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ namɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ.

english: Yams have an internal biological clock. After a few months of rest after harvest, they naturally break dormancy to prepare for a new growing season, regardless of light levels.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ wala mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko. Beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Amɛfoɔ wɔɔhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee lɛ. ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni kane lɛ yɔɔ ha

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green and leafy. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever food is left in the old bottom leaves and sends it up to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɛ baai. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ ni ebaatsu kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyaye ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain, but not during heavy downpours. If you apply it right before a heavy rain, the water will wash the expensive fertilizer away before your crop's roots can drink it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ okɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to cover the soil around my crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering bare soil, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so your plants don't dry out fast in the sun. As the grass rots, it also turns into good food for your soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akagbi oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ fite Ebafeɔ niyenii kpakpa hu kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep dropping off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or when tiny insects called midges are not available to pollinate them. Healthy shade trees and moist soil help keep the flowers on the cocoa branches.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollination. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ kookoo niji anɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing small and thin instead of getting big and fat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe tseee yɛ agbo kɛ fɔmɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if the soil is packed too hard for the roots to expand, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the nutrient responsible for making roots swell up with starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee mlɛo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni ji niyenii ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ starch.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures your main tree gets enough strength to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa otso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their young fruits before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed young fruit when they get too hot, don't receive steady watering, or when tiny insects attack the fruit stem. Giving them regular water and light shade stops the fruit drop.
ga: Pepper tsei woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji edɔ tsɔ. Akɛ nu haaa lɛ daa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa aduawai lɛ ahe Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my new young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso hee

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily in full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that create living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Why do I have to clear the weeds and make high soil mounds before planting my yam cut-pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni mawo gɔŋ ko nɔ dani madu sweet potato ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep straight down, so they need soft, loose earth to expand easily. High mounds also keep water from gathering around the tubers and rotting them.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle bulb lɛ he ni ehaa egboɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat stress. Keeping whiteflies away with neem oil spray and watering regularly helps keep leaves flat and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ gbe ŋmeii yɛji lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow and drying up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rains wash nutrients away, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after growing for a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is too hard for tubers to expand, or if the soil lacks potassium, which is the key nutrient needed for root swelling.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why do my yam vines produce plenty of big green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, yam plants spend all their energy growing tall vines and broad leaves instead of storing energy in the tuber below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high during the day or when the soil gets extremely dry, causing stress that prevents fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni tsiɔ aduawai anaa lɛ baa.

english: Why are my pepper fruits rotting at the bottom while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Rotting bottoms on peppers are caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering that stops the plant from absorbing soil nutrients properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ni esaaa ni haaa amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my cowpea plants flowering well but not forming any seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ shi amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fail to form pods when heavy rains wash away the pollen or when high heat kills the pollen before insects can pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cowpeas nyɛɛɛ afee pods kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie pollen lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani kooloi bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees curling up and turning brown at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves dry out and curl when exposed to harsh direct sunlight without shade trees, as the young roots cannot draw up water fast enough to replace what heat evaporates.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛye dɔlɛ ni efo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to bear fruit compared to other farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain growth slows down when too many suckers are allowed to grow from one mother plant, causing them to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ baa shi kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ tso kome mli. Enɛ haa amɛshiɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my okro plants covered in white powdery spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ ahe eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ lɛ?

english: White spots are caused by a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly when crops are planted too close together without good airflow.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbage plants form open, spread-out leaves instead of a hard, tight head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa ni agbele ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ najiaŋ ni ehiɛ yitsei ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage fails to form tight heads when the weather is too hot or when caterpillars eat the central growing point early in the plant's life.
ga: Cabbage lɛ yitsoŋ tswaŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji ŋmeii ye he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear the weeds under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ mikoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Clearing small weeds and undergrowth beneath your cocoa trees helps the tree roots get full access to soil nutrients and water without competing with unwanted plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ajieɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ tsei ni ataooo lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Does clearing the ground under my cocoa trees hurt their growth?
ga: Ani he ni mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ?

english: No, keeping the ground level clear under cocoa trees protects them from pests and diseases that hide in bush, allowing your crop to grow healthier.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ ahe. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the ground under my tree crops is ready to be cleared?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ he ni mitsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie?

english: When the ground vegetation under your trees is light or sparse, it is the best time to quickly clear it before weeds grow thick and hard to handle.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ mli tseee loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ. Enɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ oya dani amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewa akɛ abaakwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow very heavily in open spaces but much less under big tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ waa yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ shi ekwɛɛɛ kwraa yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds need strong, direct sunlight to grow fast. Tall trees create a thick cover overhead that blocks light, causing ground vegetation beneath them to stay sparse.
ga: Jwɛi taoɔ hulu la ni naa wa, ni tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsiɔ kane lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ egbɛ eshwã.

english: What happens on the ground when the top branches of my trees grow too bushy?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ́ mitso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ dara tsɔ?

english: When branches become very thick and bushy up top, very little sunlight reaches the floor, which stops grass and weeds from growing thick on the ground.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛyashɛ ŋwɛi lɛ Hulu la fioo ko pɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi bibii shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do cocoa extension officers advise us to keep shade trees over cocoa while keeping the floor clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo nɔ, yɛ be mli ni wɔhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ lɛ?

english: Overhead shade protects cocoa leaves from direct burning sun, while a clean ground level ensures the cocoa roots get all the water and fertilizer you apply.
ga: Shade ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ nine shɛɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ.

english: If my trees have created a heavy cover overhead, will I still get too many weeds on the floor?
ga: Kɛji jwɛi ehà mitsei lɛ anɔ waa Ani maná jwɛi babaoo lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, a heavy overhead canopy naturally controls weeds by starving them of sunlight, leaving only sparse growth on the ground floor.
ga: Dabi, ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ yiteŋ lɛ baaye jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ hulu la ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ tsũ lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time for me to use a manual slasher on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shi lɛ baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A slasher works best when ground weeds are short or sparse; if the area is a dense jungle with low branches, using a slasher becomes very difficult.
ga: Slashers tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ kuku loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ eji koo ko ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Fɛnsi baafee nɔ ni wa waa.

english: Why am I finding it so hard to swing my slasher on the overgrown part of my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ mafo miklante lɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When top branches and low bush are too thick and dense, they block your tool's movement. You need to trim low branches first before you can easily slash the ground.
ga: Beni ŋwɛi niji lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Ebaatsi dɛŋdade lɛ nyiɛmɔ naa. Ehe miihia ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. dani enyɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo

english: How should I handle a farm area that looks like a dense forest before clearing the floor?
ga: Te esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni kooi babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aha tɛŋŋ dani ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: In very thick, forest-like areas, you must first clear space overhead and trim tangled branches so you have enough room to safely slash the ground weeds below.
ga: Yɛ he ko ni tamɔ koo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ Obaasumɔ ni ojie ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ni ofo tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni oná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to make green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil or cause waterlogging around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo eha nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Excess water fills up all the small air spaces in the soil, which suffocates the cassava roots. When roots cannot breathe, harmful fungi in the wet soil attack and cause them to rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Fungi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large broad leaves that provide vital shade and hold moisture in the air to protect the cocoa trees during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi koni ebu kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they suffer from water stress. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy so it can survive the heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small root systems that easily lose the fight against weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifã bibioo ko. ni nyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi awuu mlɛo koni ena nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do insect pests seem to attack my vegetable farm more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, wild plants dry up, so insects move into irrigated vegetable farms looking for water and green foliage. Additionally, crops are stressed by heat, making them weaker and easier targets for pests.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, koo mli tsei baagbi. Kplukai fãa kɛyaa aduawai aŋmɔji ni afɔɔ nu awo mli lɛ amli koni amɛyatao nu kɛ baai eŋɔli. Dɔlɛ hu haa ŋmɔshi nibii haoɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops if I plant maize on the same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time to recover. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites that suck sap from the undersides of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy vines but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tso ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to focus all their energy on growing leafy branches instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so extra fertilizer can hinder pod production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa edalɛ nɔ yɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ pod feemɔ naa.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight lines with proper spacing instead of scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures each plant gets adequate sunlight, air, and root space. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and less wasteful.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni afiteɔ nii babaoo.

english: Why is it so important for me to start planting my cocoa seedlings early in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi kookoo tsei adumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early gives young cocoa roots enough time to spread deep into the soil while water is plenty. This strong root system helps the young trees survive the long dry season when rain stops.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli wa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I prepare my land and plant late in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshinii lɛ anɔ kɛji misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni midu yɛ be ni shɛɔ lɛ naagbee?

english: Late planting forces young crops to face the hot, dry season before their roots are fully formed, which can stunt their growth or cause many of the seedlings to die.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be akpee dani shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dalɛ naa loo eha dumɔwui babaoo agbo.

english: Why are some cocoa trees on my farm growing very fast while others right next to them remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi miida oya yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ekomɛi miida oya lɛ? Tso bibioo ko lolo

english: Uneven growth happens when plants compete unequally for soil nutrients, sunlight, or water. Planting healthy seedlings at the same time and using proper spacing ensures all your trees grow at the same speed.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji tsei kɛ amɛhe miitswa shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, loo nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kome mli, ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ fɛɛ adara oya yɛ be kome mli.

english: How does using a measuring rope to line up my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Equal spacing prevents crops from crowding each other. It makes sure every single tree gets its fair share of sunlight, air, and ground nutrients to grow evenly.
ga: Gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ po baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe. Efeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ nɔmimaa ni ekwɛɔ koni tsei fɛɛ aná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I help my newly planted cocoa trees settle quickly and start growing fast in the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kokoo tsei ni midu ehee lɛ ni amɛtsake amɛhe oya ni amɛje shishi amɛda oya yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: You can speed up establishment by planting strong nursery seedlings early in the rainy season, providing shade plants like plantains, and keeping weeds away from their base.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shishitoo oya kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli, ni okɛ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains aha, kɛ jwɛi ni oootsi kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees to shield them until their own foliage grows thick enough to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baabu amɛhe.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers if they don't have enough water or nutrients to feed them all, or if tiny insects called midges have not pollinated the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ eshɛko efɔfɔi lɛ ahe pollen lolo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce very small pods even when the leaves look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Green leaves mean the tree has enough nitrogen, but growing large cocoa pods requires extra potassium and phosphorus in the soil. Without these nutrients, the pods stay tiny.
ga: Baai eŋɔli tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shi kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛɔ lɛ biɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii.

english: Why do I need to cut off side shoots and extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie cacao tso ni eda lɛ he ŋmeii kɛ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak branches so the tree can send its strength directly into making big cocoa pods rather than growing unnecessary leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: How does leaving dry leaves around the base of my cocoa trees help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Dry leaves act as a blanket over the soil, trapping moisture underground during hot weather and slowly breaking down into natural fertilizer for the tree roots.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: How do I know the correct amount of chemical medicine to spray on my crops so I do not destroy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Using too much spray can burn plant leaves and poison the soil, while using too little will not cure the problem. You should always use the designated measuring cup provided with the bottle and mix it strictly with the exact volume of clean water specified for your farm size.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ahe baai ni ekɛ tsofa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni nɔ fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nyɛŋ atsu naagba lɛ he nii lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni kɛ tɔ lɛ baa lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be. ni okɛ nu ni mli tse afutu mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ naa.

english: Is it true that spraying my sick crops every day will make them heal faster?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaha amɛtsa oya?

english: Over-spraying can stress or kill plants just like an overdose of human medicine. Crop chemicals need time to work inside or on the plant, so you must wait for the recommended period—usually 7 to 14 days—before applying another round.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ loo egbe amɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ feɔ yɛ adesai amli lɛ. Tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ heɔ be dani etsuɔ ​​nii yɛ tso lɛ mli loo emli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ be ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii lɛ, bei pii lɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14, dani okɛ sɛɛkuu kroko atsu nii.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together in the same knapsack sprayer to treat two plant sicknesses at once?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ afutu yɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne kome mli koni mikɛtsa tsei ahe helai srɔtoi enyɔ shikome?

english: Mixing chemicals without guidance can cause chemical reactions that burn your crop leaves or cancel out the effectiveness of both medicines. Always check with an officer or read the label before combining any products.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ko ni shãa tso lɛ baai lɛ aba loo ebaaha tsofai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nitsumɔ aba shi. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, bi mɔ ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ loo okane nɔ ni aŋma yɛ nɔ lɛ dani okɛ nɔ ko afata he.

english: Why did my tomato plants suddenly wilt overnight even though I watered them yesterday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboi nyɔɔŋ kome mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ nyɛ moŋ?

english: Sudden overnight wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root-damaging pests that block water tubes inside the stem. Regular dry weather causes leaves to curl and dry up gradually, whereas bacterial sickness attacks very quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa trukaa nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa lɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi daa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ fiofio. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ tutuaa mɔ oya waa.

english: Should I be concerned if yellow spots slowly spread across my cassava leaves over a few weeks instead of all at once?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahao kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ miiho fiofio? Egbɛ eshwa mi-cassava baai lɛ fɛɛ amli yɛ otsii enyɔ komɛi amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ

english: Gradual yellowing indicates a progressive viral infection like Cassava Mosaic Disease or a slow nutrient shortage. Early detection lets you uproot the few affected plants before sap-sucking insects spread the sickness across your whole farm.
ga: ŋmɔŋ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Tsɔɔ hela ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ mli ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he, tamɔ cassava mosaic hela. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa fiofio ni anaa mra Ehaa ojieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ekomɛi. Dani koolooi ni nuɔ nu lɛ baagbɛ helai amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ,.

english: How can I tell if a disease has taken full hold of my crops beyond saving?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela eŋɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ mahere?

english: When more than half of a plant's main stem or roots turn black, soft, or completely rotted, the plant cannot recover. At this stage, uprooting and burning the infected plant is necessary to stop the sickness from moving to surrounding healthy crops.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã titri loo shishifãi lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni fe fã batsɔ ediŋŋ, amɛfee blɛoo, loo amɛgboi kwraa. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsake. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashã amɛ koni hela lɛ akaya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the roots of my cassava plants rotting under the ground while the leaves on top still look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shi baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Root rot fungi attack below the soil where water collects after heavy rains. The leaves stay green initially because the plant relies on stored food, but the underground damage is already taking hold slowly.
ga: Root rot fungus lɛ tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ. Baai lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ shishijee mli ejaakɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ nɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni efite lɛ tee nɔ fiofio.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to appear all at once in large numbers on my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall armyworms lɛ jeɔ kpo babaoo shikome yɛ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay hundreds of hidden eggs under leaves that hatch at the same time. The tiny caterpillars feed inside the leaf rolls without being noticed until they grow larger and suddenly destroy the foliage visible to you.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ baai ni fɔɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ ashishi. Kplukai bibii lɛ yeɔ baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko yɔseee amɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ yɛ he ni obaanyɛ ona amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are suffering from bad weather or from a serious sickness in the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miikpe kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo hela ni naa wa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Sun heat and dry weather cause leaves across the entire farm to turn brown and dry up evenly. A plant sickness usually starts in small patches, causing distorted leaves, swollen stems, or pod rot that spreads from tree to tree.
ga: Hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ kɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ ha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ shishi yɛ hei srɔtoi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ, tsei lɛ efuu, loo pod rot ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the upper leaves remain dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: When soil nutrients are low, the corn plant naturally moves available nitrogen from its older lower leaves to feed the young upper leaves. Yellowing lower leaves are a clear signal that your field requires additional nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Abele tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi he miihia oyale lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is stressed from a lack of water or nitrogen in the soil. When the ground is too dry, the root system cannot pull essential nutrients up into the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbala niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ awo baai lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil, causing the plant to save its energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leafy tops grow huge and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are given too much fertilizer early on, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of expanding its tuber roots below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mra lɛ, Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to apply water directly to the soil or spray it over the top of my crop leaves?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu lɛ atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛshwie mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Applying water directly to the root zone keeps the soil moist where roots drink, while keeping leaves dry prevents fungal diseases from spreading in warm weather.
ga: Nu ni oooha shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu yɛ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ ni ahaa egbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I simple tell if my field soil has enough water for my vegetables without special tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi tsuuu nii?

english: Dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of soil: if it forms a ball without dripping water, it is ideal; if it crumbles like dry dust, your crops need water.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shi inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛmimɔ shikpɔŋ ni fa fioo. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ Abuɔ lɛ akɛ esa. Kɛji efolɔ tamɔ sũ ni egbi lɛ Nu he miihia Oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans alongside my maize help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil and naturally feeds neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid planting tomatoes in the same spot where I just harvested garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tomato dumɔ he yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mifo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family, meaning they attract the exact same soil pests and diseases, which build up in the ground if you do not rotate crops.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ji tsei akuu kome mli bii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baabua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsakeee.

english: Why are my crop seeds taking so long to sprout after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a precise balance of moisture, warmth, and air to sprout; if planted too deep or in dry, hard soil, the seed remains dormant or struggles to break through.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. loo ni eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ mli

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea plants curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to shrink their surface area and reduce water loss during peak heat, though it can also indicate sap-sucking insect pests.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nuɔ nu moŋ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crop growth if my field gets plenty of sunshine every day?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baafite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛji miŋmɔji lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa daa gbi?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer nutrients directly from under your crops, leaving your plants weak even if sunlight is abundant.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why is it helpful for me to cover the dirt around my crop stems with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from competing with your crops for water.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi kɛ onibii akaye nu he akaŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my farm in the early morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the afternoon heat causes water to evaporate before the roots can absorb it, and hot sun on wet leaves can cause leaf burning.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is direct heat from the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ wo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow root systems and tender leaves that dry out quickly under full sun. They require shade crops like plantains to act as temporary umbrellas while their roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai bibii hu gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil food and water, which results in thin plants and small cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baawuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant actively pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to keep its new top leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil wears out the specific nutrients maize relies on, while allowing pests and diseases tailored to maize to build up in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmãa damɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by adult moths directly inside the soft center of the maize plant where the leaves are tender and easy to eat.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ateŋ, ni baai lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ayeɔ oya lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming any small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the weather gets extremely hot or when the roots face sudden dry soil, which interrupts the flower's natural pollination process.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ kpe. Enɛ gbalaa bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants bend their flower stems down and push them into the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally push their fertilized flower pegs down into the soil because the actual nuts need darkness and moisture underground to form and grow into full pods.
ga: Peanut tsei tsiɔ fɔfɔi ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Anɔkwale mli lɛ, yɛ ŋmeii ahewɔ Ehe miihia ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can lift off the ground and capture as much sunlight as possible, which feeds the plant and allows it to swell into big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ awó amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni ehaa efuɔ ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and produce big cobs. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It traps moisture in the ground so it doesn't dry out fast in the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when we get heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground stays waterlogged for too long, the roots suffocate and soil fungi attack them, causing the tubers to rot before you can harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eshwɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil solution can help keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: What is causing holes in the leaf funnels of my young maize plants with green droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa?

english: This is damage caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the growing center of maize. Applying crushed wood ash or bio-pesticide directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning can control them.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ ni atswa loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ wo baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye enɛɛmɛi anɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. If the plant does not get steady water during flowering, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight gives the plant energy to pump nutrients underground to grow large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛpompa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they fight with the mother plant for food and water. Pruning them allows the mother tree to direct all its energy into making a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ. Ekɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ baawu koni ená niyenii kɛ nu. Tso ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together in the same field with my maize, or will they harm each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo amɛbaaye amɛhe awui?

english: Cowpeas and maize work very well together. Cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which nourishes the maize while helping to cover the soil and prevent weeds.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛtsiɔ jwɛi anaa.

english: Can I mix my weedkiller and pest spray together in the same tank to save time on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afutu mli yɛ tanki kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Mixing different farm chemicals together can weaken their strength or cause a reaction that damages your crops. Applying each chemical individually ensures it works at full power.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai srɔtoi futu mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi loo ekɛ nibii ni baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ aba. Tsofai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni akɛtsuɔ nii srɔtoi lɛ haa etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I fell behind on my spraying schedule, can I combine all my chemical treatments into one go?
ga: Kɛji mifo be ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ afee ekome yɛ be kome mli?

english: Combining delayed treatments reduces their effectiveness and can burn your crops. Even if you are late, you should still apply each chemical separately at its proper time.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofafeemɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ lɛ, ebaaha bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ aba shi, ni ebaanyɛ eshã onibii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ oshɛ sɛɛ moŋ Shi esa akɛ okɛ tsofa fɛɛ tsofa atsu nii srɔtoi yɛ be ni sa mli lolo.

english: Will mixing too many farm chemicals together in one spray hurt my growing plants?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsofai babaoo ni mikɛfutuɔ tsofa kome mli lɛ baaye mi tsei ni miida lɛ awui?

english: Yes, mixing multiple chemicals can create a strong mixture that stresses or burns your plants, leading to poor crop growth instead of protecting them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ko ni mli wa ni haa otsei lɛ haoɔ loo eshãa amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabu amɛhe.

english: How does adding water or other liquids to my farm chemicals affect how well they work?
ga: Nu loo nu krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he Te tsofai ni akɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ saa amɛnitsumɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If you do not follow proper mixing guidelines or if you mix chemicals that shouldn't go together, you compromise the chemical's potency, making it fail to control pests or diseases.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni sa ni kɔɔ futumɔ he lɛ tsuuu nii. Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni esaaa akɛ amɛfutuɔ amɛhe lɛ futuɔ. Obaaha tsofai lɛ anitsumɔ aba shi. Enɛ haaa anyɛ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai.

english: What happens to my crops if I miss the exact week I was supposed to spray them and decide to do it later?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo otsi ni esa akɛ mikɛshwie nɔ lɛ mli ni mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mafee sɛɛ mli?

english: Spraying late gives pests and diseases time to damage your crop, and applying the chemical past the right growth stage reduces its ability to protect the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ fiofio lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai náa be ni amɛkɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshinii lɛ. Ni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbuɔ ehe lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know the right time to apply sprays to my crops for the best growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: The right time depends on the specific crop stage and the pest problem. Applying each treatment individually at its recommended schedule gives the best agronomic result.
ga: Be ni sa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofafeemɔ fɛɛ tsofafeemɔ tsu nii yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni atsɔɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaha okwaayeli mli yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Is it better to spray my farm as soon as I see a problem or wait until I have time to treat everything at once?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ tsofa afɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji ona naagba ko pɛ loo ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná be ni okɛtsu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ he nii shikome?

english: It is best to treat problems early as they appear. Waiting to do everything at once causes you to miss the right timing, which ruins the chemical's effectiveness.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaatsu naagbai ahe nii mra. as it appears Mɛɛ ni ooofee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ baaha okɛ be ni sa lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the chemicals I bought not killing the insects on my farm like they are supposed to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni mihe lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbe lɛ?

english: Chemicals often fail because their strength was weakened by being mixed with other sprays, or because they were applied at the wrong time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ tsofai lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ejaakɛ amɛhewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo akɛni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa mli hewɔ

english: Why am I spending money spraying my crops but still getting a small harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifiteɔ shika kɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni mináaa yibii fioo lolo lɛ?

english: A low yield often happens when chemical applications are delayed or mixed together incorrectly, preventing the crop from getting the full protective benefits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ loo akɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa hebuu he sɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: What is the correct way to apply different sprays so my farm yields a good harvest?
ga: Gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii Te eji tɛŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: To get good yield, apply each crop protection chemical separately at its proper time rather than delaying and rushing to spray them all together.
ga: bɔni afee ni aná nibii kpakpai Okɛ tsofa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ eko fɛɛ eko atsu nii srɔtoi yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi ohe ni okɛ oyaiyeli afɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ eŋɔli su lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in humid, dark conditions. Pruning extra branches from nearby shade trees lets in sunlight and airflow, which stops the fungus from destroying your crop.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Niji niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ amli lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers is the best way to keep your farm safe.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Taakɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without growing into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and putting dry grass around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni aduawai aba.

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from each other. Removing extra suckers leaves enough nutrients for the main tree to grow a very large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die suddenly even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil usually means soil fungi or microscopic worms are rotting the roots so the plant cannot suck up water. Rotating your pepper field with crops like maize or cassava breaks the life cycle of these soil pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii miiha shishifãi lɛ miifite. No hewɔ lɛ tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu. Pepper ŋmɔji ni atsakeɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaafite shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ashihilɛ.

english: The best time is usually 2 to 3 weeks after your seeds sprout, because that is when roots are developed enough to absorb food. Applying fertilizer too early wastes it in the soil, while applying it too late reduces your final yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food in the soil so they can grow tall quickly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why is it important to use wooden stakes to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfee sweet potato wain tsei lɛ atsu nii lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy to grow big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to full light while keeping leaf diseases away.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni eŋmɛɔ lɛ koni enine ashɛ la ni fa nɔ lɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei amli helai hu anaa.

english: How does covering my garden soil with dry grass or leaves help my plants in hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with organic material, called mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the earth. It traps water in the ground longer and cools the soil roots during dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why can't I just spray chemical medicine to cure my cocoa trees when they get a virus disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ ehiɛ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Unlike insect pests that can be killed with chemical sprays, a plant virus lives deep inside the plant's sap. Once a tree gets infected with a virus like Cocoa Swollen Shoot, there is no chemical cure, and the tree must be cut down to protect the healthy ones.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ agbe lɛ he. Tsei ahe helai hiɔ tsei amli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji tso ko hela ko tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ, tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛbaatsa tso lɛ. Ni esa akɛ afolɔ tsei koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: If one cocoa tree on my farm gets sick with swollen branches, why do I have to cut it down?
ga: Kɛ́ hela mɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eko ni eniji efuu lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo lɛ?

english: A plant virus cannot be cured inside the tree. Leaving a sick tree on your farm allows insects to feed on it and carry the virus to your healthy cocoa trees, eventually destroying your entire farm.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ atsa tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kooloi bibii yeɔ amɛ ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ yaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What is the difference between an insect attack and a crop virus?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ kɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Insects are pests that bite, chew, or suck on your crop and can usually be controlled with sprays. A virus is a tiny germ inside the plant that distorts leaf growth and causes dieback, and it cannot be killed with regular pesticides.
ga: Kplukai ji kooloi ni ŋmɔɔ, amɛyeɔ loo amɛnuɔ oŋmɔshi nibii. ni bei pii lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akudɔ. Virus ji muawai bibii. Tso lɛ mli ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ekɛ gbele baa lɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ agbe lɛ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni afɔɔ namɔ

english: How do tiny bugs like mealybugs spread sickness between my cocoa trees?
ga: Te kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Mealybugs feed on the sap of infected trees and pick up plant viruses. When they crawl or get carried by ants to a healthy tree to feed again, they inject the virus directly into the healthy plant.
ga: Mealybugs yeɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛheɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Beni ŋmeii shwieɔ shi loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii ekoŋŋ. Amɛwoɔ hela lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign of a hidden root disease, a virus infection, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Rain or water alone cannot fix plants if a disease is attacking their internal system.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifã hela ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ he okadi. Virus hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ loo nu pɛ nyɛŋ asaa tso ko kɛji hela miitutua emli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that dry out easily under harsh sunlight. Planting plantains provides living shade to protect young cocoa trees and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Can I take seeds from a diseased cocoa pod and plant them to start a new field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: No, seeds taken from diseased plants can carry infections into your new land. You should always use certified, healthy planting material from approved agricultural officers to ensure your new crop stays healthy.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ ashwã oshikpɔŋkuku hee lɛ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ enɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wash or heat my cutlass after trimming sick trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ mi-daggers lɛ ahe loo mawo mli la beni mifo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When you cut a sick plant, infected sap sticks to the metal blade of your tool. If you use the same uncleaned cutlass on a healthy tree, you directly transfer the disease into the healthy plant.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ Latex ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ baakpɛtɛ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe dade ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛ okɛ nakai dade ni he tseee lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, Obaajie hela lɛ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to leave black, rotten cocoa pods hanging on my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi kookoo diji ni egbo yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rotten pods carry fungal diseases that release invisible spores into the air. Raindrops splash these spores onto healthy pods nearby, spreading the rot across your entire crop.
ga: Rotting pods ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anaaa lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Gbalamɔ fitemɔ oshwã onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: How do crop diseases travel from my neighbor's farm to my own farm?
ga: Te tsei ahe helai tsɔɔ kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Diseases can travel between farms on the wind, through rain splashes, on infected tools, or via insects moving from farm to farm carrying viruses and fungal spores on their bodies.
ga: Helai baanyɛ aya ŋmɔji ateŋ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ, kɛtsɔ nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ, yɛ nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli, ni hiɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or floods the roots so they cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ eyi nu ashwie shi, ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my farmland is getting tired and needs a rest from planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔi lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli kɛjɛ dumɔ mli?

english: Farmland shows it is tired when your crop yields get smaller every year despite good rain, leaves look light green or yellowish, and weeds that survive in poor soil start spreading across the field.
ga: Okwaayeli hei jieɔ tɔlɛ he okadii akpo beni onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Baai lɛ hu feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ. Ni jwɛi ni hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ bɔi ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ amli gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my neighbors plant cowpeas together with their maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ duɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?
