english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and push it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize growing right beside it.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yield in a single generation. If you replant seeds saved from that harvest, the plants will grow unevenly and produce much smaller cobs than the first crop.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, Tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni baa shi kwraa fe klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Underground cassava rot happens when water sits in heavy soil for too long, suffocating the roots, or when fungal diseases spread during rainy seasons. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo beni ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: What causes small black spots to appear on my young cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads through water drops in heavy rain and thick shade. Clearing weeds and pruning heavy tree branches improves air movement to prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nugbɔshiimɔi amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni tsii ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ yaa hiɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ akaho.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by severe heat, lack of soil moisture, or when tiny pests called capsids attack the flower buds before insects can pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani kooloi bibii baanyɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not hold deep in the ground. Heavy bunches pull the stem down, especially when strong winds blow or when tiny root worms weaken the underground base.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Niji babaoo gbalaa tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa loo kɛ́ shishifãi bibii komɛi yɛ jɛmɛ. gbɔjɔmɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo lɛ

english: Is it normal for my tomato plants to wilt during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ baagbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Mild wilting in the hot afternoon is normal because heat makes water escape from leaves faster than roots can drink. However, if the plant stays wilted in the cool morning, the roots lack water or are attacked by soil diseases.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shi, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lolo yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, Nu baa shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli loo helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Should I cut off the low branches near the bottom of my pepper plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ? Ani ebɛŋkɛ pepper tso lɛ shishi?

english: Trimming lower branches helps the pepper plant focus its energy on growing healthy fruits higher up. It also stops mud containing soil diseases from splashing onto the lower leaves when it rains.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa pepper tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni sũ ni helai eyi mli obɔ lɛ akashwie baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I buy at the local market are good enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa aba?

english: Good seeds are uniform in size, clean, and free from cracks or tiny insect holes. You can test them at home by placing seeds in a bowl of water; healthy seeds sink to the bottom because they are dense and full of life, while bad or damaged seeds float to the top.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, amɛhe tse ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii bibii loo kooloi ŋmeii. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ yɛ shia kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni okɛaawo nu tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi ejaakɛ amɛmli eyi obɔ kɛ wala. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ehiii loo ni efite lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crop seeds sprout fast when I buy certified seeds, but grow slowly if I use seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ mihe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Shi edaa fiofio kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred by plant scientists to have high strength, uniform growth, and resistance to early diseases. Seeds saved from past harvests slowly lose their strength over time and can carry over hidden diseases from the previous season.
ga: Tsei ahe nilelɔi efɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo. shweremɔ ni tamɔ ekome kɛ helai ni teɔ shi ewoɔ yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela ni akɛtee kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: A general rule is to plant a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its own size. Small seeds need to be planted near the surface so the weak baby sprout can reach the sun, while larger seeds have enough energy to push through deeper soil.
ga: Mla ni afɔɔ namɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ dalɛ toi enyɔ loo shii etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Ehe miihia ni adu dumɔwui bibii. Ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la. Shi dumɔwui wuji lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and look tired during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop leaves curl and droop during peak afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing too much water to the dry air. If the plant stands up straight again in the cool evening, it is simply protecting itself from the heat and is healthy.
ga: Tso baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli dɔlɛ be mli. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe he koni nu babaoo akafite kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli. Kɛji tso lɛ damɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Eji koni obu ohe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he ni oná hewalɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers before producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or a sudden dry spell in the soil. The crop drops its blossoms to save its own life and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni eye ebua wala kɛ hewalɛ kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa mɔ daa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my tomato plants suddenly wither and dry up even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiho trukaa ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil-borne diseases like wilt that attack the roots and block the tubes inside the plant stem. Even when water is present in the ground, the blocked stem prevents the crop from drawing water up to its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa tamɔ ŋmei ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni etsĩɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ Shi tso lɛ shishifã ni atsĩ naa lɛ haaa enyɛ egbala nu kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and ground nutrients. This competition makes the plants grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in small fruits or low yields.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛwoɔ yibii bibii loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge green leaves on top but produce tiny cassava roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ ŋwɛi shi cassava shishifãi bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen manure but lacks nutrients like potassium, the plant spends all its energy producing heavy foliage above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shi niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmaa baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my dying crops need water or if they are suffering from an insect attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii ni miigboi lɛ loo kɛji kooloi bibii miitutua amɛ?

english: Water-stressed crops will droop evenly across the entire field during the hot sun and recover overnight. Insect damage usually shows up as eaten edges, small holes, sticky liquid on leaves, or yellow patches on specific individual plants.
ga: Tsei ni nu haoɔ amɛ lɛ baashwie baai yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kooloi fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmeii ni ayeɔ, buji bibii, kɛ nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellowish instead of deep green when the crop is young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Yellowish leaves usually mean the young crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is flooded with excess water that prevents the roots from breathing and feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ni fa fe nine eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛha niyenii.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying when planted in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or Gliricidia to protect their delicate leaves from scorching and to maintain soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo glicidia. Koni akɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it really necessary for me to tie my yam vines onto wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni makɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso ko he beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yes, staking lifts yam leaves off the ground and exposes them to sunlight. Maximum sunlight exposure helps the plant convert light into food, resulting in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking baajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ tsei ná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ la amɛfeɔ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during very hot and dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwie baai lɛ yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ waa ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures are high and water is low, pepper plants suffer heat stress and shed flowers to conserve moisture. Applying mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and moist, preventing flower drop.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa ni nu lɛ hu faaa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ tsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hulutsoo be lɛ he. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Tsi fɔfɔii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow down the middle in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tip down the center rib of lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's life will restore green growth and increase cob size.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔŋ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ tsitsii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ shihilɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out small and woody even though the stems look tall and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛji tsei yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai ni kɛlɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of swelling its roots. A balanced fertilizer higher in potassium encourages root expansion rather than leaf growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ moŋ fe ni baa lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny waste inside the leaf whorl?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ yeli? ni ashɛrɛ jwɛi bibii ashwie baa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying recommended bio-pesticides or targeted neem seed extracts directly into the leaf funnel early in the morning destroys the pest before it ruins the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ afɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani ebaanyɛ efite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly into little cups and stop growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa aduawai lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a viral infection spread by tiny whiteflies. Controlling whitefly populations with neem sprays and removing infected plants prevents the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem spray ye whitefly ayibɔ nɔ, ni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are all the flowers on my cowpea plants dropping off before any pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Flower drop in cowpeas is caused by flower thrips, tiny pests that feed on delicate flower buds. Spraying early with safe insecticidal soaps or neem extracts preserves the flowers so they can mature into pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ yɛ cowpea mli lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi thrips. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo ko ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ Okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nu lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra suckers steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from the main mother tree. Pruning away unwanted suckers and keeping only two or three strong ones allows the main tree to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground as soon as the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water starves the roots of oxygen and promotes rot fungi. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil so fast if I keep it in my house right after picking it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ mikɛwo shĩa mli beni akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain a lot of moisture. If you store them in an airtight or damp room without proper drying, molds and insects quickly multiply and ruin the grains.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛji akɛ okɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli ni ogbiɛɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Fungi kɛ kooloi bibii baafa oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and dark just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe tseɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a living root that spoils naturally within 48 to 72 hours after harvest because it loses moisture rapidly and reacts with oxygen once cut from the plant.
ga: Cassava ji shishifã ni hiɛ ka ni baafite yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛji afo lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Why do my stored grains get destroyed by tiny insects even when I keep the room very clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa tsu lɛ mli tseɔ waa moŋ?

english: Weevil insects often lay invisible eggs inside the crops while they are still growing in the field. Once you store the crop, those eggs hatch into insects that eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Beni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly in the barn while my neighbor's yams last for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Yams spoil quickly if they get cut or bruised during harvest, or if they are exposed to direct sunlight. Uninjured yams stored in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded barn last much longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Sweet potatoes ni pilaaa ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ baahi shi be babaoo.

english: Why do my peppers and tomatoes dry up and wrinkle so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii kɛ tomatoi lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Once harvested, vegetables can no longer pull water from the soil, but they continue to lose moisture through their skin into the warm air, causing them to shrink and wither.
ga: Kɛji akpa Aduawai lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Shi lolo lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: How do I know when my beans or maize are dry enough to be put into storage sacks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-beans loo mi-corn lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo kotoku mli ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ?

english: You can test grains by biting them or pressing them with your fingernail; if they are hard and crack with a sharp sound without bending, they are dry enough for long-term storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooomɔ loo okɛ onineshi ni ooomɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ewa ni egbɛ eshwa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni efoŋ lɛ, no lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does keeping my crop sacks off the bare floor help stop them from rotting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi kotokui ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛkafite?

english: Placing crops on raised wooden platforms prevents moisture from the ground from soaking into the bags, which stops mold from growing and keeps pests away.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekabote kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃, ni ehaaa ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: How can I keep pests away from my stored grains without using dangerous chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ he ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: You can use airtight storage bags or clean, sealed drums. Removing the oxygen inside suffocates any insects and prevents new ones from surviving without needing chemical sprays.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ vacuum kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe loo baagi ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ atsu nii. Oxygen ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kooloi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaaa kooloi heei aje kpo ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: What is the best way to handle my harvested tomatoes so they do not smash or rot on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsu mi-tomato ni akpaa lɛ he nii? Koni tomatoi lɛ akakumɔ loo akafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Harvest tomatoes early in the morning when it is cool, sort out damaged ones immediately, and pack them in rigid wooden or plastic crates rather than sacks to protect them from heat and crushing.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomato leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tomato ni efite lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni akɛwoɔ tso loo plastic adekai ni wa amli Moŋ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku mli koni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: What must I do to my produce after harvest to make sure it is safe for people to eat and buy?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ minibii ni mikpaa lɛ sɛɛ koni mɛi anyɛ aye ni amɛhe shweshweeshwe?

english: You should harvest crops carefully to avoid damage, dry grains thoroughly to prevent toxic molds like aflatoxins, and keep the produce in clean containers away from dirt and chemicals.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni nɔ ko akafite. Ha ŋmaa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ akabote mli, ni okɛ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ awo tsɛnsii ni he tse mli ni muji kɛ tsofai bɛ he.

english: If I pick large seeds from my best maize plants to plant next season, will they produce bigger ears of corn?
ga: Kɛ mihala dumɔwui wuji kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baadara?

english: Yes, larger seeds from strong parent plants usually contain more stored food to help young shoots grow vigorously. They also inherit good growth traits from the parent plant, giving you a better chance of harvesting larger ears.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dumɔwui wuji ni jɛ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ niyenii babaoo ni akɛtoɔ koni eye ebua ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa. Amɛnáa dalɛ sui kpakpai hu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa hegbɛ ni okpaa toi wuji.

english: If I plant a very big seed yam sett, will it give me a much larger yam tuber at harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu sweet potato ni dumɔwui lɛ dara waa Ani ebaaha mi sweet potato tubers ni da kwraa kɛji akpa?

english: A bigger seed yam sett provides extra nutrients to the young vine early in its growth. This allows the plant to build strong roots and leaves faster, which usually results in a bigger tuber at harvest time.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni dumɔwui wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ haa wain tsei bibii lɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Is it normal for my pepper plants to produce two small fruits joined together from one flower?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii? Yibii enyɔ ni jɛ fɔfɔi kome mli?

english: Yes, this happens occasionally when two ovary parts inside a single flower fuse together due to heat variations or natural seed traits, resulting in double or 'twin' fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei komɛi lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ fɔmɔ kotokui enyɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi kome mli lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ latsaa loo adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ ahe su tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Enɛ haa sɛɛnamɔ ni ji enyɔ loo ‘twin’ baa.

english: Why do some of my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot or the plants do not get enough water, the stress causes tomato flowers to dry up and fall off before they can pollinate and form fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Haomɔ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollination ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow multiple stems while others only grow one single stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi duɔ tsei babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu duɔ ekome pɛ lɛ?

english: The number of stems depends on how many active buds or 'eyes' were on the stem cutting you planted. More eyes sprouting leads to multiple stems, which share the food supply in the soil.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ayibɔ damɔ yibii loo ‘tso’ ni yɔɔ tso ni ofoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ nɔ. Buds ni shwereɔ babaoo lɛ kɛ tsei babaoo ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ yeɔ egbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow flowers directly on their thick trunks instead of out on the leaf branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on their main trunk and thick branches so that the trunk can support the heavy cocoa pods as they grow and mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ amɛniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ cocoa tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ beni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help bring back the rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my cowpea vines growing lots of thick green leaves without producing any flowers or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo ni fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to grow lush leafy vines instead of flowers. Reducing nitrogen fertilizers will signal the plant to stop making leaves and start fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsina tsei hewalɛ koni amɛdu wain tsei ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa lɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni abaaba shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ feemɔ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need direct sunlight on their wide leaves to produce food for growth. Deep shade slows down their leaf production and delays fruiting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛna niyenii kɛha dalɛ. Shade ni mli kwɔ haa baai feemɔ baa shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do some okra seeds produce pods very quickly while others take a long time even though I planted them on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okra dumɔwui komɛi jeɔ kpo oya waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Different varieties of okra have different growth schedules. Fast-maturing varieties are bred to flower early, whereas local late-maturing varieties spend more time growing big roots and leaves before fruiting.
ga: Okra henɔi srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra koni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi kɛ baai wuji dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the bottom of the plant, usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their green color and supports healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to pour water directly at the roots of my crops or spray it over all the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooshwie nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Crops take in water through their roots, not their leaves. Pouring water at the base saves water, ensures moisture reaches the roots, and prevents leaf fungal diseases that thrive on wet leaves.
ga: Tsei gbalaa nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ, shi jeee kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Nu ni oooshwie shishi lɛ baaye abua ni nu akafite. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Should I burn the cleared bush on my field before planting, or let the dried grass rot on the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu loo maha jwɛi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Burning destroys beneficial soil nutrients and washes away valuable organic matter. Leaving the cleared grass to decay on the soil (mulching) traps moisture, keeps the ground cool, and turns into free natural plant food.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni ejieɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni he tse ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni aheee nɔ ko

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates shade and keeps the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently watered and enriched with compost helps the plant hold its flowers and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do pests attack my vegetables much more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: In the dry season, wild bushes dry up, forcing insects to move to your green crop fields for food. High heat also speeds up how quickly pests reproduce, causing their populations to explode.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, koo lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ gbiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ kooloi bibii aya ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ oya. ni haa amɛyibɔ ​​yaa hiɛ waa

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When tomatoes are planted too close, they struggle against each other for sunlight, air, and nutrients. Giving them adequate space allows sunlight to reach the whole plant, producing thicker stems and more tomatoes.
ga: Beni Aduɔ Tomato He ni Ebɛŋkɛ Tsɔ Tomatoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ amɛhe mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa tomatoi babaoo.

english: Will trimming off some lower branches from my tomato plant harm it or help it yield better?
ga: Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye yibii lɛ awui loo ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary lower branches helps the plant direct its energy toward growing bigger fruit rather than feeding excess leaves. It also improves airflow around the base, reducing fungal rot.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha baai ni fa fe nine lɛ niyenii Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant cassava on the exact same plot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of specific nutrients and gives soil-borne pests a permanent home. Alternating cassava with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa shia ni hiɔ shi daa. Ni akɛ ŋmei tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei baatsake ŋmei Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmei lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my previous harvest produce smaller yields than fresh seeds from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from dealers are specifically bred for high yields and disease resistance. Seeds saved over multiple seasons lose these strong genetic traits, leading to smaller harvests over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni jalɔi lɛ ewo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ be babaoo lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akpa nɔ fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dying when I plant them on land where people used to dig for gold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tso lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni be ko ni eho lɛ gbɔmɛi taoɔ shika tsuru yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil and leaves toxic chemicals like mercury in the ground. Crops like cocoa need clean, nutrient-rich soil to grow strong roots, so they struggle to survive on damaged mining land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ, ni ehaa tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei, tamɔ mercury, shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe bahia ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛhi shi yɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ ni efite lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has toxic chemicals in it before I waste money planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai fɔji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mafite shika kɛdu amɛ?

english: Soil contaminated with chemicals often looks unusually hard, crusty, or discolored, and even ordinary weeds struggle to grow on it. If seeds fail to sprout or young leaves turn yellow and dry up quickly, the soil may be toxic.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsofai ewo mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wa, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ehiɛ su tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. kɛ jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ po Miibɔ mɔdɛŋ lolo koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ loo baai bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei.

english: Is there anything I can plant to help heal soil that has been damaged by pollution?
ga: Ani nɔ ko yɛ ni manyɛ madu ni baaye abua ni etsa shikpɔŋ ni mujiwoo efite lɛ?

english: Yes, planting tough cover crops like leguminous plants (such as mucuna or sunn hemp) helps trap toxins, prevents erosion, and adds organic nutrients back into the soil to rebuild its health over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa (tamɔ mucilage loo sunn hemp) ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ tsofai fɔji. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛma hewalɛ ema shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and small even though I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow, stunted leaves usually mean the crop's roots cannot absorb nutrients. This happens when the soil lacks organic matter or when harmful chemicals in the soil damage the root tips.
ga: Baai ni egbɔjɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: How can I safely inspect my crops if my farmland has dangerous open pits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe? Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ buji ni agbele ni yɔɔ oshara hu?

english: Before planting, you should mark pit edges with wooden fences or bright flags, clear safe walking paths between crop rows, and fill smaller holes with stones and subsoil to prevent falls.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ piket gbogbo loo aflaŋaa ni kpɛɔ akadi bu lɛ naa. Nyiɛmɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ tsei akui ateŋ ni okɛ tɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ awo bu bibii amli. Koni akagbee shi

english: Which crops can survive on poor or damaged land where cocoa refuses to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ni efite nɔ ni kookoo kpooɔ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Hardy crops with tough root systems, such as cassava, sweet potatoes, or local leguminous cover crops, can handle poor soil better than sensitive tree crops like cocoa.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi ni mli wa, tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo maŋ lɛ mli ŋmei haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaanyɛ etsu shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe jwɛi tsei ni waaa tamɔ kookoo.

english: Will applying chemical fertilizer fix my land so my cocoa trees can thrive again?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ koni kookoo tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizers only provide plant food; they cannot wash away soil toxins or fix destroyed soil structure. You must first add plenty of organic compost or animal manure to rebuild the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii pɛ. Enyɛŋ ejie tsofai fɔji kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli loo esaa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni efite lɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings stop growing and remain tiny after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedling roots stop expanding when they hit hard, compacted subsoil or encounter chemical layers underground, which starves the plant of water and nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kpaɔ amɛhe shweremɔ kɛ́ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nɔ loo amɛkɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kpe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: How many years do I need to wait before damaged farmland becomes good for planting cocoa?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ wɔmɛ dani ŋmɔji ni efite lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha kookoo dumɔ?

english: Left alone, damaged land can take over ten years to recover. However, if you actively treat it with compost, manure, and cover crops, you can improve the soil health in 2 to 5 years.
ga: ashi lɛ pɛ Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baanyɛ ahe nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋma dani etsa, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 5 mli.

english: Can using water from a muddy stream near an old mine harm my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ faa ni mli ewo muji ni bɛŋkɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ momo ko mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, water from streams near old mines often contains chemical residues and heavy mud that coat plant roots, block nutrient intake, and make crops wilt and die.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔji momo lɛ amli lɛ mli tsofai ni eshwɛ kɛ muji ni tsii ni haa tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ yɔɔ mli. etsĩɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni anáa lɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and failing to grow on land that was used for local mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shika tsuru ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Mining destroys topsoil, which carries all the rich nutrients plants need to eat. When that top layer is washed away or mixed with chemicals, the soil cannot hold food or clean water, causing plant leaves to turn yellow and stay small.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ni niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ afɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ nɔ loo akɛ tsofai futu mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii loo nu ni mli tse. Ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why does rain water sit on top of my farm soil for days instead of sinking down to the roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo kɛyashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil loses its tiny air spaces. Without these air spaces, rain cannot soak down to the roots. Adding dried leaves, manure, or compost breaks up the hard ground so water can sink in.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ laajeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui nɛɛ bɛ Nugbɔ nyɛŋ abote mli kɛyashɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni nu lɛ abote mli.

english: Why does my farm produce less harvest every year even though I plant the same crop at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli po.

english: Planting the same crop every season pulls the exact same nutrients out of the earth until the ground becomes empty. Changing to different crops each season allows the soil time to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ atsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi anɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ehaa ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes when the afternoon sun becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much moisture in extreme heat. It is the plant's natural way of saving water until the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ hulu la ni mli ejɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by dry soil, excessive heat, or a lack of essential nutrients in the ground.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. hulutsoo ni fa fe nine loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: If I plant beans together with my maize, will the beans steal food away from the maize?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa Ani ŋmãa lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: No, beans actually help maize grow better. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, providing natural fertilizer that feeds the neighboring maize.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ dumɔ.

english: Why does my sweet potato farm produce very large vines and leaves, but only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ wain tsei kɛ baai wuji waa, shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the sweet potato plant spends all its energy building big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers under the dirt.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing dark green and bushy, but taking a very long time to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eheɔ be babaoo waa dani ekɛ yibii baa.

english: Using too much leaf-growing fertilizer tells the tomato plant to keep making leaves and stems instead of spending energy on growing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha o-tomato tsei lɛ aya nɔ awo baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ kɛdu fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than regular crops and quickly drink up the water and take the fertilizer from the soil before your crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛgbalaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: Why do insect pests chew large holes in my cassava leaves mostly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ buji wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli be pii lɛ?

english: The moisture and fresh green leaf growth in the rainy season create ideal conditions for pest eggs to hatch and feed heavily on soft young leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ adalɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Can I use the same spray chemical meant for tomatoes on my corn farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ tomato nɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii?

english: No, chemicals are formulated for specific crops. Tomato sprays may not control maize pests properly, can burn corn leaves, or leave harmful chemical residues on food meant for your family to eat.
ga: Dabi, afee tsofai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Ekolɛ tomato spray lɛ nyɛŋ akudɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eshã ŋmãa baai Aloo eshi tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii mli koni oweku lɛ aye.

english: Why is it important to buy my farm chemicals and seeds from authorized agro-dealers instead of open market vendors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahe tsofai kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni aha lɛ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ moŋ fe jarayelɔ ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Buying from certified dealers ensures you get genuine, high-quality inputs specifically designed for your crops, protecting you from fake chemicals that can damage your harvest or fail to control diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ohe nii kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ enɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ, ehaa onine shɛɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni afee aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ tsofai amalei ni baanyɛ afite onibii loo ni nyɛŋ akudɔ helai lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if I am putting too many crop seeds close together in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui miiwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If crops are planted too close, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and small fruits or ears, reducing your total crop yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii loo toi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: What is the best way to arrange my crops so both my cash crops and food crops grow well?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mato miŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ koni mishika ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Give each crop type its own space and proper spacing, or plant taller crops like maize in rows that do not completely block sunlight from smaller crops like tomatoes.
ga: Ha tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ he ni sa kɛ he ni sa. Aloo dumɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ ŋmãa mli ni tsiii hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii, tamɔ tomatoi amli lɛ naa kwraa.

english: How should I decide how much land to plant for crops I want to sell versus crops my family will eat?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni misumɔɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ ayibɔ kɛ nɔ ni miweku lɛ baaye lɛ he?

english: Plan your household food needs first to guarantee your family's meals, and then dedicate the remaining land and inputs to market crops that bring in reliable cash income.
ga: Too niyenii ni he hiaa bo yɛ oshia lɛ he gbɛjianɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oweku lɛ baaye niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaanyɛ ahé ni haa anáa shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested tomatoes to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saved seeds from commercial or hybrid varieties often grow into weaker plants with small yields. Buying fresh, certified seeds every season ensures strong plants that resist diseases and yield heavily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ jarayeli tsei srɔtoi loo tsei ni akɛfutu mli lɛ amli lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ. Enyɛɔ helai anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: What happens to my crops if I put too much fertilizer on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer burns plant roots, causes leaves to turn yellow or brown, and wastes money without increasing your harvest yield.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. kɛ shika ni afiteɔ ni nibii ni anáa lɛ eyaaa hiɛ

english: Why do my crops grow well in some parts of my farm but stay small in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi amɛhe ehiaaa yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil fertility, moisture level, and sunlight vary across a field. Areas with poor drainage, shaded trees, or depleted nutrients produce smaller plants unless you add compost or fertilizer.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Humidity level Kɛ hulu la lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ Ayɛ tsei lɛ ahe hulutsoo. Aloo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee bibii. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why do pests quickly move to my new crops after I clear an old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli oya nɛkɛ beni mijie momobii lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests survive in leftover crop leaves and soil after harvest. Clearing field debris completely and resting or rotating the land breaks the pest cycle before you plant fresh crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei amli jwɛi fɛɛ ni okɛjɔɔ ohe loo otsake he lɛ, ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii ni baa lɛ amli dani odu tsei heei.

english: How do I know when my vegetable crops are ready to be harvested for the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-vegetables lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni akɛya jara nɔ?

english: Vegetables for the market should be picked when mature but firm so they do not spoil during transport, whereas crops meant for immediate home consumption can ripen fully on the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa aduawai ni akɛbaajara lɛ beni edara kwraa shi eyɛ shiŋŋ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafite yɛ gbɛfaa mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ yɛ shia amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same piece of land with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds the soil, helping your maize grow stronger without exhausting the land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests that feed on maize to build up in the earth. Rotating with legumes or root crops keeps the soil healthy and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant green up and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛbaa ŋmɔŋ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves. Treating the plants with neem oil or recommended insecticides stops these pests from stunting your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu tsei ahe nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist during the flowering stage helps the plant turn those flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa nakai fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ aduawai.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the heavy tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ fungal leaf helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tubers lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on the soil around my vegetables during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Mi aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: Spreading dry plant materials—called mulching—keeps the sun from baking the soil. It traps moisture in the ground longer, reduces the need for frequent watering, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa nu ni afɔɔ he hiamɔ baa shi. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack open. You can gently dig up one root to check if it has reached a good size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa Obaanyɛ Ofo shishifã kome fiofio koni ona kɛji eyɛ dalɛ kpakpa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not wash my money away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akajie mishika lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, but not immediately before a heavy downpour. Covering or slightly burying the fertilizer in the soil near the plant roots prevents rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko ha shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nɔ loo ofu lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekashwie lɛ.

english: Why does the water disappear from my field so quickly after rain during the dry season, making my crops dry out fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Mahã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi oya?

english: When soil lacks organic matter like compost or dried leaves, it cannot hold water like a sponge. Direct sunlight evaporates surface moisture instantly, leaving plants thirsty shortly after rain.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa kumai yeɔ tsei yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: I applied fertilizer to my corn, but after one heavy rain, the soil looks empty and the leaves turn yellow. Where did the plant food go?
ga: Mikɛ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ko sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli ni baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nɛgbɛ niyenii ni akɛ tsei fee lɛ etee?

english: Heavy rains wash away mobile nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground below the root zone, especially in sandy soils. Split application of fertilizer in smaller amounts prevents this rapid loss.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa sũ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mlijaa bibii bibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nibii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the young pods on my cocoa tree turning black and drying up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and shade. Pruning overhead branches lets sunlight and air in to dry the pods and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni afoɔ yɛ yiteŋ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall stems with lots of green leaves, but when I dig it up, the tubers are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi be ni mitsa lɛ, mina akɛ yitso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines high off the ground instead of letting them spread on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight and fresh air, which prevents fungal diseases from the wet soil and gives the plant energy to build large tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba, ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to destroy my entire maize field overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide deep inside the central whorl of the leaves during the day to avoid heat, then feed rapidly at night when it is cool, making the damage appear sudden.
ga: Asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, oya taomɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa trukaa

english: I have planted maize on the same piece of land for three years, and now the plants stay short and yellow. Why is the soil failing?
ga: Mikɛ afii etɛ edu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ni amrɔ nɛɛ tso lɛ efee kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔji lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients without giving the earth time to recover. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: My tomato plants are flowering well, but the blossoms just fall off without turning into tomatoes. What is causing this?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miikwɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ tomato. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely high or when soil moisture swings rapidly from very dry to soaked. Mulching helps maintain steady soil moisture.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting tight like a fist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ fiji lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viruses spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Should I use a tractor to plow my land before planting, or is clearing by hand better?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ trakta atsu nii kɛtsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani madu loo mikɛ minine atsa mli?

english: Tractor plowing loosens compacted soil quickly so young roots can spread easily, but over-plowing can wash away topsoil during heavy rains, so it depends on your land's slope and soil type.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Shi kɛ́ atsu nii babaoo fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, no hewɔ lɛ, ejɛɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ehaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ̃ lɛ mli.

english: Is it okay to cut down all the big trees on my farm before I start planting new crops?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ afo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani mabɔi tsei heei adumɔ?

english: Clearing all trees exposes your soil to harsh sunlight and soil erosion. Keeping some native trees provides natural shade, preserves soil moisture, and returns nutrients to the land through fallen leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aná oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei komɛi akwɛmɔ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take several years to produce fruit while maize takes only a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa hiɔ shi nyɔji fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are long-term tree crops that spend their early years building deep roots and strong trunks to sustain fruit production for decades, while annual crops like maize complete their entire lifespan in one short season.
ga: Kookoo tso ji tso ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yeɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni edaa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni baaha aduawai aya hiɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa afi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, yeɔ amɛwala be fɛɛ yɛ be kome pɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young orange trees turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso bibioo lɛ nɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and shedding leaves during dry periods is the tree's natural way of saving water so it can survive the heat until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce plenty of flowers but very few of them turn into real nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ fioo ko pɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fail to turn into fruit mainly due to a lack of pollinating insects, extreme heat drying out the blossoms, or pest attacks like thrips while the tree is flowering.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai, titri lɛ yɛ nɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ. Aloo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ thrips, tutuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same land, or will they ruin each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaafite amɛhe?

english: You can plant them together because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving plenty of room and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa mra. Shi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni baaha ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ afɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my young oil palm trees close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ oil palm dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná gbɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting oil palms too close causes their large fronds to block each other's sunlight and forces their roots to compete for soil nutrients, which leads to lower oil yields overall.
ga: Kɛ́ adu mu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛbaai wuji lɛ atsĩ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. kɛ ŋmei tsei ashishifãi ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, mu ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer crops after growing the same plant on it for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop year after year exhausts the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers look weak and dry right after I move them to a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛgbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Transplanted suckers experience root shock when moved, but once their new root system settles into the ground over a few weeks, fresh green shoots will start growing.
ga: Suckers ni adu lɛ baaya shoofeemɔ mli kɛ́ atsake shishifãi lɛ. Shi kɛ́ shishifãi heei lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli lɛ, Young green shoots lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Should I sweep away the leaves that fall from shade trees onto my crop land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ amli kɛya he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: It is better to leave them on the ground because fallen leaves act as natural mulch, keeping the soil cool, trapping moisture, and turning into free fertilizer as they rot.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ejaakɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko beni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell early on if my coconut trees are getting sick before they stop fruiting?
ga: Kulɛ mile nakai mra. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ dani ekpa yibiiwoo?

english: Check the young leaves at the top and the newest flower shoots; if the leaves begin turning yellow prematurely or unopened flowers drop off, the coconut tree is showing early signs of infection and needs attention before the stem decays.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi heei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mra loo fɔfɔi ni agbeleee lɛ gbee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ miitsɔɔ mra be mli ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ, ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani ŋmei lɛ shishifã lɛ agbo.

english: Yellowing that starts at the bottom leaves and spreads upward usually means the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged, causing the plant to move remaining food to its newest growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa tso hee ni eda fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ?

english: If your cassava plants drop leaves suddenly, look wilted despite rain, or emit a sour smell from the soil around the base, the tubers below are likely rotting due to poor drainage or fungal attack.
ga: Kɛji o-cassava tsei lɛ gbee shi trukaa lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ. Aloo sũ ni bɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ko yɛ. Ekolɛ bulb lɛ shishi lɛ miifite yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull water from the soil, causing temporary drooping; plants usually recover once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shigbeemɔ baa. Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ naa hewalɛ kɛji hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when day temperatures get too hot, when plants suffer from irregular watering, or when small insects attack the delicate flower stems.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei naa naagbai ni kɔɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small root systems that cannot handle direct, full sunlight. They need shade trees or food crops like plantains to shelter them from heat during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, koni ekɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tsei kakadaji adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to produce enough energy to grow large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ koni amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal food, water, and sunlight from the main stem, resulting in smaller plantain bunches and weaker overall plants.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa plantains bibii kɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ baa.

english: What causes broad ragged holes inside the central funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes and chewed leaf edges inside the central funnel of maize are typically caused by fall armyworms, which hide in the plant whorl during the day and eat the tender inner leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, asraafoi aŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ kɛ baai ni ashɛre yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei akui amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are small green insects crowding under the leaves of my pepper plants and making them curl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiiha amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Those insects are likely aphids, which suck the vital sap from young shoots and cause the leaves to curl and dry up. Spraying your pepper plants early with an organic neem seed extract or mild soapy water solution helps wash them off and protects your harvest.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji aphids, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ. Akɛ organic neem dumɔwui loo nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ saamɔ ewo mli lɛ shwieɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni efɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ ahe ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall with green leaves but produces small, half-empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Fã efolo?

english: Maize cobs fail to fill completely when plants lack sufficient soil nutrients like nitrogen or when they lack adequate water during the flowering stage. Giving your corn organic manure early on and ensuring good spacing between plants helps every cob develop full kernels.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ aha ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ emli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ha ŋmãa mra Ni akɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaye abua ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa ni ewo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: How can I tell if my land is ready and healthy enough for me to plant vegetables like pepper and tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato?

english: Healthy vegetable soil should be dark, moist, and crumble easily in your hand without forming hard clay clumps. If water drains quickly after rain without leaving long-standing puddles, your land has good drainage suitable for vegetable roots.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli lɛ afee ediŋŋ, ni edɔ, ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ onine mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni mli wa baaa. Kɛji nu lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni eshiii nubui be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sa kɛha shishifãi akwɛmɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to put my corn seeds into the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ?

english: It is best to plant maize right after the first couple of heavy, reliable rains have thoroughly soaked the soil. Planting in dry soil before steady rains arrive can cause seeds to dry out or germinate unevenly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating big holes in the leaves of my young corn crop?
