ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest that feeds inside the growing leaves of corn plants. Checking your field early and applying targeted safe insecticides or neem powder into the whorl of the plant stops them before they destroy the field.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem powder ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛkpãtã ŋmɔji lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How often should I pick my pepper crop once the fruits start turning red?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting ripe peppers frequently encourages the plant to produce new flowers and yield more fruits over a longer period. Leaving mature peppers on the stem too long signals the plant to stop producing fresh flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ajieɔ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi heei kɛ aduawai babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni eda lɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ.

english: Why do my young crops start off growing well but then turn yellowish and stop growing after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ je shishi amɛdara jogbaŋŋ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpa dalɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops turn yellow when they exhaust the quick nutrients in the topsoil and need extra food to keep growing. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a balanced fertilizer around the base of the plant gives them the nitrogen boost required to stay green and active.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii oya lɛ. ni ehe miihia ni niyenii krokomɛi afata he koni eya nɔ eda Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ nitrogen kroko ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni etsu nii.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them during the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning is much better because it lets the roots absorb moisture before heat builds up, reducing water loss from evaporation. Water droplets sitting on leaves during intense afternoon sun can also scorch sensitive leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ leebi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulutsoo lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashã.

english: Why does my harvested corn develop dark insects and powder while sitting in my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ powda ni tsuɔ diŋ be mli ni mita nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive when stored corn still has hidden moisture inside the kernels. Drying your corn thoroughly in the bright sun until the cobs are completely dry before putting them in airtight storage bags keeps these pests out.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baagbi kwraa dani akɛwo vacuum storage kotokui amli lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa nɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Can I grow corn and cassava together on the same plot of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting corn and cassava together is a great strategy because corn grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, leaving the slow-growing cassava behind to use the full space and mature over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ heɔ he ko ni edaa yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What should I do if my farm is so overgrown that I cannot even get inside to work?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni minyɛɛɛ maya nitsumɔ?

english: If you cannot access your farm, it is okay to leave it for a while and wait. Nature, decay, and natural pests will gradually break down the thick growth and dead wood, making it easier for you to enter and clear later.
ga: Kɛji obɛ gbɛ kɛya oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Obaanyɛ oshi jɛmɛ be fioo ni omɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ. ni adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baafite fãi ni mli tse kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ fiofio. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaabote mli ni oyajie nibii amli sɛɛ mli.

english: If I cannot clear my overgrown land right now, will leaving it untouched ruin it?
ga: Kɛji minyɛɛɛ majie shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ bianɛ lɛ, ani kɛ́ mishi lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaakpata ehiɛ?

english: No, leaving an overgrown or inaccessible farm untouched for a period will not ruin it. Waiting allows old plants and dead trees to break down naturally until you are ready to manage the land.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔ ko ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo ni anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ be ko mli lɛ efiteee lɛ. Mɛɛmɔ baaha tsei ni egbɔ ni egboi lɛ agbo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaatsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii.

english: Can I leave my old, diseased cocoa trees on the land instead of cutting them down immediately?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, you can leave diseased old cocoa trees standing until the disease or natural decomposers completely destroy what remains before you clear the land and plant fresh crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oshi cacao tsei ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi helai loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baafite nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ dani ojie jɛmɛ ni odu nibii heei.

english: What will happen if I just leave my old diseased cocoa trees alone on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If you leave old diseased cocoa trees alone, the disease and insects will eventually run their course and destroy the remaining tree structure naturally over time.
ga: Kɛji oshi kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ, Helai kɛ kooloi bibii baaya hiɛ yɛ naagbee ni amɛbaafite tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant new cocoa seedlings immediately next to my old diseased trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ kookoo tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting immediately while old trees are still diseased can expose your new crops to infection. It is safer to wait until the old trees are completely destroyed and dead before putting new plants in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ be mli ni tso momo lɛ ehiɛ hela lolo lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba otso hee lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi tso momo lɛ baafite kwraa ni egbo dani okɛ tso hee awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Are termites on my farm always a bad thing that I need to spray?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ ni esa akɛ ashwie nɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Not always. While termites can be pests, they also act as natural clearers by eating and completely destroying old, dead, and diseased cocoa trunks without requiring you to do heavy manual labor.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ afee ŋmeii moŋ. Shi amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛtsɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ, ni egboi, kɛ helai ni emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛfiteɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ niji atsu nii waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it okay if termites are eating the old cocoa trunks on my farm?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ ŋmeii baaye kookoo tsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, it does not matter if termites destroy the old trunks first. They help speed up the removal of dead, diseased wood, clearing the space for your future planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji ŋmeii fiteɔ tso momo lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ajieɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ helai ni emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Ha gbɛ ni abaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How do I know when an old farm with diseased cocoa is ready for replanting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔ momo ko ni kookoo ni hela emɔ mli lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ hee?

english: An old farm is ready for replanting after the old diseased trees have been completely destroyed and broken down by disease, time, or insects like termites.
ga: Okwaafoi momo yɛ ni abaanyɛ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni egbɔ ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ efite ni hela, be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii efite amɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it better to clear old dead wood by hand or wait for it to rot away?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ okɛ onine baajie tso momo loo ooomɛ ni egbo?

english: If you cannot easily work the land, waiting for dead trees to rot or be destroyed naturally by termites saves time and labor before you begin planting.
ga: Kɛji onyɛɛɛ otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii mlɛo Mɛmɔ ni tsei ni egboi lɛ baafite yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo ŋmeii akpãtã amɛhiɛ lɛ haa be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ baa shi dani obɔi dumɔ.

english: Should I wait for an old crop to completely die out before spending money to plant a new one?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni tsei momo lɛ agboi dani mafite shika yɛ tsei heei ahe?

english: Yes, waiting until an old, diseased crop is completely destroyed by natural processes ensures that you don't waste money planting new crops in an active disease environment.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛmɔ kɛyashi be mli ni adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔi baafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ shika akafite kɛdu tsei heei yɛ shihilɛ ni helai ni naa wa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure around the roots helps the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaabɔle lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ etoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds early when my crop seeds are just sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ mra? Beni midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ kɛkɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts are weak and compete directly with weeds for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nutrients it needs during its critical first few weeks of growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava produce very small tubers even though the stems and leaves look tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛlɛ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of underground tubers. Using balanced plant food and planting in loose, well-drained soil helps the plant focus on swelling its roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso niyenii ni ja tsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bɔ ni eeefee eshishifãi lɛ ni efuu lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I stop my pepper flowers from falling off before they form fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi pepper fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Watering regularly during dry spells and keeping organic mulch around the base keeps the soil moist and holds the flowers on the plant.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii tamɔ calcium bɛ ehe. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow long vines with lots of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce too many leaves and few pods if planted in shady spots or if the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer. Beans prefer full sunlight and produce more pods when not over-fertilized with nitrogen.
ga: Cowpeas baawo baai babaoo tsɔ kɛ ŋmeii fioo kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ. Peas sumɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa ni ewoɔ pods babaoo kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen wooo mli fe nine.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots on the bottom as they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black spots on tomato bottoms are known as blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Watering your crop on a steady schedule and mixing wood ash or lime into the soil before planting prevents this.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ tso sũ loo lime ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are tiny white flies clustering under my cassava leaves, and are they dangerous?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ lɛ? Abua naa yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi. Ani eyɛ oshara?

english: These tiny white insects are whiteflies that suck plant juices and spread Cassava Mosaic Disease, which curls leaves and stunts growth. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing heavily infected plants keeps the pest population down.
ga: ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ dalɛ naa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plant leaves curl up and burn during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct hot sunlight and harsh dry winds during the Harmattan. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cooler canopy that protects fragile young cocoa leaves from scorching.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa ni mli egbi yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits too long around the roots, creating damp conditions where soil fungi thrive. Planting yam on tall ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely from the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji loo gɔji anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take over a year to start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani midumɔwui lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains grow slowly when they lack regular water, shade during early growth, or rich organic nutrients. Adding decomposed manure around the stem base and removing extra suckers so only two or three grow at a time speeds up fruit production.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa fiofio kɛ́ nu ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Shade ko bɛ yɛ dalɛ be mli. loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he kɛ suckers lɛ ni ajieɔ koni 2-3 pɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai aba oya.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees or plantain trees protect young cocoa seedlings from drying out and scorching, giving them the cool, humid climate they need to survive and build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkashã. Enɛ haa amɛnáa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease that thrives in wet, dark, and damp conditions. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and air flow through your farm, which keeps the pods drier and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaakpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ babaoo ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does pruning my mature cocoa trees help them grow more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or unproductive branches so the tree does not waste water and food on them. It also allows sunlight to touch the main trunk, which encourages the tree to produce more flowers and healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. koni tsei lɛ akafite nu kɛ niyenii Ehaa hulu la hu shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ woɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to build food and stay green. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and produces bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the dry soil around my crop roots with dead grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi baawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass keeps the soil cool and prevents sunlight from drying out the moisture. As the leaves decay over time, they also turn into natural food for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa hulu lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ agbi. Beni baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ Baai lɛ hu bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same farm patch every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the exact same spot drains all the specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to uproot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and begin to drop off, usually 9 to 12 months after planting. You can carefully dig around the base of one stem to check if the tubers are large enough before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi shwiemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso kome shishigbɛ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my cassava and vegetables so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha mi-cassava kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ miiba shi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow fast and yields remain strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni yibiiwoo lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away extra side shoots growing on my plantain tree leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo sɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: If too many side shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they all compete for the same food and water from the ground. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, helping the plant grow large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ni miida yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Tsoi wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli hu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme sun heat, hot dry winds, or inconsistent watering. Giving plants steady water and partial shade during extremely hot periods keeps the flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong. When the plant does not get enough nitrogen from the soil, it moves food from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves, turning the bottom leaves yellow.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants producing plenty of leafy green foliage and flowers, but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi pods diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes plants to focus on growing leaves rather than fruits. Additionally, tiny insects called thrips might be attacking the blossoms, causing them to fall off before forming pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ fe aduawai. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ hu baanyɛ atutua fɔfɔi lɛ. Ha amɛgbee shi dani amɛfee pods.

english: Why do my young maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves with powdery waste trapped inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plants lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ sũ ni etse ehe lɛ ekpɛtɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central growing funnel of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the tender leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛbɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily in light winds once they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ? Mɛɛ be obɔi tsɔne agbo ko hiɛmɔ?

english: Microscopic worms called nematodes or banana root weevils feed on the roots and underground stems, destroying the plant's anchor in the soil so it cannot hold heavy fruit.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana shishifãi lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ tsei ahe. Efiteɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ anyɛɛɛ abua aduawai ni tsii anaa.

english: Why do my healthy green cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, humid weather. Trimming overgrown shade trees to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni edara fe nine lɛ ni aaakpa koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni akpaa oya lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the soil even though the stem and leaves above ground look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lolo moŋ?

english: This is caused by cassava root rot, which happens when soil stays waterlogged for too long. Excess water starves the roots of air, allowing fungi in the soil to break down the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi fitemɔ kɛ enɛ baa, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves get dark spots and die off early before the yam tubers are full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is Yam Anthracnose, a fungal disease that spreads through rain splashes. It destroys the leaves early, stopping the plant from making food to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ. Fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ mli Ebaakpata baai lɛ ahiɛ mra. Ehaa tso lɛ hoɔ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Extreme heat during the day or dry soil causes heat stress in tomatoes. When stressed, the plant sheds its blossoms to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my garden eggs and vegetable leaves droop and wilt during the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to reduce water loss, but relaxes when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi ejɔɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why does water stay in the ground longer on one side of my farm than the other side after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli be kakadaŋŋ fe fã kroko lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Different parts of your farm have different soil types. Sandy soil lets water drain away very fast, while clay soil has tiny particles that trap water, keeping that area wet for a longer time.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya waa. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii. Nu ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ Haa he ni eyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does putting dry grass or crop leaves around my cassava plants keep the soil damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai fataa he lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shades the dirt from the hot sun. This stops heat from evaporating the ground moisture quickly into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi muji ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my field and make mud instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ taraa miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ni etsɔɔ muji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil is pressed down hard or contains a lot of heavy clay, the small air spaces inside get squeezed shut. This stops rainwater from easily soaking down toward the crop roots.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo wu waa loo shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku bibioo Abaamɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabote tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli oya.

english: When plants do not get enough water or face extreme heat, they get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy and stay alive, which stops new fruits from forming.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛshɛɔ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli. Enɛ haa aduawai heei baa.

english: Can heavy downpours ruin the flowers on my cowpeas before seeds can form?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ agbe fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea lɛ nɔ lɛ dani dumɔwui aba?

english: Yes, heavy rain can wash pollen out of open blossoms or break delicate flower stems, preventing proper pollination so the seed pods cannot form.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ni agbele mli lɛ amli muji loo efo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. Koni akɛtsi pollination naa jogbaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ efee dumɔwui ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Why do my pepper plants take much longer to produce flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: During dry months, plants focus their limited water on keeping their leaves alive. Without enough water, they delay flowering until conditions improve.
ga: yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ Tsei haoɔ nu fioo koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi. Kɛji nu bɛ Amɛbaagbe fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing spaces and empty spots where seeds should be?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ ŋmeii loo he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ he ni esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo lɛ?

english: Missing maize kernels usually happen if the plant suffered from dry weather or low soil nutrients during pollination, preventing all the silks on the cob from getting fertilized.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni faaa yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa siliki fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔmɔ nii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with very little fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward to reach light instead of growing thick stems and plentiful fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii babauu.

english: Why do crops grow greener and produce more flowers where I put animal dung on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Animal dung is rich in nitrogen and essential plant foods that feed the soil, giving crops the energy they need to grow strong green leaves and healthy flowers.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ kooloi aŋmɔ mli. Ehaa tsei hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my crops turning yellow while the young top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant lacks water or soil nutrients, it sacrifices its older bottom leaves by moving food from them up to keep the young, developing top leaves alive.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ekɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ejieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ gbɛ aha ŋwɛi baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: How do I choose which vegetable crops like onions or okra will grow best on my land in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala aduawai, tamɔ sabala loo okra, ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Choosing the right crop depends on your local weather, water supply, and soil type. Crops like okra thrive in hot, sunny conditions, while onions need very well-draining soil and distinct dry periods to mature properly.
ga: Nibii ni sa ni ooohala lɛ damɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ okra lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sabala biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ bei srɔtoi ni hulu enyɔ shi koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I plant onion seeds directly into my farm plot or start them in a nursery bed first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu onion dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Onion seeds are very small and fragile, so it is best to nurture them in a protected nursery bed for a few weeks until they become sturdy seedlings before transplanting them into your main field.
ga: Onion dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni abuɔ he lɛ amli otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ dumɔwui ni he wa dani okɛ amɛ awo oŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my okra plants produce plenty of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: When an okra plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water, it spends all its energy growing big leaves instead of producing flowers and fruits. Balancing your fertilizer will encourage flowering.
ga: Kɛ okra tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai wuji. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo fɔfɔii ahe hewalɛ.

english: How often do I need to harvest my okra once the plant starts producing?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makpa okra kɛji tso lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Okra pods grow very quickly once formed. You should harvest them every two to three days while they are still soft and tender; if left too long, the pods become tough and woody, and the plant will stop making new flowers.
ga: Okra pods lɛ daa oya waa kɛji afee lɛ pɛ. Esa akɛ okpa daa gbii Enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛji ashi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei. ni tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my young okra plants curling up and getting tiny holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi okra tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and small holes are signs that tiny insects, like flea beetles or aphids, are eating the leaves. Spraying early with recommended organic or crop protection options stops them from damaging your crop.
ga: Baai kɛ buji bibii ni abɔleɔ amɛhe Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai Mra be mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Kɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ he. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my onion bulbs staying very small even though the leafy tops look tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions lɛ ji bibioo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Onions need loose, light soil to expand into big bulbs. If your soil is hard or compacted, or if the plants are crowded too close together, the bulbs cannot spread out and remain small.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse he hiaa sabolai koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ bulbs agboi. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Aloo kɛji tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Yitso lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ebafeɔ bibioo.

english: Why do my onion leaves start turning yellow and flopping over onto the ground near the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onion baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ beni be lɛ miihe agbe naa lɛ?

english: When onion tops fall over and turn yellow, it is a normal sign that the crop has finished growing. The plant is naturally cutting off growth to let the bulb dry out and mature for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sabolai gbee shi ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ edara. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ nɔ koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛdara kɛha kpamɔɔ.

english: How much water do my onions need as they are growing?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi-onions lɛ kɛ́ amɛdara?

english: Onions have shallow roots and need light, regular watering to stay moist. However, you must reduce watering as the bulbs mature, because too much standing water causes the bulbs to rot.
ga: Sabala shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ehe miihia ni la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nu awo mli daa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ nu ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ aba shi be mli ni bulb lɛ daraa lɛ. Ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant okra in the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu okra yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating with different crops keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ebaafite niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my vegetables are starving for nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-aduawai lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves usually turn light green or yellow, growth slows down, and stems become thin and weak instead of thick and dark green.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the tops are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛyiteŋgbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in high amounts to build green leaves and grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ he miihia babaoo yɛ ŋmãa mli koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall but only produce small, empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli pɛ lɛ?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants fight for sunlight and soil food, causing them to shoot up tall and thin without having enough strength to develop full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I stop small insects from destroying my harvested maize when I store it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii ni mikpa mi-ŋmãa lɛ hiɛ lɛ naa beni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive in moist grain. You must dry your maize thoroughly in the sun until the kernels are very hard before storing them in airtight bags or sealed containers.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa dani okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ko ni atsĩ naa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting them on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, preventing the underground roots from decaying.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why is my cassava growing plenty of big leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ baai wuji nɛkɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the cassava plant to put all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ yucca tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: How do I know which part of the cassava stem is best to cut and plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ afo ni adu?

english: The middle part of a strong, mature cassava stem that is about 8 to 12 months old makes the best planting material because it sprouts reliably and grows strong roots.
ga: Kasava tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ. Ejaakɛ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do some of my cassava tubers taste bitter when I cook them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava produces natural bitter chemicals to protect itself during periods of heat and drought. Bitter varieties need extra processing or thorough boiling to safely remove this taste.
ga: Cassava feɔ tsofai ni mli wa ni ekɛbuɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Nibii ni mli edɔ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ ko loo ashã amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ajie nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the broad leaves of my cocoyam plants burn and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoyam leaves are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. They thrive better when grown in mild shade and in soil that stays moist.
ga: Cocoa baai nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why does cocoyam grow better under the shade of big farm trees than in open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ashishi fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Cocoyam naturally prefers cool, shaded environments because the shade traps moisture in the soil and protects the large leaves from drying out.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, Cocoyams sumɔɔ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shade lɛ mɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebuɔ baai wuji lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, giving the slower-growing cassava room to spread out and mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ naa hegbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni ekwɛɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. This usually happens when the soil nutrients are exhausted or when heavy rains wash away topsoil nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: If a plantain tree produces too many suckers, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the parent plant to focus its energy on producing larger fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmeii babaoo Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibii wuji ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, enriching the field naturally for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ naa nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jara yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. When excess water sits in the soil for too long, it cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing underground rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ baa

english: Why am I seeing holes in the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ko yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in the center leaves of young maize are a classic sign of fall armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of the plant during the day and feed on the soft growing leaves.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko teŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni egbee shi lɛ eba. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Curled and distorted cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the plant's sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe ni efite lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ tomato tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb on to give me bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato tso lɛ aná niji ni kɛlɛ fe tsutsu lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines use tall sticks to spread their leaves wide to catch maximum sunlight. More sun exposure allows the leaves to generate more food, which gets stored underground as large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa babaoo koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmeii wuji

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. High heat scorches their young leaves and dries up the soil quickly, so they need shade trees or plantains nearby to act as temporary umbrellas until they are mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛyashi amɛbaadara

english: Why do my plantain trees tip over and fall so easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches at the top. Tiny pests like nematodes can damage their underground roots, making the plant weak and easily uprooted by wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Nibii bibii tamɔ nematodes baanyɛ afite amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ amɛ shishi oya.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is missing nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, or the soil may simply be tired.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛyeɔ baai eŋɔlii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ sũ lɛ etɔ.

english: Why do my rice plants produce light, empty grains when the rain stops while they are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni eyɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Rice plants need a continuous supply of water when flowering to build solid grains. If the farm dries out during flowering, the plant cannot transport nutrients to the grain head, leaving the hulls empty.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ koni amɛfee dumɔwui ni wa. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya dumɔwui lɛ ayitso. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining. Excessive moisture starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to attack and soften the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food. When the leaves spread out on tall stakes instead of shading each other on the ground, the plant produces much larger tubers below.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii. Beni baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ baajie bulb ni da kwraa fe shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Without steady water and moderate temperatures, the plant sacrifices its flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ baashã afɔle koni amɛhi shi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves. Their feeding damages the leaf tissue and can spread plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsei ahe helai ashwã.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts on my farm help my soil grow better crops next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai baa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Beans and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, that trapped nutrient remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Niyenii nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for me to spread fertilizer on my farm right when heavy rains are falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer off the surface of the land or push it too deep into the ground before the crop's roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not flooded.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eshɛreɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the middle out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa Na shia ni baahi shi daa kɛha fɔmɔ

english: Why should I leave space between my seeds instead of planting them close together to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, ground water, and nutrients, which leaves you with weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa onáa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, shading the cocoa and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛhaa kookoo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rain floods my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water sits in the field without draining, it chokes the soil and starves the roots of air, allowing fungi to attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni nu hoɔ Emɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops dry up and curl during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni ebɔle ehe yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry winds and hot weather draw moisture out of leaves faster than roots can drink from the soil, causing plants to curl their leaves to save water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha tsei lɛ abɔle amɛbaai lɛ ahe koni nu akafite.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the funnel of young corn to eat fresh growth, which can destroy the plant if not treated early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii amli koni amɛye ŋmãa heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tso lɛ hiɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do my pepper leaves twist up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or aphids that suck the juice from leaves, or a virus spread by insect bites.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow, they steal food and water from the main mother tree, resulting in much smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo yɛ lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei yɛ fɔfɔi shi amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when temperatures are too hot, water is too low, or bees are not available to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, nu lɛ faaa tsɔ, loo wuobii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Taakɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating holes into my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn baai lɛ ni eyeɔ ni eshiɔ muji yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize. Catching them early and spraying recommended neem oil mixtures or approved bio-pesticides early in the morning will protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ shi leebi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: If your previous crop had pale yellow leaves, grew very slowly, or produced thin stalks, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Adding well-rotted cow or chicken manure before planting builds up soil health naturally.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong stems and big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without growing any peppers when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa be mli ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to pepper plants, making them shed blossoms to conserve water and survive. Mulching the soil with dry grass and watering at the roots during dry spells helps them keep their flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa chili tsei lɛ anɔ. Ha amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shi ni akɛ nu wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same land with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas alongside maize is very good for your land. Cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better while giving you two separate harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa abele lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crop after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the dirt waiting for water. Clearing weeds within the first three weeks after planting prevents them from stealing water and food from your young crop.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni amɛwɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛmɛ nu Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my dried maize after I store it in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ beni mikɛwo kotoku mli sɛɛ?

english: Insects thrive on moisture, so maize must be dried until the grains crack when bitten. Storing your dry maize in special airtight PICS bags suffocates any insects without needing chemical powders.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baatswa kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi to PICS kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of soft dirt before planting seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yams need loose, raised soil to expand downwards easily. Soil mounds retain moisture, keep the soil cool, and allow the yam tubers to grow long, heavy, and smooth without fighting hard ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ kwɔ bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Gɔji yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa, amɛtsiɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa aka.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten while on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually when watering is irregular. Watering your tomatoes steadily and adding crushed eggshells or lime to the soil prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ nu yɛ mli be fɛɛ be Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmeii ni atswa loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Giving the crop nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn dark green and grow strongly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its stem to grow thick and produce larger, fuller cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to make food. When yam leaves get plenty of sun, they send more energy underground to make bigger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛji sweet potato baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo Amɛbaatsu hewalɛ babaoo kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee yitsei wuji.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only the main stem to produce a much bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri lɛ pɛ koni ekɛfee plantains babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Consistent watering and light shade can help keep flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔii ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing thick foliage but small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are given too much fertilizer early on, the cassava focuses all its energy on growing top leaves instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fe nine mra. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small, young pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani etsɔ agbo?

english: This is called cherelle wilt, which is the tree's natural way of shedding extra pods it cannot afford to feed. However, if too many drop, it can also be a sign of insect damage or lack of moisture.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ efiteɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo gbee shi lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee okadi hu ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi efite loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil-borne diseases that attack and block the plant's root pipes, preventing water from moving up to the leaves even if the soil has moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni etsĩɔ amɛnaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that stops soil water from evaporating in the heat, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la kɛji edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Can I use well water or underground water to irrigate my vegetable crops during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu loo shikpɔŋ shishi nu afɔ aduawai anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, underground water from wells is good for dry season farming, but you must make sure the water is not too salty, because high salt levels burn crop roots and stop them from growing well.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ hi kɛha okwaayeli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ koni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ni fa babaoo lɛ shãa tsei shishifãi ni ehaa amɛdalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do the edges of my vegetable leaves look dry and burnt after watering them with my well water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ aduawai ahe baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni amɛshã beni akɛ nubu mli nu ewo amɛnɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When irrigation water has too much salt content, it draws moisture out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing the leaf tips and edges to dry out and burn.
ga: Kɛji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli ŋmei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baa lɛ naagbee kɛ baa lɛ naa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni eshãa.

english: Why does a hard white layer form on top of my crop beds after I water them during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni wa baa midumɔ saatso lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ nu wo mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When water containing dissolved salts evaporates under the hot sun, it leaves salt crusts behind on top of the soil, which can harm young crop roots.
ga: Kɛ nu ni ŋmei ni mli edɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Ebaashi ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aye tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ awui.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon sun and return to normal in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants fold or droop their leaves during peak heat to protect themselves from losing too much water, and they recover once temperatures cool down.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. ni ebaaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat or lack enough water, as a natural survival mechanism to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow from the bottom up even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when excessive rainfall washes those nutrients away from the root zone.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ ho nakai niyenii lɛ he kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight, so they need shade trees to act as natural covers and keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings bend and grow tall and thin toward one side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee mlɛo yɛ fa kome lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean and stretch toward the strongest source of sunlight when they are not receiving enough direct overhead light, resulting in weak, thin stems.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa he ni hulu la ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, kɛ́ amɛnáaa la ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: When water stands on the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots by cutting off oxygen, which causes the roots to rot and prevents the plant from taking up food.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do my yam plants grow very leafy green vines but only produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ afee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam plants put most of their energy into growing leaves instead of tubers if there is too much nitrogen in the soil or if the plants receive too much shade.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tso lɛ nine shɛɔ hulutsoo babaoo nɔ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food responsible for deep green leaves and healthy growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help bring back their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji tsei aniyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying the leaves with organic pest control like neem oil solution or mild soap water helps clear them off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no bees to move pollen inside the flower. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting flowering weeds nearby to attract bees helps fruit to form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baatsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ jwɛi ni woɔ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Koni agbala ŋmeii kɛba lɛ baaye abua ni ewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are like baby trees—their tender leaves get scorched easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and provide tall, leafy shade that protects cocoa from the heat while keeping the soil cool and damp during the dry season.
ga: Kookoo tso bibioo tamɔ tso bibioo. Ebaai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛhaa baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ shade ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and soil food, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching neighboring plants. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room, air, and light to produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ahe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb up to catch direct sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture food for its roots. Keeping the vines off the ground on stakes allows leaves to catch more light, resulting in much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii kɛhaa eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie wein tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the soil when rain falls heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away, effectively drowning the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow off so the roots stay healthy.
