ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass help my crops stay alive during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like an umbrella over the dirt. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, helping soil trap moisture much longer so plants survive rainless days.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ambrela ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔ gbii anɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and weaker even when rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the natural food and water in the soil so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. koni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots from my plantain plant so that only a few remain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ plantain tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ?

english: If too many young shoots grow from one plantain stem, they all share the mother plant's food, causing small bunches. Removing extra suckers so that only two or three grow leaves more food for big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo jɛ tso kome mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baajara fɔlɔ tso lɛ niyenii. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Enɛ jieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa niyenii babaoo baa plantain tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same land where I am planting new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo hee yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa shoots burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and holding soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I prevent my maize leaves from turning yellow and drying up before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmãa baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi dani akpa?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or pests like fall armyworms are feeding on the crop. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea at the right stage and regularly checking leaves for pests will keep the crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms eye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli, ni okwɛ baai lɛ amli daa kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to plant my cassava in straight rows instead of scattering them around the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋsɔɔdoi ni ja mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ, ani ehi fe no?

english: Planting in rows gives each cassava stem enough space to catch sunlight and absorb nutrients, resulting in bigger tubers. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená hulu la ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ agboi. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: If crops from your previous harvest grew slowly, produced small yields, or had pale leaves, the soil has lost nutrients. Adding animal manure, compost, or suitable chemical fertilizers helps rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni jɛ okpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ daraa blɛoo Yibiiwoo ni baa shi loo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ efite. Koolooi ashishifãi ni sa, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to keep my pepper plants alive when the rains stop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa pepper tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the base of your pepper plants with dry grass or fallen leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ shwie pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: What causes tiny insects to gather under my cowpea leaves, and how do I get rid of them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ashishi? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ majie amɛ kɛjɛ mihe?

english: These insects are aphids that suck plant sap and cause leaves to curl. You can control them by spraying a natural neem leaf water extract or recommended mild insecticides early in the morning.
ga: Kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I save maize seeds from my current harvest to plant next season, or buy new certified seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Using seeds saved from hybrid crops usually leads to weaker plants and lower yields. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures high germination, disease resistance, and a bigger harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni he ehiaaa ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: Why do experienced farmers say I should not plant maize on the same piece of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same soil nutrients and allows specific pests and diseases to build up. Alternating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact time my yams are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo?

english: Yams are ready for full harvest when the green leaves and vines turn yellow and completely dry up. Harvesting too early reduces tubers size, while leaving them too long exposes them to underground pests.
ga: Sweet potatoes efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tuber lɛ dalɛ aba shi. yɛ be mli ni ashiɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that weevils do not destroy the grains inside the storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? Koni ŋmeii akafite ŋmaa ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Make sure the maize is thoroughly sun-dried until the grains are hard. Store them in airtight storage bags (PICS bags) or clean containers kept on raised wooden platforms off the floor.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni hulu lɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Okɛto kotoku ko ni akɛ nibii ni mli ewo muji ewo mli (PICS kotoku) loo kotoku ni mli tse ni akɛto tso kpoku ko ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I spend extra money buying certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika babaoo kɛhe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially tested and bred to resist local pests and diseases while giving higher yields. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over time, resulting in weaker crops and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why do some improved maize seeds grow much faster and produce bigger cobs than my local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji fe mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are selected for high vigor, meaning they absorb soil nutrients and water more efficiently. This allows the plant to develop quickly and put more energy into growing large, healthy cobs.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa oya ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry for fertilizer, and what actually happens to them when I apply it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni baa nakai tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves turn yellow, stems stay thin, and growth slows down. Fertilizer supplies essential food like nitrogen and phosphorus to the soil, helping the leaves turn green, roots expand, and yields increase.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. kɛ shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli, shishifãi lɛ mlilɛɔ ni nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive high heat. Adding nutrients and protecting the soil with organic cover helps the roots stay moist so the crop recovers quickly when rains start.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Nibii ni haa mɔ he waa ni akɛfataa he kɛ sũ ni akɛ tsofai fɔji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsei lɛ he waa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I plant seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow thick stems and full fruit heads.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ waa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso lɛ mli tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ayitsei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow well in one section of my field but stay small and weak in another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi eji bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Soil nutrition and water depth vary across a single piece of land. Areas with poor, hard, or nutrient-depleted soil produce weaker crops unless compost, fertilizer, or soil management practices are applied.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ mlibotemɔ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii, ni wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii agbɔjɔ. Ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ nifeemɔi tsu nii.

english: Why do green caterpillars attack the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miitutua mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are often fall armyworms that target the soft, tender growing leaves at the center of young maize plants. Treating the crop early protects the plant's main growing point so it can produce cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kwɛɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebuɔ he titri ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he koni anyɛ afee cob.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before turning into full tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ tomato ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall when the plant faces heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping water supply steady and adding balanced fertilizers helps flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Nu jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni oookwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli lɛ baaye abua ofɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does preparing my land with tractor equipment help my crops grow better than clearing by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ trakta nibii saa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ minine shwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Equipment breaks up hard soil deep underground, allowing plant roots to grow deeper, reach underground moisture, and absorb nutrients far better than shallow hand-tilled soil.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ

english: How can bringing a sample of my sick crops to the local Farmer Center help me save my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ eko ni mikɛbaaya mimaŋ okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato?

english: Officers at the center can examine the leaf or stem damage under proper guidance to identify the exact disease or insect, giving you the right treatment before the problem spreads across your whole farm.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ baa loo tso lɛ yibii ni efite lɛ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni sa shishi koni amɛna helai loo kooloi bibii pɔtɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ona tsamɔ ni sa dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply all my fertilizer to my maize crops at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ woɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: If you give all the fertilizer at once, heavy rains can wash it away before the roots absorb it. Applying it in smaller portions as the crop grows ensures the plant gets food when it needs it most.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wo mli shikome Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ akɛ fã bibioo ko tsuɔ nii Beni tso lɛ miida lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: What does potassium fertilizer do to help my cassava and yam crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Potassium helps crops build strong roots and large tubers, protects them from drought stress, and makes them strong enough to resist diseases.
ga: Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ he ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai srɔtoi

english: Yellow leaves often show that the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaa nii bibii.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has good food for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily, stays moist after rain, and contains earthworms or decaying plant matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su tsuɔ, efoɔ oya, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Can giving my crops too much chemical fertilizer burn them?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ?

english: Yes, using too much chemical fertilizer concentrated at the roots can draw moisture out of the plant, scorching the leaves and stunting growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops look weak and pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops' roots, leaving your plants hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant maize on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Is it better to apply liquid fertilizer to my crops in the early morning or afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli leebi loo shwane?

english: Applying liquid nutrients early in the morning lets the roots absorb them before the hot afternoon sun causes the moisture to evaporate.
ga: Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ji nu lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I trim off the extra lower leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shishi baai ni fa fe nine yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming lower leaves prevents damp soil from spreading fungal diseases to the plant and helps the crop focus its energy on growing healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ akagbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛba tso lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ maa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I start planting my seeds in small nursery bags instead of going straight to the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui yɛ grow bag bibioo mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooya ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Starting seeds in small nursery bags protects young seedlings from harsh sunlight, heavy rain, pests, and weeds while they are still weak, giving them a higher survival rate before they move to the main farm field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ jwɛi ahe be mli ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni hiɔ shi lɛ ayi fa babaoo dani amɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How long should my crop seedlings stay in nursery bags before I move them onto my main field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi tso dumɔwui lɛ ahi grow bags lɛ amli dani mikɛ amɛ awo mi ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings usually need to grow in nursery bags for about three to four months. By this time, their stems and roots are strong enough to handle the outdoor conditions on your main land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔji amli aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ, ni nakai beaŋ lɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu kponɔgbɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ titri lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: What does it mean when agricultural officers talk about a double-stage farming method?
ga: Kɛ́ okwaayeli he onukpai wie gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: The double-stage method means growing your crop in two steps: first raising delicate seedlings in small nursery bags for a few months, and then transplanting them to their permanent planting spots in the main field.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaakwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ŋmɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli nyɔji fioo komɛi. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsimɔ kɛya he ko ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How do I know that my nursery seedlings are ready to be transplanted to the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready to be transplanted after three to four months when they have built strong roots, developed several healthy leaves, and reached a firm height that can withstand open field weather.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ wa lɛ. Eyɛ baai babaoo ni mli wa. ni eyɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do plants grown in nursery bags need closer care than seeds planted directly in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ tsei ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Small nursery bags hold a limited amount of soil and dry out faster, so the young plants need frequent, careful watering and protection from extreme heat until their roots are well developed.
ga: Grow bags bibii lɛ hiɛɔ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ tsei bibii anɔ nu shii abɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What type of soil should I put in the small nursery bags to help my young seeds sprout well?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ mikɛwo mi grow bag bibioo lɛ mli? Koni eye ebua mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: You should fill nursery bags with loose, rich topsoil mixed with well-rotted manure or compost so the tiny roots can easily grow and absorb nutrients without getting waterlogged.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ efutu mli lɛ awo grow bag lɛ mli koni ewo shishifãi bibii lɛ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eda ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni nu bɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to keep young seedling bags under shade during their first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ dumɔwui kotokui awo hulutsoo shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts are easily scorched by direct sunlight and dried out by heat. Keeping nursery bags under a shaded canopy keeps them cool and moist while they build strength.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii oya, ni dɔlɛ baanyɛ agbi amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-grow bags lɛ to hulutsoo shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa hewalɛ hu baa.

english: What is the correct way to remove a seedling from its nursery bag so I do not destroy the roots?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotokui amli? Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akafite?

english: You should gently cut or peel the plastic bag away from the root ball so that the soil around the roots stays intact when you place the seedling into the hole on your main field.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ loo ojie plastic kotoku lɛ kɛjɛ shishifã bɔɔlu lɛ he blɛoo. koni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ akafite beni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ bu ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Does using nursery bags for crops help me save money on seeds?
ga: Ani grow bags ni mikɛduɔ tsei lɛ baanyɛ aha maná shika yɛ dumɔwui ahe?

english: Yes, nursery bags help save money because you can carefully protect almost every seed you sow, leading to fewer dead seedlings compared to planting directly in a big field where pests and bad weather kill seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, baagi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haaa okɛ shika akafite ejaakɛ obaanyɛ obu nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni oduɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ fioo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ kpataaa dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ lɛ he.

english: Can I leave my crop seedlings in the small nursery bags for longer than four months if my field is not ready?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi tsei dumɔwui yɛ grow bags bibii amli nɔ ni fe nyɔji ejwɛ kɛji mihe lɛ efeee klalo?

english: It is best not to leave them too long because the seedling roots will run out of space in small bags, causing the roots to coil and the plant to become stunted and weak.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baaho yɛ kotoku bibioo lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni ebɔle ehe kɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: How close to a river can I safely plant my crops without damaging them?
ga: Te manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: While crops need water, planting too close to a riverbank can drown their roots from waterlogged soil or cause them to be washed away during unexpected flooding. Planting a few meters back allows the roots to access damp soil without suffocating.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni nu he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa naa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshishifãi lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ loo eha nu afua amɛ yɛ nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu mitai fioo komɛi kɛtee sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa amɛhe ajɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants start rotting when heavy rain leaves standing water around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shi nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil just as much as water. When water stays pooled around the stem, it suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases that cause the stem and root system to rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi kɛ agbɛnɛ hu nu. Kɛ́ nu babɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tso lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What fast-yielding crops can I plant so my household has food quickly while waiting for major harvests?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii oya manyɛ madu koni maha mishiabii lɛ niyenii oya be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ kpeteŋkpele lɛ?

english: Short-cycle crops like cowpeas, amaranth (aleefu), and sweet potatoes can be harvested within two to three months, providing reliable food and income while longer-term crops like cassava or cocoa mature.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ tsina, amaranth (alifu), kɛ sweet potato yɛ nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. Ha niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ shika ni anáa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmei loo kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why does cassava manage to survive long dry seasons when other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni tsei krokomɛi gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava is a naturally resilient crop that stores water and energy in its thick underground tubers and sheds its upper leaves to save moisture until rain falls again.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe. Amɛtoɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse amli. Ni shwiemɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much bigger on land that was left unplanted for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduko nɔ afii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow allows nature to rest restore nutrients to the earth naturally through decomposing plants and weed roots, giving new crops a rich supply of plant food.
ga: He ko ni ashiɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ lɛ jɔɔ ehe, ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa adebɔɔ mli je lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ jwɛi shishifãi anɔ. Ehaa tsei heei náa tsei niyenii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support a good crop yield before I sow seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well without becoming muddy, feels crumbly in your hand, and supports natural weed or grass growth easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa efee muji. Enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ enine mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa adebɔɔ mli jwɛi loo jwɛi ni edaa oya.

english: When seeds are planted too tightly, the individual plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall for sun instead of growing fat cobs.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt during the hottest afternoon hours even when the ground has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Extreme heat causes leaves to lose water faster than roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant droops to shrink its leaf area exposed to the sun and usually recovers once the heat cools in the evening.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ ni eha baa lɛ he lɛ afee bibioo yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe feɔ shoo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I plant them in a completely open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my main crops and choke them if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mitsei titrii lɛ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ mi kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants adapted to steal food, water, and sunlight before domesticated crops can establish strong roots. Clearing them early gives your crops the space they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani shia tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa. Okɛ ohe awo mli mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná he ko ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and crumpling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects or infected stems. It reduces the leaf's ability to make food, causing leaves to shrink and yield to drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of the hot sun or because of a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ loo tsei ahe hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Sun-wilted plants usually recover in the cool morning after resting at night. If your plant stays wilted even in the morning or when the soil is wet, a bacterial or fungal disease is likely blocking its water pipes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hulu eshã amɛ lɛ he waaa yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ hejɔɔmɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji otso lɛ tee nɔ egbo leebi po loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ hela ko jɛ bacteria loo fungus ni tsiɔ nu paipi lɛ naa lɛ mli.

english: If I see black spots on one cocoa pod, will the whole tree wither and die?
ga: Kɛ́ ona ŋmeii diji yɛ kookoo tso kome nɔ lɛ, ani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo ni ebaagbo?

english: Not immediately, but Black Pod disease spreads quickly through rain drops. If you remove the affected pod right away, the main tree trunk remains safe, but if ignored, it can spread to other pods and weaken branches.
ga: Ebaaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ, shi black pod hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya kɛtsɔ nugbɔshiimɔi anɔ. Kɛji ojie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ baahi shi shweshweeshwe. Shi kɛji okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ emaaa nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã pods krokomɛi anɔ. ni eha niji lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why do the stems of my tomato plants turn soft and rot right at the ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually damping-off or stem rot caused by fungi in overly wet soil. The fungus attacks the base of the stem where it meets the dirt, cutting off water to the rest of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji dampening loo stem rot ni ŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine mli lɛ kɛbaa. Fuŋ lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ shishi yɛ he ni eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Ha nu lɛ agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can a crop disease jump from my neighbour's field into my farm?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ajɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plant diseases can travel through wind, splashed rain, insects, shared farm tools, or even on dirty boots when moving between different fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ amli. aloo yɛ atadei ni mli ewo muji po nɔ kɛ́ onyiɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ.

english: Can a plant disease stay hidden in my soil and attack the new crops I plant next season?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua tsei heei ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, many fungi and bacteria live in plant roots and soil for years. Rotating your crops by planting a different type of crop next season starves the disease so it dies out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi babaoo hiɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ sũ mli afii babaoo. Kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni adu yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni egbo.

english: How do I know if my crop is damaged by insects or by a fungal infection?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Insects usually leave physical holes, chewed edges, or sticky liquid on leaves. Fungal infections create dry spots, powdery coatings, slimy patches, or dark rings without actually chewing the plant tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi shĩɔ bu, ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ, loo nu ni kpɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Fungal helai kɛ hei ni egbi baa. Powder ni akɛwo mli Eji muji he ko. Aloo amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii ni amɛyeee tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: What should I do right away if I notice a strange spot or disease on a few leaves in my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina ŋmeii loo helai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ baai fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Pluck off the infected leaves immediately, put them in a closed bag, and burn or bury them far away from your farm to prevent spores from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Jiemɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Okɛwo kotoku ko ni aŋã mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, shã loo ofu lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my pepper leaves twisting upwards and refusing to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper is caused by viral infections spread by sap-sucking pests like aphids and thrips. Controlling those small pests early prevents the virus from stopping plant growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli ni nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ aphids kɛ thrips lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ anɔyeli mra Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkakpa tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain fruits drop off the bunch before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop is often caused by root-damaging pests like banana nematodes or fungal leaf spot diseases that weaken the plant so much that it cannot hold the weight of its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi, tamɔ banana nematodes lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ oya lɛ baa. loo leaf spot disease ni ŋmei kɛbaa Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ enyɛɛɛ ekɛ tso yibii lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves and make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni amɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree before growing into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they are not pollinated by tiny midges or if the tree is under stress from drought or high heat.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛji akɛ tooi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ hɔmɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody instead of soft when I cook them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tamɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo kɛ́ ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots turn tough and woody if they are left in the soil past their normal harvest age or if the crop experiences prolonged dry periods during tuber growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ebaafee tso kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe be ni sa ni akpaa lɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ be mli ni tuber lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of flowers but fail to set any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop without forming fruit when temperatures are extremely high or when excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe yibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the tomato plant rolls its leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself from intense heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted out in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sun; they need shade from nurse plants like plantains during their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do black spots appear on my plant leaves when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Persistent rainfall and high humidity create warm, wet conditions on plant leaves that allow fungal spores to attach, grow, and create leaf spot disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa haa dɔlɛ, fɔ́ shihilɛ yɛ tsei baai anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, fungal spores baanyɛ akpɛtɛ he, amɛdara ni amɛfee baa he hela.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during strong windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy and vulnerable to wind unless supported with bamboo props.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ oya. Ja akɛ nibii ni akɛ ŋmei fee tsu nii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and split under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbala yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become bent or split when planted in hard, rocky, or compacted soil that physically blocks the tuber from expanding smoothly downward.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baabɔle loo amɛbaagbala kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shi jogbaŋŋ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas after harvesting my maize make the land produce better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, while leguminous crops like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and restore it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do fall armyworms know when my maize has just sprouted, and why do they target the young leaves?
ga: Te fall cutworms lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛleɔ akɛ mi-abele lɛ ekwɛ̃ pɛŋ? Ni mɛni hewɔ amɛtutuaa baai bibii lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths are attracted to the smell and chemical signals released by young, growing maize plants. They lay their eggs on tender leaves so that when the worms hatch, they immediately have soft, nutritious food that is easy for them to chew.
ga: Autumn ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsofai okadii ni ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ jieɔ lɛ. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ baai bibii anɔ bɔni afee ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔlɔ waaa.

english: How does planting marigold flowers around my vegetable bed trick crop insects into staying away?
ga: Marigolds ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ alaka kooloi bibii kɛya?

english: Marigolds release strong scents and underground root chemicals that mask the smell of your main crops. This confuses harmful insects and nematodes, tricking them into thinking there is no food there so they move away.
ga: Marigolds jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa kɛ tsofai kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ni haa onibii titri ni oduɔ lɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ nematodes lɛ feɔ basabasa. Kɛtsɔ amɛlakamɔ nɔ ni amɛsusu akɛ niyenii ko bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛfã kɛtee jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling inward, the leaves reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, which stops the plant from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛtsɔ mligbɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during severe dry spells as a survival trick. By shedding leaves, the plant stops using water and goes to sleep above ground while keeping its edible root alive in the soil until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli akɛ teemɔŋ sane ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ nu kɛ nitsumɔ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers but end up dropping most of them without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi efoɔ amɛteŋ babaoo ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can afford to feed. The tree drops excess flowers on purpose so it can save its energy and water to grow only the pods it can properly support.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛkwɛ̃ fɔfɔi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do some of my yam seed pieces sprout quickly after planting while others stay dormant in the dirt for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ adu lɛ? yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi ehi shi lɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo

english: Yam tubers have a natural resting clock inside them called dormancy. The seed piece will not sprout until its internal hormones signal that enough time has passed and that moisture levels in the soil are right for growth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa yɛ mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ wɔɔhe. Dumɔwui amli fãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛyashi be mli ni tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ akɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa eho ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ sa kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my plantains grow better and yield bigger fruits when planted near cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains and cocoa work together well. Plantain leaves provide shade that keeps the soil cool for cocoa, while falling cocoa leaves decay into rich compost that feeds the shallow roots of the plantain trees.
ga: Plantain kɛ cocoa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Plantain baai haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛha kookoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen remains in the dirt as natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei kɛha oŋmei lɛ.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my field even after I cut it down to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifo lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spear grass stores its food in deep underground roots called rhizomes. Even when you destroy the grass above ground, the hidden underground stem uses its stored food energy to shoot up new leaf stems.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ toɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes lɛ amli. Kɛji okpãtã jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ po Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtswaa baa tsei heei.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark and rotten before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee duŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, making it hard for the roots to pull calcium up from the soil into the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbala calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya tomato ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides living shade, keeping the air cool and soil moist until the cocoa roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaha shade aba, eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: I noticed small caterpillars eating holes through the leaves of my young maize plants. What is happening to my crop?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds inside the whorl of young maize leaves. If not controlled early, they damage the growing point of the plant and reduce harvest yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra Efiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my maize field to get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Maize needs fertilizer at two main stages: a first small application about two weeks after seeds sprout to support root growth, and a second application around knee-high stage before flowering to support cob development.
ga: Abele he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: shishijee la ni akɛwoɔ mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ adalɛ; kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ ni akɛshwieɔ he ni shɛɔ tsitsi nɔ lɛ he dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni eye ebua ni cob lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of big green leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess moisture, cassava uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to store energy in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ a kɛ he wami nɛ to tso ɔ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Is it really necessary for me to erect tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko he gbɛjianɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, allowing the leaves to make maximum food through sunlight, which directly results in larger, healthier underground tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: My pepper plant leaves are curling up and twisting. What causes this to happen?
ga: Mi pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe. Mɛni ha eba lɛ nakai?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies, which feed on the leaves and can also spread leaf curl viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ leaf curl virus hu amɛshwã tsei amli.

english: My tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers dry up and drop off without forming fruits. Why?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgbeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii. Maaba?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is insufficient insect or wind activity to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the new suckers growing around my main plantain tree to grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mashɛreɔ ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ fɛɛ? Mi plantain titri ni mikɛbaafee ekome kɛkwɛ̃

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates competition for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, which leads to weak stems and small fruit bunches. Pruning down to one main stem and one or two strong suckers yields bigger plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa kɛ aduawai bibii. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso lɛ yitso titri kome kɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui wuji aba.

english: How does spreading dry grass or dry leaves around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tso lɛ ni edaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading organic mulch around plants traps moisture in the soil, shields roots from extreme tropical heat, suppresses weeds, and gradually breaks down into natural soil nutrients.
ga: Gbalamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he. Tsei mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant seeds close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?
